reviews.comment: I consider myself an above average student so all I needed to do was go to class and be engaged. If you don't consider yourself mathematically inclined and you chose not to go to see his class you will not do great. He is a good professor there is just a bit of a language barrier however nothing you can't overcome if you just attend.
Not the greatest professor, he could not translate some of these harder topics well at all. Would go off on pretty funny tangents that made the class bearable, but the exams were difficult.
Horrible Professor do not recommend. Horrible at teaching concepts that other professors teach flawlessly, incredibly hard final.

The mock exams he provides are completely different from the actual exams. He significantly increases the difficulty of the real exams to control the grade distribution. Moreover, during lectures, he is often complacent and sometimes doesn't even seem to know what he is talking about.

[AVOID THIS PROFESSOR!] He's a kind person with awful teaching ability. There is very little practice material and he puts off grading things till the last minute. The best reference material you'll get is the lecture slides, and they are organized very poorly. The lectures move very slowly and he ends up cramming the difficult content last minute.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ali is very nice and will make jokes throughout lectures to keep things from getting too stale. The questions on the exams tend to be tougher than those done in lectures. He will hint during class if a question is going to be on the exam which can help you study what you need to. Do the extra credit and go to class!

Ali is a very nice guy and I personally really liked his teaching method for the most part. I literally ended with over 100% in the class because of how much extra credit he gives and the fact that all exam problems are problems taken directly from the homeworks made for pretty easy exams. I'm no genius either considering I almost failed 2321.

[AVOID THIS PROF] He's a kind person, but oh my is his teaching awful. You think you know the content and then you do awful on the exam.

There is zero good reference material. The lecture slides are the best you'll get, and those are organized very poorly. Very little homework is given, so you get very little practice material.
CSE 2331 can be a difficult class but Ali does a good job explaining the material and goes at the pace of the class. He offers lots of extra credit for all exams which boosts grades a lot.

Ali really cares about the students, makes funny jokes. I'm going to be real, I probably would have failed the class without the extra credit :) This class has a group project about graph theory which was a nice grade boost. I would have done better If I studied more, but Ali is great! However, his lecture recordings are not that good. GO 2 CLASS.

I loved Professor Ali's class! He gives extra credit assignments throughout each exam cycle, which are super helpful! Not only do they boost your exam grades by a huge margin, but they are also great practice. He is also very caring and funny. My only complaint was that he was rather difficult to reach by email. Highly recommend!

Genuinely cares about students. Lots of extra credit that's added to exams. Disliked that we had a final project due the day before the final over something not really covered in class. Overall, his lectures we engaging and I went to his office hours and he was very helpful

Foundations was difficult and Ali did his best to teach but he is quite fast, so make sure to ask questions if something doesn't click. There is a lot of extra credit so make sure to do it for a buffer!!! Work with others and focus on understanding in class problems and study terms and algorithms and their running times. watch YT videos, they help!

Do not take this course if you want a good grade. Especially if you're better at learning on your own. I'm a commuter and had a class directly after 2321, so I worked mostly independently. Unfortunately, this professor tends to be disorganized during lecture and even more so online. Rubrics and grading are extremely vague. Be prepared to reach out.
Decent professor and lectures.  Gives the easiest examples in class and the homework's and exam's are much harder.  Heard he is one of the harder professors for the class.

Very passionate and knowledgeable. One of the few professors that actually cares and want to teach. He would repeat each concept at least three times before moving on to make sure everyone understood. Hands out bunch of extra credits. Exams aren't hard, some of the questions were even straight out from homework / extra practices he handed out.

He was a very nice guy and actually cares about his students, but he was not the best at explaining content and would often confuse me more during lectures. His office hours were useful and helpful, but his exams were extremely hard and the final was rather unfair. His final project was harder and more work than any of my coding classes.

I found Professor Ali to be an incredibly helpful professor who was very passionate about the material. I appreciated how he gave many extra credit opportunities, as it allowed for more guided practice in class. The exams weren't bad and he also provided many study materials. If you attend lectures and ask questions, you'll probably do well.

I think Ali was a great professor. His style may not work for everyone, but for me, this is exactly the kind of teaching I like and succeed with. Extra credit for thos who come to class, always welcomes questions and trys to be helpful in every way. Lots of office hours. material is hard but offers lots of practice to know what to expect.
Extremely tough grader, homeworks are confusing/ time consuming, exams are difficult, office hours packed

Ali is a very kind professor and all of his teaching is fine before the final. However, I don't understand why there are questions about graph theory in final and if I'm remembered correctly, he even didn't finish it on class??? It cause my grade fall to B+ from A.

I don't think he have a curve since there are many optional extra credits.

I had Professor Ali for both foundations 1 &2. He is an amazing professor and cares for his students. The first best skill he presents is knowing his students' names. If you do your homework and the extra credit questions then you will do well on the exams. He has office hours every day and is very helpful and easily approachable
He is a great professor and cares for his students. He is the best professor I have taken so far here at osu!

Very difficult grader. Argues with you after asking for help. Homework confusing/ extremely long. Lectures extremely confusing. Calls out for missing even one class (even with valid excuses). Avoid at all costs!

Grading scheme is extremely difficult, and although extra credit opportunities are available, the exam averages are extremely low. Asking for help is also difficult, as office hours are usually packed, and I usually walk away from office hours feeling lost/ attacked for asking questions. Made me feel very upset on multiple occasions.

- Currently have A's in the rest of my classes so I really don't like this man and his accent.
-  No clear grading criteria. 
- I failed the midterm, but The midterm is a clone of the homework and the past papers which I got 100%
- a suspicion that he will fail you on purpose if you don't come to his classes.

I can imagine this professor being good for a certain type of student, but I could not for the life of me figure out the material. If you are good at listening to lectures and understanding them in the moment then you will do well. If you are more about figuring things out outside of class, you are screwed.

Ali is funny and cares about his students. He will learn your name quickly. He cares that you understand the content and responds well to questions. He's approachable after class. The homework is difficult and takes a long time, but it's only every 2 weeks. The exams are difficult, but he gives a lot of extra credit. He posts hw answers after.

Very nice teacher. Foundations 1 is a difficult class, but he teaches well. He also consistently stays after class to answer questions from students. One note is DO ALL EXTRA CREDIT and GO TO LECTURES. He doesn't curve but offers a lot of extra credit to make up for it, and only gives extra credit if people show up to class.

He teaches a difficult subject but makes it something that almost anyone can understand if you go to class and pay attention. He is always willing to answer questions and is very nice. He cares about his students and he is funny during class. He gives extra credit almost weekly if you come to class and do practice problems.

Ali Alilooee is an amazing professor, unarguably one of the most fun professors I've been taught by so far. He really cares about his students understanding everything, he has well paced lectures, and really wants students to do well. Thanks to him, I've really enjoyed the course, if you have him available for foundations 1, definitely go with him.

Fnd2. Tons of extra credit. Optional attendance but if u attend there is extra credit.
Easy exams, exactly like hw. Just make sure to understand hw by going to office hours (where he is super nice and will explain exactly how to do problems)
He is an incredibly nice guy and really cares about his students. Sometimes funny too.
Responds to feedback.

This class teaches important concepts that are honestly not too difficult to understand, in a way that's confusing and hard to understand. I learned more from five minutes of googling. That said, he was super nice and the class was really easy. As long as you understand the homework's (literally just go to office hours for this) you are gold.

I had him for Fnd. 1 & 2. In Fnd. 2, he apologized to me for how poorly he taught Fnd. 1 (his first time teaching it). He said he made major changes to how he taught that course and made it better. He offers ALOT of extra credit outside and in class, DO IT AND YOU'LL GET AN A. Go to lectures, and office hours, do extra credit.Ali is a wonderful man

Great professor! He cares a lot about his students and teaching well and it shows. Offers basically infinite extra credit (high on midterm 1 was 143!) and will do his best to explain any questions. Tests are fair in that if you study the material there are no curve balls. It can be hard but it is very fair. He's very passionate about what he does!

I have had him 2 semesters in a row now. I think most of the frustration on here comes from his first semester here. He was a lot more difficult in foundations 1 than when I had him again for foundations 2. The tests are always fair and based on hw and he gives lots of extra credit. He has a clear love for the subject and I learned a lot from him.

Ali is an amazing professor that is very accessible to his students outside of his office hours. He is keen to help struggling students, however, improper feedback on assignments and inconsistent grading schedule for homework and midterms are factors that make his class difficult for students. But his midterms are easy and a lot of extra credit.

Although many of the tests take from the homework, there were many instances where you would get full marks for the homework, but a 0 for the same exact problem with the same exact proof on a test. Little to no feedback from homework as well. Has written things such as did you even study on a low score test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No feedback at all on graded assignments/tests/quizzes. Homework is often hard, points deduction are often unclear, average test/quiz scores are often on the failing zone, unclear on what he wants as the answer, doesn't give partial credit to an answer, bad at explaining complex concepts. I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND
Ali was a very tough and unclear grader who gave little feedback. At the least, he gave a lot of extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He was one of my best Professors so far at OSU. His office hours were 24/7. He was passionate about his job and tried hard to understand materials. The extra credit helps me a lot to boost my grade. The course wasnt easy, but as long as you dont miss the class and do all your homework and extra credit, you will get a decent grade.
Homework and tests are always beyond the level of this class. He has office hour almost every day but seldom show up before tests. Be ready to learn by yourself!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took his foundations 1 class. Overall, extremely difficult grader and gives literally no feedback on tests/quizzes. His extra credit is helpful but class averages even with extra credit were easily failing grades. Despite this, he says no to curving. If youre forced to take his class, make sure to ask for help and clarification on missed points.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I almost come to his office hours every week to make sure I understand all the things in the note and the questions in homework. Reading the textbook before the lecture could make sure I understand his class well. The exams and quizzes are quite easy because they are all in the homework or notes. With the extra credits, I got full marks on quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of my biggest issues that I had in Ali's class was that the class was never provided back proper feedback on homeworks and extra credits. Another issue was that our homeworks were often graded after tests and quizzes which should not happen. The tests and quizzes are quite hard but it is offset by the fact that a lot of extra credit is provided

Take anyone but her. She will get passive and visibly annoyed over wrong answers. Most weeks we go over the same point every day and its fully read off a slide show. Hard grader. Acts like her whole family was killed if someone gets something wrong.

She would get visibly annoyed if you didn't understand what she was saying even though she would often use very advanced vocab/grammar for a beginner class. Also, she would just read off a powerpoint & then give you a minute to answer questions she barely taught you for an hour every day. Theres a lot of homework & she's very strict with her grades

This professor was very unhelpful and overall passive-aggressive towards us. She talked briefly, gave us questions, and then made us do partner or group work for the whole class. I do not recommend taking Spanish 1103 with her if possible. Still relatively easy, but could not stand her.

The class I took was not very difficult; it was pretty enjoyable. She talks in Spanish so it helps train audio comprehension. Participation is graded and attendance is important for your tests, as we go over topics that will be on them.

Prof. Angulo was a very sweet lady. Participation is a must in this class, which makes sense since it is a language class. She truly cares about students and is willing to work through issues with you in a timely manner. There is simple daily homework and weekly homework that comes from the textbooks. I thought the exams were fair.

Take this class with any other professor. She is so difficult when it comes to assignments and what she wants and also wastes so much class time. She weighs participation and attendance more than the loads of daily homework or even the exams. No one gets a perfect score on participation which hurt my grade in the end.

There was a lot of homework and participation was mandatory but I learned a lot from her. If you're looking for an easy professor Alejandra isn't going to be the right professor for you but she genuinely cares about her students.

Super fun in class and very dedicated to getting to know her students and having a good time in a learning environment. Only bump in the road was a technology issue between us that she wouldn't accept even after we found out what went wrong. Was the difference between an A and an A- unfortunately.

She was a very compassionate prof, always believed in her students. You have to put in the effort to get grades, there are a lot of small things to learn. In class participation is a must, but for good reason, helps you learn faster. She speaks mostly in spanish, but if you pay attention, it makes sense based on knowledge and context clues.

Half of the time she spoke I could not understand the words she was saying, and she rarely spoke English. This was one of the toughest classes I have taken, not because of the material, but because of her disregard for a learning curve, and she honestly seemed like she thought we were all native speakers. Her grading is tough, but she means well.
Professora desconsiderada . Literally take this class with anybody else. As somebody who is funding these professors and the university, you deserve the best and most compassionate educators.

SHE DOES NOT SPEAK ENGLISH.... DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU CANNOT UNDERSTAND FLUENT SPANISH. YOU NEED TO PARTICIPATE TO GET CREDIT!! 15 points for each unit is based on participation, she rarely gives out 15/15s, Very small class, with 13 people. tests and quizzes weren't horrible. Be sure to have a lot of Spanish knowledge prior to this class

Genuinely enjoyed her as the semester went on. I wasn't good at spanish in the least bit and still managed an A- because of her. She preps you well for all of the big tests and assignments. You can tell she cares about her students and creates a positive classroom environment.

This class is fast paced and she mostly speaks in Spanish, but it's a great way to practice your listening skills. She seemed to genuinely enjoy teaching us and it was a fun class. The homework is mostly busywork but not hard to get through and is good practice. Study the material and participate often and you'll do great

She runs through the lectures very quickly and speaks Spanish most of the time, so you definitely have to listen and pay attention to what she says. Her class structure was pretty solid. She really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An alright spanish professor. Native speaker so speaks in spanish 90% of the time. Gets very frustrated and mad if the whole class doesnt participate for every single question. Exams tend to have a lot of questions containing stuff she doesnt go over or suggest you study which was pretty frustrating. lots of little hw assignments due every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Many people felt they were treated like they were stupid at some points. Most of the time, she just ran through the subjects and practices. Very good at getting students involved!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really good professor that cares about her students. Participation matters a lot, but participating is what helps you the most to understand the information. I took a lot of spanish in high school so this class was mostly a review for me which made it easier, but my classmates that had less spanish experience struggled. The tests can be hard.

Gives individual focus very well but can be a bit hard to understand and rushes through things that make the course material easier to understand. Expect to put in out-of-class work before every single class. Nice in nature and very flexible. Likes to wait to upload things like grades or announcements (got the syllabus 20 minutes before 1st class).

I can tell she's a very nice person who cares about teaching Spanish, but I don't know if she's a good teacher. Talking in rapid fire Spanish constantly with vocabulary the class won't know unless they're a native speaker isn't crazy helpful. HW is mostly busywork. Very strict on participation and attendance.

Do NOT take her class if you're a beginner Spanish speaker. She gets mad when you don't understand her or get a question wrong in class. She speaks way too fast and if you ask her to slow down, she tells you to get used to it. I enjoyed Spanish class until I had her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher! A lot of the homework was busy work but you need to get them done on time to get a good grade. She spoke in Spanish all the time but cared for her students by asking us to evaluate her anonymously every few weeks so she could change the way she taught. Gets off topic sometimes but a fun class if you do some work for it!

Alejandra is not a good Professor. In a class of 20 people, not a single one of us received perfects on participation despite consistent participation on whole class and small group levels. When confronted she claimed it was because we dont raise our hands for EVERY question. Very frustrating and hard to work with. Take the class with someone else

I loved Alejandra's class. She was very supportive of all of her students and it was clear she wanted us to succeed. She made it very clear from the beginning of the semester. She even started to give us nicknames. She is a tough grader, but if you do the assignments and participate in class you'll be fine.

Most of the class/online homework is just busy work. She grades based on completion and participation a lot. She is receptive to her student's suggestions to the class. Dedicates several classes to review for exams/quizzes. 2 midterms. 1 final. 1 one-page paper. 2 talk-abroad conversations. Online homework every week. 2 quizzes. Daily textbook HW.

Grades participation/attendance. Sweet lady, easy to confront. Rearranges desks into 2 semicircles and often makes you get up/interact with everyone and, while weird, it did make learning more comfortable. E-textbook comes with online hw access code. Online hw weekly/easy. Explains concepts well, I'd love to have her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Her class was easy enough but I also took Spanish in high school and it was review to me- I have a feeling if I didn't have a background, I'd be screwed. She will often break into a tangent in Spanish, which is frustrating. If you don't do your homework, she'll call you out and is harsh. Very particular grader. Not my favorite professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the more frustrating teachers I've had at Ohio State so far, as she has absolutely no organization in her class at all. She goes off on long tangents during class in Spanish, which are difficult to understand for non-native speakers. She does mean well and wants her students to learn, but overall a lecturer that I would not choose again.

Her English is pretty good, no need to be scared of people who dont speak English as a first language guys. The class is pretty straight forward, do the assignments she assigns daily (she doesnt read them but does make sure theyre done). She doesnt really have a clearly outlined syllabus which can be annoying. Tests are easy if you keep up.

Alejandra is a very kind person and has very good intentions during class  however, when you don't do your homework, she gets mad (which is understandable). While she does speak in Spanish for most of class, which is difficult for new learners, it definitely improved my listening skills. If you actually want to learn Spanish, take it with her!

Worst professor/instructor I have ever had in my life. She is extremely unorganized and forgetful as she often looses track of what we are working on in class. She does not understand english well at all and does not understand computers or carmen. Spent almost every class going well over time and yelling at students. Avoid at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I dont think I have dreaded a class more. She never spoke English which made it difficult for someone who never took a foreign language. It was very intimidating. No extra credit and she was the toughest grader. I dont think she cares if you pass or fail. She is funny sometimes but you better have your homework done or she will be so rude to you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: An excellent professor that really cares about her students. If you put effort into the class and participate, you'll do well.
Alex was my favorite professor of the semester! She got to know us on a personal level and I looked forward to going to Spanish every day. I wish I could have her again!

Alex is nice, but she frustrated me. She won't use Carmen, so you can't really see Your grades. She made us buy an online package, but the exercises didn't end up being helpful or count towards my grade. She also made her 5 question quizes worth the same amount as her exams, so getting 4 out of 5 right has the same weight as an 80 on an exam

This was her first semester teaching level 1 Spanish. It was a little rough but she makes what is going to be on the exams crystal clear. She is a very funny and fun person to be around. Very passionate about Spanish and requires her students to show her enthusiasm as well.

She is an awesome professor, and very passionate. She grades super easily and tries to help you on exams if you watch her as she does speaking parts. Yes, there is "busy work" homework every night, but its honestly so easy it shouldn't take more than 10 minutes, if that. The exams are super easy, exactly what you do in class. Easy A.

She is OK. It feels like she doesn't like her students. Somewhere, deep down in her Spanish soul there lies a nice woman, but she sure as hell doesn't come out in class.  Homework for the class is convoluted and confusing at times. Midterms are very straightforward though. Attendance is kinda mandatory but you won't want to skip class anyway
She assigns stuff ALL THE TIME, EVERYDAY.  The attendance is mandatory and you will get points deducted.  However, she is really fair if you miss class and really trys to help you pass her class

Alejandra is funny and makes an effort to get to know you if you show interest in the class. The topics are all presented logically in ppts that are easy to understand. Exams are very easy if you spend an hour or two looking over the review ppt. If you are okay at spanish, I highly recommend her.

Alex is a very kind and helpful professor. She goes over all the material while making sure that everyone understands. She prepares very well for the exams. There is almost nightly homework, but most of it is easy points.

This course is demanding per the department. Alejandra is firm but fair. She does her best to be fair with HW assignments and grading examsassignments. She does a GREAT job at preparing students for the exams. She really does want her students to learn. Reading, HW, & participation are a must.

I loved this class! Alejandra did an excellent job of preparing us for exams. While there was a fair amount of work & quite a few quizzes, it all did a great job of preparing us for exams. My Spanish improved greatly over the semester. She compiled study guides for every exam & helpful in-class projects for us to practice. Highly recommended!

Wonderful, caring teacher. My mother became very ill and she was the only one of my teachers to make sure I was ok, and to adjust deadlines. She talks fast, but uses lots of body language. Review the slides! Whatever she tells you to focus on for the tests, will be on the test in the exact manner she told you it would be. Very straightforward.

Angulo's class was the one class I dreaded going to every morning. I felt she didn't take into consideration that her class is part of my GPA and is willing to dock points wherever. She speaks very fast and treated us like children. She never clearly stated the homework then would be made if someone did not understand.

No clue why on earth anyone has given her this much credit. Spanish was fun and comprehensive until Angulo's class. Everyone in my class was confused on assignments and very intimidated by her. Students were afraid to speak up and ask for help. She is speeds through lecture and is easily irritated. Highly recommend avoiding her

Alex is really sweet and funny once she gets comfortable with your class. She tries to make sure she's clear before moving on. She does have a tendency to speak quickly, but if you let her know, she slows down. She's kind of quirky in a foreign way but its precious and makes it easy to get through the class.
Ms. Angulo is enthusiastic about the subject matter and has a great sense of humor. Although, she is very disorganized  and rushes through the course work, barely giving you time to take notes.
Love this woman to death. She's a phenomenal teacher. She even asked me to babysit her children. Haven't had a better prof for Spanish and I'm in 4557.20 currently.

Tons of homework. Alejandra is helpful, but can be rude. Book is used quite often and so is the online site to do homework. Her reviews are amazing, but are tedious. Seemingly fair grader at times. Mandatory attendance! after 5 absences she takes off 1% of final grade for each day. Overall, very irritating but a decent teacher.
Alex is so hard to understand. I struggled in this class simply because she never spoke english.  If you cannot follow along with constant Spanish, avoid her class at all costs.
I don't know what these other people are talking about. Alejandra was difficult to understand, scatter-brained, and treated us like children. Would not recommend her as an instructor.
She has so much energy! Such a sweetheart. The tests were extremely easy, but remember to study for the writing composition portions (don't worry- she grades very kindly).
She tried to make the class interesting and was very helpful if you were confused on anything.  She was really funny too!  I would recommend her to anyone looking to take a language class at night.

She was cool. Totally willing to help students, if you are nice to her she will be nice to you. Those that complained about her were just trying to get done with the class and thus did not respect her. For a 2 hr night class she makes it bearable and and easy A if you pay attention to her..
Great teacher who loves her students succeeding in class and also always has something funny to say. Great teacher! Get her!
She is a great Spanish teacher and actually cares about helping us learn.
Sometimes she was difficult to understand, but she made sure to repeat things.  She was always willing to help during her office hours and tended to be really funny during class.

For being my first economics class I really enjoyed his teaching style. He would do real life examples and his exams were straightforward and you always knew what to expect. Online homework is tedious but he did mention it was his first semester trying it out.
He makes everything really accessible. Super easy to work with outside of class and wants to see everyone succeed. Lectures are also interesting.

Great professor! I was uneasy about taking an economics class since I usually struggle with the subject, but he made the material easy to understand. He is very supportive and willing to work with students, including extending deadlines when issues come up.

This professor makes very strict guidelines that are unreasonable and unnecessary. He expects the students to write like Descartes himself. Impossible to get an A in. Also he always smells like coins which is a bit strange if you ask me. He will occasionally ask the students for money, and if you leave anything on the ground he will take it.

A very questionable professor to say the least. I am not a fan of his teaching style, as he drones on for hours about how he wishes he was a worm eating glass. He often makes strange comments to the students, such as "Girls for the win smiley face emoji", and it makes a lot of the students uncomfortable. Don't take if you're looking for an easy A.
Makes me call him Abetron. I told him I don't like this and it is weird and he will not listen. When I told him I refuse he said he could settle for Abezilla. Please do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think this professor may be juwish. Overall just an extremely unlikeable guy. Rambles on for half hour to hour at a time about the same thing. Also I saw him take some guy in my class's quarters a few weeks before the semester ended. Kind of messed up

Professor Roth is very knowledgeable in his field and delivers interesting lectures. His class is not difficult and assignments are graded leniently. Overall, I found his class to be both enjoyable and rewarding.

Professor Roth is great at teaching the material. However, his grading is not conducive to the learning process & neither are his class discussions. He is obsessed with semantics & gives poor grades regardless of if students followed instructions to the T. Would not rec.

Professor Roth, above all, is effective at honing and challenging your philosophical skills. Though he and I disagreed on most points, and he was critical on papers, I became less naïve because of him. He will show you what doing philosophy looks like and will moderate your ego. I am indebted to him for a great amount of my philosophical progress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: At first, I was concerned about this class because of the mixed RMP reviews. But as the class went on, it warms up and becomes a lot more accommodating, and Professor Roth is unexpectedly funny in his lectures. The essays are graded harshly even for a philosophy course, but if you put in the work, you can get a high grade. Roth is great!

Ok, so I took Abe for PHILOS3000 and not a well-structured class what so ever. It was almost like he was learning the material at the same time we were - like genuinely. There were never any counter argument readings to the ones he chose, which definitely does not help facilitate discussion. However, he is a sweet man, very laid back. Boring tho.

Well, he is very knowledgeable in his field. However, I feel that he had some trouble delivering the ideas to the students. He talked about one concept for the whole lecture and I was still very confused about that concept. I like him as a person, but I probably will not take his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found his lectures quite boring and repetitive and it really turned me away from philosophy. He was also very rude when asked about his vague grading system.

Passionate about the material and very willing to talk about it with you. Receptive to student desires for course direction. Grading rather opaque and a bit harsh but fair.  Considerably helped the development of my philosophical skills.

Lectures were really repetitive but at least he clearly went over the material that he expected you to know to the point where reading the text isn't really necessary. The grade was only composed of two short response exams and two papers but he was somewhat a lenient grader.

If you take good notes and come to class everyday and use what you learned and the readings to write the papers you will get an A. Study his notes too for the test. Easy class if you come to class everyday.
I would walk 4 miles in sub-zero temps to attend Dr. Roth's dissertation seminar.

Dr. Roth is an excellent professor. It is obvious that he is passionate about the material and loves what he does. He's always friendly and happy to discuss any of the class materials. If you enjoy class participation Roth would be a good fit for you.

I had Abe for Philosophy of Action and the class was excellent.  Very enthusiastic professor, loves the material as well as teaching it. Didn't do as well as I would have liked, but that was my fault, not his.  Some of the comments on here are pretty harsh, I don't understand it.

His lectures are very disorganized which is partly due to the subject matter, but mostly due to Prof. Roth's teaching style.  Wait until AFTER class discussion to do the reading for the week since it will make much more sense.  Very difficult to predict how he will grade papers.

A. Roth is a smart guy, but he's not a very good lecturer.  Many times he spoke about the same concept for an hour or more. The students often become zombies during lecture, very boring, uninteresting topics are covered. He did screen movies and provide pizza, outside of class, however. Two papers and an exam (10 short answer). Not recommended.

I came into this class expected a lot of interesting debate. Not the case. Instead you talk about ancient philosophers. Very dull class, lectures are long and at times very pointless. Course is comprised of two short essays and a ten questions final exam. He will almost never agree with what your write.
Not the best professor.  He isn't very clear in class, but if you go to his office hours he's extremely helpful.  The lectures are hard to stay awake in, and the class is very disorganized.

Professor Roth at times comes across as cocky and arrogant, often pushing his views as the absolute truth.  However, he allows for open discussion of the primary sources and does a good job in explaining the materials read.  Class would have been a lot harder had he not taken the time to make good notes for the class.  I would recommend taking him.

Kind of follows the text. Randomly takes attendance. Does not make any sense while teaching. I really looked forward to philosophy before I started taking it. Grades the papers erratically. Horrible, horrible class, is bringing my high GPA down no matter how hard I try.

im not the best at math and this is my second time taking calc 1. I thought maybe online would be easier for me, plot twist: its not even online, only the material is, which did not help at all. he talks to you in a way that makes you feel like you shouldn't be asking that question and almost too nice, like he's clearly faking it.

PLEASE READ! DON'T TAKE FLIPPED AND FLEXIBLE! Lectures are 400 years old and your TA will most likely teach like an absent father. You will never see Mr. Borland and he will ghost your emails. (It takes 3 for his attention) Also the exams are literally impossible, like 6 hour study sessions for 45% impossible. It took everything I had to get a 71%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He teaches MATH 1151 in a very different way than the other sections. Extremely participatory in class, and it really helps. Math is taught so weirdly at OSU, so there is not much explanation in the lectures; you're expected to already know from online lessons. Grading was inconsistent, but there are multiple chances to get it right.

Dr Borland is a better person than a professor. He is a great guy to talk to and he will help you as much as possible. His lectures can be boring, as he mostly gives students example problems to solve and lets them work alone, but will help students when needed. Overall, a great person and a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor and does his best to help, whether it be in class or during office hours, but honestly I found his lectures to be a little boring and not that helpful. You're gonna have to teach yourself most of the material but it's not that bad. If you're willing to put in some effort outside of class you'll do fine.

Dr. Borland is a great professor, quick to respond to emails. I am taking the class at my high school and he has been very communicative when problems occurred. Otherwise, the class is very difficult, you learn the topics for sure but the tests have very precise grading criteria. If one question is missed---10 points are gone---you get a B.

Although Dr. Borland is a very nice guy and not a bad professor, I would never take his class again. The grading system used is unnecessarily harder and more complicated than it needs to be. If you have AP credit for this course I highly suggest you take it as it is easy to miss 6/33 standards and fail the class even with 100% on everything else.

Professor Borland is an amazing professor, but the grading system he uses is absolutely awful. If you are not used to a standards and applications grading system, do not take this class. That being said, he is very much so available and really does his hardest to help. I just think I personally do better in a smaller, more traditional class setting

please do NOT take flipped and flexible math 1151. borland is probably a great professor but if he is listed for your online section like he was for mine, RUN. online "lecture" is a string of youtube videos... recitation is a joke because no one is learning anything. save yourself the stress and take this at community college or take 1156.

I loved Dr. Borland. He genuinely cares about his students. My class was well over 100 people and he learned everyone's name. He will work with you to get a good grade in his class. If you do the work and at least show your trying then his classes will be a breeze.
Great teacher who loves helping his students!

Most of the material in this class is expected to be learned outside of the classroom, with very vague online lessons that he assigns to you. The types of problems on the online lessons are much less complicated than the ones on quizzes and exams. For each lesson, you go over a worksheet in class with other students instead of being taught by him.
Dr. Borland is amazing! He is extremely caring and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He is great at explaining concepts and is also very kind.

I took math 1151 with Dr.Borland over the summer and loved it! Dr.Borland does a great job at explaining the content and he provides a lot of practice problems to do! Even though lecture is not mandatory I recommend it along with attending every recitation, since those problems are like the ones on the exam.

Lecture is alright but does not help, have to go in for TOP HAT! There are no curves even if they tell you so and you get no points if you skip even 1 step on midterms and final. BEWARE this calc class will most likely have you sit back another semester. Grading is the worst and you have to get all your information from watching online videos.
Great professor who knows his stuff and made 9 am lectures not too boring. The course is set up to make people fail, but he prepared students very well for the exams. Seemed like a genuine guy.

if you guys have a choice to select dr. borland! Not only did he care and answer our questions during lectures, he always engaged with his students. he would explain concepts in an understanding way! the calc department is notorious for being hard, but not the prof's fault. just prepare to put a lot of extra work in outside of class!

Math 1151 is the worst class I have ever taken. It is a lazy excuse for teaching students calculus. Dr. Borland did nothing for me all semester. They just post other people's videos and make you learn Calc on your own. Dr. Borland also takes 3 weeks to answer a simple yes or no email. Just watch the Organic Chemistry Tutor on Youtube...

Dr. Borland is a professor who is very engaged in the subject he teaches. The only bad part about the class isn't his fault, just the midterms are notoriously difficult and nothing like we go over in class or recitation.
Very passionate about teaching and always was available to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor and math teacher iv'e ever had (Freshman standing though). Extremely open for questions and explains concepts clearly.

Dr. Borland was an incredible professor. He explained concepts clearly, was interactive with the class, and did a great job keeping people engaged. Always willing to answer questions. He clearly cares for his students. While attendance was not mandatory, I enjoyed going to his class in the morning. And if I missed a lecture, he records all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The professor works a lot for his students and clarifies everything with absolute clarity.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Borland is by far the best lecturer I have had. He gets straight to the point, and gets class over with as fast as possible, but answers any questions you have. Best thing is, he posts all of his lectures online, so if you happen to miss a class, you don't have to worry about falling behind.

Professor Borland made an infamously tough class significantly better. The grading is tough and sometimes even unfair, but that's done by TA's so you can't really blame him for it. He provides great lecture notes online and teaches with passion. Can't recommend him enough!

I love this man so much. This class is pretty tough, but you can tell that Alexander is passionate about math and is always willing to help you after class/during office hours. I would recommend taking thorough notes and reviewing them after class. Something that also helped me was making review sheets since the exams were online/open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Borland was alright. His lectures were boring and he struggled to respond to emails but that's really it. The class was 'synchronous' but you could skip lectures and watch them on your own time.

Dr. Borland genuinely cares that students not just pass the class but get something out of it as well as he's very passionate about math. The class itself is pretty challenging and a lot of work but he consistently encouraged students to reach out for help and ask questions. Go to lecture and recitation, I found both endlessly helpful.
Excellent professor for a historically difficult class at OSU.

Honestly one of the best professors especially since this class is typically a harder one. If you go to every lecture and try to show up to recitation you will do fine in the class. Try to spend at least 1 hour a day on this class to actually understand the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is extremely challenging, but Dr. Borland makes it a lot better than it could be. There is about 3-4 HW assignments and readings due every week, plus a total of 5 midterms and 6 written HW assignments. Dr. Borland is very clear about the expectations for the class, and his lectures are helpful and fairly well-organized.

Alexander Borland taught as well as he could for this course. You can cheat on the online Ximera homework but if you do so you will surely be lost on written homeworkds and midterms which are worth a very large portion of your grade. Going to lectures and recitation (if ur TA is good) is the most beneficial thing you can do for your grade.
Best math lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class truly sucks. Borland writes good notes that you follow along with, but is just so incredibly boring and monotone. Fell asleep in his class way too often. After a while, I stopped going and just looked at his notes and retained more of the information that way. Very homework and test heavy, good luck!
Hard class

Calc 1 (MATH1151) is one of the hardest classes you can take at OSU. But Dr. Borland makes it SO much better. He is so organized and really nice and always responds to emails quickly and answers questions thoroughly. Trust me, you definitely want Dr. Borland for Calc instead of any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mr. Borland is a very good teacher but there is a lot of curriculum so he moves extremely fast and doesn't fully explain everything. I ended up with a bad grad in calc but I didn't put in a lot of effort, his notes are very clear and he knows what he is talking about

He seems like a nice guy but this class is extremely difficult if you work a lot or have a ton of other classes. You need to leave a lot of time to study and do homework as there is a midterm every two weeks, written homework every two weeks, about 2-4 assignments due every other day, and the final is cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Difficult class. Such a great teacher though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very good

Dr. Borland was super cheerful every morning for online lectures and tried to answer every single question. If something is confusing, he tries his best to clear it up for students while being respectful and not demeaning. Very heavy homework class but it is very helpful in preparation for midterms. Office hours very welcoming but email takes long.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Borland is a great prof for one of the harder classes you might be taking during the semester. His lecture format was extremely helpful and using notability you can follow along easily. He stops lecture to answer all questions and you can even email him for help. The first test is impossible but don't get discouraged, it gets easier from there.

Just like in any Calculus class, you need to practice to be successful. Professor Borland was always willing to help if you asked for it and found ways to explain the topics so they were somewhat interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Borland is a great lecturer. He managed to make calc interesting and almost fun for person whos never liked math. He makes online lecture interactive and never makes you feel dumb for asking questions. Definitely show up to his lectures, theyre more helpful than the Ximera textbook by far.
Probably the best math teacher I have ever had. He genuinely cares for his students.
Makes the content approachable, one of my better teachers.

Honestly, the math department at Ohio State is really difficult but Dr. Borland makes it easier. He goes over everything in depth during lecture. There was a LOT of homework, but overall good professor. Make sure you do the practice exams because theyre pretty similar to the real exams
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He makes Calculus fun. And his cat is soooo cute!

Love this man. Calc is super hard and time consuming, but he makes it fun. Hes engaging during lectures and has office hours often. He cares about his students and wants you to succeed. First exam is literally impossible, dont freak out if you fail it. His cat is also the cutest thing ever and he is often sitting in the back of Borlands zoom video
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Terrible online teacher, dont listen to the other reviews. He doesnt slow down when you ask, doesnt explain things when you ask, and is extremely hard to reach. Also has really annoying mannerisms that make you not want to listen to him. Switch if you can.

Dr. Borland was absolutely awesome for my calc 1 class. His online lectures were entertaining and for the first time ever I enjoyed my math class! The course itself is pretty busy, so I would recommend making attending lectures a priority and study often. If you have the choice, definitely choose Dr. Borland!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The absolute best math teacher I have ever had. I took Calc 1 in high school and had to retake it here at OSU, he made everything so easy to understand. He somehow managed to make online lectures fun and had time fly while in them. I hope I can have him again as either a prof or TA in later math classes.

Borland is my absolute favorite professor of all time. His (online) lectures are incredibly fun, and I actually look forward to going to them. The class is a lot of work, but he makes things as easy as possible to understand. He also cares a ton about his students, and has been open to giving extensions on things if you're having a tough day/week.

Borland is a fun professor who makes calc 1 interesting by being passionate about it. He is very engaging in the online lecture and is always in a good mood in office hours. If you show up to the lecture early he is usually already there vibing and happy to chat. That said, 1151 is def a class you cant slack on and dont skip lectures.

Borland is great when it comes to online lectures. Per the nature of the course, you do need to do the homework with effort to succeed, but Borland sets you up for it. He has office hours often and is eager to help students.

I had him online because of the pandemic and even though it was online, I think he is one of the best calc 1 professors at osu. The exams are difficult, but they are same for the every instructor. Highly recommend of others
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: By far the best math teacher I've ever had. Explains the material well, and doesn't skip over important stuff. Lets you know when something will be on the final and goes over it in detail. He has a way of explaining things so that anyone can understand.

He is so nice and helpful. He made me feel really comfortable asking questions and never acted like I was dumb. He is by far the best teacher I have ever had. Plus he was always in a good mood and made calculus significantly less terrible and I would not have passed this class without him.

Professor Yilmaz is a relaxed instructor. In my experience, the course focused more on general concepts than civil engineering applications, which made parts of it less engaging for me. Lectures feel long, but attending helps with the labs. Not a super difficult class, just very long.

I took CIVILEN 2060 with Prof. Yilmaz. It was completely asynchronous through Carmen. He seemed to be really absent from the entire course. I'm not sure if he's more focused on his research or what but he basically gave us all free points on almost every assignment. I didn't learn really anything but still received an A-.

He does a great job of explaining material and will warn you if he sees something wrong on your quiz (not for exams). My only complaint is that his exam questions were so poorly worded to the point that he would have to make an adjustment mid-exam or scratch the question, so I could not take them at the SLDS office like I was supposed to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I like professor Yilmaz. He is an easy grader. I had him both 2050 and 2060. 2050 is very easy if you take it with him. 2060 you need to put some effort to get an A. But 2060 final is very hard, but somehow I get an a. A good cheat sheet is really important in this class. Basically, the final is very similar to the example he shows in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I mean he is really easy for 2050, but not for 2060. Tests for 2060 were challenging.

Yilmaz is a great lecturer and cares a lot about the class. He can go at a pretty fast pace sometimes so it is easy to get lost if you aren't paying close attention. All of the homework, quizzes, and exams were online and he gives multiple attempts on exams. Easy A if you pay attention, take notes, and do the work

If you go to class, this class will not be difficult. All of his assignments are out of a possible 110-120 points, but scored out of 100, so the averages are very high. He is a little disorganized when it comes to assigning homework and setting quiz/exam times, but overall he's pretty good. Example problems in class are the same as homework/tests.

Really enjoyed this class with Dr. Yilmaz. He was a really good professor that made the material bearable, and as long as you make an effort you should be fine. Extremely helpful in class and in office hours. Although attendance isn't mandatory and slides are posted, it makes the class much easier when doing homeworks if you attend class.

Wonderful lecturer, material was really dry and was very dense but Dr. Yilmaz made it bearable and very clear cut. Gives lots of extra credit and you get to make your own cheat sheets for exams. I feel this professor cares and that's hard to come by these days. If you attend class and  take notes, no reason you shouldn't pass with at least a B.

Dr. YIlmaz is a really good guy. Really wants all of his students to understand and be interested in the topics he presents. Attendance isn't mandatory, but sometimes you will get rewarded with a bonus quiz or two. Homework and quizzes almost every week, but it prepares you for the exam.

Tests were challenging and lectures were sometimes confusing and unrelated to the posted slides, but Yilmaz is a genuinely nice guy who has student success in mind. He also offers a boatload of extra credit, enough to where I could've skipped the final and still had an A-.

Tough class.  He tried every way he could to give students the benefit of the doubt.  Midterm is tough, he grades very easy, and final project you'll get an A just by turning it in. DO ALL the homeworks, even if you know you don't know how to do one...HW is 55% of the grade.  Don't buy the book, lecture notes are online.

This class has a lot of content, so expect each lesson to be content-packed. Dr. Yilmaz can be slightly boring but its only because of the mostly dry content. Midterm was tough but he's quite lenient with it. He's VERY helpful outside of class. Go to office hours if you don't understand anything. He's extremely patient! Also, GO TO CLASS!
N/A

2001 was a mandatory class for civil, but Andre Carrel was good enough for the course. The course is organized with lots of group work and homework, but was pretty manageable overall. Professor Carrel wasn't the main lecturer of my section, but he was interesting when he had the spotlight.
Enjoyed taking class.clear material.make sure you work on worksheets before exams

The assignments take forever. The first exam was fine but the second was extremely difficult. Many hours every week spent on the assignments -- more than a 3 credit hour course should have. Very tedious. However, the Professor himself is very helpful if you have questions.

Dr. Carrel is an excellent professor.  Knows the material very well and knows how to help students understand the material.  The homeworks are long, but they are graded fairly.  Exams were fair, with practice exams being handed out for each one with very similar questions
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Carrel did a good job. He is always willing to answer questions and wants students to succeed. The assignments do take a long time, but if you follow instructions you can get a good grade. The lectures could get boring, but I believe it's due to the overall content, not Dr. Carrel teaching. The exams were fair, especially if you attended class.

Professor Carrel really cares about what he is teaching. His online lectures are well put together and the exams have been open note which is stress relieving. It is not an easy class and the homework grading is nit picky, but other than that it has been a very enjoyable class.

Prof Carrel was really great. Came into the semester addressing the poor past RMP reviews, and made a noticeable effort to teach the class well. The notes are fill in the blank, with guided examples that align w exams. Assignments can be time consuming but you have over a week to complete. Did very well with the transition to online instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are dry, but I guess you cant help that. What you can help is how useless the homework is, how tough the grading on the homework is, or the fact he doesnt attend his own office hours and instead has a GTA facilitate. Dont expect to have useful problems to practice before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The tests are HARD. The old exams passed back during class are so much easier than the ones given. Homework's are terrible! It will take over 7 hours for each one and they are pointless.
He will give you big surprises on the exam. Avoids if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: 2001 is mandatory, but Professor Andy May is fun and inviting in the classroom. I really enjoyed taking 2001 with him, and didn't find any reason to remove a star from his overall rating. Really nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good course, solid lectures. 2 group projects instead of the exam which involve making 15 minute videos to learn more about concepts. Funny professor, makes a lot of jokes to hold your attention

He was the best professor I've had at Ohio State. Fluids is a hard class, but Andy made it fun. He is extremely understanding with any absences, and loves answering any questions you might have. He enjoys interacting with his students, always heard you out, and speaks to everyone as if they're equals.

Dr. May is one of the best professors within the Civil community. He genuinely cares for his students and is willing to help them wherever they're at in the material. Fluid Mechanics is not an easy subject, but he makes it easy to succeed and to learn the material. Can't recommend taking his course enough.

This guy literally shows up to the lectures and just rants for an hour and leaves. He gives random exercises to do from the textbook, and never goes over them, never explains them. Additionally, he assigns homework material that is on midterms... after the midterm. Avoid this guy at all costs.

Not good. I have an A in the class right now only because I've taught myself everything. He calls what he's teaching "nonsense" and says "blah blah blah", "thing", "something", "who cares" instead of explaining. His syllabus is looks like it was made in 10 mins, his lectures are incomprehensible, 8 people show up max.

I tried to cut him some slack as he's new to teaching but I just couldn't because of how badly my grades were suffering. I think he should stick to research, Im sure hes amazing at math but just cant explain it. If you have him, skip lecture, teach yourself, go to tutoring, and go to your recitation, try to go to another professor lecture
good luck
Lectures were often confusing and recitations were only slightly better.

Hard to understand this professor. Usually seems lost in lectures and does not help in engaging the class. The best advice is to switch out or go to some other lecture because it is hard to learn with him. Bad handwriting and teaching skills. Recitations are the only saving grace if you decide to stay in like I did.

I SAW SOMEONE GIVE THIS PROFESSOR A FIVE-STAR RATING, AND I CANNOT UNDERSTAND WHY. THIS IS THE WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. HIS HANDWRITING IS ATROCIOUS, HE CONFUSES HIMSELF WITH HIS OWN MATH, AND HE CANNOT TEACH. IF I COULD GIVE A NEGATIVE RATING, I WOULD. DROP THIS CLASS.

If there was an option to give a negative rating, I genuinely would. He's genuinely the worst professor I have ever met; he doesn't know how to teach, his handwriting is illegible, and the whole class is always lost. I started attending a different lecture and I learned so much more even in the first day. My best advice is to request to switch out.

Avoid this professor at all costs. His rating is low for a reason. Lectures are borderline impossible to follow, and halfway through the semester his class size shrunk to less than 30 people (started at 150). Genuinely believe going to lecture makes you understand the material less. Take any other professor if you can. Good luck

If I hadn't already taken this class in high school, I would be miles behind on what was going on. Most people don't attend the lectures because it is hard to understand what he is saying, and he doesn't really teach the material; he just speeds through it. Recitations are a lifesaver, though. Good luck.

He's clearly a smart guy but he doesn't know how to teach hard concepts in an easy to understand way. Lectures are just him proving theorems. He tries to get the class to chime in but then everyone stares at him confused because nobody knows what's going on. Very generous curve in the class and he will give points back on homework if you ask him.

He is by FAR the worst professor I've ever had. His handwriting is illegible, gets lost on almost all of his own examples during class, unhelpful in office hours, and is terrible at explaining all the concepts. His examples in class were always way harder/more confusing than was expected of us on the homework and on test. Find a different section.
I've never had a professor like him before
Literally take anyone else other than this guy

Talks much too quietly, handwriting is barely legible at times, and is not the best at staying on topic with the things that we are tested and given homework on. I've heard that there are much much much better professors for this course, please seek them out if given the chance.

I had a very difficult time with this professor. His handwriting is almost illegible, and he often stands in front of the board, blocking the work. He often confuses himself with his own work and is constantly erasing and rewriting things that he later realizes are wrong. He isn't great at answering questions; I'd avoid this professor if possible.

I took Amit's Dynamical Systems and Chaos theory class in Autumn 25. Easily one of the most fascinating courses I've taken. The whole semester builds toward the mathematics behind chaos in the final lecture. Amit explains deep ideas with clarity, and the MATLAB projects + team quizzes really made the class an excellent applied math experience.

Amazingggg teacher, he is so understanding and wants everyone to succeed. I still reach out to him and go to his office hours even though I'm not in his class. He is always willing to sit down and help you no matter the math class you're taking. He has a diverse range of people he helps out, I meet someone new every time I go to his office hours.

I suck at calc but he is a sweetie pie and deserves the world. Course was overall okay I just don't like calc and didn't try to crazy on things. Lots of group homework and recitation quizzes weekly but overall not bad. bless that man
The GOAT. No more words. If all math professors can be like him, the math department will be 200 times better.
One of the best professors I've ever had at OSU. Genuinely cares about his students succeeding, and I wish I could take more math courses with him!

Genuinely the best professor at OSU. I had him for 1148, 1140, and 1141. This is a tough class if you are not the best at calculus but he is extremely helpful and is an amazing resource. There is a lot of homework, quizzes, and extra credit opportunities if you do not do well on exams. Overall, he is a super nice person and wants you to succeed!

Amit is hands down the best professor I've had at OSU. I took his MATH2568 class asynchronous, and I was a little sketched out because I usually don't learn anything in online classes but his lectures are very easy to follow and he does a great job at them. He really does care about his students and wants them to succeed.

Amit is a great professor and you can tell her genuinely cares about students. He is always willing to help and accommodate people's circumstances and goes out of his way to make sure everyone can get the help they need. If every professor was like Amit the world would be perfect

Amit is the kindest, most caring professor at OSU. He is always willing to help at office hours and since this class was online, he was very quick to respond to any questions using Microsoft teams. Nothing but great things to say about Amit.

Super good class! This professor keeps the workload manageable and understands that students have other things to do. But also makes so many resources and opportunities available if you want to learn the material well and not just focus on the grade. Really passionate about the subject and it comes through in his lectures.

I was lucky to have Amit for multivariable calc in Summer ‘24. He works very hard into making the class run smoothly, mixing ideas, theory, and real-life examples in his awesome lectures. Super chill and humble! He created a real community where everyone felt welcome and actually learned a lot.

Amit Vutha is one of the best math professors I have ever had. He truly cared for his students and wanted to see them succeed. He held numerous office hours and held online exam review sessions. He was very responsive to his emails and extremely understanding if you needed to reschedule an exam.
nice professor

lectures are useless. you have to learn all of the content outside of the classroom and then the lectures are him talking about 3 things from the learning. the learning outside of class will take you forever and be due at the most inconvenient time. save yourself the trouble and take a different class.

I don't think Buser is a bad Professor for 2002, if u listen to his lecture carefully u will find that it is useful in some aspects. His exams are not very difficult and he may add extra credits to everyone if the exam is difficult.U can also ask him questions.

Jeffrey is an amazing guy, he genuinely cares about teaching and his students. With that being said, he is not a good professor when it comes to lecture. He almost always got sidetracked and would not explain the things he would put on exams in lecture, just tophat questions.

He is a very nice man, but just not a good professor. You can tell he knows what he's talking about, but horrible at getting the point across. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: It's very obvious professor Buser loves his job teaching Economics. With that being said, he makes it a point the first day of the semester to say that he is an "old school" professor, meaning you definitly have to put in work. Go to class and do the homework and you should be ok. He's always willing to help if you have questions on anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy that wants to help his students. He reads off his slides during lectures and uploads them online. Attend class for the tophat grade. Also offers easy 5% extra credit. Just do the bare minimum (attend lectures, do all homework, study for 30 minutes) and you will get an A.

Before class you are required to watch videos on the material that will be covered, in class you discuss the material, in recitation you review and take a short group quiz, and then the usual homework. This class isn't too bad if you pay attention. He does ask some trick questions of his tests so be ready and study before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I thought he was a good professor overall. If you went to class, it was easy to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Buser is such a nice guy. I went to his office hours like twice and he always said hi to me after in his lecture. A lot of people say his exams are hard and do bad on them, but if you can do the top hat questions from class youll do fine. The only downside is you can never skip because missing just one class will wreck your participation grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: So many top hat questions during class time, so of the questions are way too hard
Buser is a funny guy who really enjoys teaching Econ! Only problem is the exams are really really hard to get an A on so your grade may take a hit after midterms/final.

. His lectures are verbatim copies of what is in the textbook, and his use of top hat is the only thing that makes going to lecture worthwhile. He often runs out of time to finish his lecture and just moves on to the next lesson the next day. The worst is that he writes the midterm questions himself and his own TAs had great difficulty explaining
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Buser is a pretty good professor. Definitely not the easiest, and you do have to work for an A. Make sure to show up to every class, participate in the TopHat questions because they will be taken for a grade, and pay very close attention in lecture. I would suggest sitting up front so you don't miss anything he says.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Buser is highly committed to teaching Economics and definitely passionate about it. The class itself had weekly assignments and a few midterms. Buser always helped me when I asked questions after class and during office hours. Overall, not a bad choice for Professor for Econ 2001.

Not a huge fan of the guy. Homework is tedious and excessive, with multiple assignments due per week. Grade relies heavily on tests, and he doesnt explain or elaborate topics in Lecture. He is basically a robot, reading directly from the slides, very few examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There's no point in taking Buser for Intermediate micro/macro. He, literally, reads the slides which are just copied & pasted from the textbook verbatim. There's really no point in him having a job, he is literally just a voiceover for the textbook. HW / Quizzes do not correlate with class material, very unorganized, and absolutely no help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: NEVER TAKE BUSER PLS!!!!THE CLASS IS BORING AND THE EXAMS WERE WAY TOOOOO HARD. HE DID NOT COVER ANYTHING BUT STILL EXPECT STUDENTS TO UNDERSTAND IT. AWFUL PROFESSOR!
Chill on Buser hes smart and will teach you alot.

He just doesnt cover enough material in his lectures, and what he does cover is not super helpful for exams. He posts Everything on Carmen so you dont have to take a lot of notes, but you pretty much have to go to lectures. I got Cs on both exams and I will still end the class with a B+, but if you really want an A dont take him.

Weve had 2 exams this semester so far and both averages were around 65-67%. He never finishes his lectures and therefore its up to the student to have to read the textbook every time after class is over to make sure he or she is getting all of the material. Do not take this guy if you have the option to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: WORST PROFESSOR EVER. HE STARTS THE CLASS BY SAYING HE DOESNT WANT SNY A's IN HIS CLASS

Very poorly run class, never on the same page with the TA's. The exams are very difficult with a 65 average on both, and have several distracting errors. He is good at demanding attention and not a bad talker, but when going through practice problems it's not unusual for him to get them wrong. Top 5 worst class in my 13 years of education.

He can't finish the content in every class, but the exam will still include this content. So you better read the textbook yourself because the exams carry a lot of weight. Tons of homework and reading with an unreliable ebook. It always gets stuck, reboots, and then resets your progress. Still, homework is a small part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid this guy at all costs. It's not what he teaches that's the problem, it's what he doesn't teach. He doesn't cover nearly enough material in lecture, and what he does cover is not nearly in depth enough to do well on exams. If you get him, you really have to work hard for a good grade. If you really want an A, do not take this professor.
Never take him for macroeconomic. The class average for 550 students was a 65%

The homework questions on Sapling are not very helpful at all. Exams were tough. Class average on 1st exam was a 67%. Need to take extremely good notes in class to be able to really understand anything, even then it is difficult because he doesn't go in depth enough to give you a full understanding of a topic, but rather hope you memorize.

There are a lot of homework to do for this class, because he cannot teach us most of the materials that is necessary for us to learn. His lecture is funny, but the exam is tough. I got about 92.8% in the end, but he curved my grade to A. He cares students a lot, and he is overall a helpful professor and easy to be with.

He does not ever finish the lectures slides and doesn't go through enough review material for his exams. His exams are way too hard and much harder than other professors who teach Econ at OSU. He says in his lectures that he expects his students to get Cs on his midterms otherwise he thinks they are too easy.
Other than the way Jeffrey pronounces measured (may-zored), he is a real tank.

This guy is great. I have a problem with falling asleep in lectures- that never happened with this dude. Very loud, little crazy, passionate for econ. Don't forget to do the online homework it was actually very helpful, he basically reviews each lesson after you learn it yourself through the hw - interesting order but seemed to work

Buser in class mostly just read off of the tophat slides. However, you should attend because tophat can boost your grade without much effort. For exams, I would review all of the recitation questions and go over the practice exams.
So on our final we forgot 4 pages in one of the version. He also almost never actually finish his lecture. However, the homeworks are easy point. I hadnt to learn a lot of it outside of lectures.

Buser is a good professor but lectures can be boring. Participation and attendance are taken via Tophat. In my class, we had 3 exams with the lowest dropped, 7 homework with the 2 lowest dropped, and 6 writing assignments with the 2 lowest dropped. He waited to assign the majority of homework and writing assignments until the end of the semester

I had Buser for both Micro and Macro. Lectures are okay and he is pretty funny. Getting a good grade is pretty difficult, though. You really have to pay attention and study EVERYTHING before his tests. Questions are wordy and can easily get confusing. I'd recommend him for Micro over Macro any day. If you prioritize this class, an A is possible.
