reviews.comment: Great professor, you will learn a lot and it is not difficult at all. He is also really understanding and an overall nice guy.
Christian is a great professor. Attendance is mandatory, but if there is a problem he is super understanding. Lectures can be dense but don't worry if you don't understand everything.
Great professor, Easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Interesting material and the slides get posted which is helpful. Not the most engaging lecturer but also not totally boring. Grade is made up of four literature reviews, a midterm, and a final, all short essay style. Not a tough grader so do the readings and you'll be fine.

Really cool guy. Class was not difficult at all. He really makes the course easy for you to be successful as long as you complete everything that needs done (which is not a lot). Used lots of examples and things like debates to keep the content exciting.

Incredibly easy, did less than an hour of work a week and did not ever have to worry. Lectures were also always insightful and genuinely interesting. I got a lot more out of this class than I expected.

Dorian is fantastic. This is the one class I was genuinely excited to go to. Lectures were engaging and very discussion based. 
There was no exams when I took the course. The only assessments were graded TopHat questions, easy points if you attend lecture.
I took this as an easy GE. Dorian just makes it 10x better, would highly recommend.

Best professor I've had. He is clear and makes you think outside the box. There is only one exam, the final. There are quizzes every week but they aren't too bad. A lot of the lecture is class discussion and we have debates, which is nothing to be afraid of. He'll ask you questions that will make you rethink your opinions which I love. 10/10

Comert was a wonderful professor who taught the material well and he genuinely cared about his students (as best as you can in a 200 person lecture). The class is just setup horribly to make it very difficult. Took AU25.
Very funny and good professor. He explains things well during lectures and is accessible outside of class. Hardest class I've ever taken though. Both midterms averaged right around 50% in my section.
Great lecturer. Super hard class. Buckle up

Comert Kural is a nice guy. He likes to make jokes and you can tell he enjoys teaching. However, the physics department not organzied. The whole grading system is a mess, you don't know what grade you will recieve till the end of the semester. The exams are so challenging, they take practice problems but add a twist.

The homework and exams are hard. You're not in high school anymore.

This isn't a class where memorizing lecture slides gets you a good grade. Mastering physics requires developing problem solving skills by working through problems on your own.

Comert understands the material, explains it clearly, and cares about his students. Great professor.

Don't get me wrong he's a nice and caring professor, but I rarely ever went to lecture because rather than going over problems and stuff with units, he would explain how you can derive equations, and how it applies to the real world, which is also important too, but because of the lack of problem review, I didnt enjoy lectures much. nice dude tho

Physics is difficult; however, this guy is funny. I didn't show up to lectures much, but when I did, I always saw him trying his best to explain difficult concepts. He tried to keep things light-hearted, didn't always provide the most resources, but for midterm two and the final, he did enough. This class definitely requires studying for though.

I love Comert. Super funny and his lectures are pretty informative and entertaining. They are a lot of copy and paste info from the textbook but he goes through problems step by step which is helpful. Homeworks are tough but prepare you for the weekly quiz. Fast paced class but he definitely cares about his students and gives life/ study advice.

I wouldn't say that it's Dr. Kural's fault, but this class was horrible. They taught us 3x as much as we actually needed. I recommend teaching yourself everything from khan academy or youtube videos, the lecture slides and textbook were pretty much useless. Also, prepare to do very poorly on the midterms as the average scores were in the 50s.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Comert as a lecturer. I feel like since most people are taking physics for the first time in this class, they taint his reputation. He goes through practice questions step-by-step and is very understandable. People saying he doesn't teach well clearly don't attend/pay attention in class. He genuinely cares for his students!
The class itself is hard but his lectures are very good. READ THE TEXTBOOK, especially before the lecture, trust it helps so much. Funny guy.

Overall, Professor Kural is the best option for Physics 1250. He is super funny and genuinely cares for his students. His lectures are entertaining and decently informative. You will definitely have to practice and learn outside of class. The class itself is not terribly hard, but isn't a class you can blow off every now and then.

Honestly, if you are taking Physics 1250, regardless of the sections, get down on your knees and PRAY. However, Professor Kural is awesome. He tries hard to make the content understandable and explain everything clearly. If you have to take 1250, please try to take it with him. You can tell that he really cares about his students.

The physics department as OSU is absolutely atrocious. The course set up has a dozen different categories, multiple as small as just 3% of your grade. There are half a dozen different homework assignments a week along with quizzes; however, Comert is a fantastic guy. He teaches the content well, cares about students, and is occasionally funny.

Dr Kural clearly cares about his students and does the best he can with the course's setup. He explains most topics very well and keeps things entertaining. That being said, the course itself is set up extremely poorly and is quite challenging, so prepare for lots of studying and hours of homework.

Dr. Kural really cares about the students, however this class was hard as the physics department here at OSU is insanely tough. He always helped if you have any questions or concerns and the lectures were sometimes fun.

Class is super hard and poorly set up (thanks to the department) but Dr. Kural does very well navigating that. His lectures are super informative, and he makes them entertaining. One of the best in the department.
Hard class but be you can tell he cares about the students.

Kural is a funny guy who gives pretty good lectures. He also likes to recommend strategies for students to improve themselves at the end of lectures sometimes, which is nice (one time he recommended "Atomic Habits"). The course is very difficult, though, so prepare to put your nose to the grindstone.

Professor Kural does a good job of creating a friendly environment during lectures. The class content can be very challenging and the homework's will require large amounts of time put in outside of class. This was my most difficult class but Professor Kural made the lectures engaging and interesting. He also seemed to genuinely care.
love his accent, made the class more enjoyable

The class is known to be difficult, and it is. I've enjoyed Dr. Kural's lecturers and he approaches difficult concepts in a way that made sense to me. Legitimately a good lecturer, makes lectures entertaining, and approachable in office hours if you need additional help. I recommend taking him as a lecturer if you can.

Physics 1250 sucks no matter what, but Comert makes it a little bit more bearable. He cares deeply about his students and is funny as can be. Sometimes he can overexplain some things which can make things even more confusing, but I think that was more an issue with my skillset. If you have to choose any professor for 1250, choose him.

Class in general sucks, but Prof. Kural gives great lectures, and is very approachable outside of class. He explains things very well, and is always open to questions. If you are taking this class, beware, it is actually awful. The homework is very hard and grade wise it is very test/quiz heavy. It is so important to go to lectures.

Professor Kural was a good lecturer for the class design. His lectures were always straight from the textbook which was nice and I found them pretty engaging. He even took some time in lectures to give life advice at the end which was a pretty funny but showed that he at least cared about his students. However, the online HW in the class is brutal!

Professor Kural is a funny and likeable person. His lectures involved flipping through pre-made slide shows. I feel like I mostly passed the class because of my background in physics, not exactly because of his lectures. I found the slide shows confusing and jumbled with many unnecessary equations. However, I enjoyed his lectures overall.

I like Professor Kural a lot, he's pretty funny and overall a great lecturer. Lots of demos in class (he even did the famous experiment, putting the pendulum against his head and letting it swing). But be warned, physics classes at OSU are extremely difficult, so be ready to do a lot of homework and attend your TA's office hours.

I literally hated physics before taking this class. Thanks to Prof. Kural, I now find it interesting and applicable to life. Overall, he really wants students to understand the material and succeed. The class was very hard but Prof. Kural was very engaging and knowledgeable and I am happy I had him.

Kural was enthusiastic about the material and made lectures exciting. Lectures mainly focused on conceptual topics, with less math, which made me feel unprepared for the majority of math-based group work and exam questions. But overall, I found the lectures interesting.

Physics 1201 sucks! It was one of the most intensive classes I've taken. But Kural is a fantastic instructor. He did a great job of explaining concepts and making the complex concepts much easier to deal with. I would definitely take him again.

Dr. Kural was a solid prof! His quizzes and exams are harder than his lectures, but the large curves (20-30%) make up for it. You really just need to beat the curve for a good grade. Make sure to go to TA office hours for the HW, do textbook problems, and study his groupwork and past quizzes well. If you put in the work, you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kural was a good professor, but his tests were so hard. They ended up getting a large curve but I would rather have just gotten a good grade in the first place. He explains the physics fairly well, and if you reread the slides before the quizzes you should be good! He wouldnt be my first choice, but certainly not a bad one

Dr. Kural is a great teacher. He is very knowledgeable about physics and does a good job answering questions. The class is group work heavy and the majority of the assignment are graded on completion. The tests are super hard but there are huge curves.

Both midterm averages are 50%, but then curved to a 77%. Kural makes quiz and test questions extremely hard and youll gain little from studying his lecture slides. He has a complex where he doesnt like to repeat himself and can be very rude if you ask him to repeat anything. Wouldve rather taken calc based physics than have to deal with him.

Dr. Kural is the single worst professor I have ever had. He is terrible at making exams (told students that is GOAL was for the average to be less than 50%) and was not willing to listen to student complaints at all. Openly talked down to students and was downright rude. I would not wish his course or even knowing him on anyone. Terrible professor.

Professor Kural was ok. Make sure you use the lecture slides and you will pass. My biggest concern was the structure of exams and quizzes. Everything was multiple choice so no extra credit for showing work. Miss one question and it will cost you on his short quizzes and exams.

Dr. Kural does not foster a very good classroom environment or communication. If you are someone who often emails their professor with questions, don't even bother with this class. Extremely rude over email and office hours. Study 2+ days in advance for quizzes. Quiz questions are extremely difficult compared to lecture. Just learn from the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: People have told me that Physics 1201 is the hardest class they have taken at OSU. I came into the semester genuinely concerned about it, but honestly it wasn't that bad. I attended lecture, took notes, and reviewed his lecture slides. Make sure that you understand all the concept questions that he puts on his slides. It really wasn't that bad.

Very difficult course especially if you don't like physics and have no interest in learning. You need to work real hard to stay on top of things. I think Kural made it enjoyable and relatable despite my struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I wanted to add a review because it seems a lot of students are giving him a bad rep when in reality it is the course not the professor. The concepts and math in this course are definitely harder than gen chem or physics 1200 - this class sucks. As far as OSU physics instructors go I think Comert gives an honest effort and is well organized.

I tried really hard in this class and still did not do well. I attended every lecture, read the book thoroughly, and still managed to do bad on exams and quizzes. This class is really tough and if you are bad at physics like me, you will probably struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Kural's 1201 class is quite difficult plain and simple. His weekly quizzes are very tricky and this class was a huge step up from 1200 in terms of how much I had to study. It's possible to do well if you spend the time and effort. Final is totally cumulative so prepare for that accordingly. Don't take if you have an easier option, he is rough.

Kural's quizzes and exams are difficult. You really have to understand the concepts and know how to do problem-solving beyond the simple examples he gives in class. We had very low exam and quiz averages, but with the median being relatively higher, the curves aren't great. I'd definitely suggest taking another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class much more than 1200, even though I thought I hated physics. Quiz and midterm medians are around 70%, so they were definitely fair. In my opinion the people who write negative reviews are just upset because the subject matter was difficult.

Kural is enthusiastic about teaching this course. The subject matter is inherently difficult but he makes it interesting and enjoyable. Quizzes were difficult but not impossible and the midterms were fair. I believe I learned a lot.

Just NO. Avoid at all costs. He is so unhelpful and does not tell you how to prepare for his exams and quizzes. I read the book and did all of the exercise problems and misconceptual problems and still could not seem to do well on his midterms and quizzes. This class made me hate physics and it is so unorganized.

If you think you can breeze through 1201 after having a good time with 1200, think again. Kural is relaxed in lectures, but his quizzes and exams are ridiculous. Simply, he doesn't prepare you enough. Coming from someone who crushed the chemistry department, I have never had more difficulty in a class before. Poor organization & unhelpful. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class requires more than what should be expected of you to even barely pass. I put in hours and had to read lectures and book chapters over and over again to even kind of know what I'm doing in order to prepare myself for his unnecessarily hard weekly quizzes. I wish I would have been told his quizzes are nearly impossible to do well on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Kural is hard and doesn't really care about students compared to his research but I mean his class is doable and you can just read the textbook and skip class and you'll be fine. Amazing curves tho so just beat the curve!

so hard! all conceptual multiple choice questions and even the ones with math are conceptual. cares about students and is sometimes funny, exams are really tricky but this class is just ugh! good luck to all
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Comert is a solid professor. He makes it clear that this class will take a lot of work to do well in, which it does. However, putting in a lot of work will result in a decent grade. Lectures are interesting and make sense, which is nice especially when it comes to more complex topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kural truly cares about his students (even if it doesn't seem that way). He definitely has the toughest test and quiz questions so don't take him if you want the easy route. If you do want to learn, he is your guy. I didn't go to all of the lectures, but USE THE BOOK AS A RESOURCE FOR MATERIAL YOU DON'T UNDERSTAND and ASK HIM YOUR QUESTIONS!

Dr. Kural was a funny guy in lecture, but some of his explanations were hard to follow. I studied hard for every exam and still had lots of trouble in this class. I am bad at physics, but I feel like I knew the material well enough for a base level physics class, but still had tons of trouble.

I thought Kural was a good professor to give you the baseline knowledge to succeed, but you also need to put in a decent amount of work outside of class. I recommend using the multiple choice problems in his slides and really understanding these underlying concepts the night before an exam/quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kural makes physics lecture interesting and fun. You'll realize this when you have a guest lecturer. His quizzes and exams are difficult but fair. Utilize the online homework and practice problems listed in the syllabus to study for his tests. Your grade in the course will be dictated by the amount of time and effort you put into studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kural doesn't do much hand-holding. He establishes a baseline of knowledge and practice problems, which is typically not enough to succeed on quizzes and exams. Lectures are funny and can be helpful, but work outside lecture is important if you want to beat the curve.
He is a decent guy, but as a professor, just not very fair. His exams are difficult but there is a curve. Definitely could have put more time into it but he could have also been more fair.
Eh, he's okay but it's a lot of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I thought Kural was great actually. One of the better professors (you'll quickly realize this if you have a sub lecturer). Had good analogies in class. Also quick at answering emails. Clear that he wants you to do well. Most would agree that overall, the exams/final was definitely fair if you studied consistently throughout the semester!!!

No. If you have him for Physics 1201, drop and switch professors. He was so unhelpful and unprofessional when I went to him for help in the course. His quizzes and tests are over questions far more difficult and in depth than those discussed in class. I spent HOURS reviewing the textbook and homework's before each quiz. Good luck, you'll need it.
Kural makes lectures enjoyable.  Quizzes and midterms were mild, final was hard.  prayer,  reading the suggested pages in the book, and practicing the problems got me through this class!

I didn't like physics much but I really enjoyed coming to lectures. Comert made classes funny and interesting. He did a really good job of relating it to things students can understand and does it in a comical way.
Comert explains the concepts very well. Exams are fair. I really enjoyed the class...
It was a tough semester but I enjoyed physics for the first time. He is a fun professor, but at the same time serious about teaching....

Funny lecturer, gives examples in class so you'll remember them. You don't really have to go to class since he just goes over the lecture slides and puts them all online. The first 2 midterms are really similar to the practice problems at the end of each lecture and the past quizzes, but the final is super hard.

Hilarious professor. He has a heavy accent, but very easy to understand, didn't cause any problems. Midterms were easy, very similar to quizzes. Homework questions are usually a lot harder than the quizzes. The final is nothing like the midterms though, you really need to study. Overall great professor.

Most down to earth professor I have ever had. He is hilarious with make the class enjoyable. His explanation is also hilarious which help with understanding the topics. The two midterms were extremely easy. But Final took me by a surprise. So study your butts off for final.

While he is a funny professor attendance isn't necessary because he just read from slides that were online. First exams were exact copies of quiz and homework questions but the final was impossible. Average was 49% and my section received a 30% curve on the final.

Only reads off lecture slides. Slides come directly from the book but make no sense. You have to read the book to understand them. Midterms are hard but doable. The final was terrible. Unnecessarily hard and everyone walked out saying they guessed on 95% of the questions. How well you can guess on answers will determine your final exam grade.

Fairly funny guy without a thick accent. Final was unnecessarily hard and almost completely conceptual. Had a high A before the final. Final grade in the class will depend on how many students failed the final as hard as I did. Lecture isn't mandatory. If you don't understand the conceptschapter in the book, go to lecture.

Comert's lectures were NOT helpful to me at all. He goes over lecture slides from the book which is helpful but does only a couple example problems and skips over the practice probs way before you even have a chance to look at them. I started doing better on the quizzes when I stopped going to lecture. His test are hard no matter how much you study

He's very good at explaining in lectures and his exams are fairly difficult; however, if you look over practice exams, quizzes, and notes; he takes questions straight from them and tweaks them slightly

I think he is a good professor. He is funny and always has a few jokes to pepper in every lecture. His quizzes can be tricky; make sure you go over all the "concept test"  questions from lecture because more than likely they will be on a quiz andor midterm. Midterms are very fair and based on previous quiz and homework questions almost entirely.

Kural is a fun professor and keeps physics somewhat interesting. He likes to trick you, but if you pay attention in class and read his quiz questions carefully you will be okay. His midterms have the same concepts as old quizzes and homeworks just reworked.
Final was all conceptual.
He is a very fun professor. Uses example questions in class.
Really solid professor overall. You'll have to dedicate maybe 1.5-2.5 hours once per week to do the assigned homework but it's not that bad and the final is open note which is nice.

10/10 professor who genuinely cares about his students and offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. There are optional lectures you can attend with guest speakers where you can also earn additional extra credit. Overall, a very good professor and a great class experience.

Great guy and great professor with tons of experience in supply chain. He gave good insight about the industry along with ways to connect with professionals. The class itself was very easy with 3-4 assignments per week that take less than an hour to do with the final exam being online and open note. Overall highly recommend.

Absolutely amazing professor! Took BUSML 3380 all online with Professor Widdifield and it ran so smoothly. He was accessible outside of class and always quickly replied to my emails. Quite a few assignments due each week, the final was open book and not proctored.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Widdifield is a really knowledgable professor and you can tell he enjoys being able to teach and share his knowledge. The class and assignments weren't too hard at all. There were quite a few assignments due each week, but it helps keep your grade up! I would absolutely take another course with him!

He is by far the best professor I've ever had. His final exam is open book and open note, as it should be. McGraw Hill HWs were easy and straightforward, same with the other assignments. Just a great guy and professor overall.
Easiest class ever. Only need to show up to select sessions to get points. Exam was open note. Lots of the mcgraw hill assignments though. They take some time.

He is a great teacher, enthusiastic, ready to help and cares about students. My class was online but he gave opportunities to get involved and had optional review sessions upon request. One thing I did not like was the textbook for the course. It was overly complicated and time consuming to read for an introductory level logistics management course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Widdifield is the definition of an outstanding professor. He has extensive real life experience in the logistics industry as well as in the military. He stands for everything good and is quick to provide help and resources needed to succeed in class. He is highly engaged with companies around Columbus and is respected by most students.
Great professor with an very significant amount of knowledge and experience.

You don't do anything in this class.  The exam reviews are verbatim the tests, but make sure you know the textbook verbatim for the answers.  You don't have to go to class, you don't have to read, just memorize the reviews and you'll get a perfect score.  Online quizzes are straight of .ppt and you don't have to do that great on them to get an A.

David is a very good professor who knows his stuff, and has real world experience to back it up. This class was the easiest class I have ever taken. If you actually do the study guides for the tests and all of the extra assignments, you will get an A. I put in minimal effort and still got over 100%.
It is impossible not to get an A for this class.
Easiest class ever, ever, ever had. Midterm and final were exactly the same as the review materials he posted online. Go to 2 guest speaking lectures. It is impossible not to get an A for this class.

Take this class as an elective. Easiest class I've ever taken at this University by far. Final was a copy of the study guide in exact order. Impossible not to get an A as long as you show up when the speakers are coming in. Saw this dude benching 3 plates at the RPAC. BEAST
DAVID IS AWESOME. Take his class. He's really helpful and also he's very keen on seeing his students' success. Such a lovable professor. May be one of the easiest As you can get from Fisher too!

Super awesome lecturer! He is very helpful and is always posting job offers or interesting information. His study guide is the exam paper and this class is definitely a nice break/encouragement from the other lecturers. Attendance is not mandatory.
His study guides for the quizzes and exams are pretty much the quizzes and exams. Super simple if you can memorize, attendance taken from the quizzes.
Very easy class! lectures were ok, guest speakers were awesome! Take him to get a good grade... quiz and exam reviews are available to get a great grade!
Class is easy, but you need a 97% to get an A...Not quite sure where that grading scale came from. I had a 96% and got an A-, never had that happen to me before. Good luck...

He's PERFECT for students who just need to finish their logistics prereq- it's honestly the easiest class I've ever taken at OSU. His quizzes & final exam are straightforward & EASY, & he even gives attendance points just for taking them! Plus he's a genuinely nice man, is VERY knowledgable about his field, & has a clear passion for what he teaches

This was the WORSE class I have ever taken! His lectures are very detailed on unnecessary information that you will not need on the test. He does not give you any formulas or constants on the exam...GOOD luck trying to memorize all of the equations on top of learning the class material. If you can get out of taking this class, DO IT!

Run! Exams had many math formulas that he refused to give equation sheet prior to the exam so we do not "reverse engineer questions". Discord for quick communication, but did not respond until the night before exams. When asked for more practice problems he said simply "No". Will laugh at your face when asking for guidance on studying or lecture.

He offers no resources to succeed in this course. Could replace him with an app reading out slides and class would become better as you would have no expectations that you're getting a professor. Go to recitation and TA office hours or else youll fail, and treat this class as 4 credit hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The TAs are the only reason I got through this class at all. If you are teaching the physics behind biochemistry, it makes no sense to test their mathematically ability (no calculator exams) as opposed to the concepts themselves. Pretentious, unreasonable, and unfortunately mandatory for biochemistry majors.

Seems to be against things every other professor I've had is ok with. Very picky-choosy with equation sheets on exams though it's an equation heavy class. Just include every possible equation if you're concerned with “cheating”? The no calculator thing is annoying and wastes time and increases chances of mistakes on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is not a very caring teacher. Even in office hours, he has laughed at a student for asking to go over a textbook question. He is not very transparent about what is on the exams or what we need to memorize, so you will have to memorize everything. If you take his class, I recommend going to recitations and going over the recitation problems.

The professor is knowledgeable but ineffective at teaching. Lectures are confusing, slides are incomplete, and homework and quizzes often contain errors. Expectations are unclear, forcing reliance on dense textbooks. The no-calculator exam policy is unreasonable given the time-consuming math.

Dr. Wilburn's TAs do more work to help students than he does. When asked if he could provide extra learning resources, he says no. The content itself isn't awful, but it's impossible to learn/study without anything aside from lecture slides and homework. He could be a good professor if he wanted to, but he doesn't care enough to put in the effort.
every avenue to make you feel overwhelmed is taken,a very inconsiderate professor whose TA's teach better than he does, which is a very low bar to climb

Seems like he doesn't want his students to succeed... lecture slides and homeworks often have mistakes, gives almost no practice problems, doesn't even give the equation sheet prior to exams requiring students to memorize everything even if it's not needed. Lectures are hard to follow and slides are almost no help.
I have nothing good to say.

Professor Wilburn is an incredibly smart man, but I honestly believe he does not know how to teach at all. I have never had a worse experience than his class. His lectures make no sense, and the only time I learned was in recitation. His coding homework is stressful and completely irrelevant to the exams.

I enjoyed the way he set up the class - the coding projects and use of genAI opened my mind to a new way of problem solving and taught me the basics of Python. But... he's not great at lecturing, I eventually just stopped going and read the textbook. The material being tested (60% of grade) was not clear, and there were almost no practice problems.

Dr. Wilburn lacks any teaching ability. His lectures consist of him going through slides without explaining any of what is shown on each slide. He also gives complicated coding problems for homework that are not helpful at all. Dr. Wilburn also refused to do practice problems in class for exam review when multiple students asked him requested them.

You can tell that Dr. Wilburn loves physical biochemistry and really enjoys teaching it, but he struggles with communicating the information in a way that students can easily understand. There were several times while studying where I had to first understand what he was actually talking about in the lecture slides. Convoluted explanations.

The math department needs to be fixed for this class. He releases no lecture notes, writes on a chalkboard, and talks monotone the entire time. His examples are not helpful at all in terms of comprehension and exams are harder than any work you will do for homework or in lecture. You will need a tutor and to learn everything yourself.

Honestly if i had to choose between retaking this class or fighting thanos, i would choose the thanos every single time. First of all, you have to teach yourself for majority of the time because he does not do a good job at all when it comes to making sure people are learning what they're supposed to learn. Recitation was the biggest joke

Let me start by saying he's a really nice and misunderstood guy that is very knowledgeable. With that being said, his lectures are very monotone and the recitation was abysmal. I stopped going to lecture and recitation halfway through the semester and self-studied to get an A. I don't recommend at all, but is doable if it's a last resort.

Not terrible, but if you actually want to learn calc 2 then skip the lectures and watch the organic chemistry tutor videos and do the homework. The exams are a huge chunk of the grade so I would recommend just grinding out practice problems to prepare for them. If its your first time taking calc 2, good luck.

The most boring class you will ever take, he will kill all of your motivation to try and learn the content and will get you into a habit of skipping class so that you dont have to hear his quiet warble of a lecture.
Incredibly frustrating to ask questions of. Provides very undetailed explanations, just repeating himself if you didn't get it the first time.

such a shame that he does not teach engr math b. he is the best professor i have ever had. really, the most helpful one. the notes he made in class is so clear and it really helped me a lot when i was reviewing for the final.
DEBOER MY GOAT! If you accept his way of teaching I promise you this will be your favourite lecturer and you will receive your greatest math grade of your life!

Great professor! Responds to emails quickly, provides practice problems that reflect the exams, and is always helpful during office hours. Explains concepts clearly and in a way that's easy to understand. Really supportive and wants students to succeed.

Took his class over the summer and was nervous since math isn't my best subject, but his lectures were clear and he's clearly passionate about math. I went to office hours a lot, and he was always patient and helpful. He's flexible with grading. A little socially awkward, but very nice and explains topics well. I would recommend his class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. DeBoer was great. He graded fairly and was always available after class and office hours. This was Calculus 1, so I was not expecting it to be easy. To excel, if you do not have an aptitude for math, you must practice solving problems until they become second nature. I'm not sure why some people scored him so poorly. Just do the work.

After getting a D the first time,I retook Calc 1151 this summer with Prof.DeBoer.I was nervous because of his bad reviews, but he's a nice person and explains clearly. He offers lots of resources, clear grading, and chances to regain points. The quizzes and midterms almost match his sample papers. I went from a D to an A and strongly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a monotone lecturer but never talks down to students or tries to explain things in the most convoluted way possible. He was genuinely helpful and understanding in his office hours and was honest about what to expect. The team were tough graders but were accommodating for retaking quizzes and tests and correcting what should be almost passes.

It's not Pf. DeBoer's fault that this course is heavy. THIS IS CALCULUS. 
Just get prepared before you go to class and complete homework on time, I promise you it is not tough to get an A!!!

I took Pf. DeBoer's class last year and it surprises me how much negative feedback is made on him. 
Pf. DeBoer is the most patient professor I have ever met in my academic life. 
In my experience, if you go to lectures on time and pay attention to the useful notes he makes, it is easy indeed to get an A.

these reviews are overstating how bad he is. he just does his job. he isnt amazing but explains things fairly well and answers questions well.the class is just hard regardless of who you have.take advantage of the recorded lectures if you are havingtrouble with hislectures. the recorded lectures + sample midterms are enough to do well in the class.

Deboer honestly is not all that bad just monotone, in this course you would watch a lecture video by Jim Talamo before going to actual lecture which did help as well. Deboer though gives a quick review of material at the start then runs example problems after which helped a lot. Come to class with questions it will help significantly.

I honestly don't understand a lot of these negative comments about Neil. In this class he was very good as a lecturer, always stopped to ask if anyone had questions, and explained topics thoroughly. Yes, in lecture he can be kind of droning but its a math professor what do you expect. Even if you don't like him the lecture videos are very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very bad! Even attempting to learn with Dr. Deboer was a total waste of time. I would recommend going to other lectures if he were to be your lecturer because you will learn nothing with him. He refuses to do problems with actual numbers and chooses to only use variables, which don't help your understanding.  Beware and please avoid him.

Dr. DeBoer is an alright lecturer. He does a decent job of explaining concepts most of the time, but doesn't answer questions that well (but you can do that during recitation as well). 1151 was a insanely difficult class and the graders are harsh. If taking 1172, I wouldn't recommend the lectures as they are basically glorified recitations.

If you have this professor for 1172,  I recommend you not attend the lectures, it is very useless and he does not know how to explain any concepts. I watched pre-recorded videos from the course modules that are from a different lecturer that you should switch to if you can named James Talamo. This course in general is not hard if you want to pass
His lectures were extremely boring and atrocious grading. If you can switch to James Talamo, please for the love of god do so.

Very monotone, boring lectures—that makes it clear he does not want to be there any more than his students. The class itself is not too hard; if you do the midterm reviews and actually understand that material, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for Calc 1 and honestly have no complaints. Went in a little worried because of his reviews but saw nothing wrong. Calc 1 professor doesn't really matter that much, no matter who you have it's the same assignments and tests and Professor Deboer did a fine job at teaching it, so don't let these reviews throw you off.
DeBoer is a terrible lecturer who doesn't explain what he writes down, he just writes. Also his handwriting is terrible so good luck trying to understand new concepts AND read what he writes.

Neil was smart, but an absolute terrible teacher. He couldn't explain things clearly. When explaining straightforward concepts, he'd make them so difficult by neglecting to explain anything he's doing. He's open to questions but sucks at answering them. Be prepared to teach yourself the course. If, like me, this is your first calc course, good luck
I did not like having Neil as a professor. He was not a good professor at all. He went through things very quickly and did not explain very well, in my opinion. Would not recommend.

Lectures were boring, but I felt like he covered the necessary content and material. His handwriting is not the greatest, but not the worst I've seen. He goes through material and practice problems very quickly. In conclusion, not a bad teacher just boring.

Neil DeBoer's teaching is a disorganized mess. He skips crucial content, forcing us to practice example problems with no proper grounding. Even with my background in Calculus I and II, his explanations leave me confused, making this class a nightmare for anyone without prior calculus experience.
Avoid. Would have dropped before the deadline if I knew how poorly taught this section would be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DEBEOR THE GOAT
He doesn't know how to teach.

Prepared students well for exams and always answered questions in class. Extremely knowledgeable with insightful lectures. Also, had a great grading system which allowed students to complete exam corrections. Overall, one of the best math classes I've taken at OSU.
doesn't seem to know how to teach. very rarely answers questions during class. focuses too much on lecturing rather than helping students

A lot of the problems that people have with him are due to things the math dept. at OSU does instead of Neil specifically. Neil was a good lecturer: he answered any questions that came up and was pretty clear with his examples. I will say that he often did fly through some examples too quickly and didn't explain a lot of things he did in detail.

neil seems like a nice person, but he CANNOT lecture. granted, he was always willing to explain and provide examples if you are confused, but i feel like most of the context was explained in very vague terms and was too fast paced for anyone to actually come up with questions in lecture. without a decent TA, i would have failed.

Calc 2 is a difficult class no matter who you end up having as a professor. I believe Neil did a very good job in his lectures in explaining concepts and always answered questions whenever people had them. In calc 2 specifically, I see no reason for him to be a 1-star as anything unrelated to lecturing is dependent on the math department.

His lectures aren't great, but I don't think he deserves as bad of a reputation. He is always willing to answer questions and do more examples if anyone is confused. He is caring, but boring. I wouldn't seek out another class from him, but it was overall okay. Having a great recitation teacher definitely made the class 10x better.

He is quite possibly the most by the book lecturer of all time. He'll usually write on the board straight from the book, wasting lots of time He does an OK job with question answering though. Would've done a lot worse if not for my recitation professor. Not the worst in the world, but he makes simple material confusing.

Very nice guy, but terrible class set up. Your entire grade is based around 7 exams that are pass or fail, which the homework and quizzes have very little to do with. Notes are also structured poorly, there are few to none example problems. I would not recommend this class to anyone.

Neil seems knowledgeable and nice, but man, I did not learn anything from his lectures. I felt like I was drowning the entire semester having to piece together random sources on the internet to figure out what was going on. He didn't make it very clear what would be on the weekly quizzes either, I often felt unprepared for the quizzes.

I used to love math, but calc 2 and 3 at OSU made me hate it. I don't want to be mean, but he was not a good professor, you have to rely on the HW and "textbook" assignments. One plus: you can continue to try to complete previous problems from exams, but grading is very difficult, you really need to work hard to even get a decent grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy. Not-so-great professor. Didn't go to lectures because we were expected to learn the content through online lecture videos and only go to class with questions. Did not help to have practically no professor since this was my first time taking calculus. Great that attendance was not mandatory though. That would've been a waste.

Went to class for about 2-3 weeks because it was impossible to hear him speak, no matter where your seat was in the class. On top of this, he rarely explained concepts, mainly focused on the answer and not how to work towards getting said answer. Showed up late to class about 50% of the times I attended.

DeBoer did little to no actual teaching in class--you were expected to watch the lecture videos online beforehand and only ask clarifying questions in class. His handwriting for the video notes was also nigh unreadable. However, you did get multiple tries on each exam and only had to redo the questions you got wrong on the last try, which was nice.

Avoid like plague. Sounds sweet when you hear pass/fail exams but it is actually 100% or fail there is also an exam every other Monday and weekend quizzes. Homeworks are random content that is not covered on exams and there is no examples in class so much of the exam questions are seen for the first time on the exam Made account just for this

Deboer's pass/fail course setup is bizarre and confusing for students. The class is unnecessarily stressful for students as throughout the semester you won't really know what your grade is until after the final and he is very lazy when it comes to posting grades or providing students with practice problems to prepare for tests. Avoid at all costs.

Avoid DeBoer. Lectures are dry and lack examples. The course set up is bizarre. It's difficult to explain and even more difficult to succeed within it. Midterms are graded pass/fail, but to pass you need a 100%. Grades are not shown on carmen and the weight of each is unknown so final grades won't be known until the end of the course. Please avoid!
One of the worst professors I've ever had. I almost failed the class but just barely scraped by with a passing grade. If you can, avoid this lecturer.

DeBoer's lectures aren't the most interesting but he does a good job of explaining the material and provides a lot of examples that closely mimic the exams. If you go to his lectures and do the practice problems he gives you, you should have no problem passing the class.

The lecturer wasn't my favorite by any means. Professor DeBoer's lectures felt all over the place and they didn't really make sense most times. I honestly learned a lot more and only passed this class because of the TA that was assigned to my particular section. The notes are also super hard to read. I recommend another teacher or Heavy Self Study

DeBoer may have been a nice guy but as a teacher, he was too nervous while speaking to us during lectures and was whispering half the time. His lectures overcomplicated the topics and did not prepare for the tests since he zoomed by topics so quickly, only to realize in recitation the actual topic is way simpler than the examples he showed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was the worst professor I have ever had in my life. He has sympathy at all for his students. At least 30% of students failed his course because there was no curve at the end. I hope he gets fired

This class was an exam based class with 3 midterms and 1 final. There is a homework and quiz EVERY single week. The professor does not teach well, he goes up there and just writes, no presentation or steps. My TA explained everything, he should have been the professor. I do not recommend him because he teaches like you already know the information.

It's a shame they let people like this teach. This kind of apathy shows a complete disregard for any student and the university. He also wastes TAs time inside recitation by needing them to reexplain something that he "tried" to cover in lecture. Even further embarrassing this guy makes regular mistakes on low level material.

I took calc in high school but was left utterly confused when I would attend his lectures - covering topics I already knew. I eventually stopped attending lecture and had to rely on my great TA and recitation to get me through the class. Neil seems like a nice guy but not my choice of lecturer.

DeBoer is a great person and seems very caring. He is understanding of circumstances. His lectures are boring and he doesn't explain the content clearly, he just writes stuff on the board with no explanation. I skipped lecture but had to go to every recitation to save my time and understand the content.

I will first say that DeBoer is a nice, caring person, but is a terrible lecturer. Like others said, his handwriting is illegible. He often did not explain the most important aspects of the topics being discussed in lecture. He seemed very disorganized. Everything I learned was from recitation or YouTube.

Professor DeBoer is a good person but not a good professor. He does not teach very well so his material is hard to understand. Make sure to pay attention in lecture because he goes over things really fast.

DeBoer is nice as a person. However, I believe the way he teaches can be improved. For one, his online notes are illegible, so good luck if you can't read bad handwriting. On the other hand, he does try to respond to people's questions well.
Enjoyed his class! Highly recommend attending his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Donald Soles, or "Donny" as he prefers to be called, is definitely the best professor I've had so far. He is super funny, flexible with due dates, liberally available, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He also writes you a letter of recommendation to law school if you receive an "A". I am currently in his 3410 class, and it's great.
He's an awesome and down-to-earth guy that is very reasonable with grading. It is not hard to do well in the class, just as long as you read and take ideas from his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super fair professor and offers good feedback. Has two papers with most of your grade, but isn't hard to get good grades on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. So insanely understanding and easy-going. Very laid back and truly wants you to do well and see you succeed. Have so much respect for him, such an amazing guy.
good professor
Great prof--lots of reading, but goes over it in class. Responsive to student feedback about test dates. Cares about meeting students where they are. Rlly funny too

He really rewards effort. If you do the readings and come to class, it's pretty easy to do well even if philosophy isn't really your thing. He makes it harder to get a solid A, but if you get an A he'll write you a letter of rec for law school. He's good about being there for students and he definitely will help you improve if you make an effort.

Donny is a super nice prof and genuinely wants the best for you. that being said, the class is based off of 3-4 big assignments so make sure to put effort into those. instructions can be very vague and there aren't rubrics, but if you ask questions he will tell you exactly what he expects. Effort goes a long way with this guy so work for your grade

Donny was pretty chill, and his lectures were interesting when he let the class discuss stuff. Sometimes it seems like he likes to hear himself talk, but that's not always a bad thing (he can be entertaining lol). 
Participate in his class, put effort into the essays, read at least a few of the readings, and it's smooth sailing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Donny is so funny! You can tell he genuinely loves what he teaches. He is so sweet to us students and cares about each one of us, he even has coffee gatherings with us! If any other teacher taught this class I would not be interested, but he keeps me engaged with the way he describes court cases.

Donny is a great, caring professor. He actively tries to create an inclusive, open discussion in his class. Donny makes himself extremely available to help, especially for assistance on the class's three graded papers. Take his class, especially if you are interested in law school. (he will write a letter of recommendation if you receive an A)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Donny is a great professor. His philosophy of the law class was engaging. He's definitely not the easiest professor, but he's very fair and gives a lot of grace.

Professor Schoon is very understanding if you notify her of extenuating circumstances that may affect class performance in advance. She genuinely cares and will work with you if you show her the same respect you want to receive. 10/10 professor.

Schoon is so nice and really cares about your success. Weekly readings and discussions are easy, you get to skip or drop three of them. Definitely would take this again, it is great for a theme. Not a hard A if you do the assignments. Quizzes are online and low stakes.

This class has 3 online quizzes throughout the semester and the final is a paper where you get 2 options to write about. There is a good amount of homework and reading but if you get through it, it shouldn't be hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was definetely reading heavy with a lot of the discussions needing some form of citation from readings. There were usually a 1-2 page paper every couple units, the tests were not that hard and it was open note. Although the lectures were a big part of the test and anything else wasn't usually in the tests. I do recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor doesn't try to give the standard 'boring lecture', she usually walks around the class and gives space for students to voice their opinion. She also acknowledges both sides of immigration, not just one (saw a comment that suggested it). There were 2 total essays and 3 tests, but no final exam. The lectures were very interesting!

SOCIOL3200 was essentially over an hour long video, 30 pages of reading and an essay every single week. 

She is very clearly biased & one sided in her beliefs and if she does not agree with you then you will lose points. She shows only one side to the immigration of America - and will protect her feelings over logic! Would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This has been my favorite class at OSU so far. Content was well organized and interesting. Directions were clear. It's 40 pages of reading, a film, discussion post, and essay (400-700 words) a week. Very simple as it's just summarizing/short analysis. A little time consuming, but I took this as a 2nd session course. Overall, a great online course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was very eloquent and well put together. About ~1.5 times/week, there's a reading response as well as discussion board, which means workload can get heavy, especially as summarizing the readings in such few words could prove to be difficult (though I get why we did it). Still, class was interesting and encouraged connections to today's world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I like Dr. Schoon. She makes the online course very easily and interesting! I had fun during the summer and get a 3-unit A at last!

I like Dr. Schoon. She takes care of every student. Her course design is very interesting, and every article to be read is unforgettable. The only regret is that she didn't have in-person classes during the summer. I chose her summer SOCIOL 3302 since I had a great time on her spring SOCIOL 3200!
I like Dr. Schoon, she is very funny and kind!

She's a very nice woman! The lectures are very interesting, and the tasks are one discussion board and reading summary per week, plus two papers and three online quizzes in one semester. The in-person section is recommended.

Took this class for a GE and loved it. The professor is great. The materials were very interesting and assignments were not that hard. Lots of reading but I learned a lot and the TA's grades were pretty lax. Lots of opportunities for extra credit so your grade will be fine even if you miss some assignments. Was clear she cared about her students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Schoon is a very good professor, she taught American immigrants very well, I as a science major only as GE to take her class, but she was deeply impressed. One reading summary and discussion board per week, two related papers and three take-home quiz per semester, very simple! Because of her, I chose her for Sociology 3302 again this summer.
took this class online which was not too bad 2 essays discussion/reading summary every week. Proffesor is very nice if you reach out for help and flexible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So much work. Each week you have 100+ pages to read (textbook and articles), full page summaries of readings, discussion post of 350 words on readings and a film, quizzes with 400 word essay q's, 6 page essay due for the final in addition to an exam. Super strict on formatting and details for each assignment too. not worth it, even if online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't care if she's passionate about immigration She needs to turn that passion into something else besides making us read 4 essays and watching a one-hour film per week. The workload for this class was insane, especially for a GE. I thank god this was an online class I could not imagine this being in person. Don't take this class not worth it.

Danielle Schoon is a very amazing woman. She makes her course very interesting. Every week we have 1 reading summary and 1 discussion board, but these are very easy. There are 2 essays, and there are lots of chances to get extra points. Good experience, easy A! (Chooese In person,  2 less reading summary and 3 less discussion board than online one)

u can tell she cares about what she teaches and is passionate but this is the most work ive had for a professor. u have papers that have readings and films, discussion posts, and quizzes every week. if u are looking for an easy class would not recommend. I wouldve had a way easier time if it wasnt for taking this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was interesting, and she was a good professor, but it is so. much. work. several readings, often a documentary, a paper and a 350 word discussion post and response for every module. I pride myself in spacing my work out well and managing my time, and I still struggled.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes at Ohio State! Professor Schoon is so kind and genuine, and her lectures are fantastic!

Professor Schoon is very understanding and really cares about her students and the course content. The class was a comfortable environment and we had frequent discussions. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and is always flexible and understanding of your circumstances.

Dr. Schoon was honestly one of the best professors I've taken a class with. She made the class enjoyable, and for a 3-credit-hour class, it was pretty chill and she gave lots of extra credit opportunities as well.

Dr. Schoon was an amazing lecturer! There was a situation I had where I had submitted something late, but after explaining my situation, she allowed me to get full credit for it. 2 of the discussion posts and readings are dropped, and there are plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Make sure you don't wait until last minute to do the work!

Dr. Schoon is such a genuine human and professor! Her class is easy and straightforward, consisting of discussion boards and article summaries. I had an issue with COAM for another class as she and my other class had the same prompt of writing my personal immigration history. She was so understanding and even wrote a letter advocating for me.

Dr. Schoon is very passionate and informed about the work she does. Her lectures were interesting but not mandatory you can still get an A without them. The textbook was only for the quizzes and it is free online and there are weekly reading discussions and extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Would def take her again,
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Though this class did have a weekly reading and discussion post due it truly is not that bad. There is a ton of extra credit available and three discussions and a reading summary get dropped. This is an easy A class just don't wait till the last second to do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking this class with professor Schoon. The workload was manageable and the course was super interesting.
Dr. Schoon is one of my favorite professors at OSU! Definitely take a class with her if you get the chance.

Professor Schoon was an amazing professor for Sociology 3302! This class was offered online over the summer and was seriously the easiest A I have ever received (plus, it's a 3 credit hour course). It is an easy GPA booster if you need an easy class! I recommend taking it online
What a waste of my time. Easy A though.

This is a very writing and reading heavy course. There are required readings weekly and each reading is around 15-25 pages long. Plus textbook reading and smaller readings. If I would have known this was a reading and writing course, I wouldn't have taken the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Schoon was a really engaging professor and had a very well organized course. However, she is very inflexible when it comes to formatting and submitting assignments. The content of her course is not very difficult however she makes things more complicated than they should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Schoon is extremely caring and exceedingly smart. Her class is engaging and expects engagement from students as well. Grading was fair and extra credit was abundant.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Schoon is inexperienced as a political science teacher, but I'm confident she will continue improving. The class was structured in a way that makes getting an A easy, Dr. Schoon is funny and willing to take feedback.. She gives opportunities for extra credit and she works hard to make sure the class discusses many points that may not be popular

Make sure you do the readings otherwise you wont pass (LOTS of reading). Her midterm and final are both part multiple choice/fill in and part essay turned in on Carmen. Class is very liberal and one-sided on topics. Lots of opportunities for extra credit. I wouldnt recommend unless youre very passionate about immigration topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: (PHILOS2465) took this class to fulfill a GE, and it ended up being my favorite class I've ever had, most of the credit going to Jason's teaching. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches and tries to make each lecture and reading engaging and understandable. Super nice, was excited to go to class. Easy A if you pay attention and go to class.

Super chill dude, took Philosophy 2465 with him (wasn't listed on rate my professor for some reason) but yeah hes a good grader, very funny and makes the content very interesting. would recommend his class for a GE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: PHIL 2332 Dr. DeWitt is a phenomenal professor. Would 100% recommend this course to anyone who needs it to satisfy a GE credit or for their major. This class is a gem in that it is not stressful or very taxing whatsoever but as long as you show up and pay attention, you will learn quite a lot as the lectures are super engaging, also just a cool guy

(PHIL2332) This was by far my favorite class I've taken. Professor DeWitt makes a 1hr 20 class go by fast, and his lectures are genuinely engaging. Even though attendance is mandatory, he allows 4 absences. Plus, his class was one I never wanted to skip, even though I skip class easily (for other classes). Very easy, yet I learned a lot. Take it!
Super chill, super knowledgeable, really glad I got him

Jason DeWitt is a young professor but seems to know exactly how to do everything right when it comes to teaching. His ability to answer questions about hard topics and explain them to students clearly was amazing. He is also lenient and very relatable when he taught. Wish I had another class with him.

Loved DeWitt. Gives interesting lectures and makes it easy to participate. Fair grader and is willing to work with you- I was able to review my papers and got feedback that always helped me on the following ones. Pay attention in lectures and take some general notes and you will do well. Very much wish I could take him again- I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hes very nice an lenient, funny guy. His classes are discussion based and there is a participation grade, but he makes the classes interesting so theres no worry there. Hes very flexible and works with you with any issue you have. Id loved this class and would love to have him as my professor again

I love her, I picked her because of good reviews here and they are absolutely true. Will meet/zoom with you as much as you want for help and genuinely seems excited to help, also gave me an essay extension for meeting with her. She is a tough grader and will be brutally honest until your work is the best it can be, but she is 100% fair. Pick Erin!!

Professor Jamieson is so kind. She responded to emails extremely fast and always gave a lot of feedback. There were two major assignments that mainly defined your grade with discussion posts most weeks to boost your grade a little. She is very fair and always accessible. I highly recommend taking her if you want a relatively easy course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very fair professor. She gives great feedback on assignments and is more than happy to help outside of class through email. She also gives extra credit sometimes. I would absolutely take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jamieson was extremely accessible, especially for a fully remote class. She gives clear feedback on papers, and is very understanding and flexible on grading and finishing assignments. There are some group projects but as long as you respond to discussion posts and keep up with assignments this is completely manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was a great English professor. She provided clear instructions for assignments and was accessible outside of class anytime. She responded to emails very quickly and was super helpful in explaining things. She actually cares on how you do in the class, makes sure everyone is doing well. She is a pretty tough grader so make sure to put effort.

She gives good feedback and responds to emails really fast. Although sometimes her answers are a little vague, but in the end your assignments are on your own anyways. Her grading is fair and there weren't very many assignments and they were all pretty easy. Definitely the best 1110 professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jamieson is great, she is available for advice on assignments and always gives good individual feedback. Two main projects and weekly discussions but she provides a lot of time for us to work on them and gives us the resources to do well and ask for help. She is also very organized and everything you need is available on Carmen.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: really chill class. she gives a lot of time to work on assignments, and she responds to emails extremely fast. pretty easy grader overall, there's a couple of pretty big projects that are worth quite a bit (but again, she gives a lot of time to work on those). super organized as well, posts a lot of reminders/tips and is so sweet.

This course is valuable, but the professor does not explain concepts clearly or give enough examples. His grading has no clear rubric; he often writes “I can't read” with no feedback. He ignores students during office hours, demands grade questions be written as a “sea shanty,” yells at students, and delayed notes for 9 days before an exam.

This Professor required sea shanties for him to show up in his office for office hours. He didn't provide feedback on homework and exams, and didn't provide a rubric. Posted notes 9 days late in retaliation for an optional attendance course. Also yelled at students in office hours and class, shaming them for their scores and "bothering him."

Honestly the goat, Katz tries his best to explain difficult concepts though sometimes falling short... The HW assigned and the provided practice exams is very good practice for exams. I would recommend reading sections of the book that correspond to the HW if stuck on a problem. The exams were very easy if you do all the HW and practice exams.

Professor Katz is an OK professor. He tries to relate to his students, which is nice, but the material is just not presented well. I recommend either taking this class and supplementing it with other resources, or just not taking his class.
I took Math 4575 (combinatorics) with Katz. He's very quirky and has engaging lectures, and tests are fair. Will mention his cousin who's a criminal at least once.

Good professor who had good lectures. Always tried to joke around and be relatable with his students. Class is very lecture dependent and he doesn't post recordings online (although he does post notes). Tests were extremely difficult and were curved immenesly after most of the class failed or couldn't finished. Decent professor overall.

Katz is everything you want in a professor and more. He was always willing to take questions, always able to help outside of class and always kept the tone light . He teaches a tough course with confusing topics, but his lectures actually teach his students and he shows his thought process. This is something other math sorely profs miss.

I found this class very difficult especially at first, but Dr. Katz wants everyone to do well, if you go to lectures and office hours for help with the homework you should do solid. I was considering dropping at one point but ended up with an A. Need to study for the exams though, they are very difficult but he curves them.

He never put practice exam answers on Carmen in advance. I have finals the following day but I don't have the practice exam answers yet. Students cannot check grades anytime. Disorder arrangement on Carmen's system.

Professor Katz is easily the best math professor I have had. I took him for 2153 and requested him again for 3345 and now again for 4575. If you do his lecture, laugh at his jokes, and do the homework (which is reasonable) you will do really good on his exams. He doesn't try to trick anyone and is willing to help outside of class always!

I did pass fail for this because it's pretty difficult. He is always there if you need help after class and office hours. Wants you to succeed and always breaks things down when you don't understand it. There's weekly homeworks and 3 exams, so keep up on the homework and you should be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Hate calc 3 but Eric is great! You'll be fine if you do all the practice questions before exams. Be prepared for his jokes!

tests are unpredictable bc otherwise people would memorize proofs but overall fair. thought he was terrible for the first couple weeks but once you get used to the bad jokes and overall goofiness he's a good teacher, especially in office hours. The hw wasn't terrible especially with a group and he grades pretty leniently on tests and the paper
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Funny guy. He's really quirky, so he makes the class more enjoyable with drawings of dinosaurs and stuff. The material isn't that hard in and of itself, but his lectures are pretty proof heavy, and I found that I understood the material better combining the lectures with actually reading the book while doing homework. Exams are straightforward, too
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great person, but the wording for all her quizzes (basically midterms) are EXTREMELY confusing. She also tests us for specific examples discussed in-class, and I don't think that helps with critical thinking, just memorization. The content isn't even that hard, she just managed to make everything else so much harder.

5 lecture quizzes with 1 free retake for each. most of the class was workshop/lab stuff. The course is kind of repetitive but it was much better than 1114 with her. Be prepared for ICAs and to get grades that end in .92, .84 though lol. her and the TAs are interesting graders. Definitely more work than a 3 credit class but still manageable.

The only compliant I had was that I felt like her lectures were very rushed, otherwise she did good at explaining the topics and seemed approachable. Attendance is graded through tophats and she does have weekly quizzes but I never read the textbook and was fine. There is also a lot of extra credit.

She's a very good teacher and incredibly smart. I think the previous bad reviews are from her teaching lab, which she stopped doing this semester. I will say her tests are kinda hard compared to the notes, but still not bad. I don't like ecology, but I didn't mind her class. I also never used the textbook or went to office hours, and got by ok.

Dr. Beggrow's class is great...there is really nothing to complain about. If you show up to lecture and participate, there is no reason to not earn the grade you want at the end of the semester. It is evident that Dr. Beggrow was also highly knowledgeable about the subject matter, and I am really glad I got to take 1114 with her.

idk everyone's mean on here so maybe she's changed her style but i thought she was awesome. Really responsive and caring during office hours. I thought the class participation aspect was really useful for this class. Nitpicky grading but i think thats a bio department thing

Some of these reviews are kinda dramatic or maybe she has just adjusted her teaching and exams. Dr. Beggrow is very sweet and it is clear she wants students to succeed. There is A LOT of opportunities for extra credit and points outside of exams. Exams are difficult compared to content but are still very doable.

Literally the worst class I have ever taken. Super easy content but is graded harshly plethora of busy work. Attendance is graded. Lab is excruciatingly painful as you do nothing for an hour and then rush to finish actual lab, which parts are expected to be completed outside of the lab period. Asking for help doesn't even improve grade.

I liked her passion for biology and the way she challenged us to think critically. However, this class was harder than it had to be with the grading. I took the peer led section so that was a bigger commitment and had a lot of vague, subjective discussions about evolution that were kinda boring.

Dr. Beggrow definitely wants you to succeed and she lectures on antibiotic resistance for 8 weeks which is semi-interesting. The class is mostly writing assignments which are graded pretty difficultly. Luckily I had Dr. Beggrow as my TA so she is more than willing to help and outline what she expects from you.

If you're willing to put in the effort you'll be okay, but she is an incredibly tough grader and doesn't always give the best feedback because she can be condescending and not helpful. Avoid having her in lab and you'll be okay. Her tests can be very hard but there's a lot of easy points to make up for it in the class. She's decently nice.

Dr. Beggrow is a very nice person but her class is very complicated. A lot of the material does not seem very intense, but she grades labs very hard. Her lectures are very informative and I highly recommend attending them. Work hard on the labs, the grades will catch up to you.

She's a great professor, despite her tough grading and lots of class points (1000~ total points in the semester) her lectures are very in depth and require good note taking, but if you genuinely enjoy biology then it's a great class! She's a very kind person and is always open to help. I would take this class again if I could.

I loved Dr. Beggrow as a person, but not as a professor. She grades very tough and no matter what you do it never seems to be good enough. The tests are very tricky and a study guide is provided.
