However, with all study guides and reviews she gives, there is no answer key. How are you supposed to confirm you're even studying the right answer?

Dr. Beggrow is nice but her class is awful. Lectures are easy but the tests are purely application questions that have no way to be prepared for and barely have anything to do with what she teaches. She grades labs super strictly and kind of seems like she wants her class to be impossible to get an A in.

If you can take another prof do it she is the absolute worst! Nice to your face but grades like a psychopath she will not let any thing slide. Condescending and not helpful with answering questions. Assignments are nothing like  what is seen on exams. I could go on forever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is the first 5 credit class I've taken that had a helpful lecture. Her use of top-hats, in class assignments, and call and response was soo helpful to learn the course work. If you go to class and follow along with her "fill in the blank" slides, you'll do well. Lab makes up most of your grade, ask the TA for help with lab and you'll do well.

Lecture content appears to be easy however exam questions and quizzes are extremely difficult and have almost nothing to do with the lectures. My TA once said he had to google multiple questions on the exam because he did not understand them. Lab heavy course, however TA's will take off points for any little mistake in lab reports.

Though I did not enjoy the fact that Dr. Beggrow's exams were significantly harder than her weekly quizzes (and that the class was basically memorization), I appreciated her as a person. She took the time to include the scientific research of diverse groups and wanted to ensure that her lectures were very engaging!

Im currently in Beggrow 1114 and I have an A+. If you come to class for attendance TOPHAT points and you take notes or actively listen this class is very easy. If you have a lab TA that is not Beggrow, lab is also very very easy and is lots of group work. All quizzes open note. Skim the textbook too! Easy if you put in the work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Had her as a lab coordinator and TA a couple years ago. She absolutely picks favorites and takes off points for minuscule errors. Office hours were useless as even if she point blank told you what to write on an assignment, she still found ways to take points off. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Beggrow is nice but she is a tough grader. Most of your grade is from lab and she grades it to the harshest degree. When asked questions she gives cryptic answers or is condescending. She reads off powerpoints but have to go to lecture for participation. exam questions are obscure & don't make sense. refuses to take critiques & blames the student
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Beggrow is nice, but the way the class is structured does not make sense. Theres two exams worth nothing (basically). The grade you will get in class will primarily be based off of lab points, which she grades to the toughest degree possible. Let me remind you, your lab work will likely be due on a Sunday and is collaborative. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not as bad as people say. She grades lab reports harshly and is not very helpful in lab, but her lectures are good and she is pretty nice. Don't skip lectures.

Dr. Beggrow might be the worst professor I've had at Ohio State. She takes off points with no explanation and for things that aren't put the way she wants it to be. I had a ton of obstacles come up during the semester such as covid and she was no help at all and continued to dock points on things that shouldn't have been. Very condescending also.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very critical grader, if you don't answer questions, especially in lab, exactly how she would answer them you get points off. Took of points for trivial errors. Can be condescending when asked questions. Doesn't listen to feedback and instead blames the student. An additional 1 credit hour class is required and is a waste of time.

Honestly I'm not sure why Dr. B has such a bad rating, I love her class. She does grade lab assignments harshly and there's lots of group work which is annoying at times. But her lectures are interesting, with a good mix of discussion and lecturing. She's very kind and enjoyable to talk to outside of class; she even learns everyone's names!

She was my lab/recitation TA in Summer 2021. The content for this class isn't hard... I got A's for the midterm and the final. But she is basically looking to take off points on every assignment. Not wording your answers the way she wants will take off points. If you can get another TA, you should. She's decently nice though I guess.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible professor, try to take any other person. The class content was very easy to learn but she would consistently ask questions that depended on information that was not presented in the question. She also doesn't let you see what you missed and on assignments, she would dock points with no explanations.

AVOID! Course content is easy to understand but she makes exam questions ambiguous and very tricky. She wastes your time with dozens of small assignments (which she grades very harshly) and lets class discussions drag on and on without saying if you're right or wrong. I love Biology but absolutely despised this class and her "teaching" style.

Don't be fooled by the grade, only A- of the semester. Took this class last year, honestly miserable. Her practice exams did NOT correlate with the actual exam at all. She docked points for literally EVERYTHING. For writing her thesis on how to teach evolution, she is the WORST. I could go on forever about her, but I have limited characters :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Actually one of the worst class experiences of my career. She REQUIRES you take an extra class no other professor requires so that she can use data from it for her research without telling you. She's nice to your face, but a nightmare to deal with. Makes you do group work CONSTANTLY even when she asked us our opinion and we said no.
Beggrow teaches very well and the information in her lectures are very concise. However, she can go a little fast sometimes, and the tests are difficult.

I took her for my Biology 1114. Her lectures were terrible. It was examples and no content. I did not learn anything. Her tests were super heard for no reason and very specific. I studied so hard and still ended up doing poorly. Her class average was terrible and she did not even care. The class is based on more discussion than actually teaching.

She is a harsh grader. Shell take points off if you make small mistakes or dont include the specific wording she was looking for. Her lecture drag and she spends most time talking about examples rather than the consents themselves. Shes sweet and easy to reach out to but shell likely not answer your questions and go on a tangent.

Terrible. She takes points off for small grammar mistakes during the labs and her test questions are much more difficult than her practice exams are. Easily accessible but not very good at explaining. She also words the questions so weird as if she were trying to trick you; knowing the material will not help you do well. MUST BE AN ENGLISH WHIZ

She is incredibly difficult to work with. The rubric is unclear and she picks and chooses how she grades assignments. The quiz questions are difficult, random, and not from the textbook or lectures. She is incredibly picky, and even if you show her why her feedback or criticisms are inaccurate, she will not change the grade. Avoid if you can!

Actual workload isn't too bad, but quiz questions are often seemingly random. 3 essays, rubric is very clearly low effort and feedback isn't great. Annoyingly, she does not allow you to look at past discussions/assignments to study for quizzes. Really nice, though!

The actual reading for her class is not that bad, however, often times, her quiz questions do not align with the assigned course readings. She requires several essays throughout the semester for which she gives minimal guidance or clarification. Annoyingly, she does not allow you to look at past discussions/assignments to study for quizzes.

Dr. Caldwell does not give clear feedback or clear guidelines for assignments. She told students to follow the rubric on an assignment for which no rubric was given. She also asks quiz questions in confusing ways and has horrible turnaround time for grading.
Justifiably easy class, easy grading.

Great and helpful professor for a very manageable class. Expectations are super clear; on some assignments she will even give you an example of what your submission should look like. There isn't a ton, so just put in the work and it's an easy A.
She was my favorite professor this summer. The class was super easy, but required a lot of work.
Very rude for some reason?

Professor is quite cold and unfriendly, also not helpful at all. The grading criteria is literally not told to you. She'll say vague things then grade it super harshly and with a rude attitude toward you. She should make her expectations and the rubrics for assignments more clear instead of expecting us to read her mind to understand what she wants

This course was much more stressful than it needed to be. The instructor graded extremely strictly, and even small mistakes could lead to significant point deductions. It often felt like the grading focused more on catching errors rather than helping students learn
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very nice and approachable, and I had good experiences during office hours. The topics in the course are interesting. However, the grading rubrics can feel vague, and expectations for citations were strict. I recommend paying close attention to the rubric and citation requirements to avoid losing points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good all around!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Provides minimal feedback on grades. Assignments are graded after the next due date, making it impossible to apply corrections to subsequent work. Office hours are scheduled during peak campus hours, making it very difficult to get extra help. Course is so disorganized due dates from the previous semester weren't fixed until AFTER the final.

I took a summer 4-week version of the course, which was manageable. The amount of work was not bad if you didn't wait until the due date to start an assignment, but her instructions were confusing. She would subtract points for "not following directions" when the assignment directions were often as vague as "make an enriched paragraph."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hardest part of the class was finding the books we were using. We had 4 essays each based on a book but she gave a clear rubric. I loved her lectures and she is incredibly passionate about Roman history. Although we only needed to attend 80% of the lectures for full points, I recommend going to all the classes. Just stay ahead and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I needed to complete my Citizenship GE, so I took Roman History with Professor Arnold. She was an excellent teacher who understood that most of her class was there to fulfill their GE, but she made sure that the class wasn't just a waste of time. She was very intentional about helping us build valuable skills and cares a lot about her students.

Professor Arnold cares a lot about the success of her students and a lot about the material she teaches. That said, the class was a but unorganized and sometimes what she wanted was unclear. I do not blame her, as she is still adjusting to OSU, and I think she is a great instructor. Ask her questions!

reviews.comment: Basically graded on the two essays which are 60% of your grade, responses and hypothesis assignments based on the material of that specific week. Professor Doetsch makes the lectures engaging and informative. Exams are challenging but fair, focusing on critical thinking. The no-homework policy is a plus. Unstuck study was a lifesaver for exam prep along with the class materials. Definitely take this class if you can.

Prof. Doetsch was a very kind and caring teacher. It's abundantly clear that he loves what he teaches, but his exams are pretty difficult. Great guy -- does a good job relating content to current events. Does a good job reviewing fundamental econ, even though macro/micro is required for course. Extra credit for attendance. Cheat sheet for exams make them easy.

tough he is a interesting guy, i just want to tell you that the average grade for each midterm is around 71, it's even curved!!!!!

he's ok.

Doetsch is very fair

reviews.comment: Dr. Doetsch is the best lecturer I have had so far. He is really good at explaining textbook jargon by using easy to understand examples. The class was graded only on exams, but the lowest score was dropped so you could afford to have one slip-up. On low attendance days, he would give out extra credit, so come to every lecture!

Dr. Doetsch is great! His classes can be difficult but rewarding. You will certainly learn a lot. If you come to class, take notes, and participate in some discussions you will do fine. When I took the course, the tests were completely essay but graded on a rubric to see if you included key material to gain more objectivity.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Doetsch is very knowledgeable & I learned a lot from his lectures. His tangents are both informative & entertaining. He moved very fast in lectures due to time constraints, so stay awake and write quickly to keep up. 3 exams & 10 homework assignments make up the final grade. Rarely gives out extra credit, but when he does it's 1 point.

Great lecturer who always provides intriguing arguments with evidence for and against scholars' papers. There's 3 open note exams and no other grades so you really have to do well on them to get an A which can be a problem. If you simply go to every class and pay attention, you will do really well
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: No homework. No projects. Only thing graded in the class our three exams. He takes your best exam score out of the three and puts it in a second time to help your grade. Offers random extra credit points for showing up to class. Interesting lectures and genuinely interested in teaching students. All exams are open note and if you go you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Proffesor Doetsch is hilarious, and teaches a lot because of it. Don't worry though, his class was such that if you payed attention during the lecture you simply had to regurgitate it to get an A, there wasn't much thought involved. But you still learn a lot.

If you have the option of taking Dr. Doetsch's class, do it. He's a great lecturer and conveys material in a clear way. I had him for ECON 3048 and the class was both relatively easy and interesting. If you go to class and take good notes you'll be golden because all his exams are open note.

Great lecturer who makes class enjoyable. Very smart man and passionate about what he teaches. Assigns a fair amount of reading, but everything you need to know is in the lectures. Go to class, take detailed notes, and the exams won't be a problem.

In retrospect, this class was really easy. His three tests are all open note so all you have to do is go to class everyday and take diligent notes; write down everything he says. Briefly read over your notes the night before exams and refer back to them as needed. Not only easy, but extremely interesting. Go to class to get those extra cred points!

I recommend taking class with this professor. He is energetic, smart and hilarious. He is well prepared and is willing to help. If you attend his lectures and take notes, you will get at least a B, if not A. I was intimidated ny some negative comments about him before taking the class but I got an A-, so all you have to do is work hard.

I've taken 2367, 4130, and 4140 from this guy, and they all were awesome.  Best lecturer I've had at OSU.  If you are good at essay type exams this is the class for you!  That being said, you don't have to be an amazing write, as long as you can convey main points in coherent sentences you will be fine.  Take his classes, you won't regret it.
You'll love him on every day except for exam day.

one of my favorite profs at OSU! The material is a bit tough, but if you go to class, his lectures are really clear and extremely helpful. His exams have essays, and they can be hard. But most students do well in his class, and he's a great professor. Also, just going to class with this guy is fun, it's an enjoyable 55 minutes.

Also 2367 and 4130. Highly Recommended. His lectures are energetic. COME TO CLASS. He makes the material interesting and makes you think. He presents a theory and then completely tears it apart. He loves making jokes in class so there are always laughs. The in-class essay tests are no joke. Prepare. You work for what you get, but it's worth it.
Don't count on this guy helping you out in any way.

His clarity is nonexistent and also somehow is able to grade 200 papers in 2-3 days which leaves me skeptical. He grades you on how he feels that day. He makes it as hard as possible and tries to drown his students with information so students don't know what will be expected of them on the exams. He rounds down with his grades which nobody does.
Gives open note blue book exams that are still impossible to do well on because he is looking for one small detail of what we have learned through the semester.

One of the best ECON professors you can have. He is extremely clear with what will be on exams, he explains concepts well, and he makes class enjoyable at 8 AM. The economics and ethics class was extremely interesting and I would highly recommend it.

Amazing lecturer. Requires a lot of reading and going to class is very important - handwritten notes are allowed for tests! He'll make you work for your grade, but you'll learn a lot and he will make it interesting.
He is a really mean professor. You would not get helpful feedback from him and I do suggest that do not take his class. Great lecturer, but not a good professor.

I took econ 4140 and he is very good and clear about the topic he is teaching. good grading criteria. and not very hard test yet you understand the material. If you do not miss the lecture and took notes it should be fairly easy class. He is funny and yet clear about the material he is teaching

I took four class with Ethan and he is one of the best professors at OSU. The class is interesting. Exam is open note but the timeframe makes you need to familiar with most of the concepts. Great experience.
He is the best professor ever! take one of his class and you will know

His exams can be difficult with the time restraint. Other than that he is a very good professor. Go to class and you will be fine. He teaches things in his lectures that are not in the book so actually go! I would definitely recommend his class!
Great lecturer.  Wants to be a professor and it shows.  Lectures are always entertaining.  Open Note exams, so take good notes and you shouldn't have a problem getting a B at worst.

If you need to take a 5000-level ECON course, look no further. The course is intellectually stimulating and fascinating if you're into it. Open notes for exams mean you do fine IF YOU DO THE STUDY GUIDE. Bonus is offered throughout. No reason to get lower than a B, and an A is attainable if you work hard.

Ethan is one of my favorite professors at Ohio State! He explains things really well and makes sure things are not too complicated. You don't need the book but you need to go to class. The exams were really fair and open notes. He also has an awesome sense of humor and I'm trying to take a class with him again!
Good lecturer although attendance is not needed if you get the book. Exams are all essay but you can have notes. The project requires a lot of work too but you have the option to work with a partner.

I took three classes with him. He is always well prepared for the material and his exams are all open notes, so you don't need to memorize too much. He is also very fun with a special sense of humor. Highly recommend him!

Best lecturer I have had at OSU.  Highly recommend him. Pay attention take good notes because both the mid-term and final were open note.  His style of teaching increased my level of interest in economics.
One of the best professors I've had. Good sense of humor and a pretty easy grader. The only negative is his voice is very load which sucks for morning classes.

Very cool guy. He has a sarcastic sense of humor but it makes the class much more interesting. You don't really need to buy the book or do the readings as long as you kinda pay attention in class and read over the slides a couple times prior to the exam and you'll be fine.  I would recommend him and you'll be in for a good class

Probably the best professor I have had at OSU. Now it was mainly a writing class so I cannot speak of how hard he would make exams, but he did not grade papers too hard. He is a really nice guy, helpful, and encourages class participation. I would take the class again if I could

Dr. Ethan is a nice guy. He is funny and always has energy to teach. He is easy to understand in class and follow what he is saying. However his exams are confusing. I would not recommend him, but if you must take him, its not that bad. Generally 3 tests for the whole semester.  Not mandatory attendance, but extra credit 10+ points.

Erich's teaching style was effective and let me learn more about the subject. The exams are relatively easy only as long as you put in the work to read every week and engage in class. Reading is about 4-5 hours per week, but with heavier weeks with reading responses it might take more. He is a tough grader, but the grades fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lectures, very knowledgable about the content. I was expecting to go over a more broad region of the asian philosophies (ie hindusim, daoism) but stuck to Buddhism the entire semester. It was still very interesting and he was great. Did not allow electronics to be out which definitely made me learn more but dislike the class sometimes.

No idea what these other reviews are on about, Erich is genuinely the GOAT. Dude is very knowledgeable, encourages open discussion, engages students, and generally keeps things entertaining. He actively seeks out student feedback, and is very clear about the expectations and grading. Class is easy and fun.

Erich deeply cares about what he teaches. His class is not an easy A, however, simply paying attention and doing what is asked of you is enough to get the grade you desire. If you are not interested in philosophy then don't take his class.  At the very max, you'll be spending 3-5 hours a week reading/writing summaries and papers. Not a big deal.

She's firm on a few classroom boundaries - no electronics in class, you need to print a lot of the readings and take hand written notes, you need to be on time. As long as those classroom expectations are met, she's fairly laid back. Her lectures are great. There's a lot of reading, but nothing unmanageable.

The reading load is extremely heavy, especially between Wednesday and Friday. The expectations are high, and the classroom environment can feel tense due to her behavior during lectures and discussions. The way questions and comments are handled feel discouraging rather than supportive. There are a lot of GEs that will fulfill this GE requirement…
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super passionate about what she teaches, interesting readings--lots of papers, readings, and group discussions. She's always willing to help out when you're stuck or stressed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: My spanish was forced to dramatically improve. Class was online, and we were on Zoom the entirety of the class, but it went by pretty fast because of how much participation required. You have to come to class prepared, yes because of the intense amount of homework she gives, but because she will call of you individually to answer her questions.

Lots of long assignments- nice for practice but amount can get overwhelming. During class she would randomly call on people- can be a bit intimidating and she doesn't try to help when getting stuck while speaking. She is nice and is helpful when working one on one with her, but be ready for lots of group work and participating in front of class.

I will say I learned a lot in her class, and I got a good grade. But the amount of homework was 10x the amount of any of my stem classes, the way she lectures is okay some days, but awful 99% of the time. You have to learn every classmates name, if you miss 2 classes your grades drops 1% after each miss, and you always work w a different person.
You get out what you put in.
She is very, very sweet, but she is very passionate about Spanish. She will hold you to a high standard, but it ultimately benefits you as a student.

She is very nice but the amount of work is insane for a 4 credit class. Should be considered 5 credits. I had, no joke, over 60 assignments in the first week on LingroHub and another 10 on Carmen Canvas. It was beyond overwhelming. Do not recommend. Tests were also very difficult. Its a passable class clearly but a LOT of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: genuinely the worst prof i've ever had. she asks on the spot questions and is condescending if you struggle. her explanations are hard to follow. she was also quite snoody abt my class absence when i had the flu (w/ dr notes)

She's very nice, but she teaches the class like a high school Spanish class. Everyone had to learn the names of all other students in the class and she forced you to work with different people every class. It's very hands on and you must participate every class period. You have five free absences before they take down your grade.

I thought Professor Steensen was a great professor! The class was a lot of work but I think that's more the requirements of the fault of the Spanish department and not her. She was fun to talk with in class and really good at teaching the material! She also has a one grace period policy where you can miss one class without an excused absence.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I couldn't finish a week in her class. I'm a typical tough it out student but this class was harder than chemistry. I felt very uncomfortable because on the first day we were expected to speak full conversations in Spanish. She assigned 9 homework assignments the first week of school. Her Canvas page was very confusing and difficult to follow.

Worst class I have ever taken in my life. She is degrading, rude and passive aggressive if you are confused. I had such a passion to learn Spanish and was even considering pursuing a minor before her course but after her class I am completely burnt out, she took the joy out of learning. I will never get over how terrible this professor was.

Overall I think she's an ok professor,was very helpful in certain situations but MAN was she difficult. It's like no matter what you say or try to offer other solutions to a problem you have, she just doesn't care. Grading is very tough and isn't understanding for something out of your control (link doesn't work, something isn't loading, etc.)

She was rude to the students and belittled them for not getting what she was asking right away. She has improved tech wise and is good with organization. Attendance matters a lot and you are required to participate multiple times a session. A lot of homework and she expects you to retain all of the information. Do not take her class.

She gets easily annoyed/frustrated if you don't participate and is very strict. If you are absent from class more than once without clear proof, then it takes 3% off your final grade. She will randomly call on people and gives a lot of weekly work. She isn't understanding or lenient with grades. The final wasn't awful, but I had to study a ton.

Prof Steensen assigns a lot of HW, due to the fact the course is monitored by the Span department. I found her classes to be extremely helpful and she kept the class interesting and had a good sense of humor (which I don't think a lot of other students understood). She's accessible outside of class and will help you with assignments whenever needed

reviews.comment: For the most part, this was a simple class, and I did see my Spanish improve! HOWEVER, it was to no help from Professor Steensen. Absolutely horrible experience in her class. I probably would have failed if it wasnt for my prior knowledge from high school. Gives a ridiculous amount of work and is a tough grader. I am not even joking or exaggerating. She asks the class questions, expecting us to know stuff she didn't teach and gets passive aggressive when you don't understand her constant unclear instructions.

Harsh on attendance and speaking grades. Rude and unaccepting of technical difficulties through covid. Docked 2-3 % because 1 min late a few times. Homework Heavy. Recieved 95% on everything but got B+ because my camera didn't work. Will not round up. Assignments in 3 different places and not put on the calendar. Not tech savy. Not organized well.

reviews.comment: THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER. This lady is terrible and super rude. reviews.comment: Her class was super easy for me because I have taken Spanish throughout middle school and high school. For that reason, I found it to be especially boring. Class is super easy for me since I am a fluent spanish speaker, but that doesnt change the fact that you're quiz grades dont get counted if you do not show up to class. The class comes easy to me but I see how rude she is towards others that have very little spanish background.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took her in the midst of COVID for what it's worth, but she's not very understanding or willing to work with you, she really lays on the assignments thick and doesn't post lectures or anything unless the whole class is doing badly, so you teach yourself. She'll answer questions during class but kinda rudely, and the assignments are time-consuming

reviews.comment: I literally would give her 0 stars if I could. She is so rude ALL THE TIME and is constantly correcting people on the smallest things before you even finish your damn sentence. I thought she was honestly kind of rude to a lot of the students in class. I also think that she definitely made the class harder than it was supposed to be.

You have homework due every week but its not too bad.

reviews.comment: Not a very good professor, she's rude and tries to be funny but isn't. Class was awkward and pretty boring. Take another professor if you want an A or B. Had to really work for a C.

reviews.comment: I would recommend her to most people. You are expected to study and come prepared to class, but I feel like she does a good job at teaching, and you can tell she cares about her students success.

reviews.comment: Worst Spanish teacher I've ever had. She's not a native speaker, which I believe makes a huge difference. She's pretty rude about answering questions and clarifying things in general. She doesn't notify you when upcoming assignments are due, and for a low-level Spanish class, she has high expectations. Didn't enjoy her at all.

AU15 was her first time teaching this course at the Cbus campus and she did fairly well. When people ask obvious questions or struggle to grasp easy concepts, she tends to mock them, but she means well. If you need additional help, you should stay after class, rather than asking questions during class. Attendance is huge in 1155.

She seems sweet but is SUCH a harsh grader and will take point off for ANY LITTLE THING. It's like she wants give bad grades, but then complains about the low average. Her handwriting is very difficult to read and she WILL cold call you. She is also very dismissive for questions and will just say "we already went over that" and is lowky petty af.
Writings are hard to read. And she will takes away every single points of the homework just for very little steps. Speak very fast during class, hard to understand.

Had her for calc 2 recitation, not good at teaching and reviewing concepts. Also has handwriting that cannot be read easily. Gives incorrect information for questions on written homework and exams. Seems nice but would not recommend as a teacher.
Had her for 1152 rec, take anyone else! She is so hard to hear and sort of just rambles the whole class. She is also super unfriendly when you get questions wrong, etc.

Absolutely does not deserve the low rating she has. She always chooses helpful topics, reviews past content, and shows useful example problems. She also definitely cares about students; she had learned everyone's name by week 3 (!), is always happy to answer questions, and has a sense of humor. However, she does work through problems very speedily!

Parisa recitations can be boring, but they were so helpful for understanding the content. Might be controversial, but Ioved how she would cold call on students. It made pay attention the entire time. Parisa would also send out extra videos, and all of the notes after class which I really appreciated. Super nice!

She is a terrible teacher. I had her for my Calc 2 recitation and she talks the whole time without engaging the class. She is very confusing and dismissive of questions. Do not take this at all tasks. Her handwriting is too fast and messy. Take anything else.
awful TA, wearing a microphone that has no effect

I ended up dropping the class but for the classes I went to, it sucked. Classes were so boring and she speaks very fast and not clear; very hard to follow along with. She also seems unsure of herself for anything she talks about for the most part, otherwise she seemed sweet. Wouldn't recommend though.

Her "teaching" is just standing at the front of the room, mumbling as she works her way through math problems. She's also incredibly rude. She publicly scolds and shames students when they're wrong. She once incorrectly docked points from my assignment, and tried to bully me out of emailing the professor to fix it. So many more examples, DONT TAKE!
She is a great professor! I enjoyed her class.
Very bad experience with Dr. Field. Difficult to work with and no rhyme or reason to grading. Don't expect any feedback or constructive criticism.
I don't recommend taking any class with this professor - please find anyone else. She is unforgiving and rude to students and unhelpful for student learning.

A very nice person, obviously very passionate about her field. Very knowledgeable and not too strict with grading. A fair amount of work (quizzes, readings, discussion posts, project). Don't bother reading the book if you're going to lectures (however, she wrote the book and gives you access for free!) The only warning is the group project.

I don't understand the negative reviews Dr. Field has. I was so scared of taking this course with her because of the reviews but was surprised by how amazing she is. She is clear about what she wants and has been one of the most amazing professors during the pandemic. The workload is the usual and nothing insanely hard if you read the material.

Reading are from POORLY written online pdf textbook.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fields was a great professor to have. The class lectures can be a bit boring at times, but she is good for a joke every now and then, which kept me awake. The class did not have many assignments (most grades being tests). The test are not too bad as long as you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Field was a great professor.  The class could be a little dry, but she tried to make it interesting and do different sorts of activities.  The tests were easy and she didn't grade any of the assignments particularly hard.  Overall, I would take another class with her.

I personally found the lectures and reading very dry. Maybe because I took this as a GE, I don't know, but I didn't really like the class. I felt the class topics were sometimes a little scattered feeling.

Dr. Field is simply awesome. Not only is she smart, but she is also incredibly organized and overall a pleasant person. She assigns SO MUCH READING THOUGH! Still, I would take another class with her in a heartbeat.
Stay away from him if you value your sanity

The lectures cover an overwhelming amount of material in a very short time, and the structure can be hard to follow, especially for slower learners. Extending lectures to 75–90 minutes (like OSU Newark) instead of 55 would likely help many students better absorb the material and succeed. Dr. Felker clearly puts in effort, and I respect that.

He can often come off as rude and condescending but its fair trade off as he understands that most students hate this course and are only taking it because we need to so he is pretty lenient. But also can be hash grader of hand in homework and tests. Im just happy he didn't try to force me to understand physics when I was never really going to.

Everyone at some point in time will have to ask themselves "do I care about learning the actual content or do I just care about getting a good grade." Dr. Felker is the teacher for those who can admit that they only care about their grade. Spent both labs and recitations on his phone, making it a cake walk to cheat on all quizzes, labs, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: All positive comments about Felker are lying or his alt, because I can't think of a single good thing about his lectures. His notes were awful, incomplete, and wrong. His attitude was bad, every class had horrible cringy jokes and off color comments. He wrote too small and explained nothing. Is he the worst professor I've ever had though? Maybe…

Dr. Felker's actual teaching style was actually quite helpful. He gave many practice problems and review sessions. His quizzes, however, were very hard, and he boasted about how he tried to trick us. His demeanor in class was poor as he was arrogant and did not seem to care about his students success.

Dr.Felker was an okay professor. You have to attend lecture to actually understand some of the more difficult concepts, but overall, he wasn't as bad as people say. The class is hard, but he does a good job in providing extra practice problems. He will prepare you for the final and exams, which tend to have a couple conceptual heavy questions.

Do you enjoy professors who make you cringe, get distracted during lectures, and make inappropriate jokes? Then you'll love him! Every one of his slideshows had at least one error in it. Makes his quiz/exam questions purposefully confusing to trick you (his words, not mine). Worst professor I've ever had.

Felker can be helpful, but you have to ask him the right questions and in the right way. Sometimes he can be lazy when explaining things, so I have had to ask for him to explain a topic a different way or do an actual example problem step by step. He also gets off track very easily during out of class hours, so just try to keep him on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Felker is not the worst professor in the world. He can be at times very unhelpful and genuinely rude. He does care about student success and he does want to help. Felker has a very odd and wannabe edgy sense of humor that does not work very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I learned more from Dr. Felker in the weekly hour long recitations than I did from my lecturer all semester. He genuinely made recitations worth going to, and he interacted with all of the students.

Dr. Felker is a fair lecturer still finding his style. If you attend his office hours, he can be quite helpful in understanding material and going through work, and he genuinely does want feedback and student interaction. His quiz questions can be niche but they are helpful for studying for exams. With time, I see him becoming even better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Felker was by far the worst lecturer I have had at OSU. His lectures and teaching style are unclear and incorporate example problems that are irrelevant to the course. He makes very corny and uncomfortable jokes to try to distract you from the fact that you do not understand the lecture material. I recommend watching youtube videos over lecture.

For the love of all that is holy, if you are taking physics 1201, and you find out you're with this guy, IMMEDIATELY drop the course and find another section or take it another semester. He is by far the worst lecturer I have ever here at OSU. He is condescending, makes unrelated unfunny dry jokes, and gets confused probably 2-3 times PER LECTURE.
Every question feels like a trick. Doesn't help and clearly tries to show he is smarter than everyone else. Avoid him at all costs

He rambles about his ADHD medication every single class (not even kidding) and is really unpleasant, cant read the room and is super edgy for no reason. I will say that he definitely knows what he's talking about and is a decent instructor, but I can't stand his personality.
Horrible experience made my friend cry.

While somewhat hindered by an awful department, Dr. Felker tries to make it better for his students, which is very appreciated. However, he has a tendency to come off as condescending sometimes and it can be discouraging. Overall, I think he'd improve with more experience in the classroom, but he's really not awful compared to some other options.

Not very clear explanations of material. I relied on online resources a lot. Accent isn't the easiest to understand. Doesn't help that she often would have students show work on her iPad despite never showing the work herself, so it's hard to see what the correct way to do things is. Tests were often difficult but similar to the practice tests.
cannot understand her as well as she does not come prepared to exams/classes

Dr. Fang is really nice. She provides lots of practice exams and quizzes beforehand so that you have expectations in mind. She is willing to help during office hours and replies to emails pretty fast. The lectures could have been done better, her accent could be confusing at times. If you are really to self-taught her class would be a good choice.

She is a very kind person, but not for a big lecture hall full of people. She sometimes made people uncomfortable by calling them up to do problems on her iPad in front of the whole class. Her office hour was helpful, though. She would claim that the test was "easy" when, in reality, it wasn't. The quizzes are weighted too much.

Honestly one of the kindest souls you will ever meet. Though it is hard to understand her lecture sometimes, she makes up for it through her office hours. Gives 2% extra credit. She records all lectures and posts all notes. Responds to emails within a couple hours. Loved her a lot and if all profs had her passion the world would be a better place.
Great professor who points out important things in lecture and goes over example problems. Tests and quizzes were very fair and reasonable. Professor cares for students.

Although the lecture is difficult to understand, her office hour helps a lot. Also, the workload is not heavy at all. You will have 4 easy quizzes, 3 midterms and a final. The attendance for lectures and recitations is not mandatory. What you have is an online homework every two weeks.

Very nice and caring professor. Cares for students. Lectures had a lot of proofs and moved very fast, but she posted the notes after class. Not much homework. 3 Exams and 1 25% final exam. Exams were very easy and reasonable.

Honestly, Dr. Fang is a great person, but Calc 3 isn't the best match for her teaching style. Her lectures felt too theoretical for vector calc, so I relied on Pearson videos instead. Recitation wasn't helpful, but she is supportive outside class. If possible, try another prof; if not, use Pearson and tutoring.

She is an incredibly nice person, but her teaching style doesn't lend itself to a large lecture hall. I get it, its hard to teach such a subject to a huge group of students. However, I've taken the class in high school and even I was lost in some hyper-theoretical parts of lectures that had little significance in the grand scheme of things.

It was tough to understand her throughout the entire semester. Much of it was very theoretical and hard to visualize. I relied on teaching myself throughout the semester using Pearson, ChatGPT, and Khan. She loves calling up people to solve problems, and would pick randomly if no one raised their hands. I've heard better things about other profs.
Really nice professor with very chill grading criteria. He really wants students to do well and will help you get there. Interesting topic as well, no complaints.

Overall, it was a pretty easy class. I took it in the first session, so a lot was thrown at me quickly. But overall, very manageable class, there's just a lot of work in the last 2 weeks, but he's pretty lax on the grading.

Professor Fernandes was great! I took this as a full-session class, there were three exams overall, all open-note and very fair. The assignments and content were also enjoyable. It was definitely very chill and an easy A!
Really good professor! You can tell he really cares about his students and the material that he teaches.

I took PS4123 as a Session 1 class and although the turnaround time was short, he was a great professor that made lecture engaging and is very fair with his grading. You get what you put into the class and it's pretty easy to get an A, but he makes sure you learn the material too and encourages active participation (but not in a scary way)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Stay away at all costs you will be happy you did
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Its an easy A Class and workload is pretty manageable for a Gen Ed. Its a Essay a Week and the directions are straight foward, and not too demanding. You learn alot and she clearly cares alot about the subject of Communication. My only real compliant is some of the stuff we learn is sort of Woke and it gets to a point after a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Continuing on from my previous review... when I asked her about the 0's she ignored it and said it is ok to miss a few assignments and get 0's on them you can still pass the class. Like what kind of a response is that so rude and acts like she owns the entire university.

She treats us like we're in 3rd grade. like, we are in college, so why do you assign seats? She also is very rude and does not respond to questions when you email her. I emailed her about a question on an assignment and instead of getting my question answered, I got a rude response. I don't know how she has a teaching degree.

This class is supposed to be a easy 1 credit class, she makes it seem like a 4 credit class with the amount of lecturing and work she assigns us, she takes off points just so students do not get 100. showed her my project before submitting and she had nothing to say to improve it. Just not a good professor, thinks she owns the place and is rude.

I honestly loved this class. If you like writing and want a challenge, I'd take this class. If you're looking to do the bare minimum and get out, I would listen to all the other reviews and not take it. Dr. Foster as a teacher was great! Her lectures were interesting, she wasn't intimidating, and it was easy to set up appointments outside of class.

For this class specifically, she was great! Tried to make the best out of a class that is required for every (transfer) student to take. As for the class, you will be making a portfolio you likely will never use. This requires writing three essays total, of which they are about you academic identity or something.

Dr. Foster was very passionate about learning and making students feel welcome, but she was a very harsh grader on papers. I normally excel in English and writing, but did not get above a B on any paper.

Dr Foster is being review bombed on here and while I feel bad, it's not totally undeserved. Class materials were thrown in with really no care, like someone just put random links on canvas and forgot about them. The TA's are strict, condescending and took points off for no reason. It wasn't hard to get an A, but just a terrible unorganized class.
HELL HELL HELL
YOU WON'T LEARN ANY FROM HER
TREAT NICE TO YOURSELF
DO NOT BE A PERSON LIKE HER
SHE IS IMPOLITE
PLEASE DO NOT TAKE IT
DO NOT TAKE HER COURSE PLEASE
My 4.0 gpa is completely ruined by her
All of these ruined my life
I have nothing to say

While Professor Froster was very nice, she was extremely strict on all grading. As someone who has always excelled in reading and writing, I was never once able to receive a B+ or higher on any graded papers. Moreover, the discussion rules lost me points. Overall, I felt the class was a glorified language arts course and ultimately damaged my gpa.

I took this class for a GE and I am passing with an A. I think this class was super easy and honestly informative. There is a 1-2 page discussion board due every week along with a quiz and its pretty straight forward on what needs to be done. I had extenuating circumstances, and her policy is the 2 lowest grades are dropped, end of discussion.

Melissa Foster has way too much work for an entry-level GE course. A two page paper every week along with a weekly quiz. She purposely covers words with memes in the slides you download so that you are forced to watch lecture bc the info is covered. Pushes way too much of her political agenda on students. TAs grade insanely strict, do not take.

Don't get me wrong Melissa Foster is truly a nice person but in this class you are just another number to the TA graders. There is a required 20 point quiz every week along with a 2 page APA formatted dissucssion post that must have peer reviewed research along with replying to two classmates with additional APA formatted peer reviewed articles.

TAs are incredibly harsh graders. This course requires too much work for an elective. Generally I would stay away from this professor. She is nice and cares about the class, but honestly it is difficult to perform up to TA standards and you are just a number.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you take this class online its very easy as professor Foster would have a discussion paper and quiz due each week which both were very simple to complete. She would drop the 3 lowest scores on your quiz and discussion paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class wasn't terrible. There were weekly discussions based off of the weekly lectures, which were an hour or less, weekly discussions which were counted as exam grades which is really helpful for people who are bad test takers or overly stress about exams drop 3 lowest. Class was easy if you turn in work, never communicated w/ professor

Class wasn't awful, but she was incredibly cold when dealing with me after I had a death in the family and missed a couple assignments. The discussions are long and require some research but they're useful and helped me learn about how to do academic research. Fine course I guess.

Although the assignments are clear and well put together. Professor Foster was incredibly rude in my emails I sent to her. She does not come across as someone who wants to help you in any way. I would avoid taking any of her classes as she does not offer any leniency even when the issue is outside of your control.

Tough grader with unconvincing evaluations. Refuses to provide explanations for her evaluations and decisions as a professor, and deliberately deducted points to prevent students from achieving high grades. Essays that underwent multiple revisions often received the same scores as those that did not, indicating unclear grading criteria. Avoid.

Very easy class to take online and professor Foster gives simple assignments that require you to watch lectures and use them to complete quiz's and weekly dissections. Loved that there was no finals or any midterms and she also drops the three loswt quiz scores and discussions.

She is a very tough grader as most assignments have had an average of around 70-75 (this is a GE theme course). Her feedback is helpful and clear but don't expect an easy A in the class. The weekly tests are also difficult but the weekly discussions (completion grade) are a great grade booster. She's intelligent and passionate about her work!

She treated her 2000 level as a 5000 level class. I'm an okay writer and typically get As on papers, but for the first few assignments in her class, I got Cs. It was irritating how tough her grades were and how she kept saying it was a "high-level writing course" when a 2000 level GE should not be harder than my 3000 and 4000-level major courses.

Professor is stuck up and extremely difficult to deal with. Class is very liberal oriented in the beginning then levels out to a non partisan view. Assignments lack clarity. Rubric is arbitrary. DO NOT email her at all. Quizzes are free 100%. Discussion posts are mini essays. This class is easy if online and if you are a quality writer.

Context, her late policy is clear, no late work, no exceptions. Sent a quick, "Can I retake a quiz", expecting a no, which is fine.

Her response was that I, "may not be accustomed to the current college environment." Just felt very disrespected, if this is how she responds to all requests that are out of her norm, I wouldn't have taken her class.
Very tough grader and rude. I do not recommend this course or professor.
Rude and hardest grader for a GE course

Dr. Foster is an evil. Avoid her. She grades very roughly. I dropped from A to B+ only after the first week! She usually deducts students' points without any reason. 19% of students (38 of 200) dropped Communication 2850 after the first week.
Run! She is a very strict grader. If you do not want a GE course to hurt your GPA, run!

The class is fine overall with easy-to-understand lectures and quizzes that directly come from the lecture videos. There is a two-page discussion post due every week which is a lot for the topics that are assigned for each week. If you do not have a lot of free writing time, I do not recommend taking the course during a busy semester.
evil

Course was easy overall and I ended with an A w/o having to put in too much work. Weekly quizzes are easy if you just skim lecture videos. You have a two pages/ 4 minute video discussion due every two weeks does not take long to complete but she grades them unnecessarily tough. Even if you follow the rubric she'll find places to take off points.
Really nice person, cares about her students. She is a really tough grader, but if you do the work it's really not too much. Easy GE, nice lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was pretty straightforward. It included a weekly quiz, weekly lecture videos, and a 2 page discussion post every 2 weeks. It is a pretty easy class if you do your work, but I noticed the lectures did seem to get a little political.

The discussion posts were graded very hard, without a lot of feedback. I took the asynchronous class, which involved weekly quizzes and about an hour and a half of online lectures each week. She is very open about her political views, which was odd considering the class is supposed to teach us how to be objective when evaluating sources.

For an online asynchronous class, it was more work than my other classes. Quizzes every week which were okay and then writing assignments due every week and the essays are super toughly graded. I didn't really feel like I learned anything and the class was strangely political
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster is a great professor, if you do what you are supposed to do. Most of her courses require a decent amount of writing. However, they are not painfully difficult. Watch the lectures and you will do fine. She answers emails fast and is happy to respond to any questions you may have.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Somehow found a way to incorporate her hatred for Donald Trump into almost every week's lectures and really pushed her liberal views for a class that shouldn't even be political.
Overall watch the lecture videos and you will get an A there is also is also 40 points of extra credit
For a Gen Ed course that was online this class was a lot of work. There are three long lecture videos, a quiz, and a video discussion board due each week, with midterm tests every three weeks.

I hated is how disconnected the professor was. There were weird grading criteria that the TA used to grade my stuff that was not mentioned in the guidelines. She ignored me when I reached out for help. She could not just quickly say, "yes, the TA made a mistake, you're right". TA was unresponsive and continued grading weirdly. Never again.

Lectures were easy to follow with lots of great examples. Her assignments were pretty straight forward; you write an essay (2 pages long), comment on two people's, and take a quiz every week. She even drops your lowest three essay and quiz grades (6 total). As long as you make time to watch her lectures and write these essays, you'll do just fine.

I dont want to say this to be mean but please dont schedule with this professor. Every week there is a quiz which isn't the bad things its the 3 lectures she puts into one and then on the quizzes it was 5 questions and for 25 point so it was very hard to study. Her lectures are very hard to understand the way she talks and all exams are cumulative
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor undeniably pushes a leftist agenda, while completely bashing the right. This class is was more political than it needs to be.
Just stay away from this professor. Does not care about students AT ALL. She grades your papers as if your are supposed to be some super star writer right off the bat

There were weekly papers in this class. However, they were relatively short and I found that I was able to complete them in an hour or two. Weekly opportunities for extra credit, as well as a longer paper that could be done for a lot of extra credit as well. No exams.

She's a very sweet professor, however LOTS of papers with the lowest three getting dropped. Interesting class but would not recommend to someone who struggles writing papers, her prompts are sometimes also very broad but overall a good class.

Assignments are pretty easy as long as you stay on top of them. Lectures are relatively short, but sometimes weren't even necessary to watch as most, not all, information was laid out in lecture slides. Weekly opportunities for extra credit. Very nice as long as you are polite/respectful.

Melissa Foster is one of the best professors I have ever had. Her lectures are easy to follow because she actually cares about the information she is sharing. There are several two-page papers that you have to write throughout the course, but she does this in place of exams. She also drops your 3 lowest essay and quiz scores.

I am honestly very surprised to see so many bad reviews. She cares so much about the class and makes attempts to connect with each student. She is very passionate and knowledgeable on what she teaches, and is genuinely one of the best professors I've had. She is very flexible and makes class fun but starting and ending each with an easy activity.

The homework assigned by this professor is often irregular, with due appearing suddenly. There is no possibility for her homework to be postponed, and the grading standard is very strange. I feel that the grading is also unfair. She doesn't want students to get high marks. I think she's the most difficult professor I've ever had.

I took this course entirely online and it honestly wasn't that bad. The weekly lectures and quizzes can be a pain, but you can tackle them at your own pace. There's also a weekly paper, but they're one page max, so you can pound one out in an hour tops. Professor Foster is witty and tries her best to make her lectures interesting.
Really sweet professor who actually cares about her students.

I took this class for my major and I really enjoyed it. She gives you lots of forgiveness and the assignments are relevant to the content. She is also very personable which can be tough through a screen.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: LOVED taking this online course. No textbook or exams, just watching about 30 minutes of lecture per week, a weekly quiz, and a weekly one-page essay. I needed to take this class as a prereq, and Foster makes the material enjoyable, fun, and easy to work with. She's also fun and cool. STRONGLY recommend... seriously a very very VERY easy A.

Mediocre at best. She sometimes gives clear grading criteria, other times she doesn't and your grade will most likely suffer because of it. Her lectures are pretty dull, quizzes and tests are fairly straightforward. Doesn't really care about the students, just kind of goes through the motions because she has to it feels like. Fairly disappointed.

Dr. Foster released all of the modules for the entire semester from week 1, so you could work ahead at your own pace! The course was pretty interesting and extremely organized. There were no exams, just weekly exam essays that were only one page long. Very well run for an online course.

Melissa Foster is one of the most average professors I have had. She does her best at making the lectures relevant to the current times and tries her best to be funny. That being said, her "lectures" consisted of her reading PowerPoint slides and there are no tests in this class, instead "Exam Questions" as she calls them. Not a terrible professor.
Professor Foster gives great lectures, and. can sometimes be funny. However, she is a very hard grader. You could meet all the. requirements on an assignment and still get a lot of points off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster is an incredible professor. I have taken her for 2 classes at this point. Her lectures are very understandable and her Canadian-ish accent is fun. Her grading is firm but she always provides plenty of feedback prior and after assignments to make sure you are doing the assignment correctly. She is very available and offers extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's a very easy grader. If you miss class, she will give you credit if you finish the work. She's super sweet and very understanding if you miss class. She is also always willing to help you before or after class.

Professor Tiglay is not a bad professor. She is caring and always there to help. She even gives you partial credit on exams if you show work, even if you get the question wrong. However, she makes the grading system very test heavy which could negatively affect your grade pretty strongly. There is also a lot of videos for the lectures. It's okay.

She was very helpful when I actually attended class. Now, at the end of the semester, I didn't go to class for the entire last month and still finished with an A. I did miss points because of attendance, but the way she grades tests with the partial credit allowed me to score high on every test. My class was a hybrid class, so lectures on your own.
Would highly recommend, great at lectures and instructing, though it might depend on how you learn. Personally   I like how she grades exams

Dr. Tiglay was a very kind, and understanding professor. I am not the best source when it comes to her teaching since I had already taken this class in high school, but she was always good at answering questions about problems and being flexible if you had to miss class even though it was mandatory.

Dont take her class. Shes not helpful when you ask questions she just rambles and doesnt answer - exams are so difficult cause of how she grades - notes and lectures are just jumbled and confusing! The final project is so much work but only 16 points. Dont recommend although shes a nice lady.

Lectures are very good, with many examples. I would suggest going to all lectures and reading the book prior to class. Homework is from the book and is optional, but I highly recommend doing it, as test questions look very similar to homework/lecture questions. She is available often for office hours, in fact I would go there as often as I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID AVOID AVOID. Lectures are very unorganized and she completes multiple steps in her head without telling the class why or how to complete certain steps. Does not explain concepts in a manner that is easy to understand. I've been an "A" student all through college math classes until this class. I will be lucky to end with a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The first time I took this class with Rao Vidynath and personally I think she blew him out the water. She gives hw problems from the book that you arent required to do but its a good practice. She tries to give you as much points as possible on exams questions you got wrong. Gave extra credit in my class.

AVOID. I took Dr. Tiglay's class to polish my Calc skills (haven't done Calc since senior year of HS). Everything was a breeze since I took AP Calc, however her Final Exam. Terrible. Class average was a 45%. Highest grade in the class was a 54% with the 15% grade curve. She literally puts new material on the final that you never cover in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: honestly a really good teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS! Although she is a very nice person, she is a horrible teacher. Her notes are all over the place and her example problems are completely different from the questions on the test. She is always confused and when asked a question gets more confused. She awards little to no partial credit and is a very hard grader. Stay Away!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: LISTEN! She is an extremely tough grader and gives little to no partial credit. She does not give very good feedback at all, and when she does, questions were not answered and more were added into the mix. When you have to add A thirty point curve to the final exam you know something went wrong. AVOID AT ALL COSTS! LISTEN TO THIS WEBSITE'S COMMENTS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is  extremely passionate about the courses she teaches. In favor of this professor, she really does care about the student. She makes herself available for the student and takes time out to answer questions about homework. Unfortunately, her teaching style is extremely confusing and her tests are pretty moderate if you study. Good luck!

She always seems very confused. Students had to correct her almost every day. She tries to answer your questions, but does not answer them well. Sometimes she would forget until the end of class to hand out notes after lecture is done. Very unorganized. Does not do well with explaining things. Would not recommend her to anyone.

Awful teacher. messed up multiple times while teaching and had to start all over and had to be corrected by students. seemed confused most of the time and didn't teach in an organized way. went through lectures fast and not very nice.

I agree with a previous review that she's a lenient grader; she was willing to give late credit for very past due assignments. She also takes a while to grade assignments but I wasn't bothered by it. There's a lot of reading, so it's very easy to fall behind. If you put in the time and effort, it's not hard to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The course had a lot of reading, but the writing assignments were pretty easy. There were only two actual essays, the rest being more opinions-based writings. Lectures can feel long, but she's very passionate about the material. She's also a pretty lenient grader, as long as you put in some effort.
Pretty easy class, and Fukumori sensei is a great teacher who makes class interesting.

Fukumori Sensei is really nice, and she offers a lot of extra credit, but it wasn't until the week before finals when she finally graded the FIRST paper. I went the entire semester not knowing my grade. The course is easy enough, but the lack of grading really soured the experience for me.
Really interesting courses, recommend for your guys to take!!
One of the best professors at the Ohio State. She knows her teaching material very well and cares about students' feelings. A really nice person.

Had her for Ancient Kyoto. She loves the material she teaches and it shows in her lectures. She does her best to make class interesting and enjoyable. She was the highlight to a very dull semester. I would happily recommend her to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a great teacher who covers some difficult material but in the end it's not very hard to get a good grade.  She's helpful and a pleasure to talk to , and her tests are pretty straightforward with plenty of opportunities for extra credit.  I'm definitely taking her again.

Professor Fukumori is endearing and pleasant, but this course was exceedingly boring. She tries so hard, but the subject matter is just not interesting (unless you love women's studies). Also, she needs to go to a speech class; the number of uhs, ums, and likes was distracting bordering on absurd. Easy A, but do not recommend.
The class puts me to sleep but the material is interesting enough and has easy assignments and quizzes.  YES.  AND she has powerpoints so you can follow along exactly.  Awesome.
Great teacher. Easy and fun class
Goes out of her way to help you.
Awesome
GREAT
Fast Shipping and product was just as described. A+++++ ebayer, will do business agian! errr.... i ment good teacher, nice lady
No Comments
As long as you do the reading, this class is a walk in the park.  The quizzes aren't hard, the writings are only 3 pages each, and only two papers per quarter.  There is also extra credit.  Easy A.
Very helpful.

This class was not challenging. I would be amazed if the class average was lower than a 3.5. If you come to class, you don't have to do any of the reading. Even though it is not challenging, you will learn about culture and literature the entire term. It is probably the most worthwhile class at OSU.
No Comments

She was definitly an amazing professor. she is very interested in her material which made the class more interesting. Yes, there is alot of reading, but she made notes for us everyday and told us exactly what was on the tests. they were extremely easy if you went to class.She was very helpful with papers, and an easy grader. take her if you can!!
No Comments
very hard and boring class
She was nice, really helpful and made the class very interesting.
Extremely helpful, one of the nicest professors on campus.  Be warned that her classes usually involve a lot of reading, but it's worth it!
Phenomenal teacher, but she makes you work hard and constantly keeps you on your toes. But well worth the effort, I left her class with more knowledge.
great instructor ! willing to help student understand the material
enjoyable
Very sociable, workable and makes class interesting.

I think many people will see the score he has and worry, but genuinely he has a great passion for teaching the subject and in my opinion is very good at it and gives great examples to help you understand the topics in this course. He's very personable as well and is very open to talking with his students after class and during his office hours too

While Ken has a certain... attitude when teaching, he is actually good at it. His lectures can be a little confusing, however, he is always willing to help in office hours. This class is hard, but is doable if you really put in effort and stay on top of the material. The exams are fair enough for the most part, however the homework is very long.

Tough Class for Sure. However, if you stay on top of the homework and go to every lecture, you should be just fine. If you have questions, make sure to go to either his office hours or the TA's office hours. They are very helpful. Finally, try to make friends and study together for this class. It is tough going through this class alone.

Honestly the tests are fair but the class lay out is extremely fast-paced and unforgiving. He continuingly calls people out in class and if you ask a question prepare for him to make you feel stupid for asking.

Lectures were very fast and sometimes difficult to understand. Midterms were easy in the first half of the class and the harder midterms get curved. The homework was often super complex and was so much harder than the exams that it felt like busy work.

Although he's really lenient with attendance, I would recommend sitting in as many lectures as possible because he makes everything really interesting and easy to understand.

reviews.comment: This class was co taught by three prof, and all of them contributed positively to the learning experience. Dr. Kim's strengths were in clear explanation and thoughtful feedback. Both in and outside of class, he provided detailed explanations of supplementary and beyond class materials, and always took the time to answer questions thoroughly.

Professor Kim is a fun and engaging instructor. Even though the class discusses in depth topics, he brings many sources that help us understand the ideas clearly. He is also very supportive outside of class and shared helpful advice about career paths. Sometimes we even had class outside on a bench, which made the course memorable.

I really enjoyed this class! Lectures were fun bc Prof Kim is funny plus the information is interesting. Quizzes/tests were a bit hard to study for since I never know what to focus on so focus on everything :( & try not to miss class bc you'll miss info that u could be tested on. overall good class.
Funny professor who makes learning Korean fun and simple

Dr. Kim's Elements of Korean Culture class was engaging and enriching. I learned so much about Korean history and culture. Though the workload seemed heavy at first, Dr. Kim was considerate with extensions and gave exceptional feedback on every essay, helping us improve our writing. A truly valuable course!

Professor Kim is a great instructor — he's informative, goes into more depth about complex grammar, and is proactive about answering questions. He's also really funny at times. However, his ACT classes are nerve-wracking. He isn't mean or anything, but he'll put you on the spot and doesn't really offer any help as you struggle to answer something.

Kim ssn is one of the few (Korean class) professors that truly cares about their students learning progress. Get ready to be challenged at his act classes! However, he is very helpful outside of the class. My advice is to ask him to explain grammar to you after class because the way he explains is very easy and clear.

Really good professor. Out of the four professor we had for this course, he was easily my favorite. Humorous, but makes sure you are learning while also being just a really personable guy. Homework isn't too bad, considering it's a language course and requires consistent study. Lenient grader.

Mr. Kim was an enjoyable professor-while maybe a little strict at times. He wanted his students to truly understand and embrace the concept of learning the Korean language. He is also a very humorous instructor and good at communicating answers. I really enjoyed having a class with him.

He is very funny guy. Love teaching his student i think...... He speaks korean with Busan dialect which is funny but he tries very hard to speak normally which is very good. I hope other student enjoy his class since it is very interesting and interactive.

Han Gil is a funny guy who cares about his students learning Korean. Like really, really cares. He sometimes grades a little harsh and is sometimes intimidating, but all in all, he's a good teacher. Also, if you get on his bad side, he might roast you in front of the class for not having a girlfriend.

Took his class at UofT; Professor Zheng is one of the kindest professors I've had over the past four years. He's genuinely caring and wants his students to succeed, which reflects in each of his actions. Plus, his class is super interesting and I actually wanted/liked the class discussions. Deffo recommend him :)

Prof. Zheng is such a sweet guy, def one of my fav profs at UoFT now:)) The readings can be annoying at times, but the class discussions that we had for them made them more interesting. He is also super approachable and very lenient as a marker. I definitely would recommend everyone to take a class with him!!!!!!!!
Prof. Zheng made the topic interesting and less intimidating than I imagined. He's so accommodating and nice I would recommend everyone to take a class with him :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's the nicest Prof. out there at UofT. Keep this angel safe.
