The review sessions were not helpful because they weren't structured, he only took student questions. Lots of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: 90% of grade is 3 exams, other 10% is "reflections" throughout the semester (on the first day he tells you when all the reflections will be). Lectures aren't too bad- he has a lot of hands one experience that keeps it somewhat interesting. Tests can be very tough unless you know the right way to study (which he tells you on the first day).
His classes feel about 2x longer than they actually are. He tells the same story at least 4 times. I don't know if I've taken a more boring class with a more boring professor.

Professor Inks is great. He really cares about his students and will help you if need be. Tests are pretty easy if you find the secret to them. I'm glad I had two classes with him in my college career. Great teacher and a great guy.

Dr. Inks makes an otherwise dry subject very interesting. He has great stories and life experience and weaves these seamlessly into his passion for teaching. Class is fairly easy - know the PPTs and bold terms in the book and you will get an A.

There are only three test that account for 90% of your grade. The class is pure memorization. The lectures are boring, but he tries to make them less boring. Only need the book to memorizes vocab words. Even though class is boring just go to class a pay attention and don't read the book until two days before test to look at vocab words

Inks was a great professor.   Lectures were engaging and he has a lot of real-world experience.  Textbook is necessary, but all you really need to do is know the vocab terms in the readings.   Download the powerpoints, go to lecture, take notes, and read the vocab terms, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class brings a whole new meaning to the word "boring." 3 non-cumulative exams, each covering about 7,000 slides with novels of useless information on every single one.  Asks the most specific questions possible on exams. Over emphasizes the importance of each subject in class, when in reality I'm sure he knows it is all useless. Stay far away
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: An amazing professor who really cares about his students. If you have any problems, absolutely go see him and you'll understand. Cannot recommend him enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Inks is the single best professor I have ever had. It is extremely obvious that he truly cares about his students. He wants his students to take away real world knowledge, not just answers for his exams. If you put forward decent effort, it is not difficult to earn at least a solid B  or higher in his class. Highly recommended.

A very intelligent guy.  I learned more practical and useful information in this class than I have in any other Business GE Course.  His tests are tough and I studied an average of 8-10 hours for them and got an A in the class.  They are pure memorization from his slides and the definitions in the textbooks.

Dr. Inks my absolute favorite professor at OSU.  I had him for 3200 and 4324.  He is extremely knowledgeable (real world application, not just the textbook stuff).   He genuinely cares about his students and teaches you for life, not just for the course.  Exams are tough (multiple choice though), but if you prepare you'll be just fine.
Awesome person

Class is pretty tough especially since almost no one in the class is an HR major. Inks is a cool guy but lectures are boring and the readings are very long. HR stuff seems like common sense, but exams are a little tough.

Overall this class really teaches you what its supposed to, and he makes a boring topic as interesting as possible. There is no homework or anything except three mandatory days you have in class assignments. The only problem with this class is the exams are a bit difficult. But if you do all the readings you can get a decent grade.

Fantastic professor and you will get a lot from this class if you are even somewhat interested in it, so fantastic for HR majors.  As mentioned, has 3 exams 100 points each and 3 pre-announced, easy in-class exercises for 5 points each.  For exams, just know the key concepts study guide and bolded terms in the book and you'll do well.

cool guy but the test are ridiculously hard, he forgets most of us aren't HR majors. Strict memorization all multiple choice, very annoying and overly complicated class. You have to remember a lot of arbitrary charts and diagrams, it would be much better with written tests.

Larry is an awesome guy, but his lectures barely cover test material. His tests are really tough. If you are an HR major I highly recommend taking this class with him because he would be a great resource for life, otherwise I would take this course with another professor where it will be much easier.

Great professor overall. You don't have to show up for lectures or buy the books but of course your grade would be better if you did. He is very clear in lecture and entertaining to listen to. There are 5 mandatory days; 2 test days and 3 "classwork" days.

Tests are very difficult. Everything sounds so obvious in class then the exams are so detailed. Good guy, terrible professor. I'd go to him with questions in real life HR, but he doesn't get that most of us aren't majors in HR. Way too hard for what it should be.
He makes easy material sound difficult.  All memorization and tests are hard.  Hardest Prof for HR

This is a very hard class, don't get me wrong, but Dr. Inks is the best professor I've had at Fisher. Always willing to meet with students and is very interesting to talk to. He is a useful source to find out how corporate HR departments work and what they want in a employee when you are looking for an internship or job.
Hardest professor in Fisher. Avoid him if you can. His exams are extremely hard.

I dont know what everyone is talking about. If you go to class and read the text book you can easily get a good grade in the class. Lots of memorization but he doesn't get to tricky on the exams. You either will know the material or wont.

Pretty much everything that needs to be said has been said. He's a great lecturer, very engaging. Quite a decent person, approachable and willing to help students. Just be prepared for a lot of memorization, some exam questions come directly from the book which I didn't buy, but I still got through. Not a bad class overall, go Larry!

If you have a high gpa, take this class in your last semester because the grade you earn won't be factored into latin honors. This class is abhorrent to the ideals of higher education - pure memorization of pp slides and textbook definitions that are not applicable to the real world, unless you're majoring in hr...

I took this class as a distance learning class from the Newark campus. Dr. Inks is a excellent instructor and really cares about helping his students understand and apply the material.To get an A, you have to do well with the take-aways, memorize ALL of the slides, and know the definitions from the book. This was a great class!

He is a great professor and keeps the class engaged during lectures. His tests are pure memorization from the lecture notes. The only reason you need the textbook is for the vocabulary terms, which he will ask about on the exam. There are opportunities to earn extra credit. Go to class because he will ask questions on the exam straight from lecture
Great teacher, but tough class. Read the book!!! The exam is all memorization, which is difficult to do with how boring some of this material is. But larry does a great job in lecture

He is a hot silver fox that is genuinely interested in helping students. 3 exams based on memorizing charts and highlighted terms in the textbooks as well as 3 "takeways" which he tells you the dates of ahead of time. They are easy opinion questions. There is no reason to not do well, the notes are online and we had the chance to get extra credit.

unnecessary make the class hard.dont take it if u don't need to.exams are hard and tricky...professor is nice and helpful but the class is all memorization.So,if u can memorize A to Z than its worth taking otherwise not.watch out for the 2nd exam.

Larry is the best prof I have had yet at this school.  He made me want to attend lecture and he is really knowledgable.  Down to Earth guy that shows clips and things that keeps students interested.  His tests ar not easy by any means.  Must know the material very well to get an A

There's a few things to know about this class. for one, larry is a good guy. however, his tests are utterly pointless. in most classes you can learn the material and be fine for a test. with him, it's all memorization. you have to memorize the 5 points of a start in clockwise order... come on larry. plus, his jokes are rehearsed (dr. fear)

Dr. Inks is a good teacher.  He teaches you a lot of useful information that is helpful for interviewing and working.  However, his tests are very hard.  It's pretty much all memorization for 3 50 question tests.  So if you can memorize everything you read and he says, then you're good.  Not the easiest.

Basically the best teacher I have ever had. Makes the two hour class go by very fast and is very engaging. Never once fell asleep in class, he keeps you awake the whole time. Only reason you need the book is for the bold definition terms.. which is awesome. Tests aren't too bad if you attend class.
easy class if youre good at memorizing a lot of information, but he is a great teacher. the material is fairly boring, but he made it interesting. would recommend and would take again if possible

This is a class of memorizing other's opinions. Do NOT take it as a class you don't need to study for--it will not work out well for you. We received a total of 8 bonus points and a 1% curve, but just make sure you don't blow it off.

Dr Inks is basically THE MAN. If you approach this is just another requirement you'll dislike it, but if you just give it a shot and consider the implications of what you're studying and what he says, you'll be so much better for it. He's a great teacher, really surprised me. Take this with him.

3 (multiple choice) non-cumulative exams make up your grade. Really friendly, funny, and helpful (if you go to office hours). Course is easy if you read the 2 textbooks, and memorize lecture slides. Easy B or A-, really has to work for an A.

Redundant course. Not really practical. Basically a test of "how good is your memory?". Tonnes of material, out-of-the-book questions on exam, little focus on real issues. Exams are hard, material is easy relatively.

There's not a ton of material in this class. Inks enjoys talking about his experiences in business rather than the general theories listed in the text. Most of the material is something we'll have to experience rather than memorize, so I found the class pretty squishy and worthless. HR701's better title is "The Life of Larry Inks"
Dr. Inks is a great teacher.  His lectures are very helpful for once you graduate school.  Know the powerpoints and the definitions from the book and you should at least get a B.

one of the best professors i had in FCOB, makes class interesting , shows clips and movies, loves teaching , and is very easy to talk to. just dont be an idiot , pay attention and try to apply some of it to your own life. thats all he is asking. great class. but imo way too many models.
Larry Inks is the man! One of the coolest professors in the entire Fisher College. Great outside of class and pretty effective inside the classroom as well.

If I was new to a firm and Dr. Inks was my boss, I would stay as long as possible!  An excellent professor, he made an 8:30 AM lecture much easier to get through.  In my own opinion (Larry, I know you're reading this and disagree), a lot of the material is common sense broken down into models.  Nonetheless, this stuff is very important to know

Absolutely love him!! He covered a lot of materials in class and some of the topics weren't that exciting, but Larry made things much better. Extremely willing to help and want students to do well. Easy to get A-, hard to get A.

The material for this class was sometimes interesting, and sometimes really boring.  Fortunately, Inks knows this and does a very good job keeping things moving at a good pace.  Mixes things up by showing us some good videos.  I would recommend both going to class, and doing the reading.  I slacked on both a bit and got an A- in this easy class.

Great! Would recommend to anyone! Very clear, knowledgeable, willing to help when asked. Never makes anyone feel stupid. Keeps lectures interesting with clips and great examples! Really seems to enjoy teaching!

Awesome Professor!! His lectures are far from boring and he shows tons of clips from The Office & movies to keep you interested. He is very funny too! He sticks to his lectures when it comes to tests. 3 tests worth 100 each and 3 "takeaways" worth 5 each. Go to class and you'll be just fine for the tests!! EASY A and Dr Inks is such a cool guy!
Awesome, knows what I need.  Easy....yet hard.

Larry will show you clips from various tv shows, documentaries and movies that are super entertaining. He is always to the point and his tangents almost relate back to the topic at hand. He is as nice out of class as he is in class. You will fly through this class with Larry.

He is a bit in your face at first, but he is awesome. Knows how to engage students and his course is very interesting and helpful. Get to know him on a personal basis; he can give great advice on interviewing, salary negotiation, internship/job search, etc. Definitely a top 3 professor Ive had at OSU.
Made class entertaining. One of if not the best professor I've had. I really enjoyed the class.

I genuinely enjoyed each of his classes.  One of my favorite professors at Fisher so far.  Asked for a lot of participation & introspection, making the class take on a more personal feel.  Showed clips from movies/TV shows almost every class.  Easy exams & takeaways.  "If you're going to be here, be here.  Use your computer for notes and not IMs."

Extremely interesting professor.  He's able to relate topics to his real world experience and also pop culture to keep people interested.  He's by far the best lecture professor I had and would highly recommend him.

I think this class is harder than people give it credit for. Still, he is a fantastic educator - best teacher I've had for a giant lecture class, that's for sure. He's pretty funny and engaging. Also, he's very helpful in office hours and willing to talk to you about random career stuff (interview advice, salary negotiations, etc.)
Best Professor I've had in college.  If he is teaching a course I suggest you schedule it.

Dr. Inks is a great professor.  He really enjoys teaching, which with the material as boring as it is, helps in the class. Very willing to help students, wants them to succeed.  He figures out his own grading scale, which is nice, because it's based on the class performance.  Would recommend getting the books, he does have exam Q's from them.
Very funny. Kept class entertaining.

This guy can be pretty boring. The material is easy, but you have to go to class and read the book. I have to force myself to stay awake every day and there are only 3 multiple choice exams with options A-E. The questions can be tricky. He means well and tries to keep you engaged and also shows a lot of video clips.

Dr. Inks is by far the best professor I've had at OSU.  He is a great teacher who genuinely cares about his students and has a terrific personality as well.  He is a lot of fun and attempts to make even the most boring of topics interesting.  His breadth of experience and wealth of knowledge regarding OB also shines through in his lectures.

The best professor I have had at Fisher! He gets you engaged in class, and he uses "real world" examples that help you understand and remember concepts. I never read the book and ended up with an A.  Just study his lecture notes, and make sure you write down details mentioned in class. He also plays funny clips from the Office in class :0)

Dr. Inks is a genius! He really knows how to teach boring stuff in a fun way. I had no interest in HR before taking his class, but now I am acutually thinking to change my major to HR. He is also a very nice person and cares about his students a lot. His exams are all multiple choices and easy. Go to every lecture to receive "giveaway pts."
Best teacher I have had at Fisher. He actually cares more about the students than the pay check unlike most teachers here.
definitely a great professor. highly recommend taking his class if you want to learn in a fun and entertaining way.
probably the best prof ive had.  makes boring material interesting, shows funny movie clips.  only terms in bold from book are on test.  great review sheet

Awesome Prof...Interesting lectures...Uses humor...Funny guy...Exams are not too bad if you read the material and attend lectures...I like his use of movie clips relating to topics...Has experience...One of the best at Fisher

Great professor.  Keeps class interesting with movie clips.  However, I found the exams to be rather hard.  I studied his review sheet and knew it front and back but was only able to pull off a B in the class.  Make sure you understand concepts. However, I do feel that it would be hard to get any grade lower than a C unless you didn't try at all.
Very professional, dedicated and inspirational in his delivery!

Great professor, is a very good person to get to know for future reference.  He has lots of experience.  Communicates class topics well.  Tests are not very difficult.  Go to class!  Study the review sheet.  averages were around 80% .  He makes class very fun, is great teacher
This class was so easy, it was boring. Inks was great though. He tried to make it interesting and relevant. Take this class when you're a senior, because you won't have to put much effort into it.
Best teacher I've had at OSU hands down...e'nuff said
I LOVE THIS MAN!!! Best professor by far. He didn't even apply for the job, he's a businessman.. Fisher college just asked him to teach because they know how awsome he is!!! TAKE HIS CLASS!!

Tries hard to keep the class interested by using video and asking questions, does very well at it I thought.  Uses "The Office" clips a lot, giving a nice break during lectures , but they aren't that neccessary due to the fact that he is one of the best speakers/lecturerers I've had at OSU.

Really nice guy.  He keeps the class interesting by showing video clips from TV shows and movies.  Attendence is taken 5 times throughout the quarter as "takeaways" which count towards your final grade.  Prof. Inks has a very nice grading scale, in which he averages the top 5 scores in the class and that score becomes the new 100%.  Recommended.
Great Professor!  He's clear, concise, fair, and interesting.  The only negative aspect of the class was the length.  He mostly goes the whole time every day.
By far the best professor I have ever had.  He is so interesting and knowledgable- you will learn a ton of stuff that you can actually use in real life.  Pretty easy to get an A too!

Easy A, however attendance is required, don't bother buying the book I didn't open it once and still got an A, Just Study his study sheet because everything you need to know is on that, highly recommend. Also generous curve at the end even though you wont need it

GO TO CLASS.  Kind of a Napolean like guy, every question on the test starts with "As discussed in class", has to have the reassurence that people are actaully paying attention.  Super nice, but you just want to hit him after the test.
this class is really easy, and its actually pretty interesting for the most part.  just go to class and look over the notes.

Read the book for a while then realized that the exams are straight from the powerpoint slides.  Go to class though!

Quality professor!  Study his lecture notes and you will do great!  He goes straight off of those notes!  One of the best profs I have had here!  Funny guy too with a lot of movie clips!  This is what a professor should be like so take Inks if you can!  Go to class and study his lectures and you will get an A!
No Comments

Class was horrible, but it was spring quarter so def didnt want to be there in the first place. He is def willing to help. Dont take things as common sense and make sure you read and know the termonology well.

Very good prof always willing to help. Definatly a class worth taking with him. Does the best he can with the material and brings in video's and real world examples.

I thought the exams were extremely easy and required very little studying. Even though he tends to keep you the whole time, he definitely isn't monotone and he does produce a lot of interesting facts and examples (ie movie clips), which does help getting through the class.

Very exciting class-love the content & presentation! Nice to have different formats (lecture/charts/video/radio)to break up 1-3/4 hrs. Nice try at interacting/students (7:30PM?). Tests are easy if you study his notes, which he puts on-line. Class is incredibly boring...he will keep you the entire time NOT MATTER WHAT
god he's boring... keeps you every frikken minute of class... even when he tries to let us out early. his exams suck too

Really nice guy! He's similar to Marc Smith, in a good way (maybe less intimidating) because you actually LEARN the material with him. Yes he makes you participate and cold calls on you, but it's not in a massive lecture hall and he's easy to talk to. As I said, he's just a less intimidating Marc smith, so take that as you will

This is the best professor I've had at OSU. He has a genuine interest in getting to know all of his students, which wasn't something I was used to. He wants everyone to do well, even if it seems like there's tougher participation requirements. I feel lucky to have gotten to learn from him. He's an experienced, entertaining, and hilarious guy.
He's the best professor I've had in fisher.

It's a hard class and you have to pay attention to succeed, but Irvine makes it so entertaining! Take advantage of any help he gives and do the readings before class and you'll be fine. Tests aren't cumulative but they are situational not definitions and 70% of your grade, so make sure to study.

reviews.comment: Professor Irvine is one of my favorite professors I have had at Fisher. It is evident that he really cares about his students and wants them to learn. reviews.comment: Really funny guy who always makes the mandatory lectures entertaining- all information needed for the exams are on the slides, just make sure you do the textbook readings beforehand. I got a cheat sheet to use for both exams so if you review well before the tests and go over concepts, you should be good.
Amazing lecturer, amazing person, and amazing sense of humor. Best teacher I've had.

Easily my favorite professor at OSU. Yes, attendance is mandatory, but he makes lecture lively and engaging. Yes, he cold calls on you, but you can simply just pass. Yes, you have to read every night, but it's literally 15 min, grow up. And yes his exams are hard, but you get a full cheat sheet. He cares, he's funny, he knows what he's doing.

Professor Irvine is a fantastic professor with lots of experience and expertise on the subject he teaches. My biggest piece of advice is to sit front row the first day of class. The more you actively participate and engage in class (which he makes very easy and fun), the easier this class will be. Take general notes of the reading before class.

Irvine is kind of goated. Dude had memes from 2010 in his slides and was funny as hell. If I was old enough I'd sit back and crack open a cold one with that man. I will ask him to be my firstborn's godfather.

Was not looking forward to this class and I have never liked law, but professor Irvine made it so enjoyable. He does cold call, but its okay and it's genuinely is because he wants you to learn. You basically work through real example cases in lecture to make it make sense. I would recommend and really enjoyed this class overall!

Professor Irvine is passionate but the class is challenging. Lots of textbook reading and participation required. Use unstuck study to supplement your studies - it really helped me prepare for the tough exams.

Great professor who tries to get everyone engaged. The exams are really difficult and it can be easy to fall behind because the class is a session class. I hope they can change the class to semester long because there is just way too much material to cover in half a semester.

Professor Irvine is the best professor I've had at OSU. He makes the law interesting and genuinely cares about his students' success. The class is not easy and there is a lot of reading, and he expects you to come to class prepared and participate. If you put in the work, you will do well and you won't regret taking this course with this professor.

Professor Irvine was one of my favorite professors this semester! His class took a minute for me to get used to, but once you get in a good habit of reading the textbook, it's super easy to maintain. If you do the readings, the cold-calling isn't bad at all. I found the class super interesting and learned a lot! Exams were difficult, but fair.

Professor Irvine is one of the best professors I've had at Ohio State. The classes are structured well—reading beforehand and cold-calling/participation while he teaches the content. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Irvine definitely takes a minute to get used to. He is a really caring guy who cares deeply about the topic and makes the class interesting. Professor Irvine genuinely cares about his students. The class is not easy, involves a lot of textbook reading and participation in class (he will call on you) but if you show up and put in the work you will be fine. He is very passionate about the material and makes the class interesting!

Professor Irvine is the best! He made 8 am lectures actually interesting and genuinely wanted to engage his students and teach them what he knows. This class is definitely one of the harder classes I have taken in Fisher. Do NOT skip the readings or lectures. The cold calling is not as bad as it sounds. Professor Irvine is a very genuine guy. Professor Irvine is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He makes the potentially boring subject of law interesting. Very smart man; extremely knowledgable about his subject. Makes law somewhat interesting. Lots of reading and he cold calls you in class. Exams are very tough (the final was 81 questions in 80 minutes) but he gives a fair curve. If you do the readings and show up to class you will do decent.

reviews.comment: Truly an awesome professor. He is certainly knows the material like no other. Its a 7 weeks course so you have to read, read, read, it is a must in order to pass. He has pop quizzes and grades for attendance/participation so it is important to be at class. Midterm and Final can be tricky if you do not study, take notes while reading. He curves well

Professor Irvine makes a pretty dry class worth going to.  He is an extremely funny guy and his lectures are awesome. Exams were tough but not impossible, and he gives a very fair curve.

reviews.comment: This was not an easy class by any stretch, but Prof Irvine makes it enjoyable. You should have fun during class. The work outside of class sucks - a lot of reading and you will struggle if you do not do the readings. Exams can be really specific. I got a B by participating, doing the hw, and getting low  70s on the exams.

Prof. Irvine is the best professor at Fisher. I had him for 3500 and enjoyed the class so much I took 4510 as an elective (Finance). Do the reading (tons of reading), take good notes on the reading, participate in class, and you will do just fine. Be professional. He will make you work hard for an A. This is how college is supposed to be taught.
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Get ready to read--Respected by students

reviews.comment: Dr. Irvine is one of the best and most meaningful professors within Fisher. All of his lectures were engaging (since he calls on people randomly, which forces you to pay attention). The class is definitely hard though, and there are substantial readings every night. Exams have huge weight.

Second round with Joe. Do the readings, come to class, and pay attention. He expects you to prepare for each class like a professional, and there is a lot of reading in this class. However, he is also fun, really engages with his students, and makes a boring subject like law pretty manageable. He is a great professor, but the class is not easy

Very intelligent, funny professor. He blasts music before class. Make SURE you do the reading, he will randomly call on people and gives pop quizzes. Offers case studies for EC. Make sure to raise your hand and talk in class for participation. He starts the day off with a joke so have one ready! One of my fave profs, although he is very strict.

Calls on you randomly and knowing the answer is a smal part of your grade so it makes class very stressful. Make sure you have read the chapter for class always and know the material. Doing this really sets you up for exams though in exchange. Also pop quizzes can hurt you when they came up if you aren't ready. Exams are somewhat difficult to.

Irvine was by far the most student friendly teacher I have had here at OSU. He is extremely knowledgable, very nice, funny and is a great teacher. Yes, you have to read a lot because he will randomly call on students but he makes the class very interesting.
Irvine is the best professor I've ever had. You won't regret four years of collage after taking his class! Lectures are amazing and what he teaches is very useful in daily life.
The final was much harder and more specific than the midterm. He is a nice guy but this class takes a lot of work and reading before you go into class

Fun class, but it was really hard. Offers a decent size curve of about 7-10%. Have to  go to class because give pop quizzes and he takes attendance. Only one midterm worth 35% of your grade and final is worth 45% of your grade the rest is homework and pop quizzes. Need the book and come to class prepared bc he calls on people randomly.

This professor tried to make class fun. He is a pretty cool guy. Always blasts music before class, and sometimes will give a quiz. If you read and go to class, you will easily get a good grade. He doesn't require attendance, but he takes participation grade.

You have to work hard to earn an A. Keep up with him in class, try to participate as much as you can. Especially for international students like me, because he speaks really fast. So do the reading, go to class, raise your hand, and that's it.

Irvine is a great teacher overall. He is hilarious in class to help keep you engaged, makes law somewhat fun! Make sure to do the reading, show up everyday, and answer some questions in class to get participation points and you will do well. There is a curve at the end with optional bonus credit available.

Class was a lot of fun.  He always blasts music before and after class, and his lectures are extremely engaging.  He WILL call on you at random, so make sure you've read the material.  Exams aren't easy, but if you've put time into reading the book well and taking good notes, you should do fine.  I HIGHLY RECOMMEND TAKING DETAILED NOTES.

Best Professor I've ever had.  Guy is a Dude! Hilarious. Phenomenal Teaching Style. Lectures fly by because he keeps you so engaged. Plays music before class and gets you HYPED for Law. Read the book, highlight stuff, take notes, do the homework, and you'll be fine. Only class in my life I've ever looked forward to going to. Irvine for President.
Irvine is the man. Makes lectures interesting and fun. I can honestly say I enjoyed going to class. Get ready to read though

Irvine is great. The class isn't easy, but it could be if you put the work i and really try to learn the information. I feel like I have taken a great deal from this course and he is my favorite professor so far at Fisher. He is hilarious and truly cares about his students. Absolutely recommend.
GREAT-Must take him

The exams are tough but if you do all the reading and attend class you will be fine. He is a fantastic professor that really cares about his students and is very knowledgeable about the material. He made class very enjoyable and unlike most classes I've taken, I feel like I actually learned something and retained the information.

Test are really tough. You have to read so much. You cover 20 chapters for a 7 week course which is ridiculous. There are homeworks due before each class. I participated a lot every class and still did not get full participation points. Teaches the material well but the test questions are 10 times harder than the information you learn

Irvine is a great teacher and is very passionate about law. You must read the book and be prepared for class because he WILL call on you to answer questions. This was a very hard class and his exams are extremely difficult. He takes attendance every day and 30% of your grade is based on participationHW & quizzes. Banking on the curve to get a C.

Prof Irvine is passionate about what he teaches and will turn a seemingly boring lecture into a funny and engaging experience (that is if you did the reading, otherwise you can barely contribute).  Must read and must go to class if you want to pass.  Couldn't imagine taking this course with any other professor.

HE's a really good dude. Makes Business Law, a normally boring topic, interesting and fun. You have to keep up on reading because he calls on students at random, but I don't think anyone minded because his lectures were so engaging.
The best professor I've had in Fisher. Reading every chapter is crucial. Substantial curve at the end.

He really makes a boring subject as fun as it could be!!I love his personality as a person. One thing to note is that you will definitely be called to answer questions so be prepared. As a professor, he's kind of strict during the semester, but curves up two letter grades in the end.
Fun prof, tests are kind of hard. Reading was a lot and very hard for a 7week class.

He's truly invested in making learning an interactive experience. While the subject is boring, he does a very good job of keeping the class interesting. Very good sense of humor, come prepared with lawyer jokes.
He is really NOT a good teacher!!!Never reply emails!!Everything is hard.Worst teacher I have ever seen
Good teacher, boring subject. He does a good job to keep it entertaining. Fair difficulty class, be sure to stay on top of the reading and attendance is mandatory

Professor Irvine is one of my favorite professors during my studies at OSU and definitely my favorite from inside Fisher. You may think that law is boring but he will find ways to make discussions interesting. Class attendance mandatory; tests are fairly hard but he gives a decent curve at the end of everything.

By far the best professor I've had in my 4+ years at Ohio State. Truly cares about the material and loves his students. He made this class fun for me, which I did not expect at all for a law class. Make sure you read because he does ask questions and will have random quizzes if multiple people don't know answers to his questions.
You have to take Irvine for 3500.  He is engaging and truly cares about his students.  Make sure you read though (He randomly questions people). But if you read, you will do fine on his tests.

Great class! Basically the same format as 3500. Far class. Like everyone is saying, an amazing teacher that makes law very interesting. I feel like I can truly apply the information learned to everyday life.
He is amazing! Very interested in student's success. This class isn't easy or hard, very fair. Make sure you read all the assigned readings! Probably the best class I've taken at Fisher so far.
Law made into a fun class! Yes it exists! Challenging during lecture, but exams are fair! Take him!

This was the best professor I've had at Ohio State. He is clear about the information that is important, which makes the tests easier. Class is generally laid back, but attendance is mandatory and you must do the reading prior to class. If you put forth  effort, you should do fine and thoroughly enjoy this class even if law isn't your favorite.

Irvine is the best professor I've had in Fisher.  He makes class interesting, which is good, because it's mandatory.  He expects you to read ahead of class and will give quizzes if there aren't enough people or people aren't prepared.  Definitely take him! Not too difficult of a class either

He is a nice teacher. He makes the subject interesting, and he cares about it.  He makes it mandatory that you must read for every class; bring your book to class. He makes the class applicable to life. Exams are challenging.
He is a very nice teacher.  He makes learning the matter applicable to your life. His tests aren't easy. He is willing to clarify a lot of the material.
not a nice person and really hard with grading, avoid him if you can

Professor Irvine is one of the best professors I have ever had, when he lectures about any information, he makes it interesting and almost fun to learn. He is also very passionate about law and very passionate about teaching as well. I would highly recommend taking him if you have the chance.

Great teacher. you have to actually do the reading every night because he will give pop quizzes even though you will usually get a 100 on the quiz if you read. Most exam questions are examples of definitions and law cases.

A great guy with a love for teaching. His tests are very hard and you have to read/take notes in class. I would disagree with others who said you can skim by and get a B. He does curve but you need it after the test difficulty. Would still recommend!

It?s a boring subject with an entertaining professor. He is clearly here because he enjoys teaching and while he wants you to learn the material, he makes sure you do it in a fun atmosphere. I have taken classes with the other professors teaching 510 and if your schedule permits, I wouldn?t take 510 from anyone else!
Probably the best professor I've had. Makes class fun. Make sure to read before class because he will call on people randomly.
Great teacher. Very enthusiastic and entertaining. Very easy B with minimal work. Have to study a bit more to get an A.

Possibly the best teacher I have had in my entire collegiate career. His personality makes attending his two hour lecture fun and productive. Midterm is hard, final is a bit easier. Read the book, take notes, do HW, and study HARD for an A. Generous curve puts majority in B range.

Nothing new to report. Great teacher, quite possibly best I've had at Fisher. If you show up and do the work you will most likely get a B, above and beyond effort makes it possible for an A. I'm ok with a B because he is that good of a teacher, especially for a boring subject. Truly has students best interests at heart, refreshing for OSU.

By far one of the best professors i have ever had. he really cares about all his students and wants them all to do well. the class is hard, but he very fair. he expects you to read before class and be ready. he made this class enjoyable and he is pretty funny. i hope i get to take him again. great teacher, take him if you can

Best teacher I have had in Fisher, or at OSU for that matter. Teaches the material very well, forces you to read everything before class and he is very engaging and funny. He will cold call students all the time and give you a hard time if you are not prepared--so do the reading! I would recommend taking him over any other professor for this class.

Irvine's class is challenging simply because you're expected to know the entire chapter upon arriving to class. While this might sound daunting, it's not as hard as it seems. Just read ahead and be prepared and you'll be fine. It's well worth it. Irvine is the best professor at Fisher and you'll learn a lot and have a lot of fun at the same time.

Prof. Irvine is the best teacher I have had thus far in college. He truly enjoys teaching, and makes class enjoyable. There was never a dull moment, and I took the class at 7:30 pm. Follow his 3 rules, and you'll get at least a B.

Really is an awesome teacher.  Probably the most entertaining class for how boring the material can be.  He calls on you throughout class but keeps a joking manner most of the time.  Just read the book before class and study for exams.

Irvine is hilarious and you will learn A LOT in his class!  I wouldn't take this with anyone else.  He is the best teacher in Fisher.  A forewarning though if English is your second language this class might be difficult for you just because he talks pretty fast.  If you can understand English well though, you will be fine!  Read the book!

Worst grade I've ever received at fisher (C-!)... I think I bombed the final, anyway I'm not going to let my grade reflect my rating like most people do...  Prof. Irvine is a great teacher, knows his material and makes the class enjoyable.  Trust me, you will learn, he calls you out if you don't know the answer!  I would take him again honestly...
Awesome teacher by far

A+ teacher. Very clear and knows what his talking about. Very interesting and keeps the class entertained. Best teacher I've had in Fisher. Very entertaining/funny. Read the book before class and review the chapters again before tests and you will do fine. Be on time, be prepared, and pay attention!

Great teacher. Make sure you keep up in class, I think that there's a fair curve at the end, which is nice. It kind of seems like a lot of your grade is up in the air, but as long as you read and understand the book you'll be fine.

One of the better professors that I had at Fisher.  The format is such that you have to read each chapter and do the homework before coming to class; know the material as he will call on you in class and put you on the spot if you don't know the answer.  Kept things light with his jokes and offbeat humor.  Be on time, be prepared and pay attention!

By far my favorite teacher in college. Extremely fun to banter with and incredibly intelligent. Wish I could take it again, it was that good! The class moved back to 10:30, which makes it a great time of day too! Always in good spirits, keep up with the book and you'll love this class/professor!

this guy is honestly the best teacher i have ever had. He keeps everybody entertained and interested in class. He makes an hour 48 minute class feel like a 48 minute class because he keeps you on your toes and really makes you participate whether you want to or not. very thorough, funny guy good humor great professor

awesome guy, very helpful and makes class fun to go to. exams we hard and he is the only teacher for this class who requires homework every class (even tho he most likely doesnt ever look at them) lecture can be confusing because he just talks and doesnt write anything down. you will earn more with him that blackburn or weinstock.
Awesome. Wish he thought accounting too.
I cannot stress this enough. Best teacher i have ever had! The class was extremely interesting and not hard at all. Do NOT take this class with any other teacher!

Irvine is absolutely the best professor at Fisher. The first day of class I was very intimidated when I saw him. Don't worry about your grade. He's very fair.

Take Irvine if at all possible. He makes the class interesting; sarcasm and jokes make boring chapters somewhat entertaining. Make sure you read the book, because you NEED to be prepared! 30% participation grade is nice, too!

This professor was probably one of my favorites so far...his class is really exciting because you actually get to interact...I don't know about any of the other profs that teach this class, but I would recommend Irvine to anyone

nice guy, funny... if you have it at 8:30am it tends to get old after a while.  lots and lots of questions, tricky ones, on the exams.  80 midterm 100 final.  read the book and be prepared.  do the extra credit cases.

Best teacher Ive had in college.  He's funny, knows the material very well, and conveys it in an a way that is easy to understand.  Must be prepared for class as he calls on everyone, but he seemed to get everyone more motivated than any teacher Ive had. You have to take him if you get the chance.

By far my favorite instructor in my four years at OSU...he is hilarious, incredibly smart and makes the class tons of fun.  I learned more in those 10 weeks then most of my other courses combined.  Highly recommend!!

This guy is funny and a really good teacher. Honestly, take him if you can. He kept me studying and I'm the worst student ever. Plus, he makes an pretty interesting class really fun. I wish he could teach all my classes.
He's a great teacher, qualified (both a JD and CPA), but moreover he makes the class fun, despite the tough material. You will learn if you take his class.
Fantastic! is really funny and fair, makes you learn, only drawback is the class was at 8:30 AM with a 7:30 final, still, HIGHLY recommended

Very Good Professor.  Tough yet Fair.  He on your toes bc he will know who you are and he knows when you are BSing an answer.  I would recommend his class if you want to learn something and be amused.  Be ready to work hard in that class though
Best teacher in fisher.  Be prepared, be attentive, be on time, and you'll get an A.
HE is just gr8. you will luv his class. he is funny and a good teacher.i highly recommend him for 510.
Excellent teacher.  Cream of the crop.  Highly reccomend.
great teacher...very entertaining.  calls on everyone and learns everyone's name.
Interesting class with real world usefulness.  He gets on your ass if you aren't prepared.  Do the work, come to class, and actually learn something.  Idiots should get someone else.

Dr. Talke is very easy to communicate with and wants what's best for his students. The class is fairly challenging, but if you take advantage of the extra credit opportunities and class resources, it can be somewhat enjoyable.

reviews.comment: Professor Sheldon is very caring and knowledgable in his field. His acumen spans many fields in international economics, as well as politics, policy, and football (real football). I enjoyed his class and learned a great deal from him. I highly recommend taking him as he makes the material enjoyable and easy to follow.

As someone who was interested in international trade from before this class, this class was everything I could ask for and more. Dr. Sheldon is a very knowledgable professor who is very caring and structures the course to help you succeed. The homework quizzes are open book and he gives a lot of opportunities for easy extra credit.

Dr. Sheldon has a great sense of humor and knows how to strike a balance between seriousness and lightheartedness, while still packing in a lot of information. Really cares about helping students understand the material. Also threw in extra credit for those who frequently attended and participated. The man is an absolute riot in the best way.

Dr Sheldon is the best professor I've had at OSU. He explains everything very well and has a lot of experience and interesting stories that tie into the course subject which makes it genuinely interesting. Great guy, loves to joke around and talk about soccer. If you come to class and put in a little effort in you will learn a lot and get an A

Dr. Sheldon is an amazing professor who is extremely knowledgable and passionate about the information he teaches. He spends a lot of time explaining the material but also moves through lectures efficiently. The material is inherently tough to understand, but Dr. Sheldon welcomes questions and also is very accessible outside of class!

reviews.comment: Professor Sheldon was one of my favorite professors. He was funny and engaging, but he also worked to make sure we understood the material.

He's one of the best professors I have had at tOSU.  He is very thorough in all of his lectures, and is hilarious the whole way through.  Some of the concepts in his class can be thought of as dry and difficult at times, but he does a great job at explaining everything and making sure the class understands.  I actually looked forward to his class.

Mr. Sheldon was one of my favorite teachers I've had at OSU. Although economics can be very dry Mr. Sheldon explains things in a manner that everyone can easily understand and he does this by way of a nice British accent. He adds a lot of genuine personality and humor to all of his lectures. One of the most relatable teachers I've ever had. A**!

Wonderful professor. He will do just about anything to get you an A in the course. He dropped one of our exam grades, gave tons of extra credit, and always has bonus questions. If you show up to class and pay attention you will do fine. No book and he prints off all of the lecture slides. He is also British and has a good sense of humor. Good class

Dr. Sheldon is one of the best economics teachers you could ever ask to have. He teaches his information and excessively reviews it during class  periods to ensure that the students understand each and every concept. He takes his time, and does not rush through material. I highly recommend taking his 4003 & 4597 (International Trade) class.

Hardest class I've taken, but he evidently has a clear understanding of his subject. He is not the most effective in explanation. Hands down a great lecturer and professor. He lets you in advance that the course is difficult, so you can study accordingly. This class is great for MCAT prep. Dr. Wu's an amazing lecturer! His exams are fair but he tells you straightforward about what will be on his exams. Take his class if you can! He helped me prepare really well for the MCAT too.

Read the textbook.

Dr. Ottesen is very peculiar. She's very smart but does not relate to her students level of knowledge on biochemistry. Go to every lecture and study hard, because she is a very tough grader. However, she does give fair exams. I advise reading textbook because she is not the best at explaining things on a simple level. Good luck, and put in the work

Friendly & cares about your learning, but teaches as if everyone knows the same amount of biochemistry as her. Her exams are all short essays but very fair. However, she is an extremely tough grader. You will think you did well on an exam then get it back and see -1 -2 or -3 on almost every question because she looks for specific phrases.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Ottesen is one of the best, if not the best professor I have ever had. She gives a great lecture, is always open to questions and to help you with whatever you don't understand. Her in class quizzes are easy, her take home quizzes are tougher but hey, they are take home! Her exams are all based on the powerpoints, but the grading is rigid
The class requires you to work hard and the details matter. These are upper level majors courses, they aren't supposed to be easy. Put effort into the course and Dr. Ottesen will put effort into you.

She is very sensitive to students correcting her mistakes. She also does not seem to appreciate students trying to engage in scientific dialog with her outside of what is written on the lecture slides. I would advise choosing another professor if you have an interest in Biochemistry.

She takes off points for not mentioning extraneous information on exam questions. You can answer a question with 100% accuracy, and will lose credit for not writing details that were not prompted for in the questions. The exams are very easy conceptually, but the the grading is extremely subjective and not reflective of what the questions ask for.

She's great at confusing you. Every time she lectures, she has this big smile on her face basically saying "I'm going to screw you over on exams". Her questions on her exams are confusing! Re-read the questions multiple times to see what she's asking. She over complicates things and assumes that you know the topic before the class. Avoid her.
Not fun

I was so interested in biochem when we started. After taking her, my interest in biochem went down a lot. It's not even the material. It's just the way she teaches. She will talk about stuff in class that isn't even on the exam. Also, her exams are very vague on what to write. Majors can't avoid taking her because she's the only one who teaches it.

Honestly this class is a pain. The tests are completely written which is really annoying. You can write a ton and her TA's grade for specific words/phrases so your understanding is meaningless if you can't spit out. In the first 2 weeks we had a "practice quiz" which then ended up being graded because we were "practicing drawing structures." Bad.

I'd say avoid this proffessor if you can, but you can't. If you thought biochemistry was about understanding chemistry important life, change majors now. It's graded by blind memory. Learn to speak her language, she will not understand you otherwise. She has a weird thing on her tests, it's like all essays, never multiple choice. Expect the worst.

This professor does not care about teaching the material. She is there because she is required to teach a certain number of classes and it's painfully obvious. She's very unclear, makes up exam keys on a whim, and incredibly short tempered. Take 4511 with anyone else.
Literally zero surprises from her exams.  Would highly suggest her to anyone out there.  Incredibly approachable and friendly.

Dr. Ottesen is so enthusiastic about biochemistry and what she does, it's contagious. She tests on what she teaches and provides detailed supplements to prepare for exams. There were no surprises, and you'll learn a lot at a good pace. I really enjoyed her.
She is not helpful at all, ignores emails, and is honestly my least favorite professor I have ever had at this school.

Difficult class and final. Each exam has a page of pure memorization (Amino Acids, Lipids, etc.) and several essay response questions. The format of her exams allows you to show what you know, which was better than having a multiple choice exam. The final was VERY comprehensive and I scored significantly lower than midterms. Hard, but fair.
She makes this class so much hard that what it really is. Questions on exams and tests are so hard and confusing. Don't take her!!

I don't usually rate profs. When I do, they are either super good or the opposite. Unfortunately, Dr. Ottesen falls in the latter category. She is super demanding but does not have an effective communicating skill that conveys her expectations. This reflects on her confusing exams. I wish OSU could listen to students and stop her from teaching.

worst teacher i have ever had. she basically reads from the slides, yet the slides don't make sense. SO many quizzes. she askes you to apply knowledge she doesn't teach or give references to study from. like throwing a stone in a pit. i have never had trouble with a class until i had her as a teacher. very unhelpful outside of class.
i learnt a lot from her class! She is demanding though.

In general she's a good professor. Very enthusiastic about biochem and knowledgable about most of the content and many research topics. Although she could be confusing sometimes when explaining some research techniques; she might assume everyone to have learn some biochem lab already. However, I wish she could curve more generously though.

Dr. Ottesen is an amazing teacher. Favorite biosci prof ever. Fun lectures, very enthused. Lots of "pop" quizzes, but they're pretty easy. Never got below a B+ on one. Midterms and Final aren't bad either. She's NOT big on mechanisms :)!!! Just review the slides and do the hw prob's. There's office hrs too if you need them.

The best science class I've taking! Dr. Ottesen is an excellent teacher who is prepared above and beyond to teach this class. There are a lot of quizzes but she warns you about them and hints at what you need to know. They keep you on top of the material. Doesn't follow the book exactly but suggests questions to do. Exams are fair but challenging.

Nuissance is a better and appropriate word to call her but she will face hers. Not everone was meant to teach and this one in particular should stay in her lab because being a boring instrutor is not what students neccessarily want at the end of the day. 614 is a better class even with all the mechanism is still more fun than 613 will ever be.

Dr. Ottesen was an excellent professor.  She presented the material clearly and challenged the students to apply this material to new situations.  You have to work hard in the class but you learn alot!

If 613 had a different instructor i believe i would be a more fun class. Teacher was as useless as T.A. unnecessary many quizzes and no scheme of exams. which one had an option of taking the class at Capital University. But she has no choice probably be tenured. she should stay in the lab and OSU should keep looking for the person who can teach the

she is pretty terrible.  she does not follow the book which would be fine if her slides were actually complete.  she is very knowledgable about research methods though.  but horrible at answering questions in a comprehensible way.  she also doesn't pass back exams or put up practice ones or tell you anything about the final
Otteson hazes students with random information and she has too many quizes.

I LOVEE HER. I'm more of an in-person student but Professor Stovers lectures are set up so well. She has amazing ways of explaining hard concepts that make it fun to learn. She posts lots of resources pre-made from prior students that work wonders. Just put in the time to study every day and you'll do great. I HIGHLY recommend!

I am not sure how every review is so positive. None of the practice quizzes, review sessions, and homework questions match the exams. This is extremely confusing and frustrating to be rigorously studying material that isn't even tested. Be extremely cautious of this.

This is a great class. Dr. Stover is very understanding and great at lecturing. As long as you thoroughly study and memorize the material, you will do fine. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. The lectures you don't have to attend, they are recorded and posted on canvas. Lab is easy, just review and relearning some of the material.
Stover is the best lecturer ever. Her class requires lots of studying, and exam averages are usually 70-80%. Stay consistent with the material and write out the slides.

Dr. Stover was phenomenal. Take her if you can she made the topics easy to understand and the exams were not made to trick you. You do have to study a lot because its memorization but if you put in the work you'll do fine.

Dr. Stover is an incredible professor. Her lectures are engaging, she always has a positive attitude, and she makes the content easy to understand. Anatomy is a tedious class regardless of the professor so make sure to make this class your hard course for the semester. 
Take good notes and study hard and you'll do great.

Dr. Stover was AMAZING. Her lectures are very engaging and she makes you learn the material very well. She is the best professor I've ever had. You have to study hard for the exams and it is a ton of memorization, but if you put the effort in you will be fine.
Very kind professor. Anatomy is a difficult topic to learn, but as long as you put in effort, you can perform well.

There are 5 unit exams, no final, and 11 labs (3 are dropped). Lectures are at 8am, but they're recorded so you can watch anytime. Stover explains everything in the simplest way possible and is super kind. There were extra credit opportunities as well. The class can be a lot at times, but if you study daily and use her resources, you'll do amazing!

Attend the lectures. They are 8am MWF and set you up for your day. Stover was a fantastic lecturer and will make this class the easiest thing you've ever taken IF YOU TRY! If you do not put effort in, you might as well drop because you will be so lost it's not even funny. In anatomy, you either know it or you don't. Stover made sure I knew it.

Dr. Stover may be the best professor I had during undergrad. She explains difficult concepts in an easy to understand way. She gives many mnemonics and tricks for learning the material. She seems to actually care about her students and if they're learning the material — which is more than I could say for many science profs at OSU. She is the best!

This class is challenging but if you actually study and take the time to draw your own diagrams, make your own quizlets, and find a way that you can actually retain the information. Then I found the exams fairly easy. So far, I have gotten above a 90% on 4 exams. Great lecturer, and lectures are recorded so you can watch them anytime. Lab is fun.

She's the best! The class is a lot of information and memorizing, but she made it easier to grasp and has such a positive personality each lecture that makes them enjoyable. Lectures are online and recorded so not mandatory but they're the only way to get the information. She also posts her annotated notes after lecture which is very helpful

Dr. Stover's lectures were very easy to understand, and she offered many helpful ways to memorize things as we learned. Weekly lab attendance was mandatory with 2 unexcused drops, and lecture was all online (recorded and posted) at 8AM but attendance was not mandatory. The exams were all multiple choice and extremely easy as long as you studied.

Dr Stover was great! There are good extra credit opportunities that can help with studying the content. She does not try to trick you with exams, so if you study you will do well. There are homework assignments due at the end of the unit for completion. Lab TA's will give you hints to what is on the exam. Loved this class, made anatomy interesting.
I loved her! She was honestly such a great professor, she made things easy to understand and gave us resources to use to help us study for the exams.

I had a great experience with Kristen. Lectures are online and not mandatory; she records them, and you need to watch them to succeed. She explains the material in a very relevant way to the tests, and she wants to ensure that every student is successful. It is a lot of course material to memorize, but she gives you every opportunity to succeed.

She genuinely cares about her students and doesn't want them to fail. There are five exams, though, and that is pretty much the bulk of your grade, so be sure to study those. Everything on her slides is on the exams, so study the slides, and you will be fine. Lots of content, but not hard. Attendance isn't mandatory & all lectures are recorded.

Dr. Stover does an amazing job teaching anatomy. This class was the most organized/straightforward course I've ever taken. The lectures are so well put together that I never felt like I needed to find other resources to do well in the class.

Best professor I have ever had. She clearly loved teaching and truly wanted the best for her students. Anatomy is a difficult topic, but her lectures were very clear in what you needed to know and they were very informative. She essentially made learning anatomy easy. Absolute 5/5, no doubt.

Such a great professor! TONS of studying but Dr. Stover breaks it down in a way to make it easy and understandable. Gives tons of study tools and tips to succeed. Lectures are great, lots of active note-taking which helps to learn. Exams are fair. Labs are interesting.

1. Watch Dr. Stover's lectures in 2x speed while having the slides open on my Ipad. 
2. Make a condensed set of notes for each lecture. Include as many tables, charts, figures and pictures. 
3. Memorize your notes. I did this on notability by using the tape tool. 
4. Quiz myself using the hw, unit quizzes, lecture quizzes, and unit review lecture.

Dr. Stover was one of the best professors I have had. Her learning objectives are super clear and are the most accurate I have seen on exams. Watch 2x speed and MAKE QUIZLETS/FLASHCARDS that exactly match the objectives and you will get an A.

By far my favorite class this semester! Dr. Stover is a very fair professor - each lecture begins with a list of objectives, and her exams are based off of these objectives so that there will never be test questions out of left field. 5 non-cumulative exams.

Great professor! Content is divided into 5 units. Material is straight forward, and lectures are via zoom recordings so we could watch them whenever. Lab is helpful. Stay up-to-date with material, so there are not loads of info to study the night before the exams. Assignments are helpful and accurately reflect the exams!
Dr. Stover is an amazing professor. As long as you keep up with the lectures and study in advance you should be fine. I would 100% take her class again.
Dr. Stover is an amazing professor. As long as you keep up with the lectures and study in advance you'll be fine. I would 100% take her class again if I could.
Dr. Stover is an amazing professor. The exams are not bad if you study. Anki was really helpful for this class. It is just a lot of memorization.

Dr. Stover is one of the anatomy 2300 professors and is amazing. Although I didn't do as good as I hoped in the class, she really conveys the information very well. The only thing I would say is how hard her exams are. They are worded in a very particular way that makes you think outside of the book so make sure you know your material.

Dr. Stover was an excellent professor. Anatomy is definitely not an easy course, however if you watch her lectures, start studying a week in advance, and actively take notes/make Quizlets - you will be okay! I enjoyed this class very much and truthfully did not try as hard as I could have and still did fine in the class.

LOVE HER!!! Literally made me want to continue taking Anatomy courses. This class is memorization heavy (duh) and honestly if you do bad in the class, it's probably a lack of trying on your part bc. Stover tells you exactly what you can do to succeed.

I have had Prof Stover for 2 years because I had to retake anatomy. I was actually happy to be taking the class a second time because of how interesting the class is. Stover is super sweet and despite such a big class if you are not doing well she will go out of her way to check on you. Exams are fair but a lot. Start studying weeks before.

Dr. Stover is great. Anatomy is a lot to learn but her and the rest of the teaching staff clearly presented the content and tried to make it as easy and interesting as possible to learn. Most of your grade comes from exams so as long as you stay on top of things and study you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: as long as you keep up with the lectures it's totally doable. can skip 3 labs. super nice prof. almost now hw besides studying so exams are important.
great prof!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very organized class, expectations are clear. Almost now homework, studying and test heavy. 3/11 labs get dropped which is so nice. If you stay on top of your studying, not too bad. Lectures at 8 am online, but posted on carmen to watch later.
Excellent professor, best I've had at OSU. Makes it extremely clear what you need to learn, and what will be on the exams. Exams are thorough, but if you use her checklists they're very easy. 10/10.

Dr. Stover is incredibly knowledgable and a great professor! Lectures were stressful to understand at first, but she makes the material very interesting and relatively simple enough for us to grasp for the tests. The class is definitely difficult, but Dr. Stover is a great person to learn from.

Amazing professor! For anatomy being the rigorous course that it is, she does an great job of breaking down concepts into a way that is easy to understand. Online lectures were always recorded. Although you have to put in some time to study, the exam questions were very fair. Exam content was easy to find by just studying the lecture notes given.

The best professor I have ever had! Dr. Stover is amazing at teaching anatomy. She actively hand writes/ draws notes and this is incredibly helpful. Anatomy isn't an easy class but if you review and know the muscle tables and flow charts by heart then you'll do good. STUDY!!

Anatomy 2300 with Kristin Stover was a great class. There are not many assignments to overwhelm students and you'll only get a good grade if you study because most of your grade comes from the exams. Everything on the exams is in the written notes and some is from labs, so if you study that, then you have all of the information you need to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stover is great at lecturing, makes things clear and lets students know what will be on the exams. There is barely homework, one little multiple-choice assignment every Friday with some exam study assignment before midterms. Love her energy at 8 in the morning.

Anatomy is a difficult class in any form, but Dr. Stover truly cares about students and makes the class as manageable as possible (i.e. telling you what you do and don't need to know, hands on lectures, memorization techniques). I would not have passed this class without that. It gets easier as the course goes on which was a big relief as well!
Please please be nice to Dr. Stover! She is absolutely amazing and we students love her.

Professor Stover actually cared about her students and made our lectures more active learning style after seeing that many did bad on the first exam. This class has a lot of content that needs to be memorized, if you do not study you will not do well. I found the labs to be the best part of the class!

I am a student who retook the course and she was a very caring professor who was willing to see her class succeed. After she saw we did not do well on the first exam she changed her lecturing style and content format to be more straightforward. She was one of the best professors I've ever had at osu.

Anatomy 2300 will be a tough class regardless of who you have. But Dr. Stover made the course as bearable as possible. The exams were online and fully multiple choice or matching. At the end of the semester, I was 0.35% off from a C+. Even though the syllabus says no additional curve was in place, she curved me up after I emailed her.

Anatomy 2300 was a difficult class, however Professor Stover made it as bearable as possible. She genuinely cares about her students. While the class was a lot of memorization, she posted the lecture videos for students to rewatch,and provided plenty of materials and resources to assist her students with studying. I would 100% recommend her!

She is an amazing teacher in terms of the way she does lecture and sets up the class. She's also an amazing human.She really cares about the whole class and genuinely cares about the teaching which makes the teaching that much better. She is one of the most memorable teachers I have had. I highly recommend if you have the chance to take her, do it.

Stover is GREAT. Anatomy is just a hard class in general but stover is great at explanations. The class is offered online at 8am Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. BUT it is reordered so you can miss and watch later. Labs are once a week for 2 hours and 30 minutes. The labs don't necessarily help but they are mandatory. Tests are hard but manageable.

Dr. Stover was a great Anatomy professor. The course was only offered online with weekly labs, but she explained the material very clearly even though anatomy can be a difficult subject. This class is really just memorizing A LOT of stuff, but if you put in a good amount of effort you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Some studies committed suicide because of her classes.  Her exams are purposely rude and difficult.  The study guides aren't helpful, she just gives you back a list of everything that you have learned.  She gets sassy when a student has a question.  Other professors do the same class, way easier, much nicer, and more convenient.

Her grading rate for the semester was abysmal. Took 4 weeks to get midterm grades back, and did not receive project grades until 1 week AFTER the final was completed, despite the harsh deadlines put on submitting on time. Felt really confident in the course until assembly, goes off topic too much to stay engaged during lecture.

I think she was pretty good. Clearly knows the material well. She grades midterms very fairly and doesn't try to trick the student. Only complaint was that projects were not graded until end of semester.

When it comes to grades, professor Jones does NOT play around and is very strict with her late policy. However, she is very generous with the extra credit on her exams, so it's not very hard to get a good grade if you keep up with the lectures. Also, her lab directions are not always clear, so make sure to attend office hours to get clarification.

Janis is a great professor and expects a high standard from the class, she backs it up by ensuring that the class has all the information that they need. I never felt that she was disrespectful and most people who think that probably have a victim mindset. The exams are all fair game too! No gotchas or questions on topics you've never heard of.

Prof Jones is stupendous! The course is challenging, but Prof Jones does what she can to provide the class all of the information that is needed to pass the course assignments and exams. There is no excuse to not do well in the class with the number of resources handed: piazza, office hours, study guide and detailed lecture slides.

She was a great professor! She's not terribly harsh, and I genuinely enjoyed her course. She also gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit on the exams, so it's not too difficult to get an A in the course.

Her comics were also typically funny!

I came in very concerned from the other reviews here, but I was pleasantly surprised. The class itself is fine, I felt professor Jones did a good job of making dry subject matter entertaining. The projects are brutal but informative. If you want an easy time, take a someone else., but if you want to actually learn, this is the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was scared by these reviews, but she's not that bad. She has a no-nonsense midwestern sort of demeanor, but she cares and has in-class practices and review sessions. Pay attention and understand the projects and you'll do fine on exams. Worst part is not grading any of the annoying projects up to this point, yet final is in two weeks??

The only bad part of her class was the amount of time spent on projects that only total to be 15% of your total grade (namely project 4). Her grading is really strict with the guidelines on projects but as long as you actually try to learn C and Assembly it's not actually that hard.

Janis probably gets a lot more flak than she deserves, but she probably does make this class a lot harder than it needs to be. She expects a lot from her students, but I never got the impression that she was disrespectful. The grading criteria are very strict, and her exams are quite difficult.

Jones' lectures are very helpful explaining the things on her slides, and the slides are great for reviewing before a test. Some of the projects can be pretty intensive, but there are only 4 real projects (projects 3,4,6,7) the others are pretty self explanatory. Jones is very helpful in office hours. For tests, all I ever reviewed were the slides.
Horrible professor. Thinks she hung the moon just because of her real world experience. She is not helpful, consecutive, and overall tries to purposely hold students back.
She was very condescending and unapproachable.

Professor Jones has a lot of experience in the real world (you'll hear a lot about it, a little too much) but she isn't too great of a teacher, from my experience. Class is very much test heavy, 40% final and 30% midterm. Projects can take a LONG time and are only worth 1.7% of your grade. Systems 1 itself is a hard course, try to avoid her.

Take Systems 1 with Janis if you'd like obtain good software engineering skills: critical thinking, coming up with a software solution when given a set of requirements, and knowing when to ask questions. I have learned a lot just from one semester.

On the other hand if you don't care about being a good SWE, then take it elsewhere.

At the center of everything, Janis is a fair professor. People seem to get mad that the projects are complicated, but that's just the reality of an engineering course. As someone who's interned at Big Tech, I can say that Janis gives enough information to push you in the right direction for projects. Moreover, she prepares you to succeed in exams!

Are you ready for tedious and over complicated project directions? Hours upon hours of debugging? NO FORGIVENESS ON SUBMISSIONS? Then you will LOVE Janis Jones! She treats this course like its our job, she tries to draw parallels between this course and real employment by being harsh, unforgiving, and giving me a 40 hr work week. Take someone else.

I was worried about having Janis for Systems 1 because of the reviews on RMP, but my experience was totally different. She's a fair professor who prepares you for exams, projects, and assignments. If you start projects early, attend and review lectures, you'll do well. Many of the complaints seem to come from students who didn't put in the effort.

The projects were time intensive and difficult, but Janis gave many work days and was willing to help. Her lectures were dense at times, but she always included stories and cartoons to keep things interesting. She also gave lots of extra credit on exams and projects, so it was easy to get a good grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't take Systems with this professor no matter what. Has been very rude and even raised her voice at me for not understanding certain topics. Not much empathy for students and extremely strict with grading. Projects take so much time and are worth so little, with the exams being worth entirely too much.

Avoid at all costs. 

-Unclear project instructions
-Automatic 0 if you have any warning on project
-Long monotone lectures
-Unsympathetic towards tough grading
-Midterm 30%, final 40%
-Takes long to respond outside of class
-Condescending when you don't understand topics
-Acknowledges her bad teaching, unwilling to change, blames course.
-Unfunny

Her refusal to draw parallels with other CS concepts and languages other than what she was intimately familiar with made it hard to like her.
