She would state plainly that "I don't know Java, so don't ask if this is like anything in there" and repeated that multiple times throughout the course. Her attitude is definitely "my way or the highway".

I thought Dr. Jones was a fine professor. The labs did take an extremely long time but if you were paying attention in class I never found them to be impossible. Her lectures weren't the greatest but were informative and engaging enough. I think these reviews are way too negative compared to what that class is actually like.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She knows her stuff WELL. Exams are not easy, but definitely fair. She provides a study guide before exam. Labs are long and not easy for sure, but not undoable. Just start them early and go to office hour. She's willing to help so don't be scared. Over 1/3 of the students earning an A/A-, 50% earning a B or better, and 70% earning a C or better.

Do labs early and study and you'll do fine. Content can be overwhelming esp if u have no prior experience w C and assembly. V knowledgeable professor tho. Don't understand the hate on here but sounds like a skill issue to me :P.

Rude, condescending, has a really high ego. Terribly boring lectures, horrible slides, extremely difficult labs with bad directions given. You must memorize everything taught to do well on her exams (and no study guides given). PLEASE stay away if you can help it. If you have her, good luck.
Please take any other professor!
Atrocious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you enjoy 20-30 hour bi-weekly labs that are 1.7% of your grade each, the most mediocre powerpoint presentations, and knowing every question you ask will be met with the most useless and patronizing answer imaginable, this is the class for you. You also get a marginally better understanding of the content compared to the other sections!

She was not approachable and often got mad at students for asking questions. Her lectures are just her reading from the slides and very boring. Her labs are very long and difficult and worth almost none of the final grade. She made me truly hate the material of a class more than in any class I have taken before.

Invest in a good therapist if you even think about taking this course with Janis as she will obliterate your mental health (and that might not even help). Being "successful" in the industry DOES NOT translate to having even an iota of teaching skill.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were long and confusing but once you actually put it into practice it made sense. The labs were hard and took a long time but you had multiple weeks to do them and they helped made the content understandable. She gave clear outlines of what the test will be on. Everyone is just blaming her for the course naturally being a hard course.

I wonder if she wrote some of these high ratings herself. Jones seemingly did everything in her power to make a course with already challenging material even more confusing. The labs took an egregious amount of time and barely even counted towards your grade. Run while you still have some enjoyment of computer science. She'll take it all.
Avoid at all costs if you want to retain some semblance of joy in your life.

Avoid taking her sections AT ALL COSTS. Unlike every other professor who teaches the course, she intentionally makes lab work difficult, has more labs, and doesn't allow her students to drop a lab grade. The lectures are dry and do not have all the information you will need to complete labs. Easily the most evil computer science class I have taken.

Do everything in your power to avoid her as a professor. After having her as a professor I no longer enjoy computer science as a subject and find no joy in the understanding of computational systems. Taking her course will be the single biggest mistake you can make in the Ohio State college of engineering.

I asked one question in the class and she yelled at me for getting "too ahead" of the class. I tried emailing her throughout a seven week time period and she completely blew off every single email. I confronted her about this and clearly had no excuse to ignore my emails. I am sick of these people who cannot have basic respect for others.
Just take anyone else, it will make your life so much easier
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Janis was a good professor. She can be condescending when answering questions if you are lost. Labs take an insane amount of time but are extremely low impact on your grade with strict guidelines that make it really easy to get a zero if you miss one. Tests are very heavily weighted but fair (she doesn't play trick the student, which I respect).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Systems 1 is a difficult class, but Jones covers the material very fairly. The exams are long but fair, and she offers a ton of extra credit on them. If you go to class and put in the effort, you'll do well. I thought she was a great professor, her expertise from working in industry for many years is insightful and interesting to hear about.

I think a lot of the reviews on here are being unfair. This was a pretty tough course with a lot of information jammed into it. I know for a fact that there are worse professors. Her lectures were very long and information heavy, which can be hard for some people to digest. Her tests were very difficult, but topics were given before hand.

Janis is truly a good instructor. She teaches a difficult course that many students struggle with due to the massive amount of content covered. Nonetheless, she cares about her students and is genuinely passionate about teaching. She also provides a unique perspective having owned a tech company and working in industry for many years.

Janis is an amazing professor! Labs are long, but they are excellent preparation for the exams. Janis will also cancel class several times to give you time to work on the labs. Her lectures have all of the information you'll need. Come to office hours and start work on labs as soon as they're assigned and you'll have a great semester.

I had a fantastic experience in Sys1 with Jones. It was clear in class and during her office hours that she truly cares about her students. Her lectures are very clear, and she gives you the notes ahead of time so you don't have to just blindly copy. She is big on attendance and being in class. If you show her that you care, you will succeed.

Easily the worst professor. For someone who has been "doing this for many years" her class seems totally disorganized. We didn't get our lab grades until the day grades were due. She also missed the deadline for reporting our grades (surprise surprise). Her lectures were horrible, and she is condescending and rude when asked questions. 0/10

I am unsure how Janis has got such a low score on RMP. She was a phenomenal professor and did everything in her power to clarify questions and keep us engaged in class. She is a tough grader and the labs can take a bit of time, but office hours are plentiful and she will take the time to work with you. Tons of real world knowledge to be gained.

She's not as bad as the other ratings make her out to be. Her slides are good. She does try to be reasonable and moves due dates.

Her recordings were very blurry so try to go in person. If you don't regularly attend, she's condescending when you ask questions.

It took a long time for labs to be graded. Grades are heavily influenced by exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jones is horrible. I have her for Systems 1 and her lectures are drab and all over the place. There is no schedule, and huge projects are assigned with no notice that take exorbitant amounts of time to complete. Also, we are now on Lab 7, and only one lab has been graded. Worst of all, the exams are HARD & the only major contributor to your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She has good slides and lectures but something about her makes her not very approachable. The labs are extremely difficult and there are a lot of constraints on how to do them. The exams are also hard and are worth a lot. She's good at teaching content but her way of testing the knowledge is not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hard lab. Hard exam. Boring class. Just don't take this class with this instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While I don't hate her as a teacher, the weights made it so labs that had been worked on for 10 hours each were worth 5% of our grade total while homework problems were each .5% of our grade. In addition the final was 40% of our grade. Overall I think she does a decent job with content but the difficulty with the weights makes this class very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had to drop from her Systems I class midway through the spring semester. Note that most classes were online at the time including her Systems class. Anyways, professor Jones lectured in a very condescending manner. and answered student questions in a similar manner. Retake 2421 with a different professor that expects students to struggle a bit.
She doesn't know how to respect her students. Never care about her ridiculous project and homework. Avoid if all possible.

Her labs are literally going to become your entire life and will break you down bit by bit. Condescending instructions and ridiculous requirements. Lectures are dry and extremely boring. Can be mean when asking questions and her grading is extremely strict.

Avoid her to the best of your ability. She intentionally designs her lab rubrics to make life difficult. Insane requirements you won't even see in industry. Not to mention labs take up so much of your energy and you won't even get anything above 5 points. Exams are crazy hard and difficult to pass. Skip this class if you care about your wellbeing.
SO hard.
lab is so hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: She can be hard at times, she gives bonus credit if you turn in your projects early. Although her grading criteria are pretty clear for projects. Careful though, once you fall behind it'll be a lot of work to catch up. Although at least the stuff from first half of the semester doesn't carry over to the second half so the final will all be for new.

Drop her class if you have a chance. Regardless of how hard you study, an average person could probably get a grade within the Cs or the low Bs. Gotta work really hard just to get a c. Rude lab instructions and just threatens to take so many points away for making one simple mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The stuff in lecture is relatively straightforward but Prof. Jones made the labs extremely difficult. You can literally spend 20 hours doing them and still only get 6% of your grade. Would not recommend! Don't get me started on the final, impossible but still gotta pass to pass the course. Run if you can.

She intentionally places important exam questions on the back, and pop quizes at the beggining or end of classes; the lab instructions contain a lot of condecending statements instead of being objective; she puts absolutely 0 effort into lectures, and posts the slides just before the class so you cant ask questions; rude behavior towards students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Well shes knowledgeable and knows her stuff but not totally focused on teaching. More concerned about drowning you in labs and homeworks that arent even worth much. Midterms and final are your entire grade. Look elsewhere if your just a beginner.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just like other RMPs for her, drop while you can. If you care about your mental health. Jones aims to teach you what she would want to see if hiring someone in the industry. But, instead of focusing on the learning, she drowns you in labs that could take anywhere between 15-30 hours each. Run, while you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dry but not difficult. Dr. Jones gives a lot of extra credit w/early due dates. Attendance isn't mandatory (read the slides) but she does have pop quizzes. Homework is long and tedious but there are only 3. Sometimes I feel like her explanations just comprise of repeating herself, but you don't need a deep understanding to do well anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's the absolute worst professor I have ever seen in my entire life. Her grading is very strict. Her whole policy is to be fair, so she does things to make students feel the class is fair but in reality she makes it so much difficult that it needs to be. Good lectures but can be really boring. Make sure you keep up, or else you are retaking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jones is one of the worst professors in the CSE department not because she just reads off the slides, but because she is very rude and condescending. The labs are extremely hard and long. She canceled class three times just to give us time to work on the long labs. Tests are heavy. Avoid her if you care about your mental health.

There are so many ways to clarify the content, Jones can always find a short path to humiliate you and repeat the same content again instead of clarify it. Yes, she was "successful" in the industry (maybe?), but I do not believe she is a good instructor. Avoid her if you care about your mental health -- mental health matter!

She does give out extra credit which is good. But she's really terrible at explaining things. Asking for clarification just ends up with her reiterating the material/instructions again (verbatim). Crazy grading criterias. Labs can be confusing and take a lot of time (or not a lot of time depends on the lab). Exams are very long. She is very rude.

The course content is difficult and Jones is a dull lecturer who just reads the notes off the PowerPoint. The labs take lots of time and effort, but she gives extra credit. Her exams are difficult and will take the entire test period. Her answers to questions are too vague and don't help you unless you already know what you're looking for.

Shes a good C teacher. However she lacks any ability to teach X86. Shes very rude. Often, she will just repeat what she said earlier, instead of trying to clarifying things. You can get the majority of your points off on projects (even if your code works). The final is not cumulative, but you still need to pass it, to pass the class. Avoid her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Difficult labs, extremely long exams, and just a rude person overall.

Professor Jones is great. The class is not easy but she's a good lecturer, and it really shows that she knows her stuff. Some labs take a ton of work (I think the longest I've worked on took me more than 10 hours), but they definitely help cement understanding of the concepts. The exams are incredibly long.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures like every other prof for this class. CSE2421 content is really important to cse majors. She does a good job teaching material. Her Midterm was stupid hard... fair but just so dang dense. Haven't taken final yet. Would recommend. Does have an edge you need to pretend doesn't exist to talk or ask questions unfortunately.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's a really good professor, both in terms of content and delivery. The course itself is hard and worthwhile. I wish it were easier but had I redone this semester, I would have had her again
She is very mean. You can learn nothing from her class. Every time you ask her question, she will make fun of you first. She doesn't know how to respect her students.

Prof. Jones is great. She can be kind of mean sometimes, but otherwise gives good advice and will make you learn from your mistakes. Her homeworks, labs, and exams were fair and straightforward, and she gives you the topics to study for the exams. The labs take a while, so start early - you can get extra credit if you finish them early, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's tolerable... Class is boring and she can be really mean when you ask her questions. She can be very nice to you if you're white though... She's very knowledgeable but sometimes she doesn't even answer your quesiton. Also don't trust the syllabus. We had half the number of homeworks specified in the syllabus and I was depending on them

She is okay. Experienced and knowledgeable, but lectures are meh. She tries her best though and is super helpful in office hours. I can see why she has such mixed reviews. You'll learn most of the content as you fumble through projects, read up on things, and reread powerpoints. Projects take forever, beware. Grading and weights are weird.
The WORST CSE lecturer at Ohio State EVER! She is mean and cynical and does't know how to teach. It's really a big challenge not to sleep in her class. If you want an A, AVOID her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Jones is a great choice for Systems 1 if you have the option. She teaches well and it is clear she really knows her stuff, plus she is kind of fun. She runs off of few but large assignments and you get bonus points for turning those in early, so you should do that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Janis is a great professor and the grading in the class was very fair. The homework assignments sometimes took a long time, but there weren't very many of them so overall it wasn't too bad. There were also extra credit opportunities on the labs and the exams. Lectures could be a bit boring but her stories from working in industry were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: We had a total of 9 assignments the whole semester, so the homeworks end up being stupidly long and the labs can feel like fumbling around in the dark until you figure them out. You get tested on things you don't really use at all. She's a nice enough person and has industry experience, so I'm not sure if this is her fault or just the course.

Lectures are a bit boring but slides are posted online. Attendance is required due to the in-class exercises (which are very easy and serve as way to take attendance). Jones posts study sheets with all the content that will be tested prior to the exam. Final exam is not cumulative. Extra Credit for Labs if submitted early. Overall great instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures were not great. Random in-class exercises (graded gently, but you have to show up every day...). Labs, HW, and tests were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I learned a lot from Janis. Her industry experience provides insight into the applications of the material, and if you have the desire to learn what many see as an uninteresting topic, you will be rewarded.

Janis Jones is by far one of the worst lecturers. Her lectures are her reading off the powerpoint slides. I HIGHLY recommend reading the class textbook. She grossly underestimated the time it takes to complete her exams, and, after a majority of the class did poorly, decided to deflate low scores by increasing coursework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She doesn't know how to teach. I have not learned anything from her lectures so I have to try and learn everything outside class. I went to office hours twice to get help on labs and both times she just sat there while I ended up finding the mistake myself. Terrible experience.

Janis Jones is a great, caring professor who brings in her many years of industry experience. She has a lot of useful anecdotes and examples. The content can be dry and the slides are a bit disorganized sometimes, and I think it's also her first time teaching the class. Occasional graded in-class assignments, so be sure to attend class.

Do NOT take this class if you do not want extremely demanding class for a 3 credit hours. She grades assignments very harshly and her exams are the worst, with the vaguest fill in the blanks with information she mentions only once in class. She used to have easier online exams but decided to have in person tougher exams this semester.

Takes attendance everyday, kind of boring professor and expects a lot for a 3 credit GE. I wouldn't have her as a professor again. Exams are difficult, and makes you do a podcast with someone at the end of the semester on a book you read throughout the whole semester. Shes nice, but i found myself kind of bored in her class.

Exams are 5 extended responses, 10ish fill in the blank, 5 short answer questions and about 25-30 multiple choice questions.This class is a harder GE which was disappointing because I was really looking forward to taking it but it turned into just having to memorize everything for exams.She is a nice professor, but expects a lot I wouldn'ttakeagain

Lots of information during lectures. Sometimes the information that was on the presentation was incomplete or incorrect. She spoke kind of condescendingly to the class. Pretty forgiving grader and exams were easy but just didn't enjoy her as a professor.

if you are going to take this class, just dont. this was the worst class i have ever taken, i studied for weeks for the exams and did not pass one. not a good teacher , expects you to read a whole textbook rather than teach you.

Kim very clearly cares about her students. This course was interesting and not too difficult as I took it for GE credit. Sometimes the readings could be annoying, but I rarely felt overwhelmed by the workload in this class. She brings in guest speakers and has in-class activities often. I would definitely recommend her and this course!

Awesome person and professor. Midterms are "open note" but have a time limit, so review in advance. Midterm FRQs are a pain. PLEASE listen to her when she says don't use AI... she's one of the few professors that will actually take you to COAM. This course is not hard, but may be more work than what you're willing to go through for a Gen Ed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely interesting class, have to attend lectures to do well on exams. Lots of in class and online discussions. Practically 1/2 textbooks was used so that was kind of frustrating because I paid for nothing. Lots of guest speakers. Lectures aren't posted online so it's crucial to attend class

Decently easy class and genuinely interesting if you attend class (lectures) and actually pay attention. Exams are fully online and open note. Sometimes there is an exam and “essay.” Only 1/2 textbooks were used so this was kind of frustrating because I paid for nothing. Lots of discussion boards, sometimes video discussion boards

I am so sad I found her during my senior year. She is one of those teachers who knows so much that you just want to sit down with her and ask for her perspective on everything. Very knowledgeable and a great lecturer. Tests are a bit short on time, but possible to do if you take notes in class. Take her if you can!!
Both this class and philosophy were amazing classes, tests aren't too difficult if you go to lectures and pays attention. Kim is hilarious and I would definitely take her again.
engaging lectures, midterm "tests" are timed, so prepare ahead of time and read the assigned book. very impactful course and kim is a very kind professor.

She is very kind and flexible. However, the readings can be a lot to read each week. The discussion board which you have to do once every other week, took me a long time to finish it everytime. You have to make a podcast at the end of the semester, which was fun to do. Tests and quizzes are open notes, but you have to study for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall pretty good, lectures were kinda fast pace but interesting material. Exam material isn't too bad, but you only have about a minute per question which makes it rough. There aren't a ton of assignments, but the big ones are a bit of work. I'd say it's more than a GE should be. Prof Lopez was nice though and had engaging lectures.

Excellent lecture and clearly very passionate about teaching. Test were very difficult and a lot to complete in the time given, but all other assignments were enjoyable and unlike any class I have ever taken. Would recommend taking again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take her class if you can!! Amazing professor, she really cares about her students and all of the assignments/graded aspects felt really enriching. This was my favorite course I've taken in all of my four years. Awesome professor, awesome course

This GE was way more work than expected. The 55-minute exams had many questions and long written responses. The professor talks fast, expects you to keep up, and includes her political views in lectures. Most of the class is just listening to her talk. She is nice and understanding, but the heavy workload makes this a class I wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Always engaging.  Interesting lectures.  Pretty laid back and funny.
Excellent Professor. Always fair. Always shows great knowledge and excitement for the course material.

Kim is a great professor. This is my third course with her. She always has interesting and engaging lectures and shows excitement for the subject she's teaching. She's also very supportive, although she is strict when it comes to deadlines. Either it's in or it's not. Rarely can you have extra time unless you have an approved excuse. Very Fair!

So as you have probably gathered by now this isn't a terribly hard class. It is just very tedious & annoying. The test extended responses take A LOT of time and normally it is during midterm weeks where you have harder classes & bigger priorities.This is going to be a class that you will have to put effort in for the tests. Tough grader, no rubric.

I love this class. I did not expect to enjoy a class about death and dying but Kim is so informative and intelligent in the topic that the class is enjoyable. If you pay attention during in class lectures and take notes this class is a breeze. The projects in the class were very interesting to me and the tests were a bit challenging but open note.

Super easy class but felt tedious at times. Exams (3) were open note and timed but very easy. Huge extra credit opportunity, easy assignments, random attendance sometimes so do go. Also rlly important to attend lecture as all info she says is important for exams. Kim is so super kind!

Overall Kim was one of the nicest professors I've had here at OSU and she is very caring. Her class is not that difficult as long as you pay attention and put in effort. The tests are decently difficult and do require review of material beforehand.

Kim is great. She is one of the best sociology professors I've had here at OSU. SOC3630 is definitely not a blow-off class, it is important to pay attention in class and study for the tests- they are online/open note but still quite hard. Regardless, lectures are engaging and she is quite understanding of personal emergencies.

Excellent, caring professor. Not the most engaging lectures but sometimes we would do fun activities. Study a bit for the exams and you'll be okay. 1 course paper but the book for it was very interesting. Grading was fair and there were bonus on exams and then bonus discussion board at end of the class. Would definitely take more of her classes

Kim is very knowledgeable. She cares much about the material that is taught, and I learned so much in the class. I would take her again in the future, if I could! Her class is weighted very heavy with tests, and with a paper. Make sure to study, pay attention, go to class, and spend a decent amount of time to have a good grade on the paper.

Loved this class and Kim presented the material really well. You have to work for it though as the exams can be tough and the course paper requires a significant investment in time to get a good grade. Great instructor overall and invites lots of guest speakers which adds to the application of the course material to real life.

Kim is literally amazing! She is such a sweetheart and taught a difficult class with grace, kindness, and openness. She does everything in her power to make the class stimulating, but it is on the lecture heavy side. I can't wait to take another class with her!

Although this was a very emotional tolling class, Kim made sure that everybody in the class was mentally okay with what we were learning. She gives out a study sheet before the tests and the tests are easy if you study and know the material. If you show up to class, you are more than likely to get an A.
Amazing instructor!

My familiarity with the content of this course made it easy in a sense but the format of this professors course was kinda wacky. There are two books used and one of them is an interesting/odd book about hookup culture in college, the other is a more traditional textbook. I comfortably got an A, but it did take completing some involved assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I've taken 3 classes with Kim and I loved all of them. Her lectures are really engaging, and it is clear that she cares about her students. The classes aren't super easy, but the expectations are clear and there are chances for bonus points. She is really caring and very passionate about the subjects she teaches. Best professor I've had at OSU

Won't get an A+ unless your assignments exactly appease her rubric to her comprehension, unfair grading. However, passionate about her field and very educated. She will discuss with you if you have concerns. She does not care very much about personal circumstances. Tough class. Heavy material. Little compassion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly have no clue how Kim Lopez has a 4.9 / 5 on here. She lacks any sort of accountability and she is not flexible AT ALL. She also pressured a student into sharing something they were obviously not comfortable with sharing, which shows a complete lack of care for that student's feelings. The worst professor I've ever had by far.
Kim Lopez is passionate in the subject matter and inspirational as a professor. Easy classes, study hard for exams and read the materials.

I really enjoyed Kims lectures, they were always very engaging and she explained the concepts very well. She was also very flexible and understanding with students situations and had very sensible late work policy. In my class we were allowed to drop 3 assignments (except really big ones) no questions asked. Any class with her is one worth taking

Be professor Ive ever had. Shes very passionate about what she does and it shows in the class. She wanted to help me outside of the class and that was amazing. I recommend her to every friend!! I would definitely join her class again!

She is an amazing lecturer and you can tell she is passionate about the subject matter. This is one of my favorite classes but I would warn anyone who is SLDS or has a bad laptop. She is not flexible and a really harsh grader. My grade dropped a whole letter grade halfway through the semester because she refused to work wth me on a testing mishap.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kim is a great professor. She is very clear on what she expects for assignments. Class is lecture-heavy so sometimes it gets boring. Tests are all open note and mostly based on the study guide. She is very easy to contact and sometimes puts out little messages regarding mental health, which are very appreciated. Overall, very manageable course.

Kim is one of the best professors I have had at Ohio State. She cares about her students so much and is very understanding. Although this class does require effort, the material and books we went over were very interesting and very important no matter your major. Kim is a great lecturer, and caring individual! I highly recommend this class.

Kim was the best professor I have ever had! I am finishing up her course right now on Death and Dying and plan on taking her course on Medical Soc, Fall '21. She is incredibly nice and is willing to work with you if needed. Her tests could be challenging but if you study you will be fine. She is a genuine person and truly cares about your success.
One of the best professors I had at CSCC. Dr. Lopez is caring, understanding and most importantly I like the way she teaches. If you do your work you will get an easy A class.

Kim is my favorite professor that I have ever had. She is flexible, communicates content clearly, and is always available for questions. Lectures are mandatory, but she makes lecture so interesting that I never wanted to skip. Her courses are reading-heavy, but it pays off to read them. I would recommend her for any class at the University.

She is clearly passionate about the subject and knows what she's talking about. The class material was very interesting. The tests were difficult but not impossible, and I always ended up doing better than I expected. The book for the class is interesting but I skimmed it, and I didn't use the textbook except for the final paper.

Kim is a great teacher that cares a lot about her students. She expects a lot out you, but it never seemed like an unreasonable amount of work. It may seem like there are a lot of assignments at first, but they are all pretty easy if you give yourself time and don't wait until the last minute to start. Tests aren't a cakewalk, but not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Kim was a great professor! I felt that she genuinely had a passion for her subject. She doesn't round up/give extra credit, which isn't an issue for many but for some it could be. Her exams were tough, but not "trick questions" if that makes sense. You'll have to study before the exams, but you won't be shocked by questions if you've read materials

Dr. Lopez is a great professor who clearly enjoys what she teaches. Discussion is a big factor of this class and is what makes it exciting. She gives easy extra credit and her tests aren't too hard as long as you do some decent studying. The book assigned for this class is super interesting and the paper due at the end of the semester is easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Lopez shows real interest in what she's teaching and appreciates when students participate. Attendance is taken every class. If you miss more than she allows, you are not granted bonus activities, which is what left me .41% away from an A. ATTEND CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I learned a lot from this class. Not a tough grader--if you write the papers you get full points of them. You are going to study a lot for exams, and they are a bit hard, but no worries, the bonus is 5% of the total grade, so an easy A even if you don't do well on exams. Kim is very sweet and patient.

Kim is the best. Good stories, interesting class discussions, and genuinely cares about you as a student and a person. Most of the assignments are fun or at least interesting. Tests are a little challenging and look for very specific information, but there's a lot of extra credit offered (5% bonus for 3 discussions + other EC activities).

Kim was a great Professor and her lectures were always very interesting. I truly learned so much in this class, even about myself. Had 3 tests and other little assignments. Not hard as long as you study for the material! Did a lot of reading out of the book for weekly quizzes, definitely will need it. She really wants all to do their best!

I have taken Kim for her death class and her child/society class and they were similar. You have to go to class because the powerpoint aren't filled out with key words. You have to read the books to pass the quizzes and tests. Kim is really kind, but she definitely makes you do way too much busy work for a 2000 and 3000 level classes. Mixed opinion
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Shes a sweet lady will try her best to help you pass. However, the work is entirely too much the tests are too difficult for this to be a 3000 level class. If you dont show up you wont be able to take advantage of the 4% bonus. Would I take her again? Idk
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easy A if you're willing to go to every lecture. Hardest part was 5-6 page paper (choose own prompt and deadline). Exams were very detailed but follow the study guide and you probably won't get lower than a B on them. At the end of the semester she gave a bonus assignment for a 4% bonus on final course grade. Don't need WL textbook need HW
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kim is super nice, however her class is very time consuming. Her exams were far harder than they needed to be and the quizzes were almost impossible to get a 100 on (but there's a lot of bonus in the class, so getting an A is def possible). Theres several hour long videos to watch and you have to read an entire book (60 page chapters then a quiz).

Heres the deal. Kim is very nice in person, but has FAR too high of expectations for a 2000 level class. The chapters of the book are long and boring, and quizes and exams rely a good portion on them. She needs to cut down on the busy work for the class. Far too many small assignments that take a lot of effort for little portions of the grade.

First class I've taken with her & it definitely won't be my last. There's 3 exams but she gives you study guides. There's articles/videos you have to do before class but they're not bad & you have to do a paper on a book. She makes you comfortable to speak out & the material is so easy to remember so exams aren't bad at all. 10/10 recoccommend!!

Professor Lopez is very kind and empathetic, and works to make sure that student's stress levels are low. Textbook isn't necessary, but there are reading quizzes on the book Medical Apartheid. Her questions can be tricky, but she has a lot of grades and extra credit. There are a lot of opportunities to get an A, and even a large bonus project.

Kim is the best professor I have ever had. The class itself was extremely intriguing and interesting. She was so relatable and chill, but the class was still structured and well executed. She is the type of professor I want to stay in contact with and take more classes from. Thisclass truly opened my eyes to a brand new world I didn't know existed.

Kim is amazing! I have taken her for four classes now, and would highly recommend. She genuinely cares about the students and is passionate about the material. She is also very helpful when it comes to life and school advice outside of her class. Incredible classes to take. 10/10
She is so nice. And she explains the questions so patiently. I feel so warm and relaxed when talking with her.

Kim is the best professor I've ever had! do the assignments and you'll get an A easy! She's not only an easy professor, she is so caring and understanding! TAKE HER CLASS if you get the chance, she's amazing!

I have taken this class (Medical Sociology 3630) and her Death and Dying class (2290) and 3630 was much harder. She is a very nice lady and cares about her students, but her exams are tough and have a ton of irrelevant and unnecessary info. Attendance is mandatory and she tests over specific numbers from guest speakers, so take good notes.

She's a very sweet and understanding professor. I would love to have a professional relationship with her, she is the best. Must come to class, attendance taken. Activities, online discussions, and quizzes, along with three tests. Very manageable, GPA booster and very different material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Kim is an amazing teacher. I really enjoyed 3630 because of her. Her test style is different but if you pay attention in class and study the notes then you'll be good to go. She's accessible outside the class and truly cares about her students. Tests and papers but relatively easy as long as you know whats going on. Also enjoyed having presenters.

Kim is an amazing and inspiring teacher. I took 2290 and 3630. The tests are not hard. Just study -memorize- her powerpoints and you'll be good as golden. She's very helpful and gives out a good amount of bonus points. Make sure you attend class, she does take attendance & always ask for help if needed. She's very accessible outside the classroom.

Kim is great! Her exams are hard but you easily learn how she tests and she also realizes if the test was harder. With extra credit I got high A's on 2/3 of the exams. I had her for SOC of Death and Dying. Overall a great class. I actually had a family member die in the semester so the class was hard mentally but still good. Do the extra credit too

With such specific and confusing attention to detail, Kim Lopez appears to have not mastered the material that she is teaching. Be prepared to be extensive in essays and writing responses, because she is more that willing to deduct points for a minute detail missed. Also, let this be your warning; do the extra credit.
The only thing hard about her classes are the exams but she has enough bonus assignments and participation/assignments to get an A.
Definitely trying to get her again. I legitimately enjoyed going to class with her as my professor.

She's easily the most inspirational teacher I've ever had. I loved her class, although it was a little tougher than I thought. You have to put in a little effort, also know the vocab on the study guides, it's essential to passing her tests.

I love Kim, but some things do get on your nerves. There are lot of documentaries to watch outside of class with quizzes in class on the days assigned. Its a great and interesting class, but just be prepared for a lot of outside class work with volunteer hours and documentaries. Kim is a great professor and gives extra credit IF YOU SHOW UP.

Professor Lopez was amazing. She understands the material because she has experienced it first-hand. Never used the book, provided power points with fill in the blank, multiple easy extra credit opportunities. 3 mini papers that took under an hour, weekly quizzes over videos (easy to watch), interesting speakers. Genuinely cared about her students.

Professor Lopez is definitely one of my favorite professor she always made class interesting. Even though it was a death and dying class, she didn't make it depressing.  It makes you think about the future and the important things in life.

Best professor I have ever had! She loves teaching and helping her students, and her classes are very interesting. You can choose not to go to class, but she does take attendance and at the end of the semester she offers extra credit opportunity for those who did not miss more than 3 or 4 classes. I wish all the professors were like her!

Kim Lopez is such a nice professor. She's funny and we did some pretty cool experiments and watched some fascinating videos. The tests were multiple choice and definitions with no word bank but there were bonus opportunities. You only really needed the textbook for the papers. Final was take home. Which was awesome.

This class was one of the best/easiest I have taken so far. If you show up to class and do well on tests you will definitely get an A. There are also 15 extra credit points that can be added to your total grade. Kim is an awesome professor, and her lectures are funny and interesting. Definitely take this class!
She is nice and humorous. I like the interaction in the class. Participation is very important. It counts 10 percent and you can only get slides note on class.

Kim is one of the best professors I've had. She is extremely personable and she really cares about her students doing well in the class. Attending class is the best way to succeed in her class, as she does quizzes and class activities for points. Offers extra credit, and the tests are really fair if you go to class. Overall, awesome professor

Takes random attendance checks but the class is really interesting. Her tests are not difficult if you study for them. Going to class is the easiest way to get a good grade. She's very helpful if you ever need anything.

Very attainable A in this class as well as an enjoyable class. Professor Lopez makes it very easy, and she is funny, and excellent with helping you when needed. Tips for exams are easily know your terms perfectly and you are fine. Also read the book and go to lectures. Exams use questions found sometimes only in the book, and also only in lecture.
I definitely recommend taking her for any class. She is really nice and does everything she can to help students.

Best professor hands down! She has the best lectures and always finds ways to keep the class interested. I loved her class. I wish I could take it all over again. I would definately suggest taking any class she offers for GE requirements!

Kim truly wants to see her students succeed. She offers bonus points to students and obviously has a passion for the material.  Tests get progressively easier once you get a feel for them.  I was very grateful of her ability to accomodate entenuating circumstances, and she cares for her students as human beings.
She's so Niceeeeeeeeee
Study for the terms (not extensively) and do the extra credit to ensure an A.
As long as you turn in each of the 4 assignments you will get an A.
Great Teacher. Fun Class.

Mrs. Lopez is one of the nicest teachers I have had in awhile.Papers are short in length and deal with cool topics. Classes are fun to attend because she gets the class involved and makes the topics interesting. If you get the opportunity to take one of her classes Do it, def worth it

Grind out recitations, as the TAs are typically able to slow things a lot as opposed to Valentin during the lecture. However, Valentin's notes are quite a great resource to review come exam time. Exams are not particularly tricky, and quizzes are just like the practices.

Although I think his resources are great, such as test and exam reviews, he moves wayy too fast in lecture and kind of already expects you to have some base knowledge on the topic he discusses. other than that, he's a great professor and you can tell he wants everyone to move on to the next step, adorable and great professor overall.

Lectures didn't include exam-style problem-solving, to the point that I left every lecture confused, and learned all of the material in recitation. While weekly quizzes weren't too difficult, the lecture's lack of problem solving made them much more stressful than they needed to be.

Valentin is an awesome professor, he is funny and cares about student success but sometimes teaches as if we already know the material. Personally I learned more from my recitation/TA but his lectures were still helpful. The math department doesn't try to screw you over, the midterms/quizzes are very similar to the practice ones. No cheat sheets.

Professor Kunz likes to heavily teach theory in a math class with all engineers who do not want theory taught to them. His lectures are very hard to follow and understand. His writing is hard to understand. He makes simple topics extremely complicated. I will say his exams were easy, exactly like the practice exams he gives us to study for.

Valentine is a very good professor and truly knows his stuff. He will definitely prepare you well but every now and then he confuses you in lecture. His accent is sometimes hard to understand but overall not a huge deal at all. He gives bonus points on all exams and it helps out the grade a ton.

Kunz was a very good professor and was always easy to reach. Getting used to his writing was a little difficult but doable. My main concern with this class was his lectures. Lectures were pretty theory heavy, and extremely fast paced. If you take this class make sure to remind him slow down and go through full problems without skipping steps.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Except the trash boardwork and puzzling accent, he's a good teacher. The lecture includes may concepts and theories. The recitation will be helpful. However, I would not recommend take his class if there's other options.
he's adorable and a great professor - easy to access outside of class and very caring!!

Dr. Kunz is so sweet! Sometimes it's a bit hard to understand his accent and handwriting, but you get used to it. He's quite passionate about what he does and cares about his students. Actually wants you to learn the course material. A couple quizzes throughout the semester that are quite easy, and exams are quite similar to the practice.

Professor Kunz is extremely caring, and is highly knowledgeable regarding the course content. His handwriting isn't always easy to read, and I often felt I learned more from recitation and YouTube than his lectures due to their theoretical nature. Good professor overall and he will continue to grow as he becomes more experienced.

Good prof. but didn't care for his methods of teaching. He writes his own lecture notes and it's very hard at times to read his handwriting. It's easy to get behind so make sure you pay attention in class but pretty easy to get caught up compared to Calc 2. Material is challenging but mostly because it's 2 credit hours so you underestimate it.
I love Valentin, he's a cutie patootie and 10/10 professor - wish I could take a class with him again!!
I really enjoyed this class. He provides everything that is needed to succeed and is very happy to help at office hours. He is also a very kind person.

He is an amazing professor and is also very kind and chill. His handwriting and notation is confusing at times but it didn't harm my learning. His practice exams were pretty much the same as the real exams and I think if you attend every lecture and recitation it would be hard to not get close to an A.

Prof Kunz has been one of my favorite lecturers. His handwriting and notation is confusing at times. There were plenty of classes I left feeling like nothing made sense but the following class, recitations, and the online textbook were very helpful. Exams are straightforward and the class is an easy B if you study and attend lecture/recitation.

Was an okay professor, he has a very thick accent and his handwriting is super hard to read. Exams were exactly like the practice, and he posted all of his notes online. We had a few homework assignments, but were super helpful and an easy way to boost your grade. There is a slight curve at the end of the class.

Great professor, definitely cared about your success in the class and how he was able to make his lectures better. The quizzes in recitation were fairly easy and so were the exams. Only complaint is that he usually starts a few min early for lectures and some of the way he writes greek letters are a bit difficult to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lenny is one of those TA's that is hated on for the simple fact that he makes the lab component of class difficult to push students—however, he cares about his class and provides good feedback. His exam reviews are extremely helpful and his attentiveness to the material can really help on the section of exams that are lecture-specific.

Dr. Lenny has been my favorite TA ever. He truly cares about his students and is super funny, a lot of people hated on him but didn't take the time to get to know him. His exam reviews were extremely helpful, and my best recommendation is to do the textbook reading weekly and study to stay up to date with things for the recitation reviews!
Bad TA, makes us play rip off plants vs zombies every day. Sus stains on all shirts.

Very tiring lecturer, makes you do zombie games as a class review instead of getting started with the lab  right away. Skipped over slides very quickly, got annoyed if you asked to go back. Very ironic guy and some people might like him but definitely not for everyone if you are not used to fast pace.
Hide and seek game of instructions. Mind games. Will expect you to know things, disregarding your background knowledge. BEST way to spend your friday night.

Explanations were very frequently unclear and unhelpful. Turned recitation into a pointless and confusing “zombie game” every week. Entire lab was often left unsure of how to proceed. If you see this name on your schedule, you may want to switch labs.

I had Dr. Wang as my TA for bio1113. He seems to find enjoyment in stressing the students out. He doesn't explain the labs well at all but he is nice when you ask questions. His review sessions for the tests are helpful but way harder than the actual tests. Overall, he tried to make the class harder than it needed to be.

overqualified lab instructor, was definitely a teachers pet. Lab starts with a long useless recitation team game, with questions that are harder than the questions on the test. nitpicky grader, and doesn't really care to explain the experiment (he just zips through the post lab answers). very dependent on ur group. review sessions are good though

I've never made a review, but this TA needs to be warned about. You can tell he hates teaching, he always flies through lab with bare minimum instruction and at x15 speed. He seems to enjoy seeing you stressed by constantly saying how hard the exam is. I asked about the best study resources and he literally just shrugged. Avoid to save your grade!

This dude has a PhD taking TA's job and salary and love to stand on moral high ground. Often use authority to scare students off and explains everything in Mach 5 speed. Does not care about how his student do in his lab section. Take someone else if you don't want your grade to drop through the entire alphabet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: PhD teaching bio lab for 7 years, all he does is treat students horribly. Made us do an experiment he knew would fail just to laugh in our faces when it didn't work. Gave 14.99/15 on a lab report just to be petty. Someone got 20% on a quiz. No help, no feedback, just pure disrespect. This guy is on a power trip. Avoid him like the plague.

You can tell he's trying but I don't think he should be in a position of teaching. There were many times we used equipment that some people had never used (and easy to break) and he didn't speak a word about how to use them. He didn't like answering questions. Very smart and knowledgeable but did not seem to understand that not EVERYONE has a PhD

def knows his stuff but doesn't know how to teach intro bio students. will go through info so fast and you have to catch it to do well. doesn't explain lab procedures at all. most of the time we didn't know how to perform experiments. very true that he LOVES to ask questions like “ready for the next test” “ready for the next quiz?” was not fun :(

If you are coming to this class in hopes of learning biology- that will not really happen. VERY intelligent person, but struggles to teach to intro students. Kind of just quickly tells you what to write in lab. He does try to connect with students, and if you connect, you will receive better help. Also, office hours are helpful in prep for exams!
Pick a different TA, he is very strict and does not explain well

Is all over the place all he cares about is getting out of class quickly. He'll just throw information at you without you knowing what any of it means, spends more time asking if we're looking forward to the exam then actually teaching. He does however hold review sessions that have been kinda helpful.
just no, very tough grader and makes mean comments to those who get a question wrong
He was a tough grader but his critiques made it easy to learn from mistakes. You knew exactly what was wrong and why. When asked questions, his answers were clear and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Fun person, but VERY VERY strict in grading. He reads every sentence you write and finds every point you miss. Then, you lose points here and there.

alright dr lenny has gotten some bad reviews but he is really not THAT bad. the recitation is annoying and he isnt very helpful for the lab portion but he literally tells you the answers for the lab reports and tells you what will be on the lab quizzes. he is just a little awkward but hes actually so nice. love this guy!

Recitation is a long game with convoluted question delivery. We get no review or deeper explanation out of the content, simply play the game for an hour then do lab. Procedural demonstration and explanation is minimal at best, many technique issues prolonged labs. He also demeans incorrect answers as a joke, discouraging figure engagement.

I had a terrible time in this class. Avoid this TA if possible. I asked him about my extended response answers on an exam and he read them in front of my group and proceeded to tell my why I was wrong and make fun of me. He also continued to make jokes about my responses in future labs. Also if you think it will be a quick lab you're wrong.

He's a horrible TA, genuinely take it with anybody else. He grades a lot harsher than all the other TAs and laughs when you get a question wrong in lab. Lab quizzes are also borderline impossible. He also has a game during recitation that you genuinely get nothing out of, it's boring and takes up tons of lab time. Never take him frl

He was so unhelpful, and often left us more confused. He would not answer any of our questions, even when our group clearly stated we were having struggles. Furthermore, he was particularly distasteful towards me, and would often ignore me when I tried to participate. This truly affected my overall ability to learn and my learning environment.

If you expect to be able to not put in any effort, he will not be fun. He can be a bit tough grading and his labs are long but he teaches you the material well. He is accessible outside of class, approachable, and genuinely cares that you understand the material. His online review sessions were really helpful and so I recommend going to those!

I think he is a nice guy, but lab with him was so stressful. I couldn't understand his directions; his questions were confusing, and asking him for help honestly made me more confused. He is the head TA so he grades lab reports super harshly.

Don't take bio lab with this instructor. He's such a hard grader and makes lab quizzes impossible. He's really not mentally there and has no idea how to teach individuals. If you are confused or need help, he just won't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very rude and a harsh grader. He really enjoyed seeing students confused and did nothing to help. He is intelligent but a horrible teacher.

He is just not mentally here - he makes objectively easy directions impossible to complete and I have never left a lab with a better understanding, only frustrated and confused. I truly do not understand how he was approved - he is not a good TA save urself the frustration.

Dr. Lenny has very high expectations of his students and expects them to know far beyond the introductory biology course. He tries to explain things as if he is talking to a professional and leaves students much more confused afterwards. Recitation is useless. His lab quizzes are very difficult and the labs almost always go past the end time.
Dr. Lenny is a great TA! To exceed in his class, participation is key! He is a very experienced and knowledgeable TA who has a lot to offer for pre-med students. He helped me get into a research lab!
Super tough grader, expects you to know what he wants even when the question is vague. Not good at answering questions about
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Doesnt try to help and laughs at your confusion.

Dr. linan is a very tough grader. He will take off points and the labs are long. Given that its online, he is not very understanding. Prepare for working very hard just to get points taken off over a small mistake.
He is so confusing and his rubric for grading is very specific. Online learning with this professor was so difficult. He does not set his students up for success.

He was so disrespectful and rude to my lab group. If you have him tried to switch lab times, he thinks your failure is funny. Honestly made me hate biology with a burning passion. The class is not bad but your TA makes or breaks your grade and he has no problem breaking it.

Dr Lenny is a knowledgeable lab TA but explains things in a way only he understands and expects you to just pick up on things right away. He is a very tough grader and if you dont put something the way he would word it he will mark you points off. Rushes students to finish labs even if you dont understand and makes you feel more confused.

Dr. Lenny is a tough but fair TA for biology. He does grade a little bit tough but he cares about his students and wants to help you. Also, he does a really nice job prepping students for the lab practical. If you can, I recommend having him as your TA. Get to know him, he's a really nice guy.

Dr. Lenny is the least helpful TA I have ever had the misfortune of dealing with. He does not care about student learning, only proving his intellectual superiority. He is a picky and condescending grader and lead to an overall disheartening experience.
Dr. Lenny is one tough TA, but really fair and pretty funny. I highly recommend spending the time to get to know him, but be aware of his lab quizzes, they are really tricky.

Professor Kroner never fails to make class entertaining and fun for students. He makes the hard material understanding and is willing to help any student. I would take every class with him as my professor if I could. He is a fair grader and LOVES talking about sports. TAKE HIM

Dr. Kroner knows how to approach hard topics in a way that makes it interesting and enjoyable. Extremely personable and wants you to learn and not struggle. By far the best lab I have taken and just a great all around guy to know even outside of lab.
IF YOU READ TEXTBOOK YOU WILL PASS
He is a nice professor and makes students feel welcome

When I took Kroners class it was all 8 am lectures, but he tried something new and recorded them and posted them. We had to do an alternate assignment to receive credit for attendance. I would say hes a decent teacher but for a majority of the class I taught myself all the material with the help of youtube. he gives lots of practice materials!

Dr Kroner is a good guy and you can tell he genuinely likes to teach. However his lectures are very confusing and fast paced. If you didn't take ap chem it's hard to  keep up. Gives lots of resources but i honestly learned nothing

Dr. Kroner is a very good professor who prepares you well for exams. Besides him having bad handwriting, he provides many study materials (practice quizzes/midterms) to help prepare you for the exams. Just make sure to prepare well for the midterms, as they carry a significant weight in your grade.

Dr. Kroner is one of those professors who truly loves what they do. I never attended his office hours, but just going based solely on how he acted in lecture, I can tell he is a nice guy. I felt as though his notes were extremely digestible, and overall, the class wasn't difficult if you paid attention.

Dr. Kroner is an overall great professor. Besides his handwriting being bad, he makes sure to go over every chapter in great detail, which I never had to read from the textbook. He also makes sure to provide a lot of study materials (practice quizzes and practice midterms), which help you have good preparation before each midterm.

The lectures are set up assuming you've read the book on that section beforehand. I never read the book but the summaries at the end of each chapter helped. He explained most concepts clearly, provided a lot of helpful practice quizzes, and alternate ways to get credit for if you didn't go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's nice and genuinely seems interested in what hes talking about. His hand writing is horrible so if you miss something it's hard to figure out what's going on which is literally the only thing people don't like about him. He posts lectures and if you dont wanna go he has alternative assignments you can do instead which only take like 30 minutes

If you just took chem in high school, you'll do just fine with him. If not, you'll struggle. He approaches the class assuming that you know a lot of the material which just isn't the case for a lot of people. He was nice and funny, and helpful when I emailed him about missed assignments. His hand writing is AWFUL! My textbook was my best friend!!!

He did a great job at being accessible outside of class and during office hours. His lectures and slides were pretty straight forward and he clearly gave hints to what was mostly likely to be on exams.

Steve is a great guy and very passionate about chemistry. He is very easy to go up and talk to after lectures and will set aside his own time to come to lectures early to review a day before an exam. His knowledge of chemistry is very concrete and explains concepts extremely well. I would take him again 10/10 times.

He's truly a great prof. He listens to your concerns and will go over topics however many times you need in order to understand especially in office hours. I had him explain a concept for like 30 minutes until I finally understood it. In order to pass the class, you need to read the textbook though but he gives lots of ways to succeed in class.

He tends to go on tangents and glaze over the exam material, but the slides are clear and easy to study, with lots of extra practice provided. As long as you teach yourself some of the more confusing topics, and study outside of class, you'll do fine. He's also extremely understanding and helpful.

Great Gen Chem experience that is low stakes but teaches you what you need to know. Lectures are a bit boring, but he gives tons of resources to reinforce your understanding. Tests are easy and there are practice exams available.

Dr Kroner is a pretty good teacher. He's very passionate about chemistry and gave a lot of good answers to my questions. The homework (around 6 questions) is due before every lecture which is kind of a pain but it's preferable to having 20 questions due every week. He teaches well  but make sure to update ur notes with info from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Kroner is kind, helpful, and very intelligent. This course was straightforward: show up and do your work and you get an A. Many of the experiments are computational, so you're only in the lab for 6 weeks. Not much take home work other than writing a final lab report. And I learned a lot of relevant, transferable research skills, so 10/10 course.

Dr. Kroner makes the difficult content of this lab easily digestible if you pay attention and participate. He sets clear expectations for assignments and is always available to help if needed. The due dates are also pretty lenient and he is very understanding of unforeseen circumstances. Fantastic professor overall.

Lectures were pretty boring, so it's hard to be engaged at 8am. Attendance not required. Posts lecture recordings. Highly recommend reading the textbook. Weekly homework: digital assignments after each lecture (9-11 questions). Provides lots of resources for studying. Always offered help outside of class. Do the practice exams to do well on exams!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's great. His writing can be hard to read at times, but him posting lectures is so so helpful. He's also great at helping you understand content in office hours, so go! If you go to lecture, pay attention, read the book, and do the problems, you should be fine.

THIS MAN'S HANDWRITING IS GODAWFUL. You can't even tell what variable we are talking about in the notes. CHEMISTRY IS ONE OF THISE CLASSES WHERE YOU HAVE TO UNDERSTAND THE PROF'S NOTES.  Sure there are other resources you can use but at that point I should've just self studied for the AP Chem exam and gotten the credit in high school. praying for u
Dr. Kroner is a great professor who makes the class engaging. Utilize the practice quizzes and textbook to prepare for exams. Unstuckstudy can also be a helpful study tool alongside other resources.
Amazing lectures. If you go to the lectures, you will be OK!
Difficult course, good guy!

His lecture notes get messy but if you're following along it makes sense. Homework is divided into three smaller sections (9-11 questions) a week and he gives us a lot of study resources like practice exams for midterms. His main piece of advice for studying is to read the textbook. He loves showing off his dog.
I really did not mind this professor. He is really nice but his handwriting for notes is messy. He gives a ton of resources to help you out.
Awesome guy who enjoys what he does. Make sure to utilize the practice quizzes as they prepare you for the exams.
Dr. Kroner is one of the best professors that I have ever come across because of his amazing lectures, accessibility, and friendliness.

Dr.Kroner made lectures laid back and fun.  He was very approachable and made it clear that he was available for any help we needed outside of class.  His lecture content is solid but what helped me the most was reading the textbook on my own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Good lectures that covered everything on the midterms. Dr. Kroner was also happy to help answer questions after class. Apart from that, the chem department does a great job of giving practice exams that are very similar to the actual midterms.
Easy on homework assignments. Very caring and funny. I slacked off and the midterms got me.

he was great, the chem department as a whole is hard so the exams were difficult if you did not prepare but he gives you a ton of practice material, he also has a ton of grades that are purely participation or showing up to recitation so he tries to not make the class too unbearable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. kroner was so sweet! He would always answer our questions during the lecture and encourage us as well! His handwriting was a little messy and hard to read, especially with an 8 AM class. Prepare to watch a lot of youtube vids online; you have to put work outside of class! The exams make or break your grade.

Dr. Kroner is an excellent lecturer for Chem 1210. I learned a lot from him, has a good sense of humor, and seems like a very nice guy. His handwriting can be hard to follow, but the slides are typed out. Very approachable and often does cool demonstrations in class. Would recommend him for Chem 1210!

His handwriting is awful, and his pace can be slow at times, but he always finished teaching the materials in time for the midterms with an extra lecture or two dedicated to review. Overall, he was a very nice person and a decent professor.
Great chem 1210 professor! Probably the best chem professor at osu. Super kind and always willing to help.

I did not like Kroner. He was a messy writer and it wad impossible to read his notes. He also didn’t finish the content for exams until the day of the exam. I had peers who took Prof Fus and had a whole week of studying. Kroner basically just read off of the slides. Kroner went slow and his explanations didn’t make the hard concepts easy.

The biggest advice I can give is to read the textbook before each lecture. Thankfully, Mr. Kroner made an assignment for each lecture that shows which sections he will be covering that day. The exams have a lot of trick questions that many people fall for. Exams took up 62.5% of your grade, so make sure you take them seriously. Go to recitation!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He seems like a great human being. He presents the material well. Best advice I can give is read the book alongside watching the lectures and attempt most of the 17 trillion or so provided practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good lecturer very nice guy. Handwriting a bit messy but other than that he's a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's a good prof and cares about his students. Attend his office hours and be specific with your questions.

Dr. K is a nice guy and is always willing to help during office hours or by email. His handwriting is messy, but you should be able to copy what hes saying. We learn material really close to the midterm which can be annoying, but he does offer a lot of review. Chem is hard in general so be prepared to do a lot outside of class regardless of ur prof
So far he has been really good at explaining material. Luckily does not give a lot of homework compared to other chem teachers. Probably best professor for the chem 1210 course.
god himself could not decipher this guys handwriting. looking at notes or work absolutely useless because his handwriting is so atrocious.

Kroner is one of the worst chem lecturers. His handwriting is so messy and he talks in literally slow motion. We never get through all the material before the exam because he goes so slow. He does provide a lot of practice problems which are helpful, but the lectures are not worth going to at all - I can teach myself the content better.

I had Dr. Kroner this past year during the fall semester. His handwriting is pretty messy and he kinda scribbles when he writes since he goes pretty fast, but I was able to keep up with his pace. He always came to class with a good attitude and while he didn't have a lot of control over testing, he does care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Kroner is the best and is always willing to help.

Dr. Kroner is really great amongst a really hard class. He does not curve or bump or anything, so do not expect that. He cares about his students and wants you to do well. Make sure you go to lecture, reading the book is also extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Kroner is really caring and a great lecturer. He tries his best to get the material across and if you don't understand he'll continue to explain it to you many different ways in office hours. He provides optional pre- lecture and post-lecture videos on each topic which are super helpful for tricky material.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Chem sucks and he didn't make it any better. Take with another professor if u have the chance but he isn't horrible.

Some reviews here review the class itself and not the prof. Chem is organized at the dept. level, so profs aren't in control of exams. With that said, Dr. Kroner is a good professor. He provides many practice problems which are BEYOND helpful, but I often found myself a little confused during lectures. Read the book before lecture to avoid this.

Dr. Kroner is a great person and but a horrible teacher. He goes so fast and will sometimes skip over things that can be asked on tests. He teaches the content as if we already have a good understanding of it and leaves you confused. He gives good resources like daily quizzes which help, but is not able to teach the content. I would not pick him.

Dr Kroner is alright. Gen Chem is really hard and he explained the subjects as good as he could. The amount of homework was a lot though, basically one for every single lecture. There are review packages before every test which is helpful but if you dont attend the lectures they wont be of any good. The tests are very hard so prepare to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I found out fast that I do not enjoy chemistry and so I switched my major right off the bat, however Kroner is probably the only thing that got me through the class. His lectures were helpful, gave us outside resources to study/practice, and overall he just did a well job and if I had to take another chem class it would only be with him teaching.

He is so great, I can't use text to express my happiness CHEM 4410 is one of the most impressive classes I ever take. I can remember, How many times, I failed to burn the organic substance, How many times, I don't know how to use the instrument, but you patiently gave the instructions How many time, you remind me to wear the face mask.

All he is responsible for are the lectures (he has no clue what happens in lab), but he does a good job of going beyond that and providing extra resources. He is really chill, but you have to advocate for yourself in this class. His explanations make sense to me.

As everyone says, Gen Chem 1 is very difficult no matter what professor you have. Dr. Kroner really takes the topics in gen chem and helps you understand them. Top Hat is used but bonus points for correct answers allow for missed classes. Dynamic study modules in Mastering allow you to get 100% on the homework by being bonus which helps your grade.

Gen Chem 1 is hard in general, but Dr. Kroner is an amazing professor who truly cares about his students and desires for everyone to master the material.
