For each midterm and the final, he provides several very accessible resources that are useful when studying. Not an easy A, but definitely possible if you put in the time and effort.

Dr. Kroner was an amazing professor for General Chemistry I. He provided us with a lot of resources to practice and prepare for exams. There are 3 midterms and a final, which do mean that you need to put in a lot of work to get a good grade. Lab is a lot of work, but recitation is simply a participation grade.

Everyone knows OSU chem sucks, but Dr. Kroner has made learning as easy as possible. He posts lectures on youtube, does chapter overview videos, and creates short (optional) lesson quizzes to test your understanding. He is a kind prof with lots of office hours. Gets back to you very quickly via email. Very much a dad and brought candy to class once

Kroner was an awesome prof. I was not the best at chem so it was very difficult for me. He goes well into detail and doesn't really get off-topic which is nice. Kroner is a great guy, very forgiving with computer issues, etc. Lots of extra credit. Would take the class again if I actually liked chem
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Kroner is by far one of the best choices for a professor. Tough course, great professor. He is easy to understand. The lecture portion of the course is not worth much in your overall grade, but he does the most for what he can help with. Gives little homework & lots of optional extra credit.

Kroner is like a dad! If you have to take Chem1210 at osu I highly recommend him! He gives very little homework compared to the other professors. Its a hard class but he does his best to make sure everyone understands!

Hes a super nice guy and clearly cares a lot about his students. Lectures can get somewhat boring but definitely not the worst, hes pretty interesting and his voice isnt annoying or anything. He can go kind of fast but its necessary to get through the lectures and stay on track
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Steve was a great teacher but the class is simply designed to be difficult. Good guy, rough class.

Dr. Kroner was a great professor when it came to lectures and he did his best to prepare the class for OSU's standardized chemistry exams. His lectures are fun to attend, but can get slow at times. The TopHat participation matters, so show up to class. He also takes into account what students don't understand and explains it very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Kroner was a great chemistry professor. He truly cares about his students success and had very accessible office hours- which my biggest regret is not attending them. Midterms and the final are difficult. Attendance is vital to be successful. Kroner is great and offers lots of extra credit and practice problems. Would defiantly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kroner is a really nice and caring guy. The class is difficult because the chemistry department makes the exams hard for no reason. However, he is helpful if you ask questions and uses TopHat frequently to boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Kroner is great!!!! I wish I could have him for 1220!!!! He is so caring and gives lots of extra credit homeworks

Dr. Kroner is really caring and such a dad. Even though he says its not a weed out class (it is) he really wants his students to succeed. He is helpful in office hours and willingly answers questions in lecture. He offers lots of extra credit so you can pretty much get 100% in homework. The exams are really challenging and require lots of studying.

If you get Kroner, you lucked out! He gives TONS of daily extra credit, both in lecture and as homework, and takes the time to give you pre and post lecture notes and videos to help review the material.
Dr. Kroner was very knowledgeable about chemistry in general and tried to help students understand the basics and foundations of chemistry.

Dr. Kroner followed the book pretty rigidly so his lectures weren't super interesting, but they were ideal for understanding for the exams. He had no control on the exams since they were standardized, but he prepared us well. For TopHat and homework, it was extremely easy to get 100% due to extra credit. Solid gen chem professor.

Kroner was the most forgiving of Chem teachers since he allowed us to make up points in TopHat and online hw. A lot of his in class and recitation problems came up again on exams so go to class anyway. YOU MUST READ THE BOOK AND TAKE NOTES AND GAIN AN UNDERSTANDING ON YOUR OWN. Most people who failed didn't keep up with the readings. Be proactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class material was pretty easy. Reading the book was the best way to learn the material. The lectures were sometimes a little boring, and I often did not pay attention in lecture. But when I did listen, it was helpful. He gives extra credit on a lot of homework assignments, unlike most professors. He's a nice guy and wants students to succeed
Never showed up to lecture except for midterms. Didn't study as much as I should have but wound up with B. Not bad.

Dr. Kroner did not thrill me. His lectures were so dry -- I honestly don't even remember any clearly because I zone out about 95% of the time. He seems like a nice guys, but honestly can not teach. Anything I learned in this class I learned on my own by reading the textbook. Homework is easy, but that doesn't really help when exams are impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kroner was OK at best, his lectures are very easy and yet still don't make sense sometimes. He is not an effective teacher. His homeworks are relatively easy in comparison to other teachers but he does not prepare you for the standardized exams. If you're set on having his class, get ready to self-teach from the textbook and from your friends.
Reading the book and doing practice problems are more important than attending the lectures.

Dr. Kroner is interested in his students' success, but learning is self driven. Lectures are mainly sample practice problems, recitation is a worksheet of questions (based on attendance). Exams are straightforward. Find Dr. Fus' online chem videos and take notes from those. I have Fus now and his lecture videos with Kroner's exams would be great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kroner is a nice enough guy, and he obviously is smart, but he is truly a terrible teacher. He gets caught up in tangents that make no sense, and he makes simple material difficult to understand. He makes it easy to get a 100 on homework and recitation, but he makes the material way harder than it needs to be and it's confusing.

Dr. Kroner is nice, really cares about his students, and wants them to do well. He gives out 1 sapling homework assignment per week, and there are helpful recitation activities too. His midterms are straightforward and not super difficult. He holds a lot of review and Q & A sessions outside of class. I would definitely take him again

I thought I was going to love Dr. Kroner from the beginning of the year, but it went downhill. It is DEFINITELY possible to get an A in the class, but I don't recommend Dr. Kroner. When I would ask for any clarification in office hours, he would go off on a 10 minute tangent that explained nothing. Dr. Kroner is a smart man, but a terrible teacher.

Dr. Kroner is one of the best Chem 1210 professors at OSU. His exams are very fair but challenging enough that the class won't bomb the final. Overall he seems to care very much about his students and their success, and sets up his class to reflect that.

Dr. Kroner wants every student to succeed. He makes it easy to get 100 on homework and recitation, so it does not screw your grade. He tries to make everything you need to succeed very accessible. He puts up several practice tests which are a real life saver. I wish I could have him again.

Dr. Kroner is an excellent professor. I took his class using grade forgiveness after having my soul crushed by Dr. Fus. He was able to actually teach me the 1220 material and conceptualize what was going on beyond the math. He's the first professor I had who made it clear that he wanted everyone to succeed in the class and worked hard to achieve it

Everyone here raves about Dr. Kroner because he makes the class easy. He gives away the homework points so that every student ends up with 100%, his recitations are just extensions of the lecture; all you have to do is attend to receive the points. This leaves the class with higher averages and virtually no curve. The no curve is a substantial con.

Took Dr. Kroner for Chem 1210 and loved him so I ended up taking him again for 1220 as well. His lectures can be slightly confusing, but if you supplement them with the book you will be fine. Do all his practice tests and reach out to him if you need help because he is EXTREMELY willing to help. Tests are fair but only if you prepare/study well.

Kroner is a great professor. Extremely likable and relatable; he is very available, offers many valuable resources, gives clear lectures, gives no busywork, and gives very fair exams. He was an undergrad here at OSU, so he knows what it was like to be in your shoes. I didn't use him much since I think chem is easy, but he is as good as it gets.

The lectures are unorganized. I felt that my knowledge of the material deserved an A, but I didn't get that because the tests were almost too easy. I would study, but miss two or three questions and end up with a B  every time because the averages are so high. If you don't know chemistry that well, I suggest it for an easy B.
Don't really like his lectures personally but I think his exams are very fair. Just do all the practice problems. Taking him again for 1220 and so far so good.

Exams are super easy, gives a lot of supplemental material in order to study for the exams. Some people don't like how he lectures but its beneficially for me personally. Even though his class tends to be at night he is one of the better professors and a good grade in chem is worth the time trade off.

Kroner is definitely a good chemist, but in terms of teaching in lecture he seemed to go off the rails and explain the material in the most complicated way possible. I personally just watched YouTube videos over the material and it helped clear some things up. However, he is very willing to help you and gives you lots of things to study for exams.
Not bad, I would say best professor to have for chemistry. Very willing to help and overall just a cool dude

Dr. Kroner was very clear that his purpose was always to make sure we knew the material and he wasn't trying to trick us on tests. This meant that it was pretty clear if the answer you got after your calculations was right or wrong. He relates to his students a lot and doesn't make the class more challenging than it needs to be.
Exams are tough but he is really helpful. I took this during the summer so we moved quickly. Taking this during the summer was tough; an exam every week, 2 labs a week, and homework... it was a lot.

Lectures weren't too helpful so I never went; I taught myself the material by reading the textbook. He is however a very helpful guy and wants you to succeed. He extends office hours before midterms. UTILIZE the online practice exams he posts on Carmen.. the questions are very similar to the actual test. Little (1-3%) curve at end of semester.

He's a great professor and he really LOVES teaching. He gives TONS of practice problems and help, and if you do them, you will succeed. He tries really hard to befriend his students, and its difficult to motivate yourself for night classes, but he does a really good job. He gives LOADS more on exams than typical profs.
Too many midterms.
Passionate. Has some interesting chemical experiment in class. Good professor but not a good chemist. Not knowledgeable enough.

Kroner definitely knows what he is talking about. He is very smart and knowledgeable in chemistry but that is also his downfall. Although he is very nice and does not do it intentionally, he explains things at a very high level and it can sometimes be hard to understand what he is explaining because it is so simple to him.

He is a great professor. He really cares about his students. Even though his lectures were hard to follow, he tried to adjust his teaching methods. His office hours were helpful and you can tell that he is very passionate about chemistry! His exams were all right. PRACTICE PACKETS were the best! He has a ton compared to other professors.
Great professor! Very helpful during office hours and quickly responds to emails. Doesn't hurt that he's easy on the eyes too. :)

He is a pretty good professor and his exams are alright. He really cares about his students though! Lectures are sometimes hard to follow because he doesn't explain thoroughly, but overall, an okay professor!
Dr. Kroner is an excellent professor. You can tell that he really enjoys what he does. Do the homework and practice exams. You get out of the class what you put into it.
I stopped attending lectures simply because going caused more confusion over the topics than reading the material on my own due to Kroner's teaching style
He is a good professor. He is difficult but if you attend lecture, do the homework and practice problems, and go to him when you need help, you will pass. You need to put effort to do well.

Very good teacher. Need to go to lectures and take notes. Lots of examples on exams straight from class and little facts he mentions could be on an exam. Enjoyed the class enjoyed lectures and learned a lot. Class is difficult but manageable if you do the homework, practice exams and listen. Helps a lot outside of class and responds to emails well.

His tests are really hard compared to the other Chem professors at OSU, but if you read the book and do practice tests you should be fine. The class is graded on a bell curve so if you get at least the average you get a C+. Overall I learned a lot in this class and Dr. Kroner was a good professor who cared about teaching.

Kroner is not a bad teacher. You should attend his lectures and seek help should you not understand. He is very open and willing to help students, especially during office hours. His tests are difficult but if you use the practice tests given to you, do sample problems from the book, and read the book, you can succeed in the class without a doubt.
Professor did not help at all. I found that I was better off reading the text book to learn.

I loved Dr. Kroner, he was an incredible teacher and you can definitely tell that he loves what he does. Pay attention in lecture and make sure to print out and work on the practice exams that he posts online. This class will be a breeze as long as you put forth a little effort.

Great teacher. I never really studied for exams but have always gotten above average.  He is extremely willing to help with any problems you may have. As long as you take notes and actually pay attention during lecture you'll be fine. Read the textbook in addition, esp. before exams, it helps. I wish I could take him for 1220. I recommend his class

THIS CLASS WAS DA BOMBDIGGITY. but for realsies for real, pchem lab is a good class. It ties together the concepts of organic and pchem and does well to show you how all that stuff you learn in lecture works. The point of the class is to understand the chemistry not to become America's next great novelist. Lectures would probably be helpful, maybe.

I took Kroner and did horibly in  the class. No matter how much I studied I couldn't do well in his class. He knows the material himself, but does not know how to present it to students in a helpful and clear way. He does have office hours to help, and is willing ot meet with you, but trying to learn something the same way is not helpful at all.

Never gave enough time for quizzes and there was always material from the next chapter on them even though he specifically said there wouldn't be. Lectures are really boring and he goes really fast so it's hard to understand. Smart guy just bad teacher.
I thought he was not very helpful. He just printed out slides didn't write much on the board that was comprehensive and did nothing to interest those in lecture.

This professor is the worst I've ever had. He is obviously very smart, but doesn't know how to "teach". No one understands his lectures and his quizzes and tests are impossible. We get between 1-2 minutes per question that take 5+ minutes each to work out. Even if you knew all the answers you won't have enough time to write them down! Ridiculous.

In my opinion he was a great professor! really laid back and didnt assign hardly anything. Basically you manage how much you wanna study. Pretty diffcult tests, but if you read, do all he puts on carmen, and book problems you should be good to go!
Okay teacher
GREAT! Breaks everything down in amazing detail and is awesome at lecturing. CHEM IS HARD NO MATTER WHAT, so expect to work hard and seek help if you don't understand.

Terrible at explaining things, but the class isvery easy if you took Chemistry in high school. Print out of lecture slides, practice midterms, and daily group questions make for a very organized and easy to follow class.

Good professor, goes into great detail in lectures which is helpful to supplement book material.  Very helpful in office hours, and quiz and midterm reviews are offered.  Overall, the course is well laid out and if you go to class, complete the homework, read the book and pass labs, you will be successful.

Kroner was a very good teacher, and if you go to class and do the homework, this class shouldn't be too bad. Missing class will make things difficult for you, though, He held exam and quiz reviews as well as posting multiple example quizzes and tests on carmen, so you will always know exactly what to expect and practice.
Awesome professor!!!! He is nice even though the tests are tricky....

Great professor - class isn't too bad if you've had chemistry in high school.  Tests and quizzes are very fair, but labs are tough with your grade based on how accurate your data is.  I would recommend to anybody

The first several weeks of class I thought he'd be okay. Easy to understand, assigns homework out of the book, etc. Then exams hit. Class average was a 55% with many people doing worse. Hours of studying wont pay off. Explains that he intentionally makes his tests hard to prep us for MCAT's. Problem is, not everybody will be a doctor. DO NOT TAKE!!

Best chem teacher you can take.  He explains things so well! Class moves very fast however and there is a lot of work, especially in the labs.  He has practice exams that are extremely helpful, the real exams are made of the same type of questions.  Ace the practice exams and you'll ace the real ones.
Does a good job of covering material and providing study guides for exams. Exams are difficult; be prepared to study hard and to read each question carefully so units/sig figs/etc. don't mess you up.

Although I found the a material difficult to understand, I thought Dr. Kroner was a great teacher. He is genuinely interested in teaching and communicating the material. He is willing to help anyone with questions and he was involved with the lab and recitations. His exams are very hard but as long as you do decent the curve will boost you up.

Great teacher! Very enthusastic about chemistry! Extremely knowledgeable about subjects and very personable.  Midterms and finals were VERY hard. They are made to DEFEAT YOU! My class average was a 55%. Which was the lowest of all the Chem professors. Great guy, just really difficult! Practice exams were easy compared to actual exams.
Good professor. He moves really fast. Definitely do the homework he gives you and read the chapters. Reading the book was more useful than his notes, but going to class helps clear some things up.

Dr. Kroner was one of my favorite professors. He's enthusiastic about chemistry, and always made class interesting with at least one visual demonstration per chapter if not more. He explains things in such a way that they are very easy to understand so that I found myself grasping concepts after one lecture that I never fully understood in HS.

Kroner did very well in responding to emails and the discussion board. He does care about his students. However, he is very, very tricky. I would recommend knowing all the exceptions to every concept you learn in chemistry. 1st midterm and Final were killer
Read before his lectures and be sure to use all of the study materials he posts online.  Midterms are manageable but the final was very unfamiliar.  Study the book more than his notes.

Great guy, even better teacher. Actually cares about the students and their grades. Exams are somewhat difficult but the curve makes up for the difficulty. Lectures are good and entertaining. If you take Chem 121 i would strongly recommend getting Dr. Kroner as a teacher. It will make this class easier then it is.
Great professor really helpful and very enthusiastic about the subject , besides that , also a wonderful person you are lucky if you have him as a professor.

Great teacher, really knows his stuff and is enthusiastic about the material. He also provides TONS of resources online to help you, you just have to use them if you want a good grade. Overall, he is one of my favorite professors.

Not a fan of this professor. He made a ton of mistakes on exams (which was really unfair to students) and wasn't really good at explaining stuff. The only good thing was that the quizzes were in class and pretty straightforward as opposed to mastering chemistry quizzes. Overall I think he was an alright professor but he could have done better
Watch out for his "ice ice tables". He explains them very poorly and it's not really in the book. If you miss that concept you will fail the first midterm horribly. His writting is also horrible.

Definitely do not agree with his high rating on here. I received A's in both 121 and 122 but Kroner will change that. He gives unfair exams and quizzes which contain information that was not covered in the book. Simply put, he makes the class much harder than it needs to be.

I was fooled by the positive ratings he received. I had Loza for 121 & 122 and did perfectly fine. Kroner has very sloppy handwriting and he lacks personality which makes lecturers boring. He tests on stuff that isn't covered in the book so if yo don't understand how he teaches it you are kind of out of luck. Not horrible but there are better profs
Great teacher, class is not easy, but thats chem. Helped me a lot. Has good notes

class is not bad if you study each chapter. Kroner gives you chances to make up points through online quizzes- DO THEM if you dont get a perfect on the in class quizzes. He also gives you a lot of practice exams and problems so take advantage of them!
Professor Kroner was a good teacher who was excited about his subject.  I would recommended him.

He is a really great guy. I thought he was a really good professor. He talks fast but you just have to pay attention! I never went to his office hours but I have heard he is always willing to help! TAKE HIM! his tests are hard. the final was very hard but Chem is not EASY so expect it to be HARD!
GREAT GUY!! this does NOT mean that he is a good/easy teacher.
Best teacher I've had at OSU. Take him, you won't regret it.

Sup Kroner!  Since I know you read these, great job this quarter.  I really like how the course was revamped.  Only qualms: your hand writing is atrocious! Oh and don't get so frustrated by stupid questions(although it was pretty funny a few times).  Would certainly recommend!  Way to be a teacher and a bro.  You stay classy Kroner (and Fus too)!
Awesssssome!

Dr Kroner is my hero. Very cool guy, excellent lecturer, very helpful & willing to assist you if you need it.  His practice exams are just like the ones he gives out! I have always struggled in chem (I got a C- in 121 & C+ in 122), but got a B in 123 because Kroner is just that awesome. He's like a big teddy bear you just want to squeeze! <3

I love this professor. He does well in explaining the material and is always willing to help during office hours. Exams are hard and require studying. Do practice problems and study at least once a week. Reviewing daily is suggested. Best chem teacher.

He was a very helpful and clear-spoken person. His exams were hard just because it involved so much memorization. He uses the board a lot for definitions and calculations, so try to find a seat up front. Overall, he seemed amiable.

Kroner is a bit confusing at times in his clarity about what he is talking about, and his hand writing is hard to read! BUT, he is a good teacher and if you read the book everything it's an easy A. He is really understanding, and if you go to his office hours confused, he is genuine about helping you out. GOOD TEACHER!

Dr. Kroner is incredible. One of my favorite professors at Ohio State. Chem 121 is a HARD course... be prepared to spend hours upon hours looking over lecture notes, reading the textbook, etc. But it's worth it because if you work hard you'll do well. Plus Dr. K is more than willing to help you anytime out of class.
Excellent, fun teacher. Exams are made to be difficult; if you do all the homework and pay attention, you will do well.
a great professor - very enthusiastic and awesome. lectures were not boring. course is challenging, but after kroner presents the material, you understand. TAKE HIM!!! TAKE HIM!!!

This man is so amazing that if you took lebron james and wayne gretzky put them together they would no equal Steve's awesomeness. Basically if u had any oppurtunity to meet this man you would be blessed with knowledge that no human being should every be graced with. Some say he's not real but we believe in SMK...Do you?

Interesting teacher, enthusiastic, lectures are usually ok to follow, but he's a challenging. Exams are not easy. Don't be discouraged by low grades, if you study alot & attend lecutre you still learn alot.

Dr. Kroner is very helpful and is very quick to respond to your questions. His quiz's/midterms are to the point. However, you must work hard and study the material to do well. No trick questions. A lot of Chapters to cover in a short amount of time...so be sure to keep up. I would highly recommend him. Just sit close to the board. He can get sloppy
No Comments

As a fellow student of mine once stated..."Never before have i ever understood chemistry so clearly...yet failed so miserably on every exam..." Dr. K did a great job with the difficult material, but writes harder x10^200 exams then Dr. Zellmer and Dr. Lousa... I recommend him...Do every homework problem to get half the points on the exam...
explains material very well.  good prof.

Enjoyed this class, Dr. Libby clearly cares about the material she is teaching and wants her students to be excited about it too. Attendance isn't mandatory but I'd recommend going if you want a good grade. 3 exams, 1 writing assignment, extra credit opportunities exist.

Interesting lectures, you need to take active notes and pay attention in order to do well on the 3 exams (noncumulative). Grading model: weekly packbacks, weekly interactive textbook questions, 3 exams, 1 writing assignment. Not an easy A, but most classes aren't.

Should have been such an easy class but she made the quizzes impossible. You have to take active notes in class or you won't be able to find answers for the tests. She expected way to much and the group project was dumb.

There are quizzes every other week and they were overly difficult for an elective course. Her averages for quizzes were very low and she wouldn't provide adequate feedback. There is a big group project which was structured weird as we hadn't actually worked as a group until presentation. Definitely take this course with another professor.

The class had relatively easy and self explanatory concepts however she graded very hard taking half points off of as many things as she could. Quizzes were unusually difficult and there were weekly discussion posts. No exams thankfully and every assignment was online except for a group presentation that was very easy.

Very nice professor with interesting material, but her online quizzes are difficult and they're worth a good chunk of your grade and lectures aren't that much help. Doable course load and easy points otherwise. Many extra credit opportunities and she's always willing to help. No final or exams, but there is a group project.
Never read textbook or went to class. Lectures good, homework kind of busywork, but easy points. Interesting topics, easy tests, would take again.

Lisa seems like a lovely woman and had an upbeat personality. Always came to class positive but when it came to her quizzes (which made up most of the grade), they were impossible!!! I get that with online learning some teachers may want to make things more difficult to make sure students are working for their grade but her quizzes were ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, the coursework is light and doable. However, she's very careful about her word choice on the exams. I would take 5-6 pages worth of notes a week on her lectures and still fail her quizzes. The content itself is fun to learn, but I didn't enjoy it as much when she made it extremely complicated. A little ridiculous for a Tier 2 course.

I thought the class was overall pretty easy. I studied around 3 hours before exam and always got an A. However, the final wasn't cumulative and so I studied how I usually did for other exams and I absolutely bombed it and got a D. She ended up curving the class so I got an A so it didn't matter. Overall, it was easy except for the final

The book isn't required, but it explains the material better than her. Her tests are based on examples from lectures. Her powerpoints suck. There isn't much to boost your grade. Tests are very difficult. She allows you to earn 0.5 points of extra credit during tests. Test averages are really low in the class.

In this class you have 10 weeks to come up with an experiment idea, create the experiment, analyze your data, and write a research paper. If you can't handle the amount of time that will obviously take then don't take the class. Dr. Libby did a great job of presenting the material in way that made the class a lot easier than I was expecting.

Dr. Libby is a good professor,however,she needs to improve her teaching style and provide students with study guides/review sheets to help them prepare better for the exams,because there is a lot of material to remember,which is overwhelming and a bit like a guessing game,because you never know what to expect on the exams.(I failed all 3 of them!)

loved the info in class, but very specific. tests were hard, averages for midterm were in 70's, final average was a 68%. opportunities for 4 extra credit, fairly easy to obtain. exams are VERY difficult. 2 "discussions" to attend with 10 other students, easy points. overall, good teacher but hard exams. read book for first exam, not for others.
I've loved every psychology class I have ever taken at Ohio State... until I had Dr. Libby for a professor. I would rather drink molten glass than have to deal with her again.

She might not use a textbook or give tests or quizzes, but she is sadistic when it comes to classwork. Plan on reading at least 3 journal articles a day, writing 1 to 2 papers a week, and when it comes to research she is the pickiest person in the world. Avoid at all costs, unless you plan to cancel everything else in your life for 3 months.

AVOID. I was so excited to take this class but I nearly failed bc of frustraction. Her teaching style did not match book which did not match notes which did not match test. 1/2 MC half essay but hard grader (nit picky...if not exactly clear no points) EC is joke, 1/2 class did not know answ. BLAHHHH

Decent class; good experience if looking at graduate school in psych. A bit unclear and slow at answering emails. Sometimes seemed like she shoved a lot of her dirty work on her TA. If you haven't taken psych 321, just be prepared for some frustration when it comes to reporting data. fast-paced and quick deadlines, but no tests or book.
pretty good class. as long as you study well you should do fine. very clear in her teaching and standards.

This class is a scientific study of human relationships, so you can't go into it expecting something out of Cosmopolitan. That said, I thought the subject matter was very interesting and the tests weren't THAT hard. She is straightforward and clear, and more personable 1-on-1. She's also very willing to help. Kinda cute in a professor-ish way.

Hardest, trickiest (essay) exams ever! They don't test knowledge directly, they ask you to infer things from what she talked about. And she's boring as crap. Explains relationships in terms of  evolution. What a joke! Disappointing. If you're interested in relationships, just buy the textbook on eBay and avoid this class at all costs.

The class could have been so much better! She is pretty boring for how great the subject matter could have been.  Tests are some of the hardest I have had in my 4 years in the Psych department.  She offers lots of extra credit but its only worth half a point.  It was overall a disappointment

Prof libby is great.  her class is kind of interesting, no homework assignments just 3 exams.  3 discussion sessions per quarter and you only have to attend two..super easy.  test's aren't the best, but definitely not hard.  if you study a little you'll be sure to get an A, B-

I found this course to be difficult and rewarding at the same time. I thought the Sex and the Cty clips worked well with the material. The tests were rather difficult, but there were plenty of opportunities for extra credit if you bothered to show up

One of the best professors I've ever had.  Very reasonable in her expectations.  I thought the exams were extremely easy, but some people had trouble with them.  My favorite course in all 4 of my years at OSU.  Material is very interesting!
If you are interested in relationships, and how to make them better you will like this class. She is monotone and boring. Tests are somewhat difficult. I learned stuff from the book.
Very boring, my friend dropped the class because she couldn't stay awake.
This prof is wonderful.  The class is great, and I would take anything else she teaches.

Really interesting class, excellent powerpoints, really clear about everything.  The textbook was easy to read and she picked a lot of good videos to demonstrate the material.  One short paper & 2 tests - pretty great for a brand new class
I really liked him; you can tell he really cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches.

He was by far my favorite prof. He made a boring topic more interesting. SO MANY extra credit opportunities. Cheat sheets on each exam. Review sessions before each exam. Genuinely would love to have him again.

I enjoyed having Dr. Jesse as a professor for this course. There was no homework, only three exams and an essay. His lectures were very entertaining and thoughtful. The only thing I wish he had implemented was a study guide or practice questions for each exam, as I found myself a little confused and wanting extra practice/clarification at times.

Dr. Jesse may be one of my favorite psychology professors of all time. He truly lectures with such a passion for the subject. You can tell he cares a lot about what he's teaching and if it makes sense to students. Man, I could sit here all day and talk about how fun Dr.Jesse is or how greatly I enjoyed his class he is just so awesome.

i love this man with all my heart. a truly invested person in what he teaches. extremely knowledgable and great lectures that you should definitely go to. he explains things very clearly and provides a lot of extra credit. amazing prof and made the class fun
Legendary. much knowledge much passion, such wow O_O

Dr. Ladanyi is a good professor and explains topics very clearly. 3 exams and 1 final, can drop 1, also can use one sided cheat sheet on each exam. One final paper and no homework. extra credit through practice quizzes and creating test questions. you get the choice of going to class and having participation count in grade or not having it count.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Ladanyi for my Research Methods class last semester and ended up choosing to take his class again for Intro to Social Psych. His lectures are well thought out and they're interesting. He cares about his students and the material he is teaching. I would take him for a third time if I could!
Easy assignments, accepts late work, lectures weren't boring
Excellent lectures and attendance accommodations. Very kind and helpful in all circumstances. Easy A if you complete all assignments!

Dr. Ladanyi seems like a great human being and is an amazing professor. I could see him being the cool white dude at a black ppl BBQ. 4 exams, the last one being optional to replace the lowest grade, 9 opportunities to be absent, one paper. Not an easy A, but not impossible because he offers extra credit and in-class exam prep, would take him again

Very cool dude & seems like the kind of person you would trust with the key to your apartment or wallet. 9 chances to be absent. Exams are kind of tough, but he gives A LOT of test prep, & ways to earn extra credit.  Lectures are interesting & relatable, but he is not weird or cringe in a millennial way. I learned a lot, 10/10 would take again.

Jesse as he prefers to be called is a very unique professor. The best psych profs teach like that tiktok of an old woman who says, "Have you ever had a krispy kreme..?" [yeah] "was it krispy..?" [no] "yeah, right...right..." and he embodies that. I learned a ton in his class and it made me a better student.

Wonderful human and professor. Take any classes you can with Dr. Ladanyi! Exams aren't easy, but they are fair and he provides you with in class review and a practice test the week of. Go to class, lectures are engaging and it is difficult to succeed if you skip, attendance matters for exam performance and your overall grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I deeply enjoyed his class, and I wish he taught more than two classes. Live laugh loved him. Super helpful works with students and is very passionate about what he teaches, and you can tell. 10/10

Lectures were very confusing, he was never clear on what exactly we had to do. For exams, I am jealous of people that took 2300 from a different professor and finished with minimal coursework and high grades (and NO exams). Def only take this professor if you absolutely need to. There are many better professors at OSU.

Best prof I could have had for this course. I ended up loving the class and he made the materal interesting. In order to secure an A, read the textbook and review. The class is extremely tied to the textbook. He cares about attendance so go to lectures,he gives lots of examples though so theyre helpful. Overall, really nice and cares about students
His classes are amazing! He is a great teacher, and I would definitely take his classes again

Jesse is a really down to Earth, who really cares about his students. If you put in the work you will for sure get a good grade. I loved this class, and he made it so interesting to learn about. He love's feedback from his students and wants to really make the class the best it can. Definitely take his class if you can!

Jesse took over this class mid-semester and was extremely understanding of the disorganization of the class. He's passionate, friendly, and funny. W ish he taught the class the whole semester--I would've liked it a lot more! Student feedback important to him, and he made several changes to the course based on students' opinions to better serve us.

easily one of the best profs Ive had at OSU and hes only a grad student! he makes asynchronous lectures really engaging, is very personable, and you can tell he really wants his students to do well. the class feels easy, but I also feel like Ive learned a lot. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him even if psych isnt your thing!!

I'm a 3rd year, and I've never rated a single professor of mine BUT i explicitly created an account to write about Jesse. He is, BY FAR, the best teacher I've ever had here at OSU. His lectures are funny (with current memes), he's super approachable, takes ALL feedback, and genuinely cares about every student. I'm actually sad the semester ended :(

BEST TEACHER EVER!!! Highly recommend taking social psych (3325) with jesse. He truly cares about his student's success and is such a fun professor to listen to. You can tell how much he loves psychology and teaching. Very interesting class and he gives great examples to help you understand. Midterms very much reflect what we learn in lectures.

The quizzes were straight out of homework.  The exams were less predictable, but were entirely based on material covered in lectures.  Huge variety in test performance:  some got practically perfect scores on the exams, while others struggled.  The curve pulled up the really low scores by a lot, while not changing the high scores much.

Was her first time teaching this course and you could tell. Read straight from the textbook and yet no one was ever prepared for the questions on the tests and quizzes. While grading was lenient, there was not many grades to recover from any mistakes. When asked questions, she would only offer math proofs instead of any physics reasoning.
Lectures generally followed the book, but explained the confusing parts really well.  This was really difficult material and Prof. Landsman made it accessible.

Lectures largely consist of reading from the textbook with little added, which makes already confusing material harder to follow. The grading is very lenient, so it is not difficult to earn a good grade, but most of the learning has to be done independently outside of class. Students looking for clear or engaging lectures may be disappointed.

I took 5401H honors quantum mechanics.  Granted the Griffiths E&M book was not easy to follow, this teacher did not make it any better.
- very little class organization
- lectures straight from the book with little to no outside input or extra example
- exams that had nothing to do with with hws
- hws that had nothing to do with lecture
DO NOT TAKE
Angel professor~
Dr. Landsman is really an angel! Choose her and choose honor intermediate E&M course, and you will never regret! (Even this is simpler than regular intermediate E&M course)
Landsman is a very good woman. Her lectures are very amazing. The homework is a little difficult but useful. The difficulty of test is reasonable. Recommend Dr. Landsman!
Tests were of easy to fair difficulty and were given generous curves. Homework was not burdensome and lectures were easy enough to follow.
Great.  Knowledgeable.  Great insights.  Excellent lectures.  I worked very hard in researching and performing in my final examination project.
Excellent professor.  Very motivational.  Clear directions.  Kindness.  You work very hard.
Interesting information.  Creative.  Kind.  Became newspaper theatre critic in later years.
great
Such a good teacher! Definitely easy to get an A if you read the plays and go to class. He will look over your papers before you hand them in and give you feedback. He is also super nice!
Easy A. Just do the readings(which aren't that long) and show up+A.
Very biased. I am liberal, but Mr.Yde takes it to a whole new level. Very easy course overall. It was also very informative. And there wasn't much reading in the course : )
He is a genius.  It is an eye opening experience to take this course and the course is highly interesting.
Not anti-american at all, just anti-stupidity. Definitely biased, but he was really cool about differences in opinion and encouraged a lot of discussion. Showed awesome films.

Well-versed.  Informative.  Protege of Dr. Woods, and a fine disciple.  Great future for this talented instructor.  He is motivated to be a good teacher, as well as keeping a fine eye upon the stated objectives of the class.
Overall, I thought it was a great class, I do think that he should give some more thought to the way the group projects are put together, but that will come with time.

Loved it. Matt is great and really well-versed in the subject matter. Though the class was nothing like what I thought it would be, I ended up really enjoying myself and getting quite a lot out of it.

Hes actually extremely disrespectful, and makes people feel uncomfortable. he once said he wanted to start his spring break early and not to send him any emails asking for help on a group project; then proceeds to send out 3 announcements over spring break. His course is extremely disorganized, and he is difficult to reason with overall

Tim is a genuine guy, and my feelings about him improved over the semester. However, his teaching style is not strong. Assignment directions and purposes were often unclear, and Canvas is disorganized. The class is very sports-focused apparently, which isn't listed. If you aren't into sports, consider another professor for your capstone class.

Really cool guy. Most of your grade comes from group work, so make sure you get a good group. He grades tough, but not unnecessarily tough. He provides good feedback for you to improve for future assignments. He's one of my favorite professors that I've had. Be ready for a good amount of work though towards the second half of the semester.

My favorite professor ever at The Ohio State. Sports Media Relations is a fantastic course for anyone interested in communications, sports, PR, etc. Tim cares deeply about ensuring we get the most out of the material and is willing to do everything he can to make sure you succeed. Three major projects but all are reasonable if you put effort in.

A great teacher and class. A lot of information to get through, but you'll be okay if you don't get everything done. It's an inverted learning style so  there's a lot to do outside of class time, but like I said, you'll be okay. 3 Major assignments to do, 2/3 are group. They are big but if you split them up you'll be ok. He cares a lot ab teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: He pretends to say that he wants to give everyone an A just to give super hard exams to sink the grades of half the class. Little to zero preparation for the exams. Records lectures but takes forever to post the videos. Labs are meaningless, as he often just stands there and gossips with the TAs.

The only thing he is good at is being sociable. His lectures do not prepare you well for assignments and exams, as he rarely demonstrates problem-solving and coding techniques in class. His exams are hard, so be prepared.

Rob is very energetic and passionate about the content, which makes it very easy to stay engaged/interested during lectures. His energy, humor, and kindness make the class much more enjoyable. While he doesn't directly give any review material, he tells you what you should look at to review and advertises/promotes outside review sessions.

Overrated by bunch of guys thinking that good socializing is the top quality for a professor, while this is the only thing he's good at. He constantly shows up late then follows by his quite meaningless lectures. Somehow provide no review sessions or material for the hard tests. This is college and teaching quality always comes first
Dude lacks any professionalism and maturity and just spends time in class socializing with students. Also, hard exams with no review sessions and little help from him.
Great guy however he does not give any material for midterms or finals and does not have a review session while other professors do.

awesome guy to be around. good at lectures and really funny, plus you can miss up to 4 labs and 4 lectures for perfect attendance. final grades were slightly curved in my section after the final. my only complaint is that there wasn't enough review material for exams; be prepared to find review Q's and exams on your own. otherwise amazing professor

I like the instructor, but the class average on Midterm 1 was 63%. I got a 94% through heavy studying and some luck, but I doubt I'll manage that again. Everyone here is smart since CSE admits are strong students, so a 63% average likely reflects unclear teaching. The projects are easy, but lectures drag and the workload is excessive.

He's a great professor - he makes sure you understand the material and are ready for exams. His lectures were great, and overall he's just a really cool person. His tests make sure you understand the concepts so it's really beneficial for the learning. Definitely try to have this professor!

Funny guy, lectures are always pretty entertaining and he explains the concepts pretty well. He was consistently ~10min late to his lectures/labs which I wasn't a fan of but he still made sure he taught all of the required content. Exams are fair, if you know the actual concepts pretty well then you shouldn't have a problem with them.
Love him! Def go to this office hours, he's a great guy to talk to and always willing to help.
Never take him!!!

Class went pretty smoothly, at the end there was a curve which was nice. As a professor he cares about his students and if you're taking the online version he makes it clear he is available in person if you need further help. Lectures were helpful and the order in which we learned everything made sense.

Software 2 generally is tough regardless of the professor, and Rob LaTour was no different. He's a chill guy, so definitely come to class. I would highly suggest against attending via Zoom because the Mediasite posts the lectures 2-3 weeks after the day of lecture. Be ready to spend multiple hours a week doing the homework/labs/projects.

Best lecturer out there at OSU, if you really wanna learn the material better take him. He made his lectures so interesting. Exams are not bad if you know the material good. He tries to trick you sometimes which kind of makes the exams interesting honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brutal midterms and projects, never got better than a 7/10 on projects and I worked HARD on them. TAs will take points off for ANYTHING, you need to go get your project checked by them before turning it in. That way if they takes points off for something arbitrary you can say, this TA checked that and said it was ok. This is the only way to do well

Teaches the material super well. Great at explaining the concepts. Had bunch of office hours and are very willing to help. Exams are hard but not impossible if you put in time and effort to study. Enjoyed the class very much.
Best professor ever. Loved his class will recommend him 100%. If you want to learn your stuff take him. He will make you suffer but you will learn a lot coming out of that class.

Consistently showed up 5-15 minutes late to class. He tries to make jokes and act like he's still in college. The jokes are funny about half of the time. 

Exams were hard but not terrible. The class is passable but not enjoyable.

Quizzes and projects are much harder than lecture examples. He does not have a syllabus posted on carmen. He takes weeks to post lectures - you have to rewatch them to take notes cause it moves so fast. Up to date lectures are not posted before major projects.

Good professor. Funny and cares about his students. Records lectures and uploads slides. Weekly quizzes/labs are hard - Rob doesn't really show coding examples, he makes real-life examples that help you understand but not actually do it. I wish he did practice quiz questions in lecture to actually see him code and see his whole thought process.

Rob is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. His explanations of concepts were so clear, and he had a great answer for every question. He had great analogies for everything. If you attend every lecture and pay attention and engage with him in class, you WILL do well on his exams. Although his exams are difficult, they were never unfair.

Nice person but DONT TAKE HIM. Long lecture without actually explaining anything. No examples of coding at all and tough grader on everything. I got A in other CSE classes but awful grade in his class...
Overrated

Can't believe he even has one good rating. Keeps trying to act like the "cool kids", is constantly late to class, and talks about nonsense that isn't even related to what he is teaching. Has no sense of professionalism whatsoever. Can't believe he is a professor clearly has no maturity whatsoever.

Rob Latour was an entertaining and kind person to talk to but he was not the best professor. He would consistently show up late to lectures and go on side tangents not related to school material. He created tough exams where the average was below 70, especially on the final where a 70 is needed to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rob is very knowledgeable and good with his lectures for what can be a tough class. Exams were tough but certainly doable with the right studying. I never had real issues with his teaching style or him being arrogant etc like some others say, but I can definitely imagine that happening sometimes based on his personality. Good overall.

Rob is one of the best teachers I have had but sometimes the lectures can be very long and boring. The exams are pretty hard and his exams consistently have very low averages. Only allowed to miss 4 labs and 4 lectures in the semester.

Thinks he's still in middle school. Has zero sense of professionalism and is extremely old school. Spends all his energy trying to act like a comedian instead of actually teaching. Is just using this job as a way to feel smarter than everyone else or as a stepping stone. Acts rude at times for no reason. Has favorites. Avoid! Take someone else!

If you want a professor who is egotistic, makes you feel dumb, does not want to provide any actual help without sounding like a know it all, or acts like a child then Rob is for you. If not, don't take him. He can be condescending and unnecessarily blunt when you ask him questions or visit during office hours. Not professional and acts childish.
Painful to interact with outside of lecture. Extremely condescending

Since he's a younger instructor he connects to students more than most. However, I feel like I ended up wasting so much time going to lecture and was better self taught. Exams were hard, and I feel like he didn't do enough to make you understand the material. I ended up not going to him for help because he can be arrogant and wasn't helpful.
Although Rob will make you suffer, he is one of the most geniune professors at the University. The course material is very tough, but you will come out having learned so much.

I just don't like his personality very much. He can be very arrogant and tries to act like the cool kids. Don't like those theoretical professors at all. They, and Rob, kept pushing others to follow covid restrictions and complained about others not doing so and acted like experts about covid when they weren't. They should stay in their lane.

Rob is the best! He respects his students and brings an energy to the classroom that really helped me follow the dense topics discussed in class. Rob is very accessible outside of class and makes communication as comfortable and humanizing as possible. He respects the material and grades tough, but with how well he teaches, it feels respectable!

Rob is extremely personable and makes a genuine effort to connect with his students. CSE 2231 was easier for me than Software I in general, but I will say that the final exam was extremely challenging. I'm pretty sure Rob is known for making a difficult final. I went into the final with a 94% in the class, and will be lucky if I get a 60% to pass.

Best professor I've had so far at Ohio State. He's extremely accessible outside of class and will explain concepts in a bunch of different ways to try to get you to understand. Not only this, Rob actually teaches you how to problem-solve and will make you a better engineer and computer scientist. Could not recommend him enough.

As a person, he is alright. I know alot of people like him, mostly because they play online games with him. As a professor, however, he's not very good. The exams are written and pretty difficult, lectures are unhelpful. Labs also be difficult. He's an okay professor, but he doesn't know how to help students who are struggling with materials.
Had a great time in this class! Rob keeps lectures entertaining and informative, and class work rarely feels overwhelming.

Rob's lectures are bomb and they really enable you to learn and understand the course content, even though the course itself is pretty tough. The only real grief I have about him is that he would sometimes make condescending comments towards students. He's definitely one of the best if not the best Software II professor right now.

If your about to take a class with Rob, you have nothing to worry about. CSE 2231 is not an easy class but Rob gives really good lectures and is open to being asked a lot of questions before and after class. He does floor the projects and typically doesn't give half points, but out of all the SW2 professors, he's probably the best one.

Rob is such a good lecturer and really teaches you the material well. Hilarious and helpful both in class and in office hours. If you can, I would snatch a class with him! One small thing: he is a bit slow when trying to message him outside class, but he makes up for it by being really understanding of situations and open to giving extensions.

Rob is an amazing lecturer. He makes the lectures fun and relevant. He also cares about how students are doing in the class. Rob tries to help out every student. He is very understanding when life gets hard and you need an extension on assignment.

Phenomenal. Compared to other professors I have taken, Rob can explain the material very well. He is really funny and entertaining.

Main issue I had is he takes quite a bit of time to grade tests and respond to emails/messages (which is not a huge deal).

Yes, he gives decent lectures. If that's the only way you plan on interacting with him, then you'll be fine. But if you want a professor that responds to emails, helps you learn outside of making himself feel smart/funny, and actually cares about teaching, then don't take him. He only cares about feeling bigger and smarter than his students.
Rob is a funny and cool guy, younger and relatable to students. I highly recommend Rob as your professor for any class.

Rob genuinely cares about his students. Apart from being a genuinely nice person, he is very understanding and funny. He made going to lectures enjoyable and was very knowledgable about the topics he was teaching about. Exams made up 70% of the grade, which was tough, but he gave out many opportunities to improve scores.
Labs were pretty brutal due to the short turnover times but Rob genuinely cares about his students and is a really nice guy.

Rob is a really great lecturer and is really engaging and hilarious. I never wanted to miss class because I really like learning from him.  Also lenient about extending deadlines and missing class. However, don't expect him to check his emails. The best way to reach him would be through discord.
Rob is a really great guy and his lectures are entertaining. I never thought about missing a class, because I genuinely enjoyed learned from him.
Rob is a really cool guy and you'll definitely be entertained in class. Don't be surprised though if you're waiting in class for 10 minutes though because he's always late. His exams are very tough.

Compared to other Systems I professors, Rob is relatively new to teaching this course and was still learning the ropes. Labs are hard (especially one of them) for my SU20 class. Lectures were really engaging and packed in knowledge and humor, and personality like a Wagyu steak. Passionate about CS and helping out students.

Rob is awesome. I took his first-ever Systems I class, and though it was clear he was learning how to teach the class effectively, he made sure to take our feedback and he worked with us on everything. He's an engaging professor who made a mind-numbing class interesting for me, and an even better dude. Be sure to study for his exams!

I think my biggest gripe with most professors is their care towards being a teacher and not a researcher that is required to teach courses. Rob is a great teacher, something that is hard to come by from my experience in university. He cares for his students and if you are struggling his office hours will get you out of a tight spot. Ask questions.

Hilarious? 100%. Caring? 100%. Passionate about teaching? 100%. Amazing lectures? 100%. Rob is my favorite prof at OSU and very much a dream of a prof. My only issue is that there wasn't a solid schedule for assignments but it's understandable since it was his 1st time teaching it in the summer. Extra credit on labs, MT, final. No curve.

Rob is seriously one steller guy. If you have a choice for systems, take him. The class is difficult and frustrating no matter what but he's one of the few instructors that can make the material actually interesting and easy to learn. The labs are tough so ask for help if you can. I would instantly take him again in a heartbeat.

Rob was awesome, only reason he didnt get a 5 was because he was horribly disorganized, he never knew when labs or homeworks would be so they were always a surprise. Besides this he was really passionate, caring and super fun. Ask lots of questions and be prepared to go to office hours though. The labs in Systems 1 are no joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rob was a decent professor for SW1. He clearly knew the material and was engaging during the lectures, which was helpful online. However, he took forever to grade quizzes/projects and left no feedback. To make things worse, he graded quite strictly on them and would never go over homework/projects in class. I felt on my own in this class a LOT.

Rob genuinely wants to help his students learn. He'll meet with you basically any time of day he can to help you out (especially if you are international during the pandemic) and his personality is comedy S-tier. As for lectures in software one, they're pretty straightforward and follow the slides. No curve, quizzes aren't bad if you pay attention

It was instantly clear how genuinely knowledgeable Rob was on all of the content, while the material itself isn't the most interesting, his lectures are well-paced, fun, and thorough. He was quick to respond to any emails outside of class and was always very supportive and helpful in answering questions or clarifying any confusing concepts.

Rob is super down-to-Earth and makes lectures amusing. He's great at answering questions and loves getting questions. Quizzes/tests can be a bit hard, but just go to class and review the lectures, and you'll be fine.

LaTour is a very kind and understanding professor. Don't be afraid to ask for a bit of extra time on an assignment. His grading is not very kind, however. He doesn't give partial credit on quizzes which makes it very difficult to ace them. Lectures are recorded and labs are not 100% necessary. Homework is completion so that is nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rob definitely wants you to do well, but he wont make it easy. You definitely earn/deserve every grade that you receive. Hes funny in class and almost seems like hes your friend. But sometimes in office hours, he makes you feel like youre underachieving. Rob explains things very well, but if youre looking for easy A, you wont get it here.

His lectures are very structured and thorough. However, make sure you ask him a lot of questions if you don't understand something cause the class gets difficult at times. The quizzes were a bit difficult, but make sure you ask him questions during the quiz if you don't understand something! Really funny guy too, so you'll enjoy the class.

Rob is an amazing teacher. He is very understanding and flexible, especially with the pandemic situation. I cannot recommend Rob highly enough. He is by far in my top 3 for all professors I've had at OSU. If you have to take CSE 2231, take it with Rob.

Rob was a funny/cool guy, and was great at explaining material in lectures. However, exams are very difficult. Pay attention to the requires/ensures on coding questions, because they're complicated. In my opinion grading was too harsh, but it's probably CSE dept grading rules. Took off points for .length vs. .size, not using newInstance, etc.

Rob is hands down one of the best teachers that I have ever had. He is super friendly and funny and is very knowledgeable about the coursework. He makes every class as fun and engaging as he can. He truly understands the material he is teaching and goes beyond just reading off the slides. If you're able to, take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hardest and most tedious class Ive taken at OSU. Rob is a fine lecturer but gives impossible exams (averages in high 60s/low 70s). They try to trick you on every question and barely cover the material. Take somebody else if you can, few did well. No curve or rounding at all. If you lose the lottery and get him, good luck with a rough semester.

He's an hilarious guy and he teaches well. His classes are funny, but his grading is just horrible, without the "no curve". I wish he just curved, coz a very few in the class actually get above an A/A- in the midterms. His highest was in the 80's for midterm 1.

Grate lecturer. After college no one will care about who taught you, they will look at your grade and judge. Rob will teach you well but he will DESTROY your grade. This inst a joke or me just hating him. I really like his lectures but I dont agree with his grading rules.

Rob is the best lecturer for Software 1. You will understand the material extremely well with him teaching. However, if you only care about the grade and not the material, then I would recommend taking software 1 with a different lecturer. On the first day he says his exams will be harder than other lecturers, and he is not lying.
Rob has a real gift for teaching. I really enjoyed his lectures and he is very helpful in labs.
my dude

He's a really funny guy who stays on topic and offers his own spin on the general provided slides. I honestly remembered more from content his jokes in class (and fierce hate of nulls), then the readings that are available. He's a bit intimidating when approached alone, but overall I think he's probably one of the best instructors I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Funny guy easy class to sit through.

Rob was an absolute goof during class but when I asked questions outside of class/in office hours he made me feel somewhat dumb. Despite that, I think he did a pretty good job explaining all of the concepts. He also refused to curve the class which was annoying. Overall though, Rob is probably one of your best options for SW1.

Some of the CSE 2221 instructors curve the class or offer extra credit. Rob does not and will not budge. The exams are very hard, but if you have prior coding experience it is a lot easier. Rob will gladly answer any questions outside of class, but he also makes you feel dumb.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best instructors I've had at OSU. I had him for 1223 which seemed to be a relatively easy course, so that may have helped. But even still, I had him during my first semester at OSU, and have yet to have another instructor whose lectures are as engaging as Rob's. (I just finished semester #4.) Absolutely phenomenal.
Great lectures! SW1 is standardized so they go off of slides from the department but he made them interesting. Very personal, responds to emails crazy fast at all times. Very helpful in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Best STEM prof i've ever had

He only goes off the lectures and its very hard to learn from the textbook if class is missed. Nothing is recorded and the professor doesn't post anything on carmen. If you don't show up to class, there might be a quiz and you wouldn't have known until 2 weeks later.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures

Mokashi is the goat, he truly cares about his students learning the material and he is great at teaching. His lectures are engaging and he clearly outlines his expectations for students. I would highly recommend Mokashi!

This professor is the best! He makes the class super easy, and I have never had to spend much time outside of class learning. Extremely lenient on graded assignments, as he will try to take off as few points as possible for the Midterms (which are 20% each). Also for the quizzes, if the class struggles he will allow you to submit outside of class.

I had him for MECHENG 2010H and he was amazing! Best professor I've had at Ohio State. Mokashi really cares about his students and wants to make sure that they truly understand the material. The class can be computationally difficult at times, but Mokashi knows this, and he is generous with his grading, especially on exams.
Overhyped but still a good teacher. Doesn't post notes so attendance is basically required. Class is hard but you are given the resources to do well if you study. Solid curve on final grade

Mokashi is a brilliant lecturer who makes complex topics easy to grasp. His clear explanations and focus on practice problems are super helpful. Definitely take advantage of Unstuck study and other study aids to ace this class.

Great guy, teaches well and makes it known that you can always ask questions. Occasionally asks class for steps needed to solve a problem. Graded on very few things, we only had a few sets of homework plus some in class (collaborative) quizzes and the exams. He'll move around dates sometimes in class, so always either go or get notes sent to you
Fantastic professor who cares a lot about students and makes you comfortable with asking questions.

You can tell Prof. Mokashi cares about his students and wants them to do well. He is a really good lecturer and explains things slowly and clearly. The only thing is that he doesn't post any notes online so try not to miss any lectures. Exams are 80% and there is barely any homework or quizzes given throughout the year.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He can't teach properly, never posts his notes online, has his textbook that skips so many explanations, and has problems with no solutions. He throws curveballs in the test, even in his posted notes that he prepared before, He skips on steps and never completes the lecture problems after skipping steps. He is a nice dude but cannot teach well.

One of the greatest professors to grace this earth. Lectures are clear and concise, examples are well led and discussed, homework is good, and exams were similar. The most important thing to take away is to take your time and to relax. The topics taught are simple (for the most part); silly mistakes will cost you dearly (30 pts/midterm).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor, tough class but Mokashi is by far one of the best professors I have had
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in the ME department. Just go to lectures, do the homeworks and you will get a really solid understanding of the class.

He genuinely cares about his students and goes out of his way to make himself accessible and approachable. Lectures are helpful, clear, and consists of a lot of practice problems. The exams can be hard but they are fair and he outlines exactly what will be covered. Don't skip class, take notes, and review what he tells you to and you will do well.

Mokashi is a brilliant and entertaining lecturer who is always willing to help out a struggling student. My only critique is that he gets very behind with grading and posting homework assignments, but is nevertheless a great teacher. He doesn't post lectures online, and the textbook is not nearly as clear as his lectures, so do not miss class.

Going to Mokashi's class was entertaining and resourceful. The combination of practice problems and actually learning stuff within class made the class a lot easier as well. He will tell you what to do to receive an A before exams, all you have to do is simply do the practice problems he assigns online and you'll pass.

Interesting professor with fun mannerisms and jokes. He cares a lot about the course material and the success of his students. The exams were relatively easy, did not post notes online though so lecture was definitely mandatory. Lab was easy as well, and that's were you truly learn the FEA.

Does not fix mistakes with grading, midterms very hard compared to practice problems. Often forgot to post practice for exams. Quizzes took whole class time with open notes because he usually made many mistakes in the question. Lectures mandatory and does not post notes. Extremely slow pace.

Mokashi is an AMAZING lecturer, he makes very hard content very easy to understand and goes slow in class to make sure all his students understand. He is very friendly outside of class and is flexible when it comes to exams/hws. he did a great job at teaching real applications of the content and rarely lectured the entire class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mokashi should stick to the easier classes. I took him for 3670 and his lectures were the most confusing and boring lectures I have sat through. Material does not make sense. Very space carmen page and little extra help provided to students. Strick grading schedule that doesn't make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Mokashi's lectures are basically just a reiteration of the textbook for the course, but the way he explains things in class makes the content 10x more comprehensible. I really enjoyed having him as my professor for this course, even though the content is rather hard in my opinion.

Online class where lectures are NECESSARY. You didn't have to attend live, but if you didn't watch then you would fail all exams and quizzes. Horrible lecturer, does not explain things well, and id not helpful when you are confused or asking questions. Maybe he is better in person, but I don't know?
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Barely anything in the grade book, so if you mess up there is little to no opportunity to make it up. Also, takes ages for things to get graded.

Does not respond to emails. I have an exam from the first month of classes that is still not graded yet (the semester ends this week). Underappreciation of points, my gradebook consists of 4 assignments. Quizzes were only during the month of September as we did not have another way to earn points other than large exams after that. No partial credit

Very lazy... did not put effort into his class. Did not follow his own syllabus and ran out of time to give out assignments. Graded exams very hard and didn't give feedback on first exam until the day before the final. Didn't respond to emails. Would get frustrated by students asking questions. Hardly taught. Worst class experience at OSU so far.

Prof. Mokashi was very good at lecturing and making sure that all students felt comfortable asking questions and understood before moving on. Unfortunately he is not the best administrator, so exam times were often chosen mere days before their date, tests and quiz grades came back very slowly, and he was slow to reply to emails. Would take again

Mokashi is a brilliant man, he is very smart. He is incredibly clear with his lectures, repeating the content at least twice for each important concept. He has a good grasp of the class, and you naturally focus on him. He is sometimes slightly late to class, but is overall helpful and a great professor.

Mokashi explains each and every problem he does in class incredibly clearly. He will tell you exactly what is on each exam. If you know how to do the problems in class and the practice problems he puts up the class will be breeze.

Mokashi is a fantastic lecturer with extremely clear examples and the best drawing skills I've ever seen. He explains things in a slow and logical way making complex problems easy to understand. Exams and homeworks are fair and he usually tells you exactly what problems will be on the exams.

he is a great professor, but hard grader and you need to do everything perfectly on the exams to get a good grade. Also, he is not lean on partial credit, just be careful when you do your exam, double check everything before you turn in the exam.

He is excellent at explaining material and gives clear examples. I thought the class was still difficult though. I went into the exam thinking I was ready and even felt good after the exam, but ended up not doing as well as I thought. He doesn't seem to be very lenient with partial credit.

He's one of best professors I've had so far. Gives clear examples and explanations. Tests were moderate to difficult. If you can do the problems on the syllabus and the extra practice problems he assigns, you should be fine. Only complaint is that he's a poor administrator. Very slow in grading and handing back quizzes and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best instructor I've had in engineering so far. His examples are so clear and he explains things in a really orderly way. His writing/drawing is a thing of beauty. Administratively lacking, but doing the practice problems listed on the syllabus is enough to keep up and he is great about helping with problems you have issues with.
Very good looking man, and great teacher

Great lecturer, there's no question about it. Very clear about the expectations and passionate about the subject. Tests were moderate/ difficult. However, he was a poor administrator.
