If you got that, you'll be just fine.  My only complaint is that the quizzes are rough. He throws in new stuff that you haven't seen before. But, collaborate and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Say what you want about Marc Smith, but he is a good teacher. Class is super organized and lecture videos are easy to follow. My biggest complaint with Marc is that it seems he goes out of his way to trick you on exams. I don't see why he wants to make the tests as hard as possible. you have to apply what you learn, not just memorize.

Well organized and non cumulative tests is the only thing he has going for himself. however, one test can be a half a semester of material in most classes. Smith assumes that you're only taking his class. If you want to question if you are cut out for college take his class and watch your life become sadder every day

Class is all online power points with voiceover.  The powerpoint are detailed/organized but they cover a lot of material. the people who pass collaborate with others on quizzes.  I hired a 25 year CPA and ex professor to tutor me and take quizzes. With his help still got a 50 percent on quizzes. no partial credit on tests and Quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tough, tough teacher. There's no face to face instructions so that people who aren't good at visual learning like me will straight up fail the class. I got around fifty percent before I drop the class. If you get one number digit wrong in the quiz, you get the whole thing wrong. Extremely difficult class, hard to follow and forced video watching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Take  detailed notes from the video lectures and make sure you have all the material understood for the quizes. They're easy and online so you can use your notes. The exams seem easy at first but once you get the grade back you realize how easily you can be tricked on questions.  Marc is great. He utilizes Carmen well and responds quick to emails.

Not one regret about taking his classes, not that you really have a choice to take Marc for 2200 and 2300.  One of the few professors at Ohio State that I've encountered that truly care about you learning.  2200 and 2300 aren't memorization, it's learning the material and applying it to real-world accounting problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Marc Smith is one of the best professors that I have ever had. People complain of his class being difficult but if you keep up with it, it's actually pretty easy. The way the class is set up it is easy to learn the material. Exams are very fair if you actually go to class and keep up. The quizzes are tough, but collaboration is allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Demonstrates how to take a complex problem and simplify it. Online videos prep you for recitation. Recitation preps you for test. Exams are fairly similar to practice problems you'll work through together. No random exam questions, can be tricky though. Very methodical problem solver. Highly recommend!!

The hardest class I've ever taken and worst grade I've ever gotten, if you can avoid this class DO IT! Got all A's and A-'s in my other course this semester and barely passed accounting. Have to learn everything on your own and teach yourself. The worst wish I would've taken it at C-State

Based on reviews on here, I thought this class would be very challenging. It was at times. I watched all the lectures while taking notes and attended every class. Marc gives hints on what will be on the exams during practice sessions. I did this and got a B before the curve and an A- after the curve. IF you put in effort, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pros: Organized; doesn't waste your time if class is over.  Cons: Hardest professor I've ever taken. Questions extremely complex and difficult, have many parts and take 30+ minutes to complete; oh yeah, did I mention he makes the class as hard as possible? Do not take any class with this Marcy Marc if you can avoid him. to get a C is a struggle.

He's the best when it comes to accounting.  He makes somewhat difficult material extremely easy.  Passed both 2200 & 2300 with A's before the curve. Most organized professor I've ever had.  If you do what he tells you to do on the first day of class you'll be fine.

Marc Smith, although very easy on the eyes, is one of the hardest professors I have ever had. You need to be very disciplined with the lectures and practice problems to barely stay afloat. He is very passionate but should not be an intro to accounting teacher, he takes it way to seriously. I would suggest taking it somewhere else. (Love the hair)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Marc Smith is the GOAT. Phenomenal lecturer, keeps everyone very engaged despite accounting being a relatively dry subject. He makes things interesting and explains topics and the details very, very well. Best professor I've ever had, very excited to take 2300 with him as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: YOU HAVE TO WATCH THE LECTURE VIDEOS. Do the practice problems 6 million and half times because he will go out of his way to try to trick you as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Marc Smith and I hate accounting. Basically how my semester went. Do the work and put the effort in for the exam and you will be fine. The content was kind of difficult for me as I've never taken a business course in my life, but Marc is a great teacher. He's great at walking you through examples.

Marc Smith is a good professor. I find him annoying as a person, but he knows what he's talking about. The material, while not difficult, is annoyingly finicky at times. Most questions on tests and quizzes are very specific. My main complaint is that the lectures have his stupid face sitting in the corner the whole time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tough class but good teacher. Very well organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: this class is so hard. the exams and quizzes are all memorization and if you don't have an iq of 150+ it's impossible to do good. i got a d because there is no way to study for his tests. he make is at as hard as he can. good luck remembering every single detail in the powerpoints!! avoid at all cost

Marc Smith is one of my favorite professors at OSU!! He condenses everything down to what you need to no, no extra fluff or BS work.  He wants to see you succeed and is always willing to help.  Make sure you do the practice problems and you are golden.

Marc communicates the material very clearly and very willing to answer any questions you may have.  The class is not very hard as long as you pay attention to lectures and do all of the work.  He is VERY strict about no cell phones in class, which is a bit unusual for a college professor, but just don't try to use your phone in class.

Marc is the best professor I've ever had at Ohio State. The class is very organized and same format week to week.  As long as you watch the videos and take notes then it is an easy class if you do the homework as well. Would definitely take another class with Marc again.

I am taking 2200 this summer. Marc is very passionate about teaching, and he explains everything clearly. It is a great course to take during summer. No homework to be graded. Midterms are tough, but getting A is not impossible.

I actually learned a lot from this course. His exams are pretty difficult but if you dont get behind and do the required hw and watch the modules each week, you will do fine. I highly recommend doing the weekly hw as many times as you can during that week. He definitely makes you work to be successful in this class. Overall, great professor.

Marc explains the material very well and is easy to understand, but the exams and quizzes are pretty difficult and they do not look anything like the homework or module problems. To receive a good grade, you need to know the material inside out because most of his exam and quiz questions are "critical thinking" based questions.

Marc is the most organized professor I've ever had at OSU. The tests are very similar to the practice exams that he posts. Watch the modules (take notes), and pay attention during lab and you should be fine. Go to the tutor room for any questions with quizzes, they are helpful.

Both classes are structured the same way. Marc is great, he's very clear when explaining things. Lectures are online videos, 6 quizzes and the lowest is dropped.  I felt like exams were usually fair, make sure you know how to do the practice problems but also review and understand the concepts/definitions. No textbook required or needed at all.

Before I take this class, I heard lots of student talking about how diff between HW and exams. However, after I take his class, i think professor smith did a good job. Online lecture is very helpful and well organized. Attending recitation and lab is really IMPORTANT!! HW are easy and you can drop one lowest. Listen video, attend class, easy A

Very poor professor. Quizzes and exams ask questions that cover very obscure concepts barely touched upon in lecture and recitation, and of course they don't at all resemble homework and practice problems. The level of difficulty for this course is insanely high, even if you diligently keep up with the material. Don't expect a good grade.
this class is a joke he baby's us through it all. tests aren't cumulative. you don't need the textbook.

Marc is an excellent teacher. Watch the online lecture modules, go to recitation and problem session, and things should come fairly easy. Take advantage of tutor rooms for quizzes, they are very helpful! Most test answers are all or nothing, so be careful and pay attention to detail. Class is mostly just memorizing a lot of formulas and using them.

If you are taking ACCT 2000 and your major requires you to take math beyond algebra, you will have no trouble with this class at all. As long as you watch the lectures, take notes, go to the weekly recitation, and do the optional homework, you will be fine. Learn the concepts and the math is extremely easy.
DO NOT SKIP THE CLASS
Much more difficult, exams look nothing like practice. Be prepared to just way wtf to yourself after exams.
All tests are all or nothing for every question. In my opinion, far easier than accounting 2. Super high curve at end of class to those with low grades, not much curve 80-85% at all.
What he taught in the class in useless in the exam and you would find what you have done is in vain

Video modules are very helpful, but that doesn't mean skip the recitation section. More helpful than the modules is seeing him work through problems in person. Great at explaining things, best professor I've had at OSU.
The one thing I like about both Marc and this class is that there are online lectures for the content he covers. He lectures VERY specifically and is extremely thorough in educating the content.

Marc is a great professor, he gives students all the tools to succeed, it all comes down to the work you put in to the class. If you watch the lecture modules, go to recitation with Marc, and pay attention in Lab with your TA it is easy to succeed. The tutor room is also very helpful for help on the quizzes. Know the material and you can do well.

As long as you actually watch the videos, go to class and pay attention, you should do well in learning the material. If you understand it, exams should be easy. Marc is great at explaining things and very helpful if you ask questions! Best professor I've had at OSU.

This class is really taught online in video modules and class time is used to go through examples - which I loved. The videos were made my Marc and they are very clear, but YOU MUST STAY ON TOP OF THEM AND DON'T GET BEHIND. This is an easy A if you watch every video and do the practice problems and go to class! But no cell phones, he's serious.
Went to the tutor room and one of the tutors said that Columbus State accounting is hard. Recommend Vignos for a problem session leader he teaches the material 10 times better than Marc ever could.
Terrible class. He does not know how to teach students. Does not provide a class for learning. Prepare to teach yourself. ATTEND ALL LECTURES!

Marc is one of my favorite professors so far at OSU. Hes energetic; keeps you interested during class. Watching the online modules for lecture helped A LOT. Going to recitation and "lab" and doing practice problems really helped cement the concepts into your head. Tests were still difficult though, if you mess up 1 thing, could hurt other problems

He does not do lectures just labs. All lecture are prerecord that you watch on line. For some people this may work but for me I need to be in person to grasp and be able to ask questions. My own advisor told me to talk this class at Columbus State or another small school and just transfer the credits.  Take that advice just get a transfer credit.

Marc is an average professor, he is great at accounting and like it but makes the class unnecessarily difficult. You have to do your own work and teach yourself every week or you will fall behind. I put in a lot of work, and did every problem available at least twice for each exam and still did very bad, he chooses the most difficult Q's on exams.
If you put in the work, you will succeed in this class. Accounting is all about meticulous detail, but Marc is great at presenting concepts.

Make sure you take the time to actually go to lecture and pay attention. If you put in the work, the class really isn't that bad. I took 2200 with cases and 2300 when they took them out.. it's a lot better without them. Be sure to go over all the in class practice problems. Exams are long, but if you know the material well, you'll have enough time.

Watch all the online modules, no matter how boring they are. Recitation and lab are a must for better understanding of the concepts. Class isn't difficult and concepts aren't tough to grasp. The effort you apply will be in direct proportion to the results you achieve.
Exams are hard. Some of the questions were just there to kill your grades.

Marc Smith was my kind of professor. Lecture modules online and class only one day a week. Have optional practice homework and mandatory quizzes every other week. If you practice all the examples given before each exam, then you should do well. I got an A on every test but I studied hard. Marc is a good, yet slightly challenging professor.

Your grade is entirely determined by your effort. Go to class, pay attention to the problems he gives you, do the practice exam, do the practice problems and you cannot get worse than a B. Also, the tutor room is very helpful, they will ensure you are always on the right track and help with quizzes
The class was very easy if you watched the videos and did the problems. Marc is a nice guy, and everything on the tests and quizzes are straight out of the concepts covered online and in problems.

His lectures and slides are straightforward and will teach you everything you need to know. There are plenty of examples, but since much of the class isn't in person there isn't much interactivity. All the exams have 100% coverage of the material, so you have to make sure you understand all of it.

Marc Smith is one of the best professors in Fisher. He's very clear about the work that needs to be done in the class and the class is very organized. In order to do well on the exams,  you have to be able to do all the homework problems as well as the problem worksheets from class without looking at your notes.

Marc gives you all the tools to succeed. HIs recitations are engaging and helpful. Unless you are an accounting genius, you will need to stay up on the work in order to do well in the class. This class will teach you a lot about accounting and sharpen your eye for detail

Marc Smith is extremely helpful in both office hours and through his online lectures. Take notes on the lectures and attend the "lab"/recitation and do the practice exams and the classes aren't difficult.

This class is time consuming, and the tests are very difficult. Test questions are often problems that you've never seen before in recitation or the practice problems. But if you understand the material, you will be able to solve the problems. Take advantage of the tutoring room.

Marc Smith is undoubtedly the most organized professor I've ever had. Everything from his video lectures, to recitations, to lab setup, is extremely clear and organized. He tends to try to trick you on exams, but if you keep up with the material and practice everything until you are positive you understand it, you will do well.

Take accounting elsewhere. The focus is more on a students ability to solve page long problems that will require you to use 2+ pages of paper just to solve. Test can have 3-4 problems and it will take most of the hour and half to complete. Many students don't finish. Memorization of formulas required. Calculus was easier. Professor is energetic.

This class is pure memorization. Make flashcards of the notes and study them and you should do fine on the exams. Marc is by far the best teacher I have ever had at OSU though and I would have taken all of my accounting classes with him if I could.

Marc Smith is the best teacher I have ever had at OSU. His lectures are interesting and he's always willing to help. The exams are tricky, but he truly cares about his students and wants to see you succeed. If you take his advice and spend the time to do the practice problems on your own a few times, you will do good on the exams, simple as that.

Marc is a great professor.  The dude absolutely loves accounting which is great but also can be annoying at times.  Tests are hard, quizzes not easy either.  Must work your butt off if you want an A or a high B.

He's without a doubt one of the best teachers at Fisher, but also the most unreasonably tough. The important thing to know going into this class is that there is no partial credit on tests, and that no topic is too small to be featured on the tests. You have to know every inch of the material, and more importantly you need to be able to do it fast.
Average class that he makes unnecessarily hard.  Exams cover every single possible thing.  If you stay on top of it, you will do well.  Don't expect an A.

The lectures are online for this class.  We met once a week for a recitation-like class. I loved this layout - the lecture modules were extremely organized and clear.  If you stay on track with them then you should be good. There are also practice problems that are great practice and the exams are exactly like them!

Very clear online lectures that have nothing to do with the quizzes. Emphasizes doing many practice problems, but the exam problems are not even close to the problems he gives. Take this class at Columbus State, the credits transfer without any issues and is half the work. I learned my lesson, and will be taking ACCT 2300 at Columbus State.

Lectures are online.  They can make sense but then when you go to do the quizzes you will realize that you learned nothing.  Exams are extremely difficult.  Accounting tutor room is very helpful but the exams just killed me.  Ended up getting a W and taking it at C-State.  Highly recommend C-state.
Marc Smith gives really hard tests but I find them okay because he is an excellent lecturer. The class is extremely well organized that if you do the work, you should do well.

The exams are way more difficult than they need to be. They have the absolute hardest problems on the exam that aren't even similar to what you go over in lecture and in labs with the TAs. I watched the online lectures, did the optional homework, didn't miss a class and I'm still stressing out about my final grade in the class.

Marc is a crystal-clear lecturer and the class environment is interactive and enjoyable. You MUST do the  related online modules prior to the class or you will not understand. Exams have no partial credit, so you must practice. To get an A, all you need to do is (1) watch modules, (2) do the homework 3x a week, (3) go to the tutor room

Just like 2200, this class is online modules and lecture where Marc does one problem.  Not helpful AT ALL. I didn't understand the information and didn't like having to teach myself.  Failed the first exam and immediately withdrew to save my GPA. Take accounting somewhere else unless this is your type of class layout or strong subject.

This class is weekly online modules where you teach yourself then show up to class and have Marc do one problem. Recitation with a TA is similar.  If you don't like classes where you have to teach yourself, take accounting at CState. This class destroyed my GPA because I didn't understand the material and he didn't explain things clearly.

Marc Smith is quite the character. He is definitely out there and loud, but knows his stuff and teaches it well. Very nice guy. I've had him for both 2200 and 2300. Classes are set up REAL NICE. 1000 points 50 attendance @ recitation (1 a week)  200 points online quizzes (best 4 of 6) 250 pt exam 250 pt exam 250 pt exam

To me, this class is the epitome of everything that is wrong with Ohio State. Taught through a series of drawn out online modules with one scheduled weekly class meeting, in a lecture hall with 200 other students. Marc does one example, then we all leave. It is so difficult! The quizzes are hard, the exams crowdedhard. INSANE WORK BUT NO LEARNING

Marc's online lecture modules were VERY easy to follow. He made the material easy to understand. He is pretty funny in recitation, but is VERY serious about the learning environment. DON'T LET HIM SEE YOUR CELL PHONE. You will be asked to leave in front of the entire lecture hall. I appreciate his dedication and would take a class with him again!

I can't believe Marc Smith is rated this highly.  I really want to give him all zeros to even it out, but I have tried to be accurate.  Do not expect to learn accounting in this class.  Expect:  memorization of formulas and procedures with little understanding of what they mean;  hours of dedication weekly.  2200 and 2300 are GPA killers for many.

Marc is great. He's there to help you learn and his exams are fair, but tough. If you put the work in, go to class, and stay on top of all deadlines you'll be fine.  If you have a question Marc is more than willing to help. He loves doing what he does, and it shows in his enthusiasm to help students.

The topics themselves are not very difficult. However the quizzes and exams are. Exams this semester were very long and difficult problems. Quizzes have questions that cannot even be solved without some sort of help. If you are not an accounting major just remember you are almost done with it.

One of the best accounting teachers I have ever had, not to mention one of the very few that I felt was genuinely interested and passionate about the subject. However, he's challenging and he expects a lot out of you, and there's no partial credit on the exams. So study and go to the tutor rooms or you won't pass

Expect to watch online video lectures and take notes for 4 hours per week. No material is taught in person. Marc is very clear, but there is a lot of material to learn which can be overwhelming. Do not fall behind. Class is heavily curved. Some say this is a weed out class for Fischer. Start studying a week in advance for each exam or you will fail

A lot of people hate on Marc but he was easily the best professor I've had at Ohio State. All his lectures, practice problems, and course materials are very organized and he gives you more than enough material (homework problems, lecture problems, practice problems, practice exams) to be able to succeed. Just need to put in the effort

Marc comes off as a tough professor at first. Once you get to know him and get through 2200 you will gain a lot more respect for him. The class is set up in a fashion that is very helpful to students but does take some time to complete all the material. Don't use your phone in class. Just don't. Seriously.

Marc is crystal clear in explaining all of the concepts in detail. This class can be challenging (especially since most people are only taking it as a prerequisite for finance and don't really care that much), but if you follow along with the modules, go to recitation, and rework the practice problems and practice exams before tests, you'll be fine

This is a tough class. Make sure you understand all the concepts thoroughly. Do ALL the practice problems. If you do this... the tests are just plug and chug and aren't a big deal. Marc is a very good instructor and if you pay attention and put enough work in you'll be fine. Also... if you've already taken Acct. 2200, you know what to expect.

The more time you put in the better grade you will get, there are no exceptions to that in his class. That goes for 2300 and 2200. Do the practice problems and print out the quizes so you have more practice problems to do when you study for exams. Speaking of the quiz, if you dont work with other people on it, you will fail. Dont skip a week on the lecture modules and if you have questions go to the tutor room, they are very helpful. Overall a great professor, but he makes you put in the effort.

Marc is extremely clear in his explanations - he goes through every concept in detail and makes sure that you get it. Do the homework problems on carmen, even though they're not graded. Exams are tough - you miss a couple questions by even a single number and your score drops by a lot. Overall, the material is pretty basic and easy to understand.

His recitations are engaging, & you must attend them regularly to pass.  He goes over more detailed, exam-like problems in recitation than the ones in lecture, and always takes a couple moments to ask if anyone has questions.  You'll spend about 2-3 hours outside of class per week.  I studied, on average, 14-16 hours for each exam. Put the work in.

The honest truth about this class- it's hard, with MANY details to remember, and truly, you'll STRUGGLE OR FAIL if you don't keep up with the material. Marc has high expectations (do NOT text during his lectures, he will throw you out), but his online lectures are amazingly clear if you pay attention. Work hard, study harder, and you'll do fine.

Impossible tests, endless hours of lecture.  Both ACCT 2200 and 2300 are offered at CState online, and can be taken at the same time.  TAKE AT CSTATE.  This course demands at least 4 hours of weekly studying, and that's not including midtermsfinals week!

At the beginning of the class, Marc will try to sell everyone that the rumors that his tests are unfair are false, and that as long as you keep up with the online lectures, attend physical lecture and recitations, you'll be good... What he doesn't tell you is that class takes 9 hours AT LEAST weekly, and that tests are impossible.  TAKE AT CSTATE!!
This class is a hard one for sure but if you spend time on it you can pass! I love the way the class is set up because I can study on my own time and it is really convenient.
hard

He is a great teacher, the class is all what you put into it. I strongly recommend watching the online modules, doing the practice problems,  and going to recitation. If you do these things you will get A's on the exams.

His online lectures literally give you everything you need for the tests.  Go to recitation, he goes over specific things that you may have a tough time with on the tests.  He is definitely my favorite professor.
Marc Smith isn't given enough credit for his teaching style. His online lectures and clear and concise, and his in person recitations are an amazing way of solidifying the concepts. Great professor.

Well, the material of the this class is not very difficult, however you have to do a lot of work every week so you can keep up with it. But, the worst part in this class is the lab, where you probably are going to lose all points you have gained in exams and quizzes.

One of the best professors in Fisher with clear logic, great knowledge and easy going personality. The two accounting core courses that every one has to take are tough, but as you do what Marc says in the first class, you should be fine. Really need to watch his videos, and finish every problems sets. A ton of work, but you can learn a lot as well

Best teacher in the Business school. Expects that students keep up to date with the information presented in class. If you show up to class, take good notes, and keep up with it, you will do well. If you try to study 2 days before the test, you will fail.

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE AT OSU. Marc Smith has to honestly be the worst professor I've ever had. Yes- the course is tough. But Marc Smith is NO help what so ever. He is rude as well. Honestly just take the class as CSCC- you'll learn so much more and you can rest easy knowing "professor" Smith isn't taking your money

GO TO THE RECITATION. His weekly quizzes ask relatively the same questions he answers via a handout during his lectures. There are a lot of slides online and they are a pain to go through, but if you do both of these things you should be fine. He is also an incredibly helpful guy. Do not hesitate to go as him questions.
Marc is awesome. Anybody saying he is a bad teacher is absolutely wrong. His part of the class is not difficult if you put in the time!

This class is HORRIBLY taught for a foundations class. You meet once a week for 50 minutes, everything else is on you to learn.. he posts video lectures online but they take hours to watch. You as basically teaching yourself accounting in this class. The exams and weekly quizzes are extremely hard. Take this with someone else or at Columbus State.
Very tough class, but online lecture is important along with recitation.  Sometimes scary during recitation when he calls out random people to answer.

Course is tough. Be prepared to spend lots of time on the class. Marc is in charge of the recitation/lecture component of the course. Marc is a nice guy who is willing to help you understand the material. His part of the course isn't all that bad but the lab component of the course makes it near unbearable at times.

Really a good professor.  Very organized and clear with regards to the lectures and material.  It is not by any means an easy class, you will get a grade based on how much effort you put in, like any other class.  This class takes some extra work though.  Online lectures are awesome.  Labs are really not helpful, and just time consuming.

Worst professor I have ever had. No partial credit. You could spend weeks studying for his tests and still fail. He doesn't know how to teach under the semester system. He doesn't understand that it's an INTRO class. If you want to pass this class, you have to do well on labs and quizzes.My advice, take it at Columbus State if you can.

Marc is a fantastic teacher. He is great at clearing things up and is very enthusiastic. He clearly cares about students. This class is tough but if you attend all of the recitations and keep up with all of the practice problems and lecture videos you will be fine. No surprises.

Marc is very helpful and will make everything clear IF you go into recitation. He is also there at office hours to help you see what you need to get certain grades and will give you his honest opinions. He is always enthusiastic and this helps make class interesting. The class is very hard though and will require a lot of time outside of lectures.

Marc ROCKS! This class is a huge time commitment and you will need to spend HOURS per week on accounting in order to pass. But Marc gives you all the tools you need to do well, it's just how much you will put into the class. Do all the practice problems twice before each exam and you'll do just fine!

Marc is an excellent professor. He really helps you understand the material well. Yes, you do need to put time into the class to receive a high grade, but what class does not need time? Overall, one of my favorite professors here at OSU. He really made accounting interesting, and the reason why I switched majors after talking to him.

This class requires at LEAST 9 hours a week put aside working on watching all the online lectures and doing all the practice problems and online quiz. This is the only way to pass this class with an A. And with this, Marc is a really good teacher and delivers all the information very clearly. The key is to just contribute a lot of time to the class

Online only. Marc grades answers only not work. If you're off by a penny you're wrong. Too bad he doesn't care. Not there to teach. There to be bitter and fail you. Not a real teacher. Absolutely no help. Does provide big curve but he still doesn't care about helping his students succeed. I studied 15+ hrs a week and barely passed. Beware.

To pass you must go to tutoring. Learn all equations backwards and forwards. Tests will make you pally equations backwards. As in Marc teaches one thing then expects another come test time.. Tests are 75% of class. He does not grade work. Just right or wrong. If you're off by a dollar you're wrong. Doesn't care to help students. There to fail you.

Marc teaches you how to apply equations on way then come test time expects you to apply them another way. If you don't know all equations backwards and forwards and don't memorize every single word he speaks or puts online you will fail. Does not teach a single thing. Expects memorization. Pointless and waste of time. Memorizing gets you nothing.

Awful professor. Expects minimum 20 hours a week of studying considering the amount of work he loads online. Quizzes are clear with materials online but only account for 25% of grade. Exams are the other 75% and are nothing like quizzes. Will spend all of your free time with tutors and studying just to get by.. Not here to help you.

EXTREMELY HARD course. Stay away from this professor. He does NOT grade your work, you are either right or wrong. The best teacher at Fisher. You will learn the material. 3 midterms are all difficult. Just do all practice problems and quizzes to prepare. Labs are awful. Marc is a good guy and there are a lot of resources available to do well. Getting an A is near impossible though

Marc is by all means not an easy teacher. This class separates the men from the boys in the business school. You have to do all the non-mandatory homework to get a good grade. It is by far the hardest 3 hour course I've taken yet. Use the lab portion as a buffer to protect your grade

Marc is extremely helpful. His exams are tough but he gives you all of the material and resources needed to be successful. Not an easy A but it is possible with hard work. The labs are terrible but those have nothing to do with Marc. His portion of the class is awesome. You can't get a much clearer professor than Marc.

Acct 2200 is sort of tough, the class consists of both regular lecture and lab. The lab portion is annoying, and i did not get much out of it. Grading depends on T.A. Nothing really new to add. Marc is a good teacher, but his tests are just a lot harder than the practice problems. If you don't want any B's to show up on your report card, then don't take this class because theres a good chance you'll get one. Labs and quizzes can help your grade but maybe not enough to get an A. Take at CBUS State.

His lecture videos are very clear and organized. Going to recitation is extremely helpful and he usually gives problems similar to ones on the quizzes. The tests are incredibly hard and much more difficult than the practice problems and quizzes. They do not prepare you for the difficultly of the tests. The labs can help your grade though.

AIS is Definitely the easiest class I've had Marc for. Typical Marc Smith class. Lectures are very structured and easy to follow. Just memorize your notes word for word that he writes on the board and study HW problems and you will do well. 2 midterms, final, and 3 quizes.  Should be an easy accounting class and it is.

Hes the most terrible professor I ever have. The exam is super difficult, is not as the same easiness as the practice assignments. He WILL DESTROY your GPA, i recommend taking this accounting class in another school! I hate this class.

He is very funny during recitation, but he is such a bad ass after class. most people can not get a good grade, not just because the course is difficult, one of the main reasons is the online lecture is so slow and boring. the quizs and exams are way too difficult. the worst thing is the lab which takes your much time to finish.

This was my third class with Marc. As always, he's extremely clear and you can't NOT learn the material if you pay close attention. No need to use the text, as he writes his own notes (which are very helpful for studying). Re-work quiz and example problems as much as possible.  Pretty work-intensive class, but he gives a huge curve.

AMIS 310 with Marc Smith was definitely a bit of a grind. The online lectures are great because you can pause and rewind the videos when you're trying to really soak-up info. Quizzes can be printed out and worked on throughout the course of the week. Exams are definitely tough, but very manageable if you complete all the practice problems/exams.

WARNING! This is a mostly online class! The online lectures are painfully slow. Not hard though if you can wade through the info and have time to practice. Taking the exams backward is good advice, as mentioned elsewhere.

When I went to the first class--the last of my 20-hr schedule--I thought I was going to drop it, as the other classes were going to keep me very busy.  I listened to his first lecture and was blown away.  Outstanding teacher! Thorough understanding of the subject, clearly conveyed.  You'll need to know the material dead cold to get an A.  STUDY!

Open ended problems at the end of each exam can be very tricky. Most of the time they aren't covered at all in the quizzes or lecture slides. class is rough, but if U keep up(watch online leactures B4 every fri, do HW, go to Fri lecture) U should do fine. On average, quizzes that are online take about 30-45 minutes(which depends on how well prepared U are). Exams are are tough, so study well in advance. Watch your time b/c thats what hurts students on exams. there was a nice curve @ end.

exams can be hard! prepare at least a week in advance. Helpful hint:work backwards on the exams! the last 10-15 questions are fill in blanks that are worth 10-15pts each. the bad thing is, its either all or nothing.no paritial credit given. the first 30 questions are multiple choice so you can guess if your short on time. go to fri lect & good luck

Good online teacher.Slides book helps a lot.Keep on track with hw.Take your time on quizzes thats where it will get you.All or nothing point on both quiz and midterms.Dont have to show work on either.No tb.Study lots for the midterms and do the practice problems.

VERY hard to get an A. Words of advice: Study A LOT for 1st Midterm and Final, they are both a lot harder than 2nd Midterm. Go to Terri for help on labs, LAB TUTORS ARE WORTHLESS! Great teacher. He is very clear and organized. Gives great notes. The class (211) is a hard class. The tests themselves are hard. The group projects in labs are all but impossible with no lenience for anyone.
The best professor at Ohio State. He is crystal clear and sorta entertaining. The tests are hard though, especially in 212. Do all the practice exams! Go to the tutor labs!

Best teacher I have had a Ohio State. He is funny, nice, helpful...everything a teacher should be. Many kids complain about how hard 211 and 212 are but if you go tho his lectures and do his practice problems you will get an A.

While the material is not hard, it is VERY hard to get an A. Marc is a good, clear prof, but no partial credit on exams kills students' grades. No doubt he teaches really well and the course work is not actually that hard. HOWEVER, this guy has some ULTRA HIGH expectations from students. He grades EXTREMELY hard and his exams are beyond comprehension. Take at your own risk, if GPA doesn't matter to you, which I doubt

If you actually follow the online lectures it's pretty easy to grasp all the material. However, it's a really basic class and Smith won't help you if you want to learn more. And if you ever try to prove him wrong, he's too full of himself to listen to anyone else's opinion.

BY FAR the best accounting professor OSU has to offer. This is not and should not be an easy class, but Marc makes it doable. If you want an easy A try a different class. Before taking this class, you should decide what you want out of it.  If you are going for the easiest "A", do not take this class. Great professor.  Completely clear with everything he does.  Do all the homework problems and sample exam problems and know them thoroughly, and you will do fine on the exams. Do not take this class at osu. it is much easier at columbus state. i failed it at OSU and got an A at Columbus state
Crystal clear.  Labs are a joke-points will be taken off for the same things you were told to do the week before.  Material is not hard, but there is a lot of it.

Exams r hard esp. the final exam. if u know nothing about accounting, then this is a class u have to review all your notes and new notes daily in order to do well throughout the quarter & final.ALSO* U WILL TAKE A EXAM ON THE FIRST DAY OF ACT 212 OVER WHAT U LEARNED IN ACT 211...SO LEAVE THIS COURSE KNOWING THIS STUFF INSIDE OUT

Good teacher,Hard class. take this class at CSCC if your not specializing in Accounting. The quizzes are hard. The lectures are online so make sure you keep up and watch them B4 recitations. Albeit Marc is great at teaching accounting, but when it comes to the tests the practice problems and practice test do not even compare to what the actual test is. Marc is a great guy but this class needs to be restructured and not taken online.

I've never had a teacher, on any level, who is as genuinely excited and interested in teaching as Marc is. He lives to teach and is very understanding. Great Professor, highly recommend taking his class, probably best professor in the accounting department, accounting is hard and he understands and does everything in his power to teach accounting as best he can, go over the online lectures before quizzes and tests and you should be good

Not an easy class by anyone's standards, but Marc is certainly the BEST accounting professor Fisher has to offer. This was my third time with him and it was another great experience. he is a very good teacher with friday sections that help a lot with quizes and midterms.  This class can be hard but if you watch all the modules online and do the practice problems it is very managable.  Also try to get in a good group for the labs as it will boost your grade alot.

This was a very difficult class. I would highly recommend taking this class at another university. Marc Smith is a fairly good teacher. It is Ziegler the course condinator that makes the course material difficult. No need for the book.

Very smart, intelligent guy! His speech is extremely clear and he tries to interact with his students in the lecture. since Acct211 is a hard class everyone who wants to get a better grade should work hard.

He is a good professor but this class is so dumb.  Its an accounting class thats online.  In my opinion that is just stupid. But Prof Smith is a good teacher even though you meet once a week for 2 hours to go over everything you have covered that week.

he's in charge of the exams and lectures. go to lecture, it is helpful and he'll answer questions. WATCH the online lectures. it's annoying but it's the best way to learn the material. book is unnecessary. exams are hard, be sure to study a lot...

Marc lays out the material with exceptional clarity. I do suggest doing the practice problems prior to taking each quiz as well as during the week of the exam. Marc is a very clear teacher.  He will call on students randomly in a 200 person rec. which is not always fun. He is a great teacher who is very methodical and teaches the material in a very clear manner. The lab is the portion that really sucks, though. The labs seem disconnected from the actual class, and they just get in the way of studying the material that you will be graded on. Great prof though.

This class is not as difficult as everyone made it out to be. However, it is imperative that you complete the online practice problems independently and regularly. If equations had been allowed on tests, I would not have stressed out nearly as much.  This a minor course.  The minor Finance course allows a sheet of examples, which I think furthers learning of subject, not focusing on memorization.

Rough course to get through.  Used to get people out of the business college.  Alot of people drop the class and don't end up getting through it.

online lectures are annoying to watch every week, but he is clear about the material. exams are easy to mess up.

easy class. why does this guy talk like the way he does? does he think hes some kinda news announcer or something like that? he really likes attention. look at all the video lectures! instead of formula & concepts & stuff, we have to watch his close-up face for 2 hours/week.

Online lectures were long and it got to the point where you get excited when he changes polo shirts, but overall, VERY good class! I LOVE MARC SMITH!!!!!!!
Good Prof... Midterms are hard... nothing like quizes he gives in class.... do homework you will be fine

Marc is a very cool teacher. Nontraditional i guess. Very concerned on making sure you have the concepts of the class down. He's laid back and very approachable. I asked him about my grades and he was able to e-mail me them...a couple days later, but otherwise well organized. His notes may not be his, but he does a good job at lecturing.

Great professor.  One of the best I have had at ohio state.  Really taught the material well on online lectures.  This class should be offered in a classroom instead of just online because there is a lot of material and hard to follow, but he does a great job teaching.  2 midterms, a final, and quizzes every week.  A VERY CHALLENGING COURSE!
not a bad prof, prolly the best possible for the acct 211 class at OSU

Tough class.  Smith is a little rough around the edges but one-on-one he's really nice and helpful. Make sure to go talk to him during the quarter. I did and he gave me some suggestions that allowed me to really improve my grades. Overall one of the better classes I've taken at OSU and I've been here for 4 years.
He does a very good job with this tough class. Everyone says how much better this class is now than what it used to be.  Overall a very solid prof.

The online lectures were slow and boring if you are already taking 20 hours finding another 3 on top of that to watch the lectures is difficult. Had it been in a lecture hall it might have been easier to deal with but having to make time and watch it on a computer just sucks. The class is hard and the Lab groups even worse. Good luck though.

OK, first off, scheduling is coming up for sophomores to be and if you have to take 211 or 310, TRUST ME, TAKE HIM.  Best professor at i've had so far.  If you are one of the people complaining about him, you prolly are taking 310 and don't know anything to begin with and if not, you simply are trying to place your own blame on someone else.

I can safely say I hate Marc's online lectures. I feel I don't retain information, and his slow speech, and unfunny, quirky remarks do nothing but make me want to shove my pencil in my eye, rather than take notes. If this class was taught in a lecture hall, it might be more reasonable but I can't justify the time required for so little gained.
He made me love accounting and I wish i could have him for the rest of my acct classes.
OBNOXIOUS!

Awesome class structure.  He posted video and audio of all his lectures as well as a transcript of all of them, including slides and comments he makes.  All I did was go through the transcript and took notes and I got an A.  Very cool guy too.
No Comments

The class pretty much sucks, but u have to take it. He talks about him self a lot, even in the online lectures. You probably will wanna throw your speakers out the window by the end of the class. Had a couple run ins with him and he wasn't really nice. He kinda makes you feel stupid for asking questions.

He knows the material well, but the class in general sucks.  Ohio state doesn't seem to care about whether or not its students actually learn and can apply the material.  And sometimes the TA's are wrong, so make sure you reference the book.
My favorite teacher so far at OSU.  He's really funny and explains things clearly in a wau that its easy to understand.  His online modules are great.  Definitely recoomend this instructor.

Cool guy very nice and approachable but teaching isnt meant for him. Hes terrible with giving back grades or really doing anything on time. we had a midterm the last day of class and then had a final four days after that. never responds to emails and misplaces some grades.

I TOTALLY DISAGREE! Marc was a cool person, yes,  but his class sucks. He doesn't give you back grades so you have no clue how you are doing in the class. He doesnt answer emails or respond to web CT. Lecture is all over the place and he doesnt even write his own notes or test. Awful.

Marc Nathan Smith is one of the coolest teachers you will ever have. His phonetics class was so funny b/c he makes all these crazy sounds from languages (his Hindi impression is hilarious). He goes over the material and answers everyone's questions very well. you can get to know him outside of class too (80s night at Skullys!) awesome teacher
everyone said his tests were really hard, but truthfully, if you know the material, you'll get a 100% on the test.  If you fail this class, you are either not doing the work, or simply retarded.
No Comments

Horrible!! The only way you can get a business minor is if you take his online course (at least when I took it, that was it) - completely hideous and boring.  After staring at his face online for hours and hours each week I wanted to shoot myself.  This is the only class I had to take over ever in college.
This is a tough class. You have to be on your toes for this one. Smith is a tough, yet solid prof.
What a great prof! Everything was extremely clear and you always knew what to expect from him. I don't know of many profs that can make accounting enjoyable; Marc certainly does that!
He was very enthusiastic and knew his material well. His Quizzes and Midterms/Finals were challenging though.

He is a good teacher, he gives lots of examples in which he gets the class involved so people can understand and learn from other mistakes. However, his exams are a little difficult because every acct. mistake you can make he has a mulitple choice answer for. So you think you get it right, but you really don't. Over all great teacher!!

Impossible...(take accting at Columbus state; guarenteed A's)!  This is an online class--with an optional class on Friday (optional book as well).  Quizzes are taken online and are really hard, he drops 2 though.  Exams are hard and all multiple choice, but throws a lot of tricky questions in there. Good Luck.
unbelievable helpful;clarity is excellent;great guy;easily the best teacher i have ever had

He is the best professor i've had at OSU!!!! He made me like accounting.  This guy is amazing.  I hope OSU gives him the  money he deserves.  I don't care what this guy's teaching. Whatever it is I'm sure he'll do it better than most people.  TAke his class don't be afraid
Had him for 522 and auditing.  He was fantastic in both.  Truly enjoys teaching and holds your attention well in class.  Very fair.  I owe him a debt of gratitude for sticking with accounting.

Straight up, Marc has some of the hardest tests ever. However, if you go to class and put forth the effort you should do fine. Class was always fun and the dry sense of humor was great. Best prof yet. Take this guy.

Very clear in lecture, not boring! Genuinely wanted to help students learn. The textbook was awful, but the online lectures were helpful and the in-class recitations were indispensable. Often, I went to the recitation instead of watching the online lectures.

I was terrified of the online format of this class but loved it. It forced to keep up. Marc is awesome, gives you every option of how to do the lectures and offers optional reviews once a week(no mandatory class time) Very fair tests, straight forward lectures. If you keep up it will be fairly easy.

Awesome.  Most enthusiastic Prof out there.  Good at answering any questions. Clear formulas and defintions.  Go to class and follow his notes for the exams.  Reminds me of Corky Remano in a good way.
Great teacher.  Last class before graduation.  Helpful. Just ask questions and keep up with the material and you'll be just fine.  Online courses usually scare me, but this one moves smoothly.

Although this was a computer-based class, I still made attempts to attend some of his optional lectures where he clarified homework/quiz materials. As a non-Acct/Biz student, I managed to understand most of his VERY comprehensive materials. Very clear and straight-forward lectures and slides.
Best professor I have had at OSU!  I absolutely loved coming to class.  You will never be bored.  Get this guy if at all possible!  He is very fair too which is nice to see in a prof.
Great prof!  Really explains things well and is very entertaining in class.  I strongly recommend him for this class to all students!
very good instructor. always will to teach. the easiness of the class is the result of brief explanation of the material

Marc is an amazing teacher.He actually teaches the material with out putting you to sleep. He is very concerned with making sure everyone understands.  His tests accuratly depict what he has taught in class. Class Average: 75% Impressive =)

He' SO adorable; and really loud; his lecture is very organized and straight forward; he won't torture you over b/s in the book; he just teaches you what you need to know; take him; avg test grade = 70%(in our class), usual curve is about 3%: 90% for an A
Good prof, online lectures went too slow, but thats good for business students. Just download the PDF files the night before the exam and you'll be money.
AWESOME!!  Best class & teacher at OSU and this is an online course!!  Marc is great and he doesn't take any crap from whiny students.  Highly recommend!!
Good sense of humor.....makes the class fun!

Man, this guy needs some ritalin. He doesnt stop moving the whole lecture and his little sayings make me question the value of my life. He is a bit unorganized, and for not having to teach at a class, could be a little more on top of the ball.
marc did a great job.....a teacher that actually cares.  one of the best teachers i have had.
great teacher! energetic! have a jim dandy of a weekend! and remember that assets ALWAYS equal liabilities and equity!!
Excellent instructor, one of the best in AMIS!  His classes made me want to keep on coming back!This guy is certainly worth taking!
Very nice Professor. He works hard to try to get you to understand. Accounting is just a very very hard subject to grab a hold of...
No Comments
Good teacher did his best with accounting. Funny, nice, easy to understand.
Very interested in student's learning material. Best Prof I had at FCOB.
TRIED to make acct fun & easy. Overall good teacher
very energetic and funny for accounting

only the two midterms and the final exam counts towards out grade, but he does curve at the end of semester. However, his lectures are a pain to decipher. I could not understand a single thing he explained.

Lecture is all chalkboard (literally 0 canvas) and he's not great at answering questions. He once answered a question with "well I hope you figure it out soon." He convinced the entire class there was no curve and then added one (W). Exams were basically the entire grade but they were almost identical to the practice exams (given 2ish days before).
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a chalkboard lecturer so no slides uploaded to Carmen but I find that it forced me to pay attention better. Take midterm 1 more seriously, looking back I could've done so much better. Also, our class was curved at the very end (86% to A-)!

Almost no supplemental material to the class. All you get is 1 practice per week, some practice exams, and the textbook. The only things that counts towards your grade are the exams. The final exam takes up 45% of your grade. His lectures and his handwriting are hard to understand. Only way I learned was the textbook and youtube.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 90% of the class is exam based but he makes all of the exams very similar to the practice exam and the final also follows a similar format to the previous 2 exams. He can take some getting used to from a lecture style but overall is a chill dude who just really tries to have people actually learn the content and it's curved class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maybe the easiest Ochem professor if you want to get an A. Exams are very straightforward (not many mechanisms) and nearly identical to the practice exams. However, he made it unclear what grade you need in order to get an A. He said to shoot for 95 for an A, but I ended with a 92 and still got an A.

McGrier is a likable lecturer, but he is not good at answering students' questions. He frequently disregards the hands in the air and gives vague responses. He does not upload review material until 2 days before an exam. I have an 88% before the final curve, so you can do well if you study a lot. Probably the best option for o-chem profs at OSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ochem is a hard class to start. He moves through content extremely fast. He isn't great at answering questions, typically leaving the class more confused. The exams are much harder than the quizzes or other practice problems he supplies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very old school, hardly uses technology. Lectures are done on whiteboard, tests/quizzes are paper/pencil only. Moves very fast and answers questions in a way that makes things seem more confusing than they really are. Quizzes are fairly easy, exams are very hard, there is no homework (grade is only based on test scores). Doesn't give much practice.

I think McGrier is a pretty good professor. He does write his lectures on the chalk board and sometimes it can be hard to read. Attend recitations!! The recitation activities are just like the quizzes and the exams are just like the practice ones (which get released two days before the exam). You can get away without buying the textbook for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took a chance on taking McGrier and I am SO HAPPY. Firstly his lectures are amazing and he always answers questions. Ochem is hard but, he explains the concepts well. No homework, weekly quizzes, 2 exams, and 1 final (45% of grade). He gives problem sets exactly like the quizzes! His exams are just like the practice and I recommend him to anyone!

Easiest exams for 2520, but there are tradeoffs. He gives no practice material for exams, so be prepared to ask your friends in other classes for theirs. No homework grades, only 6 recitation quizzes (10% of grade), 2 Midterms (45%, 22.5% each), and a final (45%). He takes notes on chalkboard, so his lecture style may not be for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
- Attendance is recommended because there might be something that is in his online lecture note but not in his lecture and will not be tested. Must pay attention to follow his pace.
- Exam is kinda straight forward. Mainly predict products, reagents, mechanism(may take 90% of the points). Have a little bonus pts.

This course is undoubtedly very difficult, but if you put in enough effort, you can get good grades. Professor McGrier teaches clearly. Even if the score of this course comes 100% from examinations, his grading will not be particularly strict, and all students will be given an additional 5 points for each examination. Recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Writes notes on the chalkboard, which was pretty hard to see even from the third row. The content was challenging, but the exams were fair, and all midterm material was covered in the lecture. The final exam was worth 45% of the grade, and the 2 midterms were worth about 25% each. Always let the class out early. Graded by very few things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have him for 2520 but there isn't an option for it. He is a very good professor that clearly explains what you need to know and the quizzes and exams are all things you've seen in lecture. People here are just complaining because they don't know how to study properly but he's arguably the best science professor I've had at OSU. Take his class!!!

Not the best professor. You can tell he knows what he's talking about, but the way he teaches it is not helpful. Students would ask questions & not understand the content after several attempts at understanding. It's too hard of a course to be so mediocre in teaching it. Would take someone differently if I had the chance. Thank god for the curve.

Dr.McGrier wants his students to succeed, he is very willing to answer questions during lecture and after class. However, showing up to lecture is very important and he does move pretty quick. Gives out a practice midterm before both of them. 2nd Exam is the hardest in my opinion due to it including retrosynthesis. One of the better choices at OSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, he's a consistently good lecturer who isn't an asshole and provides good feedback. His notes are also pretty damn useful if you miss class. In the OChem Department, he's absolutely one of the better picks.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did feel that he would move quickly through the content in lecture, and he often would not understand what students were asking when they asked questions. Lectures were well organized though. Going to recitation is helpful because that's really the only place to get practice problems. Overall not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doing well is guaranteed as long as you put in the effort, pay attention, and ask questions. The professor and TA are readily available to assist you, but be prepared to study diligently as the course is challenging. Quizzes and Exams were relatively straightforward as long as you studied. Overall, it was an intriguing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you just study and pay attention in class doing well is definitely attainable. The exams are very straight forward and exactly the same as the practices. My only complaint would be there is a lack of resources for practice but if you find some from other professors you will be fine.

All he does in lectures is draw messy notes on a chalkboard. Doesn't give many practice resources. The second exam has retrosynthesis which is an Ochem 2 concept so why he includes it is beyond me. Would not recommend him to anyone.

I believe that if you go to lecture and pay attention, even most of the time, doing well in this course is attainable. Dr. McGrier provides very good lecture notes, which are handwritten and are highly legible. I do however, wish that there were more graded assignments. The grade breakdown was 45% final, 45% (2 midterms), and 10% quizzes.

He gives a generous curve of about 12%. Exams are tough, but they're exactly like the practice exams. The 2nd exam was the hardest because of Retrosynthesis (which is an o-chem 2 concept). Not sure why he tests us on it in o-chem 1. No resources on this topic, I recommend get a tutor for this topic. Final was fair, heavy on predicting products.

Out of all the professors, he writes his exams and they are just like the practice exams which are given 2 days before the exam. The averages were pretty low; first exam average was a 70% and then 2nd exam average was a 55% and final was 52%. He does go fast. There were 6 total quizzes and 2 of them were take home. They were also a little difficult

He doesn't communicate with his TA regarding what we're talking about in class. It was simply an excruciatingly difficult class. Moves very quickly through lecture and doesn't give you very much to help you prepare for exams. Gave a practice exam the night before the midterm but I don't know. This class was a struggle and I don't think he helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Mcgrier prepares his students very thoroughly with quizzes and practice exams that are in the exact same format as actual exams with slight variations. This is a hard class but Mcgrier makes it much easier than many of the other chem professors on campus. The curve was GENEROUS. Lecture, quiz and practice exam examples show up on exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Force yourself to study a bit a day. If you do that you will get an A. Dr. McGrier teaches to the level of expectation and the curve is generous. Not a lot of practice material outside of lecture, so master the lecture examples and find more from other profs. Curve is very generous. I would definitely recommend his class. Work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Annoying that he doesnt post notes and makes mistakes often in lecture. Take ochem 1 with anyone else if you have to take ochem 2. This class underprepares you for further classes in chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. McGrier, but quite frankly he could teach this class better. He definitely wants his students to succeed, but he doesn't communicate well with his TA and he teaches material in a very basic way, then tests it in much more complicated questions. This class needs homework and more practice problems with less concept work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Given the options for OChem 1 professors at Ohio State, I would say he's a very good choice. He doesn't give a practice exam for the final and he only gives 1 practice per midterm (which is given out 2 days before the test) but the practices he gave were very useful and the exact format of the exams. All the exam material is covered in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was by far the hardest class I have taken but Dr. McGrier is helpful and wants his students to succeed. He doesn't provide a lot of practice material or post his notes on carmen so GO TO LECTURE. If you put in the work you will do well. The format of practice tests are EXACTLY like the actual exam. If I can pass this class, anyone can.

Dr. McGrier is a great professor to have! His organization of lectures is admirable. He stops after a section to ask for questions. Friendly and timely email response. Willing to help after lectures, where I spent a lot of time and learnt a lot! Though averages are very low, it pays off if you work hard for it! I got 90% on the final!

McGrier (from what I gather) has improved tremendously from last year to this year.  He doesn't utilize many online resources but practice exams are EXACTLY the same as the actual exam, he's always willing to help inafter class and the grade scale is generous (86A, 78B before a curve).  Reading before lecture is a must!

He does rush through lectures; however, so would anyone who needs to teach 10+ chapters. The problem is that he is not thorough and pretty much recites everything that the book says. He also doesn't take note of small but important things which somehow end up on exams. Good curve, though. Went in with a 78 after the final and ended with an A-.

The class very much requires you to rely on the book and other professor's notes and practice problems. He would frequently make mistakes in his notes and a TA or student would have to correct him. He says he won't curve the class, but does significantly.

He does speed through lectures so you have to be awake and ready to keep up. Quizzes and exams were hard, but the TAs helped a lot to learn the material before quizzes. Read the book before exams and use other professor's practice exams prior to exams. Someone else said he didn't curve, but my grade was absolutely curved! Very low averages..

Not as bad as everyone is saying.  His lectures go fast, but that's going to happen no matter who the professor is. He is very clear about exactly what he expects to see on his exams. However, he doesn't provide any study materials like the other professors do. Reading the book before lecture, and doing (& UNDERSTANDING) the homework is a must.

By far the worst lecturer I've ever had during my three years in college. He flies through material, doesn't answer questions thoroughly, writes chicken scratch notes on ungodly amounts of paper that he projects onto an overhead screen. He laughs when the class freaks out and decided a 60% (failing) class average was enough to not curve it. AVOID!

He goes very fast during the lectures. He isn't helpful since he doesn't answer questions during lecture. when he gives "study guides" during lecture for exams, they are not helpful. If you get him, switch classes.

Cool guy but confusing teacher. During lectures he  writes down notes that project onto a screen while he talks. I find that he goes fast through lectures and does not let us write everything down. For tests he does give a "study guide" but there are no other practice problems but for the book. Tests/quizzes are hard and I find my TA more helpful.

Rather than explaining new material, he teaches as if it is a review which makes it very difficult to understand what is going on. I didn't understand nearly any concept until my TA reviewed it. He also refuses to answer questions in class but complains about receiving too many questions in emails.

Speeds through lectures and does not teach. He simply writes out notes and does not explain anything. He does not answer student questions in class but encourages visiting the TAs and Office Hours. However, once visiting office hours he still does not EXPLAIN mechanisms and reactions. He is VERY impatient also.
Very easy class. If you need extra time for an assignment, simply email her.

I'm honestly not sure where all of the negative comments are coming from because Dr. P is great. She does expect a lot from her students so as long as you read the syllabus and follow it you'll be fine. I also think she is a great person outside of class as well.

I reached out to her and it took her a long time to respond and when she did finally respond she completely avoided my questions and honesty was really rude. Very tough grader and even being slightly late she practically fails you. A lesson I learned, but also would be nice if she was more considerate and not rude
definitely would not recommend her. terrible grader

Probably the worst professor I have ever had. Taking off pretty much all of my points is not teaching me anything it's actually ruining my GPA. This is way too much work for a 1 credit class it's ridiculous. Do not recommend her and there are other classed out there. Lets be nice to kids during finals week and not fail them because you're the worst

yeah no I hate this class. why take off 80 points after 2 days of being missing. that's messed up. sorry that you give vague directions and not everyone has insane materials at home to work with. lets consider being more reasonable and a good professor for once thanks.

A very manageable class to take as an elective, even as a second session course. It's a bit annoying to buy some of the cooking items if you don't already have them, but grading criteria is super clear and most of the points are on participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She makes mistakes while grading assignments and quizzes and you have to go to her to fix them or else your grades will not reflect your effort. The lab assignment topics were not always taught in lecture. Go to class as lectures are not recorded and TAKE NOTES from lecture because she quizzes on specifics and things not always mentioned in slides.

Dr. Pohlschneider is an amazing professor and really cares about her students. I just don't recommend taking FDSCTE 1140-Kitchen Science if you live in a dorm or don't have access to a kitchen as every assignment is done in the kitchen. She grades fair and as long as you give effort there should be no issue.

Great class compared to Caffeine Science. Far easier and doable. You can work on the assignments with others taking the class, just have to do your own written portions. Mostly an easy A if you're looking for a 2 credit class.

This is a 1 credit class. I took the 2nd session class and there are 2 quizzes every 2 weeks along with 2-3 assignments. At the end of the semester (last 2 weeks) there were 3 papers all 2-3 pages. Way too much work for a 1 credit class. Not clear on rubric. Responds quickly to emails though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pohlschneider was organized and her expectations for students in this course were very clear. Not a very difficult class but a good amount of work for one credit hour. The posting of grades for class assignments often took a long time. Ultimately a good professor who communicated the course material very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Fun class, fun labs, TA's grade hard for no reason, but overall loved the class.
Three papers towards the end. A quiz every two weeks. Two projects that aren't too bad. A lot of work for a 1 credit class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is a good professor and my course was not showing up this was for FST4597.02 and it was not hard work. It was a lot of work but it was not hard. You have to do a lot of writing but it is mainly opinion based.. You do learn a good amount but this is an easy class for the grade.

One of the easiest A's I've ever gotten from a college course. No lectures at all. Just read for 10 mins and you will be good for quizzes. The only thing that required some work was writing the papers almost every week. Good thing is that they were easy to write and the topics we interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Caffeine science is a pretty easy class, several interesting papers to write, and great content. Seems like a bit of work for a one credit class, but well worth it if you're looking for an easy 'A'.
She has one of the easiest class yet she tries to grade like it's something important like calm down. It's just food.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's rude in emails, giving unclear feedback. She addresses herself with Dr. (yk what that means). She tells you one thing in emails while her grading says otherwise (I asked her if blank would work for an assignment, she says yes, but when grading, the criteria for the blank specifically was 4/10). She tries too hard honestly. Still easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the online version. Would say it is easy A.

Easy class, have 2 weeks to make 10 discussion posts, 3 short papers on recent events, 2 papers on movies, and a final paper on what you learned. Piece of cake just do the work and follow the requirements on how to write your papers

Dr. P is a great professor and one of the best the FDSCTE department has to offer. 2400 is not a difficult class. The material is straightforward, the project is easy if you split the work up with your group, and the labs are kind of fun. Sometimes the TA grading the pre labs was harsh, and some of the quizzes were all short answer. Put the work in

Mary did a great job teaching the class on chocolate's science and history. She made the class enjoyable by incorporating chocolate tastings and provided extra credit on the midterms and final. The science side of the class was a little more challenging than expected for a non-science major, but nothing overly complex.

The class itself is super easy but, in my opinion, it's a lot of work for a 1-credit class. You have 3, 2-3 page papers due throughout the course which more than I've have in some 3 credit classes. She makes you take your quizzes on a LockDown browser but you are allowed to use notes.

Great teacher, passionate about chocolate and it shows in class. You get to try different chocolates in class and she does a good job teaching the different topics around Chocolate. The midterm was surprisingly harder than I expected. Definitely put in a couple hours (2-3) for studying for the tests. Project was very easy. Fun class, fun teacher.

Dr. Pohlschneider was a great professor. She truly cares about her students and she tries to get to know you. She keeps her class interesting and her exams and pop quizzes are fair. There's a decent amount of work to do for labs but it's manageable if you stay on top of it. And you get to eat food in most of the labs! Would take her again.
Chocolate Science! Awesome class and easy A. Fun prof for a fun elective!

Chocolate science is a fun class, but I thought the prof was just okay. She does give a TON of bonus points, but the group project is absurd for a ONE-CREDIT class. Tastings are fun, though. Participate or she gets cranky. All lectures on powerpoints, but she does like throwing trick questions on exams.
