The BEST professor I've ever had. I look forward to lecture, she's willing to meet with you outside of class. She's one of the few chem profs who genuinely cares about your success. Makes a hard class fun and delivers content clearly

The best chem professor at OSU. Caring, accessible, very helpful. Genuinely wants to make chemistry accessible to all students. Does lots of practice in class. I cannot speak highly enough of her. A gem.

I liked her, but that was because her teaching style matched my learning style. You have notes before class that you discuss in class as well as guided practice. My only problem was that sometimes I felt the tests were graded too harshly, there wasn't enough time to complete them, and you didn't get to look back. Homework was fair, too.

Dr. Ricciardo has been my favorite professor by far. She sent out lecture videos before lecture as homework, and then go over practice problems in the actual lecture. This approach, although very different, has been by far the best for me. Very accesible, I reached out to her and heard back within a day. I genuinely loved learning in her class.

I had this professor for zoom lectures in chem and honestly she was so great! You'd watch short videos of the content before class, and then she would do a lot of step by step problems during class time. It felt like a flipped classroom, but it was super helpful for me. She was super sweet and I wish I could have her again for spring semester.

This semester we had a hybrid-style of learning in which lectures were done through zoom and some labs were done in person. To make lecture time more efficient, Ricciardo assigned us prelectures in which we learned the class content before class and then learned how to apply the concepts during lecture. It was asynchronous and very helpfu.

The Ohio States chem department is trash and we all know this, however Dr. Ricciardo is not. She makes good use of in class time and is always available outside of class for extra help. Chemistry is a hard subject for me so I cant really discuss the difficulty. But the exams are hard because you have to do one question at a time and cant go back.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doesnt prepare for exams at all. Teaches basic concepts that cannot be applied to exams because theres such a contrast in the difficulties.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was easy enough, but there was a lot of busy work. I didnt really use the textbook but you have to buy it because it comes with Sapling Learning that is used for homework ($80). Also, it was annoying that she dropped grades after everything was finished for the semester bc grades were inputted into Carmen wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: this class was so stupid. It was pretty easy but just so much busy work that was so irrelevant to what we were doing. also the professor barely does any actual teaching. cant stress enough how stupid all the assignments were. really annoying for an online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. R was a great professor who genuinely cared about all of her students and their success. She chooses main parts of units to go over in class, and expects you to have a general knowledge based on the reading and online homework. Her office hours were a great resource, although a lot of times they would be cut short due to meetings, so go early!

If you have the opportunity to take Dr. R, do it! She is very motivating and believes in all of her students! The class itself is very easy if you have a strong background in chemistry. I've never met such a caring woman, and she is very knowledgeable in chemistry. She has great teaching style as well.

She's a very nice professor who cares about her students, but her lectures don't make 1210 any easier. Be prepared to put in work throughout the semester and go to class, the lectures still do help. Hard class but if you try enough, you'll get through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She posts nice inspo quotes on each lecture that are very nice. She is always thoroughly explaining any questions that arise during class & is patient with students. However, she does not prepare you for the level of difficulty of the exams. She never recovers important or difficult concepts and is never available outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Ricciardo is a GEM of a woman. She is extremely passionate about chemistry but very good at bringing it down to a level that is understandable. She reminds me alot of a high school teacher and is very nice and understanding. Go to her office hours, unlike the rest of the OSU chem department she wants you to succeed.

Very good professor. However, she does not prepare her students for exam materials. There Will often be material on exams that she did not cover thoroughly in lecture. She is also not accessible outside of class. I scheduled several meetings with here and she did not show up. Read the book and work the problems in the back of the text to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rebecca was a good professor, however she did little teaching. There are many assignments, which is nice, but the weight of the assignments didn't seem fair. If you do poorly on one, it brings your grade down quite a bit, but doing well didn't seem to positively affect the grade at all. Overall, good professor but could be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Ricciardo is great! I took the online Chem and Society class and it was actually really interesting. Organized really well and you are able to do things on your own time. Each module usually has a few readings and questions to answer, a discussion post, and a 10 point quiz at the end. Very doable and the expectations were clear!

seriously the best professor at osu. I'm retaking chem 1220 and I'm so glad i switched my schedule around to take it with her. She is not only a great professor, but she genuinely cares about her students and wants to know whats going on in their lives. She'll even set up online office hours. Honestly the only professor worth taking 8 ams with

Dr. Ricciardo is an amazing professor. I really struggle with chem so I was super nervous coming into 1220 but her lectures are great and she gives actually useful studying tips and advice. She is even willing to spend time with you and develop a personal study plan. It is chem so you have to put the work in, but you're not alone.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ricciardo is the BEST! As a student with a major pet peeve for unorganized professors, I was highly pleased with the way she laid everything out for us from the beginning. She makes it clear how to get an A and wants her students to succeed, but you will have to put in the work. But beware, her averages were high and there was no curve at the end
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Ricciardo's lectures are clear and easy to understand. If you do not understand something, definitely go up to her after class and ask questions. She is very approachable and genuinely cares about her students. Do not skip lecture! She does sample problems that are very similar to the ones on the exams. One of the best chem profs at OSU.

Best lecturer I could have ever hoped for! She engages the huge lecture in in-class activities/calculations and really cares about her students. She lays things out simply, let's students know where to relearn things they've forgotten, and never goes too fast. No denying this is a very hard class, but she is truly a teacher, not just a chemist!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Ricciardo is just amazing! She is great as a person, and great as a lecturer. I took chem 1220 before and got a C. I retook it with Dr. Ricciardo, I got an A. She is very very helpful and make chemistry so much easier to understand. Her tests are fair. Do the homework and the recitation activities and you will get A-B range on the exam.

Not my favorite class for many reasons, none of which relate to Dr. Ricciardo's teaching.  She was very nice, clear, and helpful.  I appreciated that she would walk around and talk with students before class and kept lectures very interactive.

Very nice professor! I do not like chem but Dr. Ricciardo made it much more bearable! We had time to work through problems on our own during lecture which I liked & recitation  is easy attendance so go to them! The  only complaint I have is that her exams are a bit harder than her practice exams. Ask for help when you need it and you will be fine.
Nicest chem professor I have had. Her office hours are extremely helpful. Warning don't rely on a curve in her class.

Any chem class is going to be hell ,  but Ricciardo is definitely the way to go! Required course for my major and it's not my favorite to say the least, but I sat in the front row and she made lectures bearable and clear. Though her math-teaching was very watered down, she made sure you knew all the conceptual stuff. Willing to help you if you ask

Dr. R is amazing. She is very clear in lecture. I had to read the book for 1210 but with her it was straight forward as long as I went to lecture. Her demos and videos are entertaining as well. Her practice exams do not really reflect her exams. They are a little bit more easy than the actual tests. Do the homework and study everything.

She is a very good conceptual teacher that helps you better your knowledge of the subject. However, she does not go through math questions thoroughly in lecture. Also she goes super quick in lecture and is hard to understand at times. Overall, she was better than my 1210 prof and I would take her class again.

Dr. Ricciardo is the perfect teacher for an introductory CHEM class because she makes it enjoyable! While almost all of the topics in 1220 were covered in AP Chem (I watched Breaking Bad during class) she had lots of experiments, quotes, surveys, and examples that made the lectures engaging even for those who have seen the stuff before.

Dr Ricciardo was awesome.  She really cares about the students and making sure they understand everything clearly.  She is very much a people-person, unlike some of the other chem professors.  She also gives out candy for participating in class.

I was very disappointed when I took this class. It was basically just notes that she read that she seemed to not understand herself. Relied to heavily on Mastering Chemistry to teach sections of the class. Exams weren't like the homework. She puts up powerpoints to try at home but doesn't give answer so you never know if you're doing it correctly.

She is by far the worst chem prof I've had at OSU. She doesn't teach merely reads notes to you. She rarely gives the examples to math problems that would actually be beneficial and help the students on the exams. She relies on mastering chemistry too much. All in all, if I were you I'd spare myself and switch teachers.

Very good at simplifying often complex material by rephrasing concepts in the book to make them seem much less daunting. She is always willing to help if you ask--she seems to genuinely care and wants her students to do well. Best professor I have had so far in my 3 years at Ohio State! Definitely recommend her :)
Dr. Ricciardo is a great teacher. Really cool, laid back...exams were fair - if you studied hard. She's enthusiastic about learning too
Very helpful and nice, willing to help students during her office hours. Quizzes and tests follow her notes, so attendance is pretty mandatory.

She was a pretty good teacher, I liked her. She handed out candy and other goodies to students that bothered to come to lecture. While I vastly prefer Dr. Stoltzfus as a Chem 123 instructor, I did not pass his class... I'd say Ricciardo's version of the course is a bit easier. Well, easy as genchem at OSU can be...
Really disappointed in this professor solely based on comments from this site. I knew the class would be challenging but I felt the exams were more ridiculous than those I saw in 122.

Ricciardo is very nice and very helpful. Her notes make sense and she does practice problems for every variety of problem, including labs. Her exams and quizzes are based closely off her notes. The book is not needed to fully grasp the material. It wasn't easy, but it was much better than 122.
She's a really nice professor, really young. No use of the book - all practice problems are made by her. Lecture notes are incredibly important for quizzes and exams. Not too hard, but not too easy.
Very friendly, but her teaching skills are very sub par.

Dr. Ricciardo was the best prof. I've ever had in the sciences at Ohio State. She is ALWAYS willing to help, and as long as you actually do problem sets and study for each quiz/midterm, you'll be fine. She goes by the book pretty carefully, but makes it fun and interesting, too. Not an "easy" prof, but she's a good one. Very personal/enthusiastic.
Made a boring class fun and exciting.  Very good Prof.

Worst professor ever. She reads her notes to the class instead of actually teaching and explaining the material to us, she relied way too much on Dr. Fus's old stuff (she is new, and she used to be his t.a); half of our second midterm were questions from his (how is that fair, we are not in his class)!  Take someone else, you'll thank me later.
Good teacher with great materials and stories, but grading is interesting. You can certainly learn things here. And you can certainly lower your overall GPA here at the same time as well.

First of all, this is ECON 2367, not 2001. There is no option for me to choose 2367. Grading is too tough. You never know what grade you will get, unless you go to the office hour every time and discuss literally EVERY single thing with her to make her satisfied. Get prepared to be shocked by your grade.

She is a fine lecturer. Not super engaging, but well enough to learn the topic. Attendance is not mandatory, but show up to class for the extra credit. Exams are really challenging and require a strong understanding of the concepts to do well on
Professor Zhang is not the best lecturer, but she offers so much extra credit opportunities. Her exams are super difficult, but if you do the homework and extra credit you will be fine.

THIS WAS NOT FOR THE CLASS CODE PROVIDED it was for Econ 2367.02. Do not take this class with her. She was an intense grader and change the course weight 2/3 of the way though the semester which ruined my plans. In her words "made the class similar to that of MIT econ curriculum".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were manageable when I prepared through practice tests. Homework helped a lot when I was confused during lectures. SHOW UP TO CLASS, you'll get extra credit which helps a lot at the end of the course. Overall very manageable class and Professor Zhang was great
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My expectations for ENGR1300 were completely wrong. Professor Tichgelaar is engaging and funny during lectures, and allows you to choose your own topic as a student with complete liberty. I found that choosing my own topic made me much more engaged in all the assignments, and I had lots of fun and also learned good writing techniques. Great guy.

I took this class to get a gen ed done, but I feel like my writing/communication abilities def improved as a result. All of the assignments were interesting, and none of it felt like busy work. Early in the course, you pick a thesis to focus on for the rest of the sem, making working enjoyable. Put in effort, follow the rubric, and you'll get an A.

It is fairly easy to score an A, as long as you put in effort. Drafts and discussion posts are an automatic 100% if you tried. My biggest tip is to write a good draft, so you can receive an effective feedback. Overall, you will be fine if you follow the rubric and formatting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lenient Grader, easy-ish class, although there was considerably more work at the end of the semester than the beginning. Gives good lectures/easy to follow.

Overall a fairly easy class to get an A in if you put in the adequate time and read the rubrics. But I did feel that his grading was at times random and not very fair. He would sometimes respond to emails late but was fairly accessible outside of class. This class took me more time than expected but still, not difficult to get an A.

I took ENGR 1300, would often come to class unprepared and would sometimes end class after 10 minutes for work time. I felt I could do the entire class online asynchronous and still get an A. Other than never responding to emails, the content is outlined well and his rubrics are self explanatory.

He would have students turn in drafts and give very good feedback that made it easy to score well on the final copies. He would also change due dates if he had fallen behind in any capacity. It was a very low stress class with good, practical writing experience, and he was a very kind professor.

relatively easy english GE. he has drafts due for every assignment (automatic 10pts) to give feedback for when u submit the real thing. his grading is semi-hard but if u ask him questions he will tell u what to fix. the last part of the course is mainly a big group project so make sure u have a good group, its presentation, visual art, a long paper

Great professor. Funny, flamboyant, colorful, super caring. You'll never feel intimidated by him. Gives pretty simple feedback to your assignments, just do what he asks and it's both an easy A and an easy course credit. Group projects so be ready for that, but he's always eager to help. Would absolutely recommend.
A lot of works. Instructions are super unclear, so you may get lost on assignments. Lectures are super boring but short. Not an easy A for a writing GE 2367 class.

You can tell in lecture that kimo really cares about students. Hes a chill guy and offers a ton of opportunities to ask for help. Rubrics are vague, yes, but there are drafts for everything that give you 10 automatic points and he also gives exact feedback for the final draft. Not strict with deadlines and grades easy. Easy ge with minimal work!

Dr. Tichgelaar is a really caring guy. His rubrics are somewhat vague, but he gives great feedback on rough drafts so you know exactly what to do and its no issue. If you have a question, I would recommend office hours over emailing him to get a faster response. Overall awesome guy and awesome class. Great preparation for later in life. Take this!

Not complaining because the class is too difficult, its really easy if your keep up with the work, but the problem is that Tich gives very vague directions on how to complete assignments and then marks people off for missing out on stuff he never explained. He grades kinda tough as well and likes to knit pick on things.

He is a really good professor but my only catch is that the class is a lot of work for a GE, really only with the group project. It's much longer than it really needed to be and the asynchronous class content is extremely long and not very engaging. Would't take again but he isn't bad. Its mostly just how the class was structured and the project.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class itself isn't any more fun than your other classes. Slightly more work than what you would expect in a GE course, but is still pretty easy. The group project can suck big time if your group doesn't help that much. Kimo is a pretty cool guy and is always willing to help when you need it. I would take this over the summer though. Save the stress

Interesting teacher but seemed very disorganized. Due dates are changed without notice and assignments are created sometimes without making it clear. Nonetheless, the stuff he teaches is pretty good for the most part, like the resumes, cover letters, and follow-up letters! There isn't too much work and it can usually get done without much effort!

- He is a very odd person. - Does not respond to emails until a week later. - He has assignments hidden from the Modules and Grades pages so you'd have to look at the To-Do list that's only on the Home Page, the little thing on the right when you click and he doesn't tell you about that anywhere in the course/class/syllabus.
Not understanding, very weird. Does not give clear instructions for assignments and response time for emails are very slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's great. He dresses like he thinks he's doctor who, but he is a very funny and interesting person. Everything he taught was useful to the course or to our careers in general. You will like him. He grades pretty easily, but don't take that for granted- what you are learning has a good chance of being important to you at some point.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a great prof! He really prepared me for writing resumes and cover letters. His class is easy and you will learn a lot!

Professor Tichgelaar taught very well and this course is very useful (CV, Resume, Memo). The only thing I want to mention is that there are so many papers. We need to finish about 27 assignments in the whole semester. If you already have a heavy schedule, don't take him. If not, please take him. Soft grader & Helpful teacher!
lecture is long and boring. not clear
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Kimo is the man. If you do all of the work the class is an easy A. You turn in a draft for each assignment and he gives you feedback. If you do what he says, you'll get an A. There are two major group projects, make sure you get with good people or you'll be doing a lot on your own. If you're ever confused, his office hours really help.

Odd dude, but friendly and helpful. Lots of busy work in the class, but nothing really hard. Few group projects to be wary of - try your best to get a good group.  Attendance is taken and skipping classes hurts your grade, so make sure to show up.
It's engr 2367, it is easy with any professor. Kim is the man. He has a very flamboyant personality  and a great sense of style. He alway seems enthusiastic to come to class. Would recomend

He made probably the most useful and applicable writing class for engineering majors.  Much better than having to take a random writing class with long term papers or something completely irrelevant to engineering.

Strange neo-victorian style steampunk dude. Nice though. The class was stupid and boring. The assignments were stupid and boring and busy work. Not a tough class at all, but just took time that I didn't quite have to do the assignments.
Quizzes are vague and assignment due dates are switched around a lot. Assignments overlap quite a bit too which makes completing them difficult at times. Assignments were fairly easy but long.
Lacks clarity in what he wants you to write about. Quizzes ask very subjective questions. Very boring. Do not recommend.

He grades papers strictly and he doesn't really teach what we are supposed to write. Even though he gives extensions to due dates, he teaches us little and wants us to write everything...do not recommend him.
Highly recommend his second-level writing course. Overall, a great and informative class. The professor was very helpful with the assignments and material, also making the lectures engaging.

Ty's class was frustrating for me. I felt like the expectations around group work were unfair, especially because I ended up doing most of my group's work. In the end, my grade was affected by another group member's presentation performance, which did not feel like an accurate reflection of my own effort or understanding.

I took the honors version of this class so Ty himself was my TA. He grades more easily than his TAs and the groups you get for the group projects are usually better in honors. Not much busy work outside of the group projects and there are two exams. The class helps with public speaking and I found it to be useful. Be prepared for the Crisis Case.

Very likely you won't ever see Ty in this class as his lectures are online, and recitation is taught by TAs. There are 4 extra credit points you can get and that's really the only way you'll be able to get an A, as it seems like his goal is to have the top part of the class end at an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I don't know why people are slandering my boy, because I genuinely liked this class. Rubrics can be unclear and grades feel a bit luck-based with group strength, but in honors your group typically pulls through. TY makes recitations fun. Learned more than expected and now love Shell Oil. Would take again.
MUCOAT - most unnecessary class of ALL time. can't believe I had to pay $70 for his self-written tophat "textbook"
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TA's teaching the recitation classes are pretty cool. There are several group projects, but as long as you have a good group, it is enjoyable and valuable. The class really helps with public speaking because of presentations, and you really learn how to work as a team. Be prepared for the Crisis Case.

Note that unless you are in honors your class will be run entirely by a TA. If this is the case, your grade will come down entirely to who your TA is and who is in your group. Ty does not have a say in his TA's so this is not really his fault, it's a problem with Fisher. Matheus was the worst TA/professor I've ever had. Avoid him at all costs.
War criminal
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely this class is not hard, but it is hard to get an A, because he'll always take points off for BS. I guarantee you can get a B very easily, the class is not hard. Ty is a terrible person as a human being, and he will lie, and give his favorite students A's, but still, not a hard class. The class is pointless, but it's easy
Literally no reason for this class to exist.

I can't talk about how much I hated this class. It was an absolute joke and I don't even know why OSU offers it. I learned nothing useful, had to buy a $50 textbook that served no purpose, had a TA that I can only describe as “lost”, got graded unfairly on projects, and took exams that ask your to remember the smallest details from videos

My TA was chill but graded like an absolute idiot. Unnecessarily hard grading for stuff that was super easy. The exams are even worse bro. The material is the easiest stuff ever but exam questions will be like, "what color was my shoe in the last lecture?" like bro what?
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ty is great, but your grade will come down to your group and TA. Matheus was the worst TA i have ever had at osu. Stay away

You never see Ty, only while watching lecture videos. My TA was Kylee Ginter, I had her class online at 8 am on Mondays. You have Top Hats to do before class every week. The material was easy to learn but the TA failed to provide more information about projects (there's 3 big ones that affect your grade heavily). Don't miss class.

You never even see Ty and your TA basically dictates your whole grade. I was lucky to get someone who was fair but you may not be. This entire class is just pointless and basically has taught me nothing relevant at all. Ty's exams are really stupid too bc he'll ask you the most pointless questions like "What was I wearing in this video"

You never see Ty in person, just the TA's. I had a chill TA so the class wasn't hard, but that's DEFINITELY not the case for everyone. Crisis case can be annoying and stressful, but I thought it was kinda fun. Also, the exams aren't too hard but can be annoying because they ask specific unimportant things from the video lectures.

Never saw Ty, just the TA. Just pray you get a chill TA and a great group. Luckily I got both of those so this class wasn't bad. Little to no homework every week. Crisis case week is annoying but it's not that bad.
A lecture with no content; Try to include most unnecessary details in exams to make students' lives harder; Successful man's success science, very results-oriented value
Shepfer's class is a hit-or-miss - you either get a great TA or a not-so-great one. The material and grading can be quite challenging, but Unstuck ai has helpful study tools to prepare.

Although the content of this class isn't too difficult, the group presentations are strictly graded. Ty makes this class pretty fun and enjoyable. The honors version is better as the students are more motivated and easier to work with. The course content was not super interesting; most of it was common sense and the two exams are pretty specific.

I recommend taking this Honors so you have Ty. He grades harder than if you were to take it non honors, but he does make the class fun and is a good guy. The exams are silly though as he asks you very specific and meaningless questions from the textbooks and videos. Has this weird crush on shell oil. I wish someone loved me like ty loves shell oil
Great teacher interesting class style I took honors because the students cared more so group projects were much easier.

I took him for BUSMHR 2292 but I never saw him. It was run by TA, the class itself is super easy to do. A lot of working with groups but pretty enjoyable. However the exams are super specific and are pretty difficult to study for and to do well on.

This class is mainly presentations and group work. Easy to get a B, hard to get an A. Exams focus on very specific points of material over the course of the term and make it almost impossible to study. The class is ran by the TAs. Never saw Ty.

This class is overall easy, and you never even see Ty. He makes his TA's grade very strictly and he also does not believe in perfect grades. This class is a very easy B, but hard A. The group projects are worth most of your grade as well as the mid-term and final. As long as you read the textbook he wrote and watch the videos you will do fine

Group project heavy definitely need a good group. Exams focus on details about the examples and specific phrases in the text. Look out for anything he says a lot or says from the readings. Never met the guy but my TAs were cool.

The class itself was interesting to me, but the exams are ridiculous and will focus on the smallest of details. The TA's do everything and attendance is mandatory for the recitations. The lectures are all online and you have to buy a textbook that Ty wrote.
Absolute joke of class. Exams don't cover course material rather very specific examples that you don't actually need to know outside of the course.

The only time I saw Ty so far at OSU was him getting coffee at Rohr, otherwise you'll never see him in person. The TA will be the only one that is running the class and the group you are assigned to will be really important for the biggest assignments. HIs exams like everyone said asks way too small details.

You probably won't meet Ty in 2292. The course material itself is not hard. The main assignments are the group presentations and 2 exams. For the groups pray you get put in good group because if you don't you're screwed (you are graded as a group not an individual). Tests require you to memorize tiny details which aren't useful outside this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never really understood classes where the biggest chunk of the grade is determined by the competency of an 8-person group rather than yourself. Dude makes it unnecessarily difficult to know which assignments are due when, tests have the most obscure questions on them, and the whole layout of the class is just pointless.

Dude makes you pay $60 for his shoddily written "textbook" used to answer 3 questions on Tophat. Lectures and book are full of mistakes and typos and overall represent his lack of effort in this course. Most sections never even meet the guy. Probably the most overpaid staff member at OSU

Ty is very organized and explains exactly what he wants out of you to do well in his courses. He cares a lot about the personal development of his students and is genuinely interested in the material. He can be a bit of a tough grader, but more by just having higher expectations than most professors. If you put in the work you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This quite possibly is the most useless course created by mankind. You have to buy a TOPHAT textbook just to answer 3 multiple choice questions a week for homework. To ace the exams all you have to do is memorize every single niche bit of information in the textbook, lecture slides, videos, and record every second of your TA's breath. Get real Ty.

Lectures consist of old videos he did during covid. Exams are tricky and target very very specific questions like a question from a paragraph you read in week 2. The only thing you can gain from this class is the desire to drive without wearing your seatbelt just to see if you can die before you make it to his class. Most useless class at Fisher

Every concept you learn is pretty much common sense, but on the exams, he tries to trick you. I get he wants to make the exams difficult, but doing so by asking the most niche and specific questions is just cruel. The score I got did not reflect my knowledge in the class. ex: "what CEOs did we talk about in week 2?" Like okay.

This class is horrible. The whole class is just given to your TA so if you don't have a good one you are in for a long semester. The lecture videos that Ty uses are all multiple years old and the exams are based on the lecture videos despite the fact we never talk about the videos in class.

Good luck if you even get to meet the guy. He pawns off his classes to be taught by graduate students and reuses lecture videos from Covid. Honestly feels like dude somehow conned OSU into letting him teach for an easy bag. Worst class in fisher you will take. Beyond the professor the material is actually useless brainrot information.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Never even saw Ty. entire class was ran by TA and grades were really designed to have a C average in the class.

I made the mistake of taking the non-honors version of this course, leaving me stuck with an uninterested (and often uninformed) grad TA, and leechy group members for two of the largest assignments in the course. Besides requiring his own $60 textbook though, I don't have many qualms with Ty himself. +1 point for the Buckeye Donuts office hours.

You don't meet Ty unless you're in honors, so all his lectures are pre-recorded. The exams are harder than they seem, so make sure to watch all the lectures and read the TopHat. Oh yeah, the TopHat is $60 and mandatory for the class (did I mention he wrote it?). Overall not a great guy, no wonder he fit in so well at Shell Oil!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Class literally relies on your TA for your grade and the group you are placed in for the two big 60 point group projects at end of semester. The 2 assessments are meh, i thought this class would be a free A but i got stuck with a a**hole of an TA. Don't be like me and research ur TA before you take this class.

Never interacted with Professor Shepfer personally, the entire class was run by a grad TA. Pretty much a coin toss if you get a good one or not. My TA was uninterested in teaching the class and sometimes didn't know what we were meant to be doing. Presentation grading is quite hard, even the best presentations in the class can end up with an A-.

I took 2292 thinking it was going to be a pretty easy class, but this is not the case. The homework assignments are all completion. The group projects are not awful if your group can work well together, but the learning assesments are way too specific and its very hard to receive an A in this class. Ty Shepfer will not stop talking about Shell Oil.

I enjoyed having Ty as a professor. He expected more out of us so graded us a little harder, but honestly, I liked it. It can be time-consuming depending on how much work you want to put into the projects but it was pretty simple stuff. I would highly recommend taking this class in the honors format.

I could tell how much Ty cared about this class when I never saw him in person the entire semester. The textbook is written by him and littered with grammar and spelling errors. Your TA will decide your grade based on group projects. The exams require you to recall irrelevant facts that have nothing to do with the content.

My TA wasn't even a business major (figure out a good TA to take it with), knew nothing about the course, and clearly had no interest in the material. You also have to pay like $60 to get a book written by him that could've easily been a PDF. The exam questions were nonsensical. Don't have a single positive thing to say about him or this class.

Boring material from a book he wrote that he makes you buy (you submit weekly homework through it and use it for class attendance so you can't get away with not buying it). My TA was fine and my group was great so the class ended up not being that difficult, but the learning assessments (basically the exams) are awful.

This class and your experience of it relies solely on the TA you get, not Ty Shepfer. The TA for my class was very bad, only grading things towards the end of the semester, clearly not caring about actually teaching it, and always had a "bored" demeanor for literally every class. This class could be great due to its content, but mine was not.

Ty made us buy a $60 book that was written by himself, and he never shows up to class. He already makes $211,000/ yr. The lectures he provides were recorded in 2018 and just reuses them year after year. The class is run by two TA's who are grad students, so you better hope you get good ones. Grading and criteria is extremely unclear and unfair.

Ty is a very self-centered person who never once showed up to our class. He relies on the TAs to teach everything, so hope you get a good one. The guidelines/due dates for assignments or projects are very unclear, and they didn't even give us a rubric for the final crisis project until after they graded it. Choose another professor if you can.

I was required to buy a textbook THAT HE WROTE for $60. He then proceeded to never attend a lecture(I've never seen him)and throw us in a room with a TA. The book is also horrible and stuff you could find on google and None of the assignments are on carmen so you're constantly scared that you've forgotten something. Worst class I have ever taken.

- makes you buy his book for $60.00 which is on Tophat which is information that literally can be looked up on Quizlet or the internet 
- never even seen his man yet he is our professor 
- None of the assignments are on Carmen to remind you
- TA makes or breaks the class honestly
- the grading is so hard for this class, which is so pointless

TA is so boring that most of the class doesn't pay attention, ironically within a class on large part about how to make an engaging presentation. Professor is nowhere to be seen, with old required online lectures. Grading scales/rubrics are vague and completely based on the TA's opinion. If your TA is incredibly boring like mine, drop the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ty clearly doesn't care about his class. Avoid him at all costs
He is absolutely nowhere to be found when you need him. Your only hope is your TA. He also doesn't post ANY due dates in Carmen. Overall just careless about his class.

Ty cares a lot about himself and is pretty self-absorbed. TA makes or breaks the class, I had a pretentious MBA student who put little to no effort into their sessions. Lectures have nothing to do with group projects, exam questions come straight from the lecture videos.

This class felt like a waste of time. The group projects were graded far too harshly given that at least three of your eight group members don't contribute at all. Graded negatively for the poor performances of others which is just unfair. Was still able to finish with an A through the extra credit and studying for the two exams.

Engaging professor & content. He genuinely tries to pick and present information that is relevant to our future careers. However, the bulk of the grades rely on the competency of your group. Also, the 2 quizzes require you to take overly detailed notes (open-note quiz).

I never met Ty, and all though he seems like a great and genuine person, the class just wasn't as good as it could've been. All the lecture videos and readings were online and the content was barely discussed in class. This class is strongly based on your recitation leader and group. A lot needs fixed to make this class actually useful.

Lectures are posted online, lectures are fine but need to put them on 2x speed because he is monotone. Class is mostly all group projects and presentations. Two tests that are open book but timed so you will not have time to look anything up. Grading is extremely tough and one group project there is no rubric and assignments are not posted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He hasn't updated his content in 3 years and seems to have no interest in actually doing his job. The class was laid out poorly and it felt like he copied a lesson plan but didn't know how to actually implement it. The TA will decide all of your grade besides the exams. Ty is useless and if you want to get anything out of the class id avoid him.

Loved the class but hated the structure. Why try to be different and only put assignments on the syllabus? Its an intro level class there is no need. I also thought it was hard to get a good grade, at least in my recitation section. Lots of groupwork but thankfully I got lucky and had a good group.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grades harshly and is VERY unclear about grading guidelines. More than half of the grades in this course are out of your control. You get stuck with a team for the whole semester and if you get a bad team then you'll likely not do well. Overall, this class is very disorganized and just hard for no reason.

This class definitely has its benefits and is very beneficial in helping students find future jobs. Outside of that everything else in this class sucks. No homework is posted online, Ta's grades are really hard and tell students on the first day of class that it's impossible to get an A in this course. Lecture videos are not beneficial at all.

This was a terrible class. First of all, this class is like 70% group projects, and you're stuck with the same group throughout the entire semester. Lectures are all pre-recorded and are from who knows how long ago. Trevor Gillespie was my TA. Worst TA ever. Do not recommend. He was the head TA this semester. If you end up getting the head TA, run

Ty as a person is wonderful. He genuinely does care about students and is willing to meet with them regarding their concerns. However, the class is way harder than it needs to be. Depending on your TA you may get a low score on projects. Our got the highest score on the ethics presentation and still missed 5 points. Hard to get an A.

Ty has a very very big ego. He isn't clear about grading standards (grades are often based merely on his opinion not a set rubric). He isn't willing to work with students, and doesn't give the rubric for a project worth ~40% of your grade until after the project is completed. Take the non-honors version of the class to avoid having Ty as your prof.

Missed an A- by 0.25%, professor doesn't round up at all. Gave 3 points of extra credit. Received the highest crisis case score in my class which was still a 54/60. Tests are 40 LONG questions in 40 minutes. You can use notes on exams, but the questions are EXTREMELY long in comparison to time - it takes a whole minute just to read the questions.

Ty's lectures were videos posted on Carmen, so I never got to meet him in person, but I found the class to be one of the most practical ones I'll take in Fisher. I think the class is organized pretty well, but definitely put a TON of effort on the 2 group projects and study a bit for the learning assessments if you want an A.

This dude thinks he's so sweet. I didn't learn a single thing in this class, he just likes to hear the sound of his own voice. On the crisis case as a the recitation leader he gave everyone a C average, just cuz he picked that arbitrary number. He didn't outline clear grading criteria at all for the biggest assignment of the year. He is the worst.

Ty is a great professor who genuinely wants to get to know his students. I learned more from his class than I have from any of the other classes I have taken combined. Be prepared for group work, and do your best to get everything you can from your experiences in his class.
Ahhh... good ol' Ty Shepfer. I had him during Spring of 2021. I won't say he's anything exceptional (if I could I'd rate him a 3.5), but it's a solid choice for the profs that teach this class.

He has little interaction w students and videos are obviously old. The reading is pointless but he makes you pay for it. Weekly inquisitive discussion boards, 2 tests, and 2-3 partner/group projects that are most of the points. If your group sucks oh well, all students in group get same grade. Extra credit & class is easy but its not easy A

Ty Shepfer seems like an interesting person, but you never see him. He just recycles recorded lectures once a week and this class entirely depends on your TA and your team. If both are good, easy A, if not then good luck. There were only two exams, both weren't too bad but definitely prepare for them.

Ty is a nice guy, but does very little to no actual teaching in this course. The course includes lecture videos from years ago, and Ty uploads a 30 second video of himself presenting what is due in the coming weeks. Wish I got paid to teach this course. Multiple group projects, TA's run the course. Learning assessment are harder then necessary.

This class is my favorite class I've taken through 2 years and the class I've learned the most in. I really enjoyed Ty's pre recorded lectures and my in person recitations. You learn extremely useful skills that you will use in everyday life. I also got to know the students in my group who will be in the same classes as me throughout school.

Really don't like how he set up this class. It's not really him teaching it's mainly watching pre-recorded videos and then having a mandatory recitation where the TA's give out group projects. If your group is bad you're basically screwed. He seemed nice but you have no interaction with him whatsoever.

There are too many group projects, especially in an online course. He doesn't actually do anything for the course except release weekly announcements that are just copied from previous weeks. He makes the TA's do all of the work and grading, and recitation attendance and participation are a big part of your grade. He makes you buy the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Mandatory recitations (with cameras on and graded participation for online version) is the most annoying part of this class. Lots of busy work but there are some useful things such as assignments that require you to complete a resume and LinkedIn profile. Ty is a decent lecturer with a ton of cool experiences to hear about.

This class is hit or miss depending on your TA and your group. If both are good then it's an easy A. Ty basically just does the lectures, I don't really see him as the professor cause I don't interact with him at all, the TAs are the main characters. Tests are pretty easy, hardest things are the group projects if your group doesn't help out much.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This was one of the worst courses EVER! Trying to do the group projects in an online environment is difficult at best. The TA's are morons, as they have no industry experience, yet are grading you on real world situations. They are MBA students, and most of them are full of themselves. 90% of this course is rehashing material from other courses

I wish all Fisher profs were like this. He lays a great foundation for all business students. Taking it in summer didn't feel rushed at all (with 2 other courses). He is genuinely interested in helping you, even for things that might seem below him. Everything was clear-cut with open-note exams, but you still learn so much.
AWFUL Experience! He DID NOT response to ANY question about the course agenda clearly!!! If you forget one, you will not receive an A anymore
Great professor! Watching the lectures and doing the readings makes the tests super easy! Make sure to attend class and participate! There are several group projects, but overall a super easy class!

For the "global awareness survey" MAKE SURE you don't click through it quickly, I got a zero on this because I was below the minimum time threshold (15 min I think)- otherwise he's a cool professor, recitation is annoying with the group projects. However, every other Fisher student is in the same boat with you. Readings are important for quizzes.

Lots of group projects which can be annoying, especially if you do not have a good group. Learning assessments are very specific about the content from lectures and the reading material. Make sure to participate in the recitation.

Ty is very passionate about what he teaches and genuinely cares about his students. I enjoyed both recitation and lecture and feel like I learned a lot from him that prepared me for the business world. Participation is important, and getting a good group matters because most assignments are group projects. You definitely have to put in the work.

This is my all time favorite class I have taken so far! All of the lectures are so interesting, and Ty is so knowledgeable and wants to help all his students in any way he can. My TA was awesome too, but there are a lot of group projects in recitation throughout the semester. I loved this class!

2292 was not the most exciting class, but I really liked Ty. He was a really cool guy and I could tell he was genuinely passionate about what he was talking about, and he cared about his students. He also rocked the blue plaid suit almost every class. I took this class at 8 a.m. but Ty made a class that early bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ty is a great guy and I enjoyed his class. You can tell he's passionate about business and wants to develop his students. I'd recommend taking his hybrid class so you can watch his lectures whenever you want. Lectures are bearable so don't worry. Recitations are long and require group work, but the assignments are not terrible. An A is possible :)

It's not a tough class, but it's a lot of work! You'll be working with a group off and on through the semester on top of doing other busy work in his class. Expect some mock business situations thrown at you. The work isn't hard, just time consuming on top of other classes you may be taking. Plus, you'll do 4 "learning assessments" (exams).
class is utterly pointless, and ty does his best to make it fun. can't say he succeeds, but he tries
Horrible class that is not taught very well. Lot of the material is just a rehash of microeconomics and macroeconomics. Waste of time.
This guy isn't bad but his learning assessments are unnecessarily hard. His lecture doesn't really help. If you want to get a good grade you need to be lucky to have good teammates.

I don't understand why people hate on Ty. I have found his lectures to be interesting and him to be very approachable outside of class. The key to this class is taking recitation at favorable times and having a good group for the projects. If you pay attention in his lectures and skim the readings, you'll get a B at least. Loved this class.

This guy really does not care if his students are not performing well in class, his only agenda is to give a very vague discussion of business jargon which ends up on exams/quizzes. The first quiz had 8 detailed mc q's over material he just spoke about (not on slides) for 2 minutes out of the whole hour. Anyways, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The readings for the class are easy, and there are not many. Read all, and read carefully. The material in them is not directly discussed in lecture or recitation, but the test questions are very specifically based on them. Pay attention in lecture, there are questions about those on the tests too. Graded by VERY few things. Turn everything in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 2292 is a hard class because the material is very unrelated week to week so studying for the tests are hard. Ty is a good lecturer and he is very helpful during his office hours. The weekly readings are important for tests so make sure to review them. Recitations are unrelated to lecture but they aren't difficult to get through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you watch/attend lectures!! And you HAVE to read the readings like ten times because hell ask super specific details on tests and quizzes. Overall an awesome lecturer and interesting and subject material is totally useful, but the tests and quizzes are definitely harder than they should be! And btw- most people dont get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ty is by far one of the best professors at Fisher; his passion for business is evident. If you're in his honors class (like I was this semester), participation is crucial to getting a good grade. In addition, don't skip lecture. Even though it's not mandatory, he goes over specific info. Tests are hit or miss; he likes to throw too specific Qs in
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was a lot harder than what it should have been. Lectures were somewhat useful in understanding the business world. Ty is super friendly and makes it interesting. If you want an A you really have to put in the work. Don't go in like me and think that this class will be an easy A :/

Ty is a cool guy and I enjoyed his lectures, he keeps them interesting and engages the class. Its really about who your recitation leader is tho since they grade your projects. Hope for a good recitation group or youll hate it cuz youre stuck with them. Recitation is also unnecessarily long and sometimes pointless. Just participate a little.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, wish I took him in person instead of online. Overall, a lot of the material is common sense, yet many of the test and quiz questions are very subjective and specific from certain readings/lectures. Pay attention during lectures and earn the easy points during recitation and you'll be fine.
Interesting class that had real life applications. Great lecturer that was interesting to listen to and made me want to attend class. Clear instructions for grading made this class pretty easy.

Taking the recitation with Ty is a completely different experience. Taking 2292H is the only way to know what is exactly on your midterm, otherwise you just read lecture slides in hopes of an A. Ty cares a lot for the honors class and will be much more forgiving than the TA's who seem to grade much more arbitrarily.

Ty is a good lecturer. Don't forget any small HW if you want A. Presentation is hard, especially the final group presentation, be sure to prepare as early as possible. Try to fix the problem based on your rec leader's opinions, because grading is very subjective. For 3 tests, mainly focus on the lecture slide.

This class really depends on who your recitation instructor is and how harsh of a grader they are. Unless you are in the honors class with Ty, then he does not do much for you. The exams question you on every little thing, so study the PowerPoints and take good notes in lecture. Recitation is pretty pointless, but you need it for the points.

What is universally an easy class through most business schools, and known to be an easy class at OSU, has become tougher. Ty mentioned this on the first day of class that this course has now become tougher. I'm not totally sure why this was done because it really will be the most unimportant class you take. Content is simple, but exams are ticky
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good professor. The concepts and terms in this class are very easy to understand, but they make the quizzes and exams very tricky which is frustrating. I think they do this on purpose to try and call the class "rigorous" and not an "easy A". The lectures and recitation feel completely different.

The lecture and recitation felt like separate classes. The lectures were full of general content that was made confusing for the quizzes and tests. The recitation projects were great for practicing public speaking, but other than that the class felt disconnected.

Ty takes this class too seriously. In all seriousness, I felt this class only had a couple days that were quite useful like when giving presentations or writing CSR paper. Other than that all test and quizzes are made unnecessarily difficult and wordy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I didn't like how this class is set up. The wording on his quizzes and exam were supper confusing. This should be an easy class but he made it harder than it should. He said final exam questions would be primary focus on the metarials after the midterm but actually 40% came from metarials before the midterm.

The tests and quizzes are vague even if yo read everything and did all the work you ended up guessing. The class easy but designed to be hard to get a grade in. If you forget one assignment your hopes of an A are gone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: 2292 was the most general class I have ever taken. The exams were not hard just confusing and wordy. He covered anything from resume building, to presentation skills, to a large range of general business definitions. Hard to put his class into a short description.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Ty is a really nice guy and makes lectures on very simple material bearable, but my only issue was how unpredictable the exam questions were. You definitely should go to lecture if you want to do well on the exams. Recitation is brutal however, each class is 2 hours of going over material that can be done in 15min. A lot of presentations too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ty is an okay lecturer, somewhat entertaining. As the coordinator, he can be a bit disorganized. The syllabus is a bit weird in terms of layout. Some quiz and test questions seem like he is deliberately trying to trick you. IMO a very fair grader for presentations and the final paper. Not a ton of room for error in this class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's nice and a good lecturer, but he made so many errors on tests and quizzes. Easy class but tests very specific, random details. TA's are inconsistent on grading. Felt like this class could have been fit into a half semester. A lot of our 1 hr 50 min recitations were over in 30 min. Learned some good stuff but often felt like a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Lectures from Ty are posted online or you can attend them in person. Make sure to watch them! The recitations were simple but lengthy. The class material is easy, however, the midterms and quizzes contain questions about specific stuff so you do have to study! Participation matters in recitation! Lots of little point assignments that all matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ty had some great lectures, but this class was a tireless effort to make difficult a class that should not be. Tests and quizzes were tricky, points were deducted for silly things, and there seemed to be no consistency among TA recitation leaders. Team building stuff was cool. Would be more effective if it were more straight forward and focused

I don't really get the purpose of this class but.. His quizzes and exams are more challenging than it should be i feel like its the way he asks the problem. class doesn't involve too much work but is super boring with recitation that is pretty much 2 hour long. Like him as a professor but not the way he makes his exams

Ty is cool, but this class sucks. Quizzes were unclear, essay was poorly explained. Going to lecture makes it easier, but even then the material you need to know isn't flushed out well at all. Class shouldn't be hard at all, but the way they revamped it makes it sort of difficult. I'd take Ty again, but not this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Ughhh I HATED this class so disorganized and confusing and really a huge waste of time. Not specifically Tys problem maybe its how the class is designed or set up? Just an awful experience

Ty is easy going, caring and pretty fun overall. The class is straightforward and he has worked hard to make it more useful to the students seeking internships and life knowledge. The quizzes/exams can be tough if you don't attend lecture or read the materials. I would definitely take him again.

Class is an easy A if you follow the directions, work with your group, and practice the steps they teach you for presentations. A few short papers, but other that it's presenting in front of your peers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class itself is an easy A as long as you do the readings. Grades the presentation kind of tough.  Ty is great. He cares about his students and their success beyond the classroom. If you put in the work to achieve your goals, he'll do whatever he can to help you. If you can take one of his courses, do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: While Ty is the course coordinator, he teaches some recitations and that's where I had him.  He is a really laid back easy going guy who makes the 2 hour long class somewhat fun.  The class itself is in my opinion pointless, I took nothing away from it, it's basically just another freshman survey class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Shepfer is so nice and wants you to succeed. He's understanding and I liked having him as a lecturer, but he wasn't my TA so I can't say much about that.  As for the course material itself, this class is absolutely useless. I think I actually became stupider by taking this class. Such a waste of my time + semester.

Ty cares about his students like no other. There is no textbook, he prefers articles and encourages discussion. Ty is a great guy and is always there to help a student in need. He assigns group projects because teamwork is his thing. 2292 is an easy class, make sure you have TY!

Seriously one of the coolest professors I've ever had. Really approachable, funny, and actually cares about you as a student. Wish I had another class with him. Lectures got long real quick, but he brought you back into it. Fair grader imo because he gives really specific criteria on rubrics. Real easy on the eyes as well, definite stud.

Reading is really important! Reading is really important! Reading is really important! As an international student, this course is not that easy if you skip reading! I did not do the reading, so I just got 72/100 on my midterm. Then I start to do that, I got 90/100 on my final. Lots of stuffs need to do but fairly easy grader.

If you attend lectures, you should get above a 90 on the midterms.  This was his first time organizing the course, but overall, pretty easy.  Has Group projects and presentations but fairly easy grader. I usually don't like these kind of classes but Ty was an awesome professor and made the class fun.
Awesome! Very helpful. Entertaining. None of the TAs for this class are bad though.
He was very helpful and the class didn't take too much time.  Recitations took attendance, but don't bother with the actual class, Tansky just drones.
Ty is an awesome TA!  He teaches better than most professors.  He actually thinks about what he is saying and doesn't talk just to hear himself talk.  He has helpful and insightful things to say.

best TA for this class. sooo much easier than the others. cool guy, fair grader, knowledgeable, helpful, and understanding. good recourse beyond the class. best TA you can get. do whatever you can to have him. i'm a guy and i think hes a stud so ladies you're in for a treat!
Great teacher and makes class fun! Really nice guy and always has good career advice.
A really great guy. Very passionate about the subject. Seemed to grade slightly harsher than the other T.A.s but you really can't get a horrible grade.
Awesome!!
Simply awesome!
Great TA.  Really passionate about teaching and his students.  Nice to look at too...
mean guy, "act like a business student," gets mad when one student out of 268 is not paying attention to him
Dude will press you for quite literally anything.  Basically breathes on you while your taking your exam, maybe the last guy i'd grab a beer with.
Don't take his class. You'll fail
Exams are extremely hard and confusing
The words I have to say are "not meeting the site guidelines" do not take this professor!
A mean professor

Not being able to see your grade the whole semester makes no sense at all and most grades didn't even go into carmen until the day they were due. I'm still lost how I ended up with the grade I did because it's not matching up the grade I calculated. This class was just a mess and so beyond confusing ugh

Didn't post like half the grades in the course until the day final grades were due on Dec. 22nd. Carmen page is unorganized, and doesnt tell you your grade (which doesntmatter cuz he never posts them) Not a super challenging course, but the exam material is tough to study for becuase there will be random questions thrown onto the exams

My issues with his course: Inconsistencies in instruction between his videos and Schroeder's lectures, miscommunications to TAs re: what is on exams, poorly organized Carmen page, repeated errors on quizzes, unresponsive to student concerns.

I believe that I, a 20-year-old with 0 teaching experience, could run this course better than Terry. :)

Condescending guy who thinks he's better than everyone around him. The class felt unfair especially with the exams becoming more tougher since its no longer all multiple choice anymore. You have to have an average of 50% over both the midterm and final or else you won't pass the class even if you did well on the other assignments. No curve either

Teaching style is authoritarian. Students may be publicly called out for being late, and there are frequent moralizing comments unrelated to course content. Exams this semester were harder than expected, with many fill-in-the-blank and formula questions despite review sessions suggesting mostly multiple choice.

You never know your grade in the class and if you want to know it you have to calculate it yourself. Exams were completely different then he said they would be and it takes months for assignments to be graded as they are also filled with so many mistakes
The worst class ever. TA's blow. No one is helpful. Way to much work for a 1.5 hour class.

The midterm was extremely challenging, and the fact that it was almost entirely written felt unfair especially since exams in previous semesters were multiple choice. In terms of exam performance, I've found this class more discouraging than stats 2.
Straight up terrible
War criminal
Gives bad instructions on the MBEs and expects people to figure it out
Terrible professor. Changed up the midterm from all multiple choice to majority application and acts surprised when the average went down. No curve either
Just awful
Klinker was alright, but the class is not. Either you get or you don't. Felt like the tests were different from what was learned in the modules. Definitely something you have to study for. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Today Terry made a joke about Jeffery Epstein's island. WILDLY inappropriate coming from a professor. He makes a point to single students out if he deems you are not acting as a "business professional". He will publicly shame students in front of the entire class which is a HUGE distraction from the material. Terry tries to make students fear him.

Professor Klinker is a great teacher who cares about his students and teaches practical material. The course is heavily based on two exams, so stay on top of the practice work. I didn't do well on the midterm but made up for it on the final.
This guy blows
Midterm and final are most of your grade. If you do “well” on them and get 10% better than the average on them, you'll end with a B
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terry Klinker gets somewhat of a bad wrap for no reason. The class is not difficult if you show up to the lecture and recitation. Terry explains concepts very well and has a ton of resources available to students. Super nice and funny guy too. Some students think he comes off as strict, but he just wants students to succeed.
Sarcastic, rude, and not even a good teacher to boot. Publicly shames students in the middle of class and forces you to pay to access content and videos that he recorded himself.

Professor Klinker is a very straightforward and knowledgeable professor. The assignments and quizzes are very straightforward. The exams can sometimes be a little more challenging, but overall very straightforward and fair. Extra credit is given based on attendance to lectures and recitations, but can be easily acheived.

He isn't a bad guy, but did not love his teaching style. The PowerPoint presentations did not always line up with the lectures, and he was impossible to reach outside of class. The exams were not awful if you were prepared but challenging. Overall, I would see if you could have another lecturer for this course.

You will waste a lot of time figuring out what horrible directions mean, and you have to spend $100+ on a textbook you will never use so you can take quizzes and watch his youtube videos (yes he puts quizzes and lecture vids behind a paywall).

Very bad directions on model building exercises, for how long this course has existed these should be organized, waste a lot of time figuring out bad directions. Also forces you to to buy a useless textbook (that I never used) so you can watch his youtube videos and take quizzes. (Yes he puts quizzes and lectures vids behind a paywall)

Class was disorganized and Terry came off as arrogant. I didn't find him helpful at all in lecture. Videos are the only thing that helped. Exams aren't hard content wise, but he'll frame questions on the test in a way that is completely foreign to example problems. Just make sure you use common sense. Do every easy assignment to cushion your grade.

Quite possibly the worst course I have ever taken at any level of my education. The homework had typos and errors ever week. Klinker did not submit grades on time and took several days after the hard deadline to post them, JUST TO GET THEM WRONG and email every student that he needs an EXTRA WEEK to fix them. We pay 35 thousand a year for this bs?

This class is an absolute disaster. Almost every model building exercise had errors in the instructions, completely forgot to post a quiz to the textbook publisher, and awful communication to students on due dates or guidelines. All the course content is reused yearly (Lecture videos from 2015), how is this class so disorganized? Waste of tuition.

This class is really just an applied algebra 2 class, but with how disorganized this course is it feels like everyone is rooting against you. Like 6-7 times a TA would announce a day before a hw was due that there were 3 errors in the instructions that we had to fix. The exams and group project really arent as hard as people say though.

Klinker is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. Every assignment he sent out had SO many typos. They make you buy a textbook that you only use to click youtube links that Klinker recorded himself. So, essentially, you're buying youtube links. Nothing was ever clear in this class, lectures were unhelpful, and the group project was a mess.

Klinker is a good guy and cares about his students, but it's hard to get anything out of his teaching style. The lectures are online videos with the powerpoints, however, they are unorganized on the modules and the powerpoints don't always match up. The class in person is not really helpful. Exams are difficult as it's hard to know what to study.

Klinker was good. He wasn't too accessible from email but the feedback I'd get from him in person was great. He's an old fashioned military guy, so some in the class didn't like his style. If you've ever had a tough boss at an internship, Klinker is that tough boss. Overall, he's smart and a good professor. He truly cares about your success too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Klinker himself is a good guy and the class is pretty easy to follow if you attend lectures recitation. However, this class is the least oranized class I have taken. Due dates are always wrong on slides, incorrect directions on weekly assignments and quizzes with the wrong answers. Should not be this bad when he's taught this course for so long.

Klinker is the course coordinator for BusOBA2321 and the course is structured horribly. All MBE instructions were posted late and always had many typos and incorrect instructions so I ended up going to office hours solely to ask the TAs what the directions were actually supposed to say. Would not recommend if you aren't required to take.

Professor Klinker's teaching style takes some getting used to, but the structured format and helpful prerecorded videos make studying more manageable. unstuck ai complemented the course materials well for exam prep.
Rude, makes very distasteful jokes about women, disorganized

Although the class material is not hard, the teaching style makes it way harder. Lectures are extremely hard to follow, and the material skips from class to class. For a 1.5-credit-hour class, you will easily do more than that. Instructions on assignments are always wrong, and then points will be marked off, would not recommend.

Worst professor and class I have ever had. Spends half of the class berating his students. Makes mistakes on the instructions for virtually every assignment posted. Gives students no leniency but doesn't hold himself to the same standards. The actual content is easy to understand but he seems to enjoy making it intentionally more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Klinker is simply the worst. Wish I had more space but; Extremely rude, harsh grader, unorganized (mistakes on every assignment), 2 exams are 60% of your grade, Payed for a textbook just to watch youtube videos HE MADE, Feedback is vague and not helpful. Klinkler seems like a guy who has is out for his students. Would give a 0 if possible.

What an awful professor LOL. Vague grading criteria and no willingness to help. Not responsive at all. What a disgusting class. The group project had no clear criteria or assistance with difficulty, so prepare for sub 50% grades on that. No info on the exam yet as I have yet to take it, but wow. What a horrible course.

He's okay overall. his classes can be entertaining, but honestly, he's a little too full of himself. This isn't much of a problem, but dealing with a professor w this personality, means don't expect much leniency. also, its funny that he complained about us having to buy the book because we dont use it, but come to find out it's his book lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His grading criteria on the assignments is very vague and he takes points off for ridiculous things. The homework we're assigned barely pertains to what is going to be on the midterm and final, and doesn't help much at all. He's not approachable and doesn't seem to want to actually help his students.

He is very stern and just not a nice guy in general which makes the content even harder to process. It is a lot of work for a 1.5 hour class. The group project is extremely difficult as well. Still, he's the better option of him and Bonnie. He does not care about his students outside of class whatsoever.

Screamed at us on the first day of class for people wearing hats or sweatpants to class. Everytime you talk to him he makes sure that he has power over you. You think he would be nicer to the students that pay his $120,000 salary! He is also profits off his job because you have to buy the book he then I found out HE WRITES THE BOOK!!! Like Really!

He makes a lot of mistakes for homework and quizzes. It is pretty annoying for someone like me who gets work done as soon as they're open. There is no other professor to take this class other than Bonnie, who still uses Klinker's materials and the exams are the same.

Acts as if he is above all of his students and needs to baby us through college when in reality, he is the worst professor I have had.
