He is a teacher first and a researcher second, so he is committed to his students. He also sits on the committee that makes the exams, so he knows what to expect

I was so nervous about taking this notoriously difficult class, especially considering Chem1210 is full of pre-meds and I hadn't even taken AP Chem in high school. Having Dr. Clark as a professor was an absolute blessing. He is a clear, funny, interesting instructor who completely renewed my passion for Chemistry. Best professor for a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ted Clark was the best chemistry professor/teacher I have ever had. He makes class easy to understand and really enjoyable. He does fun experiments while in class and is overall amazing. He taught the major chemistry course (1610) which I took so try to get into that if you can.

I loved Dr. Clark. He made lectures interesting and was super helpful during office hours. He also makes connections between real-life scenarios and the concepts being taught to make the material more tangible. I'd recommend everyone take Dr. Clark for gen chem if they have the option.
Dr. Clark is one of my favorite professors I've had. He really works hard to make sure lectures are engaging, and he is always more than willing to help students with any concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chemistry 1210 was a very difficult class, but Ted Clark made me more prepared for exams. He keeps lecture very interesting and is a very nice person. I wish I could take him again for 1220. He doesn't make the recitation TAs give quizzes so that is a huge plus. My final grade was not too good, but it would be a lot worse without Ted Clark.
Dr. Clark was amazing, but the tests were very difficult. However, if you read the chapters and do the practice questions, you should easily pass the class. Lab reports help bring your grades up.
Funny and genuine, great lecturer. Understands you get tired in lecture. Explains concepts patiently and clearly.

Best professor at Ohio State. I couldnt imagine a better professor for gen chem at OSU. You can definitely tell that he genuinely cares about his students. He is also great at responding to emails in a timely manner. Extremely accessible outside of the classroom. He truly prepares you for what will be on the exam. But get ready for a lot of work!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really great at explaining the topics, obviously knows the material really well. Very accessible outside of class for extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attend lecture with Dr. Clark: he keeps things interesting, he looks like Trevor from Grand Theft Auto, and his deprecating humor is actually funny. He knows how to relate to students, and makes his material challenging though accessible. I highly recommend him for inorganic chemistry. I'd say the exams were average difficulty.

Dr. Clark is probably the best professor I've ever had. He is very passionate about helping students succeed in his class. It would be very beneficial to go to his office hours as he tells you exactly how to study for the exam. Exams were very tricky so be prepared to not only read, but understand the textbook and lecture concepts inside and out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hes pretty good would recommend

Dr. Clark is literally the best professor at Ohio State. If you have to take gen chem, try to get into his class. He cares so much about his students and wants everyone to get good grades. I've never had a professor reach out to see if there's anything he can do to help. One of the best people/teachers I've ever met!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I started going to his lectures b/c my actual prof was terrible, and I was rewarded beyond belief. His lectures are engaging and really get to the root of understanding the material, which is crucial for exams. He is incredibly caring and does everything (reasonable) within his control to ensure his students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Clark is AMAZING! After having a terrible lecturer for chem1, I can assure you Clark is the real deal. He makes difficult concepts so much easier & hes a pretty funny guy. I actually didnt find the concepts or the class any harder than chem 1 thanks to Clark. If youre taking this class, take it with Clark!
Great lectures. His review sessions were particularly helpful, especially for the final.

Dr. Clark was an incredible professor. He made lectures fun enough to stay awake and interested in. He's always willing to answer questions during, after, or outside of class. Promptly responded to emails and was very caring and accommodating to personal emergencies or issues. Highly recommend!

He is very good at conveying overall concepts. His class wasn't too hard, but I feel it didn't prepare me well for my future chemistry class. The first exam was graded very easily and then the final was graded completely the opposite.

Dr. Clark is easily my favorite professor at OSU. He really does a good job explaining the material in lectures and keeps it interesting, even for a full hour and 20 minute lecture. Take him if you can!

Clark was a great professor! He always had great lectures and was always available outside of class. Attending lecture is extremely important though in order to get a good grade. Definitely prepares you for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: After finishing with a C- in this class having Dr. An Coe, Dr. Clark is the best Chem Professors at OSU. He keeps you engaged my making chemistry interesting in any way that he can from funny memes to hilarious anecdotes. Hes a great guy all around and he makes this hard course seem easy becaause he is a great teacher!

he wears flannels and also teaches chem good. Also go to lecture because he is hilarious, a wonderful man, a skilled lecturer, a helpful giver of feedback, and an all around quality dude. Did I mention he wears flannels?

Read and go to lectures. Read because Chem 1910 and Clark both go really fast. Clark also talks about certain things that aren't discussed indepth in the textbook but will be on the exam. Also he doesn't give out review materials before midterms and finals. He's an ideas type of guy which I enjoyed but it does make some of his questions really hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Ted Clark was an amazing teacher. He made Gen Chem interesting, and I always found myself looking forward to his lectures. I would take his class again in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Disclaimer: I had this man for a week before an unexpected schedule change. From three lectures, my impression of him is phenomenal. He's super knowledgeable, he really cares about your learning, he's good at breaking things down, and he's an incredibly engaging professor. My friends who stayed in his section said the tests were hard but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is an amazing professor. He makes the more complicated concepts of general chemistry much more simple. His lectures help a lot, I recommend not skipping lecture! He is very much so willing to help students when they don't understand something. Overall, I really enjoyed having him as a professor.
Although Gen Chem 1 at OSU was extremely hard, Dr. Clark made the class much more bearable. I specifically chose him as my professor for Gen Chem 2

Dr. Clark is a great professor. His lectures are engaging, and he explains the materials in a clear manner. He really wants his students to succeed, and is very encouraging. His class is not an easy A like any other science classes at OSU, but he definitely makes the process a lot easier. I would highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is a great professor! In lectures, he explains the material well and wants students to ask questions. He gives his students many materials to help prepare for tests and is extremely approachable. The Chemistry Dept. at Ohio State hold chemistry to a very high standard, but Dr. Clark strives to make it more manageable for everyone.
I had Ted Clark in AU2015 for FEH Chem 1210 which is no different than regular Chem 1210 besides more A students. He explained the content very well and he is one of the best profs in the chem dept.

I loved Dr. Clark. He does everything in his power to help students learn how to succeed in his class. He is more concept heavy than the other profs which some think makes his class more difficult. I preferred it because there was less memorization and I learned way more. Very sad I couldn't have him both semesters of chem. Definitely, take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very nice guy who truly cares about students. Im miserable at chemistry and even I didn't it find unbearable. The exams can be hard but he gives plenty of exam resources and even writes you emails afterwards telling you what to work on. The lecture notes are online.  He welcomes questions and answers them very well.  Final grade is curved!
He's a really nice guy, tries to make lectures as fun and engaging as possible. Really cares about the success of his students, but his exams are really hard.
Hard exams compared to the easy final. Very accessible during office hours, online homework, labs every week and lab reports take a long time. Make sure you get a good lab TA

Clark is a very good professor and I would highly recommend him as your first time gen chem professor. He's very conceptual and will teach as students haven't learned chem before. Some exam questions can be difficult but overall, the average in any gen chem course will be a C. You really gotta work to get a better grade. Recitation and lab helps.

Dr. Clark is a good professor, but his class is quite challenging. He likes to ask a lot of conceptual questions on exams and I am more of a math-based person so I really struggled in that area. However, I feel like I still learned the material and was prepared for Chem 1220.
Views more heavily on conceptual things rather than the math to it.

Chemistry sucks but Clark made me love going to his lectures. He is really funny/quirky/nerdy and it helped me pay attention. Make sure you read your material before going to class and print off his notes. Midterms are tricky but the final is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is a legend. As long as you put forth the effort and attend every lecture, the content is easy to understand and the test aren't unreasonable, albeit a little tricky. However, he provides a ton of practice tests for each midterm and the final, and truly cares about teaching. An all-around great guy.

Dr. Clark really is a great guy. His lectures go in depth and he explains concepts very well while still being interesting. He's a very funny guy and he cares about his students and teaching Chemistry. His tests are very conceptual, but if you read the book ahead of time and take good notes you will be fine.

His tests are extremely challenging, and are heavy on conceptual problems. If you're more of a math-based learner, this class is going to be very difficult, and you will be leaning on your lab scores to carry your grade. (Better hope you get a good lab TA...)However, his lectures were fine and he seemed to care a lot about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall I really liked Dr. Clark as a person and lecturer. He was very easy to reach out to and I would highly recommend talking to him in person if you are struggling. The hardest part is by far the tests. If you are more of a calculations person like myself, the tests do not work in your favor and you will heavily rely on lab carrying your grade.

Dr. Clark is hands down the most caring professor I have ever had. He makes class enjoyable, cracking jokes, and truly wants students to do well. He taught me actually how to learn and study, and for that, I will be forever grateful. He is funny, caring, and smart af. Take him.

Dr. Clark was one of my favorite professors this year. He makes his lectures interesting and tries his best to relate everything back to real-life examples. His tests are pretty conceptual, with averages usually around 70-75 (which isn't uncommon for Chemistry). Definitely going to lectures and taking notes from the textbook were necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is my favorite professor I've ever had.  He makes lectures enjoyable, and he really engages his students.  His tests are very hard because they're so abstract, but once you learn how to study for them you can succeed.  It is extremely important that you read the book thoroughly for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark has some of the harder tests in the chem department, and loves his concepts. His tests have very little math, but really test hard on your understanding of the conceptual parts of chemistry. He's super nice and energetic, and his tests are probably the most like the standardized chem final. Wish I would've had him for 1220 as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Full of himself and thinks that his way is the only way to do things and tell you how good he was at things when he's just meant to be teaching the content not telling us about how good he was in school.

Dr. Clark is an excellent instructor who really seems to care about students. However, the course is set up to have lots of online homework and his tests are extremely difficult and there is no curve. Most of the questions require deductive reasoning more so than chemistry knowledge and they often go above and beyond the material in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is easily the best Chemistry professor I've had at Ohio State. He cares about connecting with as many students as possible. I found myself understanding concepts in his class that I hadn't understood in previous courses. His exams are a deal easier than those of other professors, but this also leads to a higher average and a smaller curve

Dr. Clark is hands down the best professor I have had here at tOSU. He really cares about his students grasping the concepts and does everything he can in order to help make the material more easily understood. He is very straightforward and will tell you from the beginning, if you do the work for the class, then you will succeed.

Clark will literally give you the best lecture you've ever had. He's an all around amazing guy and I would go to his office hours just because he's such a cool dude and I wanted to know him more. However, his exams are HARD, even if you study. It's chem at Ohio State, it's always going to be hard. But Clark makes it fun

I enjoyed having Clark, but I must admit that I didn't get to know him too well since I only went to a couple of lectures (I should have been in Chem 1220). He's knowledgeable, funny, and clear, but his tests are meh. They are extremely abstract, conceptual questions that you won't see from other chem profs or classes. I'd still recommend him.

He graduated from Michigan... He brags about it in Class.... I was very confused when he tried to explain things. Very inconsistent and scatterbrained.  Some students love him. I Don't like him. This course is programmed to weed out students. If you receive a bad grade its normal. The 10% who get an A is all they want, everyone else is a $$$.

Dr. Clark is a phenomenal professor who knows his chemistry inside and out. He gives plenty of opportunities to participate in class and really see what you know instead of just giving out answers. I would highly recommend him to anyone who needs to take 1220. Chemistry is a difficult subject but Dr. Clark's class is conducive to learning.

After taking AP Chem, I can still say that this class was still pretty challenging. Dr. Clark's lectures were generally pretty interesting, though he requires you to "discuss with the person next to you" a little too often. I've heard that he is really kind and helpful in his office hours, but I personally didn't need to attend them.

In my opinion the best of all the Chem 1210 and 1220 professors. I built my entire schedule around making sure I got into his class for both. He's such a dork and loves what he's teaching which makes his lectures interesting. He's very engaging by proposing questions and then letting you talk about it with the people around you.
His class is more conceptual than others but he teaches it in a way that makes you understand it.

Dr. Clark is honestly a great teacher. I hated chemistry for the most part because of the stress it caused me but props to this dude for making an otherwise terrible experience slightly more tolerable. Class is still hard, though, obviously.

The class is very difficult. You can get by if you don't go to lecture as long as you know your stuff. Dr. Clark will always help you if you go to his office hours. His tests are killer and tricky. Really nice and funny dude though, I enjoyed the class despite it being so hard.

Prof Clark is there to help his students succeed. The lectures can be confusing and boring and the tests are difficult. However, I took AP chem in high school and the 1210 was not very hard at all. The tests are a very large part of your grade and make a big difference (only reason I got an A-). He is worth taking over other professors.

Dr. Clark's lectures were key to doing well in this course. He explained the content very clearly and provided additional details that couldn't be found in the book or determined purely by looking at the presentation slides on Carmen. He was very helpful at office hours, and although his tests were hard, he was very fair with grading.

His lectures are interesting and Dr. Clark is very funny but I also found him very confusing and felt the material covered in class was not comparable to the difficulty of the tests. His tests are VERY hard and have very low class averages.

I loved Dr. Clark so much, even though I hated Chemistry. I really believe that he is the best professor for chem that you could take at Ohio State. He is a great lecturer, and so helpful if you ever need it. His tests are very difficult, but the new final is so much easier compared to midterms. If you put in the time and effort, you will succeed.

Ted is an awesome professor.  His midterms are insanely difficult, but the final was a breeze compared to the midterms.  He made lectures fun, and you have to go if you want to do well in the class.  If you skip class, you will suffer the consequences later.  I am taking 1220 with Ted next semester because I really enjoyed 1210 with him.

I really liked Dr. Clark's class and he was always available for help. I thought the class was pretty challenging and had to do a lot of extra work outside of lecture and the online homework. It gets easier once you understand how to study for his tests which are pretty conceptual. I would definitely recommend Dr. Clark if you have to take 1210.

Dr. Clark was an a great professor. I could not have hoped for a better professor for my first semester of chemistry. He is very good at explaining concepts, and definitely tries to keep the lectures interesting. He was very entertaining and kept our class laughing. I would recommend him to anyone wanted to succeed. Still requires effort and work.

Clark is a really great professor and person in general. Very funny and makes the Lectures interesting. Tests are pretty difficult and mostly conceptual but do-able. I was a little disappointed in the lack of a curve this semester, which I didn't think was a possibility.

Chem is hard. Clark is the bomb, though. Very helpful lecture that I actually felt was useful and helped me understand what was going on. Read, people. Read and outline. Read it again. Ask questions. Do practice problems. Work and you will be okay. I also heard his office hours were good, though I never went.

Tests are very much based on concepts - but when the tests Did have math on them, they were the type of questions that required  you to do the math for each answer choice to figure out which answer was correct. Lots of online HW (uses Mastering Chemistry) - it's graded with limited tries. But not to worry, the HW is only 70 points out of 1,000.

Good guy. Lectures are fine but long. If you study the notes and take advantage of office hours, you will be fine. DO NOT MISS A CLASS. He has notes on his site but in all honesty are you going to check them after a long day of classes
Ted Clark is an amazing professor.  He makes chemistry interesting and he helps students to clearly understand the concepts.

Dr. Clark is extremely conceptual. It's important to really understand the underlying concepts in the material to do well on his tests because they're extremely concept-based as well. He's tough but fair and he responds to emails quickly. He also has a great quirky sense of humor.

Clark is one of the best professors in the Chemistry department. Chemistry at OSU is HARD, so be prepared, but he will give you all of the material you need to know, but it is on you to actually learn it. He loves conceptual questions and history. This class will be hard no matter what, but he is such an interesting guy. Highly recommend him

Clark is one of the best chemistry teachers at OSU. The tests are difficult but he will make sure you are prepared for each exam and is clear on what he expects his students to be able to do. Chemistry is difficult no matter who you have as a professor but Clark will make sure that you understand the concepts well enough to succeed in the class.
Funny lecturer and engaging. Wants you to participate in lectures. But it is chem and at ohio state it still hard. But clark is one of the best 1210 teachers

Chemistry is super hard; dont take it if you don't have to. And keep in mind there is a  lower, easier chem you can take! If you have to take 1210 though 10/10 times I would recommend Professor Clark he's hilarious and helpful I just hate Chemistry.

Does a very good job preparing for the midterms and finals. Class is kinda difficult but no more so than any other lecturer. Explains concepts very well and backs them up with demonstrations. Lots of class participation is encouraged.

Ted Clark is an amazing man. He's always very stylish, and I love his lectures. Visual learners will have a lot of great input from him, as he does a lot of examples in class and a lot of simulations. He's one of the funnier teachers I've had my whole life, and his office hours are always worth the wait. I definitely recommend taking his CHEM 1210.

This is a very tough class but Dr. Clark makes the lectures very interesting. He is a professor who's tests are mainly conceptual instead of calculations so beware. In his lectures he very frequently put up questions and told us to converse with our peers which was helpful most of the time but sometimes so frequent it was frustrating.
Great professor who teaches the material thoroughly -- wonderful class

I thought his exams were inconsistent in terms of difficulty. I stayed above the class average in all the midterms and then bombed the final. I found the conceptual questions to be confusing since I relate to the math part of Chemistry more. He doesn't really give out much resources to help prepare for exams either.  He's approachable though.

Clark is a great guy, his lectures aren't for everyone though. He likes to have discussions in lecture, which I wasn't a huge fan of. Homework and practice exams are really helpful, and reading the book is a must to do well on his exams. His exams are hard, and often have multiple trick questions, but I think he's one of he best in the department.
Did not like him one bit. His test are extra hard and boring lectures.

Dr. Ted Clark? If you don't know who he is, picture the real life version of GTA 5's Trevor with a little less guns and a lot more liquid nitrogen. His tests are the equivalent of trying to complete a 250 piece puzzle in one hour whilst chugging a gallon of milk. However, he will be your Opera and will truly inspire you. BEST chem professor at OSU.

Dr. Clark is by far my favorite professor here. He is not only willing to help, but it willing to listen and understand your questionsconcerns. He makes chemistry fun to learn and always has a joke or two for each lecture.

Dr. Clark is very likable and presents the information very clearly in the lecture.  The tests are unbelievably difficult as he really likes the trick questions.  He likes history of chemistry, so be prepared for that too.  He is friendly and loves to joke around with the students.  I suggest him over anybody in the Chemistry department at OSU.

Dr. Clark is one of the best Chemistry professors for students who are visual learners. He uses many simulations in lectures that help you observe what you're learning about. He has classes that are exciting and engaging. I actually attend his 1220 lecture now in addition to my own because I couldn't get into his lecture this semester.
The exam questions are tough. Don't bother reading the book because all of the information on the exams are on the powerpoints, which are very detailed and full of examples.

Awful class, awful labs, but I loved Dr. Clark. I think the class itself was just painful, but he was funny and enjoyable. Chemistry at OSU is just something you want to avoid altogether (coming from somone who got a 5 on AP Chem and didn't even have to take this class)
tough grader

I liked Dr. Clark as a person, but not as a teacher. His exams are very conceptual. I wouldn't recommend taking his class if you are more of a math person when it comes to chemistry. His office hours were very helpful though!

Dr. Clark is the reason I passed Chem 1210 at Ohio State.  He is fair and a great lecturer. You don't need to read the book just take notes in class and know the material on his power points.  The only bad thing I have to say is he likes theoretical question and history of chemistry so look for a few of those types to show up on midterms.

Exams are very history based. Trick questions galore. Don't have this professor if you get the choice. Goes over example problems in class. Mc exams. Do well on labs and hw and go to recitation to balance any bad exams. Thinks a 65% avg is "good" so be ready to be babied through the work and butchered on exams. Very helpful if you ask questions.

Does not give quizzes during recitation, but the recitation assignments are required.  The midterms and final are hard though.  Clark focuses more on the theories behind chemistry rather than the math behind it.

*Disclaimer: I got a 92 raw score before a pretty big curve (at least 4-5%)* Dr. Clark is a great guy and I love his audience participation in his lectures. However, his tests are extremely conceptual and has curveballs like history. The average test grades went lower every time from 75-high 60s-low 60s-60%(final). FOLLOW HIS LECTURES!!!

Nice guy who's funny, but typical OSU chemistry. The tests are pretty tough, even if you have taken chemistry before. Mastering Chemistry assignments are annoying and can sometimes be tedious if you can't figure out the answer, but usually the answers are on Google. Would take again, probably a lesser of the evils in the Chem department.

He provided a lot of help, practice midterms etc. He uses mastering chemistry which is annoying. His tests were unfair asking questions about history and such that doesn't apply to my knowledge of chemistry as an engineer. He sometimes makes mistakes in lecture that he didn't get called out on and made things confusing at times.
Always enjoyed going to lecture. His tests are hard but he gives you everything you need to be successful. Study hard and the class isn't bad at all.

An intriguing and entertaining lecturer! I really enjoyed his classes though the tests were largely conceptual and tough for me. The key is to attend every lecture and definitely go to his office hours.

The way he creates Mastering Chemistry multiple choice questions are horrible and astoundingly terrifying. He gives a lot of 50-50 questions and if you choose the wrong  answer you get a 0%! How does this reflect your knowledge? Tests are hard as hell!

Chemistry 1210 is super hard, but Clark was one of the best chemistry teachers I've ever had. He's so helpful and he's hilarious! His lectures are so interesting and never boring and he gives a lot of practice midterms to help you along the way. Definitely recommend him as a teacher!

Dr. Clark is extremely helpful, cares about our grades, and somehow makes sure everyone in the huge gen chem lectures understands the material. do NOT skip lectures. his practice midterms are GREAT, just like the tests, and his recitation activities are easy and helpful.

Study the practice exams like crazy!! If you don't understand something, go to office hours and he will take as much time it takes until you understand it.  The online homework is good practice.  I didn't open the book once

Dr. Clark is an all around good professor. Yes, Chemistry at OSU is hard, and you will have to do the work in order to get a good grade, however, Dr. Clark gives you the tools to be successful. You MUST attend lecture because he goes into detail about concepts that are not discussed well in the book, and the homework is a must in order to practice
An all around good instructor.

He is corny but he genuinely cares about you learning the material. His exams are more difficult, but he gives a pretty good indicator of whats going to be on the exams by sending out a practice exam beforehand. STUDY THOSE! If you arent understanding something, visit his office hours, or make an appt. He is always willing to help you learn topics.

Dr. Clark is an awesome guy. He genuine loves teaching and offers his time to help his students. Exams aren't surprising if you study the practice midterms he sends out. He does move a little fast, but not ridiculously faster than any other chem lecturer. Funny in a corny type of way. I would take him again if I had the chance!

Excellent and caring prof. It helps to do the reading before lectures. Clark is very helpful in office hours, especially if you go in with questions regularly (not only just before the midterms). His practice midterms are very helpful so do them. Also, redo the Mastering Chem assignments or the problems at the end of the chapter for extra practice.

While the content of the class is a little difficult and the pace is somewhat quick, I found Dr. Clark to be super helpful in his office hours and emails. And the lectures were very informative, if you actually pay attention.

Pr. Clark was a great teacher for gen Chem. Although he went a bit fast through lectures his knowledge was apparent and he was extremely friendly and willing to help whenever. I would definitely recommend his Chem class over all others.

Dr. Clark is the best, if not of the best, gen chem teachers at OSU.  Lectures are valuable -- when I skipped them and only read the book my grades tanked.  He often emphasizes different things than the textbook.  His exams are very difficult but A's and B's are doable when you do the recommended homework questions.

Dr. Clark is a good professor who loves what he teaches. I was bad in chemistry to start with, so the class was difficult for me. Office hours helped a lot, especially if you catch him when he is alone. He is also flexible at arranging meetings if you can't make office hours.

He is the best Chemistry professor here! He is a great lecturer and answers questions perfectly. He is funny! His exams are difficult but Chemistry in general is!  His only downfall is that he is a M!ch!gan fan! :(

His tests do have ambiguous questions, but he is extremely helpful and in my experience is indeed a great teacher. Make sure you attend EVERY lecture as there are exam questions not covered in the textbook. But most importantly, READ EVERY PAGE OF THE TEXTBOOK AND DO THE RECOMMENDED PRACTICE PROBLEMS! They seriously help so much.

The class is challenging no matter what professor you have, but in comparing Dr. Clark to some of the other Chem professors I think he's one of the better teachers. He goes a bit fast material wise, but there's always help if you need it.

Dr. Clark seemed like he would be a great lecturer. At first, he was conceptual and easy-going but expected mathematical work on exams not covered in class. He is not usually helpful when emailed. Although I am sure he is an intelligent chemist, his rarely helpful reading quizzes and lack of instruction do not help prepare for his difficult exams.
The way he tried to teach his class did not work well. I had a very difficult time understanding the concepts and preparing for the midterms and the final.

Pretty boring lecturer, especially if you have the 8 AM lecture. I feel like he wasn't too interested in helping students pass the course. I spoke with multiple people who emailed him with questions, and he just blew them off with vague replies. Exams are very unclear, and included questions on material that we only touched base on.

Dr. Clark is a funny guy, but it seems as though he doesn't want to extensively help during office hours. Lecture is also not helpful at times. Exams are similar in difficulty to other professors, but the material is taught worse by Clark. If you like ambiguity, this is your guy.

He is a really nice guy, but moves too quickly and is not clear about what he is teaching.  In class and going over the review problems you think oh i know what I am doing he has prepared me well, but when you receive the exam you feel very unprepared .  He could use his time teaching us and going  over examples rather than cutting class short.

Does not give good tests. I aced advanced chemistry in high school and got Ds after studying my butt off on the exams.  He is a nice guy but does not really help you out in lecture and he asks you to answer questions on exams above the knowledge he teaches you in lecture.

Dr Clark was nice at first but towards the end he seemed to get lazy. His lectures were boring and the way he taught was super unclear. You have to read the textbook to be able to do anything and to do his ridiculous reading quizzes that dont help you at all. During finals, when all other teachers gave exam reviews and sample tests, Clark did not.
Clark is not a bad guy. Tests are wordy, and often have very ambiguous questions. Attend lectures, as there is always a question or two on the exams that were only covered in lecture.
Funny but moves quickly

His tests were very "down to earth". As long as you pay attention to his lectures, read the chapters, and read the test questions carefully. His tests are not that hard at all, they were not super easy but they were not impossible!

Really nice guy. I loved how he would come and chat with students. However, he teaches from a very conceptual standpoint. He doesn't quite work enough actual problems to back up the material in my opinion and his tests are difficult and wordy. Lectures don't really prepare you well for them. He tries to be helpful though.

Dr. Clark was always willing to answer questions and elaborate. Dr.Clark replaced Dr.Loza for 161 for half the quarter. Midterm was ridiculous. Did not give credit for a problem where 14% of students received a correct answer. Questions poorly worded.
amazing teacher!! had lots of examples and lots of different ways to understand material! came prepared and answered every question clearly

Horrible! he taught things at such a fast pace I couldn't keep up.  I did all the work and read the chapters but apparently that's not good enough.  His tests are extremely hard and there is stuff on there that we didn't even cover until two weeks after the exam.  He's not fair at all.

Tests are nothing like what he teaches in class. Even reading the book I thought the tests were ridiculous. Was a nice guy but would never ever want to take his class again. Chem sucks no matter who teaches it, but Dr. Clark didn't make it any easier.

HORRIBLE. His Test are completely ridiculout they go past your ability to comprehend. I received an A in every other chemistry class I have taken and got a D in this one. If you can take it with another professor DO. His tests are just ridiculous I read every word of every chapter we went over and passed only one test. Extremely Hard
Teaches the material but his tests go beyond your level of comprehension of the material. He makes terrible tests.
Excellent Professor. Was always willing to help students with their questions. Very friendly.

Dr. Clark is very demanding.  His midterms are difficult and often require complex problem solving.  The wording is  sometimes obtuse.  Averages in his class are typically much lower than those in other comparable classes.
His midterms suck!!! The way he words his tests are really confusing.
No Comments
dr. clark is amazing!  he is very helpful with the statistics lab, he actually made it make sense!!  i would take any class he taught!
simply amazing!  he made lab not as much of a living hell

Great professor! 4 papers (grades super easy), and one final group project (if you show up and present you get full credit). Mandatory attendance, but very light work class for a 4000 level course. Definitely take him.
This was my favorite class, and Dr. Urban was so great. He really cares about what he's teaching and he knew everyone's names. Attendance is mandatory but there's only 2 papers and 2 tests.

Professor Urban is a phenomenal teacher and person. Every day he makes a point to approach each student and check in with them. It's amazing how humble he is despite being possibly the most well spoken person I have ever met. Discussion-oriented lectures (attendance mandatory), minimal assignments, open-ended group project for a final.

Fantastic, one of the best classes I've taken & one of my favorite professors. He clearly cares about his students and wants them engaged with the content and takes the time before class just to talk to you about how your day has gone. There's not a lot of opportunities for points, but they're easy to get, so just be careful for the four papers!

Dr. Urban is a phenomenal teacher. The class is very interesting and students learn valuable information about how to understand various religions and religion as a whole. He is beyond knowledgeable of the topic and presents it in a very fair and unbiased way. I wish every student in the world could take this class. The field trips were very cool!

He's a very nice guy, he makes an effort to know your name and asks how your day was before class if he has time. Class is very easy but is interesting. Very few assignments - occasional essay, one midterm (easy if you study), and then there is a final exam essay. Lecture attendance is mandatory as it is part of the grade. Easy GE.

He is very passionate about what he teaches. There is a lot of in-class discussion and he asks fascinating questions. If you attend class and pay attention then you will likely do very well in this class (RELSTDS S2370).

Urban is the coolest man ever. He is so down to earth and everyday would go around and ask us students who our weekend was and how our day is going. 3 papers, worth 45% of your grade but are super easy. Group project as final but can be whatever you want it to be about. There are a crap ton of readings but I didn't read a single thing and got an A

I had professor Urban for Religious Studies 2370. The lectures were honestly pretty interesting and I didn't find the class to be super difficult. Attendance is worth a decent chunk of the grade and it's hard to know what to write papers on if you don't show up but overall I would recommend taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool guy

Hugh was a really great professor. He cares about his students and tries to make conversation with everyone before class starts. His powerpoints cover everything that's on the exam. So you don't have to buy or study the textbook. You have to go on 2 field trips outside of campus and write observation papers about what you saw and experienced.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've taken several courses with Prof Urban and I have enjoyed all of them. He truly cares about his students. However, material from course to course was the same in some places so it was repetitive for me. I still enjoyed it though. Loves final group projects so pick who you will work with early on. Really great dude!

My man Hugh. . .What can I say? This dude really knows his stuff and I honestly left the semester feeling confident that I actually learned something! Enjoyed/learned so much, I am taking another one of his classes! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very nice, and cares about student opinion. He is very well spoken, and does his best to explain all questions, would take again.

You need to go to lecture to be able to pass the class. He is very lecture heavy, but they are really interesting classes so it's actually fun to go to. He loves to debate, and loves to listen to everyone's opinion. Not very many grades in the class except you have to write a discussion post once a week. Really great professor, I loved his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Showing up to class is automatically 30% of your grade. He is a great professor, his class is interesting and well taught, and the material is fairly easy.
Honestly, this guy is the best. I'm amazed at his ability to keep a lecture on religion discussion-based, level headed, and conducive to learning.

Prof. Urban deals very well with the touchy subject of religion, and keeps his own opinions to himself pretty well. He really lets the students discuss the issues than touting his own opinion and he does very well at moderating the discussion, too. Attend lecture & recitation and take notes, and you shouldn't have problems with papers and tests.
Definitely one of the rock star professors at OSU. His class will be interesting and worthwhile.
Greatest professor in Comp Studies! If you have a chance, take a class he is teaching. Any class. Do the work and you will be fine.
Class is very easy, he explains things very clearly the tests are easy.  You have to do two papers a quarter but their only three pages

Dr. Urban has a way of making what could be a very controversial subject fair and balanced.  He is fantastic at seeing all points of view and encourages discussion.  You would never know that he disagreed with your point of view.  He gets the modern student. He does not make you read his own work, but you should anyway.

I absolutely LOVED this class and Dr. Urban. The content of the class was extremely interesting and the professor was awesome. By far, one of the best classes I've taken thus far. I definitely recommend this class and professor.

He is a great professor! Comp Studies 270 was one of the best classes I've ever taken at Ohio State. If you're looking for an A and an interesting class all in one, this is the class for you. He is very clear with his teachings and is very passionate about it. I would recommend this class and Urban to anyone!

Good teacher, very very very easy. If you're looking for a class you can blow off and not put any work into I suggest taking his classes. You will never have to prove that you did any of the readings. His class was fun but I didn't learn much because I wasn't forced to.
Most amazing prof...ever
He is a great professor . . . take as many classes as possible from him.

The Hughru is a GREAT professor. He is very passionate about the subject matter and likes to have a good time while teaching. He uses a lot videos and class discussion to keep you interested. He is very skilled at rewording your answer to make you sound like a genius.

Awesome teacher. The class itself was very interesting, and Urban made it even better. The questions he posed were always thought-provoking and I frequently discussed them with friends and family for days afterwards. If you put any effort into this class whatsoever you can expect and A- minimum.
very good
very knowledgeable
so wonderful, don't graduate without taking a class from him!

AWESOME! I loved this class. EXTREMELY interesting and I learned a lot. Attendance is taken every class so GO and you should pull off an A no problem. Tons of extra credit opportunity. All together AMAZING class and prof!
He was a really good teacher with a real grasp of the information he was teaching.

Hugh is fantastic. He helps in class; he helps outside class; he helps after you graduate. Forget that he is internationally recognized in his field, Dr Urban teaches each class like someone who still believes in teaching and someone who cares about small discussion and growth. Take whatever classes you can with this man!
He's an awesome professor!! I loved this class!! If you still need to fill this GEC, TAKE THIS CLASS!!

Great prof.  Makes religion interesting even if you don't believe in it.  Plenty of extra credit so there is no excuse for getting lower than an A if you try and do the extra credit.  Several field trips requried and 4 papers.  Easy and interesting GEC.  I would highly recommend for GPA booster if you're not afraid to do all the extra work.

He was such a great professor and I would recommend him to everyone! He made class very interesting with videos and references to the simpsons.  Also you get to take field trips to different religious buildings.  Overall an awesome class.  Didn't really read the books and print outs much...just take notes and youll be fine!
awful! useless!

This was the best GEC that I took at OSU, mainly because of Dr. Urban. He was very clear about each subject, and very helpful with questions. His lectures are actually interesting to attend. Dr. Urban tells you exactly what you need to know for his tests. If you go to lecture, easy A.
Very easy to follow along with and explains himself very well!!  Very easy class overall.
Prof. Urban is the Man, he is very in touch with the modern student and makes even the most difficult subjects relateable.  i recomend very highly any course he offers.
He's friggin awesome, he's also my advisor and he ROCKS!
Prof. Urban is very good at what he does. You will learn quite a bit from him, and his classes are entertaining as well. I would highly recommend him.
One of the best classes of my sophomore year...
By far the best professor I've had so far.  He is really funny and is incredibly knowleadgable.  The midterm and final are a cinch...definitley recommended.

My favorite teacher by far. So funny, very helpful, tests are easy but you learn a lot. He is such an interesting person with so much knowledge, and he really wants to help and encourage people to think for themselves.
He is a really good teacher that doesn't expect too much.  Well worth taking any class with him.
Great sense of humor, encourages students to think for themselves.
Guy dumped water all over my girlfriend right in front of me. Super weird.

reviews.comment: TOP lad.... stood at the front of class with a super soaker and absolutely drenched people for getting questions wrong... righteous stuff
Had a tendency to pour water on students when they got answers incorrect. Super unprofessional.

reviews.comment: Honestly just not a good guy. Demeaning with his vocabulary. Needed a bit of extra help and my questions were deflected and left unanswered. He is borderline unreachable and would cancel class at the last possible minute, rumored to be due to impromptu beach trips. Never felt so talked down to by an individual

This Guy went out of his way for kids to do bad in his class.  He would never answer any questions in class and was not a good guy overall.  Really wish I had the chance to leave the class when I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He once walked into office hours with a 5-gallon container of purified water slung over his shoulder, and proceeded to dump its contents onto a nearby female student. Thereafter Jacob immediately began to boisterously celebrate, punting the empty gallon at the ceiling and beckoning observers to chant as he completed a victory lap around the room.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: taught me fractions :)
Professor Urick poured water on a female student. He is a funny guy, but way too smart to understand.
Very intelligent guy. However, he has a tendency to make you feel inferior upon asking for help

Had him for Chem 1210. Everything was ok up until he served out the final exam that had 10 extra multiple choice questions and double the amount of short answer questions (when compared to the normal exams) and still gave us the same amount of time as if it were a normal exam.
an amazing professor just make sure to go to class

I took 1220 and 2540 with him. Chemistry is hard but he made it easier to understand. He has a good sense of humor and definitely really cares about his students. He might grade hard, but he will always explain why. His class is difficult, but he is always willing to answer questions during lab and explain things at office hours.

He is a very nice and great professor, and he knows how to teach. He really wants to let you understand. He encourages you to ask questions in the class and he will even give you a penny for finding his mistake. 
Accessible outside the classroom, and very knowledgeable, will answer your questions in math, physics and engineering.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gerlach is such a great lecturer and mentor to general relativity. He apperantly has vast knowldege on mathematics and physics. He is trying to help you build solid pictures on physics. You may think the course is lack of examples. But he is super available and willing to help everyone! Talk with him outside of the classroom. Respected!
Outstanding professor, who used to give you a penny if you caught him making a typo/mistake on the whiteboard. Kept you alert!

I took a class in General Relativity from Professor Gerlach in 1973. He set me on a course of learning Physics, in which I previously had no interest. He was the biggest influence on my way of thinking ever.  I have spent 40 years pondering and reviewing the things he taught me. I am very grateful to Professor Gerlach.
Very good teacher.  I learned a lot from him. He makes sure you understand and if he sees the class does not understand a topic well he would revisit it.  His way of teaching is really good also.

The subject matter is not lightweight.  The concepts are difficult to convey in the best of worlds...but if you have the patience to persevere so does the instructor.  I managed to learn more from this instructor than any other at OSU.

I totally agree with the last respondant. Incredibly difficult hw and final. Takes off points without explanation. Very nice guy, but it is hard to connect concepts from day to day as we seem to jump around and dont follow the book
Am I taking crazy pills?  This guy is bad.  Unfair harsh grader, litte-no feedback on hw, impossible take home exam.  knows his stuff and nice guy, but bad proff
Do not follow his syllabus. He is the top guy who monitors other faculty in the department. An young professor was changed from 601 and 602 to other courses after a student whispered to Gerlach.
As long as you show up and pay attention, you can do quite well in this class, and learn a lot.  However, under NO CIRCUMSTANCES should you EVER ask for a take-home final... He'll eat you alive.

He is an excellent professor and teaches great mathematical techniques. His English is very good. The only thing is that it needs a lot of time and effort on the student's part for the material to sink-in.
The material was very difficult, but he made it easier and was also funny!
Ridiculous turnaround time on grades. 4-6 weeks to get grades back on papers. No responses to emails. Vague instructions with no clarification.

Communication was horrible. I have an assignment from March 4th that hasn't been graded yet and it's almost May... The course has assignments that build on each other (parts 1-4) but you will absolutely not get any grade or feedback by the time the next part is due. When multiple students complained, we all got 20/20 with no feedback the next day..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at OSU! She has so much knowledge beyond what she's teaching. Class is easy, with lots of open conversations and guest speakers. She clearly cares about the mental health of her students. Was not a fast grader, but was an easy grader. I highly recommend taking a class with her!

Prof Upchurch is incredibly caring, knowledgeable, patient, uplifting, and wise. Class was over Zoom, lectures weren't very structured. Takes a while to grade papers but isn't a tough grader. Tip: do the study guide before taking quizzes, and skim readings prior to lectures
Really great teacher and also a great person too.

Didn't learn anything from her. Online class, she was extremely late grading assignments, didn't respond to emails and would accept no late assignments, although she gave herself permission to be late and provided no feedback on assignments. Wasn't engaged in the course at all. Avoid taking courses from this instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Erin is very transparent about her expectations and background as a social worker. The class emphasizes diversity and advocacy, and she really brought her experiences to the table. Participation was key. Erin really connected us to the material and the reality of the social work profession. Always respectful and honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Did not learn much class content. She showed up late every class. Takes at least a month to grade papers even though there are only 3 in the semester. Not quick to e-mail back.
easy class if you go to class and pay attention easy pass

She is top of the line, nothing less! Even if it was a Spanish course, it was something to look forward to. She's engaging, entertaining, and often funny.

Coursework is challenging, but enough to feel rewarded about it, not exhausted. Show up to class, raise your hand a little, and you're golden!

11/10. I hope to have her again!

I cannot speak more highly of this professor. She was kind and understanding to work with and completely changed the way I approach my Spanish classes. Since 1155 combines two classes, there is a lot of material, but the homework was manageable and consistent each week. I definitely recommend her.

In my past, I've never really liked spanish due to some poor professors ive had in the class, but profe made spanish for me fun again. If you just do the work and it will be an easy A. She's very nice and caring and sent a great email to the whole class about her appreciation.

Linda has been one of my favorite professors by far. Keep in mind this is a 1101+1102 class combined, so the work load will not be as light as it would be if you took a single level. However, she always makes the subject as simple as possible. Very nice grader, and participation is a must. TAKE THIS PROF IF YOU WANT A GREAT FOREIGN LANG EXPERIENCE!

Prof. Linda is the best Spanish prof I've ever had. I couldn't imagine taking this tough course without her—she made it fun and easy to learn. After a bad 1103 experience, I almost gave up on my minor, but she reignited my love for Spanish and always encouraged me!

Professor Villarreal was a great professor who was happy to help. Though the class at times seemed to drag on due to the large amount of content she made it easier with her cheerful way of teaching. Too bad there is no longer the chili pepper rating on here.

Professor Castillo is a great guy. Really cares about the material he teaches. Such a valuable class that also touches on using/understanding AI. This class continues to keep me interested and wanting to learn more about demand planning and AI. The use of coding and RStudio is something that could be very beneficial down the road too... 10/10 class

Not a good professor teaches material that is unneeded for jobs after graduating. Races through powerpoint slides during class and especially on lab days. Overall I would not take him again. Really bad teacher avoid at all costs.

Probably one of my favorite Professors. He cares about the material he teaches, and you learn applicable material and programs that you can apply in Logistics. I highly recommend his course. Only advise I'd give to others is to brush up on stats, because a lot of the material will make more sense if you do.
Homework was difficult, and the video lectures often didn't provide enough information to answer some of the questions. Takes off lots of points if formatting isn't perfect on homework documents.
Vince was a good lecturer, however, his tests were very difficult and he graded quite harshly. The midterm averages always hovered around 50% or 60%.

Awesome professor who explains the concepts clearly. He runs the class in an efficient and high quality manner. However, he grades the exams very harshly and requires precise answers (but it is curved). Overall, a great professor who I would recommend!

Vu gives clear lectures and replies to emails quickly. He is sometimes a bit sassy/intimidating one-on-one, but it's coming from a good place. His exams are difficult but fair, and the HWs are reasonable. His occasionally super shiny head can be distracting during lectures - aside from that, he's much better than I expected.
Teaches well, excellent (free, online) textbook--R4DS 2e. Gave detailed instructions including occasional extra clarifications on the six weekly homeworks.
teacher is amazing, provides very clear videos and explains concepts very clearly. homework is a bit long though.

Vince is a organized teacher, but there were some problems. Firstly, whenever me or people ask for help in the discussion board, Vince would usually say "DId YoU nOT seE the LEcTure VideO?". I did see the lecture and readings and thats why I am asking for help in the first place. Secondly, the homework can be really challenging and really long...

Pre-recorded lectures and weekly hw.I hadn't had stats/math in a while but was able to follow along and do well, though I'm not sure how much I'll be able to apply in real life. Professor had clear expectations and grading structure &was available in a weekly Zoom office hour for questions. Homework is key. Sometimes I wish there were more examples
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's always talking like in 2x speed in his pre-recorded lectures. Have to stop frequently and rewatch several times to understand what he's talking about. I understand that you need to look up stuff for a coding class, but he often tells you to "Google it" in lectures and leaves people confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Ulstad was a very nice and knowledgeable teacher, yet her class was a pain to me. Some of the homework had wrong answers or incomplete questions and it would make them take twice as long. Otherwise, good professor but this got on my nerves. Would be 5/5 without this.

Professor Ulstad is the nicest professor I've ever met at OSU. Although the class was online, it was super engaging, and she seemed to truly care for her students. She broke things down and made things really easy to understand. She gave a lot fo real-world examples, which definitely helped a lot too. Definitely recommend.

Professor Ulstad was kind, and seems to care about the class. 

The course is very, very easy. Also very, very bad. Exams & homework assignments always had mistakes, & the lectures were incredibly long - the material could have been taught in a quarter (or less) of the time we spent in lecture. Lazy class. Waste of time. Nothing useful in ISE 2040.

Aimee makes it easy for anyone to understand engineering economics. Her lectures are quite straight forward, especially because she provides A LOT of in-class examples that will aide people in homework and exams. While the class content and her teaching style may be boring and repetitive, Aimee does a good job overall conveying all important info.
I took this class online but she was a pretty good professor. As long as you put in the work, the homework and exams are pretty easy and its not hard to get an A.

Literally my favorite human ever! I found this class so interesting and applicable. TA's are really nice and Aimee is happy to help. She just wants you to learn and if you put in effort she will notice. 10/10 recommend!!

Aimee is a great professor, but her class is so unbearably boring and uninteresting. I have flashbacks to econ because the curriculum is so wording dependent and which formulas to use are never clear. Homework takes a really long time to complete and theres too much of it. Aimee grades very fairly and gave ample time for all assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: The course is 2 credit hours, with lengthy weekly homework, pre-class quizzes due before each class, and exams that have questions that were never on any lecture material. The exams are open for 6 hours and most likely take you that long, with NO PARTIAL CREDIT. If one little number or something is off on a problem that takes you an hour, no credit
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are long winded even at 1.5x speed. Course materials have been uploaded late and every assignment has at least 1 question that is so poorly worded you will need to go to office hours, finishing homework early has never been so tedious. It's unfortunate because Aimee really seems to care about the course material and is very genuine.

I would definitely recommend Aimee for ISE 2040. She is very clear with expectations, and there is plenty of time to complete your assignments. She bases the class on what she's seen in industry, and she even mentions on the first day that the class is not meant to be difficult. As long as you do/understand the work, you will be fine.
Aimee is awesome even though her 3400 class is a bit heavy on projects. You will learn very useful concepts.

Very easy. Once you start an exam you have 8 hours to finish it so there is no need for you to study (it's an open book exam). The content is easy and all excel. The "big" project is ridiculously easy. She is very nice and wants you to succeed and learn. Kind of boring in class but you learn a little bit. Again, to emphasize, she makes it easy.

ISE2040 is boring but not hard - econ principles and straightforward plug-into-equation problems. There's one group project but if you space out the work it's not that bad, and she grades easy. Exams are multiple choice, so any questions missed will significantly affect your grade. Aimee herself is very nice, and teaches you what you need to know.

Aimee really knows her stuff. She's worked in industry for years and let's you know how the stuff you're learning will actually be applicable to engineering in the real world after college. There's not a lot of assignments in this class and none of them are hard. You can tell she's taught this class for a while and has the material down pat.
Big group project during the semester, she said if someone wasn't participating she'd give them a zero (and she did). Super caring of students and willing to help, very available outside of class
One of the best teachers I've ever had. 10/10 definitely recommend. Show up for class every day, there is usually a quiz.

The class was definitely not as easy as others say it is but there are so many opportunities for extra credit that you can easily manage an A or B in the class. The tests are multiple choice but each one you get wrong will hurt your overall grade greatly. The professor is really caring and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: AImee tries to pack too much into this class, diluting what is actually useful. Lectures are 2 hours long and very boring, but don't skip because she'll have surprise assignments and tophat questions. Overall, she's a fine professor, but the class could be a lot better if it weren't so boring and group project based.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: In class quizzes every day that are easy. Useful material. SHE IS SO HELPFUL! The GTAs were good as well. I thought what I learned will really help me. HW due twice a week. Be sure to go to TAs for Excel homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Aimee is an awesome professor. She does a great job of explaining the course material rather than just regurgitating it. She also gives you a chance to miss a few classes by putting her lectures online and dropping a fair amount of quizzes you take every day in class.

As far as classes in the engineering department go, this is about as easy of an A as it gets. She worked for anheuser busch and shell tell you all about it but its pretty interesting stuff. If youre an ISE major youll enjoy listening to her experience in the industry.

Solid prof. Go to class, she gives tons of hints. There's a group project where you do a case study. Pretty easy tests, easy class in general. She said she was going to use TopHat to do participation grades in class, but she never did. Seems to care about us learning something.

Aimee is an extremely nice person, but this was one of my least favorite classes ever. The content is boring (and lectures are 2 hours long), and Aimee regularly makes mistakes during her in class examples. As long as you review the slides and do the in class examples before the exams, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She doesn't lecture, she just kind of talks at you. This class is slow and incredibly boring. Also, the online homeworks were twice a week and painful to do. The content is not hard, the class just sucks.

The class is boring but fairly easy as long as you understand how to do the problems. Textbook is not necessary but you have to buy homework access. She is a decent professor and explains the material clearly. Exams are not very many questions so any question you miss will impact your grade significantly so be aware of that.

The course is short but the lectures can be boring. Purchasing homework access is forced but save yourself the money and don't bother with the textbook, it's not helpful in anyway. Forces you to do clicker questions from a phone app at random points during random lectures. The course isn't hard, just tedious.

Not many grades in the class, keep on top of the work. Aimee explains everything really clearly so just don't sleep through class and you'll get an A. Start the homework a few days in advance, sometimes it gets confusing and she'll give you the answer if you ask.

Lectures can be a little long and boring BUT she knows it and does her best to make it interesting and fun. She's one of the best when it comes to relating what you're learning to real world applications.

Prof. Ulstad is a solid lecturer. She is knowledgeable and always willing to help. She does assign a lot of busywork, but her class isn't too hard in the end. Beware getting a bad group for the group project. If you have to, you can do it all by yourself pretty easily.

The class itself is really easy. The best part is it is a 7wk course though lectures are longer. Aimee really wants to see you succeed in the course. The only drawback is the majority of students are incredibly uninterested.
Loved Aimee, homework was very helpful, test were fair. Very good at giving feedback. Absolutely hated the completely useless GTA.
Lectures were long, but overall an easy class. Had to buy online access for homework, but could've done without the ebook. Save some money and just buy an old print edition of the book.
Class is long and required so that sucks. But the course itself is very easy. Don't spend money on buying the textbook though, it's not worth it.
The classes is a little bit disorganized but when you get used to it, it will not be challenging. She is kind and not stingy on giving good grades.
Class was really straightforward and you will actually use this stuff in projects during the rest of your time here. She is an MBA and definitely knows her stuff when it comes to project analysis.

Not the best at writing questions, but her ISE 2040 class is very simple and straight forward so long as you show up to class and participate in the group project. Go to her office hours if you are struggling or unsure about the homework; she gives you the answers.
Easy class, come to lectures, study example problems and it's an easy AB+. Lectures are long but I heard that's changing to hour lectures so it should be a good class

She goes off on tangents and tries to use too many real world things that she doesn't test on so lectures get really boring. So happy this class was only 7 weeks. Test can be tricky so some studying required and the sunday hw help sessions were really useful.
Easy class.
One of the easiest class. Just do the examples. Class is very long, really boring, I find her office hour classes are more helpful.
Has no idea what she is talking about.  The only useful parts of lecture are the example problems.  Class gets long and boring but very easy.
Very clear and always willing to help with the material. The 4 hour lectures can drag on and become very boring though as she goes through example problems at a slow pace.
Very helpful
DO NOT TAKE FOUNDATIONS 1 WITH THEM. IF YOU ARE ANYTHING LESS THAN STELLAR AT MATH, THIS PROFESSOR IS NOT FOR YOU.

She's extremely kind and easy to talk to after class. Good professor and engaging lectures, definitely gonna try to get her as my professor for 2321! We had great conversations after class. She doesn't belittle you for saying the wrong things or asking questions. 10/10

She offers a very tough course, but not one that is impossible. I consistently took notes and made sure to revise them often, especially before exams. I did a lot of generated practice problems as well to prepare for exams. Exam review materials aren't provided for this course so be prepared to do lots of self studying - slides are helpful.

I really enjoyed her teaching, I thought that she gave really insightful feedback during labs, including how to fix mistakes in the lab, as well as ideas in how to improve my abilities and further my learning in the topics.

Really rough tests, even when given curve. She was a really nice and helping professor, and made CS more interesting, but the software class itself more boring. Lectures and labs barely relate to tests and there is no test practice for her class. You will need to put a lot of effort and time into this, but I believe it is doable.

Lectures are often overcomplicated and somehow lacking of helpful information. Projects are graded extremely strictly, follow every word or be ready to lose points. There is zero practice material outside the first exam. Pay attention in lab as they are more beneficial than lectures for learning exam material. Reading is optional atleast.

Tough grader who doesn't give partial credit, but there are extra credit opportunities during the semester and the success criteria is fairly clear. She is a good lecturer and you can succeed in this class pretty easily if you just pay attention during lectures

She was definitely a tough grader but an amazing lecturer. I can sense that she is very knowledgeable and deeply passionate about CS. She is honestly a very good teacher and I learned a lot from her and I find CS more interesting now. Her tests are hard but not terrible after the curve. If you do projects and take notes you will be fine.

I'm not one to leave reviews but I can't help but point out how well her class prepared me for Math 3345, Foundations 2, and even a little bit of Systems 1(with the whole bit shifting scheme.) A lot of foundations 1 courses don't introduce you to the topics she does, and in doing so I was able to easily pick up topics from higher level courses.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I dont know why she has such a low score. She is a great teacher and provides amazing feedback. Like everyone who said before the lectures are recored and the notes are amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A great professor. She knows what she's doing, which can be her own downfall at times, as things get technical pretty fast. Grading can be harsh sometimes, but there is plenty of extra credit so this shouldn't even be an issue. Her notes are detailed so even if you miss a class or 2, you can read them and know exactly what was taught.

A lot of homework, but also, a lot of extra credit on said homework. Great lecturer, and gives you every chance to succeed. Lots of resources if you can't make class on a particular day. If you have any semblance of work ethic, you'll do just fine.

KT's rating on here is insane. Easily one of the best professors at teaching. Great content and lots of opportunities to truly learn. Go to her office hours with work done and she will review. People hate because there are projects but if you do them and put in work- midterms and exams are SO EASY compared. Also lots of extra credit!! 10/10 take KT
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I saw KT's rating before taking the class but now I don't understand why the rating is so low. The content was easy to understand, and when I missed class the notes on Carmen were a decent enough summary that I could understand the continuation the next day, and I especially liked the exercises at the beginning of class.

I don't know why KT gets all the hate she does. She records all of her lectures, gives extra credit on projects, and hosts review sessions before exams. I read this rate my professor page before taking her class and I was terrified, now I know to take all of these reviews with a grain of salt. Hard class, but good teacher.

KT explains the concepts in very technical terms while they could easily be explained in laymen's terms. The projects do not have anything to do with the exams so focus on learning the HW. Watch Professor Painter videos online to understand the concepts because she does not do a good job of explaining.

She was great at teaching foundations 1. A lot of extra credit on projects which make up the majority of your grade. I did below average's on midterms 1 and 2, but well on projects and the final and finished out with an A. She's is obviously a very passionate professor.

I absolutely loved 2321 with her! She cares so so much about what she's doing, she's incredibly understanding, gives tons of extra credit, and is such a lovely person. Assignments are hard but help was always available. If you genuinely like math and CS, and you're willing to put in the work, you will love having her.

I had her for Software 1 and Foundations 1. Her lectures tend to be very confusing. Never provides practice exams. The notes she posts on carmen are really unclear and don't cover everything covered in class. Reviewing for exams is basically impossible with the lack of study material and projects are graded very strictly.

Horrible class. Take foundations 1 with any other teacher (because this teacher makes it harder)--I had to put up 10+ hours a week to grind in this class (lectures are very hard to understand but attendance is required).

Foundations 1 is an inherently difficult class and as far as her class goes it is definitely on the easier side. Lots of homework, but the homework and projects really help you learn the content. Her class is more "project focused" with projects making up 35% of your grade. Lots of extra credit, and she is very willing to help you on the projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I would say I found the other negative reviews here to be pretty representative of my experience with this professor.

I don't think they are quite ready to design their own course.

They claim to really value criticism but in my experience they do not seem interested implementing changes that would improve learning outcome.

Was worried taking this professor for CSE 2321 after hearing that her CSE 2221 class wasn't great. But man, she can teach the hell out of CSE 2231. Lectures are engaging and she is eager to help you learn anyway she can. Midterms aren't bad at all and HWs and Projects can be challenging but really help you learn the content. Lots of extra credit.

Teacher has the worst lectures by far. Thinks she gains something by introducing brand new topics in the most confusing way. Skims through one example and moves on to new topics. Gives way too much homework/projects that are often things that have not been covered yet. Does not provide exam study materials.

I wish I had checked this website before enrolling in this professor's class. Be prepared for extremely difficult exams that barely align with the course material and a harsh grading style with no partial credit. Every answer must be flawless and match her exact expectations. Definitely not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish I visited this website before taking the class with this professor. just be prepared for extremely hard exams that have nothing to do with course material + very tough grader who does not believe in partial credit. Every answer has to be perfect and the way she wants it to be. HIGHLY UNRECOMMENDED.

KT really tries to make the lectures engaging and you can tell she enjoys her job.
