I don't understand what other people are saying by she is never available as she had office hours 4/5 days of the week and provided 12 other times run by the TAs throughout the week. If you show up to class and legitimately do the work, she is a great teacher.

OSU's courses follow a sequence, with professors preparing students for the next level. Her lectures and tests, harder then other sections, introduce these complex topics for future classes; however, she provides limited exam materials and does not tell students about review sessions, so make friends in other classes.

I actually don't advise anyone to take a class with this professor. the exams are incredibly hard and you will feel like it has nothing to do with the lecture materials. She is such a tough grader who doesn't believe in partial credit for the question. Save time and money by investing them in a different professor.
The exams were incredibly hard and she was not very helpful if you did not understand a concept.

I can't imagine why there are so many fake positive reviews. Her ‘curve' is purely because her exams are unnecessarily difficult—it's just a form of torment. Her class is completely useless. I heard she's teaching Foundation 1 next semester—good luck to you all. Hopefully, your grades won't end up ridiculously low.

She lectures as if you have a background in coding but it's not needed to pass her class. I came in with only the prereq and did fine. Yes she is much harder than others, but every SW1 section is curved to the same level after the final, so her difficulty didn't make a difference. My raw scores were bad but if you can beat the curve you'll get an A

She's caring about her students and would ask if anyone need any more insight on a concept we'd be learning. Her tests weren't that horrible and completely doable if you just put in some effort into studying. Her class is really easy if you come in with some experience in Java, but even if you haven't just put in a little effort and you'd be fine.

If you like the concepts behind programming, you will like her lectures. The examples on the slides in lecture are too easy, the test requires you to think more. So overall, she is very informative but her tests are very difficult. The 2nd midterm and final were curved by +5 and +15 respectively. Her tests focus heavily on concepts and not coding.
Don't take it with her, trust me on this you will struggle and end up hating cse. She makes her own exams that are x10 more difficult from the other professors and is a tough grader

This is a reply 2 the post that said if you cant pass her SW1 class CS isnt for u. If u have an extensive coding background then ok, but if ur only background is the 1 CSE prereq class for this u will struggle and likely fail her class. HOWEVER this BS comment is NOT true this class is designed 2 make u fail if u dont have experience outside OSU.

She has high expectations for students and her class is hard, as expected for a weedout course. Her exams are definitely worse than Bucci's but not that bad after a curve. She infodumps in lab/lecture so I only recommend taking her class if you're actually passionate about CS but tbh, if you can't pass sw1 with her, CS might not be for you.

she's a nice person but i don't recommend her class. she expects you to have extensive prior knowledge (beyond what's taught in the prereqs) and the exams are harshly graded with questions that are purposefully tricky/confusing.
If you want a low enough grade, take her class, I regret immensely not dropping out of her class before it started

The exams are very difficult and the midterm is only out of 50,  meaning that one wrong multiple choice question (out of 2) turns your midterm grade into a 96%, whereas the other professors' are much more fair and reasonable. Her classes do little to nothing, you need to study on your own. If you want to get a low grade, take her class
Good professor IMO

Only 50% of students passed her class last semester.  Assumes every single student has an extensive background in coding. No chance to pass if you don't, and even if you do, like myself, you will struggle. Avoid at all costs.

Tests are way too hard and don't go over what you learn in the slides. She is a nice person, but an extremely difficult professor. Some of my friends in other classes got much easier and fairer tests, don't take her class. Probably half or more of my class failed.

She is knowledgeable and encourages you to think for yourself, but her exams are difficult because they are very conceptual and graded with little to no curve. You are required to get 60%+ on the final to pass and I think about half the class failed. Projects are hard too but they're not under her control.

i cannot emphasize how badly people need to avoid this prof. she can't explain any concept properly, will only do one example of a topic, and move on quickly. my notes don't even make sense when i write everything down. projects are very difficult. overall AWFUL!

No slides, no lecture notes, and attendance is worth 7% of your grade. The projects are virtually impossible to complete without going to office hours, they have content that is not covered in the lecture or textbook. You are expected to be able to learn material and know it 1 or 2 days later for quizzes and midterms.

JUST RUN FOR YOUR DEAR LIFE!!!!!!. She can't explain, does one example in class, and expects you to know everything. There are homeworks,quizzes and projects all of these have questions that she didn't explain. There are no slides or recordings to go back and review. AVOID.
Not nice

I loved KT as a professor. She is incredibly kind and willing to help. I learned a lot from the projects- but you NEED to go to office hours and class though (no recording or online notes if you miss).

If you put in the effort to go to her office hours for projects, you'll be fine and learn a lot for Foundations 2. Lot of work but really worth it.

I really liked how the course was set up. I thought she did a really good job teaching the subject matters, and I feel like the homeworks, projects, quizzes, and midterms were all pretty fair. Homework was completion and she always posted the solutions which was very beneficial.
Horrible professor can't explain things for her life. You are much better off watching painters videos and not going to class. But even then she add extra content that no one else teaches so.

Extremely hard in comparison to other teachers. Lectures not accessible online, and she is not accessible outside of class. Please take any other professor. This is extremely hard for no reason at all.
Extreme

There is SO MUCH hw in comparison to other teachers. She forces you to learn more content than the other classes. She also has projects, which are painful. Lectures aren't recorded and there are no online notes. Tests are all short response and FRQ questions. Other teachers have their exam on Carmen, and those exams are genuinely easier too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There is no PowerPoint, the difficulty of the lectures and the assignments and exams don't match at all, there are extra projects and assignments compared to other teachers and there are quizzes every two weeks

The professor makes all of their own assignments, quizzes, and tests which are all way overly difficult. You will be left confused trying to do the assignments because you only got to one practice problem in class which is not at all as difficult. Loves to put difficult math tricks into problems in which the concept is not supposed to be that hard.

The lectures are difficult to follow and the notes aren't helpful at all unless you annotate heavily, which is impossible because of the fast pace. KT gives a formula and does an example or two and you're expected to be able to the HW/quizzes which go 0 to 100. The Prof Painter videos don't help at all so if you miss class you're screwed.
The GOAT. Awesome professor who knows AND cares a lot about what he teaches. Class was both educational and fun. Take him if you can!

Sabina is an awesome professor. I learned so much from his class and he really cares about the subjects. As long as you follow directions and do the homework, he grades pretty easily. I am taking a second class with him and I would suggest him to anyone who really wants to learn something.
Professor Sabino is an amazing instructor. If you show up to class and participate in his class you will be good. He is not a bad grader just put in the work and you will pass the class just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: So finicky. Craft your every discussion post meticulously and make them half-page long or you will lose point! Vague directions and you have no idea why he is grading stuff that way. One word, picky.
A lot of writing but very rewarding! She clearly puts so much time into preparing lectures and grading papers. I got a lot out of this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gives 3 assignments each week with readings. She makes you pay $80 for a textbook she wrote, embedded in a different program, not Carmen. Gives clear instructions but even if you follow she takes points off. One of the weekly assignments is consistently a 3-7 page paper. Only benefit is 100 free points in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Thoroughly enjoyed this class and the professor. She was very helpful and had great communication, and returned grades in about a week. Left wonderful and encouraging comments on all assignments, and provided an abundance of resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. VanGundy was great! Be ready to think critically and apply many concepts to papers and exams. She lets you think for yourself and gives little to no instructions when writing papers. She grades easily, as long as you apply everything discussed in class. She is super inspiring and smart, and it is definitely reflected in the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Van Gundy is one of the best professors I have had at Ohio State. There were few assignments that held most of your grade; however, if you attend lecture and put in effort toward your responses, you'll be fine. It is a level 4000 course.

I would not recommend her. In lecture she often criticized our class stating we were one of her lowest grades and would make us feel like we were the problem. There were only five grades the entire semester which were two reflection papers, one legal analysis, a midterm, and a final. The exams were four questions, written, and worth 200 points.

Tough grader. Midterm was multiple choice/true false but very misleading questions (average 65%). Final exam was 4 written response questions (each 2 pages in length) + a final 5-7 page paper (both worth 200 points each). Takes a long time to grade. Not a terrible professor but definitely would not take a class with her again.

Professor Van Gundy is one of the best professors I've taken at OSU. She's very passionate about the topics she's teaching (I took gender & crime class.) Her lectures are intriguing and not boring at all. There are only four graded assignments in the class, but they're not bad.

This class is horribly weighted and the exams are very unrealistic. He gives extremely little time to complete multiple problems that very well take over 10 minutes to complete each, making it impossible to even finish an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely hard to follow. Stopped going to class.

Yiyu is a chill guy but it's evident he's new to teaching. I can't blame him for this but it's what's holding me back from me actually learning. Also the exams  make or break your grade so make sure to study for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lack of examples for the concepts. Lecture are mainly just copy and paste the text book. But passion for teaching. Overall not a bad lecturer but need some improvement.

Not a bad lecturer, but way too fast and need to be supplemented. He copies the textbook as notes. I self studied the whole 1st and 2nd midterm because he does not teach concepts at all. Also harsh grading, 80% is exams with relatively small curve. He gives very little time for exams too.
Taught directly from the textbook and provided little to no examples for complex theories. Exams were also worth a total of 80% of the grade making the homework seem useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm pretty sure he's fresh out of grad school, but I don't know. He rushes like crazy during lectures, and his accent makes him hard to understand, so you'll find yourself sometimes walking out having learned nothing. Tests are weighted very heavily, 20% per midterm (2 of them) and the final is worth 40%. He doesn't explain concepts well also.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall pretty easy A if you put in some effort. Not a super hard class, it just requires a big time commitment for the final and midterm. Lot of extra credit, pretty easy class if you're willing to devote time to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Vlad is honestly a really good professor. One of the POLISCI profs that you can't tell off bat political standings (more right). Guest speakers were pretty ehn. Take home exams take up HOURSSSS. very time consuming and TAs grade them. pretty accessible. participation gives EC so either that or office hours will help buffer grade. MC exams cake.

If you want to talk about voting and gerrymandering for 16 weeks take this class Take home exams are incredibly time-consuming and difficult. Attendance is not mandatory but you lose so many participation points if you don't go, so you have too. He's a nice guy i guess but wouldn't take his classes again

This class is not hard, it's just time consuming. The only difficult part is the written midterm & final, which took me about a full 3 days to complete each. The grade criteria is very clear, it's just so many parts and a lot of combing thru long readings to complete. The MCQ is incredibly easy, the debate was brownie pts, and quizzes were simple.

Prof Kogan is very engaging and passionate! The midterm and final exams are difficult but if you attend class regularly and complete the daily readings it should not be difficult to do well. Loved this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best professor I've taken classes with. I recommend his classes to all my non political science friends because they're interesting. Midterm and finals are more work than average class but if you have a brain and listen in class you will do very well. Can't recommend him enough

Very biased professor who pushed his VERY right-wing political agenda in class and was rude & insulting if anyone had a different view or EVER questioned him. I studied hard, but exams are next to impossible. Never responds to email for weeks. He basically refused to meet for office hours. Kogan should never be a teacher.
Kogan is an amazing professor. He is the most organized and knowledgeable professor I've ever had. He genuinely cares about the content and the students.

I absolutely loved his Law & Politics course. He provides so many opportunities for extra credit (just raising your hand) that your grade is a reflection of your effort. Daily reading quizzes aren't hard, very engaging lectures, and exams you can easily do well on. He gives real advice to students; every PoliSci major should take this course!

I'm not sure why others rated him so low... the majority of negative reviews are downright inaccurate evaluations. Kogan BY FAR is one of the best polisci professors at OSU with his extremely interesting and engaging lectures, great class structure (debate + guest speakers), and relevant reading assignments. He's knowledgeable and passionate!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I would not say he is a terrible teacher, he is not that bad but I wold say  pay attention and  make sure you understand because emailing him asking questions are not going to help. emailing him for help is a no go unless its a question about attendence or something along those line but question about midterms or final HE IS NOT HELPFUL.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice guy, interesting lectures, responds fast to emails, easy grader. Tons of extra credit and you can tell he wants you to do well. Midterm and final mcq is all from reading quizzes which are easy. Writing part of the midterm/final is long so start asap. 1 group project that you present in front of the class but grading is lax so don't stress

One of the best classes I have taken at OSU. The content was really interesting. This class has tons of extra credit. It is honestly really hard to get a bad grade. He had take home exams which he gave us two weeks to work on. He would also have multiple choice portions of the exams for which he would give us all the possible questions beforehand!

THE EXAMS ARE EASY: Multiple choice is a free 50%, and if you attempt each item on the rubric for the essay, you will receive another 25%.

Each time you participate in class or attend office hours, you receive one point of EXTRA CREDIT.

Best to go to office hours with a clear ask, he's hard to talk to.

Nobody understands politics better.
He literally might not be real.

Kogan is one of the most organized and intelligent professors I've taken thus far. It is fairly easy if you are interested in the material and do all of the daily readings. Exams are lengthy and tough but applicable and useful. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I realized why he offers so much extra credit in class. He does in-class quizzes on Top Hat but manipulated the syllabus so that even if you have a valid excuse for missing the quiz and want to make it up you can't. The four "dropped quizzes" that he offers are a fraud, and my grade dropped after missing only two from an A to a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The information was engaging at times and the lectures were organized. Attendance is taken along with reading quizzes at the beginning of each class which could either hurt or help your grade. The exams were easy. The take-home questions required an in-depth ability to apply the material. Every time you speak you get a participation point.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kogan is now of the most interesting and well-thought professors I have ever had. He is incredible knowledgeable and interested in his students success. The written exams are very long so make sure to start them early but he is a fairly gracious grader.
Spends all his time complaining online about unions and talking about how he deserves to make much more money than public school teachers.

Can't say enough good things about Kogan. Probably the most organized prof at OSU, responds in 2 minutes to emails, everything is very clear in syllabus. Can get extra cred for speaking in class, asks thought provoking questions. Exams are half take home, half online and aren't very hard. End of sem group project is engaging and fun. 10/10!

Very closed minded and hard to talk to. Some people just view themselves as too self important and he is one of them. You'll do well if you agree with him tho, just don't dare to have a differing opinion or outlook on a topic because MY GOD how dare you?!

Professor Kogan was the best professor I had during my time at OSU. He is really passionate about the subjects he lectures and keeps you engaged. His involvement in local politics and the examples he provides in class from his advocacy efforts prove that he cares about what he is teaching. 10/10!

Professor Kogan is really kind and extremely intelligent. He makes lectures easy to understand and always keeps them interesting. The downside of taking his class was that the readings are not easy and attending class is a must (otherwise your grade drops). The exams are also challenging and you have to plan ahead of time before starting them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Vlad is a political scholar and is respected as such. You must show up to class everyday having read the assigned readings. Gives extra credit every time you go to office hours or participate in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Law & Politics class is a great option for anyone considering law school. There's lots of reading and exams (take home) take a few days to complete. This class is a lot of work but there are so many points available that you can miss a day or fail a quiz & get points elsewhere. It'll help you decide if law school is for you or not!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This man kogan is a absolute mad man do not take his class and Im saying this with a B. His group projects in a online setting is so stressful it feels like a dream thats how bad it is, his take home portion of exams are extremely long so do not try and do it the day before its due. Absolute nightmare and he does not care.

Super unaccommodating. I am in his class in the midst of the Covid-19 outbreak and somehow the class has gotten more annoying. He has a group project with 9 people so its impossible to meet and he doesn't give class time to do so and hasn' canceled it. There have also been at least 4 assignments not on the syllabus at all that he expects you to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is unaccomodating. He has a clear class structure--great, but if you miss class, he refuses to let you make it up. Even for excused absences. Participation IS graded. Every single class. His "take-home" exam takes 7 hours to complete. If you miss tophat by 5 seconds he will not let you make it up. Dreaded going to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor is not understanding of outside circumstances that may require you to miss class, even if its excused. Participation is graded in a large lecture and if you miss Tophat he will not let you make it up. How to do the take home exams were not something ever taught in class and would only loosely apply to lectures.

Vlad has teaching down to a science. The course is a lot of work but if you do it all you should have no problem getting an A. He takes so many grades that its easy to bounce back if you do poorly on the reading quizzes. Participation is extra credit. Exams are takehome, a lot of work, but if you follow the rubric you'll get an A. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Vlad is a great professor. His course requires a decent amount of work, but it's very interesting. Some units were more stimulating than others , though. It's also worth noting that a lot of extra credit is given out. Overall, I would highly recommend this course.

Professor Kogan does not care about his students. He refuses to give students with disabilities accommodations. I would not take this class again. I am doing well in the class, but the lack of respect for students, especially students with disabilities, is discouraging and makes succeeding in the class difficult. Course content is interesting.

Although I have not yet completed the entire course, Professor Kogan's "Governing Urban America" is the best class I have taken at OSU. The class is straightforward. As long as you put in the effort, you will undoubtedly succeed. The lectures are highly informative and sometimes comedic. It is clear he loves to teach this class. Take this class!

One of the best classes I've taken at OSU. Participation and attendance matter for your grade. Class is very structured with reading quizzes (which you can do online) and a group project. He uses a lot of videos to aid his lectures, which I found helpful. Overall Vlad Kogan is a very good, straightforward teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kogan gives you a solid, no nonsense class. He is very smart, has interesting lectures, and his expectations are very clear. As long as you show up every day and pay attention you can easily get an A. Class is easy if you do everything, reading quizzes every day make up 25% of our grade and participation is another 20 so don't skip consistently
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really loved this class! Would highly recommend going on the police ride along. gives a lot of extra credit and tests are taken online
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Kogan is a clear grader and an overall solid lecturer. Although the attendances are not mandatory, it is in your best interest to attend as many of the lectures as possible because they can give you a clearer view and a better understanding on the course material which are mainly cases that will be a huge part on the midterm and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class is fine, but his methods for grading attendance are draconian. If you miss just a couple of days (as in you don't do the online participation portions that correspond to the class) it can drop you a letter grade. Otherwise easy.

Very organized, which can't be said of a lot of professors. Have to read because of daily quizzes and participation on Top Hat. Midterm and Final are take-home and not graded harshly. Debate and legal brief at the end are a bit overhwhelming. If you go to class and ready, you should do well with him. Good class for those thinking about law school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think he's fairly straightforward as a professor. There's a lot of reading in this class and the take-home questions for the mid-term and final are time consuming, but the class intellectually is definitely worth it and he presents the material in a clear, structured way. Participation and reading quizzes are the key to doing really well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Reading quizzes every class, but once you get used to how he quizzes you they're a piece of cake. One group project that isn't too intense. Participation is a huge part of your grade, and the more you participate the more bonus you get. Exams take some time but they're not graded too hard. Interesting class and Vlad is a cool guy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kogan is an awesome professor and class is always interesting. Do the readings and go to class and you'll be fine. Not to mention, he is fine as well so take the class.

Vlad is a great professor. I took both 4130 and 4127, and if I had time, I would have taken State Politics as well. Attendance and participation does matter. The reading isn't excessive, but it is required for the daily quizzes. Read the material, participate in class, and you'll do well. Among my most memorable professors at OSU.
Do not take if you are a student athlete, his participation and grading policies are very clear. If you don't come to every class, you might as well chop 5% off your grade.

Great professor. Attempts to not only add relevant multi-media content to each class but he also gives students the opportunity to network with Columbus community members relevant to the course. You'll have to work hard, especially on written portions of exams, but steady preparation should allow even the laziest student to get a "B" or higher.
He is a terrible teacher. Worst class ever taken!

Vlad is a pretty cool guy, and I felt he gave great lectures. The daily reading quizzes are super easy SO LONG AS you do all the readings. The midterm and Final each have 2 parts: take home responses and in class multiple choice. You're given all the questions for the m.c. ahead of time. The take home portion take a decent amount of effort though.
Professor Kogan is a great professor. Lectures are very interesting and as long as you pay attention in class and do the readings this class is an easy A.

This class is not THAT difficult if you put the time in. You have to go to every class, there are daily reading quizzes. The reading quizzes aren't that hard, they're just tedious. But 50% of your grade is condensed in the last two weeks: group debate, ten page legal brief, take home questions for the final, & the final. Overwhelming in the end.

This was an interesting course to say the least. Professor Kogan is enthusiastic about teaching students and also immerses you into the subject material. He is teaching at an entirely new level at OSU. He plays videos and has guest speakers, lectures are never boring. There are daily quizzes though so don't miss any days!

he was okay. A lot of reading with online lecture videos. you have quizzes at the beginning of class. watch movie for 2 hours and then last hour is set aside for discussion questions. I think they should have another teacher for politics in film in tv. His idea of having a meaningful discussion concerning politics is dry. Overall, not hard to get A

Way too much reading! There are daily reading quizzes as well as specific questions on reading in midterms and final. Very dry material and oftentimes seemed to have nothing to do with the course. Expectations for the 5 papers required in the course did not match up with what was taught in class. Professor is rude and unhelpful.

Dr. Kogan was extremely unhelpful and unclear. His notes were not straight forward and his expectations were not consistent with the subject material. Do not recommend taking this course. Found Kogan very rude and unwilling to help students.

Kogan is by far my  favorite political science teacher that I have had at OSU. His classes are extremely organized, he is very clear as to what he expects on assignments. He answers emails almost immediately, and the workload is extremely manageable. His material is highly compelling and as long as you remain diligent, you will be successful.

Professor Kogan really gets a bad rap. He is a very nice guy who recognizes students who do the work. Skim the readings for the jist of it and highlight quotes to use for the writing exams and you will be fine. All exams were take home essays that were under 5 pages and one massive paper that wasn't really too bad.
Interesting class. Midterm and Final are not easy and his grading is harsh on exams. Projects are interesting and not hard. He brings in city officials to talk to class...overall good class.

The majority of this class was spent in dreadfully dull lectures, the man has a genuine interest in the content but the way he communicates it is very dry.  The class requires 2 books which would be useless if not for the midterms and the finals which are graded primarily on stuffing the papers with quotes. The class is good but he isn't.

State politics can be a bit dry, but Professor Kogan conveyed the information in an engaging way & was open to feedback. Material was well organized. Readings required for the take home essays, but the lectures really helped to clarify readings. Possible to earn extra credit. The assignments were reasonable and grading fair. An overall good course.

Dr Kogan lectured for most of the class and encouraged discussion for the end of class--participation was required. He is young and inexperienced as a professor but he is very helpful. His grading is fair, and he offers a good amount of extra credit. I found his lectures to be interesting and engaging.

As a political science student, this was the 8th political science class I took at OSU. It was by far the worst of them all. He is not clear on what he wants from students on assignments, and grades harshly. I  have never appealed a grade in my entire college career but appealed every one in this class. I would avoid any class with this guy.

Extremely tough grader for not expressing expectations. Attendance/participation mandatory. Reading incomprehensibly difficult in large quantities. Teaches/grades like it's a grad school class. The dept. had to come in & whole class expressed dissatisfaction. Take-home midterm & final is a paper, which sounds easy but is NOT. AVOID at all costs!
My favorite professor of my collegiate experience. Talk's about useful, current information and gives general advice he has learned and experienced.

Of my 4 years at Ohio State this has been my favorite class. Prof. West is the most relatable professor I've had. In each class, we talk about the stock market's current situation(s). Mr. West has provided advice that I've taken to heart. The exams and were easy if you went over the slides. I recommend taking investments with Prof. West

The assignments always go ahead of the lectures. We need to figure out how to solve the problem by ourselves.  It is a self-study course!!!! If the homework is not used to consolidate the knowledge learned, I don't know what its score can represent in this class.

Great guy, but terrible delivery of the material and did not explain things very well or in depth. His tests were extremely hard and pulled mainly from material outside of class. We did not cover how to do about 20-25 questions (out of 50 questions) on the final. It seems like he was kinda winging the whole class the whole semester. WOULD NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I have ever had. Took the time to make sure you understood the topics. Helped you understand what was going on in the market and how to evaluate stocks. Highly recommend taking this teacher.

really nice guy but does not know how to teach. He was all over the place with his lectures. He would tell use things would not be on the quiz, then they would still should up on the quiz. Quizzes and exams were super hard. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.
It's not necessarily an easy A. You definitely have to keep up with assignments and study, but if you participate in class, you'll do well. She also had the best outfits.
excellent, kind and compassionate

Professor Willging was very kind and passionate about what she does. She is easy to understand and learn from in class and creates an environment conducive to learning, however, for being a 2101 class it was HARD. There were many people in my class who were fluent in French and still found that their papers and quizzes were graded too harshly.

Heavy work load out of class. Especially for a three credit hour class that most people are taking for a GE credit. Extremely long readings that are never discussed. Do NOT recommend taking this class. She is a nice person overall, but a terrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Willging is  very nice and clearly cares about what she does. That being said, she relies heavily on the textbook which seemed to have no real information other than short stories and poems in french. I did not feel I really learned all that much, and I found her class to be kind of boring. She also cold calls on people, which sucks.

Prof Willging challenges her students, but she is extremely fair. You will learn a lot from her class if you put in the time and effort, but it's not unreasonable. Yes, this is upper division French, you have to speak in class, but if you speak 1 or 2 x per class and have good attendance, you will get an A. She is kind and funny. Loved her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Willging clearly cares about her students and does her best to improve their learning experience and performance in class! Participation is important in this class, but she's very kind and helps you feel comfortable answering questions and speaking. She also gives a good mixture of grammar, reading, and discussions for assignments.

Prof. Willging is the kindest professor I've had at OSU. She's always willing to explain difficult topics and she presents the material in a way that makes it fun. Exams are pretty straightforward and essays are graded fairly. Participation matters, but I have no complaints.

Dr. Willging is amazing and her lectures were really helpful and funny. She's a joy to be around. There's vocab and reading quizzes every now and then, but if you pay attention in class and do the review sheet, you'll do well. She doesn't grade too hard on the essays.

I love Mme Willging. I had a one on one with her and she let me vent to her. She is relatable and understands her students. She really loves her job as well. She is challenging but you CAN do well if you study. You MUST participate in class and take notes, she sees all. Very down to earth and knowledgable. You will learn a lot.

If you want an A in this class you have to put in the effort; read the book, write the papers, study for the quizzes. Graded on papers, quizzes and participation along with two group projects. Not a terribly hard class, but stay up to date and you'll be fine. She really does care about her students and makes the class interesting with discussion.

Dr. Willging was the best French professor I've had at OSU. The readings assigned in her course were difficult, and took quite a while to get through, but everything you needed to know for the tests was discussed in class. Exams were extremely fair and she always respected your opinion, as long as you could support it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Willging is the best.  She teaches excellently.  She is chair of the department, and does a great job.

She is a very professional woman and its clear she is good at her job. She is good-natured and very kind to students, but definitely challenges you. She is very helpful in all her feedback and really cares to make you better. she is direct and even when she is talking about abstract things, she does her best to make things clear.

She's not an easy A. I ended up barely ever doing the readings and getting by. There's a class discussion on them every class. The tests are kind of hard even with the review. I always got a B or C on them and I studied. If you're talkative this will get you far. You have to write 2 papers. She's a good prof and she's patient with everyone.

You have to talk in this class or else you'll get a horrible participation grade. It doesn't matter if you understand what everyone else is saying, you take notes, etc. You'll get no participation grade. YOU HAVE TO TALK! It's stupid. Plus her exams are hard. You really have to study for them. She thinks she's an amazing lecturer, but she's not.

I do not like this professor's methods. She is more interested in style than substance, in terms of writing. Discussions are very superficial and she expects people to know stuff that is never explained clearly. Expectations are not well outlined. Not particularly tough grader, but picky about little insignificant things. Didn't learn from her.

Prof. Willging is great. She does a good job of trying to break down complex ideas for beginners. She's also quite patient considering that she has to repeat herself a lot. I don't want to linger too much on comments about her appearance but she dresses very well, her style is nice.
I've had several grad classes with her. She's the best thing since sliced bread. And hot.
Dr. Willging was an extremely enthusiastic teacher and very patient with this intermediate-level French class.

Loved her and her class. She is genuinely interested in helping students. If you attend class and listen, her tests require little studying. She makes material relevant and interesting. Favorite professor I've had at OSU.
Great teacher, I feel like I've learned a lot from her.  Can be tough but is still fair and understanding.
Prof Willging is a great teacher, and shes super chic!
Tough, but if you give a damn or try at all, she's there for you.

Loved her class.  She was easy to understand and made lectures fun.  A lot of reading was required, but the subject matter was generally really interesting.  Tests and quizzes weren't too hard. Overall, she's a great professor, and I'd really recommend taking a class with her!

Such a great teacher. Even if you go in to the class hating French, you'll come out with at least a better appreciation for the language. She makes learning about a language interesting, and she has an amazing ability of keeping the students engaged. I definitely reccomend her!
Excellent class with hard but very rewarding books.  Definately worth taking classes from her no matter whether you are a beginner or a grad student.
she really knows her stuff
I love her!  She is one of the best professors I have had at OSU.  She's tough but fair and if you work in class you'll do fine.  I completely loved her class.

I thought this class was hard, but am I ever glad I took it! She's a very cool(& SMART) lady who helps kids who want to help themselves. She covered topics that were really interesting. Whether you want to or not, you will learn something from this prof.
She is so sweet and loves to teach.  By the end of this class I could read French soo much better!
Prof Willging is smart, funny, and can analyze literature like there's no tomorrow.  Plus she's a babe.  Learn French just so you can take her classes!
He very focus your attendance.
dont choose him

This class covered many topics in traditional Chinese culture. Professor delivered the lectures very well. He gave out plenty of bonus opportunities toward the end of the semester. But his frequent cold calling in class sometimes created an anxious atmosphere. Easy A for me.

Xie laoshi is a great lecturer. He's funny, takes questions/comments well and makes you feel smart every time you talk. Class is long but he makes it enjoyable. Biggest thing is to do the readings, because the quizzes are rough and will hit your grade hard. Very fair on all other assignments. Lectures don't cover the readings, you have to know both
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nothing but easy A. Sometimes I don't think he understanding what he said by himself. Go to class, read Powerpoint, finish homework, that's all.

All tests and quizzes are open note so you don't really have to actually read, midterm was take home too. Class itself is pretty boring and I did other HW during class, you have to go because he grades participation/attendance, and you only have 2 skips. Unless you're super into Chinese culture I wouldn't take this as a GE unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Xie Laoshi was a really good teacher. I learned a lot from his class and the work was very very easy. Everything is open notes!

Professor Xie is very nice, engaging, sometimes humorous. He is willing to share his own personal experience in relation to Chinese culture. Attendance is taken every class,  but he is generous in other grading and gives a lot of bonus opportunities. I feel I learned quite a lot about things I did not know or understand.

If you can understand each syllabus he utters, then his English is excellent. I showed up to every single lecture, which was 1 hr and 20 min long and he gave me 14/15 participation pts, but a mere 12 hrs later... it was changed to a 13.5! o.o Anyway, I got an A. Super GPA booster class: take home midterm + open notes final. Generous guys he is.

Xie laoshi was great! He had a hard time sometimes explaining things bc English isn't his first language, however, he always did what he could to make sure you understood. Extremely nice guy, gave us candy on Valentines day and Chinese New Year, I hope I can take another one of his classes.
Class was super easy. Sometimes interesting, sometimes boring. Mid-term is open book and notes. No final. I don't speak any Chinese and I easily got an A in the course.

The low reviews from other students seem to be from very long ago, but she is an amazing professor! Her lectures are very clear and insightful, and she doesn't hesitate to reexplain certain concepts to ensure everyone understands them. Lectures are recorded and posted online alongside her notes. Lectures prepare you well for the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy A course. Online lectures. No attendance

Not sure why some people rate her a 1. She's a decent and pretty nice teacher. Her handwriting is ok, and she explains the material again if people are confused in the chat. There are also office hours after class. The exams are quite similar to the notes examples, with few homework assignments throughout the semester. An easy A class.

Easy A, but I felt like we spent too much time at the beginning of the semester and were in a hurry of catching up in the second half of the semester. Homeworks are a bit harder than in class materials but aren't too bad. She's very willing to repeat concepts to make sure people get it. Exams are easy and fair.

Great professor! Her lectures are very clear, and I constantly would use her lectures after class at 2x speed. Very good at explaining things in detail, and she constantly goes over information multiple times to help you truly understand your material. Do feel that I have a much better understanding of ECE basics, even though it's not my major.

Idk why her other reviews are this low, but I really liked this class and thought Professor Zhang was a great lecturer. Her lectures were easy to follow and her exams were also very fair and often followed in-class examples. She was great at answering questions even though the class was on Zoom and there were 100+ people in the call.
Easy A. Clear lecture and notes. Awesome professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was very clear and very nice. Her notes were also very clear and she was a great professor
Great professor

I really don't understand why her ratings are so low. Her lectures were very clear, to the point, easy to follow, and easy to understand. The homework was just a slightly harder versions of the exact problems we did in lecture. The homework lined up with the lectures perfectly, and her exams were very fair and easier than the homework. Great prof.

I have NO idea why her ratings here are so low; she is good at teaching (i never had to learn anything from the textbook), is a genuinely nice person, and has trivially easy and open-note exams. the homework is pretty much just tweaked lecture examples. she has an accent but i can understand it just fine at >1.5x speed despite my hearing issues.

Professor does not provide a letter grade towards what percentage the student has in the class. She answers questions when they are asked and answers them fairly well. She does not allow for late assignments, and the course is a bit fast. The material is not bad, just lots and lots of work. She is unfair with grading and late to email responses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unsure how these reviews are so low. One of the best professors I've had. She is a VP of IEEE Circuits and Systems. She explains very clearly, knows how to answer every question regardless of wording, and offers plenty of opportunities for questions. She shares various experiences in industry, providing ideas on real application of the material.

Talks very fast and doesn't answer questions directly. The homework is ambiguously worded and she only answers homework questions with "its in the notes". Also the only class I'm in where homework is due at the start of class and not midnight which throws students off.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was here first time teaching this class. I feel that compared to other classes reviewed, she enjoys this one more. She follows the book closely but will provide interesting and relevant examples when questions are asked. A large chunk of the grade comes from a free form project which I enjoyed. Provides plenty of examples. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Although I learned the material for this class well, the grading seemed pretty unfair. There was no curve, the TAs were awful, the textbook wasn't great, and she had no office hours. I worked hard in this class but felt constantly ripped off for tiny mistakes on exams. I also get the impression that she doesn't care about students at all.

She was not the best professor, although some students here are harsh. The exams were somewhat fair, although I feel as if most of the content was only briefly brushed over after the first midterm and not explained in detail. You need to refer to the textbook (which is not good either) to do homework and to supplement learning.

The class is easy and interesting, however, the instructor can make the class boring, and hard to understand. If you can study on your own, this class would be easy, else it would be a hell. Overall, AVOID her if you can, or study yourself. There are better instructors for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: All I have to say is, really Ohio State? Don't bother going to class and If you take the class online, don't bother watching the online videos. Everything I learned was straight from the textbook, and her lectures pretty much are a text-to-speech of the text. Not to mention the lectures don't line up the homework. Bring back Mac Ohio State, pls.

I should be studying for this class's final, but here I am rating this class. I didn't learn a thing form her, and probably going to get D in otherwise easy class. She is not interested in helping students, and is hard to follow. She is not fit to teach, and rating of 1 is me being generous, since I cannot rate her 0 here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This is the worst lecturer in the history of school!!!! I dont know what she is saying 99% of the time. Im sitting here crying because I dont know any material for the final since this professor hasnt helped us one bit. No office hours (always cancels), never responds to emails, shame on you ECE dept! Shame on you! RIP my GPA.
Great prof, cares about her students, and puts emphasis on learning over memorization. Would take again!

She is extremely smart, but not very good at conveying the content. The course was laid out and structured well. I think she must be new at teaching because she would get flustered at times when a student would ask a question. Her accent is also extremely strong and created a barrier to understanding.

New at teaching. She has good intention and wants everyone to learn but sometimes the way she taught wasn't very clear. Very accessible outside class and willing to help. Large curve, helpful review session and could bring many cheat sheets to exam. Remember to really review your linear algebra and probability before any AI courses.

Professor is a great guy, who genuinely cares about the students. He showed he respected the effort we put in. His lectures were useful but very text and slides heavy, and he can be hard to understand at times. Exams were very hard and all conceptual until the final, but he gave us chances to prove we learned from our mistakes and get points back.

Professor Liu is a wonderful professor to have--he takes great interest in his teaching. He responds to emails almost immediately and answers questions very well. The Midterms and Final are worth a combined 90% toward the final grade, but he curves them extensively. Beware of conceptual questions, which occupy the majority of the exams!

Professor is very nice in person and cares about student's success, but midterms and final are impossible and worth 90% of the grade. The questions are all conceptual so no partial credit and very easy to get low grades.

The professor is a good person, but his teaching style is not good. He uses slides to teach mathematics, which feels like memorising rather than understanding. His midterms contain concept questions only; no mathematical questions at all. Everyone in the class did horrendously, and he had to do a curve, which is not a rule for this course.

He's not a bad person and his lectures aren't that bad, but his midterms (worth 20% of our grade each) are completely multiple choice and true/false. The high on our midterm was a B and the median was an F because of trick questions. If you need a high GPA for a scholarship, switch profs ASAP because the HW does not prep you for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attention is all you need!

NOT AN EASY A! but felt very fair - exams were very similar to the homework and during office hours+on piazza he basically walks through hw/exam questions if you ask. have an open mind - comes off as really intimidating at first but he cares about his students and puts in the effort towards being a good teacher, it just looks diff from other profs

Dr. Zhang is a passionate and proficient Professor who is fair and thorough with grading and teaching. The class content is difficult, but his lectures are highly informative. Lecture is intimidating at first but he only calls on students who raise their hand, so there's nothing to fear. One critique is sometimes his questions in class are unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is brilliant in his field, having won numerous awards. However, his teaching style often leaves people struggling. He primarily reads from the slides and says not to memorize much, yet you're expected to know everything on them. It's an exam-heavy class, and the grading is very strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're not religious, pick a religion and start praying.

Makes an already boring and tough subject unnecessarily worse. Tough grader who insists on students memorizing specific things he reads straight from the slides but maintains that tests are "basic concepts only" and "no memorization." Simply another professor who is not capable of teaching his knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dry lectures, doesn't care about students, doesn't care to listen to any views that don't align with his. Avoid.

As someone who took this class after reading this page, I was terrified. I don't feel that the grade accurately reflects his teaching, but more so the 3421 content itself. He tries his best to make all of the content inside of computer architecture as accessible as possible and does his best to give real world examples. Office hours help a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang makes computer architecture seem not as boring as it actually is in his lectures which is nice. His exams are also heavily based on the homework so as long as you do the homework and attend class when it's haded back you're golden. The fact that he takes attendance only when he hands back homework is lame though, so make sure you show up.

Don't skip his lectures, a lot of the content on the exams is based on in class discussion and examples, and when he hands back homework (which you can only turn in on paper...for a cse class) is the only time he will go over the answers. The exams are largely based on the problems in the hw, along with a lot of concepts. Very tough but fair.

Hard to understand but very smart. The material is incredibly dry and it wont get any better. If you take him and sys2 at the same time make sure your sys2 professor is good cause it's practically the same material. YOU HAVE TO ATTEND CLASS. If you don't you wont be able to hand in hw find out the answers to hw, find out what you got wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think his rating is a little misguided. His lectures are dry, its a computer architecture course, no one is going to make the material interesting, but he does a good job making comparisons to real-world examples. His class is very exam heavy, but they were pretty fair as long as you follow the slides/homework. He also does not give good feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is a big language barrier between myself and the professor. His lectures lack appropriate English grammar which makes it even harder to study or recap material. While the professor himself seems very knowledgeable on the subject, he is not very accessible outside class. His homework assignments aren't extremely difficult but are hard to grasp
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HIs lectures are incredibly dry, and while he tries to use analogies to real world scenarios this doesn't help. Homework is graded without any feedback, with only a number being posted, which isn't helpful in understanding the content. He refuses to give 100's on the exams, and hasn't posted the final because the distribution is likely awful. Avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor requires attendance and does not post solutions to homework online, even if you are out for a legitimate reason. Exams aren't terrible but it is hard to focus on lectures. Attending office hours can be helpful but, he is very busy to scheduling office hours outside of his one hour each week is difficult.

Dry Lectures, very unorganized slides, all the lectures are basically a review session. Always says every topic is a review of System 1&2. Very rude, never posts the grades on time. Requires everything turned-in during in-person class and answer keys are not posted online all due to the reason that "this is not an internet class".

Terrible slides. Terrible lectures. Everything is "review". Does not accept digital submissions because "this is not an internet class". Does not post homework keys. Very little material to study. I learn more going through old computer architecture PowerPoints on the internet than I do from going to lecture. I leave class everyday discouraged.

This class was horrific. He seems like someone who is very knowledgeable in the subject, but an absolutely terrible teacher. All he does is read off his slides (which are very poorly organized). He is very rude and posted barely any information on the course page (including the dates of exams) with the reasoning of "this is not an internet class."
Organized notes that are easy to understand, useful midterm reviews, always replies her emails and homeworks are similar to her exams. Super nice person overall! (gave us candy for halloween too)
Dr. Li makes diffeq a breeze. Graded off of weekly homework and exams which look exactly like the homework she may be the best professor the OSU math department has ever seen

I had Professor Li for 2177 but its not here but she is genuinely the best professor Ive had her lectures are very organized and she explains topics really well and if you dont understand her topics she is willing to help after class. Her exams are also very similar to homework problems which makes it easier and just all around a great professor

Professor Li is amazing for Diff EQ. She's very patient, answers q's simply & makes effort to remember everyone's name. Homework's are simple as are the exams (closely relate).Notes are very easy to follow & will slow down if the class does not understand. Strongly recommend office hours if stuck, she walks through an entire problem if you need it.

She is extremely kind and always explains topics clearly. The exams match pretty much exactly what was done in class and arguably easier than the homeworks, so as long as you put some work in you'll get a good grade. She is honestly the best math professor at OSU that I have taken so far and I highly recommend her.

Dr. Li is incredibly knowledgeable and patient with students. The grade is based on weekly homework, 3 midterm exams, and a final exam, and she always reviews before exams. She explains the material well and genuinely cares about students' understanding. She also answers emails quickly and extends office hours. Amazing professor for Diff Eq!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very kind professor, extremely organized. Everything was thoroughly planned and lectures always made sense and were very clear. Numerous midterms and weekly graded homework gave a nice cushion. Good review guides provided. Really good for OSU math.

Very compassionate professor and a good lecturer. She remembers names, has prizes for participation, always stays after class to answer questions, and answers emails quickly. Only 1 homework assignment a week and the 3 lowest scores are dropped. Very lenient grader. I would recommend anyone who is interested in taking MATH 2415 to take her class.
Very nice teacher, patiently answer all the questions after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr.Wu last semester and thought he was ok. His lecture notes he provided were pretty helpful, however I felt like he gave little material outside of class unlike many other professors I have heard. Overall I would take him again, however it definitely was a bit of work outside of class to get a good grade.

Overall Dr. Wu was a good professor. His lectures were easy to understand, and while somewhat boring, he covered the material well. He also did demos occasionally to break up the lectures. He did a lot of practice questions during class and you submitted your answers. His practice tests were a good reflection of the exams. The textbook was helpful.

wasnt bad but he didnt explain things the best and i had to do a lottttttt more work outside of class bc the lectures werent helpful but the textbook and supplemental lectures were very helpful for exams
Very clear that he cares about his students but was hard to understand at times. I needed suplemental material to get through the class.
Professor Wu is a great professor. If you attend his office hours and do the homework on time and keep up on the studying, its an easy A. He is very helpful in explaining in his office hours.

Great professor who gives you a good foundation for studying for the exams. Do the practice tests and the exams should not be that hard. Does fun experiments in lecture sometimes and is very kind. Not very hard to understand unlike what some of the other reviews say.
Was a bit hard to understand his accent and he talks quiet

I genuinely hated this class. I'm already not good at chemistry but every time I walked into the lecture I got even more confused. I definitely would choose another professor if you could, I cried multiple times over this class.

He was super sweet and answered our questions. He's available outside of class, and he answers emails in minutes. The exams are made by the whole chem program so if you think it's hard it'll be hard with any prof. Lectures may be boring but they're easy.

The lectures are very boring but do include all the required information for exams. The exams are not too hard but can't really get partial credit because of them being fully multiple choice. All homework is due at the end of the semester so you can work at your own pace.

Dr. Wu is a very caring guy and knows what he is talking about. I found the lectures helpful to get an overview of the topics, but I stuck with the textbook to fully understand it. He is a genuine guy and enjoys what he does, which has a positive effect on the students. While some concepts may be in the gray zone of teaching, he is still the goat.

I was intimidated at first because of his reviews, but he cares about his students, is very kind, he takes lecture slow, and sometimes he has to speed up because that's the class speed, but he always reviews with us, provides extra practice, homework is due at the last week of the semester, and he's always so sweet. I love Professor Wu!
Overall, great professor and I didn't really struggle in his class. I had to study less outside of his class because although boring, his lectures were phenomenal and thorough.

Very lecture heavy. Attendance not required. He cares very much about his students, but couldn't always answer questions. Not the best prof., but not the worst. Better off independently studying/reading the textbook.
Hard to understand and isn't very good at explaining things. He does care about his students though. Try to get a different prof. if you can.
Does not engage with students very well and often fails to explain mathematical topics well.

While this course is difficult, Dr. Wu was a pretty okay professor. He was always very nice and tried to engage with students, but doesn't do the best job teaching material and being thorough. His lectures are kind of vague, so I do recommend reading the textbook before lectures. Not the best chemistry professor, but certainly not the worst.

Dr. Wu is a great person, and brings his kind energy to the lectures. However, he is not the greatest teacher. I would not take his class again. He knows chemistry, but does not teach it to a group very well. I find that he does not show the simplest way to do a problem, and when someone has a question, he has a difficult time answering.

He is a great teacher. Although his class is boring, he tries to engage with students by providing demos and class participation questions. He is a very nice person, and he has office hours every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at least for the fall semester. I am bad at Chemistry, so I go to his office hour every week. He is patient with students.

Dr. Wu does a great job at explaining and breaking down very tough subject matter. His lectures can be a bit dry and boring, but he makes jokes and tries to keep students engaged. He also posted practice tests and held review sessions before exams, which were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu was an awesome professor and explained things in great detail and went over practice problems in class to further understand chemistry.

Not a great lecturer but allows lots of learning to be done with the homework which is made to give you high grades. Ended up learning a lot without the burden of heavy homework and weekly quizzes. Definitely puts in the effort to make sure his students succeed. Also skipped lectures a ton to sleep in which was worth it.

Pretty easy class. Didn't really show up after the second week and still got an a. The lectures that I went to were fairly interesting and helpful. Compared to other chem lecturers, he assigns minimal homework.

Dr. Wu himself is an awesome person, but I struggled in lectures and felt like I could have made better use of my time. I wasnt taught so much as told what I should go over by myself. The dynamic study modules saved me.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is a good person but not the best professor. I had to teach myself most of the material because the material covered in lectures is quite confusing and not explained thoroughly. Its like being told what your learning and not actually taught, leaving you to need to practice, read, and watch videos consistently to understand the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr. Wu as a person, not so much as a professor. Make sure that you seek extra help if you are not doing well, I should have done so sooner into the semester because this class was very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is the sixth-ranked materials scientist in the world. He is a very great professor. It may also be the first opportunity for us to get close to celebrities. He is very famous in China and is equivalent to Jackie Chan in the education world. I hope that everyone in his class will take the opportunity to communicate with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Taking CHEM1220 this semester, there is not a day that goes by that I don't miss Wu. I would say that my experience with him was amazing. He was very caring to his students during the COVID-19 time and would frequently give us breaks from recitation work. Doesn't know a lot of info about midterms/finals but is a phenomenal teacher nonetheless!

He doesnt give as many practice tests as other teachers. He didnt know much when it came to the midterms and what was on them. The practice tests from the chemistry department help a little. I would say overall he is harder than other teacher because he gives less opportunities to succeed. I would chose Dr. Fuss instead

Dr. Wu truly cares about his students and has a great depth of understanding of chemistry. The lecture portion of this class was entirely online because of COVID and I think that Dr. Wu was a great professor to have during this time. If you are willing to put in the time to understand the material, you have all the resources that you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: It's hard to put all of the blame for my hatred of chemistry on Dr. Wu, as it really isn't entirely his fault. The chem dept. at OSU aims to break students down and make them feel terrible to drop their majors. However, Dr. Wu is unapproachable and is not good at teaching a chem class to students who have likley never taken a college science class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid taking him if you can. Doesn't explain concepts in depth and asks hard questions. I have learned everything by myself. Lots of hw which is time consuming. Definitely read the book or you will hard time understanding things. Try to choose a good TA. Exams were similar to practice questions even though there were a few hard questions.
Dr. Wu is a great teacher and is very proficient when you assess his knowledge at office hours. He gives good notes however somethings are left out so you must read. Dont skip class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Yiying Wu is a fine professor. He communicates information how it ought to be. His lame jokes and mannerisms are quite adorable. Would take again
Hes very good at breaking things down. Highly recommend

Dr. Wu was a great lecturer and did a good job of explaining each concept in depth. However, he does assign a lot of homework (worth 7.5% of your grade) that takes up a significant amount of time. The material on his exams were very similar to the examples he explained during class. If I had to take another Chem course, I would take it with Dr. Wu
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I am horrible at Chemistry and still managed to get an A- so if I can do it.. you can do it. Not saying it was easy because it took a lot of time to understand the material and do practice problems. His practice exams are kind of similar to his exams and sometimes the practice problems you do in class will appear in the exams (with different #'s)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: First and foremost, the chem department at OSU is messed up. so no matter what don't expect too much. Dr. Wu is pretty much your average gen-chem-in-a-lecture-hall teacher. He's not incredible, but he's a smart guy. He's actually the easiest gen chem professor in terms of tests, but better teachers can get you better scores on harder tests.

He is a top guy. But whenever he comes to teach a gen chem class he talks about his battery research. Most of the time he brings couple of Duracell battery and he used to compare that with his one. He even told that the efficiency of his battery was 10  times better w.r.t  Duracell. He even claimed he can surpass the efficiency of Carnot cycle.

I really really love his teaching!!! Very good notes. It's better to attend every class because all those in class notes will help to get an A. Honestly, I do not read any chapter of book when I took his chem1210. Midterms are not tough but final is tricky. Be prepared of both lab and lecture notes when you take final.

He's very intelligent, but it was hard to get him to explain it in a way that I could understand. I asked for help and he basically explained it the same way again. Be prepared to work and ask for help often. The grading system isn't too bad in my opinion, the curve helped my grade. Also, labs can cushion your grade so pay attention and work hard.
Exams could be harder than expected but nothing impossible

Chem at OSU is really tough, but  I think Wu is the easiest chem professor you can get. Most of the exam averages were around the 70% range, and the final wasn't that bad. I suggest always reading the chapter before lecture, doing the problems in the book as you go along, and using the TA help room as often as possible. Get Wu if you can!!
Wu is great. I recommend him, and his tests are fair.
Kind of hard to understand at times but has no problem answering questions if you have one. Also cracks jokes occasionally to lighten the mood.

Unlike another calc prof I had, Dr. Wu was very good about not just covering the concepts, but also covering the math in detail. It can feel a bit tedious and slow if you already understand the math side of the class, but if you don't, you'll love him for the time he spends to teach you what the book may not cover in detail.

Tough tests, but awesome professor. You won't regret taking his class. Unfortunately, his class is pretty hard. I had to put in some major effort to keep up. The online homework helps and other online resources like clutch prep will do you good. Take his class, but don't expect an easy A.

Dr. Wu was by far one of the greatest professors I have ever had. I absolutely loved him. Phenomenal professor, and extremely helpful. His midterms were very fair, but to be honest, his final was extremely difficult. I would have gotten an A in the class if I hadn't bombed the final, but woulda coulda shoula. Great class, study for tests!

Dr. Wu was awesome! As long as you do your homework, attend lecture, and study hard for the exams, you'll get a good grade. Exams were based off of lecture notes. He's extremely helpful answering questions in-class and in office hours. Final was quite hard, but I think everyone survived. Highly recommend Wu over any 1210 professor.

Professor Wu is AWESOME. I went to lectures for the Demos but I also gained a lot more insight in the process. Loved the lectures and passed the class after 91 friggin hours on ALEKS...which I hate. But needless to say GREAT PROFESSOR.

Dr. Wu was an excellent professor, he wrote everything he said on the board (because he has an accent). Attend Class!!! He is pretty funny and entertaining. If you have a chance to get Dr. Wu, GET HIM!!!!!!!

Dr. Wu was one of the best professors I had my first quarter. He was very helpful, obviously cared about his students and would keep us awake by conducting interesting experiments throughout the lecture. His exams were very fair, if you don't mind multiple choice.

Dr. Wu is an EXCELLENT professor. His lectures tend to be boring, but attending them is important. Everything he gives in notes will appear on the exam. As long as you do the online homework and study your notes, the class is easy to get an A in. The curve is not huge, however; the course is fairly easy and a curve really isn't necessary.
The only thing good about him is his jokes. The course is awful. The chemistry department at OSU is terrible.
Can be very difficult to understand, making lectures pointless. I stopped going because I wasn't getting anything out of his notes. Keep up with practice homework in the book and you'll be fine.

Dr. Wu knows what he's talking about, but he makes his lectures uninteresting. We have no quizzes in his class, and as long as you do the online hw you'll understand most of what's going on. The midterm was challenging but fair, and he curved as needed. He can be hard to understand (he has a thick accent) but overall he is a good teacher.

Despite his accent he is quite clear, and also very funny. He makes lecture interesting with corny jokes and some fun experiments. His midterms can be tough, but he curves appropriately. If you have him, rejoice! His quizzes can very easily be 100%ed if you just do the hw a couple days before, giving you some nice breathing room.

Overall, great professor, who answers all your questions thoroughly and helps you work through any homework problems you have difficulty with. has funny/ corny jokes and is always interested in teaching the class. His exams and quizzes maybe tough sometimes, but the curve in the end actually helped me out a lot.
Funny guy. You'll like him

His lectures are amusing, but useless; your time would be better spent doing as many homework problems as possible. His tests are unnecessarily difficult,and he doesn't give much of a curve (if any?), in spite of the fact that averages are in the 60's. I knew this material and busted my ass studying for this class, but only walked away with a B+.
Great teaching had really good corny jokes!
Its hard to understand his speech but he writes everything out and takes it nice and slow for you. He ends up being one of the best chem teachers you can get. consider yourself lucky if you have him.
He is a very good professor. I love going to lecture because of all of the corny jokes and experiments. He's really easy to approach to ask a question.

Well really good with some fundamental concepts of chemistry. I had a little problem with understanding what he was saying.(Sometime) But Thats understandable I guess. Random homework trick worked well to keep me involved with assignments.
