Really, really enjoyed this class.  Do the homework, go to lecture, and pay attention, and you'll be fine.

I have now had the opportunity to compare prof. wu to another chem professor. So,from what i have gathered, professor Wu, is a very, very good teacher. Also, he has corny jokes that will make you laugh just because they are that stupid. I went to maybe one out of every two lectures and did great... if you don't do well, you should switch majors (=
he's a cute little asian who wears sweater vests and gets very excited about the corny jokes he tells. I would go to lecture just to see him even though I couldn't understand a word he was saying!
has a thick accent, but explains very well, and makes the class interesting; is also very approachable

Was very hard to understand....Did not like him as a teacher atall. He just starts writing on the board and does not explain too well. Loza is harder but is a better teacher and will curve your grade much more in the end. Wu barely curves at all so do not expect any help at the end.

Where to start....let's just say this class consumed my life for this quarter.  I went to his office hours and he didn't help whatsoever.  I went to lecture and didnt understand a thing.  Basically...had to teach myself everything and go to tutoring.  He's a nice guy but not so good at teaching.  Just angered me cuz lectures were a waste
Easily one of the best teachers I've ever had. Requires some effort to understand at first but it gets easier. Explains things well. Tells jokes and does demonstrations to keep people entertained.

Chemistry isn't my subject, so the content was difficult for me, but Dr. Wu was really helpful and tried to make it interesting. He always had a joke or demonstration :) If you study and do the practice problems, you'll do fine
Can I say, "researcher"?  How about the chemistry department hires a mime to act this class out while Wu writes notes on the board?

Dr. Wu is very nice and willing to help and he tries really hard to keep lecture fun and interesting.  Unfortunately, it's chemistry, so there are dry bits, but he usually does a demonstration each class that's pretty cool.  He's can also be really funny, though he doesn't try to do it intentionally. Overall, good professor.

Very fun teacher. Extremely funny. uses his cute asian accent to make you laugh. tries to make class interesting but doesnt hide the fact that he knows some parts are boring. tests and quizzes are very easy and he is there to help you not trick you with exams. love the accent and love his Wuisms.

Wow.. after taking Zellmer, who is a psychopath, I look back to Wu's class and really, really miss it. I did reasonably well knowing the material reasonably well, unlike in Zellmer where I did horribly knowing the material reasonably well. I miss good old Yiying.

I was thinking back of my old chem 121 class today, and comparing Wu with Zellmer (chem 122 prof.) I would prefer Wu. He is a nice guy who uses the blackboard. He makes his letters big so everyone can see, not like Zellmer, which uses overhead. Wu has good humor, and if you study even a little, you will appreciate his teaching. Wu is the man!

It was amazing to come back from a class and actually understand what was going on, unfortunately this was after coming back from loza's 122. If anything i felt like i am behind in chemistry due to Wu's lack of teaching. His accent is hard to overcome in class and i found myself sleeping in almost every lecture. The book taught me everything.

Hated him!! His chinese accent is VERY thick.  Gave up on going to lectures because I couldn't understand him at all.  Didn't come across as caring for his students at all.  Attending Loza's 122 lectures and come away having learned was a great feeling after having a quarter of wu.  Got a C, and am a science major...thanks wu...

He's kinda hard to understand but definitely a likable guy. He's nice and will provide as much help as you need. I never personally went to him for help but I saw many people do so. His lectures get boring after a while and I fell asleep in 4-5 of them so bring food to stay awake. Take notes, read the book, attempt homework.
good teacher, had a corny sense of humor. He breaks up his lectures with demonstrations, which helps pass the time during lectures.

This class is a phenomener. Very nice, adorable guy, likeable. Hard to understand english, his voice does put you to sleep. Heavily recommend bringing coffee/food to lecture to stay awake. He does cool demonstrations every class too, many involving fire. Tells corny jokes he got off the internet, recommended, there are definately worse out there.
Not that interesting, but I loved the thermite demo :D

Is a really nice guy. He had about a demonstration a week to help comprehension and keep people awake in lecture. He's a little hard to understand at times, not the best at explaining things to those who haven't had the material prior to the class. Assigns homework and a quiz every week. Two 25 question multiple choice midterms and a final.

This was Dr. Wu's 1st time teaching H202, so there's room for improvement. His examples came from the book & he sometimes makes mistakes in lecture. He's willing to explain things in office hours. He assigns homework after every lecture and quizzes every week to help you learn the material. Do the hw. Tests are difficult.
he's really boring and his tests are really unfair. the average on the midterms are in the 60's. don't take this class if he's teaching!
Worst teacher I've ever had in my life.
easy to understand
Hard Tests.
good guy
Funny but hard to understand sometimes.

Very good at explaining to people who haven't taken high school chem, hard to understand accent if you don't listen really closely, lectures are ok but it is possible to just read book for first 4 chapters at least,
a little hard to understand but not bad at all

He doesn't speak english very well and he hasn't been teaching long.  Lectures are crazily boring, but if you took chem in HS, its all just a reapeat anyways, read the book and its not that bad. I never went to lecture, or when i did i slept.
If you have any HS chem at all, this class is a joke.  He made it so easy.

I'll give the guy a break since he did say it was his first quarter teaching.  Needs to work on the english just a bit, but he really wasn't that bad.  Overall, I think i learned the most by reading the book, but the lectures weren't entirely useless.  I never visited him during office hours, but i hear good things. He is nice and non-intimidating.
Just read from the notes and did not do very many example problems. This coupled with a bad TA proved to be a terrible combination. Find a different lecturer if you can
The lectures were quite clear if you pay attention. Very helpful during office hours. Fair exams and useful review sessions. At least tried to make sure the TAs to do good jobs.
If you have had any high school chemistry and pay attention in class, this class is not too bad.  Plus there is always a generous curve.  A lot depends on your TA, so dont always blame the prof.
Didn't teach well at all.  My TA was terrible, so I had another hard time.

Only covered 1 or 2 things from each chapter and rarely did problems. Did almost nothing we had on our exams in class. You have to teach yourself almost everything unless you have a great T.A. which I didn't:-/
Terrible. Tests had typos. Lectures were boringgg. Did not care abt you at all. Exams were outdated. All group based and unreliable. No feedback. Do not take.

Very nice professor! For the most part does a great job teaching. There is a decent amount of reading that is needed outside of class, as this content will be on the exams. Content is also quite interesting. 

Good class and good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Deng is super nice. The group papers and projects are really easy if you have a good group. Her exams are long but not that difficult, I would suggest to take her for consumer behavior.

Professor Deng, is very caring. The class itself is pretty easy just know the verbatim for the exams and you will be fine. Her lectures are long and kind of boring, but she is the best out of all the 4201 professors. Take 4201 with her I learned a lot and most importantly I felt like she set us up for success.
Her lecture is very very boring...

EXTREMELY easy class. Half of the grade are in gimme group assignments that are graded on effort and following instructions.  She gives exam reviews that contain 2 - 4 questions that will be on the exam.  Did not need textbook at all (there are maybe 2 - 3 questions per exam from book, easy to figure out).  Wording on exam is fuzzy but manageable.

Dr. Deng is great.  You have 5 assignments that account for half of your grade, and she is a very fair and lenient grader on them as long as you put in the effort.  Attendance is not mandatory, but if you go to class it will pay off in the end.  Exams are a little tough, but study the notes (no need for text) and you will be fine. Take Her!

This professor is terrible. If you have the option, take someone else. She does not explain anything clearly and will send an e-mail to you the day before a presentation is due  to tell you that you have a presentation to do! The class has potential to be VERY interesting, but she rips that away from the subject completely.
Professor Ren's class is terminology heavy. Exams are somewhat hard but the review sessions helped.
Hands down one of the best professors I've had at OSU. Participation counts but she's fair.
Caring professor. Class involves assignments and group projects. Not much busy work. Fair grader.
The absolute goat for 4380 and 4383. You are in good hands if you take her classes.
I don't like this professor. Because she asks you to answer questions in class. I didn't know this percentage was significant until the end of the semester.

- truly challenging - pushes us beyond comfort zones, inspiring to explore new ideas & approaches.

- extraordinary depth of knowledge in their field 

- lectures are intellectually stimulating, thought-provoking and incorporate real-world examples, which brings the subject matter to life.

-challenging students to think critically and analytically
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Agreed one of the nicest teachers I have ever had! So willing to help you with anything :)
Good professor, willing to help and offers help. Quizzes and exams were somewhat hard.
worst instructor I ever met at osu. She left me with bad memories!

Dr. Ren really cares about her students. If you have any questions, you can just send her a message, and she'll schedule a meeting to help you. Some group projects, but not too much work to do if you're in a good team. Exams are closed-book but not hard either if you go to review session. I learned lots of professional terms in these two courses.

Professor Ren is great! The class was a little weird since we were online because of COVID and she had never taught this class online before. She is very open to responding to questions. We only did a few cases, two tests, and a team project.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Hadad is a very caring professor who genuinely wants his students to succeed and learn the material. He is very helpful in office hours and he sometimes responds to emails.That said, his canvas page is a little unorganized and his lectures are hard to follow. I learned most of the material for this class from the textbook.

I found Dr. Hadad to be friendly and straightforward. I went to a lot of his office hours and he will answer any question you have without making you feel bad for not having paid attention in the lecture. And its easy to zone out in the lecture so if you want to know what this class is about, read the textbook. And you only have to do 5 HWs!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hadad is a very fair professor and has a great personality.  This was his first year teaching at OSU, and the class had a bit of a shaky start, but I think he got the hang of it and things became more clear.  His Carmen page could use some organization, but I believe he taught the concepts of 2050 very well

No recorded lectures, no PowerPoint slides, no textbook and no answer keys for homework or midterm practice questions. His handwriting is hard to read, and as an associate professor, he does not seem to take sufficient responsibility for teaching. He often solves problems incorrectly in class and never replies to emails.

He isn't nearly as bad as some people claim. While his lectures can feel a little unstructured, he uploads all the notes and only requires 5 out of 13 homework assignments to be submitted. He goes over homework and midterm solutions in class, allows a cheat sheet, and reviews the material multiple times with examples.
Very unorganized, hard to follow along the notes (handwritten), no textbook other than the handwritten notes he posts and hard to follow along in general
unstructured

The class is rigged in a way that some students have to fail. You better make a good impression on her the first week to even have a chance. Attendance is optional but you better go because she knows who goes and who doesn't, if you know what I mean.

The exams are straightforward, and going to office hours before the exam really helps. If you do the readings and show up to class you will get an A. attendance is pretty important but you can skip one class a week if you participate enough in the other class. you can skip an exam and she will sub in the grade from one of the other exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Graded on only 3 tests, a final project, participation. Tests are hard, you HAVE TO READ. Zoe is an extremely strict professor, she thought I used AI and was going to report me to COAM, like wtf I didn't. It was eventually fine got 100%. what we learned was definitely interesting thought, mainly statistic and game theories with philosophy stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough grader. Unsure of how she really grades the video assignments/slideshows. Must be exactly to the reading or else you might as well not even make the video. Quizzes are short so if one question is missed its an automatic B pretty much. Otherwise it isn't a difficult class, interesting topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Ashton is a tough grader in this course, and at times it felt as though it was more of a "let's get it out of the way" rather than "let's fully analyze why/let's learn at a different approach" class. She's a very nice person and easy to get in contact with, but this course is a bit difficult navigating with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared for lots of videos and readings. If its not in the reading do not write it.

I am not sure why the other person had a problem with the video assignments. There were 6 total 4-8 minute videos recording assignments where you make an outline and then talk about the subject. She takes the 3 highest scores for the videos. This class really should be an easy A for anyone trying.
Not a fan of the videos, they are not to the point. Difficult to have office hours since there was no scheduled drop in time.

I just felt indifferent about Professor Ashton. It was very much "let's just get this over with". Homework is very straightforward, and the exams can be tough. If you do the work, you will be fine. The video recordings aren't my favorite.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Ashton was a wonderful professor! Her videos and readings were great and her assignments were very fair! Videos instead of exams were a nice take and fun, and quizzes were very reasonable, being open-note. It's a shame students tried to use ChatGPT, however, evident by announcements. Great class and pretty easy!

Professor Ashton was extremely kind, understanding, gave clear feedback, and helped us understand the material. The beginning of the course was stressful and she made things less stressful and she had faith in me. She has an amazing sense of humor as well which made the class fun.

Zoe was not my favorite instructor in the beginning because of a few grade misunderstandings and miscommunications but she will recognize when youre putting the work in and will try to bump up your grade. She offers many extra credit assignments if she realizes the class is struggling. Lots of writing assignments, but better than math.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Ashton is amazing! She will adapt the class if needed and truly wants you to succeed. There is no midterm/final but instead small quizzes and written assignments throughout the year to make your grade. She is extremely helpful and makes the class interesting. I highly recommend taking this for Data Analysis GE to avoid math!

From previous ratings and comments, I can tell Prof. Zhang is changing. Her lectures are great, and exams are not too challenging. However, she is still a TOUGH grader. I have also worked as a grader for other professors and I can tell her grading policy is much stricter.

I was wary due to her rating on here, but genuinely such a sweet woman. Her lectures are very clear and she works through problems as well as guides on how to think. Exams are similarly formatted to practice exams and are a little tough but for our class she allowed revisions which genuinely helped me learn the material better. 10/10 professor!

Julia is awesome I really enjoyed the lectures! The homeworks usually have a question that goes a little beyond the scope of the class and they are usually graded a little tough, but she goes out of her way to give you plenty of opportunities to get good grades.

Im taking her right now for ECE 3040, I have some SLDS accommodations and she is so sweet and understanding. Very flexible if you are honest and show effort. Attendance is mandatory but I find that it's more helpful. In my opinion her way of teaching and lecturing helped me learn the material without needing to find online resources. She is amazing

I took her 3040 this year. She is a little bit strict and harsh, mandatory attence and computer not allowed during lectures, bc lectures really help a lot, offer credits back for midterms. It's should be an easy A class if you go to her lecture and review the notes before the exam. Very recommened.

I took 3040 and 5041 with Dr. Zhang, and did independent study with her. She really cares about her students that put in the effort to learn in her classes. She is very direct, stays on topic, and focuses her coursework on practical skills needed in industry.

She's very strict and harsh in grading. My concept was wrong for the first question, so she only gives 1 point to the rest of related questions though my steps for the wrong concept are right. I lost a lot of points but i dont think she cares of her students. Her hw is also very long. I regret taking class with her. So please avoid.

Very harsh professor. I highly recommend taking in it with someone else if you could. Her homeworks and exams take a long time, and they are graded in a very harsh way. And I really regret taking her course

If anyone from the department is reading, please just get another teacher for this class. I don't understand what I'm paying for. I'm just learning everything by myself. It's like I don't have other classes too

Very bad professor. Her exams are too long. And she really enjoys making things much harder for the students. She wants students to suffer through out the semester. Ohio State should have a better professor to teach this course. I blame the University for having a bad professor like her.
One of the worst professor that I had in my life. She always try to make things more difficult for students. She also doesn't know how to teach. Avoid her.

This might have been her first time teaching 3040, I'm not sure. But the lectures were very difficult to follow. However, she does care about students and gives great career advice on the material which is a breath of fresh air.

Class is not hard but she isn't a good professor. I don't really pay attention in class because it's hard to understand her explanations. Instead I just go back over the material later to learn everything.

Julia is very caring professor. She cares that you understand the material rather than just going through it. She actually slowed down to make sure we understand before moving on. I suggest you don't take any notes and just focus listening on the lecture. She records all the lectures. Office hours are very helpful to go to. And she is cute tho.

Do not take this professor. The lectures are disorganized and hard to understand. The only thing that helps is the textbook. Material on midterms are not hard but they are very very long, thus making exams hard. She is extremely difficult to contact via email and her office hours do not help.

Most of your grade comes from reading excerpts. She is caring and kind, but its pretty stressful to do the excerpts. Make sure you read the textbook and learn the word definitions and grammar. Japanese is just structured that way, it isn't her fault. It is super easy to get an A. Just make sure you try your hardest to get those excerpts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: I really loved taking this class. Professor Kuwai is very enthusiastic and passionate about teaching. It's very clear that she loves what she does and she's good at it. As for the class itself, it really helped me actually speak Japanese as opposed to just reading. Do NOT skip class unless you have to though- very lecture heavy.

Kuwai-sensei is the best teacher I've had, hands down. She makes it difficult to not care about class, and it was well worth taking at 8am five days a week. All the TA's are great. Daily performance is 60% of the grade. Would 100% recommend for learning Japanese
We love Kuwai-Sensei :)

Kuwai-Sensei and all the other TA's are amazing! I had her for JPN 1 and it was a small but awesome and energetic group. Mon,Tu, Thu, Fri class will be in Japanese, and Wed class will be in English. If you show up, prepare for all the activities beforehand, and don't give up, you'll have a lot of fun! Can't wait to take JPN 2!

Class is taught in Japanese 4 days a week for a grade, and Wednesday is always taught in English. Instructions on what parts of the textbook to study are posted clearly; practice the scripts and the activity book diligently. The TAs are very helpful when they teach, and Kuwai-sensei is a very welcoming professor. Watch out for the FACT quizzes.

Kuwai-sensei and the entire Japanese language department truly cares about their students. They make learning the difficult language a much better experience. The class itself is difficult for sure. Japanese is one of the hardest for English speakers to learn so be weary.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very easy and interesting class. The grade is based on a lot of things, and the daily grade is 60% or something. So preview the script and vocab and show up.
Easy grader, very kind. Teach with passion and very kind. I enjoy her class and have the power to learn more about Japanese.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kuwai-sensei is such a sweetheart. She truly wants her students to succeed and takes notice of effort regardless of results. The class is difficult and composed mostly of acting out scripts with your peers, but sensei helps a lot if you get lost or confused about the material. She typically teaches once/week, but the other teachers are amazing too.
Kuwai is absolutely wonderful, for the like, 40% of the semester she actually teaches, since they rotate grad students and such. I wish she taught the upper levels as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Kuwai-sensei is such a caring teacher, it's hard not to love her. You'll have a host of TA's in the lower-level classes, and they can all be pretty variable, but Kuwai-sensei is a real gem. She's very understanding and patient with her students. However, it can be a bit difficult to understand her. Her English is not quite fluent.

Kuwai sensee is great! She is very funny and easy to get along with. Class isn't too hard, as long as you properly prepare for each class. She is easy to schedule a meeting with or go to office hours for extra pronunciation practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I love Kuwai-sensee! She was so funny and personable and made class fun. Although we only had her part of the time, her classes always went fastest which is good cause attendance is most of your grade. You need to read the textbook section for the day and have the conversation ready for class. She's a pretty easy grader though and helps you a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Kuwai-sensei's lectures are the best. She's funny and although participation is mandatory, it's done in a way that's both fun and helps you memorize the material. Grading criteria is very clear, but you do need to prepare at least 30 minutes a day to do well in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Such a sweet and kind lady. She's your typically quirky Japanese and she loves to speak with her students. Given, you won't have her every class, but when you do, you know it will be fun, interactive, and actually really helpful in learning the language. Just memorize what you are supposed to (takes like 10 minutes a night) and you'll be fine.

First of all, if you take a class with Kuwai listed as professor, if it's a lower level Japanese class at least, you'll only have her about 20-40% of the time.  When you do have her, class is awesome.  When you have one of the other teachers/grad-students, it can really go either way.  But overall, you'll have a great time.

Kuwai-sensee was fantastic! She was a sweet lady who always brought her enthusiasm with her to class. The material itself is not easy and requires studying, but she is always willing to help if you ask for it. As long as you put effort into this class, you'll end up with at least a B+, if not an A.

She is actually really sweet, adorable and enthusiastic. Although it is a bit nerve racking at first because 45 classes per week are conducted completely in Japanese, class actually turns out to be fun or even funny if you study every night before class. She tells you exactly what to study and if you study it, then you will do great.

Kuwai-sensei is helpful and is not afraid to correct you so in turn don't be afraid to make mistakes. She speaks quickly and has an accent so she might be difficult to understand in English, so when she is teaching grammar make sure you read the concepts before hand. Listen to all audio and drills and do all activities mentioned in the ACT box.

Overall, I really liked having Kuwai Sensei. She sometimes got a bit confusing, and she does talk very fast. However, you could always tell she loves teaching Japanese. If you put the effort into her class she will tell, and help you out when you need help. Her quizzes are pretty easy, and are for the most part exactly what is covered in class.
She's always very enthusiastic. Her English isn't the best, but somehow she managed to get the point across, anyway. All lessons pretty much come from the book, though.

Really great class, recomend it to all those studying Japanese, really helps you learn better ways to study. Only complaint was how many times she mentioned the "how to use this textbook" section of the JSL books. These books are really different from other Japanese books and this class helps you understand them a bit more.

Had Kuwai-sensei for SPEAC J-2 (1103.02/2102.02). Frankly, I'm thankful that she taught level 2, because I'd have been so discouraged if level 3 had been my first encounter with her as a teacher. Definitely stick with it, and her teaching style will sink in. I'd say she grades as fairly as all the other teachers (Kiyosue, Terada, & Nozaki). ???????

Kuwai-sensei is dedicated to teaching students and very helpful if you're struggling to understand the material.  She has a great sense of Japanese humor which makes class lively and interesting.  The class is by no means easy, but very enjoyable.  She's definitely one of the best teachers I've ever had.

Kuwai Sensee is great--animated and makes an effort to keep students interested.  She's very willing to help students outside of class, and as many others have said, she cares about students' progress.  Fair in her grading, she constantly encourages students to improve.  She even has a Facebook fan page, Lol!
Kuwai-sensei is a wonderful teacher. She knows her stuff and knows how to teach very well. Keep in mind that the class requires a great deal of improv, so know the vocabulary that you're supposed to.

My favorite Japanese Sensee but also the one who grades the hardest. She's often very amusing and I always enjoy her lectures. She has always been very willing to meet students one-on-one outside of class too. The course is difficult but she genuinely seems to care about the students in 1st year Japanese and wants them to succeed.
Kuwai-sensei was awesome. She was so funny and helpful, and geniunely concerned for my understanding of the language.
one of my favorite teachers ever!  she is hilarious, thorough, animated, and genuinely cares about her students as people.  the best!
Very nice teacher... hilarious too.  The only thing is that her accent is hard to understand (but we have Kern-sensee so it's OK).  She helped me a lot when I was having trouble.
She is a great professor. Her accent is difficult to understand at times, but in terms of lessons she explains herself well.

She knows her stuff!  She has all the books memorized !!  She has no problem with explaining things but she gets frustrated easily.  The worst thing, she will interrupt you, constantly!  She already has a sentence in her head and you have to be a mind reader to get it right.  People either tolerate/like her or hate her, there's no inbetween.

Kuwai-sensee is probably the best teacher I've ever had. Once you've gotten used to her teaching style you always know what to expect, she is very focused and if you pay close enough attention to her exercises they are extremely beneficial. She can grade pretty hard but she'll give you the benefit of the doubt from time to time.

Yeah - she may be good one-on-one, and she may be interested in teaching.  But she cannot communicate clearly, and rather than explain she just repeats the same nonsensical BS over and over until you guess.  Guessing until you are right is not learning, it is exhausting all other options.
Excellent Instructor. She really wants to help you understand and is extremely nice. Funny too.
She's rough, but a good instructor. You know your material when she's done with you. Funny, too.
She's so nice!  The class might seem overwhelming at first, but if you stick at it, it becomes a lot easier and more fun.
Funny, intelligent, and intent on helping anyone who asks for it. Best instructor since coming to OSU.

Very Difficult!  FACT classes all in Japanese, no English (like ACT).  Fast talker, faster than Japanese fluent speakers.  Often times singles people out and 'picks' on them.  If you want to take all Japanese series, you'll eventually get her without a choice; Good luck!
Great teacher and hilarious most of the time!
hilarious, yet can make you feel pretty dumb, excellent teacher overall as after a few weeks you feel like youve learned so much
dedicated and has genuine interest in students
Extremely nice and helpful. A tad difficult to understand but she is a great teacher. Funny too.

Hard class for students who just want to get an easy A, tho her English is not that good, she's willing to help. For ppl who really wanna get to use Japanese very quick, take her class.  Her Japanese style of learning might make u feel anxious, however it's the best way to learn different system of language. It's worthful.
Took a little getting used to but has a great sense of humor and loves anyone who takes an interest in the language.
Great teacher, very funny and animated. The other instructorss are great also!
She is an awesome teacher. She's funny, explains everything well, and is willing to help anyone that wants it.

John was alright. Kind of dry lectures, but you will learn a lot about professional writing, and I really got a lot out of the projects we did. It's an easy A if you put the work in, but you do need to go to class everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Most boring class of my college career and I'm a senior. He was an okay teacher. Really helpful if you needed it. But pretty boring to listen to.
OMG. I LIKED PROFESSOR ACKER.  YOU SHOULD TAKE THIS CLASS.  DO YOUR WORK, SPEND SOME TIME ON IT AND YOULL DO GREAT.  HE IS GREAT AT HELPING AND GOOD AT RIGHTING.

An extremely dorky teacher, but overall very nice and always willing to help. He grades relatively easy but you still have to put in some effort in order to get a good grade! Any reading he assigns you need to read, but none of them are ever over 20 pages long.
Great prof. We read a living writer and then he brought him from out of town to talk to our class about what we read. I really liked this teacher.

Pretty nice guy. This class is boring, but SUPER EASY to receive an A in if you are a decent writer. I never really needed help, but he's always willing to hold office hours. I never bought the textbook (almost all of the stories can be found somewhere online).

Bit of a dweeb, but he likes teaching and makes sure his students understand the material. He's a conservative, and doesn't do a good job of hiding it, but he doesn't let it cloud his judgments of your work too badly. Read the assigned material, do the classwork and an A will be no sweat.
He is cool. He will work with you.

Very strange, but nice and helps students with anything needed. Lectures are very tedious and elementary and are online, but attendance is mandatory unfortunately. He doesn't grade very hard and can easily pass with an A. Easy class, but boring at times.

very nice and helpful... go to his office hours... it will help your papers and grades so much. it's obvious he cares about each student. highly recommend to take him if at all possible, definately one of if not the best eng 110 teachers!
Going to class in mandatory and it is a pretty easy yet useful class if you are going out in the business world.  I would recommend this class any day.

Very understanding teacher and really cares about you doing well. Lectures are a bit boring but definitely go in for office hours and he will help you out if you need help on any paper or anything. Cool guy, take the class
Great teacher! Extremely clear, funny, and cares about you as a student. He grades generously too! Highly recommended.
He gives really good paper comments but grades to hard. Seems nice; actually cares.

Acs is a very bad lecturer and is a boomer when it comes to tech. There are no study guides or clear guidance for the 2 exams that make up 70% of your grade. The readings are very long. Acs shows up late to class and didn't bother to show up for his own final. The exams are unnecessarily difficult. This was my least fav poli sci course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded by 2 Exams and random participation quizzes. Lectures were difficult to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved the subject and the readings, but he turned that love into boredom with his slow, drawn-out lectures. He gives only occasional (easy) quizzes for attendance, a midterm, and a final with no study guide. The readings are long and dense, and the lectures are the same. Learned a lot, but at what cost...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Acs is an amazing professor in my personal opinion. Some do not like how slow he speaks in class but he wants to make sure everyone is able to understand and succeed. The course is graded by 2 exams and an optional extra credit paper/presentation on a topic you pick based on course content. I wish he taught more than 3 classes! 10/10!!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
> Class is useful for understanding how laws are created and implemented. Lectures were useful and well-organized.
> READING IS REQUIRED to pass the class. The midterms consist of T/F, multi choice, and shortanswer questions which directly reference readings. You NEED to reread.
> Grades: 30% Quizzes, 30% Midterm, 40% Final. 1-5 ex credit points
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Acs' assigned readings for each class, each of which were pretty easy. He had pop tophat quizzes for attendance, but you could miss a few without penalty. Two exams, each based on information in the lecture slides, but he rarely covered the slides during lecture and instead went off on random tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've had Acs for 3500 and 3115. Classes are incredibly boring; he's not the best lecturer and if you want a grade that's higher than a C, go to class, read everything, and study constantly. The only benefit is that there is a group project at the end of the semester, and he grades that leniently. Very mid.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The Professor is great, but he doesn't know how to explain the material and his classes and readings are boring.

The professor is knowledgeable, but there seems to be an assumption that students in this introductory-level class share his same level of knowledge. Lectures are painful to sit through and the readings are incredibly dull. Only four grades all semester.

Only graded on 4 assignments (30% Midterm, 30% Final, 20% Reading Quizzes, 20% Group Project). Extremely dry, boring content, kind of assumes everyone has an advanced level of knowledge even though there are no pre reqs to the class. Exams are unnecessarily difficult - both the midterm and final had to be curved by 20 points each.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Final grade is only based on two exams, reading quizzes, and a group project. The class is pretty difficult, he had to curve the midterm and final for a decent amount of points, think 10-20. The lectures can be boring but he does a decent job teaching, willing to answer questions, and is overall a pretty chill professor.
Class was super easy. One reading quiz a week which was common sense if you read the book. Curves the midterm and final a LOT. Highly recommend for a GE and he was super nice.

Lecture could be dry at times, but I still liked this class. Just a midterm and final (both administered online), final paper, and pop tophat quizzes based on the readings. He has students best interests at heart and everything was pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Alex was an excellent lecturer. Insightful, even handed, and willing to answer questions and have a discussion. The class was based mostly on the midterms, final and paper, but he gave a generous curve and graded fairly. I really enjoyed this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is unnecessarily tedious and difficult. Endless amount of policies to choose from to study, and this prof seemingly picks the most boring topics possible. Doesn't give clear guidelines or content of exams, the quizzes don't even match the readings, and was pretentious with occasional out of pocket things said. -900/10, don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy, if you took high school gov you're off to a good start. I really liked Prof Acs, and though I probably could've gotten an A while skipping some lectures, I genuinely enjoyed being there. Classes kind of feel like a casual chat but he does teach the material well. Funny, chill, will lightly make fun of people.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Many questions are completely ambiguous or have conflicting information which makes the midterm luck-based. Everyone ran out of time, average was initially an 80%. Now it's a 78%, and we're confused whether he curved it down? No lecture recs, mandatory attendance, midterms open at 9AM for 1 hour, & no slides released until weeks after his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Acs is a really great professor. He is clear about what his expectations are for your assignments. There are 2 midterms, 1 final. Lots of extra credit opportunity and he also curves almost all the exams. He is very smart and yet is easy to learn from as he explains things flawlessly. He is also funny and really nice!

Aces clearly loves the information he is teaching, the class had only three test- which he curved and extra credit was able to be given. There was a textbook- but I never bought it. I put this class on the back burner of 18 credit hours- not that it is easy, just never any commitment besides the three exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Your grade is determined based on the final and midterm exams. The exams are extremely hard he had to curve grades 12% because a lot of our class failed. Lectures are really boring. Wouldnt recommend this course or teacher. This intro class definitely hurt my gpa. Take with another professor if you can!

The only grade in the class is the midterm and final, which isn't an easy exam, but he does curve it! I would take it with someone else if possible, but have learned a lot. It is an intro level course, but is much harder than that. Other students in my class do not like him, but I do not mind him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The only grade in the class is the midterm and final, which isn't an easy exam, but he does curve it! I would take it with someone else if possible, but have learned a lot. It is an intro level course, but is much harder than that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a great guy who loves this topic, but you don't actually get through much content in the class because he talks about it all a little too much. Graded by three response papers, two exams, one final paper, and some reading quizzes. You really need to do the reading and it's very unclear exactly what he expects you to do in the papers.

He is a very nice professor who is willing to meet with you after the class. Also, he responds to email in a constant manner. For mathematics course, besides the help of a professor, yBou have to work and practice in order to get the score you want .

Patient and frequently available for help outside of class. As an educator myself, I appreciated his efforts to teach us how math works, rather than just how to plug and chug numbers. I'd recommend this TA to other students.
He is very quiet!

TA for Math 161.02 recitation: gave fair quizzes that were doable (usually) only if you read/prepared/did the HW/etc, explained topics well when reviewing, and didn't object to taking questions from students and did his best to answer. Has a Turkish accent but he worked though this and verbal clarity was never a problem.

I am very picky in regards to who I will actually take classes with. The course time for this was later than I would usually bother with. However, my academic advisor  said to; "take it with him, I know you'll love it". She was completely right! The material is spot on and makes you really consider perspectives. Justin is brilliant.

Justin really makes you think, especially when the topics get more abstract. The grading and expected requirements are never very clear, and I feel like the grades were rather random. However, it really provided me with a lot to think of and enhanced my skills in writing. If you take his class, make sure to take notes and attend his office hours!

*1st time teaching this class*  Grades: reading summary due every class, 2 papers + final.  Advise:  read/do every homework & pay attention in class  it'll make papers and final easier. He is very unclear of what is expected in assignments therefore loose unexplainable points.

One of the few classes where I felt like the information I got out of it mattered more than the grade.  Class consists of discussion and 3 papers. If you read the articles and are engaged in discussion you will get a lot of out it.  I personally feel as though I am able to think more clearly about political issues and understand political arguments

Very helpful, and genuinely wants you to get the material. Format of class is an open discussion, which is nice. Discussions can get abstract at times. There is a lot of reading, but as long as you get the principle of the reading you're fine. Basically the entire grade consists of 3 papers that consist of how you feel about politics.

You get used to the work throughout the semester. Dr. Aguolu most of the time gave feedback on assignments. I never noticed a rude demeanor like other students previously stated. Just do your homework and you'll be fine.

Terrible professor do not take her class!!! She assigns weekly papers and homework over breaks, Her lectures are long and drawn out all of which is read straight from the slides. Attendance is mandatory and she assigns wayyyy too much for a 3 credit hour GE. All of it feels like busy work and unnecessary. SAVE YOURSELF AND DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Inconsistent in grading
No feedback when asked for clarity or guidance 
Extra credit deducted from grade (how is that extra??)
Inaccessible - non responsive
Do not take any class by this prof!!
The tough grading comes from the TA's in my experience not her, and compared to my other Gen Eds, the workload seemed similar. If u just do your work you will be fine and learn useful stuff.

Told us to ask and email questions when needed, but would give passive-aggressive responses or not respond at all. Her rude demeanor made many nervous to talk to her. So many assignments and she is not an easy grader. Constantly nagged about being prepared and professional, but couldn't even uphold her own standards herself half of the time.

Avoid her classes if possible. She knows her stuff but is not a good professor. She encourages students to ask questions then acts very annoyed and rude when people do ask her questions. She spends about 15 minutes at the beginning of every class yelling at us for emailing her and asking questions. Also way too much work for a GE.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: nope!!! She knows her stuff and the quizzes, but her demeanor is bad! She encourages questions but then is annoyed when you DO ask. I went to her office hours and she was angry the second I asked my question. I did not feel comfortable asking her anything else. I as more comfortable emailing the TA about a grade than her. Way too much for a GE.

As a freshman, this class was overwhelming. We have an APA paper due at least one paper each week. Graders are PICKY, often taking points for stupid stuff. Much of the work felt tedious, and Dr. Aguolu marked attendance weekly, adding pressure since missing class could hurt our grades. Would only take this class if it's required for you.
She is AMAZING! She makes everyone want to go out and change the world.

Dr. Acton is an inspiration to anyone who takes her class, she is incredibly brilliant and really cares that you're passionate. She always has a smile, and cares about your interests. It's one of the easiest classes I've taken, and if you show up you'll pass.
Life-changing class. Easily the best class I have taken in college, Dr. Acton is amazing and will inspire you to find what you're passionate about.

Ms. Acton is a heart warming teacher that is very inspirational. The class is not difficult at all. I would recommend as a GE. Barely any test or quizzes. No exams. Just group project, a  2 quizzes on 2 reading that aren't that bad, and a small 4 minute TED talk you have to do in front of the class on a topic related to public health.

I would absolutely recommend this class to anyone and everyone! She is so amazing and welcoming and really makes you feel comfortable coming to class! I always looked forward to coming to class, as it has been my most enjoyable and stress-free course. Very inspirational professor, and one of the sweetest people!
so wonderful, would recommend to anyone, a true asset to the college

Amy Acton's global public health class I took my first semester of freshmen year is by far the best class I've taken at OSU. Her passion for public health, personal teaching style and inspirational life story makes it easy to be engaged in the class. You don't have to read the books to get an A but you should! Just go to class and you'll be fine.

Dr. Acton is incredibly smart and inspiring.  Her class is truly interesting and thought provoking and she does everything she can do get to know each and every one of her students, which was very refreshing.  There is minimal work, only a couple projects.  I would recommend any one from any major to take this class.
Dr. Acton is one of the most amazing professors and women I have ever met. Her lectures are inspirational and interesting, and there was virtually no homework. Would absolutely take again.

Professor Acton is an incredible professor. The class was so interesting and she really inspires her students to be better people. There aren't exams in this class really, it's more project based and the projects are also really awesome because she leaves the topics super open so you can pick something that interests you. LOVED this class.
Dr. Acton is such a genuine, good hearted person. She really loves her job and works to get to know each of her students. I loved this class because of her!

Dr. Acton is an amazing professor. Her class inspires me to be a better person and care about others every day. This was the best class I could have chosen to take my first semester of my Freshman year because it will lay the foundation for the rest of my college career. I definitely recommend taking Dr. Acton's Public Health class.

She is such an inspiration. Her stories are extremely motivating and she uses her class for us to have a break between our harder classes. She always has a smiling face, no matter what and I always left her class feeling happier. Such a kind-hearted person and learned a lot more than just public health from taking her class.

Open discussion class and will sometimes call on people at random to hear their opinions. He truly loves his job and being with students. He is very funny and brings up interesting topics. Test are easy. Would recommend looking over the reading material, it is on the exams.

The best professor I have ever had! Always in a good mood and smiling. She is so passionate about her job and is such an inspiration. Gets to know all of her students even in big lecture classes. Great person inside and out! Take her class even if you are not a public health major!
Inspirational

Professor Acton is probably the best public health professor I have ever had. She is awesome, funny, and willing to meet you outside of class to discuss things about life in general and about the class.  She says that its hard not to pass the class so you should have no problem at all with this class.
She's an absolute sweetheart. Very passionate and willing to help. She makes it very apparent that she genuinely wants to learn about her students. Highly, highly, HIGHLY recommend.
I love Dr. Acton, she is a fantastic woman with so much enthusiasm and care for students. Definitely, definitely, definitely take her!!!

Oh Dr. Acton. I can honestly say she is my first real teacher crush. I want her to teach every one of my classes. She cares so much for her students and their success. She really tried hard to guid them into their career "callings". There is a real sense of community within the class. I wish she was my mother, or aunt or something! 3 for ever

I loved Dr. Acton! Best professor I have came across at OSU. I sincerely wish she could teach me every class. She is very pleasant and concerned for her students. You can tell she cares about her students and them actually learning. OSU needs to find more professors like her!
Absolutely loved this class! One of my favorites at Ohio State. Dr. Acton is so nice, and very helpful. I highly recommend taking this course!

Dr. Acton is the best professor I have yet at Ohio State. She genuinely cares about her students and is really passionate about what she does. She's extremely willing to meet with you too! She's awesome
Great teacher and great class! Changed my outlook on public health and life in general.
Extremely enthusiastic and understanding professor. She empowers students to explore topics and gives tons of encouragement. You need to take her class.

Best professor I have ever had. So inspiring and genuinely interested in her students, and helping them find their own passions. Go to office hours! Fantastic professor. Very engaged in the class and full of knowledge. She takes great interest in her students, go to her office hours!

she really knows how to teach and make the class so interesting, also she has a great sense of humor which makes the class easy to focus and learn unlike other sociology course instructors I took. it is quiz heavy but if u do the readings you will be fine. best sociology professor I had so far.

Took 1101-1103. Plenty of homework, but almost none is graded, still should do though, often gone over in class. Great professor, very friendly, sometimes may expect a bit much from students.

A truly wonderful human being. You don't feel like you are in a class but having a meeting with friends. Leave your phone in your pocket. She does not like phone usage in class. I am taking the Swedish series at OSU and am so happy I have her as my instructor. She is truly a treasure.

Agi is a wonderful human. She is so sweet and really just wants you to do well. If you ever need help with anything, don't hesitate to ask, but she really does go above and beyond to make sure everyone is learning and keeping up. Brings snacks pretty much every Friday and she loves to find ways to make class fun. Plus Swedish is SO easy!

Agi is Awesome! She is probably the sweetest person you will ever meet. Even if you have no interest in the Hungarian language you should take her class just so you can have her as your teacher. She will go to the end of the world to help you, immerse you in Hung. culture and knowledge and she will even bake for you! I love her!!

Tough tests usually with a curve, heavy homeworks with busy office hours.  She is not a gifted lecturer but overall a decent teacher and decent class. I failed because I did not do the homework, kids don't fail ME 2010, its literally the one class in mecheng you cant fail.

She makes statics extremely easy and is very very understanding of the class's grades.

She's one of the most professional teachers that I have had while I've been in college for 4 and a half years.  With that said, she expects a lot from her students at the same time.  I learned a lot from this class but I would only take it if you are really interested in Bioimaging; and if you are, be prepared to work for your grade.

Although Professor Agunga's very sweet and always has positive energy, I really didn't feel that I learned anything in this class. Agunga is a horrible professor, this class offered absolutely no extra value to my academics. I feel as though the class was a waste of time. Not worth the time or money, DO NOT take it unless you have to.

not an easy class. TA and him know very little when I ask question. professor is a happy guy and will brings food to class?but his assignment is pointless.
Really a bad pro, he is so bad at teaching, and all the assignments are pointless. To be honest, I dont think getting A is easy. and most of my friends get B. He is the worst pro I have ever know
Very interested in the success of his student. Very energetic and generous guy, would bring coffee and donuts in!  Passionate and knowledgeable about his work.

Easy class, but not a particularly interesting one.

a really interesting seminar very helpful

Very cool teacher, goofy guy who always brings snacks to class and makes all feel welcome. Easy assignments, as long as you attend class its a guarantee A...

I didn't like this class too much while i was in it, but afterwards i realized that it was a good one. He's a pretty goofy guy, but overall a good class that was pretty easy if you went to class and did the work.
Very helpful and knowledgable. He tries to work with you in every way possible. He has great contacts and is very helpful if you want to do anything that relates to international topics.

Prof. Agunga is a real fun guy.  His philosophy is everyone is an A student and if you turn in everything he asks for then you receive an A.  MT and Final are easy and all other assignments (solo and group) do not require much effort.  Highly recommended!

You'd get the most out of Calmette's class if you already have a lot of political science experience as the lectures are very complex and so are many of the jargon filled papers, he isn't always very brief. If you have that background though you can learn a lot and the grading is not harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Chaudhry may be the Fisher Goat. Lectures were extremely engaging and easy to follow. Your grade is mainly determined by how well you do on the quizzes, midterm, and final, however I thought all of these were very fair tests. Another plus is that the homework is extremely easy and you still get credit for it. Highly recommend, great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think he's a good and knowledgeable guy, and he tries his best to help you understand the material. But his quizzes and exams were weighted 80% of your total grade and he did not know important details about how many questions the quizzes and exams had. The time limit of the final exam was not very clear either. He did curve in the end though.

He is a responsible lecturer and tries his best to help you understand the contents. And also he is accessible outside the classroom. However, his 2 exams and 2 quizzes weight about 80% of the grades. And some conceptual questions in exams are never covered in slides.
Mandatory attendance with unclear lectures. Adam Champion is a nice guy but is awkward and frankly not an effective teacher.

Champion is very smart and knows his stuff, but he has trouble dumbing down complex topics for people who have never seen it before. The class is very lecture and slides heavy and his lectures are very dry and hard to follow.

Champion is a good person and seems to care a lot about his students. If you go to him during office hours, he is very helpful. The labs can be long, but they are very interesting and informative. However, his lectures don't really teach you much, and you have to rely on the textbooks to truly understand the topics covered.

Great guy, very knowledgeable, and respects his students' time. I appreciate how straightforward his labs are compared to some Systems 1 teachers. If you do well on the labs and homework, the midterm and final aren't stressful. The exams will be easy if you go to lectures and understand the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Learned nothing from class. Nice guy but good luck if you want to ask a question and get a direct answer and not a 30 minute lecture about random details from the Android framework. Please find a different professor for your own sanity.

Memorize how to implement the patterns and by memorize I mean letter by letter because tests are on paper no notes. So forget keeping documentation up while you're working on your project cuz memorizing is what he wants. Lectures are dry and impossible to stay awake for. My second time having him as a lecturer and he was even worse than before

Truly bone dry lectures where he does nothing but talk at students. Often goes off topic to discuss tangential topics. Often times is unable to help with homework and labs or points students in the wrong direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Like everyone else said, veryyyy boring lectures there wasn't a day where I didn't almost fall asleep. He often goes off-track and talks about things that have nothing to do with this class. Start your labs early because none of the lecture material actually teaches you how to do it. Exams/homework were graded fairly easy though.

Most unhelpful lectures I've ever attended. 95% of content on exams I had learned myself because the overwhelming majority of lecture slides were just implementations of something in a mobile app written in java, then kotlin. I know he means well, but he's just not made to teach a class.

Made the intro to OS class incredibly hard to grasp for people with limited knowledge of OS. Brushed through slides faster than lightnings. Always went on Amazon websites and played dumb YouTube videos rather than taught students useful things. Minimal help in office hours.

Terrible class, terrible teacher and terrible grader. They did not give any rubrics and just reduced your points as they wanted! The course was very boring and just reading the textbook or material. Do not take it!!!

Champion's lectures are extremely long, dry, and boring. He tends to talk at students for the entire lecture, and sometimes goes off on random tangents that contribute nothing. He is also not really knowledgeable about the material he assigns for labs, and can't provide helpful explanations/answers in lecture or office hours.
Very passionate and really smart professor.

Not sure why all the awful reviews, lectures were boring but informative, homeworks/labs were easy and graded leniently, and exams were fair imo. Not my favorite professor or class but I would take it with him again.
Avoid at all costs that is all I have to say if you want to keep your sanity.

This class was bad and in large part because of Champion. Lectures were extremely dry and hard to follow and the lectures slides are hard to look at and study off of. The times I went to office hours to get help on assignments and I was never directly asking for the answer but the most common reply I would get is "try printing it out on paper".

Adam is extraordinarily smart, but he isn't a good teacher. His lectures are horribly dry, and he often goes on long tangents. There's only three homeworks and four labs, so the midterm and final are 50% of the grade. The exams and homeworks are full of "gotcha" questions, so you better memorize every detail from the internet and 700-page textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were pretty boring and hard to sit through, but his exams were relatively easy as long as you read the textbook. Slides are pretty pointless as well and he doesn't post lecture videos. I went to his office hours and he is an extremely nice and caring person who I enjoyed getting to know. Exams are fair but a little lengthy.

Grading is pretty lenient. Dryest lecturer I've had, so I stopped attending class. His lectures are all taken word for word from the textbooks, and his labs from other profs. All of my learning done was from the textbook, and I still got an 88% on the midterm. If you can't learn from textbooks well, skip him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class. Easy labs. Stupid and boring lecturer.

Good professor, I like his class because of his knowledge of Operating systems. I went to every office hour to get answers to my questions. Labs are great and enable me to understand how to improve the codes because the second lab depends on the previous. I studied the book before the lecture and that help me a lot. Great Dr.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Adam Champion is like the Sheldon Cooper of Computer Science. Not the best professor I've had, but his class is fair. I would recommend occasionally glancing at the book and making friends in his class so you have a reason to show up for it. We made a bingo board with all of his quirks and phrases (and won within two lectures).

Basically all he did was read the textbook for 90 minutes straight. And he never put an assignment out that had correct info. Had to go on piazza and ask questions and he says oops Ill fix that. One assignment was missing an entire file of words he meant to use. Worst part is his lectures are the most dry lectures ever.

Dr. Champion is not a good professor, he is a good guy but his lectures have no sustenance in them and don't really set you up to do the projects or the exams. That being said the projects are graded very leniently, and he is a very forgiving grader on the exams. If you can get through the dry lectures and exams you will be okay, not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: I'm writing this review to stay awake during his lecture... So insanely dry and ridiculous amounts of readings.

He seems scared or bored when teaching. Very smart guy who knows his stuff. Very long awkward pauses and always goes off topic from the teaching material. 2 HWs are easy but 5 labs are average to hard. Exams are fair (83% avg). Struggles to answer questions live but is helpful on Piazza. If 2431 wasn't so boring, he would be alright I guess
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good: Recorded lectures, super receptive of feedback and cares that the class is fair, reasonable expectations, provides a list of topics on exams, follows books closely. Bad (that was his fault): Boring (albeit optional) lectures, half the labs are easy but half were super annoying (i.e. C string manipulation)

As many have stated, the lectures are very dry. Feedback is not given for assignments for over a month, so it's tough to tell whether you're on the right track in class. The good thing about his class is that he has Office Hours essentially every weekday, which is really convenient.

Lectures can be dry, but also sometimes hard to follow. There are many labs, but he will not look at your code in zoom, which is not good. Homeworks are fairly easy and the midterm was not bad either. The final exam was very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sure the lectures were a bit dry, but overall taking mobile app development with Champion was a straightforward and enjoyable experience. Exams were a bit tougher than average, but graded pretty generously. The average grade in the class ended up being an A-. Just put in the work to have the project ready for each checkpoint and you'll be fine.

Rather dry lectures along with exams that force you to memorize useless Google-able info instead of actually testing content mastery. It's probably better because this is a project course because less of your grade is dictated by his inability to teach well. He cares, but it doesn't show too well. I'm glad I have a chill TA who's actually cool

Champion is a awkward guy but his heart is in the right place. Hes willing to help outside of class and during class. His grading is a little bit harder than others. Two exams, incremental project gradings and small homework assignments. Its not easy but its not difficult if you put in the time its not hard to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you can avoid him, please do. Lectures are dry, hes a tough grader, and at this point no one can get an A in his cse4471 class. Don't take him as a cse elective. His exams are memorization and his projects are graded very harshly because of his standards.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 6 quizzes, 2 exams and 4 projects. Although Dr. Champion is always glad to help, he is not a good teacher. His lectures are boring. It is hard to get a good grade.

He is very awkward and often doesn't understand the intent behind a question, making him either sound demeaning or go extremely off topic with his answer. You have to be up to date on material all the time because of pop quizzes. Textbook was mostly helpful; he was open to answer any clarifying questions that I had during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly, I learned nothing in lectures. Terrible professor.

All the labs were in python. We never learned any python. We had pop quizzes (exams) that took the entire class. Adam was awkward and couldn't answer questions clearly. Lectures added nothing to the slides, and the slides were pretty bare. The book was supposedly helpful for others, but I found it too boring to use. Goodluck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Possibly my least favorite professor I've had the mispleasure of having at OSU. The class only happens twice a week yet there's a pop quiz every two weeks that takes the entire period. The topics on these quizzes and midterms range from basic principles to gosh I hope you really remembered that one obscure detail that was talked about for 30seconds

Champion is one of the few professors I've had that has actually helped me understand the material. He's a genuinely nice person and he always wants to make sure people are clear on the topic before moving on. Networking is a dry topic in general, but I think he makes the best of it.
His lectures are pretty boring and he probably knows that too. All his pop quizzes and exam questions are from the book. No homeworks and a few labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sort of difficult because the lectures are dry and the book is also really dry. Averages are low but the labs are almost guaranteed 100% and the curve is nice.

Adam is a nice guy, but he is a HORRIBLE teacher. Lectures are worthless but mandatory; however, you either stay for a 30 min lecture or have a "work day" most days. Nothing from his lectures will help with the group project or the exams. The textbook for the class is really good and is the only way to really learn the material to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class was less of a "class" and more of "Teach yourself from this book because the lectures won't teach you anything." The book is pretty good, though, so if you want to teach yourself mobile app programming and get credit for it, you can make it through this class. The prof is nice but does not seem to know how to teach.

Champion gives dry lectures that are not aligned with the semester project. He is usually not helpful when answering questions and is just an awkward person. Attendance is mandatory, so basically everyone would work on their laptops and pay no attention to him. If you're interested in mobile apps and can teach yourself, though, the class is doable.

Words can't describe how awful of a professor he is, but I'll try. If you have a class with him, get ready to bear with learning nothing from and him and everything from the textbook. He doesn't even know what's going on, so don't bother asking him questions either. Highly recommend not going to class and just reading the textbook.

The best way to summarize my experience with Champion is to simply tell you about the first homework we were given. Nothing on the homework was covered in lecture, nor was it covered in the book. He gave us problems with no resources or mention of how to solve them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really didn't like this professor, it was so hard to pay attention in class and he goes straight from the book. I wish I skipped and just read the book and looked at his slides. One time he did go over a lab in class before it was due so we could see a similar example. Only time class was helpful. Hws taken from book. medium to tough labs.

A very socially awkward guy which makes him not the perfect teacher. The class itself if poorly organized though. The main point of it is the self done project, but the lectures don't match pace with the project well at all. You will be lectured on content that you won't use until a month later at times. Otherwise, he gets the job done
I had an awful experience in the class. Boring lectures, hard homeworks, hard labs, and hard tests. If you also aren't familiar with python, the class will be torture
Homeworks and labs  are easy. Exams are tough but Dr. Champion curves a lot. Lectures are not interesting and you have to learn by yourself.  Overall, an easy class.
Great curve!

Here's the deal.. I had a really good TA so it helped but between the project, attendance, and curve that he gives at the end of the class, overall it isn't all that bad. Like others said, lectures are BORING and the exams are difficult but just make sure you do well on everything else. The majority of the class bombs the exams so that helps too..

In one word: terrible. The only good thing is there is a decent curve in the class. Lectures are pointless to attend. Labs are tough and the exams are tough. Don't waste your time asking for help, because he has no clue.

For this class: Project is broken up, so most points are easily attained. Attendance is 10%, while Exams are manageable accounting for 40% of the class, which is easy if you attend. For other classes: His slides are color coded, anything in red or underlined will most likely be on the test. Study the red slidestext and his exams are fairly easy.
One of the worst professors in the OSU CSE department.  Avoid!

Did not know class material. When asked a question he would repeat what he said in lecture verbatim or would tell you to look it up in a book or would talk for 5 minutes, but never answer your question. Lab guidelines were sometimes vague. Did nothing about the terrible grader our class had (gave people no/wrong grades). Should not be teaching!

Nice guy but never helped with the labs if you had a question. He got confused frequently on the topics. Always told people to look up the book section...that's why we asked him though. Grader's okay, but not very helpful on labs either. Never graded harsh though. Adam grades too harshly on the midterm, so even with a curve it was tough...
Dry and confusing lectures, no lab discussion, homework that has nothing to do with lecture, and difficult exams.  He often seems to not know the answer to questions.  Avoid if possible.

Gives exams with short answer and does not give partial credit. Very harsh exam grader.  Very unclear lecturer and seems confused a lot.  Pretty much refused to help me at all on the lab when I came to  his office hours. Didn't seem to know what was required/expected for the labs he assigned.

I transferred with software I credit, so i wasn't really used to OSU components. But his lectures made it easy to understand. He tells us what's going to be in the exam and what are not. His lectures are monotonous but he does what he needs to do.

Not as bad as people make him out to be. He's really caring and definitely smart. His voice can be a bit monotone, so I record the his voice during lecture to re-listen when I'm tired. His exams aren't as difficult as everyone says, but there is definitely some challenge, but if you prepare and put in the effort, you can get an A.

lectures are boring at times but he's very intelligent and will answer your questions/dive deeper into topics if you ask. exams were very fair and he prepares you well for them. overall not the most engaging but a solid option for software 2, you can easily end with a high A if you put honest effort into labs, hw and projects.
Most dry lecturer I've ever had. The one time he made a joke the entire class couldn't stop laughing. Then 2 more months of dry lectures. Very knowledgeable though. Took SP25.

Very boring and monotonous lectures. Will have you questioning whether you even like computer science anymore. Hard to know what exactly is being taught in class when the homework, labs, and lectures, sometimes cover different topics. If you get this guy, get ready to become a proficient self-teacher.

It's actually insane how difficult his exams are compared to other Software 2 Professors. He gives absolutely no resources for exams, and barely reviews in class. Exams themselves are just the hardest coding questions possible back to back. If you get this guy make sure you put triple the amount of effort you normally would.

I genuinely GENUINELY believe that he doesn't want students to get good grades in his class. I mean he PURPOSEFULLY makes it so much harder than it has to be. He gives NO exam prep, his exams themselves are stupidly difficult and there's no curve or anything. He made the semester miserable for sure

My biggest issue with Adam is the lack of information provided to study for exams in a meaningful capacity accompanied with the fact that he never puts out his study info until the week of the exam. I would think with the overwhelming majority of the weight of the course being put on the exams we would get more to work with besides lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this guy's tests are impossible

He seems like a nice person but his lectures are really boring. They are all in a really monotonous tone which makes it hard to pay attention.
