His midterms are difficult and it's important to study if you want to do even remotely well on them. Overall projects weren't too hard, and the grading for them depends on your TAs.

Overall a very nice dude. He is always willing to answer questions and clearly wants you to succeed. Allows you to have a notecard on all exams as well. The class itself is somewhat difficult but he is a great teacher!!
I dropped out
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Deeply knowledgable of course material and very open to answering any questions you have. Lectures are very clear and concise, though expect a good amount of homework. Although grading is somewhat strict it is nonetheless quite fair. Exams are also very fair; as long as you put the time into labs/homeworks/etc this can be a very fulfilling class!

He's a nice person, always willing to help, and often provides extra study resources. His grading is fair. The course content, slides, and assignments are all department-designed, so there's not much to comment on. The exams get progressively harder, but overall they're reasonable and within the standard range.

"Tough but fair" is the best description I can give. The course itself is hard, and if you fall behind on lectures you will struggle. However, Grupa is helpful if you ask questions in class or during labs. Sometimes he delivers the lectures monotonously, but he still understands the material and will help you understand it too if you need help.

Lectures are kind of boring, but he gets the job done and is open to questions. He might not always give the best feedback, but he's always open to questions. Exams weren't that bad, just make sure to understand all the labs/lectures and you're good. TLDR: He's a good and smart guy but kind of quiet/shy

Just show up to and genuinely pay attention to lectures, and make sure you do/understand every lab and HW, and you should be fine. It's borderline useless to study for any exams if you just do these two things, because they're pretty much all you need to understand everything on the exams. He's always willing to explain anything that's confusing.
He's generally very helpful, although he can be a bit intimidating at first.  Asking questions about the projects is very helpful as well.

Professor Grupa is a nice professor, although somewhat dry. He and the TAs are always willing to answer questions about projects, so completing them early can be very helpful for grading as attention to detail is important. I found the exams he wrote to be somewhat difficult, so make sure to study for them if you want to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Grupa cares a lot about his students and was very approachable during the semester make sure to have good time management and get the projects done ahead of time to ask Prof questions at office hours

He's okay, he speaks in the most monotone voice ever and he's not super fun, but once or twice a semester he will be in a good mood and say the funniest thing you've ever heard as if he didn't just decimate your GPA on the last exam.
Very good teacher.

In the words of Gus Fring, "Acceptable." He tries his best. Good enough at teaching the course. He is more willing to help than he seems to be. Offers a pretty pure software 2 experience. Doesn't make anything easier or harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good professor, knowledgable on the content of the course, and is willing to answer questions. A little bit intimidating at first, but tests were relatively straightforward and graded fairly. Lectures are pretty boring, but get the job done.
Great lecturer, willing to help outside of class, and an "A" grade is obtainable in this course.
He's okay, he tries. I almost fell asleep during 50% of his lectures, all of his lecture is in a single tone, and classes were boring. Exams were okay though, not terribly hard.
Man's got a more bland voice than Justin Bieber

The class isnt easy by any stretch of the imagination, yet it is still doable. The lectures are prerecorded. Adam does a great job presenting the material and explaining the concepts. The quizzes arent easy, best advice I can give is read the question carefully and relook at the slides and labs before attempting the quiz. Would recommend!!

Hardest CSE class I have ever taken until now. The projects are fine however this class is based on tests not based on projects. Took this class online and quizzes make up 60% of your grade. You really need to think during the quiz because some of the answers can't be found on the lecture slides. There will be a lot of coding questions. Not enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The older reviews seem like it's a different person. The class was essentially without a professor, the labs were all done alone and all the lectures are pre-recorded. Anytime he would be asked questions he gave back a grumpy response. The quizzes were absurdly difficult. The TAs carried the class

Do not take him. Please don't. His quizzes are extremely difficult and timed, so it's very very hard to do well on them and they make up a lot of your grade. I had him on line and he required cameras to be OFF, so I never saw him or any of my classmates, which made working together on labs difficult. He was unapproachable and didn't explain well

Quizzes were so difficult considering how little time you got, and complexity of the questions. One time I attended his office hours to ask a question about lecture. He didn't like my question so he made someone else explain to me. Never attended another office hour again. Take advantage of TA's if you are in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Adam's class online. His labs were very frustrating because he does not require labs to be checked off and does not allow cameras to vie on, which makes it hard to work with other classmates, and know if you are doing labs correctly. He does though give detailed lectures which helps a lot and is very open to help in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Grupa fall 2020 so it was all online. His lectures were very well put together and he was good at explaining harder concepts. You're gonna have to study well for the quizzes since they're timed and a good percentage of the final grade. Sometimes he seems hard to approach but he has the best intentions and cares for his students success.

The quizes are the killer. You really do need to look through all the slides before the quiz. Other than that the course is pretty good, not having final saved my life cause I was about to fail another class.

I would say he is a good teacher, but I'm taking it online for this semester, and the quiz are extremely hard and short on time, you would have very limited time to do the quiz, and most of the question aren't "text book answers" in which you would have to apply a lot more on your own thinking. you would haveonly 40 mins to do extremely hard quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took the summer online COVID version of this class and was not a fan. He's kind of scary to approach in office hours and feels impatient to helping. The quizzes are also really hard like worse than exams on paper because they expect you to be cheating. I think he's an ok prof but didn't translate well to virtual in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Grupa consistently asked the class if we had questions and explained concepts further if necessary. He was reasonable with grading and accessible for help outside of class. Lectures were not the most interesting, but I think thats just the nature of the course.

Not much to say that the other responses haven't: professor Grupa can seem intimidating at first, but he is a nice guy that truly cares about the students. He's available during office hours and is happy to help. The 4.0 difficulty is if you're shooting for an A; if you just want a B or a pass, call it a 3.

He's awesome! I didn't like him at first because he seemed intimidating, but he cares a lot about his students and will go out of his way to help you. He's passionate and knowledgeable about CS, and can explain difficult concepts in a way that's easy to understand. His lectures were enjoyable and he can be pretty funny. Wish he taught more classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: At first, he seems really intimidating but GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS and talk to him cause he's a really nice person. He's very passionate about teaching so he'll answer any question you have until he's sure you understand the material. He's also very fair in grading but make sure you know the material and pay attention to the slides in class!

He is a funny guy and is great at explaining the lecture slides. His exams are fair; not incredibly easy nor hard, and he tells you exactly what you will and won't be tested on. Generous with partial credit for exams. He also recognizes when he makes an exam harder than usual and will grade easier or make the next exam easier to compensate.

Professor Grupa is there to help you, he also does a good job of explaining the material and making sure students are following along okay. I enjoyed this class a lot because he doesn't get sidetracked and makes things as clear as possible, there are also times where he'll discuss cool events happening in the modern CSE world.

For him, there is a time to play and their is a time to study. By play, he would sometimes start lectures by going over something significant happening in the news on any given day. That being said, he still made sure that he went through everything as much as possible so students would not be left on their own and he was very accessible during of.

Grupas extremely dry. Goes through material quickly and its all conceptual. Get accustomed to strange way material is presented for 2221/31 series, the entire sequence is presented like this, exactly like this. Its a difficult class with a ton of work, and he doesn't do examples in class, you have to teach yourself how to apply nearly all of it.

Grupa initially came off as condescending, but it soon became clear that his demeanor is simply easily misconstrued as uncaring. In reality, he really cares about his students and does everything he can to help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very passionate about computer science. If you attend his lectures and pay attention you'll do fine. Will take time both during and outside of class to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable guy, and a good teacher. Lecture was usually just going through slides, answering questions, and sometimes a funny or interesting story beforehand. I don't ask questions during class, but he created a good learning environment, and was also very helpful in office hours. Exams are hard, but he wasn't out to get you in grading.

Taking ASL with Ade was the best decision I made last semester. Adding a foreign language on top of a pretty rigorous schedule was daunting to me, but I could not be happier with my experience taking ASL with Ade. Attendance is very important as the quality of his in-person teaching is irreplaceable by online video. He genuinely cares about you!

He's one of my favorite professors. He genuinely cares about teaching and helping his students. He is deaf, so it makes you learn so much quicker because voices are off. He is super funny and I looked forward to going to class.

Professor. Oyeniyi was an amazing professor. His class is extremely fun and he genuinely cares about his students. My only minor issue was that dates of quizzes could sometimes be unclear but they were so easy it really didn't matter anyway.
Professor Ade is the GOAT. Favorite Professor this Semester (Fall ‘25)
Great teacher and very fun to be in class with. He cares about his students and would definitely take his class again.

The best professor I've ever had! He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Very humorous and gives his own experiences as a Deaf person, it helped with understanding. A lot of class participation and some projects but overall great course.

She will act like she has no issue but secretly find reasons to lower your grade. She made racist comments and use terms like aggressive to a black woman. Don't hang around & talk to her after class she'll use it against your grade. Created more stress because you don't know your final grade until the end. Very snarky, disrespectful.

I took this class as an elective, and I am not a Fisher student and have no marketing background, so I felt this class was a bit challenging. I would recommend Claire as a professor because she genuinely cares about her students success. I am not sure where all of the negative reviews are coming from because I really did enjoy her teaching style!!
Claire has a deep passion for marketing and helping her students, if you put in the effort this course is so much fun and fairly simple. Claire rocks and these reviews are so mean.

Claire was a great professor, truly cared about her students & always gave insightful meaningful feedback. I will say there is a lot of work, however it was all very informative and useful. By far one of the most beneficial classes I took in college. Also Claire is very knowledgable, & I loved learning from her. Really recommend taking this course!

not sure why Claire has all these bad reviews, I'm assuming she changed her Digital Marketing class because its mostly group work and activities. Quizzes are closed note but only 10 questions and combined 10% of your grade. She is funny and passionate about marketing and I am learning a lot from her class. It's fun and many grades are easy points.
she is a nice person but her quizzes and exams are hard, she puts questions that are very detailed and written somewhere in the textbook.

The homework assignments and reading the text do nothing to help detailed quuestions and exams, which are 60% of your grade by the way. 60 detailed questions on exams and homework does nothing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Claire is an incredible professor, and by far the most caring professor I have had at Ohio State. She wants you to succeed in the class, but more importantly, she wants you to succeed in your career. She communicates the material well, provides great life advice, and she grades very fairly. Put the work into this class and you will be golden!

This class is a semester long group project, where you meet with Claire once a week for ~25 mins. Some of the weekly assignments take a long time to complete, so don't procrastinate! She gives great feedback & going to office hours will really set your team apart. Put in the work, come prepared with questions, and you'll be set for success.
One group project, served in consulting role for a business, fun real world class that i think was one of the best to prepare me for an actual career
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had a great experience with Claire as a teacher for BUSML 4204. She cares a lot about her student's success but expects a lot of effort from them. She gives critical feedback, but only as a means to make your end project the best it can be. Ask as many questions as possible and put in the work and you're bound to be successful in her course.

The way this class is designed is abhorrent. The homework assignments and reading the text do nothing to help prepare for the proctored quizzes (and exams, which are 60% of your grade by the way). The readings/assignments are vague and chock-full of definitions that all sound the same and the exams, 65 questions each, are mostly definition based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes are proctored and more than 200 terms each, and there's essentially one every week. Exams and quizzes are difficult and lectures and readings don't help to prepare you at all. Claire does very little to help you and relies on having the textbook teach. One of those professors who believe that their class is the only one you're taking.

I had Claire for 3250 and she is my favorite professor in Fisher so far. 

Do not miss lectures, or else you will miss key information for the tests. The tests can be difficult... don't expect to do well if you don't prepare. But the class offers a 5% extra credit if you attend marketing studies which makes an A in the class very achievable.

Worst classes, Worst Teacher. Had a meeting with her right before the final and she told me that she is aware that most kids understand the materials but fail the test. However she wont change the exam format. Exams are 60% of your grade. She doesnt care about you at all but claims she does. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!! Find another teacher. Terrible!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have never received a B in any course before this one. And I worked harder than I ever have in any other class to try to get an A. You do 8 assignments a week plus hours of reading textbook chapters and taking notes on them, all for none of it to be on the exams. Why make us study the chapters when we will get asked the most random things on test
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I was scared to take her because of her reviews, but she honestly was a great professor. The exams are based on her lectures, and the other assignments are based on the textbook. There are a lot of chapters to know but if you watch her lectures and take notes you will do fine in the class. I would take her again.

Claire was a wonderful professor to have for marketing projects! She cares a ton about her students and wanted to give her time and guidance throughout the semester to ensure success in the class. She responds to emails quickly and was willing to review our presentation over Thanksgiving break, even though she didn't have to.

I would not take this course again. The class is much more work than it's worth. She has an outrageous policy where if u miss 1 assignment you cannot receive an A in her class. Her tests cover 1-9 chapters at a time with no study guide at all and are proctored so you need to memorize everything (65 questions in 80 min). DO NOT TAKE ONLINE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Adams covered a lot of material, but it was all relevant and she made sure to bring it back to the real world. Felt like I could actually use stuff she taught in a job in marketing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She seems really nice but DONT take the online class. She has it set up in a lazy format because she clearly doesnt want to hold zooms for the online lectures. She turned all the online classes into asynchronous and just records one of her in persons and posts it but the audio is horrible and unbearable to watch. Beware.

I love claire so much! she has been my favorite professor at OSU so far. she made lectures and class very engaging. assignments were not difficult however, they did require time to receive a good grade. she had guest speakers come in and speak to our class about their real-world marketing knowledge. the class had the opportunity for 5% extra credit

Her class isnt hard but shes quite literally unreachable outside of class, which is unacceptable in my opinion when youre teaching an entirely virtual class. Luckily her class is easy, but I emailed her three different times during the semester and never got a response. If you expect to communicate with your professors, dont take her class.

I felt like I learned a lot from Professor Adams. She truly cares about her students succeeding and she shows it, especially in a live setting. Not the usual blow-off work you would see in a Fisher class, but it's good to actually learn something from the class for a change. I'd rather take her class that one where I skate by and don't learn.

Overall this class seemed like it was a lot harder than it needed to be. There was so much reading and so many assignments each week, it felt excessive for a business core class. Definitely do all the extra credit, it is worth 5% and really boosts your grade. The final was impossible to study for, over 22 chapters, had to curve 8%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her first year at OSU, so it's understandable that she's still learning, but I was surprised by the lack of professionalism. The homework is extremely time consuming. Her exams have little to do with the homework. The exams are cumulative and proctored. It took another teacher to convince her to accommodate for an exam conflict. Rude over email.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is mostly book work, which is time-consuming but easy. Exams ruin the class. You're expected to know material from 22 chapters of the textbook for a closed-note exam. Nothing even remotely resembling a study guide is offered. 90-minute lectures aren't enough to summarize a full chapter, but you're expected to memorize 20+. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Extra credit 5% and lots of points from a ton of book assignments which is time consuming but nice. If you complete all of that its easy to get at least a B. However the exams are ridiculous, the final covers 22 chapters closed note, and the lectures are vague. Praying she curves the final.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was horrible. Avoid this professor at all costs. So much homework every week that wasnt even applicable to the exams. She made lectures wayyyyy too long when they shouldnt have been and had way too much information loaded in. She also automatically discounts you from an A if you miss an assignment. Exams were cumulative and proctored.

Her 1st semester at OSU, understand but clearly shows. Huge amount of busywork that rarely translated to exams and felt like it was there she didn't have to grade anything herself. Very unclear about what content to study for exams and exams were very inconsistent with what was focused on during class. Final exam is 100 questions 100 minutes. Yucky

Unclear on what to study exactly for exams, Too much information to do in a weeks worth along with 5 other classes. Workload for this class is more of a 4-5 Credit hour course, This was this teachers first semester at Ohio State so of course we got the worst of it, Take a different professor for this course

Her first semester as a Prof at OSU. Really dry lectures that are recorded, with lots of out of class work compared to other marketing professors. Extra credit up to 5% which is pretty easy to do. Mini simulations that are some of the worst assignments that you will do while in the business school.

Dr. Ibrahim is a rather dry lecturer and, in my opinion, gives very challenging and unfair exams. He listens to feedback, and we got a curve for the exams, but his class felt a lot harder than it needed to be.

His class was very difficult. He would never respond to my emails so I had to rely on the TA. Attendance was 10% and was mandatory for labs and lecture. However, if you read the textbook, both were not helpful. I did like that the grade breakdown wasn't weighted heavily on one project or exam tho
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Adil has certainly improved from what past reviews have said. Echoing others: he is very kind, caring, and accommodating and truly wants all of his students to do well. He is VERY hard to reach outside of class, but always makes time after class to ask questions. Exams are hard, but he curved and gave us extra credit, very open to feedback as well.

(For 2221), He usually doesn't reply to emails, his lectures are worse than other professors, exams are harder than other professors. He often says that he is very generous in giving grades, but you won't feel it at all, unless you are about to fail the course and you can benefit from his curve. In general, I don't know how to evaluate him.

(for 2221) it's obvious he knows what he's talking about but the lectures weren't very helpful and a chunk of his office hours were skipped for some reason or another. be prepared to use outside resources to learn the things you're expected to.

also, grades are HEAVILY weighted toward exams. i had a B+ before the final and got screwed over, lol

It was hard to follow his lectures, especially if you sit at the back. He is often late for classes, and many times he skipped office hours due to his personal issues. However, he also tried to improve his previous teaching style
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For 2221: Adil was nice and showed genuine interest in what he was teaching, but he didn't know what was going on most of the time. He forgot that we had a final, graded the first midterm incorrectly, and the second midterm had an average of about 60. If you have him, be prepared to fight for your grade.

He seems to have taken past feedback to heart and made improvements. Clearly laid out what would be on the exams, so there were no surprises. Labs and homework were straightforward, and he is very friendly and accessible outside of class. It's great to see when professors adapt based on criticism. Highly recommend

Adil was a great professor and I really enjoyed his teaching style. It's a bit hard to see and understand things from the back of class but front row it's much better. The content was difficult but I felt like he did a good job simplifying things. Exams were also not easy but he accommodated for it. You definitely need to study a lot for exams.

Definitely the worst professor I've had. He showed up late almost every single day to lecture, and would often forget where he left off with teaching and re-teach slides he had already taught. "Teaching" is also a loose word because I learned nothing. He also graded nothing until finals week which made it hard to know what I knew. Definitely avoid.

He barely taught and when he did he just read directly off of the slides. Does not write his own exams or teach what will be on the exams. Had the audacity to talk on the phone with tech support (and had one of them come in too) through our ENTIRE final exam which was very disruptive. He will come up with a BS excuse for all of his shortcomings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: please just look at his Wisconsin RMP where he used to teach at. Same thing different school. Uses older midterms from other professors will tell you it is his own work despite getting it from the university repository therefore the content on the exam will not reflect what is taught to that point. Expect little help on hw or labs since not his.

He's nice but please don't take this section unless you already know the material. You will not learn anything that you don't already know. Asking questions will lead you to a tangent on something that was already discussed or will miss the point entirely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to learn something in systems 2 then do not take this class. His lectures are awful and you do not learn anything in them. His tests are completely different from what he teaches in class. His carmen material is also not good either. Just take someone else.

He is very caring, and is willing to listen to feedback on his shortcomings. Unfortunately, that feedback is frequently because he is not teaching well enough to do well on the homework or exams. He may have a lot of patience, but the rest of us don't.
I want to like him because he's a nice guy but his teaching is awful and he is disorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This professor is a really nice guy however, from my experience and students from other colleges that have taken him this is his shortfalls. 
- Inaccessible
- Tests do not equate what is learned or on homework (study ahead)
- loses track of what has been taught so you will go over the same stuff a bunch
- Does not know lecture content ahead of time

So extremely passionate and knowledgeable. He is a phenomenal lecturer and he taught this class incredibly well. I would absolutely recommend taking this course with him. The material was fascinating and the course itself was easy and engaging, even though the topic may initially sound intimidating.
Def take him more for his lectures than any class work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Al-Jallad is the best professor I've had. He's intelligent and extremely passionate about his field, with an infectious enthusiasm that makes lectures lively and interesting. You can get away with skipping some readings, although you'll probably be hooked enough to explore them on your own. Don't worry about the grades; enjoy the experience.

Professor Al-Jallad is one of the most passionate professors whose passion is undoubtedly matched by their mastery of the subject. Lectures are thought-provoking and easy to follow. He's more concerned with making students just as fascinated he is than he is with assignments. Generous feedback and available for office hours with tea! Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best professor and best class at OSU by a million. Every class had very very high-level discussions which I could honestly never get anywhere. OSU needs to cherish Ahmad and this class and publicize it a lot more because I believe every Muslim or anyone interested in Islam NEEDS to take this course. He is a very light grader and very personable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ahmadi made waking up for an early class better. She is extremely caring and passionate about teaching for the world instead of teaching only for the class. She is extremely kind and will work with you. I appreciated her teaching methods and learned a lot in this class through tons of class discussions (felt v comfortable)

While obviously knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches, Dr. Ahmadi is painfully unorganized. She is easygoing and cares deeply about her students, but is constantly changing her mind on the criteria for the readings and assignments and takes weeks to grade. Ultimately a relatively easy class, but can be frustrating.

Would avoid. 

Thinks highly of herself and looks down on others. Entitled is the word that comes to mind. 

Not balanced. Not fair. Not objective. 

Fails to understand context and is generally non observant.

Awful person. 

Resorts to being a keyboard warrior and forcing her opinion on individuals regardless of circumstances or negative consequences. 

Should lose her job. Immediately. Maybe then she will see the negative effects of being a keyboard warrior and negatively impacting other people's lives!

Dr. Ahmadi is extremely passionate, and it shows through her teaching. I had a great time in this course, it was relatively easy, and as long as you do the readings, you're pretty much guaranteed an A. Extremely kind and thoughtful, and the class was engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall I loved taking this class with Dr. P. She truely cares for her students and wants them to succeed. Their were different reading prompts each week where you would have to annotate and some homework assignments that really did not take long. 10/10 recommend taking this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The hardest class ever. It ruined my GPA!

Micro 5536 is a difficult class, but Dr. Yousef is there to answer questions and offer assistance. Starting studying early and studying often, memorizing the many details and critical thinking will give you the best result. Dr. Yousef makes you earn the grade, but it is possible to do well!
I don't think the assistants or instructor were disorganized but the grading was a mess. The course is difficult but critical for food science students.

The lecture is fine, but the reviews are the lab are accurate. Disorganized, unprepared instructor and TAs take off points for following exact direction or over things never told, like question set format. This lab is a serious embarrassment to this school. Avoid if you can.

He's one of the most brilliant and inspirational people I've ever met. Yet, his exams are so hard and there are pop quizzes here and there. Absolutely the hardest Food Science class I've ever taken (even harder than OChem). OChem is a piece of cake compared to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Avoid this class at all costs. It's an embarrassment to the Microbiology Department. Poorly organized, grading is extremely meticulous, assignments worth virtually nothing take hours to complete because of formatting requirements and vague instructions. Be prepared to lose points for following directions and stay over for 30+ minutes many times.

Don't take this class. The class sounds interesting, but the professor is not helpful. He does not post keys for quizzes/exams and does not give you any practice problems. Quizzes are unannounced.  You will just be making flashcards to try and memorize the content. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Being a Meat Science student, I will be using the information I (should have) learned from this course. However,  the instructor does not explain his notes or importance of charts/graphs very well. Knowing the lecture handouts will not receive a passing grade. Tests are very detail oriented, miniscule details are necessary to grade high. Avoid.

It is true that Dr. Yousef's class could be challenging. Memorization and exceptional note takings are key to getting good grades. Having said that, if you come to class and take a good note, you will be fine. I am a huge fan of microbiology and his lectures were inspirational. I learned so much from his class and it was so worth it.

The class is ridiculous!  You can know virtually all the slides but still find a way to do poorly.  He expects you to know details that are not on slides and is picky about spelling when he spells words wrong on the notes.  He grades on a curve when the class is not even a weeder course.  He does not have office hours and is not helpful.  AVOID!!!

memorize, memorize and memorize!!!!! the course is food microbio but the approach is clinical microbio with little food topics on the side.... course is for graduate level but there is no analysis but purely memorization!!!!! we are thinkers, not photocopy machines to put every word and detail to stay in our minds!!!

prof does not explain details/significance of tables/graphs,etc...he just wants you to memorize everything at all cost!!!! and he cares about spelling and ironically, pronunciation as if the clasd has an oral exam. i am a grad stude but i do not recommend him as a teacher to this course!!!

(con't) for graduate students? the class averages were pretty low and many of us didn't know if we were going to make it, i got a c+ and i can tell you that is what i earned. i didn't take the labs, but from what i hear they are a lot of work and you may not want to take the lecture and lab together with a full schedule..

(con't)for graduate students? the class averages were pretty low and many of us didn't know if we were going to make it, i got a c+ and i can tell you that is what i earned. i didn't take the labs, but from what i hear they are a lot of work and you may not want to take the lecture and lab together with a full schedule..

this class is extremely hard but i don't think it is fair the way everyone is bashing professor yousef. he does his best in presenting the material, but it is up to you as a student to take the time to study everyday. i will admit that he is an anal grader (he will take off points for spelling, etc.) but what do you expect when the class is meant f

The worst class that I have ever taken and will ever take! I don't really see anyone doing well unless you have a photographic memory, because that's what you need to get an A. When a prof. asks what particular organism causes a particular disease off a list of 20 organisms and then takes off for spelling...on a quiz, you're in trouble.
it is note an easy class and it is very tough. This course is designed for graduate students. just to let you all know

The lectures are informative and relate well to current events. The exams are VERY specific and detail oriented.  Expect to know specific numbers and minor details about everything!  I can't complain about the lecture being difficult since it is a 600 level class.  However, the lab is very disorganized, lots of work, and the TAs are clueless.

This is a serious course with plenty of information to learn. The instructor brings meaningful examples, sometimes touching on our own lives. I don?t recommend it for anyone wanting easy course, get an ?A? and learn nothing. There is plenty of this type of courses already at OSU.

this class is a tough one.  Don't miss lecture and definetely take good notes.Lecture is ok; however the lab is a lot of work.  I think dr Yousef is a good professor ; he's a good grader but because the class is 600 level; it's designed for grad students so you have to think about stuff in order to do well.

i really dont understand what youre supposed to know for the tests. i have never had a class where you can 100% understand everything in the notes like the back of your hand and only be able to answer 65% of the questions on the test. quiz average is like 40%. the content is definitely interesting but a really tough class.

He is by far the worst that I have EVER had! He makes his pop quizes & exams as hard & as tricky as he can. 70% of the material he tests you on aren't even in your notes! It's the only class were I could know the notes he gives perfectly and still fail the exam!! And don't even bother going to him for help. He is terrible! AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!!!

took it thinking it'd be easier than any other available class... wrong, expect a lot of work especially in the lab.   the lecture is not that bad a lot of repetitive learning but still this teacher does not give you much information to go on when trying to answer questions properly (doesn't want abbreviations for anything)
not a fun class

Do NOT take Food Microbiology 636.01 or 636.02! These classes only intentions are to ruin your G.P.A. Understanding and fairness are not qualities of the class and the actual Professor absolutely does not know what he is talking about. I usually do not take the time to write bad about a class or even anybody for that matter but PLEASE be aware!

(3312, not on RMP list)
Good guy and solid prof. He talks really fast so be prepared to either have a hand cramp or revisit some slides later. Because he gets through lectures quick, class usually got out 15-20 minutes early. Extremely versed on African history and passionate about the content. All required readings posted online. Very easy grader.
You will not learn much of anything from him and he is unwilling to help his students out. Just an overall terrible professor.

Even though the class was entirely online due to COVID, I did learn a lot from the readings and online forums. The content was very interesting, but you do have to read some very long and slow passages. It is a pretty easy A though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is normally cut short, but not unreasonably. Always provides extra insight as to which lectures to focus on for quizzes and is available upon request to assist with papers if one is question the criteria or what direction to take. Overall enjoyable class and very nice professor, am taking another course with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sikainga clearly knows his stuff and the content of his classes is very interesting. The class was not engaged but thats not his fault. Some said he was boring but everyone understood that he was a fair grader. I liked him a lot, and I would take a class with him again!
Hes a great teacher. His content is actually extremely interesting and if you show up to clsss then youll pass. Hes very nice and tries to connect with students but the class was quiet.

Just by showing up to class and paying attention, you will likely easily pass this course. The criteria for each quiz and exam are clear. My class bombed a quiz and he was nice enough to offer a makeup quiz. Nice guy, interesting subject, he wants you to participate with the material and by doing so you'll easily pass
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He posts the power-points from lecture online and they contain everything that are on the quizzes and in the books. He even tells you what power-points to look at for each quiz and the final.

Lectures feel ungodly long as he reads line by line from his power point.  He knows his stuff but is incapable of relaying any information in a clear and interesting way.  Also readings are long and pointless, I was better off making crap up for exam.  So yeah don't even think about taking this class. You will regret it.

All he did was simply read off the powerpoint. Really no point in going to class even though he does take regular attendance. He's also not very helpful. Most of the time, you will not find him at office hours or get replies back from email. Super late in posting grades. He's knowledgable it seems but did not learn a lot. Would NOT recommend at all
Doesn't explain assignments, never went over the syllabus, readings are long and irrelevant

It is important to stay awake since most of his information doesnt even come from the books.  For the tests though, he requires outside information from the books, and if you dont use it, you wont get a very good grade on the exams.  He is extremely intelligent and knowledeable if you want to discuss things with him outside of class.

Dr. Sikainga's class was disappointing at best. Most of my classmates agreed that he seemed not to want to be teaching our course, which was evident through consistently late arrival, unreasonably early dismissal, dull lectures, zero discussion, and minimal to no outside assistance. Don't take this class if you actually want to learn something.

Kahraman is a masterclass in delivering lectures. Despite the amount of content in the course, his teaching never feels rushed and he takes time covering plenty of examples. He has high expectations but is a super cool and funny prof. Exams and homeworks are very fair. Go to his lectures and you'll get a lot out of this course
He's very funny and taught the material really well. Some concepts can be confusing, but that's just the nature of the class and he did a solid job of teaching it. Made the class pretty fair.
He's a good professor, and made a pretty tough class fair. Homework and exams are all doable as long as you put in the work. He's pretty funny too.

I took this class because it was a technical elective and it fit in my schedule, but it ended up being my favorite class. Dr. Kahraman seems to genuinely want to teach his students the material as well as keep them entertained. He is by far the best mechanical engineering professor I've had, and I had him in my final semester of undergrad.

Very good teacher. He makes the class very interesting even if the material is boring. Gives a lot of practical examples. Funny guy. I loved this class. The grade is split between 2 midterms and a Final. Homework is only 10%. I'm not good with numbers , so I got only a B+, but  the subject is not tough at all.
One of the best professors I've ever had.  He's very interested in the material he teaches, and he's very organized.  He likes Pink Floyd so he's OK in my book.
No Comments

No curve, it seemed; grade weighted almost exclusively toward exams.  Worked very hard on homework, had what I felt was a great grasp on the material, got a lower grade than I expected.  VERY helpful professor, though; presents material well!

He assumed an honest assignment was AI and from there on was passive aggressive with grading & email responses. It's like he has a complex to make sure people who visibly care don't get a fair grade (like a weird power move & would intentionally mess with grades). I took this course out of genuine interest for the material and completely regret it.
Dr. Graber is extremely knowledgeable about the field of bioethics and had very interesting material to discuss and learn about.  Definitely one of my favorite courses I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The structure of the course is very clear, however, far too much work for a GE course. Written grading was subjective and did not reflect all points of view. Take the class if it is required, otherwise find something easier that won't take up too much of your time. Post-tests were written super confusingly that it made some questions illegible.

Overall, good professor. He's very thorough about AI, which may unintentionally penalize you if you're naturally a good writer, so keep a record of timestamps when writing. Also, no matter how close you are to getting the next letter grade up at the end of the semester, forget about it as he doesn't believe in rounding grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was very easy to contact and although there were a lot of assignments sometimes they were fairly easy to complete. Also allows to make up credit for the midterm which was nice. He is very big on COAM and will report anything that he thinks might be AI. His lectures were also simple and entertaining with his humor.

I loved his class! It seems like it will be a lot of work but I don't think it is, but I found the class very enjoyable! You usually have a quick reading, pre test (completion grade), discussion post (completion grade), and a post test. The pre-test and and post-test are the same questions and only like 8 questions. Great Professor and easy class!

Dr. Bob is a gem. From day one, he says "I'm excited to learn alongside you". He genuinely wants students to succeed. He has a beautiful way of sandwiching a helpful critique between a beginning and ending praise such that you feel how much he cares about forming a good relationship with you. I've had three classes with him and enjoyed every one!

The professor doesn't really use the website. He didn't add due dates, so make sure(!!!) you add them to your calendar from the syllabus. Class was in-person, all students were female, and he made several creepy comments. Mostly lectured about himself. He's a nice guy but not my style of professor. Maybe his classes are better online.

Wonderful professor ! He is very knowledgeable, gives excellent in depth constructive feedback and very supportive and understands the challenges of being a grad student and working FT. I am currently taking my second course with him.

Bob was AMAZING. I cannot express how great this class was with Bob, it is clear how incredibly passionate and dedicated bob is to his clients, students, and work. He was a personable, caring, insightful, and overall wonderful person. I wish I had more time to take another course with Bob.

Bob was such an incredible professor, especially for someone just starting graduate school. He is very clear about what his expectations are and often begins and ends class with a self care exercise. Bob is an absolutely fantastic professor and you will be lucky to have him as your mentor.

This professor has poor pedagogy. He lectures for hours at a time without having the students do in class activities, loses track of what is he saying in the middle of the stories he tells, and prioritizes telling stories about the most difficult clients he has had over going over the texts, power points, or having students practice skills.

If you ever get the chance to take Bob do it right now! He is one of the best teachers I have had during my MSW. He wants you to pass, will give extra help, funny, and very caring. This class had some bigger projects but he told you everything he was looking for to make it easy to get an A in his class.

Bob is the best professor I have had in my entire educational career. He is an easy grader, but he provides a lot of helpful and encouraging feedback. Not only does Bob tell you he cares about his students, he shows it as well. He's also hilarious. I wish he taught all of my courses because he's a great professor and a great person.

Bob is very understanding and a fun/funny guy. He brings cookies and really cares about his students. Show up, put some thought into assignments and you will pass. This class is also pass/fail. It would be a shame not to take him. He gives plenty of case study examples.

Bob is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is super engaging and gives great feedback. He truly cares about his students. I learned more in his class than any other class because he made it applicable.

Bob always connected the class back to his practice. He is one of the most realistic professors I've had thus far: I came out of his class knowing what to expect in the social work field. He is understanding and genuinely cares about student success. He always kept a 4 hour class interesting and had reasonable expectations for assignments.
Good professor, good class very clear, and you learn something.

Dr. Bob is a gem to the MSW program at OSU. He truly cares for his students and will gently challenge you to continue learning and perfecting your skill. His lectures are inspirational (peppered with real-life stories) and he treats you as a colleague from the very first day. Take any class by this man; you won't regret it.

I love Dr Bob! He genuinely cares about his students and clients. His class is enjoyable and upbeat. He encourages students to interact with one another and get to know each other. He teaches useful integrative mind body spirit interventions that are helpful for clients with practically any diagnosis, and also great for personal use.

Great class! He is a great professor and I will continue to take his classes. I even signed up for an 8am with him next semester because it's worth it! He cares a lot about what he's teaching and his students. I learned so much from his class!

Dr. Ahern is an absolutely wonderful professor who cares passionately about teaching and students.  He values creativity, and encourages students to keep on growing.  His assignments are reasonable, flexible, and can be completed with little to no stress.  Dr. Ahern ties his own life experiences into lectures.  You will want to go to his class.

Professor Ahern is the best teacher I have ever had. He is passionate as well as compassionate, has countless captivating social work stories, and genuinely loves teaching students going into the field. A great resource!!

Bob was the first professor I've had who has ever REALLY held my attention the entire course (which was surprising because our class was ~3.5 hours long!). He was so entertaining and engaging, and his stories always illustrate the lesson he's teaching perfectly. I love the experience and passion he brings to his students! Try to get in his class!!!
Very funny, nice, helpful, and knowledgeable!
He is an amazing teacher.  Extremely passionate and knowledgeable.  I would highly recommend him and take him whenever possible.
Awesome! will take him whenever possible- makes Saturday class enjoyable!
Ahern is a great guy, there is a reason why his classes are always full.  He tells lots of funny/relevant stories and is a fair grader.

Dr Ahern is the best prof!  Take this class for Individual Counseling if at all possible.  He concentrates on CBT to the point where you feel fully capable of actually implementing it!  Also, it's a GREAT prep class for comps. He's highly entertaining and so nice to students!! TAKE HIM!!

Dr Ahern is the best prof I have had so far at OSU.  His lectures are SO applicable and he uses TONS of great examples.  He's funny, flexible, and COMPLETELY understands his students.  He really makes the material applicable to your life.  All students are captivated during class because he's so interesting!  TAKE HIM!!!!

THIS WAS A GRAD LEVEL (MSW I) SPRING 09 CLASS & IT WAS A WASTE OF MY MONEY-IT WAS A JOKE. NICE MAN BUT THE CLASS WAS HIGH SCHOOL CONTENT AND NOT PRACTICAL, RELEVANT, ORGANIZED AND DEFINITELY NOT GRADUATE COURSE WORTHY-AVOID HIM IF YOU WANT TO LEARN-IF YOU'RE JUST IN THERE FOR A GRADE THEN YOU'RE OK-I THOUGHT IT WAS A JOKE W/O A PUNCH LINE-TERRIBLE!

Professor refuses to post completed lecture notes after class, claiming they will be stolen by AI if she does so. This makes it much more difficult to study for the exams, but the class is relatively easy so this doesn't end up mattering as much.

Prof Abell is great! While lecture can be boring at times and long-winded, it's a lot of good info! Groups make this course fun and engaging. Homework is minimal and pretty easy. Exams are very fair and mostly MCQs--review the readings!! My only gripe is brevity being encouraged when it wasn't practiced. Otherwise, great prof, great class!

Loved Professor Abell. She's very down-to-earth and understands what the students are going through. The projects are fun, hands-on, and informative. The exams are taken on Carmen and relate directly to the course material. I had an advantage that I had previously taken a manufacturing class, but if you are new to it, she explains it nicely.

cares a lot about mental health and her students, loved how understanding she was. would require lengthy readings that were hard and academic pieces that were boring though, is an easy grader just have to put some type of effort in. loves to have discssion in the classroom

Professor Abell is fantastic. The only professor in my four years to call students by name, and shows she really cares. The group projects were well structured and graded fairly. This class was a breeze and really fun. Has a passion for engineering. Her lectures can get kinda rambly, but honestly that's just her personality. Great professor.

Annie was amazing! She will answer all of your questions and talks to you like a normal person. She doesn't look down on you because you are a student and she is a faculty member. She really wants you to succeed and if you go to class and do all of the homework and lab reports, you will.

This class is only 2 credit hours but feels like 5. The papers are a ton of work and you are constantly doing group projects. Annie is very nice but at times long winded. She is willing to help if you need it. Overall a good professor, but be ready to put in the effort. Do not buy the 1182.02 textbook we didn't take the quizzes so it was useless!
Annie Abell made me want to stay in engineering. The class workload is a lot but Annie makes it fun and worth while.
I loved Annie!  She was one of the best professors I've had at OSU.  She always tried to bring something fun into the class.  I would definitely take another class with her!

Great class. She's really there for you. The TA's were excellent. However, for a two credit hour class (1181.02), it had the work of a 4 or 5 credit hour class (lab reports and the like). But beyond that, the class was straightforward the grading was fair, with extra credit (to our surprise). Just do your homework (always something).
Annie is amazing, her class was difficult, because engineering is.. But her teaching style helped me so much. Also get to know her, ended up with an A-, but aksed her to bump to an A and she did.

Annie is a great and smart professor. She made this class material easy to understand. Turn in your homework and pay attention in her class, then you will do great. TAs are also helpful in her class. I strongly recommend her if you can take class with her.
Very helpful instructor for a very time intensive course. I would definitely take a class with this teacher again.

She was very helpful in and outside class. Lectures were easy to follow, but it seemed she wasn't interested in the subjects herself. She was very friendly, knowledgable, and overall a great professor.

Although I said she is an easy teacher, the subject material and workload is heavy. She makes her own powerpoints (good thing) and sometimes rewrites the departmental homework when she thinks the instructions are confusing (good thing). If you have to take this class, try and get her as the Professor.

Class was okay. The TA's graded the homework,labs,memos,assignments. She does not really grade them. TA's were harsh in grading. She is always willing to help. She can be lenient at times(she only took 10% off a late memo because she felt like being nice. Overall a good teacher. She is very good looking too.
Not a great professor. Nice and friendly, but grades rather harshly and seemed disinterested in the class.
Annie is great. Her class is totally clown shoes and she once told me I look like a young Nigel Terry. TALK ABOUT A COMPLIMENT! Take her class (don't beg for compliments).
This was her first time teaching this class but she's pretty good. She's very helpful and answers everything she can or gets someone else to answer it if she can't. Overall, would recommend.
She is a pretty good teacher.  I would recommend going to class.
Very fun and very nice. But will grade you way harsher than you think she will. So beware.
Annie is young, fun, and very helpful. Definitely recommend taking this course with her!
Just amazing. Fun class, need to show up for sure.

She is a very helpful and upbeat teacher. I enjoyed taking her class. It's not that difficult as long as you complete the homework and projects, but you do have to show up to class. I thought she was pretty funny and would take another class with her.
BEST grad student to have teach! She knows her stuff, is always willing to help, and is a generally fun & sweet person!!
annie is super helpful!! this course can be a little hard if youve never done technical drawing before, but annie knows her stuff!

Dr. Lindo is among the best professors I have ever experienced at the University. She has a vast wealth of knowledge in her field, has plentiful connections, has incredibly engaging lectures, and is invested in every student. She isn't condescending and exudes her entertaining personality in every lecture. Even as an engineer, favorite class taken.
I learned a lot in this class and Dr. Lindo was cool when I went to office hours but it was a lot of work for me. I feel like she meant well and gave extra credit but it was a gen ed class.

Very rude professor did not help students when asking questions . Every time someone asked a question she would get very smart. For the final, we did a review that was NO help at all. She's also a very harsh grader. Would not take her unless it's your last option.

I enjoyed Dr Lindo and the material for the class, but it was definitely way too much work for a gened. I managed to get an A but this class had way too much busy work when it shouldn't have. Wouldn't recommend one way or another on this class to be honest but I didn't hate it as someone who's interested in the music we learned about.

Dr. Lindo is a nice and knowledgeable instructor. But her course had way too many things to do. For a GE class, it had more work than my Chem 1210 class. She has two quizzes, assignments in the class, and other random things every week, making it hard to keep up. She grades harshly and the class is harder than it has to be. DO NOT TAKE THE CLASS!

Fantastic professor. I obv saw the other reviews so I know its repetitive but Jorge cares a lot about his students and our wellbeing. He pushes you basically every class and you need to be okay w him calling on everyone every class but also Jorge made me feel safe making mistakes in front of everyone?? Slay tbh 10/10 would take again
Eloquent but quite poor in his understanding of the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Jorge is a great guy, funny and cares about his students. But you have to work for this class, the class is taught in German and he called on students randomly every class to answer questions. Grammar heavy class but he offers help outside of class if you reach out. Definitely not an easy A but worth it in my opinion.

Jorge is a phenomenal teacher. The entire course is taught in German and Jorge really pushes you outside of your comfort zone. Despite this, he is really lenient with due dates and really cares about his students. You really have to try hard to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: It pains me to write this, but if you are not a German major, or didn't do very well in German 1101, do not take German with Jorge. Don't get me wrong, he is a great guy, cares about his students, and is passionate about the material. The only problem is he teaches about 80% in German, so if you aren't already good you will fall behind quickly.

Amazing German teacher. He cares a ton about his students and their understanding. He speaks very clearly and wants his students to participate. Just don't get on your phone during class and he will like you. I had an A- and he rounded it up to an A for me without even having to ask. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, great guy overall. Cares tremendously about his students (words can't do justice about how much he cares about his students and their success) and is so passionate about teaching. This class is intense though - tons of assignments, participation required in nearly every class, mandatory lectures, etc.

There's really too much to say about Jorge. He's just a great teacher: fun, helpful, serious when it's needed. He's a 4 difficulty in class because he pushes you out of your comfort zone, but the actual tests are fair and not there to get you. He's a cool guy and really makes learning the language fun. If he teaches 1103, I hope to take it with him

Lectures were good. A decent knowledge of proof based math is required that I didn't have which caused me to struggle early on. Content is very difficult and there is a lot of it. He records all of his lectures and post them on the same day which is very nice because attendance isn't mandatory. Overall hard class but he gives enough to succeed.

The course is hard- you have to put in a fair amount of work for the homeworks and midterms. Project is graded very lineantly. Abhishek is helpful on office hours and teaches VERY well. You have to follow the lectures very closely to get a hold on the material but it is by no means un-doable.

Abhishek is a great professor. The class material wasn't super tough, but you need to be on top of things. Ask him questions during office hours and he'll do what he can to help you understand the material. Could've done a better job with the material in the 2nd half of the course, but overall I learned a lot. Would definitely take him again :).

Great professor in the field of optimization. There are 6 HWs that may take a lot of time, but as long as the material is understood, you will get a good grade. Tests are generously graded. A grade over 90% makes you an A (approximately 50% of people get an A in this class).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is an excellent professor. He is very knowledgeable in the field of optimization and tries to give examples from different domains with electricity markets being his favorite. The lectures are useful in understanding the concepts and homeworks deal with their applications. Since it's a 5000 level course he does not cover proofs of many theorems
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is one of the most inspirational professors I have had- he really pushes you to work hard and give it your best. He is old school with teaching, (blackboard and no spoon feeding) but very friendly and accessible. Truly wants his students to learn the course and do well in their lives!

I was very interested in learning Optimization and Controls until I took his course on Optimization in Fall 2017. He just write some mathematical equations on board without explaining the purpose or the applications. He seems too lazy to make slides. He considers himself to be very smart. I took a ton of courses at OSU and this was the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Overly Difficult. Posted lectures have little or nothing to do with homework. Code expected in R, but I'm not sure he knows R. Many wrote in discussion that we understood the math but didn't know how to write the R code. I have seen no evidence that could teach the code he's requiring. Don't do this to yourself.

Theory based controls, nothing is applied. A lot of derivations and doesn't explain why what he's teaching has an impact in the EE field. Find someone more applied to be able to apply 3050 in future courses.

Would recommend another teacher for 3050. More mathematical based than putting the concepts to use in MatLab codes, like I've heard that other  teachers do. Low class averages on easy tests, which doesn't make sense. There are better professors for this course.

Most boring class, there is a reason less then half the class goes to lectures. class average was a 72% but the grade scale he used was very kind. exams and quizzes were not similar to any homework what so ever so unless you know the material extremely well you will not be getting an A. I  100% recommend taking another prof.

Great professor, can't remember the last time I enjoyed lecture so much every time.  Doesn't write too fast, giving you a chance to actually think about what we're talking about.  His approach to lecture made the material understandable and not confusing or intimidating.  Gives some challenging HW problems, and exams are completely fair almost easy

I enjoyed Professor Gupta's class. Solid guy, gives a lot of information on the exam paper to help you pass. He is really trying to change his image from a tough grader to a more helpful professor, and I would say he succeeded. I would say just like any class if you come to class, take notes, and engage with the professor you will will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is the only teacher for the 30X0 series of classes that I actually enjoyed the class of or went to the lecture of. I still missed a good number of classes, but he was always extremely helpful during office hours and he is one of the main reasons I am going to take more controls classes in the future.

Posts nothing to Carmen. Moves too fast during lectures. Skips too many steps during examples. Some test/quiz questions don't match homework questions which leaves students unprepared for exams. 5031 was easier than this. Caring but hard to learn from. There needs to be a serious curve for this course. I'll edit this post once I get my final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Smart guy, but really tough when it comes to HW and quizzes/tests. He just doesn't seem to get teaching undergrad level. Probably good for grad school, but not great for undergrad.

Had him for two courses. Brilliant professor who knows the subjects in-depth and does a very good job at summarizing the books. As another person has pointed out, the optimization class relies heavily on proofs/Multivariable calculus, which he assumes you know, but that's more of a fault of the course's designer! Don't skip class! Take notes!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great!

Nice professor. Very available and cares about his students. Gives advice and has a good sense of humor. Knows the subject very well but has the assumption that students know math that is not part of the prerequisites, like multivariable calculus, which makes the class a bit hard. Mathematical approach to optimization.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: All he did was write notes on the board, never did a good job of explaining or teaching. Then expected you to know everything he did on tests.

He gives two week to do each homework assignment, which are based out of the textbook. He will do his best to answer your questions and is pretty personable. His tests can be long and tough but he curves fairly at the end. If you try at this class, expect at least a B

Professor Abhisheck Gupta tries to do his best in order to teach and help students. After taking his class, I am interested in the control system area. If you are willing to study the control field, I highly recommend his class!

I took her Advanced Writing class on dystopian and utopian literature, and it was one of my favorite classes. She made the readings connect to real-world issues, and our discussions were always engaging. Her feedback really helped me improve my writing. It's not an easy A, but it's definitely worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Greff is one of the few instructors who actually explains the material instead of just reading off slides. She gives real examples in class that make the concepts way easier to understand, and you can tell she puts effort into every lecture. The workload is fair, and if you show up and try, you'll learn a lot.

I don't know why people don't give her more 4–5 star reviews. She genuinely teaches and truly cares about her students' education. She's engaging, supportive, and wants you to succeed. The class isn't the easiest, but she's the kind of professor you'll be grateful you took—she actually makes you learn and grow.
Nice, interesting class

poor class theme, strict grading by instructor, far too much work for an intro course. I am displeased to say the least. She expects you to write perfectly cohesive papers as an intro student. Peer reviews suck in my opinion and did not help whatsoever. She also took forever to grade our work because she was busy. AVOID AT ALL COSTS IF POSSIBLE.

reviews.comment: The comments she leaves on papers make it so you have to start over. No clear grading criteria.
