reviews.comment: Despite the ratings here, I think Professor Petrov is one of the best psych professors in OSU. He ensures that you truly understand the material, and spares no effort in teaching you. He's extremely passionate about the subject. His syllabus was very well organized and his grading was fair. Anyone would be lucky to have him as a teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was intimated to take this class due to the low ratings on here, but I actually really, really enjoyed him as my professor. He not only was funny and kind, but could teach the material in a concise way and made everything very objective so that there was no confusion with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I love Professor Petrov's class. He's always ready to help, provides great resources, and his lectures are engaging. The quizzes are frequent and the pre-class readings are many, but they prepare you well for the exams. His passion for the subject and dedication to his students is what makes this course amazing. Overall, he's a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Not sure if it is a cultural disconnect but Professor Petrov is very verbally disrespectful to the attendees of his lectures. Insinuating a lack of basic knowledge to a room full of people is not very conducive to a healthy learning environment. 
Read the textbook and required readings and you'll be fine.

Dr. Petrov assigned almost 50 pages a class, and we had a class quiz every class and an outside quiz after every class. Exams were not that hard if you came to class & paid attention, but it was just A LOT of reading & work. He expects you to memorize charts & schematics (of memory paths, for example) I'm not a math guy, so the cog. part was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Man I didn't expect his rating to be so low here... I've had difficult profs but he is definitely not one of them. Detailed study guide, well prepared & organized lecture & materials. On the overlapped content with my PSYCH3513, Dr. Petrov's explanation is better. He is one of the few professors that can catch my attention throughout the lectures.

- The quizzes he gives to start every class can be very specific and it is hard to remember such details from the required reading
- The lectures are long and cover some irrelevant information

Other than these criticisms, Dr. Petrov is a good professor. If you follow his instructions on how to go about learning the content, you will do fine.

Very enthusiastic professor, but course was very content-heavy. In-person lectures were a waste of time; the content we were tested on was in recorded lectures (which were hours longer than the amount of in-class time every week), the textbook, and additional videos/readings. You are expected to memorize everything; I truly mean everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's intelligent, funny, likeable, and most of all, a sadistic grader. Grades grad students less harshly than undergrads. Exam averages are C-; not a single grad student got an A and he still didn't curve. Gives 6-8 lectures per week including recorded ones and extreme expectations for time commitments. This is basically a 6 credit hour class.

Content is the most amazing thing, but undergrads only had 2 exams, 45 ques 90 points each. total points in class only 280. rest of the points come from lame online quizzes that don't help you but you'll get 100% on most. Doesn't finish the material in class, so makes us watch his online video lectures, read the textbook chapter, and do discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I dropped this class 2 weeks in. I saw these ratings but needed the class so I gave it a try and quickly regretted it. His lectures are messy and hard to understand. The content was so dry and he made 0 effort to make it bearable. After the quizzes, I dipped. Don't even bother with this guy, take a different prof.

This teacher is possibly the worst teacher that I have ever had the misfortune of having to be taught by. Petrov was never consistent with the due dates of his modules, which was contradictive of his syllabus. For example our final module was posted on Friday 12/4/2020 and due on Saturday along with the previous weeks module. Don't take his class!

Yeah, this class is not it. Try to get a different professor for 3312. Gives quizzes at the beginning and end of every lecture, and his lectures are incredibly confusing and uninteresting. The content is already a little confusing to begin with and his explanations do absolutely nothing expect make it more confusing. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is literally all over the place when he teaches. He goes back and forth on all the slides. Then there are not only 1 quiz but basically two quizzes every day in class, one is at the beginning of class and another at the end. Im sure he knows what he is talking about and seems like a nice guy but is just such a horrible educator.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really hated his class. He quizzes on the material he is supposed to cover in class, before class. The quizzes aren't easy, so you have to understand the material before coming. They are a big part of your grade. Then he spends too much time explaining easy things and makes them over-complicated. It's more confusing to pay attention than to not.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class was a nightmare. Make sure to read the book and review the slides before class because there are quizzes at the beginning and end of each class that ask specific and advanced questions. Study literally every assigned page of the textbook for exams because he asks about topics that were never discussed in lecture but appeared in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is not worth the stress, I would not recommend. The professor is all over the place and makes no sense. If you zone out for five seconds you're lost for the rest of the lecture. The book is boring to read, but important because he asks questions on exams that were not covered in lecture. He also gives a quiz every single day of class.

Alex is knowledgeable and funny. I took the intro and advanced cognitive science class with him in 2012. I was a computer science major so some of the stuff many people find difficult was probably easier for me.

NOT easy, but not impossible. "Pop" quizzes nearly every lecture, but they also count for extra credit once you hit a certain amount. Tests are challenging. HAVE to go to class and keep up. I went to class, reviewed every lecture, and I did fine. Not a walk in the park but not as bad as it sounds. Drops an exam and grading is curved significantly
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Petrov is very knowledgable about cognitive psychology, but tends to be all of the place when teaching. The material itself is not hard, but lectures are all over the place and difficult to follow. Tests cover specific topics that may not have been covered in lecture, only in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy, but he is so passionate about the course that it makes it enjoyable and interesting! Has a great philosophy of how putting in the most work can guide you to an A. Would definitely recommend taking this course!

Had to retake this class because I didn't take it seriously the first time, but he really is not a bad professor. He is passionate about psychology and it shows in class. Lectures are almost entirely being lectured at, and almost every class has a pop quiz at the end. Read the book, take good notes, ask him questions if you have them! Nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ridiculous. Avoid at all costs. If you are taking him for an elective, find someone, anyone, as a better choice. He snaps at people and he uploads 50+ slides a lecture and makes it to slide 22,then assigns 20 readings for exam on top of the slides he didn't get to. You cannot even apply what he teaches to any aspect of life. Huge language barrier.

Incredibly smart, and teaches a hellishly fast-paced course. If you don't care about the material, you will fail in a week. If you love the material, you will learn a ton and STILL almost fail, but enjoy it the entire time. Would only recommend him (and the course) to current or aspiring graduate students, though.

I was pleasantly surprised by Prof. Petrov's class compared to his ratings; although his lectures are long, you can honestly see that he enjoys teaching the material. Read the textbook and attend lectures, and you'll do just fine in the class.

Gives pop quizzes almost every lecture. His lectures are long and always go over. The material is dense and sometimes confusing, especially when he goes on a tangent about a topic. If you read the assigned readings and review before class, the pop quizzes can help your grade. I did well in his class because I reviewed the material almost everyday.

He's nice and has an interest in the subject, but every lecture is 80 minutes of constant lecturing, hardly any chance for questions, and no in-class/group review before a test. There is a pop quiz after almost every lecture that's supposed to be given during the last 5 minutes, but he talks so much it's usually the last 2 minutes. READ THE BOOK!!!

He really likes what he is talking about but he talks for way too long and can be confusing. Lectures always go over time. Pop quizzes almost every lecture. He doesn't test on specific concepts, so you have to study every single little thing. Instead of a study guide he says to read the book, lecture slides, and other required readings.

Alex is comical. The class was extremely tough,and he doesn't go over exams. (Only one question that everyone missed). The book was so helpful. Go to class because those pop quizzes really save you. I thought I was going to fail the class, but a miracle happened. (I don't even know how). Drops one exam grade. And I really enjoyed what the class.

Don't take this class if you hate reading. Students who work hard are rewarded; I did the  assigned readings after every lecture, studied material before class the next day in case of a pop quiz, and ended up doing well. Highlight things he emphasizes in class- it will be on the exam. You can earn extra credit through extra pop quizzes.
GO TO CLASS! If you are an average student you should go to class because the pop quizzes saved me this semester.

Dr. Petrove is very interested in the subject, but unfortunately he is not good at teaching. He talks the whole lecture, and he usually takes minutes after to finish; however, he does not use the lectures much in his exams. Dr. Petrov unlike all professors, he refuses to give any helpful information for exams; furthermore, he says that everything (
Pop quizzes in class but not too bad if you've gone to lecture and reviewed the material a little. Textbook heavy class but doable. Very interesting subject material though, and I learned a lot!

Do  not take him if unless you are ready to be bored, frustrated & unrewarded for hard work. This guy gave a pop quiz almost every class. There was no way to guess what was on the test & he tested on things not focused in lecture

Gets through about 20 of his 50 slides each lecture but still tests you on what he didn't cover. Extremely boring and hard to pay attention even though the material is hard. Don't take this class if you don't have to.

Boring ! Not an effective communicator. My section would struggle to stay awake. Hard to follow at times because he can't deliver his lecture effectively. He knows he is boring and doesn't care. Exams are hard because you don't really know what to expect out of the 200 pages you just read this makes him smirk. Class Average 1st Mid 71% D.

If you are interested in Cognitive Psych you will enjoy this class. There is a wealth of info in the readings and Dr. Petrov posts additional readings for those really interested in the material. He is a pleasant guy and offered help to students who needed it. The exams are difficult! He gives 30 points for simply attending classes though, so go!

Alot of work for a class..He tends to use some of the same slides for both the 612 and the 312 if that gives you a hint as to how hard it will be. I studied for a couple weeks before the tests and ended up getting C's as well. I usually get A's. I like the guy but material is not explained well and you are not sure what will be on the test.

His class was terribly unorganized. He took four weeks to grade the first assignment, which was a mere 500 word summary. His tests are unfair and require memorization of, mostly, the graphs and charts he uses in his lectures. No one finished the first exam because he had 12 essay questions and gave about 30-45 minutes to do them.

Class was not mandatory, however there was role and the extra points are deffinetly needed to help your grade. Tests were very difficult, I read every sentence in the book and still came out with two Cs on each test. The hw were time consuming and hard. If u have to take this just do everything to get every point possible I came out with a B.

absolutely HORRIBLE professor.. i felt like he felt he was better than everyone. i asked for help on the 2nd day and was basically told to do it on my own. homework was graded way too harsh by TA, and tests didn't even follow the notes. just try to get a C and move on.

Gets annoyed easily.  5 homework assignments with medium difficulty. 2 exams with unexpected information covered on them. neither professor nor TA very helpful. subject matter is very dry and difficult to understand at time. also, petrov has a pretty thick accent

A very likable guy, but I agree, don't take this unless you are a computer sci grad student. Even though the grading was easy, it was miserable to sit through the incomprehensible, mandatory lectures. Intense essay exams. Seriously, unless this is your area of interest and you know computers, stay away!

Petrov is a SMART man, but sometimes he jumps around too much... Hard to understand if you don't already have a good general understanding of the material. DO NOT take this class if you know nothing about computer science. On the plus side he's a VERY lenient grader!

I took this last quarter with another professor (shulman) and had to drop it because i could not understand anything he was talking about.  Petrov is WORLDS better.  He's interesting and funny, he's an expert in the field, and he really wants you to learn.  Go to class!  Lenient grading scale too, 86% was an A this quarter.  GREAT PROF.

Just do your best to avoid a class with her. Her lectures were all over the place, and she often had to be corrected by students during lectures. She also has incorrect answer keys for practice exams, so I was often confused about whether what I was doing was right or not. I went to her office hours early on as well, and she was not helpful AT ALL.

The other ratings are pretty dramatic in my opinion- she really cares for her students and wants everyone to learn. She has a strong accent but works hard to make sure her handwriting is legible for everyone. The homework was long at some points but prepared me well for the midterms and final. I felt that her grading was fair as well.

I feel like everyone is being dramatic. She has a bit of an accent but is definitely still understandable and responds to emails fast. I didn't go to lectures much but she had all notes posted and the grading was fair. Easier exams than the other linear / differential teachers!!

Switch to any other professor for this class save yourself the headache. If you're stuck with her just watch YouTube.

The other reviews speak for themselves and are incredibly accurate. I'll put it this way, I probably would be very bad at basic addition if she taught me addition in 1st grade!!

She is very different to rate as opposed to other bad professors. She is very kind and wants to help us succeed, but she just does not make that happen. Karrer isn't terrible as others may say. But you're in for a treat. She is very difficult to understand and has TERRIBLE handwriting. Your best bet is getting a good TA/going to every office hour. She does care about her students and will provide help, but she is a very unorganized, sloppy professor. Most students I know stopped attending lecture.

I don't typically leave reviews on professors, even if they are bad, but this professor it was a MUST that I leave one. She is flat out terrible. A 9 year old should just teach this.

For a tough class to where exams are worth 85% of your grade, and the USELESS lectures overlap the USEFUL recitations is completely unfair to everyone to have this professor. I know it is rude to comment about things that cannot be changed. With that being said, it is impossible not to comment on the language barrier and sloppiness that came from this teacher. I have never left a bad review anywhere in my life. That being said, I had to for this professor. Easily the worst teacher I've ever had through all my years of school. Mind boggling and UNFAIR

This professor has to be a joke that the University is pranking us on. I'm positive she doesn't even know how to do math, she just copies notes off her iPad during lecture and still makes errors. Full disclosure, I stopped going to lecture after the National Championship and it was the best choice I ever made. The only way to get through this class is to go to recitation and teach yourself. thick accent, overcomplicates everything, learn more on your own than in lectures, recitation is the only good part about this class

She writes like a third grader and she overcomplicates everything. It is quite possible that she was hired to teach a different class, and she is teaching the wrong class. She should be teaching Math Excursions (1116), but quite honestly I don't even think she would be able to teach that properly.

For a class where exams are worth 85% of the grade it is an absolute shame that she is teaching it. You will only learn the material two ways; on your own, or through recitation which is only twice a week. Hard to understand her and read her handwriting. If you have her don't even bother to go to lectures. I just skipped and went to office hours with my TA every week. Difficult class but still ended with an A.

ABSOLUTELY ATROCIOUS. She writes like a first grader and explains things so bad it completely messes up my knowledge on the problem when I watch her do it. The worst professor I've had in my entire life. The worst. The absolute worst. How did she get a job. I hate to grade her like this because it isn't necessarily her fault but she needs to teach something else where it doesn't matter as much because no one had any idea what she was saying or writing.

Annette is very nice, but she is not the best at teaching. Her handwriting is often illegible, and her accent is hard to understand at times. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR. She takes over half the lecture to go over tophat questions, and then spends the last 15 minutes teaching new material. Please do not take this class ever, I have never had a worse professor than her as I learn more sitting at home and not doing anything than I do attending class. Thick accent that you can not understand and the worst hand writing I have ever seen. Nothing she does or says makes sense in any way I have never been more confused in a class ever
Thick accent and horrible handwriting. Do not pick this lecturer. Everything is overcomplicated and you're better off learning on your own.

If you want to go insane and have no regard for your mental wellbeing, then this is the professor for you! Otherwise, avoid at all costs. BY FAR the worst professor I have had since being here. She doesn't speak good english due to a heavy german accent, and she has the handwriting of my 4 year old sister. Don't take it.

this is the absolute worst teacher i've ever had. just wait till you have a lecture with her. you can never understand what she is saying and her numbers don't look like what she is trying to say. i'm seriously considering dropping out of college because of her
Heavy German accent, not a good pick for lecturer
make sure you study since exams are worth 85% of your grade

A little slow during the lectures and gives way too much time for the group problems in class. But his jokes and side rants are very funny. His exams are open note but you don't really need them for anything outside of formulas, they are fair.

Course content was among the most difficult of any physics class I've taken outside of 5400H, but his clarity and organization made it manageable. He was always available for questions and truly wanted students to succeed. Showing up to class consistently is enough to put you in a strong position. Easily one of the best in the department.

Professor Boveia truly cares about his students and was an amazing teacher! Taught the difficult content really well in my opinion. Try to participate in class because you do TopHats every day basically but it really helps with the hard homework assignments. Also office hours was super helpful
Good guy, good lectures, difficult homework, and tests with appropriate difficulty!

Outstanding professor! The lectures were well organized, with students doing practice problems and lectures interspersed well! Weekly homework is usually tricky, but quizzes and exams are open-book, so avoid being too complicated. Recommend him!

Very solid professor. Although Physics 2301 is very difficult, Mr. Boveia makes it very clearly. The homework is difficult, but the quizzes and exams are open-book and difficulty-controlled (The difficulty of the tests are controlled to not very high).

Boveia was a legend for how clearly he explained difficult subjects like rotation and relativity. The homework is very difficult and takes a long time to finish. He deliberately controlled the difficulty of the exam, and allowed us to open the book, and finally gave curve a friendly. Highly recommend Boveia!

cool guy, bad homework. 

open note exams very nice.

really good teacher loved the lectures

Lectures suck but for tests he sends out an email with the topics that are going to be on it and generally sticks to what he says so if u study tests aren't that bad. But final is most of the grade which is annoying and he is not helpful in emails or anything

This is the worst professor I have taken in my entire college career. His lessons follow no structure, he is unorganized, and there is zero chance anyone can follow what he writes on the board. He is EXTREMELY bad at arithmetic, which resulted in errors in nearly every calculation he did. As someone who pays for college themselves, WASTE OF MONEY.

I know many students didn't love Prof. Derdzinski, but if you attend lectures (even if you don't) and stay up to date with the syllabus and the topics covered per week- you will be just fine. I really recommend watching tons of YouTube videos for many chapters as he doesn't necessarily go over things again and again, but I enjoyed his class a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your entire grade basically comes down to how you do on the exams, which often require either remembering or having previously learned some trick to simplify the problem. Each problem missed results in a sizable penalty to final grade. Exam averages were well below passing, and no curve was applied to exams or final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Professor Derdzinski. I looked at these reviews prior to taking his class and decided to take a chance on him, but I really should not have. I have never once dropped a professor, but I really wish I did in this case. His exam averages are well below passing grades (yes, well below a C-). Please do not take this class.

It says I got a C-, but I should have gotten a B, because he completely forgot to put in my midterm 1 score. When I asked him to input the score, he told me that he did not have the test records. However, even though I took the test, he refused to give me anything but a 0 on that test, causing my entire grade to drop from a theoretical 81 to a 66.

So much to say with so little room.
He is living proof that SEIs do nothing. The horrible ratings here are completely true. DROP HIM IF YOU HAVE HIM. I am retaking this class and there are at least 4 (out of about 24) students retaking this class in my section because of him. He does not follow the textbook and his exams do not follow the lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have him as your instructor, DROP THAT CLASS! He doesn't post notes online. He doesn't do a good job explaining in class. Reading the provided book is more reliable than his teaching. He got mad at me when I asked for help at office hours. Many students failed his exams. Many even tried to get the math department to do something about this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this guy at all costs, drop the class for the semester, get a different professor, literally anything but this section. Nonsensical math vomit lectures brushing off advanced topics as "arbitrary" and ridiculous grader. Uninterested in answering questions or helping students. Class average of 62 right now. Keep the D off your transcript.

He is impossible to understand during class and does not take questions. He is rude and uncaring during office hours. I read the entire book and still got a 50 on the exam. (Higher than the class average of 40, though.) He grades extremely harshly, one small mistake and you get a fourth of the credit on the question, each exam is only 4 questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yeah, I read these reviews and tried giving him a shot to see for myself. I mean, he can't be that bad, especially 'cause he has some good reviews, right? Yeah, no. He is truly that bad lol. I delayed my math curriculum just to drop his class. Rather that than a D in a class that doesn't give curves or use any technology.

This guy sucks. He never actually teaches, he just tells. I can tell that he's so smart and knows what he's talking about but he expects you to be on the same level as him. He starts by teaching chapter 5 and expects you to know everything else. He hated the entire class for asking questions and got mad when we were confused about his content.

Classes are punctual and completely non-interactive. Professor will arrive the minute class starts, write as many proofs as they can on the board without turning to face the class or ask if anyone has questions until the last five minutes, but only to see the exact second they can leave. Exam means were 50%'s with no curve. Avoid them at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have ever had, avoid at any cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One positive is that he does not assign much homework. His lectures are dry and he does not seem very friendly. He never responded to emails and was extremely hard to reach outside of class. You can tell that he is a very smart guy and has a deep understanding of mathematics, but that does not translate into his lectures. Good luck if you have him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely a very smart man. However, it's difficult to understand him. I gave up on in-person classes and watched his youtube recordings instead because I kept needing to go back & repeat. His exams are only 4 questions with short answers; barely any partial credit. So if you're smart and prepared but just don't know one thing, get ready for a C.
I never really understood how he graded and never did corrections on paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You basically have to teach yourself class. He's very hard to understand and teaches in a way that is confusing and makes no sense. He will rarely teach the material on the exam and doesn't even test you on the stuff in the study guide. I honestly don't know how he's still teaching here.

Professor Derdzinski is a genius person. He cares about students in office hours. His lectures are dry and long, but if you review textbooks before exams, it will be an easy A. Tests are heavy but very straightforward. There is not many homework per week.

Smart man, poor professor. Lectures were recordings on Youtube with no editing to remove mistakes and long, stammering pauses. Jumped around between topics with no clear connections given between them and explanations were poor at best. I only passed because the book is decent and TheMathCoach and Faculty of Kahn on Youtube helped immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly a little misunderstood on here so far I think. He really is a great guy and absolutely brilliant. Read the section in the 'textbook' before class and it helps your understanding a lot. He goes a little too fast sometimes but he really knows what he's talking about. Unbelievably tough grader.
Nice handsome fellow trying to make people smarter day by day. Easy A.

Good professor in my opinion. 3 homework problems per week and every lecture starts pretty much on time without any sort of small talk. He is very specific on the board when he is talking and makes things clear through his writing (although it is very mathematical writing). He doesn't remind you to do your homework (but it's due every Monday).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Andrzej is amazing at explaining the content of this course in a thorough and easy to understand way. He goes a bit fast but not so fast that it's impossible to keep up with. Midterms are fairly easy and the course load is dealable with. Make sure you read the textbook alongside or even before the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had. Yeah, I mean it. He is obviously very smart, But he makes every single thing complicated and just talks to student in his way. I basically learn stuff by myself for whole semester. In addition, he graded heavily on exams while every exam has only 4-6 questions. If you miss one, you are screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great mathematician. Loves imparting his knowledge to eager students. Loves proofs. Office hours are quite good if you walk in with specific questions and are willing to put in the effort to understand what he says. Note that he doesn't like dumbing down ideas. He's a purist so don't take his class unless you love math and like a challenge.

Professor Derdzinski, while a brilliant mathematician, is simply a terrible teacher. He speaks directly into the board while lecturing, never stopping for input from students. If he stays on topic in lecture, it's a miracle - he flies through proofs without explaining any concepts. Midterms were 4 questions each, final was 6. Don't take his class.

The guy very obviously is versed at what he teaches, but is pretty bad when it comes to actually transferring the information. Tests are few, weighty, and there is basically no partial credit (we had a group of ten students approach him on this matter, only to get a short and rude response). If you learn from practical examples, AVOID.

Complains about how the textbook was written, but fails to explain the material clearly himself. Lectures do not prepare you for the quizzes or the exams, so be prepared to read the book and try to solve every problems. Very general explanations about the topics, but will require more knowledge on the exams, even for simple problems.

If you choose to attend his lectures you will more than likely end up staring into space or sitting on your phone more than taking notes. He does not clearly and efficiently go over the topics that are on the tests in class and during recitation he discusses random topics that will never be needed. Basically you will teach yourself the course.

Well-organized prof. tried to cover everything in complex analysis but only tested on major topics so don't get panic if you cant't follow in the lecture.  will post topic(s) before every examquiz and they are fair if you review notes, read textbook(very important) and do the practice problems he suggested. he is fair and wants you to do well!
Excellent professor ... highly recommend.

He makes many mistakes during his lectures so taking notes becomes pointless. Test and quizzes all boil down to remembering some "trick" or be punished with lots of algebra. Sometimes, he will place a restriction on the way you can solve problems - thus forcing you to try and figure out the "trick" or get zero credit. Horrible.

He is the worst instructor I have ever had at OSU and it's not even close. More than half the class dropped when I took the class Autumn 2014. The answers and help he provides to students in office hours is inconsistent with how this mysterious graduate TA graded. Dropped my math minor because of him. DO NOT take this class under any circumstances.

Quite possibly the worst professor I have ever had in my entire educational career. Lectures are abstract and worthless. No solutions are available for any of the practice problems, so you have no idea if you are doing anything right ever. Tests are very short and partial credit is non existent. Avoid if you don't want to take the class twice.

Quizzes and tests were very easy in retrospect. Although, you really have to do the homework problems because his lectures are almost completely abstract and proof-oriented. If you mess up, it's not likely you'll get a lot of partial credit...  You can tell this guy is a genius, it's not a surprise he doesn't want to be in that room.

Second midterm average was a 39 and he didn't curve. He also refused to help the students. With three weeks to go, the entire class went to the math department and requested to switch sections and things were so bad that they let us do that. Do NOT take his class!
Derdzinski is by far, the worst professor I have ever had at OSU. He is of no help and he is the most ridiculous grader I have ever had. Studying is of no avail in this course.

Listen, I read these reviews before I took the class, but I found a few redeeming ones so I chanced it.  90% of people here say he goes into class, talks really fast at the board, and runs away after it's over, and that's the TRUTH!!!  I could go on about how terribly he conducted our course, but I don't have room.

Quizzes and tests were fair, although you have to be careful not to make mistakes. Homework was very light. His teaching was passable, although I skipped a lot. Easy class if you read the book and do the homework.

This guy is your standard foreign teacher. His lectures are difficult to understand.  Shows up late for every class, and exams. His exams are fair.  The first one was hard, but the second was very easy. Final was fair. His exams consist of very few problems, and he gives aweful partial credit.  Without a good ta, this class will be difficult.

Derdzinkski marches rapidly through proofs, and it's very easy to get lost.  I often can't make sense of my notes when I look at them after class because he goes pretty fast and doesn't write every important step down.  In addition, he seems a bit resistant to helping during office hours.  He covers more material than other sections.  Avoid!

Like several before have said, he is late to class and then the first one to leave.  He talks continuously to the board, without giving a second for students to think through each step.  He is extremely unhelpful, in class and in office hours; he just re-reads the question back to you.  I would not have him as a professor again.

Andrzej is a brilliant (slightly scatter-brained) man.  If you ask him questions in his office, he is quite nice and helpful.  His lectures can be hard to follow in real time, but if you review your notes, you will find that you can learn a lot from him.  His tests and grades are fair. With a little bit of effort, you will be lucky to have had him.

Horrible teacher yet extremely intelligent. Most lectures were way to advanced for students in the class. I went to every lecture (don't know why), because I am making myself teach the material. Without a good TA, I would be more lost than I already am. If anyway possible-AVOID
Horrible!!! This guy just eats math books, comes to class, and spits it all out really fast. Doesnt realize other people are actually in the room. Totally awful lecture.
makes things harder than they r, way to fast, jumps around way to much
This man speaks to the board, rushes through examples, never prepares, somehow manages to cover neither theory nor applications adequately, is horribly unsightly and should be avoided at all costs.

Teaches more theory than most engineers could handle, which is the source of most complaints here. Linear algebra background helps for dif eq. (period) Extremely unorganized. He chose a worthless textbook. Easy class, easy exams if you read carefully.
Not a very good teacher.  I suggest making bets on which tee shirt he wears each day.  That was my only   enjoyable part of the class
Horrible Teacher.  Comes in late, talks to the board, doesn't seem to care if you succeed or fail.  Seems to try as hard as he can to trick you on tests.  Definitley run the other way from him.

Always late, late for final. Always wore the same clothes. Found ducks in lake were more interesting. So unclear. Told us something WAS NOT going to be on final, then reviewed it and said we would need it to solve a problem..yup. Final was not as expected. Namely: crazy!

He is not a good professor but he should work for Nasa or something.  You cannot approach him to ask questions because he is late to class and is the first one out of the classroom.  If you take his class I would recommend attending every recitation, to understand what is going on.
No Comments

This guy is somewhat unorganized, but overall, I believe he is a good teacher.  He knows his subject matter, but doesn't explain it the best ways to typical students.  He speaks to the class like they're getting their PH.d.  He tells you what is going to be on tests and is a lenient grader.
This guy is awful.  He takes what should be an easy class and makes it way too unclear and confusing.  Stay away from him.
Anyone who complains about this guy is just plain lazy.  He tells you what is on the tests, gives good examples and his final grades are way nice.
This professor was horrible, I learned nothing from him. I would advise people not to take his class.

A math genius, but imagine a physics student getting lectured by einstien (in german). tough to understand, but practise tests were helpful. I had to retake, as did several friends. It is very easy to cheat if you sit in the back of class (still got a D).

Terrible teacher.  Too smart to teach.  The only way he was helpful is because so many people complained that he now gives practice tests.  He got behind and decided not to teach things that we needed to know for later.  Don't take him.

this guy will release homework assignments or final projects and upload instructions that have incorrect information and then the day before its due say oh my bad i made an error and you end up having to redo the whole assignment. This has happened multiple times over the course of 3301 and 3303

He lectures way too fast, and doesn't clarify any material. The material is difficult as well, but he moves past it quickly expecting his students to fully understand it on their own time. The exams are completely inconsistent with lectures and what he covers in the homework. I would not wish this lecturer on anybody.
Funny guy, kinda strict. Grading is pretty strict but curve is pretty forgiving

The powerpoints are provided beforehand, but you need to attend lecture to record the notes he adds during class. He does not record lectures, if absent you need to join the class zoom which is very annoying for an 8am class. He lectures very quickly as if students already know the material. Try to read the textbook before lecture. Good luck!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very hard to understand

Very interesting guy. His lectures aren't bad but he does not record them and he's a very fast talker which doesn't work well with my learning style but I made do. His exams weren't bad at all and the homeworks helped in understanding the concepts. He isn't very friendly and makes no effort with the students.
He is just an average professor. I wouldn't say he was bad, but it could sometimes be boring, but maybe that has more to do with the content than the professor.
Exams are so much harder than practice exams and homework.

Professor Richards is very rude and condescending to students. Lectures are boring. Homeworks are long. Exams are hard. Doesn't reply to emails. Overall, I would avoid him as he is very rude and difficult to work with.

He has a lot of homework, but what he teaches in class cannot help you complete the homework very well. The exams are very difficult. The practice exams he gives are completely different from his actual exams. The practice exams are very simple, but the difficulty of the actual exams is 100 times higher.

He is a great professor! His lectures were excellent, and he gives you the slide shows on Canvas which was really helpful for studying for exams. The exams were very fair and were similar to homework. One of the best professors I've had!

In terms of teaching abilities, he does a good job. However, his personality is awful outside of class. Don't ask for any extensions or help with exam corrections; he'll berate you for not keeping up and LITERALLY wants you to beg for help from him. The material itself is hard, but luckily his exams are relatively easy. Dont take unless you have to
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm surprised at the poor ratings Professor Richards has received. I found his exams to be very fair and similar to the problems done in class and on the review sheet he provided before each exam.

Professor Richards gets a bad reputation. I found this class very fair as someone who had never taken stats before. Homework can be tricky but there are plenty of resources to succeed. Exams were usually easier than expected, and Professor Richards allowed one page of notes for each exam. Don't be discouraged by other reviews.

His lecture is meaningless because he actually just reading the powerpoint. For the homework, he usually give student homework after he finished whole chapter and since to that time, it is hard to remember the previous knowledge. And the worst thing is his office-hour, suffering and painful. Dont take his clasee
Lectures are chaotic and unclear and don't prepare you for homework
Overall a good professor. Not that accessible outside of class and sometimes doesn't seem to care about students. However, he teaches the material in a clear way and has a good sense of humor.
solid teacher but a little mean honestly, exams weren't too hard and he prepared you pretty well for it

Horrible attitude. I once emailed him about a problem I had and he replied very passive aggressively. He knows his stuff and tries to joke around, but it's obvious he doesn't enjoy teaching and seems to have a distaste for his students. The class itself wasn't too difficult, but I would take it with a different professor if you can.
This guy has quite the attitude on him. Extremely inappropriate for the environment he works in.

Lecture goes very fast and he spends time explaining things that don't even matter or come up in homework or exams. Very unsympathetic and not accommodating for students. Going to office hours was scary because he made you feel stupid for not understanding the material. The lab for this class was pointless because TA didn't know what he was doing.
He is a horrible lecturer. I am saddened that my tuition goes to pay this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Even basic statistics concepts will seem like a nightmare with him. Many did not do very well due to his poor teaching and yet he still refuses to curve the course (but instead made lab attendance required which was taught by a clueless TA). Completely unsympathetic and is very childish in his behavior. Avoid at all costs!

Genuinely terrible, does not explain concepts and whatever he talks about in lecture does not show up in the homework or exams. If you like a professor that doesn't know how to teach, this guy is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is so bad at explaining concepts that even material I knew well from my physics and math courses seemed confusing when he explained it. Noone wanted to attend his lectures so he made lab attendance mandatory which was taught by an incompetent TA. Avoid if possible or just read the textbook if you can't and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Richard is nice, but his teaching is average, mostly covering the slides. The course itself is very difficult,but he struggles to explain difficult concepts clearly, and exams aren't straightforward. Many students skipped class, preferring to self-study, so he made attendance mandatory. I suggest using extra resources or avoiding his class.

This course was difficult, but Dr. Richards does his best to make it less stressful. He's very willing to help and explain in office hours if you need extra help. Homeworks could get quite difficult at times, but a lot of the material in class lecture helps with it. He's also extremely funny and has a good sense of humor. I'd recommend.

Not a terrible class difficulty-wise but the exams make the class worse than it should be. They are not an accurate reflection of the class material and are worth way too much of your grade. I would not want to take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework can be rough sometimes but the lectures help with them for the most part. Practice exams are usually a great tool to prepare for the midterms, but I found the practice final was nothing like the actual final. Overall he's solid but far from easy.

Homework is the hardest thing here, exams were very reasonable and nothing you haven't learned in class-100% study exam reviews/practices! Prof goes quite fast in class, but if you have a good math(calculus) background you should be able to do fine. Book can be helpful, mainly try to understand the notes from lecture. It does get better later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is good at teaching. Office hours helped me a lot for the most part. For stat 3410 we got to use our notes and homework in our exams which helped a lot during exams. However, I do understand the negative ratings. His class was extremely stressful at time and the exams had time pressure. He gives off pressurzing vibes, I wish he was more graceful

Dr. Richards gives you everything you need to succeed in the course as well as being accessible and helpful outside of class for extra help. Everything in the class is graded very fairly and his other experiences that he uses as examples make the class more interesting. Also he's kinda funny, intentionally or not. Too much hate for him on here imo

Lectures were very confusing, but he explained concepts very clearly in office hours. Homework wasn't too bad, but it was difficult not to get at least a few deductions every time. The exams were extremely fair.

Richards was ok. He's a good communicator and consistent in his grading. The first couple homeworks, and HW7 felt pretty relevant to lectures and very manageable, but around the middle of the semester it felt very difficult and a little unfocused. Bayesian stats isn't my strong suite and it felt very manageable- just go to lecture and ask for help
Slides and lectures almost never matched the homework given, very difficult to apply the material. Not very open to questions that seem simple to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Flies through lectures lacking elaboration. Teaches like we already know the material. Not enough examples to grasp concepts. This made exam prep confusing. Allowed 1 sheet of notes for exams which was helpful. Treated me like I was an inconvenience. Passionate about Stats but not teaching. My advice: Correct exam errors, visit with TA

Most unprofessional professor I've had. He does not care about students and their learning needs. He can't explain a single topic and always rushes through the lectures. I feel extreme sadness in his class and any time I think about it. Extreme. Sadness.
He is very great and helpful. Follow his lecture and you would get a good grade.

Andrew Richards is so great! He was very helpful. If I have any questions, he will arrange a zoom meeting to explain. He will also give a lot of opportunities to improve students' grades, such as midterm exams, there are opportunities for make-up exams.

The professor really doesn't care the students. There is no relationship between his sample exam and real exam. He puts two exams together in two consecutive lecture days and claims it will increase the sample space and it will help you know your position in the class. It is ridiculous. The exam is really tough. Get away from it.

Nice enough guy, brutal sense of humor, and lectures are tough to get through. He knows his stuff and he's passionate, but even the most simple concepts are convoluted beyond belief. His tests are fair, and lectures are pretty good test prep, so I'm (reluctantly) taking a class with him again.

Prof Richards gets too way much hate on here. I enjoy his lectures as I find him engaging and explains concepts well without using advanced terminology. He treats the lectures like a conversation and has interesting stories from experience. Tests can be difficult but I find his review days help you prepare well and he does his best to help you.
Sort of tough lectures, exams range from super easy to real hard. Good curve though so it evens out. Could be better at lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The knowledge is not very easy to understand actually, but in his lecture, you can never understand that. Also, you have four exams in a semester, and the final exam including all of the things you have learned before, and he is really a tough grader. His class is so boring that I feel like I am in jail during his lecture time.

very smart, but an abysmal teacher. incapable of explaining ideas from the bottom-up to people that have never seen the material. skims through ideas without explaining them; passes through lectures as if the material is completely intuitive. this is an already challenging course made impossible with such a horrific teacher. avoid avoid avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He always makes concepts more difficult

He is smart, but he just doesn't have the ability to bring knowledge down to a human level. Teaching students as if he is talking to his collogues, so you know he is never able to explain things is a clear way. Act like students have learn this before and just fly through materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely monotone. His lecture is very dry and oftentimes confusing. I would not recommend him at all no matter what classes you are planning to take. Avoid him if you can

Easily one of the worst profs Ive ever had. Dont get me wrong hes super smart and passionate but incapable of bringing topics down to human levels of understanding. And when you try to get him to explain he just looks at you like an youre an idiot. Lectures were not helpful at all.
If you want to know how to make easy things obscure, take his course, take it twice!

He actually didn't know how to explain anything. He would just put stuff up and not understand when we didn't understand. I went to his office hours and leave even more confused. The exams were fair, and I ended up doing fine in the class, but it was not because of him. Every lecture left me more confused. I learned it on my own with other students
Pretty standard. Put in the work and get a good grade. Grading is a little hard on tests, but did curve the overall grade a few points.

Tests make up 70% of grade, but are fair and he tells you what will be on them (and gives practice probs). Lectures are amazing, clearly explain the process. Textbook only used for hw problems, so have a friend send them (don't buy it). 10 HW sheets, 5 quizzes (to make 20% of grade). Recitation mandatory (but very helpful). But DON'T FALL BEHIND.
Very considerate and understanding of everyone in the class. The coursework was not too difficult, but there were many texts to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: April is incredibly supportive of learning and made me excited to show up to class. Overall the workload is not too much considering you are learning a new language, but keep in mind you do have to do work outside of class and studying is necessary. I am DEVASTATED that I cannot take her class next semester!!

She's awesome, it's a challenging class as any foreign language class will be, but Weintritt makes it the best experience possible. Would take again, would recommend anyone else to take Weintritt as well!

Prof. Weintritt is a lovely, caring professor that wants her students to succeed in learning the Italian language and culture. The majority of the lecture is in Italian at a normal pace and you are required to participate and communicate back, so certainly a step-up in intensity from previous courses. However, she grades generously.
This class was so bad, don't recommend taking. It was so pointless and repetitive and you had to have the exact wording she had for a quiz answer or you don't get full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
April was amazing! She speaks only Italian in class, so it is difficult, however, she was always willing to clarify anything if you asked! 
She was quick to respond to my emails and was always so caring when I spoke with her. Fair grader and an amazing person - I'm going to miss my Italian classes with her.

I had her for both 1102 and 1103. By far my favorite professor. Very understanding, grades fairly. Lots of online homework but it was pretty easy. I loved the class and her. Ill miss her Italian classes.

April is the absolute best professor I've ever had. I had her for 1102 and 1103 and would definitely take more classes with her if I had the chance. Attendance is mandatory (you're allowed a couple skips per semester) but April makes class engaging and fun. She's very understanding and actually cares about her students. Highly recommend

Absolutely love Professor Weintritt. She cares so much about her students and is an amazing teacher. She is considerate with homework and tests. Had her for 1102 and 1103 and would take more with her if I could. In class, she speaks only in Italian and you have to follow, but if you need something clarified with something, she's eager to help.

One of my favorite professors. It was definitely more difficult than my previous class, but April Weintritt was always willing to work with students and always made me excited for lecture. One time I was mentally not doing well and accidentally missed the timeline for an exam, and she let me take it with no time limit. Very considerate, she's great

April is a wonderful teacher. The class was fast paced and there was a lot of homework every night but it wasnt checked so you could get away with not doing it. She is very considerate and kind as well

By far the greatest Italian Professor Ive had. Most previous professors have been rude and impatient, but Professor Weintritt has been very understanding and truly shows a concern for her students. The class is fast paced and can be tricky, but if you show up to class consistently and make an effort youll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class is kind of fast paced, definitely a lot if you're new to the language. Weintritt is very helpful, engaging, and positive in class and outside of it. like any language class participation is part of your grade, but there's lots of opportunities every class to get points.
Cares about each student's success and takes personal interest in your performance in the class. Very understanding and forgiving, and makes lessons interesting and fun.

April is probably my favorite professor Ive ever had, and Im not even a foreign language major. She is caring, accommodating, helpful, funny, and overall very fair in how she grades. The class was tough, but you should expect that from OSUs foreign language department. I couldnt have imagined taking this class with any other professor!

April is one of the best foreign language professors I have had, and I have had many. This class was challenging for me and I considered dropping it at the beginning; but, April talked to me and convinced me that I was going to be fine. She was always available to help and willing to give feedback. I definitely recommend taking a course with her.

April is very energetic and passionate about her job. I was not a great student and am poor at foreign languages, but she was always very encouraging and helpful. Very accessible outside of the classroom and will give favorable grading and breaks to you if you show up to office hours. Not a laidback prof but you could find MUCH worse language profs
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: April is extremely friendly and caring. She's funny and great at teaching. She has a clear passion for her job.
Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: April is a must-take professor. She cares so much about her students, makes every class something to look forward to, and makes a lot of the difficult topics very easy to learn. 10/10 one of the best professors I have ever had definitely take if you are able to.

Professor Appel is super sweet, really helpful, and works hard to make sure you understand the language. I highly recommend her if the course is available, and although the Spanish department has a tough and strict curriculum, she does great working with it and providing a good learning environment.
she was super sweet and nice and really cares about her students. Most of her class is on nearpod. Super sweet and always willing to help her students.

Professor Appel is so nice!! There is weekly homework through the online textbook and assignments to bring to class completed, but the work is not challenging. The exams, writing assignment, and oral exam are graded fairly. If you attend class, do all the homework, and show effort during class, youll do really well.
Ms. Appel teaches at OSU and a nearby high school. She was very helpful and passionate about the language. Definitely helped me achieve the A I wanted

Do not take this course with her! There are many other Econ professors that will teach you the content much better. She often got confused herself while she lectured. Not very open to student feedback and will go out of her way to prove herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She seemed confused half the time and it made understanding the material difficult.. Three exams, not hard. If you do all the work, answer the top hats, and go to class, basically an A.

Rama's class is well organized and she clearly explains how to succeed. You will get an A if you follow her instructions. She teaches with flipped lectures so you must do your homework before class. This practice helped me comprehend topics extremely well. She is also incredibly understanding and worked with me when I was sick and missed class.

I went to all of her lectures, did all of the HW assignments, and kept up with course content. However, in her lectures, she mostly read off of slides & just walked through problems; not really explaining her steps or breaking it down deep for us. Expected us to rely heavily on the online textbook/homework.
Definitely wouldn't take a class with her again. Went to her for help and she was kind of rude about it, acted like I was an idiot because I didn't understand what we were doing in class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ms. Luginbuhl I thought was an excellent teacher. i had a hard time at first due to a terrible class (not hers) when i expressed concern she readily helped.  Also sent emails to make sure i was understanding everything from there on out. She is very knowledgeable and helpful!

I agree with the last comment, there was alot of material that wasn't covered in class that was on the exam.  And I DID read the insanely large amount of reading material as well.  Her lectures were interesting but it was not what I expected for a world regional geography class.  It seemed more like a poli sci class.  Grading was pretty harsh.
Exams cover issues not explained in class.
april rocks and rolls!
she's a great TA... approachable and easy to understand, even when she gets lost in a topic
This is a great class for those of us who are not into science, especially physical science. April is really nice and helpful, and very concise with the material she presents. Take her class!
The labs for this class was a joke, but she taught the class very well and will make the effort to answer every question that she gets.
On time, knows the material well.  OK sense of humor, especially when pertaining to her spelling and artistic abilities.  I would recommend her to most anyone.
She was a TA when I took this class with Dr. Bryan Mark.  Very helpful and her lab's were easy.

She was a TA for Professor Robbins. She lectured a few times and was good, but said "right?" a few too many times... it got annoying. VERY helpful outside class... she went over exams with people and that helped clarify the material.
Very cute, pretty easy class; "Here is my lame drawing of Ohio";nice person,very helpful; a little disorganized,but not too bad.
Amazing. She will be greatly missed here at OSU. But she is not only a conductor but an educator as well. She is unbelievably kind, resourceful and wise.
never steps out of her box.
Dr. A is wonderful! Period!
No Comments

Women's Glee.  She gave me an "A".  I worked hard, and sang at a lot of extra gigs where I didn't have to show up.  Our public concerts were just awesome, especially at the Wexner Party Barn for the Beat Michigan Party.  Yay Women's Glee!  Hope we can sing at the football games with Coach Tressel!!

Women's Glee Club.  A nice person.  It is early in the quarter, but so far she seems like an excellent instructor, and a nice and caring person.  I hope I can stay with this club a very long time (it can be repeated).
No Comments
Her online classical mythology was very well organized and she was great at teaching through her videos, exams where also easy.

CLAS2220; Dr. Amey is very passionate about the topic, and her enthusiasm helps make lectures interesting. RMP doesn't allow any mention of course content, so I can't get into specifics, but she always kept students in-the-know and was very involved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor was very likeable, and the homework was not too hard. Lectures and readings were very easy to follow, and she doesn't bombard you with work like a lot of professors do.
Really enjoyed her class. Great teacher.

Prof Amey was great for 2220! Based mostly on lectures and some light reading, so be aware of some time necessary to do the work. She genuinely cares about the subject. Class is quiz heavy but they are simple and based straight from the lectures. Would recommend this class and Prof Amey!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class online, but I actually enjoyed her lectures, and watched them all the way through. Some of them are long, and I turn up the speed, but I still enjoyed listening to her, and I recommend her lecture style. Class is only slightly demanding, and she gives clear instructions and feedback on what she wants and expects from you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Don't take him if you can

Yes, he has an accent and some people think he's yelling at them, but it's just because he's passionate. He likes to answer your questions and will only lecture for 5 minutes each session then do practice problems which are pretty much what will be on the test. Great teacher, tests weren't bad if you do the homework and practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gilat lectures well, his midterms were fair, his final was difficult, but he curved the class afterward. His office hours are helpful, and while he comes off as demeaning, he does not mean it. His homeworks are much harder than midterms, so it prepares you well for them. I think his bad rep is undeserved, people who show up and study do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AVOID. Take this class anywhere else, do not interact with Amos Gilat at all. Nice guy, sure, but not good teacher. Tests are 88 percent of the class, they are WAY harder than the homework, and no other opportunities for extra credit. Our final grade average was 55. THAT IS FAILING. If the average student fails your class, retire.

Bad lecturer and even worse at setting up a class. All combined, the entire class came down to how you did on exactly 16 problems. Nice enough if you meet him outside of class, but still won't help you much. He means well, but still avoid him if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gilat was one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. His lectures only include solving problems, with little explanations as to why we solve them. There are only 4 grades in the entire class: 6 quizzes, 2 midterms and the final (44%). Refuses to curve, even when the midterm avgs were below 65%. Exams are lengthy/hard, he doesn't care if you pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amos has some of the worst lectures at OSU, very hard to understand and most of the concepts require you to learn from YouTube. The class consists of 3 exams worth 88% of your grade. This concept alone should make anyone want to run away. When someone asks a question in class they are belittled. Worst experience Ive ever had. Avoid at all costs.

Don't take his course. You will only be graded on quizzes, midterms, and the final. The quizzes are worth 12% of your grade, midterms are 44% and the final is 44%. He is incredibly rude and will get upset if you ask a question that he doesn't think is a "good" question. He hates repeating anything and expects everything to come easy to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid by any means necessary. Its a hard class but his teaching method makes it 10 times harder. It is example after example with little to no explanation behind his problem solving strategy. The final is hard and worth 44% of your grade which is outrageous. Unfortunately the worst experience I've had at OSU.

Professor Gilat doesn't teach you any of the material. He expects you to learn it on your own and he does practice problems in class. This method of teaching may work for some people but it doesn't for me. He is available outside of class and will answer your "good" questions, but if you ask a "bad" question you will get made fun of.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not a bad person, but he is ignorant and kinda dont care how you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible and old lecturer, doesn't put anything online and it really isn't worth going to lecture or recitation. HW takes a good 10 hours a week. Exams are all open book and fairly simple however.

1181 is just a semester long hot mess. If you have never programmed before, the MATLAB is a little confusing. The class just isn't structured very well for practicing and getting good at programming. Also, it's an "inverted" class which means you just go a lot of stupid work at home, in addition to homework, and quizzes before every class.

Professor Gilat seems nice, but has no interest in this course, as he mentioned multiples times throughout the semester. Requires you to buy 2 of his awfully written textbooks, in which you will realize wont help you much for the 10+ hours of homework a week. Advice for incoming students: be prepared to learn this course on your own.
He is a nice guy. If you go to office hours, ask him questions. He is a bit condescending, but he will answer questions and he knows the material well.
He will refuse to help during his office hours. He says he doesn't have time for you because he's too busy writing his text books. Terrible professor.

Made everything seem easy in class then I would struggle on homework and midterms, often not knowing what ideas to apply. The examples in class were helpful but it would have helped if he taught it in a way that we would know what concepts to apply depending on the problem statement and given information.
Gilat was awful at explaining things, does not give equation sheet on tests

I wish he was more clear explaining what his mindset is in solving problems. He does nothing but do example problems in class, which I liked. I found this class is immensely difficult. Doesn't provide or let you make an equations sheet, so have fun memorizing tons of equations instead of actually studying. Just terrible.
Terrible. Goes over a few simple examples in class that do not prepare you well for the exams or homework, both are very difficult. Take this course with Dr. Mokashi if you have the chance.

This class was terrible. I dont think i learned one thing the entire semester. The material is so bad so it's hard to say how he is as a teacher. Lectures are pointless but his exams are really easy due to the open book policy. Homeworks were very hard and long, and only time I had a problem and went to his office he refused to help me out.

Well, if you're ME you have to take this class and you probably have to take it with him too. Homework is awful, as everyone agrees, but his exams are OK as long as you have a good idea of how to do stuff. Lectures are a waste of time. This professor is AWESOME for FE series, but for the actual ME class it's a rough ride. doable though!

His lectures are an absolute waste of time.  The material in the class is very straight forward, but the exams do not reflect the material that was gone over in class or the HW.  HW takes 5+ hours a week, is graded very late, so you do not know your grade until it is too late. Try to avoid for  ME250

Gilat's teaching is purely from powerpoint presentations. Programming classes should not be taught in a classroom! We need lectures to be labs. He forces you to use his incomprehensible textbooks. Homework is tedious and takes at least 5 hours per week. All seems well until the final, get ready for complete failure.

you're forced to use his crappy text books which are hard to follow and full of typos. the class is basic math but you are forced to think think a computer on all homeworks and tests, and they take a while to complete. he isnt very articulate so it can be hard to understand him.

One of OSU's worst teachers. If you have prior experience with MATLAB and can teach yourself quickly, then you may be OK. Otherwise, it will be a battle. Fast-paced, entirely not enough time for homework assignments, which are graded without mercy. You are on your own in this class, I don't know exactly what tuition paid for with this class.

The whole class is matlab and numerical methods.The grading is very tough,not enough time for the tests,the homeworks was very hard.20%homework 35% midterm 45% final.What he does in class is going through the slides which is really close from the book.He didn't give review sheets or examples for the tests,he didn't clarify what the tests are.
Real laid back guy. Goes over slides quickly which leaves you plenty of time to do your work.

The worst professor at The Ohio State, he gives no partial credit, the only reason he teaches this class is so you have to buy his book, you dont have to go be cause he reads straight out of the book, if you do go take a pillow.
He seemed uninterested at times. Although it's useful at TIMES, he swears by his MATLAB book (I think he just wants your moneys?). I did mediocre on the exams and still managed to get an A-
Funny guy.  Kept lectures short and sweet.  Made fun of the program's slides and made to sure to avoid confusing us.  Great professor, made 183 a breeze(not that its not easy already)
He was a pretty sweet teacher.  He keeps lectures short and sweet, but sticks around to help students 1 on 1.  He is pretty funny, but has a mild accent that isn't too bad.
Great teacher.  Was always available for guidance whether it was for the class or just life in general.  He just wanted to see his students succeed.
pointless class, homework a complete waste of time

awesome professor. Helpful and intrested in helping students succeed. Class is way too long but he tries to make it fun. Both the matlab book and numerical methods books are really good. Fair tests, hard homeworks at time, but you learn alot.
Explains things well, even if it takes a bit to hear what he's saying through his accent.  His book explains exactly what to do, homework takes a while but is never too hard.
He knows the Numerical Methods material he is teaching. He explains the code a bit too slowly for my tastes, but there are some folks who it's a good pace for.

wow...ummm way too much homework for only 10% of your grade...so your midterm and final are worth 90% of your grade...awesome....class is useless...i just  printed the notes offline and taught myself...dont buy the book...just mooch off of someone else when you rarely need it....overall...this class=worthless
No Comments

He's really into his research. With some professors, this can be a problem, but with Gilat, just talk to him about his research once or twice and he will become more interested in helping you out and seeing you succeed. Plus, he wrote the MATLAB book; I mean, seriously, who else could teach it better?
Hardly cared to teach or help students in my class.  He wrote the book on Malab, but refuses to help students with it at all.
Accent gets in the way sometime, but he wrote the book on MATLAB and there is no better person to talk to about it. He'll teach you to program so well in MATLAB you'll wanna use it for everything.
Helps he wrote the MATlab book
He is down to earth and seem to understand the student's thought.  Fairly flexible and available to  help.  Sometimes funny but his accent make what he said so serious.
Has a slovic accent but usually dont have any trouble understanding him. Not very hard, but it was a very easy course. Seemed willing to help. Has a light sense of humor and keeps things interesting
I had him as a lab instructor.  The lecture can be boring, but he's a very helpful teacher and makes the class interesting.
An accent, but you can still understand him.  He knows English very well but phrases he's used sometimes have made me crack up.  Very funny, helpful, and knows what he is talking about.
No Comments
No Comments
Funny and interesting! Makes class 10 times better!

I remember that a couple of years ago, I asked during office hours if I could get the study materials for the final exam early because I hadn't done very well on the previous exam. She did provide the materials as I requested, but later I heard that she complained to her earlier lecture about a certain “student” asking for them ahead of time.

I enjoyed Professor Sheneman's audit class for the most part. The exams were difficult, so you really need to understand the "why" behind the concepts or you will struggle. She does not lecture in the traditional sense, you must read the book to get a grasp of the material. There is opportunity for extra credit and she does curve.
Treats class like her therapist, so there is no time for teaching… getting paid $300k a year to BS
She is not teaching the material, and the exam is extremely hard. No matter how much I study, everything I prepare for the exam feels pointless.
She is of the opinion that there can only be a certain number of A's per semester. This means she will reduce your grade if she thinks enough people have gotten A grades already.
Very curt with students. She couldn't have cared less that the material is challenging and that she didn't make it any easier for us.
Lectures are not substantive.  Students have to teach themselves.

Prof. Sheneman's energy in class was great and she definitely knows her stuff. Lectures were well-paced and there were a few in-class team assignments that were good for solidifying knowledge. Rote memorization won't really help you learn the material; you have to understand how the topics actually work in order to do well on her exams.
The exams were extremely challenging, and the results didn't seem to reflect the effort I put in.
The exam content was not related to the sample questions and the exam was very difficult. CRAZY！！！

Professor Sheneman is one of the best professors I have had at Ohio State. Far and away one of the best at lecturing/teaching you material I have ever seen. That being said, her exams are hard and she is a strict grader on her papers.
