The class is pretty easy but she is disorganized and would assign things randomly with little notice.
Dr. Ard was very unorganized, but a fine professor. She and the TA were awful at answering emails, and I missed an A by them not communicating with each other very well.
Were not many assignments for this class, and when there were they were mainly 5 points or less. Lectures connect on a personal level and she welcomes but does not require participation.

Her lectures are interesting and projects are pretty easy. Homework is also really easy. Attend every lecture unless its online. Most of the exam questions are verbatim from the lectures and what she says so take good notes on important points. Referencing only the PowerPoints during exams will get you mediocre grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a great person outside of class and funny. Her assignments are very easy, however, her lectures go all over the place and she gets distracted easily. Her TA grades everything and is a very tough grader.
Meh. She was pretty unhelpful and hard to contact, and her class felt a bit messy and disorganized. Still an easy A.

Kerry is a captivating and inspiring professor and I suggest taking a course with her if possible. The only critique I have is that the final project was poorly explained at first, but it isn't too bad. Lectures are extremely interesting and this class is easy if you put in a bit of effort.

The lectures got boring towards the end but the Professor has a lot of passion and cares about her work and students. There are assignments for each class, due 2 days after that lecture, and they are easy and not worth many points. 3 exams and a final project (which couldve been explained better).Exams are fine as long as you take notes in class.

This class was horrible. Lectures are worthless. She posts things a couple days before they're due, so you never know when you'll have things due. The final group project is incredibly vague. Don't expect to be able to ever talk to her, as she doesn't respond to any emails. She turned this into a sociology class, and rarely mentions the environment

Dr. Ard was a very good professor. Lectures were interesting and required class participation. She did Kahoots that were for extra credit so make sure you show up to class. As long as you review her powerpoint and your notes the tests were fairly easy. Make sure to pay attention to the examples she gives in class. There is a group project as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very respected and caring of the students and the materials taught. Very personable and approachable. Class is lecture heavy and the tests reflect it. As long as you review the slides, the tests will be easy.

Love Kerry Ard. Her lectures are interesting and easy to follow. The exams do control the grade a lot, though, and I underestimated how hard the exam would be. Be SURE to study closely the lecture notes and write down the examples she gives. She is also strict about deadlines and doesn't accept late work. Fairly easy A if you put the effort in.

She is super sweet and really helpful. A lot of random assignments in class which help boost your grade. She does random kahoot quizzes some days which count as extra credit so go to class! The final project is incredibly confusing and unnecessary but it's not too much work outside of class, just difficult to communicate with your group.

She's the best! My favorite class AU19-- interesting, fresh, & relevant lectures for someone studying the environment. Attendance is important as midterms are lecture-heavy (pretty easy though) and most of the extra credit comes from Kahoot quizzes, but she doesn't take formal attendance. Lots of small assignments and 1 group project. Fairly easy A

Professor Ard is a great lecturer. Her class was really interesting and well presented. I didnt know what to expect when I took this class, but Im glad I did. Prof Ard is very passionate and intelligent. The class was graded off a few things and exams are lecture based. The poster project isnt difficult as long as you put forth effort
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting and Dr. Ard was very passionate about the topics we discussed. You definitely want to go to class because the exams are strongly based off of the lectures. There are also extra credit Kahoot quizzes.

Super easy tests. Frequent attendance checks (short groupwork or Kahoot quizzes). She is so sweet and cares a lot about what she teaches. Not always objective in the way she teaches controversial topics. The final is a poster project, it was very unguided and the requirements were unclear, but it was her first semester teaching ENR2300.

She was awesome! Her lectures could be boring sometimes but overall she is really funny and had a lot of things in the class I never thought about. There is a final poster project which is easy but the rubric was really unclear. Overall she is an easy-grader and really fun in class!

Professor Ard is energetic and shows enthusiasm in her teaching. Exams are based off of lecture down to the fine details, so show up and pay attention! Final project is vague and more frustrating than it needs to be. Interesting content, important to participate.
The lectures were interesting. She was nice and really enthusiastic which made lectures more fun. The final research project was frustrating because of my group but fine overall.

She's a great professor, but at the beginning of class during syllabus week, she said that attendance was non-mandatory. It is technically, but not if you want to pass the class. Tests are HEAVILY lecture- and example-based. Go to class, pay attention, and participate and you will do fine. Very nice woman, and interesting lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is awful.  It's held in a movie theater far away from any other class I take.  Parking won't happen for under 15 dollars a class.  The class itself is boring and doesn't look at all like what my friends in another section of the class are learning.  Dr. Ard is beyond rude.  No office hours.  The video final project is a waste of time.
Genuine professor, eager to teach! Simple course, weekly quiz (

Arya was an amazing professor, he provided feedback on each submission. His rubrics were clear.

Great course. Great professor!
he's a tough grader

He docks points on the most trivial of matters. The rubrics are very rigid in what he's looking for, and there's no room for nuance. I found his office hours unhelpful, and his reasoning confusing even after talking to him a few times. On extra credit he will dock points down the hundredths for random reasoning. I don't recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Athreya is a very good lecturer, and he was very lenient on grading. I wish I would have gone to more of his classes.
He is very caring and always willing to explain the content to those who may not be understanding or following along with the rest of the class.

Although his class wasn't the easiest, I learned so much from taking Networking with Professor Athreya. Showing up to class is very important and making sure you have the energy to keep up in lecture is as well. He was very good with clarifying things to his students. Exams similar to homework's but still tough.

Didn't respond to any emails the whole semester & Carmen was barren, so missing 1 lecture was catastrophic if you didn't have friends in class. Lectures were ok, but there were very few examples. He did them on a chalkboard, then they were lost to the void. You get a cheat sheet (& answer keys to hw) so the exams weren't impossible, but still hard.

Very knowledgeable, caring professor who can teach you a lot if you pay attention (dense lectures but never any extraneous information) and ask questions (he is fantastic at helpfully answering questions and taking the time to make sure everyone understands). Would recommend!

Lectures can be long and dense but if you can pay attention, he will explain everything in a very understandable way. Great at answering any questions you may have. For online, attendance was required either synchronously or asynchronously. Understand how to do all of the homework and the exams will come easier

She is super sweet and cares about the success of her students. HW assignments are not graded till the end of the semester though so you don't know what you did right or wrong. While she was super nice I think I would've learned more with another professor. Attendance is not mandatory and class often gets canceled.

Geri is a great teacher. You can tell she is passionate about what she teaches, and she explains concepts clearly. She is always available outside of class. The homework is manageable and she gives grace periods. The tests take a while to be graded though. She managed to fit a lot into 1 semester and did it in a way where it wasn't too hard.

Class so far is ok but her grading criteria is never clear. She even sometimes gets annoyed if we ask her questions during lecture. Canvas page and her "whiteboard" doc is all over the place too. She seems like a nice person but it feels like she is never prepared to teach us during class.
BEST GE course! Lots of content but she made it enjoyable. Highly recommend.

Amazing class, amazing lecturer. This was only a second session course that I took last moment but it turned out to be one of the best courses I've taken at OSU. Dr. Geri made the material relevant to everyone and so interesting! Totally accessible outside of class, great feedback on assignments and very flexible. I'm taking more classes w/her.

She's a sweet teacher and person but class was often canceled last minute, which threw off the schedule for the class. She also doesn't know Arabic? My dad is a native speaker and told me she was just straight up wrong about a lot. She's not a native speaker and you can tell. Also the class had a confusing structure and I didn't learn very much

The best Arabic Professor out there! She is really caring and patient and is really helpful when you ask her questions in class. I really learned a lot from her and even though there was a lot of homework, she was accommodating and allowed for late submission.

I've had Geri for 4 semesters and she has always been a very clear and generous grader. Very patient. She really wants you to succeed. Class is what you make it. She puts effort into it, lots of culture, music, videos, food. We read books and not just stupid Maha. But it's still a college class, not entertainment.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Takes years for her to grade just ONE assignment, assigns TOO much homework, and takes points off for no reason. Tells you to buy the textbook but uploads a picture of each drill on Canvas. Class is very boring as well.

She really just wants to see you succeed. There is homework every night, but it isn't excessive, just a worksheet normally. If you have a question, she'll take class time to answer. Sometimes she's a bit discombobulated and classes weren't very productive. If you participate, you'll get a lot more out of class. She includes culture lessons too
Fantastic professor! A heads up: she take a while to grade assignments and exams.
She was a great professor 10/10 would take it again!

Professor Geri is extremely knowledgeable and very clear about what she expects from her students. She's always willing to answer questions and she presents the material in a way that makes it accessible to everyone. Shes one of the most understanding and caring professors Ive had at OSU.

Not an easy class. Homework every day sometimes multiple homeworks in one day. Way too much work for a GE class. left no time for other coursewprk. Textbook an online drills pretty bad and expensive. Shes nice though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's amazing! She assigns very little homework, yet still teaches you the language well. She clearly loves Arabic and teaching. She really cares about her students and spends a lot of time ensuring that they do well. But you need to be there in order for that to happen! Tons of extra credit opportunities and super flexible!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved her! She gives an enthusiastic and inspirational intro to the arabic language. It's clear she's very passionate about it. She gives daily homework but it usually isn't too hard, and neither are the tests if you actually show up tp class and do your homework. She's so helpful and sweet, uses the language a ton in class. 100% would take again

She's been my favorite professor here at OSU. She cares very much about her students and it's obvious her opinion has a lot of weight in the department. Like most OSU language classes, the content is not particularly difficult but there's a lot of work. She is more than willing to work with you if you are struggling. Overall amazing teacher.
My favorite class this semester.

Geri gave me a great introduction to the Arabic language. She was caring and helpful, but her consistent tardiness and lack of follow-through left me frustrated at many times. At the end of the day, I learned a lot, but to get the most out of this course, she is not the most advisable choice of the professors at OSU at this level.

Geri cares about what she is teaching and is always wiling to answer questions. You are taking a foreign language class so it will be difficult, just stay up to date on vocab. I have had Geri for 3 semesters and so have many other people in class.

This is the second class that I have taken with Professor Geri and she is INCREDIBLE. She is a great and accommodating lecturer and really helps in office hours. It is clear that she wants you to pass but it IS NOT an easy class even for some heritage speakers. KNOW THE VOCAB and study! If you don't care about this class you will not pass.

Absolutely worst class ive ever taken. Atiq did not care for her students and used a filpped classroom model which is the absolute worst for a CS class. I understood nothing as a beginner to coding, I struggled so much and the lectures makes absolutely 0 sense. I would rather anyone else.
Disorganized teaching yet requires obnoxious amounts of busy work. Read the previous reviews and really think whether you want to take an elective she teaches. She hasn't changed for the better.
micromanagemaxxer
this lecture wastes my 3hours each week, the content in this class is so easy, but this teacher spend so much time on this meaningless activities. if u get her class, drop immediately

she makes me want to drop out of school and pursue a job in the fields in remote romania to work with cattle. and just thinking about doing that sounds like an absolute vacation compared to having to learn to code by reading a textbook. it makes me angry just thinking about walking into lecture and having to hear her ramble for 55 minutes about bs

The class is fine as long as you put in some effort. I got an A and don't have any CS background. She is a good professor, the lectures are engaging. But, she is unapproachable. There are stupid questions and she will make it clear if you asked a 'stupid' question or answer in class.

She was boring but was clearly passionate about the material. Please go to office hours; sit down and go over the quizzes/homework. TAs were average. She doesn't mind using AI to help you but don't depend on it. She uses AI to generate quiz questions lol. Quiz and Projects alternate every other week. Tip: include projects in your portfolio.
Quizzes are the hardest part of the class, but as long as you do the work you can still pass with an A.

Treats students like middle schoolers when no one answers her questions. Lectures aren't helpful whatsoever (she rambles). The hw for the week is for the lecture a weekish after it's due, so you get lectures on topics you've forgotten. Ended with an A but only after proving her wrong through TEN EMAILS that she gave me the incorrect grade. AVOID

Any time a student would get a question wrong or asked a question she would look at them like they were absolutely clueless. When emailing her, I felt that her responses were a bit rude and she was unable to comprehend simple questions. Class structure was also not ideal, if you have no coding experience it's even worse.
Lectures are a waste of time. The structure of the class is ridiculous. Homework is due before you even get a lecture about the topic. Didn't learn a single thing.

She uses a flipped classroom teaching style, and lectures are not that useful. Having taken programming classes beforehand, it was not difficult. During lectures, she treats students like middle schoolers whenever no one answers her questions. No final exam, only hw, labs, and projects, nothing too difficult. Acts entitled, try to get another prof

She is degrading to students in class and humiliates anyone who has a wrong answer, while at the same time getting mad when nobody answers her questions because they're scared of getting humiliated. She acts like a middle school teacher. She has a temper. She is not a good lecturer. She was not that helpful the one time that I went to office hours.

Her lectures are a waste of time, and you learn nothing. She assigns pointless tasks and doesn't create a good learning environment. She's critical whether students talk too much or too little. The class is easy, though, so it doesn't really matter.

As a first time java learner this class did not teach me anything at all. She uses a flipped classroom so get ready to teach yourself everything through a online textbook. The good thing is there are no exams, instead there are bi weekly projects and quizzes which are very time consuming if you don't already know how to code.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You learn everything on zybooks so lectures are pointless other than the random participation assignments. The "labs" are just computer rooms where you do homework independently. Both should be optional but attendance is graded. She's super inflexible as well. Not too hard to get an A but even missing one week can drop your grade down.

This professor is extremely difficult and is very inflexible. She was very unclear with how she was grading the attendance. Once she actually put in her "participation" grades, my grade dropped significantly despite showing up to every lecture and lab. Do not skip out on any of the tophat questions or try to take this class with another professor.

Not happy with this class one bit. She put us into groups from the beginning and none of my group mates ever showed up. Had zero coding experience beforehand which didn't help. Zybooks is stupid, the professor just relies on it to teach us the material then the labs do not correlate to the reading. Complete mess. Made me cry on multiple occasions.

DO *NOT* TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! If you want to learn, you won't; her lectures are useless and weeks behind the quiz/textbook material. She grades for participation: attending class was 1 point for the first nine weeks. After our final quiz/project, she began cramming in 5-point questions to deliberately fail students who didn't go. Inflexible. Awful!

The most challenging professor I encountered at OSU was incredibly unhelpful. Her teaching style lacked effectiveness, and she seemed unwilling to offer any guidance.she exhibited rudeness, making the learning environment uncomfortable. she was not accommodating when it came to assignment extensions, for students who missed deadlines.
She doesn't teach whatsoever, and you can't understand her. Would never take a course with her ever again.

Professor Atiq was awful. I had an issue with my projects not being graded and instead of being apologetic and trying to solve my problem she brushed me off and made excuses for my grader. She couldn't remember who I was and she said it was asking a lot to have a different grader grade my work and she can't force the graders to do their job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The "flipped" classroom that Professor Atiq uses is not a conducive learning environment. We were always a week behind the lectures compared to the assignments. Didn't learn anything in lecture and she would get side tracked very easily. Would not recommend taking an intro to Java class with her.

Although she is passionate about what she teaches, she often goes on rants about things off topic that tend to make her lectures confusing. Definitely go to the TA's office hours and lab blocks as they can often explain things that are confusing during lectures.

Super disorganized and often gets distracted during lectures. Posted all the slides and lectures online and relied mostly on those and the online textbook to teach myself. She is incredibly forgiving though and will give you reasonable extensions if you need them. Poor and disorganized lecturer, but a good person.

Not the greatest lecturer but a very forgiving professor as long as you show effort. I would recommend utilizing her and the TA's office hours when you can. If you don't have an interest/expereince in coding, this class might be more difficult to you due to the flipped classroom way of teaching, but still manageable.
Prof. Atiq's class is designed to be online but is now instructed in person with no changes. She gave projects and reading assignments over spring break.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most programming professors hand you a textbook and say "email me if you have questions". This woman actually teaches the content. She goes over concepts in depth in a way that everyone can understand. A+ professor.

Her lectures are a week behind when she has the associated assignments due. Also, she doesn't really answer emails and her lectures are not very helpful. The quizzes suck and they're trick questions rather than testing your knowledge. She is disorganized and often doesn't even know what is on the homework she assigns through Zybooks.

Ok professor. As long as you teach yourself well with zybooks, you're good. She seemed kind of mean at first but once I got to know her better she wasn't all that bad. The deadlines and grades are pretty forgiving if you reach out. The TAs for the course also helped a lot.

She does not answer emails and is an awful lecturer. This is pretty much a self teach class... the TAs are helpful and she has office hours too but it simply isn't enough. The flipped classroom format is awful at such a big school.
Please don't take her class. She teaches nothing and is extremely rude

The course was disorganized. We used an interactive website called Zybooks and basically you learn everything on Zybooks. She assumes that students have a previous knowledge about programming which makes it hard for students to keep following her. No exams, you just have to finish the projects so thats nice. Be prepared to study on your on.

First programming class, I ever took and it was a struggle. Primarily used Zybooks with barely any help from her. Should've bought Zybooks on my own and taught myself since that's what happened anyways. I asked her for information on getting a tutor and she told me to go to her office hours for help, then didn't show up.

While not my favorite professor, she is absolutely a solid choice for learning Java. I had no coding experience before starting, and now I understand most concepts with only a slight bit of hesitancy. Zybooks was used quite a lot, but her quick lectures and self-checks are actually useful. Overall I'd say 8.5/10, would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: If you have to take this class, Dr. Atiq is a great option. I think I listened to her teach on Zoom for maybe 5 hours over the whole semester so this class is very self-driven but extremely doable with office hours and the internet. If its your first coding class give yourself a HUGE advantage and practice with a free online java website before!

Dr. Atiq was a great teacher and I really enjoyed her class! She was very forgiving wehn it came to extending deadlines. Super nice and made sure she took time to explain things if you were confused. I had no coding experience before taking this class and she did a great job teaching everyone from scratch.

Dr. Atiq was wonderful! I never talked to her much, I usually communicated with TA's, but she's great to have in class. I was in the first CSE 1223 class to be taught entirely online, and I think she did a pretty good job handling it.

I honestly forgot I had a professor for this class. All she did was host the zoom meetings and send us to breakout rooms for online group projects. We learned everything from the online book (which isn't helpful) or videos that she uploaded of another professor. I learned everything from the internet by looking it up than from her. Hard projects.
If you have no coding experience youll be fine in her class. Shes willing to help you and shell drop your lowest lab and project.

I had never programmed before in my life but it honestly wasnt that bad. She very obviously is trying her best to help students learn. If you have any prior experience at all in programming should be an easy A and if you dont you can still more than likely get an A.

Michelle seemed like she wanted to be literally anywhere else. She had no grading criteria and then would take points off for stupid stuff you werent aware you needed to say in your reflection. She was very unorganized and the lectures were all pointless.
Good teacher and class was easy. Took it online and finished all the work for the semester in 1 week. Weekly quizzes and 2 work sheet assignments. You won't find an easier class at osu.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the online standard instructor OSU is known for. Inconsistent grading criteria with assignments. Did not provide feedback on weekly discussions regardless if you missed some or no points. Final grades posted to Carmen without acknowledging the semester has ended or wishing students success going forward. Very uncaring, and hands-off.

The entire course consists of weekly discussions/posts, one Art viewing and one Film review assignment. She ONLY provides feedback on your two viewing assignments but none for the discussions, regardless if you earn all points or not. Her email communication style is very dismissive, curt and uncaring.

Atilla is great and communicates the material as clearly as possible. I found sometimes the topics were explained better by other sources, leaving me confused in lecture. He gave brutally difficult homework and exams, and grades reflected this. However, he understands the class is hard and curves generously in the end.

The course material is very difficult to truly comprehend. No matter who's teaching the course the material will still be hard. But Atilla is an extremely bright and understanding professor. The class has a generous curve and if you stay engaged and truly make an effort to at least somewhat understand the material you will be just fine
Good teacher. you will learn a lot. Take him
He is super nice and helpful.  Class is hard, but it is ECE Signals and Systems.  Really good at giving you the materials you need to succeed.

Atilla is a humble, nice Prof. He is really smart, much smarter than you thought. The class material is a little hard. He made his class easy to understand. You actually can learn things in his class.

This guy really should have a higher rating. One of the more quality professors I've had in EE. Relatively new, so the ratings listed might be when he was starting out. Went at a reasonable pace. Very conscious of students' workloads. Midterms were challenging, homework was never too hard, and the final was easy. Highly recommend for control class.
Know the materials very well. Make great effort to teach the course well. Kind and helpful if you have any questions. Hard exams. But you learn the things after the course.

Relatively difficult assignments and exams. Made his greatest effort to make his lectures clear and have students learn, but didn't seem terribly interested in the subject matter. Final grade was slightly higher than expected.
Very difficult assignments and exams. But the course is interesting. Posts lectures, solutions and grades on Carmen. Liberal with the final grade!
Uses alto of technology in class, which is good. Need to work to get an A.
Once put a problem on a midterm, in his own words, "because I knew you would all fail it". Would post slides but only the blank versions. Worst teacher I ever had about testing and good assignments.

very interesting material and well explained. The only problem is examples in class are easy compared with the homework and tests. So understanding the examples in class doesn't help you on homework. Needs to hold more office hours. His use of technology is great and refreshing though. I'd reccomend him!

This professor cares about the class and tries to be helpful although more office hour and better examples would be nice.  Homework is hard and long but if you try to understand it rather than just completing it, it would help you on the exam.  Exams are fair but really test your understanding of the materials.

Knows what he is teaching. Notes were helpful and the homeworks, midterms and finals were application of the course. Though the no. of problems worked out in the class were less and not helpful. In a nutshell, the class was good and would recommend it to my friends

I agree with those before me who say the hw and exams are hard.. however, I used his office hours every week and he always cleared things up. He's helpful, he just tries to test our knowledge a little too thoroughly. After thinking I would tank in the class, I got an A-. Bottom line: Ask him lots of questions and attend class, you'll be all right.

Teaches only theory with almost no examples(and the ones he does do are somewhat useless). The book is also almost all theory. Midterms/Finals were hard with not big basis on Homework. I would not recommend this to somebody who has a hard time following only theory.

Lectures are clear.  He is helpful in office hours. Exams are finishable in allotted time and really do test your understanding. However, examples in lecture are much simpler than homework or exam questions.  He does not hold enough office hours. Exam questions tend to be shockingly different than what you've seen before in homework or lectures.
The teacher was Kind hearted but his exams were much different from homeworks and reviews. The textbooks examples were also hard to comprehend.

Notes in class are clear and easy to read.  Knows how to use a computer unlike many other prof who were born before the 1900.  No prob worked out in class.  HW is more complicated than notes, midterm more complicated than hw, and final more than midterm.

Notes in class are clear and easy to read.  Knows how to use a computer unlike many other prof who were born before the 1900.  No prob worked out in class.  HW is more complicated than notes, midterm more complicated than hw, and final more than midterm.

Horrible.  He has lots of easy examples in class, and posts his notes!...Or, rather, his blank notes templates.  Unhelpful in office hours, unable to answer any questions, unable to teach.  The last 3 weeks or so out of 10 were spent on ECE 600 material.  Seriously.  We finished the syllabus so he went on...but didn't give us any examples or good h
All examples that are worked in class are easy. Enjoy them because you wont see anything like them in the homework, midterms, or textbook. There cannot be a more difficult person on the planet!

I took Theatre 2100 in the first semester of my Freshman Year. I expected it to be miserable as I had it as an 8 AM. However, Jacob made the class awesome. Hes genuinely passionate about what hes teaching and will always listen to everyones feedback, and he also grades generously. Easily the best 2100 teacher. Would highly recommend.
Such a good teacher. Easy to get an A in his class. Cares about his students and is understanding. Made the class more interesting and was super funny.

Jacob was awesome, really cared about the subject and introducing it to people who may not have any theater experience. Made sure the class was fun and everyone got involved. Worked with anyone with scheduling issues. Really a teacher who cared about the students and the subject.

You have to show up to class. It's like a lab/lecture combo where if you miss a class it's hard to get the material since you're trying to keep up with your group. Patel understands and helps in making sure you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I wish I had more Professors like Atmiya, he cares and takes time to address all of your concerns and ensures you understand the material fully.
so much fun!
Group lab based class. A lot of fun and helpful. Every teacher should take this class.

Did a good job of going over the material in class and was helpful if approached with questions. As long as you study all of the theorems, definitions, etc. everything should come fairly easily. None of the exams were unreasonable. Makes it so you're basically guaranteed a C (50%) and will take final exam score if overall grade is lower than it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Any introduction to discrete math is going to be a hard class.  However, I found that Athipat's lectures were clear and he answered questions patiently both in and outside of class.

I thought Athipat was a pretty good professor. His lectures were interesting and enjoyable, and he gave plenty of hints about what would be on the final. It's not his fault that an introductory proofs-based course can be hard for students.
Don't even bother. Drop now while you can. Get a different prof by any means necessary,

Horrible professor, debatably worse professor ever. If you have this professor for MATH 3345, I strongly recommend that you switch professors immediately. If you cannot switch professors, drop the class, it is not worth it.

Avoid. He reads directly from the book. He doesn't post grades. He varies on how he grades. His exam averages are sub 50. You don't get feedback on homework, and you can't find the solutions anywhere because they are all proofs.

Lecture is straight from the textbook. Grading scale is never explained and there is no way to tell how well you are doing in the class. No feedback is given on exams, and very little partial credit is granted. Avoid this professor. Even if you end up with a good grade, it's not worth the stress of wondering for the entire semester.
Just take my word and avoid him.  He shouldn't even be a professor.

He is absolutely terrible.  This guy has no clue what he is doing and can't even explain to you what you did wrong.  If you make a mistake in a proof, the whole rest of the proof is incorrect.  So if you make a small mistake in the first line, you get a 0 for the problem  even if the rest of the proof is correct.  AVOID ATHIPAT!!!

Completely unclear grading scheme, and no grades recorded on Carmen. Literally laughs at sub 50 averages on midterms, and gives us no indication of how well we're going to do in the class. You may get an A, you may get an E ... only Athipat knows!

He lectures straight out of the book (shared for all 3345) and doesn't give much context for anything. Assignments come without much warning but average a homework or two a week. The final is basically everything and his tests are basically made up of proofs that are easy to lose points on. If you test well, you might be okay.

His lectures are extremely boring and he has no passion for what he is doing.  He also grades ridiculously hard and refuses to negotiate points under any circumstances.  Athipat also does not always write scores on assignments, so it's impossible to track your grade since he doesn't use Carmen.  Avoid.

He lectures straight out of the book. Grading is up to his discretion. Homework is lightly graded, while exams and quizzes are taken point for point. The average for midterm 1 was a 60, which I quote, "That's a pretty good average" by him. Average for midterm 2 was so bad he just said "It's below a 50," and proceeded to lecture. Avoid.

If you have to take this- take it with professor raferty-semon. Sanchez isn't the main lecturer and can only offer limited help. the group projects are so unclear and way harder than they need to be. Content is so easy but the instructional team is such a headache.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There are 5 exams, no final, a fundamental assignment (open note), a pronunciation assignment, and an application assignment (open note) due each week. These assignments don't take too much time to complete, and directions are straightforward. Never interacted with the professor, but I enjoyed the class. She also provides extra credit too!
The content is moderately challenging but do not email her with any issue because she's extremely unprofessional and not flexible at all. Do not recommend.

This professor was great and the class was very straight forward. It consisted of roughly 5 midterms which were very easy in difficulty and then weekly assignments. I would say I spent maybe an hour per week on the course and ended with a 99. Highly recommend.

Dr. Atkinson is a wonderful professor! He is very smart (a part of MENSA) but socially awkward. He had trouble the other day when he wasn't able to use the powerpoint. He may seem like a total klutz/ nerd, but he is right on top of things. Just do ALL of the reading and listening for the class and you are set. Hard teacher, but definitely worth it!
Class was great
very quirky and fun, but the tests were difficlut (particularly the listening aspect)
Worst teacher ever! He's so scatterbrained, it's impossible to study for the exams. The notes make no sense at all and the class is so boring! Whatever you do, don't take a class taught by Atkinson!!

Great professor. A lot of listening in this class but interesting discussions in lectures. The only bad thing is that he teaches the class vertically as far as genres and dates. You need to think vertically to be able to do the essays on the tests

I've never come across anyone so humbly brilliant in my life. The man thinks everyone else speaks fluent French, German, and Greek, but it's not beyond him to explain concepts more clearly. It's a great class taught by one of the greatest Musicology profs in the nation.

Having taken the class at another institution, I feel that Prof. Atkinson's version is much easier.  The class is not too difficult if you attend and listen to the discussions.  All the notes given in class are posted on-line, so you never have to worry about writing down everything.  Two books are required, but only the listening guide is used.

He is VERY smart...and that makes his class VERY hard. His tests were impossible...nothing he emphasized in class was on them, and he never seemed to care that people were not doing well on them. The class was miserable.
Absolutely brillant and a very nice guy

This man is an expert in medieval music, so it was very interesting to have him as a teacher for this course. His tests are hard, but it isn't terribly difficult to get an A. He is very helpful and willing to explain something to you until you understand. He is also very funny if you pay attention to what he's saying.
He's an extremely difficult professor, but he knows his stuff, really loves jazz, and is generally a really nice guy.
Brilliant, brilliant, brilliant.  Is very accomodating when you show interest in his subject. Tests are difficult, but not impossible.

Very Intelligent, he knows his stuff, but conveys it in the most boring manner possible. His tests are way too difficult and provides no study sheets, course packs, or anything to help students whatsoever.
Lock this man in a room and let him do research!  He's brilliant, but keep him out of the classroom!

Easiest class ever. Maybe 2 hours max each week with work. Quizzes were open note-took 5 min if searched up key words in articles. She dropped lowest quiz grade. Reflections were incredibly easy. Gave a lot of extra credit (even though I got 100% without it). Cared for students and gave weekly activities going on around campus that were low-cost.

The BEST professor I have had at OSU! The material interesting and participating in class comes very naturally. I promise you will be able to relate to many things in this course, even if you do not think you will. No midterm. No final. One paper, about 2-3 pages in length. All you have to do is show up to class and contribute. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!
Super easy class, attendance is mandatory though. Just make sure you show up and pay attention in class and you'll get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bermea is a great professor! She is nice to students and accepts feedback. Multiple times throughout the course she changed our group work based off of what students wanted or added extra credit when asked. Attendance is mandatory and you will have to go to all the lectures, but other than that it is easy to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bermea is a great professor. She is passionate about what she is teaching and cares about her students. The class is mostly based on class discussions and group projects with a few quizzes and assignments here and there. If you follow her rubrics, you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His teaching was clear. Problem set was useful for preparing exam.
He shows no enthusiasm in teaching, hardly provides any study materials, and gives out the worst test questions ever. Easily the worst professor I've ever had. RUN AWAY FOR YOUR OWN GOOD

To be honest, he is the worst Professor I've ever seen. The concept of the ppt is very disarray, and he always need students to point out his mistakes. The most common thing he says is, "I don't know." If you want to get a good grade, just learn it by yourself. The assignment and quiz has nothing to do with the class content.

The only grades are the two midterms and the final. Honestly, this class was just so hard. If you didn't do well on one exam, it was just too hard to make it up. The teaching style was odd and he constantly had to have students correct him in lecture because his notes were wrong. Attendance is mandatory so make sure you go to class.

This guy really is a gem. He's hilariously blunt, but took a little to warm up to the class. He is really smart and can sometime come off as cocky, which he totally is. but also hes willing to admit when he messes up. Class isn't easy but very rewarding. If you don't understand something the first time, don't worry, he ll go over it at least 4x.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Aubhik Khan's class gives a glimpse into the real world of an economist and his classes were practical, funny and insightful for an intermediate econ course. Though his explanations can sometimes be confusing, a reading from textbook will reinforce the concepts better. the class gave a satisfaction of learning something new and cool every time.

Aubhik is incredibly smart and super funny. HOWEVER, he has a hard time sharing his knowledge, class lectures are repetitive and drag on and you felt as if you've learned nothing. TAKE NOTES and definitely read the book, it will help make clear things that Aubhik made unclear. Tests are based off of major concepts and are hard but doable
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DO NOT take a class with Dr. Khan. He is funny and clearly knows the topics, but he is very, VERY bad at communicating the information with you. He will lecture all class, only to be corrected by a student at the end of class on a mistake he made at the beginning of the problem. Relied heavily on the textbook, but even that wasn't great.

is this dude honestly kidding? Have no clue how I received the grade I did because he doesn't put individual grades on canvas. Literally just got a notification on my phone that my grade was in and thats it. did not learn one thing just showed up. exams are easy if you study the previous quizzes but i would never take a class with this guy again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: lol what is this guy doing. honestly better off just studying from the textbook and then just show up to class for quizzes. the dude isn't confusing as much as he is redundant and unorganized. he kind of gave up midway through, stopped posting solutions on canvas; gave us 4 chapters to study in last lecture, none of them were on the exam. #feelsbad
Overcomplicated material, contradicted himself half the time.... terrible class, terrible professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Stopped going to class and just used the textbook and I still didn't miss any material. Only went for quizzes. Pretty easy class that he makes unnecessarily confusing. Honestly don't know if we'll get through 1/3 of the syllabus, exams aren't bad if you study from homeworks and textbook. Funny, self-deprecating, poorly organized: Professor Khan.
Aubhik is pretty funny, but he teaches the non-calculus based section with a lot of calculus. You'd be better off taking this course with a different teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You take 5 quizzes, but only the best 3 count. There is one midterm and a cumulative final. He posts homework online, but it is not for a grade. You have to attend lecture to understand the concepts. The quizzes and tests are all based off the optional homework. I would recommend taking this class with him; I heard other professors make it hard.

Really good lecturer and made micro pretty easy. Didn't cover much material though, only about half of the syllabus. 2 midterms and a final, all pretty easy. 5 quizzes, best 3 count. as he gives hints for exams. Don't need book other then to check info from lecture. DO THE HOMEWORK and the derivations he covers, all exam questions come from these.

Good guy, easy class. Kind of a joke though. I had him for micro, and you can tell he's a macro prof. Do the homework sets and understand them and you'll get an a, the tests are based off the homework not anything he says in class

Aubhik is a very entertaining professor. He's very funny and is always making jokes that make lecture enjoyable. He doesnt cover everything he sayshe is going to because he spends weeks on each chapter. But he makes it clear what he expects for his homework sets and exams. Overall he is a good professor and its not hard to get a decent grade
Not my favorite professor. He was rude and off putting.

Dr. OQuinn is a good lecturer who takes time to make sure students are following the material. The required/graded workload is light, but optional content is heavy: optional content consists of videos or readings (you need these to do well imo). 
Pros:
Good lecturer
Pretty easy grader
Very nice person
Cons:
Hard-ish tests
Slow grader

The lectures are interesting and he genuinely cares about and has experience in the material. The problems on the tests encourage thinking about real-life scenarios rather than regurgitating lecture notes. The only thing I'd say is that he does not give much feedback, although he is quite lenient.

The lectures are good but dry. He moves a bit fast at times but consistently checks to make sure people are following. The real reason I am writing this review is because he was so understanding and helpful when I went through a major life event. He is a very understanding and clearly wants to help students succeed and understand.
Yeah nah I hate the class but it's easy as hell. Take her to get rid of Race & Diversity GE. Free A.
amazing take here
Class is back heavy but there are no exams and she is a very engaging teacher.
She is a great professor and very caring about her students.  The class is a little back heavy but there are no exams so it is compensated.

Professor Kearney is one of the best I have had in my time at Ohio State. She is personable and makes class something you want to go to and engage with. Be sure to read or watch any clips before class as it makes everything click more and gives you a better chance at being engaged with class! The papers are not too hard either.

Professor Kearny is an amazing teacher! She takes some complex concepts and theories and breaks them down for better understanding. Assignments are straightforward and easy. I recommend coming to class prepared, such as watching any clips or read articles she provides, to make the learning experience more engaging. I would take her class again!

She is a great professor and cares so much about her students. Her class was so interesting, and I loved to show up to each class. There are no quizzes or tests, so you are just graded on writing assignments that are really easy. In class conversations helped me to learn a lot of new things and they were great to be a part of.

Ms. Kearney's class was very informative and worthwhile as someone taking the course for a GE requirement. She does an amazing job at connecting with her students and hearing our input. There are no tests or quizzes and the short writing assignments are mostly based on personal experience and topics discussed in class. Definitely a 10/10.

Autumn has been my favorite professor that I have ever had the honor to work with. She is amazing at explaining complex topics and treats her students with the utmost respect. She is truly an inspiration and mentor in my academic career. Her class is always interesting and kept respectable. She is understanding and an absolute gift to work with.

Great lecturer and I really enjoyed this class. I also found the content enjoyable which helped. I would recommend this class as long as the topic sounds interesting to you. There is some homework involved, but I didn't think it was too bad.

Great lecturer, really cared about the subject and wasn't boring even though the class is mostly lectures and discussion posts. If you show up and pay attention, it's an easy A and a fun class. If you don't care (and already know some) about the history of music, it'll be a lot harder

There is way to much information in each class and exam with too much work for a Gened which doesn't apply to 99.9% of students majors. He also gives too much work and is a tough grader for a class where you don't learn anything you would ever use again. I also had a 89.72 as a final grade which he refused to round up.

I did not enjoy this class and wouldn't recommend. The lectures were very boring and long and the slides were packed with information. The tests were moderate and there was always a take home exam to go along with the tests. The take home exams were easy and just a short essay, but at the end we had a paper along with that which was a lot for a GE.
Gives entertaining lectures and works to make class worth attending. Exams are not very difficult. Attendance is graded.

I really enjoyed Dr. Juhnke's lectures! This class changed the way I view music and I feel so much more knowledgable now because of it. He's such a friendly guy and very easy to talk to and ask questions. You have to do a takehome essay with each exam and a final 1000 word paper, but it was graded easily and didn't take too long. Highly recommend!

This was a fantastic gen ed for me to take. Austin is super knowledgeable, and keeps his lectures interesting, engaging, and funny. Plus, I've learned so much about music and you literally listen to rock for 1/3 of the class. If you pay attention it should be an easy A.

No brainer - take this class!
Austin teaches a pretty interesting class to begin with but does a great job to go over the top and make it even better. Lectures are lengthy but still easy to pay attention to.

I love Austin. He is such an interesting person as well as very approachable and caring. He is so open to discussion and allows students to express their ideas openly without judgement. He is fun in class and is always smiling. He is also very available if you have any questions or concerns. His class was always a highlight.

The class surprisingly had a lot of work for a Gen Ed but I enjoyed listening to Austin. His lectures were engaging and I learned ton in this class. Exams/work aren't really difficult as long you pay attention.

Austin is a good guy but incredibly disorganized. He does not give us a clear idea of what is being tested until the last minute. For our second exam we had to memorize 30 songs and he wondered why the average was a D+. Luckily he gives enough extra credit and curved that exam so that the class average remains slightly above a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class isn't bad besides the fact that at the beginning of the semester, we were told that you didn't have to have any musical background whatsoever. I found this class challenging at times because I had no background. Also, there is an essay for all three exams and a big final paper. This professor is also pretty boring!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Austin is a wonderful professor who cares a lot about the topic. I took him for History of Rock and Roll and it was one of the most interesting classes I've taken so far. Biggest downside is that there are so few grades, 85% of the class is on 4 assignments. On the plus side, the grading on the papers is easy. Definitely recommend him for any class
If you're not religious, pick a religion and pray. She does not care about you one bit.

reviews.comment: Don't take.
This Professor brings OSU to a lower standard

reviews.comment: Audrey Light is straight up poverty. Hours upon hours of mind numbing lecture videos and problem sets that have nothing to do with the exams. She might as well write the exams in a different language. I don't know who hurt her, but someone did and she wants to take that out on her students by making their lives as miserable as possible. The worst.

Rudest person I've ever met inside or outside of a classroom. She seems extremely unhappy and to genuinely hate people. I actually feel sorry for her in that she's so unhappy. I blame the university for accepting tuition money from students and subjecting them to a woman who obviously needs professional psychiatric help.

I do not know how Light is still a professor at this university. I have never left a RMP review before but she, even though I took this online asynchronously, still managed to be the worst professor I have ever had. Rude in emails + impossible midterm and final. The quizzes she gives are NOTHING like the exams. Please take a different professor.

I’m currently taking her course and was expected to “skip” the midterm because of health issues explained to her. She said there is no extension or makeup allowed, instead I’m expected to take the final which would count for 80% of my grade and cover the midterm and final exam. never experienced this with a professor before.

Very tough Professor, made me hate economics. So much so that I changed my major. She should not be allowed to be teaching. Does not help you at all, exams are ridiculously though. Does not post PowerPoint because "it does not help", rather makes us watch 1 hour long video. Videos where you are on the verge to fall asleep. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took ECON 4001.01 asynchronously with Professor Light. I read the textbook and took notes, but didn't watch any of the lectures. The midterm average was around a 60%, but I personally found it straightforward. Would probably be a lot harder if it wasn't all multiple choice! Grade was determined by 10 quizzes, a midterm, and the final (50%).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: No friggin clue how in the world I got a B. Sooo hard! Other profs teach the same class and its fine. Her class is dreadful. She wants you to buy the textbook which doesn't help at all. She doesn't teach ANYTHING and is sinfully boring. I learned absolutely nothing because she just talks and talks and talks while the only grades are exams.

Throughout my time at OSU, never left a single review. But after her class, I felt like I owed an honest review. I have always been a 3.7/3.8 student and a LOVER of econ. Her class made me hate econ. Her class & exams are ridiculously tough so one advice: DON'T TAKE HER CLASS UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE, you & your GPA will regret it. Just like I am rn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor light was one of the rudest professors Ive ever had. Most of the class had failed the midterm and the final. Throughout the semester she would send emails with very derogatory comments to her students. She was not in any way motivating or welcoming to her students. This class made me second guess pursuing economics.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: why are all other professors for this course simple and she is terribly hard
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For accounting, econ 4001.01 is a requirement. I saw the class listed as online and was like "cool, least I don't gotta go to Columbus." But Light says: Nah bro, you go to Columbus to take the exams!". I took a quick look at all the practice exams and they are really hard. She says quizzes aren't gonna be on exams as well. Just horrible and pitiful

Exams were impossible. Avoid at all costs if you can. She tells you the exams will structurally look like the practice exams, which they did, but maybe one or two questions were carried over from previous practice exams, so be ready for curveballs on the exam. Impossible course to get an A in.

This class was by far the most difficult course I've taken at OSU. Prof. Light was extremely unhelpful and disrespectful to her students. Instead of offering help to struggling students, she  blamed them for doing poorly and not being prepared enough. Her entire class rides on a few grades. My only hope is that she will read this and reevaluate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dont take this class. She is an awful professor that builds her ego creating overly complicated lectures and tests. She belittles her students over email in a very unappealing manner. She also puts 80% of the grade into 25 MC and 7 short answer which means each wrong answer is a critical hit to the your grade.

So many people gave Audrey such a bad review but in all honesty, she's not that bad. It's true that her video lectures are boring and the tests are quite challenging, but she lays everything out clearly and if you do the problem sets and study Q's then you should be fine. Also, there is a curve!

By far the worst teacher and hardest class I've taken at OSU. Online lectures are tediously boring with her monotone voice. Expects you to memorize 7 chapters of detailed information for exams. No formula sheet on exams. Grades unnecessarily hard on the open-ended questions on exams. Should not be teaching at a respected university.

Out of everything she could have done to make an economics class more relevant to her students, she chose to record herself in the banalest and uninterested monotone. You see this attitude when you talk to her and in her exams too. Poorly structured and lack of instructions. If you're not interested, do us both a favor and don't teach.

This is a very difficult class. The midterm was different from the problem sets and study questions we were given. When sending the email about the  midterm grades, she made it apparent that she will not be giving a curve at all. I would not recommend taking this class at all.

Audrey has to be the absolute worst economics professor I have ever had. Never have I encountered a professor so ridged and difficult. The midterm mean score pathetically hovered around a D. When posting grades, she clearly stated that no curve was to be allocated and to just drop the course if you did poorly. Simply put, this class is ridiculous.
Very very tough class, exam is nothing like the practice problems or weekly quizzes!!! Do not recommend taking her course, avoid her at all costs

She is the worst professor I have ever seen. Lectures are stupid and long but has no connection with exams. The average for the first midterm was only 68%. If you are going to take Econ 4001 don't choose her!!!!
Just awful. Won't take hers if I could choose again. Worst decision ever.

Have to say this class will give me the one and only B that I will ever get and drag down my GPA. I can't see why it is not because of the teacher or the way she teaches. Extremely LONG online lectures that dull you to death, not helpful at all practice problems and negative attitudes, I am just speechless regarding this class.

Awful. Worst professor I've ever had. Most people failed the first midterm. When asked for extra practice problems she said she didn't have time to upload any. Extremely belittling toward her students. Refuses to do anything to help. Do not take. She does not deserve to be a professor at this university.
awful

Class starts slowly, but gets better as it goes. She is genuinely interested and has no problem with debate during the lesson. No essays, two midterms, 6 problem sets of moderate difficulty.  You will learn econ, and it could be a lot worse!

A: the class was really interesting. B: this professor was very caring and took the time to respond with thoughtful comments on multiple assignments of mine even thought it was an online course. She seems very excited to engage with students and hear their thoughts. Even though I was unable to attend, she also invited students to meet once.

Sierra was fantastic. I appreciate that she doesn't grade on facts, she mostly asks for out opinion. This class had weekly modules consisting of a show or a few readings, and occasionally a Google Form with questions about the reading, or more often a discussion post about our thoughts. This was my easiest class all semester and was stress-free.

I really liked Professor Austin. The course material was super interesting and while the class formatting was a little hard to get used to at first (no lectures, a lot of independent work) I think it was overall a great course. It is really easy to get a good grade if you just participate. I feel like I learned a lot and had fun doing it.

This professor is one of my favorites. I am taking my fourth class with her and every time she has been great. She is very pleasant and will work with deadlines. If you don't understand some thing just ask and she will explain clearly of what she is looking for. Her assignments were fun yet challenging. She is very warm and cares about her student

This class reworked my feminism for the better. She is passionate and willing to talk outside of the course even though it's online. If you do the work and comprehend it, easy A and she works w/ you on deadlines. First few weeks are reading heavy so you have a good fundamental grasp of the issues, but past week 4 or 5 the work load wayy gets easier
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Sierra Austin is a PhD candidate whose online Black Women Writers class couldnt have been more irritating. Long story short, dont enroll in one of her online classes. She: provides no feedback as to what is an adequate analysis; isnt a consistent or standardized grader; is kinda petty; and literally doesn't teach. You get links to read & thats it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This is the best professor I have ever had at Ohio State, I had such a difficult time during the semester with my attendance due to health issues, He went above and beyond to help me and make me feel included in the class and made sure to check on me often he helped me get in contact with slds and since then I have been much better in my classes.

Clint was one of the best professors i've had. I love how he talks so much about his background and how he was as a person. Super funny and supper passionate. Overall a great dude and I would take another one of his classes if I could.
Awai-Jennings was the best professor I've had in my career at OSU, HIGHLY recommend for any courses!
A great instructor, and really helped me with my disability accommodations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Clint is absolutely amazing! He was always super understanding in any circumstances you communicated and was very flexible when you needed it. As long as you show up to class and try to participate a little, participation is easy, and the homework and final paper was very straightforward, and he gave great feedback for both.

Clint is hands down the best instructor I've ever had. He's so passionate about the material and explains it in an easily comprehendible way. A genuinely kind and likeable person AND he shares great Linguistics memes! The class was very interesting and easy but if you do struggle, he is more than willing to help. Highly recommend!!

Clint is an amazing professor who brings you food from Hawaii and is very relaxed. He is so nice and would do anything to help you. If you can you should take this professor in any course that he teaches!

This guy is the best professor I have ever had. Accessible before, during, and after class, I cannot recommend him enough. He knows his stuff and he makes sure you do, too. He connects everything to his Hawaiian heritage and everyone was there for it. He would bring in food and demonstrations. I would take every class he taught if I could

He is easily one of the best professors I have ever had. He goes above and beyond to make sure that you understand the material. He encourages the class to email him with questions and responds right away. He has such a warm and caring personality and he creates a great environment that makes you look forward to his class. Also a great cook!

Clint is one of my favorite professors I've had. His class is super engaging and personable, and he genuinely wants every person in the class to succeed. He made the course content interesting and also shared some great linguistics memes and Hawaii language and culture facts. If you can take a class with him, DO IT

Clint is one of the most genuine professors that I've ever had. He's hilarious, always willing to help students, and knows the material very well. He is very engaging and makes the material fun and easy. This is the only class to which I look forward everyday.

Awai is one of the most authentic and empathetic instructors I've ever had! He is genuinely excited to share his love for historical linguistics. It's hard NOT to like this class. He created a positive environment, never condescended us, and folded in elements of his Hawaiian background when it was appropriate.

He really cares about whether you understand the material and is always willing to meet outside of class and office hours. He makes lectures as enjoyable as possible, knowing full well that this class isn't the most riveting. Show up, ask questions, stay after if you're still confused, and you'll pass with flying colors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Clint is awesome! He really cares about his students and wants you to do well in the class, so he makes himself readily available through email and office hours. The class is organized really well and the expectations are clear. He is from Hawaii so you learn a lot of cool authentic stuff, and he makes yummy treats to eat on exam review days :)

Very interesting material and lectures. Discussion in class is super fun. He has a unique sense of humor.  And he's from Hawaii so he has tons of examples in Hawaiian pidgin language. Overall highly recommended!
This professor is so helpful. Take her class. You won't reared it!
Enjoyed her class very much. Wonderful character. Full of Light.

This teacher is very kind, helpful, and goes over and beyond to help her students. She does ask you to online assignments, but they are for your own good in the end. She goes not only into the language, but also the culture and the different norms in arab countries. Just be willing to put in the work, and she helps you to talk arabic in class,

The professor is nice and very willing to help you with anything. As this is a language get ready to use your text book a lot and also do the homework. Participation is very important in this class. If you do your assignments and show up to class you'll be fine.

The professor is really nice and willing to work with you to help you understand the material. It is important that you study a little every day. The teacher assigns homework  most days and attending lecture is crucial.

The teacher is a great instructor and I recommend this class from this instructor. As long as you ask questions and do your work you'll be fine. She is the best for learning Arabic. She is very knowledgeable on all subject matter.

My personal experience with Dr. Elnour is that she is a nice person. For non natives, her teaching style can be very confusing, but as long as you ask questions and do your work you'll be fine. She is a generous grader, but expects you to do work. The grading criterea does not seem to be clearly defined, and sometimes the class seems unorganized.

I struggled to keep up with her teaching style.  It seems like she bases her class of off the performance of native speakers - who are taking the class for a GPA boost.  Poorly paced class.  Nice person, frustrating teacher.  Teach yourself through the book if you want to succeed.  310 do not recommend.

Absolutely the worst professor I've ever taken. I've never reviewed a teacher before because I've never felt the need. This man explains NOTHING. He simply reads from a slide word for word that doesn't even describe how to do anything he's asking you to learn. He expects you to come to class having all ready known everything he's trying to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures are kind of boring but hes still a great teacher. He wants everyone to do well and gives everyone the opportunity to do well. If you show up, make note of the important points, do the assignments, and study a bit for the exams, youll do well.

Axel is a nice gentleman but he is german and it is hard to understand what he is lecturing about. His exams are multiple choice but somewhat confusing in what he is asking. In class and online assignments each week are necessary for you to pass but they are extremely simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 3331 is the most boring class I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Axel is hilarious, and his class is so easy. He gives In class assignments for attendance, and you only have class 2 days a week. You have opportunity to earn extra credit, and he tells you exactly what will be on the exam. Study what he says, and you will get a 100. Do the work and it's an easy A. I would recommend taking any of his classes.

Dr. Westerwick is a clinical professor at OSU. He has strong German accent but he is very nice and helpful. He tells what will appear on exams every class so getting a good grade is not hard at all. Online assignments and in-class assignments require you to turn them in on time for credits.

Professor Axel is really knowledgeable in IT, Engineering, and Communication. He is really laid back and he explains the majority of the material well. He has a German accent but it doesn't get in the way and we laugh about it in class often. The exams are very straight forward and participation is about half of your grade.

Axel Westerwick is a good professor. He is enthusiastic, knowledgeable,  and has real world international business experience. He has a German accent but he speaks slowly and clearly. You do not have to go to class, but they are unannounced in-class assignments that make up a good portion of your grade. He is very kind and willing to help.

He's willing to help but he goes very fast during lectures and his explanations aren't clear at all. His notes barely help when looking back to try to understand and study. He's enthusiastic and motivated about the material.

He's bit hard to understand. You need to go to lecture and read the book if you want to do well on the test. In lecture, he tells you the topics from the notes that are going to be on the test. And then he gives out which parts of the book to read for the test. If you can take another professor, do it. Not bad but not great.

Axel is awesome. He's funny, charming, helpful, and has an intriguing German accent. He has real world examples, understands the nature of comm courses, and is very realistic in knowing that his class isn't the only one his students are taking. He gives in class assignments which is an easy way to get points. Take any class he offers!

I had Westerwick for 3554 and 4556. Lecture slides are posted online with blanks in them that you fill in during class, then he tells you which slides to know for the exam. Attend class for notes and random in class assignments and you'll pass with flying colors.

Dr. Westerwick is a great teacher. He brings real world experience, which helps much with learning the content. i felt i could really use that material later on. Some of the stuff wasn't all that easy, but he does great with explaining it.
Westerwick is an excellent professor I took him for 3 classes. If you go to class you will definitely get A's!

Everything you could ask for in a professor. All the other reviews are right-go to class and there's no way not to get an A. Classes can be boring but he is helpful/nice/funny. I have also taken 368/531/325 with him and all his classes are set up the same way. No textbook, ICAs, 2 hw assignments & 2 easy exams if you go to class & get the main pts

Axel is in one word fair. If you show up to class he gives you "the most important points" which are the slides to study for your exam. You study those you get at minimum a B. Then he has "In class assignments" this is nothing but your opinion on a topic that class that he gives you 15 minutes in class to do, it basically is attendance.

Axel is everything you could ask for in a professor: straight-forward, offers EC, not much hw and genuinely wants students to succeed. Notes are fill-ins in class. Go to class, review for exams and you'll be fine.  Also, hes fresh outta Germany and tells legit hilarious stories ab his encounters w American culture. Taking him again next quarter.
One of my favorite professors at OSU. I took comm656 and then 368 with him. Go to class for all of the ICAs. He tells you what you need to study, so the info load isn't too bad. take him!

GO TO CLASS. it will only benefit you. All i did was read other homework/or for fun during class and I still was able to complete the ICAs. Also he will tell you EXACTLY what is on the exam. JUST GO. its freaking easy.

Axel is a really nice guy, very helpful. He'll gladly email you information if you didn't catch everything on the slides [sometimes he goes through them kinda fast] GO TO CLASS. He tells you what to study for @ the end of lecture, and you dont wanna miss the ICAs... It's not a hard class... everything's laid out plainly. Just lots of info sometimes

I thought Axel did a great job of communicating a really boring subject. Comm Tech is required for a communications minor and is the only reason I took the course. Don't bother getting the book and make sure you go to class because at the end he goes over the important points i.e what is going to be on the exam. He is a very nice man.

the subject matter is pretty boring but he tries. shy and very quiet but friendly and really works hard to help students out. GO TO CLASS. at the end of every lecture he tells you questions that will be on the exam.

Boring. This class was awful. I don't think it was all the profs fault, the subject isn't that exciting, but he could have tried to make it more entertaining. His accent and volume made it difficult to hear what he was saying. You have to go to class or you might miss an in-class assignment. He seems like a nice guy, but his class is so boring.

Kind of boring but he tries.  He tells you almost exactly whats going to be on the exams if you show up to class  don't miss class there was only 109 pts in the class so if you miss one in class assignment you lose...

Axel was great. Class was boring most of the time, but showed clips from office space and some good do****entarys.  He's a nice guy, understanding, and always goes through at the end of class and tells you what notes to mark for the exam!

Great guy who really wants to help his students succeed in a hard course like chemistry. He really enjoys helping his students, even going beyond his assigned office hours to help prepare students for exams.

Best TA I've had! He really does take an interest in his students. He is there to help and gives his students 100% of his attention. He's also really cool to talk to and is a quality human being lolz.
chill bro. the burns are hawt!

Best TA I've ever had, not to mention a rad sense of humor. Would put meme's in his weekly emails. Cool dude I who I would totally hang outside of class with. He really cares about his students, and works the sideburns and beard like no ones business.

Avi is definitely the best in the WE program. He recognizes students who put forth effort, and those who consistently skip class and don't bother with the homework.  He gives warning at beginning of the semester, class assignments will take at least 8-9 hours at least to complete and he's not joking.  Amazing class and even better professor. A+++++
Don't waste time going to class. He develops equations entire time. Just find the equations in the notes and use them. Tests are hard but fair. Quizzes are hard and totally based on the hw.
