Nice teaching and easy to understand. 5-6 hws, 3-5 online quizes and 2 midterm + 1 final. Avarage final grade was B. he gives E, if you deserve. not like many other WE faculty, he is the most fair grader. if you are looking for an easy A, this class is not for you. ANSYS and MathCad is required. You will do 1D-2D heat equations, some FEA and FEM.
She speaks very clearly and you'll have no trouble understanding her. She knows what she's doing and her lectures are meticulously planned. Very knowledgeable in the subject and she's very helpful.

Extremely well prepared and helpful. Notes were clear and was always ready to answer questions.  Goes over a lot of example problems which is good for this class. Her review sessions are always helpful!

She speaks very clearly and her notes are very well organized. She doesn't do a lot of practice problems in class. She was a harsh grader, however she does give partial credit on tests. She is also very helpful after class and in her office hours. You should attend her office hours if you can. Overall good teacher
Awesome. Really good at explaining things, thank god, as the TA's really don't. Oh, and she's American, which is also pretty nice for clarity reasons!
Nice teacher!
talking clearly, extremely helpful teacher
understandable

She might as well have taught Math 132 because everything I learned, I learned in recitation. Unlike many professors which go into too much detail about nothing, she made everything so much easier than it really was. She also posted a lot of useful things on her website. She is by far the best instructor I have ever had.

Isabel was very helpful. She made me understand everything and even gave the class helpful tips, like what to remember for tests and such. She even brought us candy for the final. Really cares about her students.

Excellent TA and willing to help. I wish she was with a better professor for one, and that she didn't collect homework though I suppose I understand why she did. Sometimes she moves a little fast for me to understand and since my professor did also it made it hard. However, she is a great TA and always uploaded notes, etc. to her website to help us

She is a very good TA and you could tell that she put a lot of work in through her OSU website, it is part of the reason I got a decent grade.  I would have have rather had her as my professor honestly...
she's the coolest... probably my favorite TA b/c our class is so fun...
not a very godd TA

She is absolutely AWESOME!  I had her as a TA and she was GREAT, so keep an eye out for her as a professor.  TAKE HER CLASS if you get the chance... you won't regret it--seriously (especially if you're having trouble)
Good teacher....she knows her stuff and is one of the better TA's I have had so far.
Isabel is very helpful and she teaches math in a way that easily understood
Very helpful. Teaches what's on the tests. Good TA.
great teacher if you can get her do it

The 80min lectures 3 days a week (session 1) were very draining but Dr. Hereid usually explained concepts well and the course is pretty average difficulty. The formula sheet he gave for the final exam was so clutch half of it was basically plug and chug. Seems passionate about his research which was cool

Not a great lecturer, but the lectures represented homeworks and the exam very well. Content is straightforward plug-and-chug for the most part. He gave the class a choice between in-person final and take-home final, we chose in-person. His formula sheet was very good and the exam was incredibly fair (but 50% of grade). A is attainable, I recommend

Professor Hereid is a good lecturer and a very fair grader. His homeworks, while long, are very helpful and really helped me learn more about the class. He did have a 50% exam to end off the class, but he made it fair and in line with the in class material. Overall a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were dry, but covered all the material on both the homeworks and the final. The homework wasn't too difficult for the most part, although some of them are a bit long. Although the final was 50% of the overall grade, it was somewhat easy and graded fairly. Overall, decent professor

Professor Hereid taught the class well even if the lectures were occasionally difficult to follow. His homework, while long, helped you learn a lot if you did the work yourself. He understood that an exam worth 50% of the class grade should not be impossible and proctored a very fair exam that reflected class material. Good professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework and exams aren't extremely difficult; recitations are helpful. He mainly just reads the slides but they are very helpful to study and are easy to follow. Not the most entertaining lecturer, but still worth attending

Interesting guy, but not the best professor. He mostly read off of slides and was not very good at showing which formulas were part of the derivation or the final form. Exams were easy and open for a long time.

Seems like a nice guy and the research he does outside of class seems cool. This class in particular was not difficult besides some homework just took a while. The notes he posts are pretty good and that's pretty much what I went off of the entire course and did well. Exams were open for a whole day or two which was nice. He was an okay Prof.

Dr. Hereid was okay. His lectures were nothing spectacular, a bit boring, but he did communicate the material okay. He is a nice guy, just do the homework and communicate with him about issues and you'll be ok for 3751.

Midterms were not too difficult, but he had to make the final exam on the very last day of school, and in person while all midterms are online. His notes are terrible, a lot of terms are not explained, too lazy to make any equation sheet for us. You would have no clue what to do on the hws most of the time, u would have to go to TAs office hrs.

Bonnie is a very genuine professor who cares for her students. There is a lot of assignments but the due dates are not super strict, but keeping up with the assignments is ideal. She brings baked goods to every class and is always willing to answer questions.

Bonnie is great because and the entire purpose of this class is to boost your personal and career development. She knows what she is talking about and gives lots of good advice. You will also get an A as long as you put in the effort.

I love Bonnie, BUT. At first the class is fun. As you go through the semester things kind of become more and more unorganized. She gives assignments last minute and expects a fast turn around rate (even with finals week - we have an exam, a quiz, and have to give an oral set of reasons, doesnt sound bad, but theyre all difficult). shes unspecific
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVE Bonnie. She is amazing. She is hilarious, caring, and knows how to teach this class. You take trips to farms to see cows, and she brings snacks and homemade baked goods to every lecture. She also is very generous with grading, and with the extra credit she gives. As long as you show up, youll get an A

This is a lot of work for a 3 credit class but well worth it. Learning is hands on and in the field in addition to classroom. Opportunity to make many connections to the dairy industry to make contacts fore furture employment.

This review is for ECE 4021 instead of 5021 (because there is no option to select 4021):
Dr. Fayed is an EXCELLENT professor, you will learn a lot, not only IC knowledge, but also about the industry.
However, this class is extremely challenging. Unless you have a strong interest in IC and want to make it your career, do NOT take it.

Amazing lecturer and teacher. Loves to teach the subject, and expects a ton from students. I learned a ton, but had to put a lot of effort in. Grades aren't as forgiving as the rest of the ECE department. You will have to do near the top of the class in every assignment to do well.

He was born to teach analog. He really cares about teaching and his lectures are amazing-- you will learn so much. That being said, he is a very harsh grader. Exam and quiz averages are regularly less than 30%. The final project takes about 40 hours per person in the group. He curves somewhat harshly, especially for graduate students.

Dr. Fayed is a great professor to learn from. Tough tests, tricky quizzes, and challenging final project. However, he has worked for TI for several yrs so his knowledge is very solid and he is very helpful if you reach out. He is also kinda generous in terms of grading also. Wish he was my older brother due to his dedication and personalities!

If you are a graduate student and you care about GPA, DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. You will get a grade less than you expected. The lectures are great, and you learn a lot. But the grading is unfair for graduate students. Try to attend lectures instead of registering with credits unless you do not care about GPA. The exam and quizzes are always tricky
He is a great guy, knows a lot of real world stuff and gives good advice. Lectures were usually extended +20m, quizzes and exams are some of the hardest I have had at OSU. Get ready to regret life.
A solid, big-hearted and inspirational professor who wants his students to excel in the class. Take his class if you want to focus on electronics and circuits stuffs, and you won't feel disappointed!

She did a really good job making the lackluster content of the slides easy to manage. The class ends with everybody giving a presentation and writing an 8-page paper, but she made it easy to tailor those projects to cater to our interests which made the whole process way more enjoyable.

Seems like a difficult class at first, but she explains it very well. Although I asked many questions about the assignment, she responded with patience. She is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the subject. Additionally, she made use of real life examples based on her political science background which was very interesting.

Very nice and helpful. She is not an easy grader but papers and projects are easy to understand. All in all, she is an easy and helpful professor. As an international student, I receive too much support which I have not received in other classes.

She is a nice lady but EXTREMELY tough grader. She is a grad student so you would think she would understand the struggle. But no. You do A LOT of papers, and still have two midterms. She's very particular about what she wants and to get an A you have to learn the way she likes things (papers, projects), and do it that way.

I really don't understand the hate for Ayaz. This obviously isn't the most fun class, but it isn't hard either. Attendance is mandatory, but you pay to go to school here so just show up. He is happy to help with questions but can be a little hard to reach at times. The final isn't bad, there are no "right" answers so just back up your responses.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Hyder, along with the other head professor for this class, did not support students well throughout the semester. The class felt very disorganized. He was also not very accessible through e-mail or through direct messaging through the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Do not take public health data analytics. It was unclear and unorganized, though it was made sure that attendance was taken every class. They assume everyone who takes this class knows R and has the background knowledge of a math major. Those who do not meet those criteria will struggle immensely, and you will not get help when you ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are not enough characters to complain about how horrible this class was. Attendance every day, which forced you to sit through boring lectures when the slides are posted online anyways. Group projects are assigned by Dr. Hyder, and are groups of 10-11 people, which was impossible to coordinate. Grading is hard and instructions are vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Hyder cares a lot about environmental health and it shows in lectures. Speaking of lectures, they are boring but you need to go for attendance. Quizzes are online and pretty easy but you better hope your group is responsive because mine sucked and I had to do a lot of the work for those four projects
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: You can tell he is a caring and nice person, but this is one of the most unorganized courses I have taken. The lecture slides either have overwhelming amounts of information or barely anything other than key terms. Unclear criteria for the assignments and paper as well. Pretty easy to pass but not a great time.

Lecture and attendance are important because the slides seem super random. Although if you miss classes its not a big deal, you just wont get points. Didnt feel like I learned anything. Exam was easy but didnt feel it pertained to much of what we learned
Horrible, very unorganized, tough grader, he's friendly, but I really wouldn't recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It is evident that Dr. Hyder has a really good heart and is very knowledgeable on the subject of environmental health, but he doesn't do a great job translating this knowledge in an understandable manner to his students. Don't let this scare you, because it's not hard to do well in the class, but beware that you probably wont learn much from him.

Just Ridiculous, he makes his quizzes and tests based on things that aren't even discussed in the slides or lecture (???????). Everything about him and his class is so unorganized. I don't even know how or why OSU hired him. Just b/c someone has a Ph.D.. it doesn't mean they will be a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not a hard class but insanely boring and unorganized.
He is not that great of a professor, but also not that bad of a professor, but his class is very easy if you attend and take notes, so do that and you're set.

He has gotten SO much better this first semester at Ohio State. Don't pay attention to his past reviews. No tests and no textbook. All quizzes are online and straightforward for the most part. The papers can be annoying but he will help you through them. Not hard to get an A, just attend class on TopHat days aka Fridays.

I'm going to be more lenient because I was in the first class he ever taught. He clearly knows a lot about the subject, but struggles to deliver lectures (at the end he got better about involving us. My biggest complaint is that he was not very responsive to family emergencies/has very strict due dates. He also didn't ever have office hours.

Wouldn't recommend taking this class with him. His lectures are boring and unclear. The papers are a large part of your grade, but are graded very arbitrarily. He's condescending  and rude when spoken to in person. Makes it clear he doesn't want students to succeed. I learned nothing from this class and am avoiding any future classes taught by him.

Class grade is based off of online quizzes over lecture material and two papers. The papers are very easy and graded generously, however the quizzes often included details from lecture that were barely mentioned making it difficult. He was extremely boring but the guest lecturers were much more interesting and provided more straight forward content
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Content has potential to be very interesting, but the lectures are very boring. About 1/4 of the class shows up to lecture each time. Quizzes often didn't make sense at all, but papers were graded generously.
This is his first semester teaching here. He is not as bad as the previous review. Need to take notes, slides are posted online but notes are needed to get decent grades on quizzes. No tests!

Failed quizzes from lectures given by him, and a's on those given by guest lecturers. The lectures make little sense and are supplemented by power points that are little help. Guest lecturers make up probably a little less than half of the classes. No tests, only quizzes and two papers.

Zeynep is a great professor and is extremely knowledgable, kind, and respected. The class though, is not recommended for anyone who has pride in America. It had an anti-American sentiment and most assigned texts are biased towards how America is viewed. This is not Zeynep's fault, but should be warned before taking the class!

Zeynep was truly one of the best professors I've had thus far at this university. Not only did she provide lessons that showed how much thought and time she put into creating it, but she established a constructive environment that fostered really strong discussion.

I took this course for a GE credit and to balance out my challenging, upper division, courses for my major. Unfortunately, I made a huge mistake. This course was alot of reading for a GE 2000 level course. She would assign a new book every week. She was a strict grader took pts off for things that were not in her instructions/prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I absolutely adored having her as a teacher. She is clearly passionate about what she teaches, which makes the class that much more interesting. We read a total of 6 novels for her class, and each one was interesting and thought-provoking. You're graded on participation and in-class discussion, and she encourages you to think for  yourself.

Professor Aydogdu has been one for my favorite college professors thus far. She clearly lays out what the class will be like and what you need to do to get an A, which turns out to be not much. The class is really interesting and actually changed my perspective on how I view the world. I'm so glad I took this class and  I recommend it to everyone!
Her lectures were really interesting and easy to understand, I really like her as a teacher

She is seriously AMAZING. She gives you all of the information that you need during her lectures and offers extra credit assignments. Attendance is mandatory and as long as you take some notes, you will definitely get an A. Her powerpoints don't give the information so you have to go to class. But she is so nice and a great teacher!
Great instructor and very easy to get an A

She's a very nice and fun teacher. Majority of her tests come from her lectures. She likes to listen to your comments and questions.As long as you go to class and take a few notes then you'll pass. You will need to read the book sometimes. She posts Powerpoint notes online and those are very helpful. Easy class.
awful. tests were easy. papers were alright. lectures were pointless. attendance was mandatory tho.... just awful
Amazing teacher. Exams were so easy as long as you go to class and listen. I didnt read at all and got an A in the class. Ms Bayram is very interesting and fun lady.
Attendance is mandatory, participation encouraged but overall a great professor and knows all the material
Best woman ever!!! Ms. Bayram helps you with everything and allows you to draw your own conclusions. Best class and Best prof at OSU by far.

Best professor I've ever had! She makes class interesting, and honestly cares what her students have to say. TONS of interesting discussion, so if you get involved it's never boring. Exam was easy, just as long as you go to class and pay attention. She's a genius!!
This was an easy class but attendance is mandatory and she'll make it awkward if no one participates. If you do participate you'll be on her good side for sure.

Wonderful class! She is extremely intelligent, but she explains everything until class understands. Notecard allowed for exams, no surprises on exams. One of the best professors I've had, if not the best! Awesome discussions during class, encourages you to think for yourself. If you get the chance, DEFINITELY take a course with her :)

The first thing I have to say about Ms (hopefully still Ms) Bayram is that she is HOT!! She has a smile that is so tantalizing. As far as the class, it was pretty easy. She allowed us to use a notecard for our tests so hopefully you can write really really small. I walked away with a B but I could've gotten an A. I just got lazy.
Ayoola is a great teacher and scholar. A compassionate man. He respects his students.
I am yet to see any Professor that know his stuff like this. I have no complaint or regrets. Only loafers find his class tough.

The person who said Ayoola was rude only said that because HE PRINTED OUT THE PPT and even told us not to write. But the class was an easy A. Both midterm (yes, only one) and final are essays & he gives them to us beforehand. Doesn't grade at all and leaves TAs to handle grades. One pop quiz, but he hinted at it. One of the funniest profs ever.
Dr. Ayoola rude? Not at all. But he could be very hard on students who do not have a clue why and for what they are in the university. He did not accomodate loafers and lazy students.

Dr. Ayoola is RUDE. There were many times when I asked him to return to the page before for notes, and we would argue in front of the class because he didn't want to. Although he was funny, he grew boring as the quarter went by. He tries to make simple assignments more difficult. but he is easy. He isn't useful, the TA's did all of the work.
Professor Ayoola is cool and quiet.He could be funny and jovial at times, and firm and stern on occasions.

Ayoola is a very good teacher. The last comment is from a lazy, intolerant, opinionated,and arrogant graduating student who did not want to take notes in class; wants an automatic A grade without working for it. He wants to be spoon-fed all the time. Lazy you braggart.

You will do nothing but scribble off his slides as fast as you can.  He talks during this and expects you to take notes on what he says (which is often unclear) during this.  Boring class.  TA's have too much control of grading.  Gave a 50 point POP (!) comprehensive midterm.  I'm an honors student, and would advise to AVOID AT ALL COSTS
Ayoola is a very good teacher. He is a funny man, who is genuinely interested in the well-being of his students.

Dr Ayoola is cool. I like professors from different countries. You might have a hard time with his accent but it's defintitely doable. I took both 121 and 122 and got an A in both. My advice is to take notes from his slides BUT ALSO note down how he elaborates on each slide. This is helpful because you take essay tests and the more info the better.

Rather mundane, though there are far worse options for Intermediate micro. Study guides are pretty close to the actual exams, homework is graded on completion. Lectures aren't all that helpful but as long as you do the practice exams and the homework it's doable.

He knows his stuff. Smart professor that will teach. You will fail the class if you do not attend lecture. You have to. You HAVE to take good notes. These notes are what will help you with the hw and exam (the entire class grade). I usually rely on book to teach myself for other classes,can't with this one. Class notes are only way to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Youll fail if you dont attend lectures, write everything he says down. Tests are pretty similar to homework questions and office hours are extremely helpful if you need help
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty good lectures and you need to show up every class period because he does not post any form of notes on carmen. 80% of your grade are exams so there is a small room for error. As long as you show up and are actively trying to learn the material you should get an A. I recommend him! Has an accent but easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yaron really is a good guy a little hard to understand sometimes as he goes into detail on some things that we don't end up using. Skipping Lecture is not an option as you will only be able to answer the HW if you have the notes and have a grasp on the content covered. One thing I wish he did was cover Exam/HW type problems instead of theoretical
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 6 homeworks (drops the lowest), and 3 exams (drops the lowest, can skip the final!). He gives pretty great lectures and explains concepts super well. Really enjoyed learning from him. Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It is a little hard to understand him, but go to class! Taking notes on what he writes on the board is imperative to succeeding. It will help with the HW, as well as the exams. Redo the HW and the exam practice problems to study. He drops the lowest exam as well as curves a little bit at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Homework and exam questions are more complicated than what is covered in lecture. Drops the lowest of three exams. Tests are only about 20 questions long so little margin for error. Large curve, my 81 was a B+. Requires strong math skills. He is a decent lecturer but provides few practice questions to work with. Prepare to learn independently.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible professor and horrible class. 3 exams, 6 homeworks. He drops the lowest exam. His lectures are almost pointless because he goes on and on about material that seems easy but exams/homeworks are much harder to understand. Good luck trying to get help. He is not willing to take time. This class is designed for a math whiz. Heavy curve at end!

This is a difficult class but I though Yaron taught it very well. You don't need the textbook as long as you attend class and take notes. If you take notes during class, the homework shouldn't be a problem. Homework is mostly (but not completely) a completion grade. He allows a full page (front and back) on exams and drops the lowest of 3 midterms

I thought he actually taught this class pretty clearly.  If you did the homework, you would get full credit for it regardless if you did it wrong.  The only real negative I have for him is that the tests were all multiple choice, and there were usually only 13-17 questions per test.  So not much room for error!

When people ask questions in class the way he responds is condescending sometimes or he replies in a way that can make students feel dumb. He skips important steps when explaining how to solve things too. I think 4001.01 shouldn't even be a course because you can't fully understand intermediate micro with out understanding the Calc behind it.

Yaron is a great professor who teaches the content well. He allows you to prepare one sheet of notes for each exam and there is a slight curve at the end, so take good notes and this class should be pretty easy.

Nice guy and a capable teacher, this class covers a lot of material so go to office hours if you aren't a math whiz. He is very helpful there. Two exam structure was stressful, as the final was half of the grade, though he decided to curve the grade. I'd recommend him.

I took this class because I was interested in learning more about micro theory and how different markets worked. Yaron explained things in great detail and he definitely knows his stuff. As long as you try hard to understand everything you'll do fine. And don't get behind in this class because it covers a lot of material fairly quick.

Extremely unprofessional and disrespectful. I don't believe I took anything out of her class. I did not receive thorough feedback on any assignments and when I regularly sought assistance I was repeatedly told that she prefers ambiguity. Expectations were never clear and she refuses to listen to anything you have to say that she disagrees with.

Dr. Manouchehri is overall a great professor. She provides extensive feedback on assignments and is very willing to work with students on her assignments. Her expectations aren't very clear and she has difficulty organizing the assignments for each week. It's clear that she cares about her students and is passionate about education.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Terrible instructor.

Indeed lots of work. Do not take her class if your goal is to reach the minimal requirement of graduation. A good professor who cares about how much you learn instead of how easy it is for you to pass.
Horrible person.  She has quite a high opinion of herself and let me tell you, it is not deserved.  Avoid at all cost!!

u think he's decent until you have someone else like nagib and u realize he had absolutely no structure to his lectures and practically no organization. u definitely need to use the textbook so u know ever mech and reagent u need to know for each test

Made it very clea what was on the exams, dropped one quiz and one exam. Liked his style of teaching with writing on a chalkboard, made it so that you could keep up with taking notes in class. He broke down hard concepts very well. Wish I could take him for ochem 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Because Badjic's exams are much easier than other orgo professors, I didn't go to 75% of lectures and used Youtube videos instead. The lectures were fine, but didn't get into solving exam-like questions, and lecture notes weren't posted on Canvas.

He's lowkey an aura farmer, and it made me more interesting in attending, but he explained concepts pretty simply, and the class was a bit hard becasue there wasn't much to grade with, be sure to pay attention though because its real easy to get behind
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He explains concepts in a v simple way that makes a great building block for future hard material. Test/quiz content is directly from the single practice sets he gives so you are set up to get a great grade if you do those until you really understand them. I honestly miss his teaching style and would take him for ochem 2 if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Badjic is a very good professor for 2510.  The lecture and resources provided correspond almost directly to what is on the exams.  Doesn't prepare the best for 2520 though.

Overall good professor but gives few resources so be prepared to look for others and study a lot. Weekly quizzes are easy but need to study. Midterms are the only main grades, curve is pretty good at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I very much enjoyed Badjic! Out of all of the ochem professors at OSU, he provides 3 midterms, and you can drop your lowest grade. All of the other ochem professor's at OSU only give out 2 midterms and no drops. His quizzes are similiar to his practice sheets. His TA's are very helpful and nice. Personality wise, Badjic is a blunt and chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His chalkboard style forces you to pay good attention. He does not cover functional groups which are needed for ochem II. He does not provide enough of his own practice problems or provide clear indication of what topics will be on each weekly quiz. The only reason I took him was because he is easier than Baldwin.

He was the worst. His answer keys always had mistakes, and he didn't cover the concepts needed for OCHEM II. He constantly told us to “read the textbook” instead of explaining. His sloppy chalk notes, one-color writing, and contradictory statements made everything even more confusing.
Doesnt post a lot of resources and is really test heavy

Dr. Badjic is a really good ochem 1 prof. He tells u only what u need to know and makes topics very easy to understand. no homework-only exams but u can drop 1. if u like chalkboard style and are okay with reading the textbook/practicing on ur own, you should like his class. he's funny too so it helps me pay attention

I really enjoyed Dr. Badjic. I love his lecture style, which involves writing on the chalkboard. It allowed me to follow easily since we were both writing things down at the same time. It wasn't like Baldwin, where she goes insanely fast. I really enjoyed Badjic.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst professor ive had yet dont listen to the other reviews. exams arent the worst if you put in a lot of work but there are barely any resources and the ones you do get are given last minute and always have mistakes. the tas are unhelpful bc he doesnt care or keep them in line. such a frustrating class and the curve was pretty small.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally loved having Badjic. His lecture style is very different because he only uses the chalk board but I liked it since it made me pay more attention during lecture. I think the tests are pretty difficult but completely fair, if you study you'll do great. I do recommend his office hours he seems scary but is actually nice and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Personally, I was not a fan of Dr. Badjic's teaching style. He simply writes on the chalkboard each lecture and provides 1 problem set per week.I felt like he did not provide enough explanation and practice material, making the exams very difficult. I would rather take a professor with harder exams that provides all the materials needed to succeed.
Dr. Badjic was amazing! He is good at explaining such hard material.

If you are taking ochem 1, take badjic. He is a messy teacher, he makes a lot of mistakes in lecture and the keys to problem sets are frequently incorrect and given last minute, however he has extremely fair exams with a drop on one midterm and one quiz and he teaches right from the textbook, giving you nothing from left field on the exams.

I think he is your best option for ochem 1 professors. Your grade is only made up of exams and quizzes so be mindful about that. His exams are very fair in my opinion and ending with a good grade in this class is doable. Go to every lecture, stay on top of problem sets, quizzes, etc and you will do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was a bit worried when his method of teaching was the old shcool chalkboard, but if you pay enough attention then you'll pick up. Prioritize doing the problem sets as soon as possible, I believe they are the number one thing that will help you in this course. For the exams, the problem sets work better than the practice exams.

Dr. Badjic does a great job at teaching such a hard topic. I was hesitant when I found out that he teaches on a chalkboard, but it forced me to pay attention and copy notes. He explains things in a clear-cut way. The only points are tests and quizzes, but you get one drop on each. My only complaint is my TA. Avoid Chris.

Very good professor. Some occasional mistakes in lecture but he explains things very clearly. He is very clear about what you need to know for exams. The material isn't too bad if you study, but the whole course is only graded on exams and quizzes- but there are no curveballs. They only encompass what he went over in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He looks serious but actually very nice. The course is difficult though.

Lectures were so disorganized and hard to follow, he just scribbles on the chalkboard. There was a heavy curve (My 60.22% became a C+), but the only pints in the class are from tests and quizzes. He seems like a nice enough guy, but his teaching style is not conducive to learning organic chemistry
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For teaching a very hard topic, he did pretty good. Sometimes hard to understand but not awful. Used the chalkboard religiously. Recorded lectures. No posted notes/slides. Has practice exams and questions but personally didn't find them very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While he may seem like a Soviet operative infiltrating the OSU Chemistry department, he actually is not as scary as he looks. Compared to other Ochem classes, he has by far the least homework (none). He is a nice guy, but there are virtually zero practice problems beside of practice exams. He also did not tell us what the cutoffs were for grades.
The best ochem professor. Very clear explanations, only tests what is covered in lecture.

90% of the grade relies on midterms and final but he is very clear about the material on each. Only downside is he spent a little too much time going over the easier stuff instead of on mechanisms. He was a funny lecturer and I really enjoyed his teaching style (chalkboard). I would choose to take him for ochen 2 if he taught it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bajic was a good lecturer, he very much focuses on the basics of organic chemistry and doesn't expect you to know information that he doesn't cover in class. His problems sets were useful and tests weren't super difficult if you studied the material in depth. I highly recommend reading organic chemistry as a second language for this class.

He teaches the basics of organic chemistry and only tests the basics. Pretty funny guy. He does make mistakes here and there, but there will be that one guy in class to catch him. Simple to understand. Read the textbook. Again exams are straightforward, tests what is taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: very good professor that explains all ideas needed for class so we can easily understand and for the exams. only one quiz per week and 3 finals where one gets dropped so make sure to study and u will do perfectly fine. made mistakes here and there on practices but overall great professor that i wish i could have for ochem2. very likable and funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The points were made up of 3 midterms (lowest gets dropped), quizzes each recitation, and a final so not a lot of wiggle room. In comparison to other sections, the tests were easier but his lectures I felt were not focused so the exams were still hard. Didn't show up to the final and overall I didn't feel like he cared. Made lots of mistakes.

Dr. Badjic is a decent guy who puts little effort into teaching his class. He makes frequent mistakes in lecture and on practice answer keys. He doesn't quite explain overviews of concepts (or mistakes) well enough. His tests are fair if you study well. He doesn't care what goes on in recitations, lab, or even show up for his own tests and final.

Dr. Badjic was an amazing professor. O chem is a hard subject and requires a lot of outside work. Attendance might not be required but it is extremely beneficial if you show up. He only teaches you what is important and doesn't focus on anything that would not be on the exams. Overall amazing professor and person in general
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Plan on being at every lecture. If you fall behind, there is NO catching up. 90% of the grade is based off of 3 midterms (lowest gets dropped) and the final. Lectures are extremely information dense; however, he is genuinely a great lecturer. Would highly recommend using Organic Chemistry as a Second Language as supplemental textbook. 9.5/10 prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would advise anyone who does not have Organic Chemistry already mastered against taking this class. Frequent mistakes during lecture and in the answer keys for the homework. Talked very briefly about topics that were on midterms and quizzes. Lecture was disorganized and taught with a piece of chalk. Professor does not care about students.

This man skimmed over important details of many concepts, and was so unclear about what would be on exams. Lectures were an absolute bore and he expected us to memorize every bit of the textbook. Recitations were just time to take quizzes, with very little time actually reviewing anything. The worst college class Ive ever taken in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really smart guy but found his lectures to be confusing. Personally just did not like his teaching style (very old-fashioned with chalkboard). Content gets really tough near the end. First two exams are easy, but the third exam sucked (get one drop tho). Final is 40%

Im currently in his class, man does it get hard fast. Starts out pretty easy with a review of Gen Chem and basic stuff, then it gets to the point where he is writing down reactions and moving on to the next one before you finished adding to your notes, let alone even understood the mechanism. Likable guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sweet guy, badd prof. Course was disorganized, exams were so hard that the class average was ALWAYS an F (a 49% one time!) and he never responded to emails. Neither did his TA. The quizzes and exams often had content that was not in the lectures and there wasn't enough time to finish them. Probably the worst course I've ever taken tbh.

I was really struggling, especially at the beginning of the semester, but the final grades are curved. To do well in the course, read the textbook section before or immediately after lectures to help fully understand. DONT FALL BEHIND. If you stay on top of reading, do the practice problems at the end of each chapter and on canvas youll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The hardest teacher ive ever had. His tests made me want to kill myself. Really study for the first 2 tests, they are easier than the last 2. The quizzes are difficult too, read the book before lecture and dont be afraid to ask questions. i had a 47% before the curve after the final. Do your best. Go to tutoring if youre really having trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a really passionate guy who tries his best to make lecture interesting. O chem is hard in general but he has very fair exams that follow exactly what he teaches in class. O chem is hard but thats not his fault. No points outside of the exams and quizzes which is rough but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Badjic gives extremely fair exams and covers all important material in lecture. There are no graded assignments (only 1 optional worksheet per chapter) so you have to put in a lot of effort yourself by reading the book and doing book problems. He is extremely accessible outside of class if you need help and does want you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Overall a very interesting professor, he was clear about the material that would appear on exams and he was always available and helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Badjics class wasnt the hardest ochem class at OSU. We got 3 exams and dropped our lowest one and our lowest quiz. But the averages dropped after each exam. His final was pretty tough so be prepared for that. As a person, he seemed distant and intimidating. Even though he was funny in lecture, it was sometimes confusing. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Badjic was an okay guy. He has a fun sense of humor but didn't seem to care about teaching. He came in at the last minute and left the second the class ended. The class is difficult enough. He showed example after example but very rarely went into more detail. Thank god for the curve in this class or I would have definitely failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Badjic's lecture helps but isn't always necessary to show up for. The class follows the book. To succeed, a student should read the book, do the problems in the back of the book, and MOST IMPORTANTLY do the practice tests and materials several times over. These give students a chance to understand how to take the exam which is very important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable and good professor. He does not give out what to do in lecture directly, he always wants students to use the think for themselves and use the textbook as that's directly what he teaches out of. His tests can be difficult but they are fair to his material, would recommend for anyone who wants a very good but challenging professor.

Unbelievably difficult. If you do not understand chemistry and can't commit 40 hours a week to teach yourself then you will struggle with this professor. Every point in the class comes from quizzes and exams, no assigned homework, and his lectures are just him doing reactions with no explanation

Do not take this professor. I honestly would suggest putting this class off a semester if he is your only option. Badjic doesn't care about teaching at all, he walks in class 30 seconds before it starts and runs out the door when its over. Have had a sub 5 classes this semester already. badjic makes this already had class, next to impossible.

Make sure you go to class, there are no notes posted and he will not give them to you in office hours. Exams are super tough, you have to study at least a few days before. No homework but do the suggested problems. Badjic just doesn't care about teaching, he shows up to lecture and runs off, don't expect to ask questions after class.

Although I know he's probably not a bad guy, professor Badjic is not interested in teaching. He does not walk you through things. Just comes in a minute before lecture and starts scribbling on the board and when questions are asked he is almost demeaning. If you want to actually understand and learn ochem don't take this you just end up memorizing

Organization? Horrible, no real structure to course. Multiple lecturers, all had no idea where previous had left off! --Exams? Easy, basic-- Grading? Horid! Absolutely awful! Clear mistakes made on grading. Got 15 pts back on final after regrade.-- Beat average by at least 13%, got B- for class. Not Reccomended

He missed a ton of lectures. You get to drop one quiz and one exam which is nice, but that final will kill you. Averages were super low and sometimes partial credit isn't even given. A 60% is a C- but I might have to take the class again anyway.

Do not take this class. If it's required for your major, change majors. Badjic is super confusing so you teach yourself. He's gone for 50% of lectures and our subs never know what they're supposed to be teaching. I hated this class. The exam averages are ridiculously low. I seriously considered throwing myself off the McPh balcony after every exam.

I learned everything for this class from the book, lectures were useless and the grading of exams was terrible. The averages on exams were stupidly low. You're better off just attending a different lecture if you take this class.

This is the Ochem 2510 that you should take. He is very thorough. All his exam comes from the textbook end of chapter problems. Although they may become hard, they are doable. If you are a premed, you should take him. Great preparation for the MCAT

He's horrible. One of the worst professors I've had at OSU. His exams are easy, but his grading is horrid. He made some random undergrads grade our final exams, and they were graded so poorly, we had to go back and ask for points back. I got 15 points back... can you imagine?!

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Easily the worst professor I've ever had. His lectures are jumbles of reactions that you have to go home and teach yourself. His exams are difficult and the averages were always at least 10 points lower than every other class. He just seems like he does not care at all

He is good for some of the material and not so good for other parts. After the first midterm the material was much tougher and he could be confusing at times. You get to work in a group for quizzes, but if your group members are stupid you won't do too well on them. You will need to read the book and do lots of practice problems to do well.

Avoid taking this professor if possible. The lectures are not clear and the Midterm exams are difficult and unlike homework and quiz problems. The averages in this class are much lower than other sections.

You get to see the quizzes before you take them, but that makes it sound easier than it is.  He is very bad at teaching material.  You have to go to class already understanding it, and only then will his lectures mean anything.  His midterms are very hard.  I do not recommend this professor if you can help it.  There are much better ones available.
you think he will be easy but he is useful, unclear and wastes time. good scientist... bad teacher. makes little sense... ever

He is an awful professor, averages consistently lower than other sections of ochem.  Dropping a midterm does not really help that much, just makes the final worth even more because there are only two midterms that count.  He is really disorganized and unclear.

Group quizzes started off easy. My group did not understand concepts very well late semester. Midterm 1 easiest/Midterm 2 hardest. Study hard for the first one. His lectures were terrible... He can go really fast on hard concepts but waste time on easier ones. Read book, do the problem sets, and end of chapters questions.

His notes on the board are very hard to follow and he doesn't explain how he gets any of his answers. The quizzes are easy because you get to take them in groups but the exams are super hard and wordy.
The MTs are freaking HARD!!the average of MT2 is 44.85/100. If you are really good at organic chemistry, just take this class because you have a chance to drop a MT.

If you want an A in ochem, TAKE THIS CLASS. Don't get me wrong, of course it is hard. But the grading format and the way that Badjic creates exams makes it the easiest OSU organic class. If you are somewhat smart put in lots of time, you will get an A. The same CANNOT be said about other OSU profs. Also, he is pretty odd/funny/ cool

Badjic is an awesome professor. His tests are very fair and consistent with what you learn in class. The quizzes can be taken in groups, and your lowest midterm grade is dropped. Doesn't get much better than that in the OSU chem department
An adequate professor who was hard to understand in lecture and we had to cover two chapter in a matter of 4 days!!! Disorganized but you will learn a great deal. Exams are fair

I loved having Badjic for 251 he is definitely easier than the other professors (Callum and Mattson) but he still explains the information well. He is very nice and laid back.  Go to lecture and do the problem sets because that's where the exams come from.  You also get to take group quizzes and you get to drop a midterm.

He is one of the best professors I have had in the Chemistry department.  He goes over the essentials that you need for OChem. Take notes and do problem sets and do some practice from book if you are not sure. Exams are fair.
The best chemistry teacher. He is so calm and laid-back. He knows how to teach and is definitely not full of himself like some other professors.

I'm in his 251 class right now and I love the way he teaches. If you do the book problems and go to class there is no reason you shouldn't get at least a B in his class. Tests are fair, if not on the easier side compared to other professors like Callam. Let's you pick when your exams are which is a plus. Way better than gen chem!

He is the worst Chem professor I have had so far. In his 251 class he is unclear on the topics and is often unable to answer questions. When he does answer a question, the answer is usually incomprehensible.
Great guy and really knows how to teach chemistry. Go to lecture, take notes, and the exams will be easy (as easy as Orgo can be)

Before the Paul cronies attack...Badjic doesn't goof around in class and try to make you understand concepts with cute analogies...he gets it done.  In conjunction with the book, there is no reason to struggle in his class.  The tests aren't easy, but fair, and if you struggle, he's more than willing to help. If you don't like BS, I recommend.

If you're premed, take this guy!  When studying for the MCAT, the organic chemistry portion is really easy. I got a 14 in Bio partly because of Badjic.  Plus, it's pretty easy to get an A if you do his practice problems he posts online.

Its OChem, so its supposed to be hard. But if you had a good 251 teacher, his class is pretty easy. He was hard to follow during spectroscopy, but the rest of 252 wasn't bad. His tests are very conceptual, the averages are usually low in his class. He's helpful during office hours.

He's kind of a goofy guy which makes lectures light hearted and easy to sit through. The tests were easier than Callam (who I had for 251). Averages were in the 50s so if you had anything in the 80s you got an A. Just study and know the theory behind the mechanisms. If you did well in callam for 251, be prepared for an easier quarter!

I really didn't like him as a teacher.  He was missing for half of the quarter because his visa expired so we were taught by random chem profs.  The first midterm was really easy but so was the material. The second midterm was extremely hard. The group quizzes were okay but most of my group members just mooched answers off of me. Callam is better!

i am not that smart with a 3.3 GPA i pulled out an A in this class. Exams are really straight forward. Read the textbook take notes and understand concept and dont even do the problems coz his exam problems are easier than the book no trick ?s and his class is already curved 85% u are guaranteed A- and on top of that u will haf another 5% curve

took both 251+252. this guy is awesome but i would not recommend if you just want to memorize rxns and mechanisms. his exams always ask to explain why something happens. LITTLE TO NO SYNTHESIS PROBLEMS!!! i expect why people do bad is b/c they just try to memorize instead of understand WHY something happens. prof is not for everybody.

Awful professor. Teaches fairly simple material, then hammers students on tests. First midterm is ok, and then waits several weeks before giving the second one, which contains a huge amount of difficult material. Class averages were in the 30's. NOT RECOMMENDED!!!

started SUPER slow then started blazing through stuff. First midterm was easy but so is the material. Second midterm had a lot of material on it but wasn't too hard if you studied the book. His lectures are ok but I got an A just by doing all the problems in the book and studying it. lectures are super boring (no questions, just rambling.)

Goes ridiculously fast. Starts INSTANTLY after the bell rings. By the time ONE MINUTE has passed, he has one whole reaction on the board and is already half way done explaining it. Test averages are very low (22% on the first midterm). As far as the "group " quizzes go, seriously consider the previous person's advice.

Lectures were very fast paced, and nearly impossible to understand, I just wrote everything down and tried to make sense of it later.  Group quizzes are great if you're in a good group, otherwise you may as well take it alone.  Test averages were around a 50%.  Taught myself from the book and did decent thanks to a laughable curve.
Clear lecturer. Quizzes/midterm/final were straightfoward, no tricks.

Great guy. Had Callam for 251 and and this guy was much easier , however i feel like I learned a great deal from him.  His exams are fairly straight forward and no curve balls.  Also if you have any ochem intuition what so ever, you'll end up with an A for sure.  I did it. you can too!
Great teacher. Very easy to understand, very helpful and fair tests. AMAZING HAIR, seriously.

Best ochem teacher EVER.  Some say Chris Callam is the best, but that's definitely not true.  Badjic is equally as clear, if not more and gives group quizzes.  His exams are what you would expect, without any surprises.  In my opinion, he kicks Callam's ass.

He's awesome. Teaches the fundamentals and doesn't worry about the useless details. If you want to learn the basic concepts and have easier exams than other profs take Badjic. He teaches by doing examples of the types of problems that will be on the exams. Dude rocks the house down.

Graded on 2 exams, a plant collection, and weekly PackBack posts. Very straight forward class. Barker is very personable and funny. I enjoyed taking the class. There is an optional lab (HCS2205) that I suggest taking if you are an HCS or related major but otherwise it is not needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Barker's class is very relaxed and easygoing. However, his lectures are a bit difficult to pay attention to since you get a lot of materials that seem unrelated. The tests are kind of difficult but the labs are easy.

Great professor. The labs are super easy and the professor really wants the students to learn so he answers all the questions in depth and gives answers. He also really loves his job and is interesting to talk to. A little older so he talks kinda slow but he's a great person and teacher and cares. would take again.

Lecture's are very dry and not interesting. Attendance was not mandatory for lecture. Lab was lead by TA's and were fine, mandatory attendance for lab. If you took the midterm you didn't have to take the final. No one showed up after the midterm. Still an interesting class, professor cares about students and teaching. Just kind of boring

Dr Barker is willing to help you outside of class.  All of the notes are available online, but going to class helps one remember the material better.  He is very personable and likes to tell stories of his travels.

Dr. Barker's class, though often boring, was made a bit more interesting by his humor and occasional jokes. The class is a good general overview of agriculture, and Dr. Barker was always willing to answer questions and emails. All of his lecture slides (which he just reads in class) are posted online, so going to lecture is pretty much optional.
Be sure to do the practice tests, the actual exams are almost the same! He is a really great professor-- funny and respectable.
Dr. Barker is a great professor and has an easy class.
Dr. Barker is provides a lot for students but can sometimes go off on tangets. It is easy to zone out in class but the information is all on his webpage.

Dr. Barker is an awesome professor! He is really funny, but he does get his facts mixed up sometimes. He does not know that much about ornamental plants but he'll be more than happy to talk your ear off about forage crops. He reads off of his online pdfs so you don't really have to go to class.

Dr. Barker is an excellent instructor. He is extremely well organized, fantastically knowledgeable, does a great job of conveying the material and writes fair exams and assignments. His lectures can get a bit boring at times because he has a tendency to read directly from the slides but it's not unbearable.
He allows you to use a cheat sheet with the exams,but is very picky about giving full credit for the answers.

I took this class online but we did meet with Barker once a week.  I felt that the classtime was useless and did not support the lectures.  If you're not familar with agriculture expect the B range because the exams require a general understanding of Ag. which the lectures don't help with.  Overall an easy A for anyone who is from a farm.
This professor is good.  If you miss class, you miss learning.  I enjoyed HCS 612, and use that material in my current work.  Thanks!
Interesting class.  He's a great teacher.
A very good teacher, modest and helpful

I took the course during the summer - 1st term.  I think it would have been easier/less work if I had taken the regular 12-week class.  However, Dr. Barker is really nice and helpful and cares about the students.  He has a great New Zealand accent too, but he is really easy to understand.
No Comments

Funny and entertaining guy, but when it comes to the actual content he teaches in lecture, he was all over the place. I talked to many other people in the class, and almost everyone had no idea what was going on and had to find material elsewhere to teach themselves the content.

Personally, not for me. He was funny and a nice guy, so I have nothing against him personally. As a professor, however, I found him a bit unorganized. He gives a notes outline to fill out; however, I found his slides would often jump around, making it hard to follow. Grading was also left until the last minute.

Baker never answered emails and would provide important information very late.. or not at all. There was a project worth 20% of my grade and he provided no rubric to complete it. He doesn't keep his TAs in check and slacks on posting homework and exams. Expect to be cold called in class. Easy exams and homework's which makes up for bad lecturing.
Was a decent professor but never answers emails. Pretty sure he just doesn't care and doesn't check. And attendance is mandatory even for recitation.

Never responds email. Unhelpful recitation by a TA. A lot of recitation paper to solve and homework online separately for only 3 credits hours. Online textbook sucks and does not allow round error. Never tell you recitation grade till the end of semester. Just avoid it. Definitely okay for DA students not to take it to pre-study stat and prob.
Baker is a humorous professor, but sometimes his lectures can be difficult to comprehend. The slides are not very helpful and may cause confusion. However, overall, he is a great professor.

No grading transparency. Random grades in the gradebook that were not reflected in the syllabus. Horrible lecture style, seems like he doesn't know his own content. Exams are easy, but he will tank your grades with all the random grades he decides to put in just for sh**s and giggles.

Disorganized and unclear about grading, due dates, and the setup of the entire class. Uses online third party source for his exams which aren't too bad but are harder than his own written exams that he used in the past, which also had partial credit. Only redeeming factor is the extra credit offered, but is also unclear about that.

He was an enthusiastic and fun professor with little homework, but things were not always clearly explained. You definitely have to be proactive in learning and practicing outside of class because of the light work load. All exams are online and open note, and lectures are available via zoom.

The content was a bit disorganized in comparison to the textbook, HW, and Quizzes, but Baker had great lectures. Very funny, respectable guy. Doesn't teach you formulae by hand, but how to compute them online and in TI-84; very efficient. Accommodating for students who wanted to be online for class. Accessible if you email him and ask for help.

Dr. Baker was a funny guy, but his lectures were not helpful and disorganized.  If you don't do well on something it really hurts your grade.  Always answer the tophat question because that is apart of your attendance grade. Recitations were not helpful. Dr. Baker goes off topic and the notes were never helpful for me.
The class was kinda hard, and Dr. Baker wasnt very accessible outside of class which made learning very hard. Chegg carried me through this class.
lecture is just awful, fast speed and no explanation of everything. Quiz are not difficult, but the grading system of quiz is just tough.

Yes, the class is pretty disorganized, but as long as you keep track of what's going on and keep up learning with the textbook in advance before the lectures since he goes insanely fast, you will do fine, expect to use a lot of calculator/Crunchit, but that's the good part, little to no math on your part, and I love Dr.Baker for his personality

The 1 star is for personality. Dr. Bakers funny but his lectures are impossible to follow, I passed the AP Stats test and still felt lost. Hes quick to give accommodations but beware because he NEVER answers email. Had to contact the director a month after he told me I could make up a test because he never answered my 27 emails or zoom messages.

At the end of the semester he admitted to doing worse than usual, so maybe in other semesters he will be more on top of the class, but this one was so stressfully disorganized. Luckily he was forgiving with grades because of it. You never know what assignments are due when, the lectures are missing a bunch of stuff, and it was just so stressful.

Dr. Baker is so disorganized and does not care to ever answer any students emails. He also does not answer the TAs emails. His lectures are confusing and the examples do not make much sense with the material. Hes a nice guy but hes a horrible professor.

He won't ever respond to your emails. He doesn't even respond to TAs emails from what it sounds like. He may have potentially been more busy this semester but he is still a professor at the end of the day and his performance was sub-par. The class material was thankfully easy since most things could just be plugged into the calculator.

Most disorganized professor I have ever had. He never responded to emails and never changed my quiz grade that the online homework portal messed up from week 4 of the semester. Inaccessible to both students and TAs. Go to class for attendance, but you are better off learning from Khan Academy.
Will not respond to his emails no matter what. Teaches his lectures too quickly and is impossible to keep up with.

He's a very funny and entertaining person, and you can tell he truly wants to engage his students. However, he is incredibly disorganized and if you are taking his class online, you will sometimes struggle to get your question answered or be able to fill in all the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took his online class and as lots of people have already said he is a personable and funny guy. His exams are pretty fair as they pretty much cover the same things in the weekly hw and quiz. At times the online class is a bit disorganized but nothing too bad for me.

Dr Baker is very cool and down to earth. He knows the stuff and knows how to treat his students. His exams are not too difficult. He gives opportunity for extra credits. I'll recommend him taking him especially for any STATS class

Offered abundant chances for extra credit throughout semester. Gave a fair amount of assignments but never too much. Exams were provided through course learning software (Sapling) but were not too hard. Really cares for each and every student. Wants to see students earn good grades. Very accommodating as well. An excellent and knowledgeable prof.
Dr. Baker is very hilarious when teaching Stats. If you stay up with the material this class is not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Baker is comedic. He makes statistics personable and relatable, making lots of jokes. Everything else about this class was a joke, too. The midterm/final are difficult, comprising 70% of the grade. His poor articulation in lecture means you should develop a relationship with your TA as soon as possible. No curve but slight grade scale change.

He is better one on one than he is in person. Go to his office hours outside of class. he skips a lot of material in lecture and doesn't stay focused. His tests are fair and if you use the study guide it will aid you preparing for the test.

A funny guy. Good at teaching stats too and tries to make stats relatable to students with sports and current event examples. He'll really help you out if you go to office hours. Only complaint is the final is worth 30% of your grade you really have to rock it out the whole time. Can't just get to an A early in the semester and relax.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Awful professor. It got so bad that 30 students went to report him but nothing happened because he is the head of the department. We had our first midterm well after the point to drop without petitioning and it took him 16 days to grade it. The class ends next week, and I have no idea how I am doing.
He is a good statistics professor. I think he is good at business statistics.
He is a good statistics professor. He is an interesting elder.
Dr. Baker is hilarious. Hes a very personable guy and homework is very light. Exams are a breeze and he wants his students to get good grades.
I did not think he was a bad teacher, but the things he taught us and the homework and quizzes we took every week on Sapling were different, so that made it hard.

I heard great things about Dr. Baker, but they didn't really show through on the online class. He was often late in posting the week's materials, sometimes waiting until Thursday (when the homework is due Friday). At the in-person exams, I could see he was funny just like everyone said, but unfortunately, I didn't really love his online section.

Dr. Baker was a great professor! Even for someone who doesn't like math, he made his lectures easy to follow and engaging. The class is very clearly laid out for you: no surprises- just 1 homework and 1 quiz per week and a few midterms!
Dr. Baker's lectures could be confusing, with lots of examples. But that's how math can be. The tests were very fair and you could definitely get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Would take again

reviews.comment: I didn't do well in 1450, but mostly because it was easy for me to get lost in his "steps for success." He does outline how to solve problems in lecture in a lot of detail, but I found that his steps were more than necessary. If you just learn how to do the homework well (don't use google) every week and do his practice exams, you'll be fine.

Dr. Baker definitely makes learning statistics better, with his humor and engagement with the people in the class. He is interested in getting to know students and ensuring that they succeed. Attendance definitely has a decent impact on your grade, and his practice exams, in my experience have been helpful when  preparing for the test.

Dr Baker was AMAZING. Math in the middle of the afternoon was not my idea of a good time. But he made this class so enjoyable. He even danced to "Juju on that Beat" on stage for us. This was my second time taking Stats (1st at a different school) and I am so glad he was my professor for it. Definitely recommend him!

Dr. Baker is one of my favorite professors. He is very funny and always willing to help. He holds office hours right before his lectures and exams. GO TO THEM. He will drop extremely obvious hints about what will and will not be on the exam.

Amazing professor and very easy class. More than willing to help you if you need it and his tests are extremely fair if you're going through lecture, homework, recitation, and quizzes. Only missed about 10 points in the whole class. I suggest taking this class in person if you have no statistics background and/or are not self-motivated.
Funny guy but wouldn't recommend if you want to actually learn the content. He isn't the best at explaining concepts.

Dr. Baker is so hilarious, and even came to lecture on Halloween in a costume. Uses TopHat to take attendance, which is graded. He is a really great professor, and is always willing to help during his office hours. Provides you with old exams that are very similar in content to the exams you take. He was great to learn from. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I have taken Cal 1, math 1172, linear algebra and passed with an A. However, this course is very difficult. I strongly believe it is because Dr Baker isn't the best professor. He is funny but that doesn't help me honestly. His tests are very difficult. The study guide he provides suck. Don't rely on them like I did. Probably gonna fail unless curve
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I enjoyed taking Stats with Dr. Baker. He's funny and laid back (he even did a lecture in costume during halloween.) The lectures were straightforward and all the slides were available online, though he regularly took attendance via TopHat in class. The exams weren't difficult. He was a flexible grader.

I really enjoyed Dr. Baker's teaching style, though I recognize it may not be the best for everyone. Because everything builds on everything else, it is important to have good attendance, otherwise the brief explanations he gives in class might get lost in the shuffle. Funniest professor I've had, and very willing to help with questions.

Dr. Baker is incredibly nice and has the jokes, but his class requires some effort.  There's online homework and quizzes which aren't necessarily hard, but his tests can be difficult.  Takes attendance every class.  Very nice professor, but expect to spend some time on the material to get an alright grade.

Dr. Baker is nice guy but not great lecturer because he is not very clear about his explanation and skipping steps made it more difficult to follow. His exams are relatively hard and long for the amount of time given. Not recommended unless you have good statistic background!

Dr. Baker is a great guy, outside of the classroom. His teaching style is very laid back, to the point where it almost isn't teaching at all. He just goes through a powerpoint and students follow along in the notes, but he's never clear on what he's doing or how he got answers. Very difficult to learn from.

I had him for an online class so I never actually talked to him, but he seemed nice enough in his videos.  He did tend to drag on a bit on easy concepts. The only problem I had was that he constantly changed the dates of assignments and with an online class I wasn't checking daily to see if he had changed the due date once again.

Dr. Baker does not explain the concepts well as statistics is a whole different set of concepts than what most people have seen before. He is a nice professor but is not very good at explaining the content.  He goes through a slideshow with the solutions worked out but doesn't explain where each # comes from or why he solved it in that way.

Dr. Baker is a genuine teacher that will listen and try to be as flexible as possible and he also understands that outside factors play in a student's life also. Stats not really my thing but he made the class interesting. You may get called on in class to respond and you should be able to do so and give the reason why.

His lectures were interesting because he liked to joke around, and he keeps you involved by using a software called Tophat to answer questions about lecture that he used for attendance purposes.  But statistics just is not an easy subject unless you are good at math.  I thought the tests were okay, but I am a math minor.

In the beginning, the class was common sense. Later on, it got tough because I did not take it seriously. When I did take it seriously, it actually was easy. Everything builds upon each other, so you have to keep up. Dr. Baker is awesome and so are his lectures. If you see him in his office hours, he breaks down the stats real nicely.

Dr. Baker is a great guy, but this class certainly wasn't easy. As the semester went on, concepts seemed to become more and more unclear and they all built off of each other. All I can say is practice on your own more than just the mandatory homework and go for help before you get too deep and it's too late. Also slightly curved.

I never actually dealt with Dr. Baker, only his TA, but the class is definitely doable. The midterms are easy, the final is a bit harder. There might be a tiny curve which is good. There's homework every week where you get 2 attempts at each problem and then there's a quiz which isn't too bad. I would recommend his class.

Baker is truely a great guy. In a lecture of 400-500 kids he tried to get to know and memorize names. Has notes that you print out and bring to class and just fill in the blanks. He often makes reference to Drake and Migos which is funny. He doesnt really believe in extra credit and midterms are okay but the finals tricky.

Similar to the previous comment, he's kind of odd. He gives the vibe of a Discord moderator. His lectures are very dry, and he reads right off the slides. He's strangely defensive when questions are asked, but at least his exams are fair and easy if you read the slides.

Huge ego but maybe the weirdest professor I've ever had. He gets offended when students ask questions so we just stopped asking. During review I asked "could you also go over xxx" and he replied "You mean 'would' I also go over that. Obviously I can." Like man I was just being polite obviously I know you can.

The entire semester consists of being lectured at with dry and slow slides. Assigns a few homeworks throughout the semester but weirdly they are primarily all coding which is never discussed in lecture and does not show up on exams.

Professor Barker is a pretty great professor. While his lectures are a little dry, they're very informative and leave you well-versed in the material. His exams are very fair and the TAs give good feedback on the HWs so that you are able to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best professor I seen in OSU. he is willing to provide inner depth concept about the lecture instead of read off. It helps you understand the idea instead of memorize things. Homework is easy if you follow along the lecture. lecture gives you pseudocode of homework which make thing super easy. Exam reasonable and easy (avg of 80 in my class).

Good lecturer who is obviously very experienced in his field. The homeworks are doable and I learned a lot of useful skills as someone new to Python.
