I took GEO 3801: Political Ecology. If you are not a geography major do not take her class for a GE. She is a really harsh grader and would constantly leave vague comments on what needed improved. never gave our 100%, always took off .5 of points. she wont like you if you arent into geography

Becky is amazing and GEO3801 is so interesting. No tests or quizzes, but there are discussion posts twice a week and optional attendance. There are also one page write ups due twice a month. What makes the course difficult is that some of the readings and academic journals are long and take time to comprehend. Easy B+, Hard A. Final is a project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There are no tests or quizzes: instead, there are homework assignments mostly consisting of readings and short-to-medium write-ups. Attendance is extra credit. Prof. Mansfield is awesome, very passionate about what she does and what she teaches, flexible, and accessible outside of class. Not the easiest but definitely recommended for this GE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her classes are all discussion based, she doesn't like quizzes or exams so it's mostly analyzing readings. She is very laid back about late assignments as long as you communicate with her often.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very decent professor. I enjoyed her classes when I did go but because attendance was extra credit/small part of grade I think many people skipped the class. The lectures were interesting and she is definitely enthusiastic about what she teaches, and I think your grade reflects the work you put in. Class is very discussion and reading based.
Probably the most intellectually exciting class I took at OSU even though it wasn't super hard

She is a very kind lady and a good professor, however her grading on quizzes is horrible. Very picky on responses no matter what the question is asking. One question asked about your thought on a topic and she only have half a point cause she didn't think the response was thoughtful enough.

Becky is incredible. She has a real interest in this topic and thoroughly enjoys teaching the students about the subject matter and getting them involved in discussions. Random activities for points but participation is not mandatory. Very relaxed and helpful.
Becky is a great professor! She's clear, helpful and seems to really care for the students. Class is easy and interesting. I definitely recommend this class!

Becky is great! I had her for 430 and 635. She is very passionate, approachable, and makes her classes incredibly enjoyable. She is a great resource and is always willing to talk with students. One of my favorites!

I was ill most of the quarter and she seemed pretty reasonable about participation grades. A large part of your grade is just being, mostly from pop quizzes. I averaged a B- on the midterm and final and I missed quite a lot of classes, though I did most of the readings. If you go to class and do the readings, this class will be easy.
very interesting material. communicated clearly-tied together well with course themes. very helpful. great teacher.

She was a decent teacher overall. The course material wasn't very interesting. A large part of you grade is based on being there every day. There are random pop quizzes, which can be annoying. If you are the type of person who never misses a class, this is the class for you. If you miss a class occasionally, you might not want to take it.
She was not very helpful in assisting me during a time of personal difficulty.  Her class was pretty basic and boring for a 400 level class.
Enjoyed the class
Great teacher.  Great interest in the students.  Really cares about the subject matter.  A rare find at OSU.
The course wasn't too hard for upperlevel.  If you show up youll do fine.  Dr. Mansfield is trys hard to be helpful and is a decent teacher.

"you've raised some excellent points, your sentences are clear, and I like what you've shown in your thesis.  you spent a lot of time proving your point and did so very well even though you took a difficult stance.  great job"  B+
Spent more time trying to control the class than teaching.  Way too wet behind the ears to be teaching an upper-level class.

Taking ECE 2020 with Steven Bibyk, anyone can get an A without knowing or learning a single thing. Complete lack of preparation or education for continuing ECE students. He is notorious within the department. Take for an easy A, but if you are relying on this course to learn Analog Circuits you won't.

He is trying to teach but it's so hard to understand what he is talking about. 
His lecture is jumping all over the place. He uses a word doc with same font and size for his lecture notes throuout the semester, which is really difficult to read and comprehend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he needs to retire. if you got stuck with him like I did, get ready to learn the entire course material yourself.
Does anyone actually understand his lecture? He just yaps about spice and abstraction.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's 80 years old. During the lecture, he yaps like he is drunk. He expects you to answer questions without him teaching anything. I registered for this class as a 1st yr student, and it's bad. He expects you to know things from Linear algebra and 1251 even though they arent prereqs for the course.
Class was confusing without clear notes and I struggled to learn very much.

Labs were outdated and the instructions were unclear. Multiple broken links and PDFs. He didn't post them until the morning of the lab so you don't have time to prepare in advance. He showed up once on the first day for 20 minutes and then we never saw him again. Never responded to any emails either.

Doesn't teach anything. He rambles every class about abstraction, and always talks about things you're "going to learn," but never actually gets to the learning part. Massive waste of my time and now I know nothing I need to continue on in ECE. Avoid at all costs.

I switched to the better 3020 professor (Musah) after one lecture. I suggest you do the same. Musah is a amazing teacher, unlike this one. Any good reviews of this guy didn't actually show up to his lectures, or he wrote that review.
Take him for easy A. Avoid if you actually want to learn.

Bibyk is a hobbyist not a teacher. He goes over LT spice homework questions in class and posts zoom recordings but still left me head scratching if the answer I submitted is what he wanted. Grades very easy but I did not learn much. Class schedule was very disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bibyk is an incompetent teacher who preaches about flaws in the American education system while providing an even worse experience. His course fails to teach analysis techniques or calculations, essentially weeding me out of higher-level electronics. Do yourself a favor—avoid him for 3020 and find a professor who actually teaches the discipline.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Everything in the other awful reviews is still true. He seems to acknowledge that he is disorganized and lazy with how he teaches and does not care. His teaching style would actually be good if he was just more organized in lectures and on canvas. I mean his notes are unformatted, not labeled, and just all through together and typed in a Word doc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He will legitimately never go through a single practice question in class. Instead he will just yap about an upcoming makeathon. Unless you really take the time to go through the MIT lectures and textbook material, you won't pick up on anything. I did so good in ECE 2020 just to forget it all when I had Bibyk.

All this professor does is use the word abstraction about a million times, assign MIT lecture videos because his lectures are awful, and give homework that is "participation based" however the answers are legitimately impossible to find. Do not take.

I loved Bibyk. His methods aren't conventional but by god it works.... he encourages you to search and look for answer. I'm not used to answering essay questions but I feel like I learn a great deal from working on the homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Didn't teach, just told us to look at Wikipedia pages and MIT course slides from 2007.

Dr. Bibyk is indeed very human. He likes online classes, Wikipedia, and biking. Also loves MIT lectures more than his own. Encourages involvement outside of his class. While his class is an easy A, I switched to a different professor because you can actually learn the material.
He loves ECE but cannot teach, you will learn nothing. However if you want a free pass through 3020 it is much easier than any of the other professors.

This ece hobbyist does not deserve to teach. He cares nothing about learning. In fact, he simply points you to Wikipedia if you actually want to learn anything. No effort in lectures. Assignments are directionless. He is the scum of ECE at OSU. Avoid at all costs if you even remotely care about ECE. Only praise possible is that he is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Another semester still no changes from Mr. bibyk. If you want to learn about electronic do not take this professor. Lectures are very broad and he doesnt teach specific or problem solving. Homeworks and exams are confusion and have no correlation to anything. Everything seems to be for effort so thats a plus but you wont learn anything.

trust these reviews and don't take this class. We're 7 weeks in and we haven't learned anything. he's too selfish to share how he knows stuff, so instead he tells you to look everything up. Doesn't care whatsoever. Uses other people's material (MIT, wikiversity, etc) and doesn't even teach them. Expects you to be an MIT student. DO NOT TAKE HIM.
Man's straight up teaching from a wikipedia article

Just started the semester and already wanting to drop out. He expects you to remember everything you've learned before, and does no actual teaching. He just gives you links to find information for you to learn YOURSELF. I don't understand why he can't just teach the material. He just tells you what to look up. I'd much rather pay for khan academy.
Don't take his class, especially 3020. If you don't believe me, just give it a try.

The homeworks arent bad, as most problems are explained in class. This genuinely makes the class so much harder because exams are graded are on accuracy as opposed effort like the homeworks. Class was made a lot more difficult and definitely not accommodating during COVID-19. Avoid taking it with him if you can

If I could give him a negative rating I would. You will not learn a single thing in this class. Homeworks are graded on effort but then both midterms and final report are all for accuracy which is almost impossible to get a good grade due to him teaching nothing. Not accommodating at all for COVID-19 and strived to make the class harder for us.

Really nice guy, very knowledgeable, but not meant to be a teacher. He can answer any questions you have, but email responses take several days (if he does get back to you). If you want to learn, you'll have to read the textbook and definitely study the stuff he posts online. Lectures are brutally boring, but have important info. Generous grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Bibyk is an awesome guy. He cares a lot about his students and wants to be a resource for success for the future. However, he is not an organized or gifted instructor. It feels like I haven't learned anything in his classes and now I'm walking into a final that I'm pretty sure I'd get the same grade on if I took it at the start of the semester.

Horrible. Literally told our class he could do a better job at teaching, but he'd rather spend his time creating a makerspace, pathetic. Extremely disorganized, not even given a syllabus. When applying for research with 3020 prereq, I was told to take I would have to take the class again with another professor. Don't take him if you want to learn
Waste of my tuition. Did not learn a single thing.

This course with Bibyk gave me the knowledge to interview for industry level VLSI jobs.  He doesn't spoon feed material which makes lazy students mad.  Rather he teaches what things to look for and how to find the material for yourself.  I literally just got a top notch VLSI job because of this course. If you work hard, you'll get a lot out of it.

If you watch his video lectures then you can follow him during class, but he isn't the best on explaining topics. Nice professor, wants people to succeed and be creative. Loves jokes and isn't intimidating. It's an easy 'A' course if you put some effort into the work.

Terrible professor. Doesn't really teach, just expects you to learn. Get ready to make stuff up for his class. Also he usually cancels class about every Friday and does a "distance lecture" (worthless video that might be helpful on the homework). One good thing though, he helps you answer the homework (even on the day it's due), which is nice.

Steve Bibyk is probably the worst instructor I have ever hard. He is a funny,  laid back guy, but I have never learned less in a college class. You will take this class, not learn a single thing, and pass the class with a B by making things up on the exams and getting "partial credit". It is a true shame to not learn about a fundamental EE subject.
You will not learn one thing about circuits in his class. Awful teacher.

Bibyk teaches differently. He doesn't teach linearly and expects students to put in a lot of time outside of lecture (watching separate lectures, googling, reading). He knows the subject, is happy to help and is quite lenient when grading, but his rambling  way of lecturing can be really frustrating. Find a group, do the work and you're golden.
Sucks. Worst professor I have ever had. Decides not to teach and tells you to look at 3 other sources of material instead.

Terrible. Avoid if at all possible. I have learned more about circuits from my device physics class. He tells you to just look at the online MIT freshman circuits class (for a junior level circuits class).

Dr. Bibyk is the worst professor I have had yet at OSU.  He babbles during class about what you're going to go home and teach yourself through other college's online courses and doesn't teach a thing.  At 6 weeks in and I had less than 1 page of class notes.

Don't take his course if you really want to learn something. He is the worst the instructor I have ever seen.  He taught nothing in class. And I'm happy he does not continue to teach ECE5021 this semester.  He is the shame in my college learning life.

If you are willing to take initiative, his classes are informative and somewhat easy. He provides answers to homework, even tests during lecture, but projects and studying for the final should always be a group effort.
You have to have some IC background to attend his class otherwise you will never what he's talking about... It's not hard to get an A though.

Dr. Bibyk is a great guy, but not a great teacher. It's not that he can't teach - he prefers to not teach. He gives vague assignments, cancels class every Friday, doesn't post homework/exam solutions for weeks... etc.  If you need rigorous logic, don't take Bibyk's class. Beware the final project - its more arduous than you think.

ECE3020 in AU15. The guy is really cool, but he's a god awful teacher. He doesn't teach. If you ask for help in office hours he's helpful, but he doesn't teach or lecture in the slides. If you have him for 3020, read the book early, ask questions often, and watch the MIT OCW videos quickly.
Not helpful at all. But it is a good course to raise your GPA and make the credit hours you need.

Truly a great guy, but I don't recommend taking his classes. He doesn't lecture, just rambles about random topics and the homeworks. Exams aren't bad if you know the material, which means you needed to have read the textbook, read the random slides he provides, and Googled it all.
Worst IC professor ever. I don't even know why he taught digital VLSI while knowing nothing.

Prof. Bibyk does not lecture like 90% of profs. He simply introduces you to the material and expects you to read/skim the text book and websites and learn the material how ever you can. He does not spoon feed at all. If you take his class and follow what he says to do YOU WILL LEARN SO MUCH.

Awesome prof.  Study hard and go to class. The students who don't learn anything don't do either of these and just do the minimum to get by (pure laziness.)  Bibyk doesn't spoon-feed but is incredibly helpful towards students who show initiative. After all, we're in college, not high school.

Dr. Bibyk is an awesome professor!  He is difficult (especially regarding the tests) but definitely fair.  He is genuinely interested in helping students understand the material and knows his stuff. He has wealth of knowledge in Digital/Analog VLSI.  I definitely recommend him, just don't be lazy student. Put the time in to learn all th

Proffesor Bibyk is an extremely difficult professor BUT you will learn SO MUCH. Be ready to spend alot of time in the lab! Even though it was difficult, I did learn alot about VLSI design and I'm glad I was exposed to that material. Very helpful after class also!

Be prepared for a lot of individual work. If you are interested in learning the material well, be as resourceful as possible. Hard to follow in lectures, but if you know what questions to ask, he gives good answers. His grading is not always very easy, but the material he quizzes you on you will have seen before, so grade wise the class is easy.

Lecture is the most worthless stuff to go to for this guy. I guess he tries to teach, but you learn absolutely nothing. He tells you to go ahead and watch the MIT OCW lectures. Not too hard of a grader bc of his lack of teaching skills though. I don't know what to say.

Worst professor ever. Nothing he has ever said has been useful. His notes are useless and he tells you to go to Wikipedia instead of using the textbook. I seriously don't understand how he is able to teach. The class isn't that bad if you watch the MIT lectures. Avoid him at all costs.

Steve Bibyk is simply the worst professor at Ohio State. He never teaches anything, uses powerpoints made by other professors, and basically tells you to look at MIT lecture videos in order to learn. He gives partial credit randomly, tests over material that he never covered in lecture, and tells you to memorize the material rather than learn it.
He's the laziest guy in the department.  I went to his office a month after final grades were posted, and I asked to see my final project grade.  He told me he didn't actually look at them in detail

May know his stuff, but terrible at teaching. Never actually teaches, just mentions what he is going to teach. But never actually does it. Never works any examples, just goes over how he would do it. No math in class, no thought processes. Just skimming. Telling us to go home and teach ourselves.  Very frustrating to deal with.

Steven Bibyk was a very good teacher who challenges his students to work hard, and if you pay attention you will get a lot out of his lectures. He's very prepared and informative and you will learn a lot from him if you really want to; he's also a big fan of Darcy Egan and the Great Outdoors and the table of contents. The book is also very good.
Put simply, the worst professor i've had in my 4 years at OSU.
unorthodox style of teaching to say the least, but the class is so easy it doesn't matter... tests are straight forward, a recitation would make this like any other class with a useless lecture

Totally unorganized. Uses MIT lectures and PPT's to teach and is all over the place. This guy will have 10 different windows open on the computer and click back and forth between them. Grades dont matter to him either just write down whatever he says in class on the exam and youll get a pretty good grade. I cant believe they let him teach.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He teaches absolutely nothing at all in class. I can't believe anyone would defend his teaching style. All he does is open the MIT website and read their lecture PPTs. I'm pretty sure I don't pay thousands of dollars a quarter to have PPTs read to me. AVOID IF POSSIBLE!
Spends 10 minutes a day looking at the table of contents. Doesn't explain anything well. The only positive  thing he has going for him he speaks english. Should be fired.

Absolutely terrible professor.  If you need to advance in ECE, do not take him.  Grading was very easy - he gives points if you write jokes on the tests or quizzes.  I missed a 30 point (out of 100) problem on an exam and got a 91%.  Take if you want an A and to learn nothing.

Bibyk is for people who want to learn on their own. He is a true teacher only when you apply yourself. He understands not everybody in the lower classes(as all of the other ratings are from) are there to learn. Much better teacher in higher level courses. Good teacher who gets a bad rep from people who don't actually apply themselves.
horrible

Take him if you dont need to understand the material.  Write down every word he says, then repeat them in any order on the test and you cant get less than an A.  It doesnt need to make sense to you or him.  Let his classes be a GPA booster and thats it.  If you want to learn the material, get another prof

"The biggest thing you need to learn in this class is to skim the book"-beginning of class till a week before exams.  "You should memorize everything relevant in the book"-week before exams. Had 4 exams in 1 day. Asked to switch his to another day. "I think you should suck it up and take it then." Note that all of these actually are quotes of him.
If you take 323 with him, go to class every day, write everything he says down, and on the exam write everything back to him, even if you don't understand it.  No way you can get less than 90%
Teaches inverter very well. But that's almost it!

Graduate students: He is not advisor quality - not smart, gives you the run around before giving your recommendation, his lecture and his courses are useless, in a word totally unprofessional.  Undergraduate students:  Dont waste your time with his classes, if you think you cannot understand him, its not your fault neither does he.
Constantly puts down other profs and the department. Very unprofessional. His "lectures" are nothing but scribbles on an overhead. Buy the book and read it on your own time, you will learn more!
Never take class from this guy. He is a terrible teacher. You don't learn anything. He is so unorganized and very hard to follow.

Very helpful. If you want to learn VLSI take it with this guy and pick his brain after class. In class lectures are VERY scatter-brained and hard to learn from. The textbook is awesome though. This guy (unlike other profs) is based in reality and isnt affraid to tell it like it is.
Dr. Bisaro is a very nice person and co-teaches with Dr. Ottesen. His exams were certainly easier, but it is difficult to pay attention during lecture as he isn't very engaging.
It is difficult to rate him. Bisaro is such a sweet guy with amazing intentions. His exams are really hard to understand, and you never quite know what he's asking. I think hes simply alright.

Dr. Bisaro is a nice and caring guy with a good sense of humor. He takes the material slowly, but at the same time, he kind of goes too much into it for the intro bio course. He is good at explaining stuff, but I think sometimes he forgets that it is supposed to be an intro course; test questions are mixed with many poorly worded ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He put me to SLEEP! Let me say that you should take any course of his when you are most awake because by the end you will be on the verge of falling asleep. He was very boring, but I found him very funny, which was somewhat helpful. I did not think he was good at explaining lectures, so be prepared to do a lot of work on your own to learn content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Slides have alot of material so he goes really fast. Super funny professor but can be easy to zone out when going over super lengthy material. Exams are difficult.
Great professor, has a good grasp on everything he taught in the class. Takes time to answer question in and outside of class. Also just a cool guy, 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Bisaro gave very engaging lectures (at least to me). His background is in epigenetics and plant pathology and you can kind of tell when he lectures what he's passionate about. Very funny. Was nice to me when I was stressed about a grading mistake.
he's a very knowledgeable guy, but he is very boring. try to pay attention because there's a lot of content
Excellent and organized, clearly cares about and respects his students. Never makes you feel stupid. Not great with technology, but great lecturer.

His lectures had a very good set up of starting broad and then adding in all of the details. The exams were fair and were derived mostly from his powerpoints. Reading the book helps because he tried to follow it closely.
Excellent lecturer, fair grader, lots of material but extremely well organized, reasonable tests.

Dr. Bisaro was a great professor! His lectures were easy to understand and he was great about answering questions that students had about the material. His exams were easy as long as you studied what was taught in lecture.

He's awesome, incredibly informative, gives easy and straightforward exams, his notesets are excellent preparation for the tests, and his name makes me think he'd fight Batman.  He was really good and I look forward to having him a few more times in the year to come!
Love his classes! He's awesome!
Very good professor! he explains things slowly and have his own noted which are exteremly helpful. His test was fair. I recommend him.
I love this guy! He is so cool, and he knows stuff and explains really well!
No textbook for the class, simply provides extensive handouts.  They are very helpful.  Very clear in class... expects you to know your stuff but doesn't trick you too badly.
Cool dude, goes nice and slow - easy to follow lectures.  Excellent Noteset, straight forward test.  Would definitely take another class with him.
Very slow and concise. He does not try to cram too much into a single class period. Pretty good teacher.
He gives notes and he's great! I love this class.

Going to lecture and paying attention will be the most valuable thing for the exams because she often tells you what is important to know. My biggest tip is download, learn how to use, and then make Anki flashcards because that is all I used to study for the exams and I ended with over 100. She also gives generous bonus questions on every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bishop is very nice and approachable. Class itself is only 4 exams and follows the typical neuro course structure. Exams can be difficult, but she offers a lot of bonus points that make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire class is made up of only four exams (definitely a weed out class). Each exam has 6-10 extra credit questions. People are complaining about how much memorization there is but hello, that's neuroscience and medicine. She is very easy to walk up to and while yes, the lectures may be boring, the topics themselves are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has 4 exams with 6-10 extra credits for each. The slides are really hard to follow and study. The lecture is boring. You just have to memorize everything on the slides if you want to do well in this class. But she is generous with extra credit and also has a curve at the end (87-89 is A-). Prepare yourself to do lots of memorization.

All she does is read off slides, so if you're keen to skip class, this won't be bad for you. I wouldn't say this class is extremely hard if you make quizlets, draw pathways, study with classmates, etc. She's just boring and never responds to emails.

Dr. Bishop is not very nice. When you go to office hours, she makes you feel stupid and judges you for not knowing the material she studied for years. The class only has 4 exams and that makes up your entire grade. Her lectures are not helpful because she just reads off the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture slides are very unorganized, it is obvious that she has been reusing the same slides for years. In class, she reads directly from the slides, therefore attendance to class isn't necessary. The reason this class is difficult is because there is just so much information to know. You have to memorize every detail from the slides
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bishop is very nice and clearly knowledgeable, but I have never been happier to finish a class. She was easily the most boring professor I have ever had (and of course the lectures are 80 minutes). The only grades are 4 exams (all have EC), and they are strictly from the slides in class. Study the slides a lot before exams and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bishop was extremely clear on what information students should know for the exams (all of which were very fair). Lecture attendance is crucial, but if you show, up, pay attention, and review lecture slides on your own you will be just fine. Dr. Bishop is incredibly intelligent and caring, and makes every effort to help students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bishop is one of the best professors I have at Ohio State. She is nice and does care about her students. NS3050 is a combination of neuroanatomy and neuroscience, which is as hard as it is supposed to be. Dr. Bishop is trying to make it as easy as she can. Make sure you study hard and go to her office hours.

Bishop is so monotonous, her lectures are useless to attend and she is likely one of the most inconsiderate professors I have ever met. The course is graded only based on 3 midterms and 1 exam totally 100 points, which have very little room for error.

The class is about brain anatomy and physio, it's not supposed to be fun. Dr. Bishop makes it as manageable as she can. The only grades are four exams, each covering the lectures in that block. You can tell she wants students to succeed because she provides everything you need. I recommend studying early and often, and she'll curve it at the end.

Dr. Bishop is a kind person and has good intentions. Although Neuro 3050 is a very difficult class, she only makes it harder. The lectures are long and difficult to pay attention to. She likes to read off the slides without much expression and the slides are all over the place so it is extremely difficult to organize. Overall good person, meh prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Too much content on each exam with little to no direction of what would be on it. Her powerpoints are a mess. So unorganized. Better off reading a textbook and organizing it yourself. Much of the material on exams is SPOKEN in class and not even on the slides. Basically. Teach yourself. Lectures are so dry and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is SUPER lecture/test heavy. There are 4 tests, 50 points each (200 total) with 5-6 bonus questions/points included in the last three exams (we had a total of 16 bonus points/questions)(& a 3% curve). For me, I REALLY needed to attend/record the lectures. Dr. Bishop is a very good professor who does a good job of explaining the lectures.

I wouldn’t take this class if I had any choice whatsoever. Dr Bishop is your introduction into the most complicated, convoluted, and overwhelming material you’ve ever read. Dr Bishop has negative sympathy for this and decides to only grade you on 4 Midterm Exams. If you do poorly or any of these, good luck graduating as a neuroscience major.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class unless it's something you are interested in learning about. A lot of the material on the tests is not found in the power points and, Dr. Bishop was not the professor for the block 2 and 3 exams. Her 3050 class is much better and only has her teaching, which she excels at.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The tests were absolutely nothing like the material in the lecture. It's no surprise she has to curve her classes because everyone struggles and stresses over remembering every little detail.

Dr. Bishop was very accommodating, considering the pandemic .. Her lectures were easily accessible and she allotted time during her weekly (non-mandatory) Zoom class to clear up any doubts or go over difficult topics. It was the most straightforward class I took this semester. This is a heavy class in terms ofthe amount you have to learn but doable
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Georgia is an absolute GEM. She did awesome teaching this course online due to COVID.

Pretty difficult class but the instructor is so very knowledgable about the subjects. She explains difficult material well, but be prepared for a lot of it. She mentions many times the importance of drawing out tracts and pathways, and I completely agree. Drawing everything out helped me raise my grade from a C to an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was so lecture heavy, with the class only being out of 4 exams. Lecture is hard to sit through since the content is so dry. There were some bonus questions at the end of the exams that helped a lot.
Dr. Bishop is awful. Her lectures are so boring and its hard to stay awake. She is monotone and her lecture slides don't make sense. Good luck!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bishop is not the worst teacher but she does have implicit bias towards specific students. She only clarifies a question on a test for specific people (only If you go to class on a regular basis). She is also a very boring lecturer. After taking her class I began to question her integrity as she lied about personal grade adjustments.

clear explanations of what you need to know to pass the exams. She doesn't make the exams harder than it is, its brain anatomy its already extremely difficult. She lectures and draws questions straight from lectures. She likes to use the pictures a lot on exams so really study where structures are in brain and what they do.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bishop was phenomenal. After the first exam, you get 5-6 bonus questions on the next 3 exams. She also curved our class (90%-100%A). Everything on the exam is from the powerpoint-don't waste your time on the book. For exam 2, KNOW THE CROSS SECTIONS. Exam 3 and 4 had no pictures, and 4 was by far the easiest. Her exams are difficult, but fair.

Dr. Bishop is a good lecturer, it's just that the material isn't always interesting. Exams are fair (w/ bonus questions) and the material comes straight from the slides. The book can be used to enforce pathways and concepts. Overall, good class but be prepared to put in the time to memorize a bunch of information in a short amount of time.

You'll definitely have to work for your grade. She isn't very interesting to listen to in class, but is always more than happy help students during office hours. Her tests are pretty fair and there's always carry-over material from exam-to-exam; she also offers bonus questions on exams. Be ready to have a lot of material thrown at you all at once.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really loved Dr. Bishop! She was always really clear with the concepts and went over things multiple times and at a pace that wasn't too fast. You can tell she's really knowledgable about neuro. The exams were hard but not crazy.

Dr. Bishop is a really good teacher. She is very sweet, she is very quick to respond to questions you have, she is very quick about grading  ( grades posted within 24 hours of your exam) and she is pretty straightforward about her requirements. Excellent teacher. Most of the people that do not do well in this course do not actually like neuro.

Dr. Bishop is a wonderful professor!  She is a very fair grader and it is clear what she looks for on exams.  She is very accommodating and understanding of extenuating situations which may impact students.  She is very knowledgeable and I definitely learned a lot from her.

The topic weren't interesting to me, but its Structure & Function of the brain. She is a wonderful professor though. Although the information was dry, tests were a bit difficult,  and there was a lot to memorize, she really did empathize with students.  Going over the notes often, making flashcards, drawing visuals, etc is really helpful.

I would take everything being said right now about Billy with a grain of salt. This was his first semester teaching the course and while it does unfortunately show, I think it will without a doubt get better as he continues. He is very accommodating and has listened to student suggestions. We were just his guinea pigs, but I see it getting better.

This class isn't as tough as some say. Billy has been accommodating, letting us drop the lowest exam grade and giving a 40 point curve on the second exam. Exams are challenging if you don't study, but with effort, you can get an A or B. I think lectures and course structure could improve, but I believe this will improve with the coming semesters.

Worst class I have ever taken at fisher, IDK who put him in charge of teaching this course because 50 average on the second midterm really says alot about him. Apologies every time for making the exam too hard and so many kids failing but yet again the next exam is as hard as the previous one. Don't take him!

Take it from me, i bombed the first exam. The 5s and 1s are lies. He made mistakes but tries to fix it. overall a good prof, willing to meet outside class. People are hurt over grades or thankful for the curve. Also everyone keeps mentioning his other job and sports, but he rarely brings them up. Not gonna say he's the best but ppl are dramatic.
Like this is we should all boo him collectively during lecture

Had a very rough start in the semester. 1st exam experienced technical difficulties, which resulted in him changing the syllabus to allow one dropped exam grade. Second exam was too many questions and less time which resulted in class average very low, and he gave us a 40 point curve on a 180 point exam. Overall content of course is tolerable.

Worst professor ive had thinks hes better than everyone and its the students fault for failing when his online exams dont work or he gives basically no time to take an exam. He talks about his personal experiences instead of teaching or asking questions, we get it you work in the cell phone tower business; that doesnt help me pass the class.
He sucks and is so unfair. Horrible tests no matter how much you study, gave a 45 question math heavy test in 70 minutes. Class average was a 50 for that exam. Do with that what you will.

I didn't want to leave a review until I saw all those 5 star reviews below. DO NOT TRUST THEM. "Billy is better than most professors at Fisher" my butt. Some of these 5 star reviews are really suspicious, because who would unironically write "THIS is what college is all about- learning how to fail, and making things right. Billy the goat!"

Fake 5 star reviews. He also does not deserve any credit for "owning up to his mistakes" and "trying to make things right". He literally had no choice. He messed his first semester up so badly, and was in danger of losing his job. He still is, and for good reason. He got scared after the disaster of the first exam reached Ted's ears.

Yes, hes owning up to some of his mistakes. No, that does not mean you should give him a 5. To the review that told everyone to "study" and "grow some balls", quit brown nosing. If the entire class gets a 50 in an intro class that's on the professor. I'm giving him a two because he is trying to make up, but the class is still objectively awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Those who think Billy is the worst professor at fisher are in for a rude awakening. Very nice guy who wants his students to succeed. People make mistakes and Billy has owned up to every mistake he's made in this course (exam curves, exam drop, etc). As long as you actually put forth an effort and study, you will do just fine in this course.

Lots of mistakes were made during the first half of the semester, but he is trying to change. Appreciate his effort to make the class better but right now the class is still horribly setup and we are already two exams in.

Let's read the writing on the walls, consistently got 1s then randomly got a bunch of 5s out of thin air, yeah, not obvious at all! Don't listen to a thing the positive reviews say, if you do a bad job teaching and the average is that low, sounds like a proper reflection of his teaching abilities. "Lock of the week" (these don't hit btw)

Looks like a couple of people handed him a 5 star for curving a test by 40 points. This is intro to finance not calc 3 the tests should not need to be curved. If anything it speaks to his inability to teach material that shouldn't be that difficult. He's trying to trick you guys into saving his job and some of you are falling right into his trap.

Very confused by all the 5 stars given AFTER his exam. He curved it so much because the average was a 50% -- he didn't have a choice and that grade is a reflection of poor teaching. Not only is he not a good professor, he is not a nice person and doesn't seem to like teaching. Worst prof I've had in Fisher and probably at OSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Billy makes sure that you don't fail!
Worst class I've ever taken

These new 5.0 reviews are very strange, whoever is reading all of these reviews take it with a grain of salt. AU 24 is Billy's first semester teaching this finance class and it is a struggle but he is genuinely striving to improve. He communicates clearly and although the class is frustrating at times, this class is completely doable with this prof
too difficult

What is with the influx of these five star reviews just because he curved an exam? If an exam needs to be curved upwards of 40 whole points because the average was so low, that speaks to an inadequate teaching ability. Exams are harder than Marc Smith's despite teaching and preparation being significantly worse. TA's aren't good either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
To my glorious King Billy Patterson, the true savior of students:

Thank you for taking accountability and curving the test—it's a rare thing to see a professor look out for us like that. You've brought some much-needed relief to our stressed-out lives, and for that, we are grateful!

His lectures are literally giving out textbook definitions for terms. No calculations are taught at all and expects us to take the exams with little time and so many problems. I don't know how anyone can actually work through the exam of 45 questions in 70 minutes with so many calculations.

One of the worst professors at Fisher. Lectures are rushed and don't match exam content. Recitation TAs are out of sync with lectures and explain concepts poorly. Horrible testing environments and not nearly enough time to complete 45 questions with "none of the above" as an option for each. More interested in sports betting and golf than teaching.

Worst professor at OSU. Billy treats this class like a side gig and probably spends most of his time golfing after his two lectures. We never get enough time on tests, and it feels like he's not interested in helping us succeed. Ball don't lie, Billy. Your Rate My Professor rating is a 1. OSU, give your $130k to someone else.

Billy Patterson might be the worst professor in fisher. He does not cover the content well at all and his tests are ridiculous. It almost feels like he actively wanted his students to receive a poor grade…

Despite teaching an intro finance class, he expects prior knowledge and gives exams every two weeks, with only one lecture per week. This leads to rushed explanations, making lectures ineffective. I've studied and completed the homework, but it didn't help my grade in the slightest. He's a good person, but ultimately an incompetent teacher.

Absolutely the worst professor I've had at Fisher. Course is set up terribly, students don't get nearly enough time on exams. It seems like him and the teaching assistants aren't on the same page every week as they ask if certain topics have been discussed in lecture yet. Overall just a very bad experience for a core class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is absolutely awful. The hardest Fisher class I have ever taken and it is an intro level course. I have never written one of these but this is SUCH a bad professor that I felt the need to tell you. The exams will ruin your GPA because there are too many questions with too little time. Terrible testing environment. Do not take w/ him!

Billy Patterson is more focused on giving "sports betting locks" than he is providing a deeper understanding to his lecture material. His exam gives way to many questions with not enough time. I hate Bonnie Schroeder too, this guy not as bad, but boy does he make it close.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are extremely tough, with 45 questions in 70 minutes with around 13 of those being math problems. Formula sheet was on the same page and on the back of the answer sheet we were required to fill in, which was not allowed to be removed from the exam.There is literally no reason to handicap your students like this. Lectures are useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Does not care about his job, tests are incredibly difficult and unfair towards students. He has no idea how to be a professor, no idea why Ohio State hired him.

New professor. Don't think he's qualified. Says his side job is selling phones? But he definitely treats being a professor as his side job instead. Lectures are not beneficial because he just gives answers with no explanations

Took Dr.Bilik for a music class at UConn this semester and he was great. Very engaging and passionate about what he's teaching. The course itself was very interesting, even coming from a STEM major taking this as a gen ed course. Would definitely recommend; not challenging, just some memorization. Grading is pretty split up between multiple things

His lectures aren't super entertaining, but he keeps everyone pretty engaged and is pretty clear with his instruction. He also chooses music that is more interesting to analyze using music outside of classical very often. Make sure you go to class and there's only one homework assignment a week plus a reflection which is very low stakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Many of my classmates could not stand Dr. Bilik, as he can come off very power hungry. I didn't necessarily enjoy him, but you will do well in his class if you kiss up to him and do the homework correctly. He has a dry sense of humor, so get ready for uncomfortable moments. I learned a lot from him and he is easy to reach outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Alber is very intelligent, but the way she presents each topic with her lectures and the way she asks her exam questions were unnecessarily hard. You literally have to teach yourself everything because her way of lecturing was so hard to understand. So my advice: get ready for stressful hours of studying after class, DON'T MISS LECTURE!

Dr. Alber will interrupt your exams at the last 15 minutes just to discuss questions about the exam when she is already making the exams too hard to even finish in the given time length. Her lectures are very unorganized and her office hours were in the evening (5:30PM), which is hard to attend if you have a job or commute to school.

When my friend passed away during the semester, I reached out to her to postpone the second exam. Instead of compassion I was met with strictness and lack of care towards my situation. While Dr. Alber is passionate about her work, she does not extend kindness or empathy towards her students.

Nice and willing to help outside of class, however, exams were truly hard to study for. Content was not hard, however, be prepared to have many of what you studied in class to not be on the exam at all. Not much big picture understanding, felt like random fact regurgitation most of the time.

Dr.Alber is a really good professor. She is very caring and accessible outside of class. Her lectures seem to be disorganized but as long as you attend lecture and do the problem sets, you will be fine. She is a tough grader, so make sure to say write precisely what is on her slides and don't say anything incorrect (she will mark more points off).

Dr. Alber is knowledgeable, articulate, and happy to answer questions. Her teaching style emphasizes critical thinking and will prepare you for a career in science. She took time out of her schedule weekly to host a journal club for research-minded students. Extra credit problems are abundant and earned by your hard work.

Dr. Alber (like many microbiology professors) is very caring. Show up to every lecture and go to office hours when you need to, she is ready to help any student that comes her way. Her class' topic is one of the hardest in the undergraduate classes, but it can be interesting if given the chance

Difficulty was similar to other Microbiology courses at OSU. I appreciated that she offered bonus points but the grading was ambiguous and there was no real rubric. Exams were difficult to study for and I think the class should have been graded on a curve. Some students put the effort in and did not deserve to fail the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Alber is very knowledgeable and cares a lot about her students, but the class is a structural nightmare. I found the lectures to be very chaotic and unorganized. Her problem sets and exam questions are very vague and unspecific. This class was required for my major, and it seems that Dr. Alber is the only one who teaches it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is based on the 5 problem sets and 3 exams. The problem sets are basically exam level questions and are sometimes confusing. Her lecture slides are just as confusing. If you want points you have to answer questions almost exactly how she puts them on the slides. She is really nice, she just words things difficultly.

She is brilliant, but as an instructor she isn't very good at communicating. She isn't clear on what is going to be on exams, nor is she clear when explaining content in the classroom. Her tests are fair, just... a crap shoot.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's not bad. She's kinda all over the place in lecture (or so I thought) made recordings listened to it later, realized she wasn't speaking gibberish. She gives you 3 problem sets which help direct you to the things she gives you on the exam. Not bad, I thought she was going to be terrible from the reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: can't understand a word she says. never got a C in a bio class before this. the tests aren't impossible, the final was what tripped me up. essentially a biochemistry course, nothing really related to physiology. diversity,eh. KNOW EVERYTHING ABOUT RHODOBACTER SPHEROIDES.

Dr. Alber meant well, but taught so poorly. Her notes were all over the place and didn't follow the ones she gave to students. She grades based on opinion, not on a rubric, but will give extra credit on HW if you go the extra mile. DON'T miss lecture. Study the material over dry weight of a cell and similar math sections because it's on every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This isn't a hard class in terms of material, she is just very picky about how she wants questions answered. I can't say there's a lot of new material if you've taken micro 4100, but again she is pretty picky. She brushed over questions people asked in class. Also, she gave bonus on the assignments if she "liked your answer", give me a break.

Does not communicate well with classroom, in lectures or on exams and assignments. The grading on exams and assignments seem meticulous and somewhat random. Will disregard questions on clarification of major concepts.
Dr. Alber is very respected and a good lecturer. She makes you really think about material instead of just memorizing. The class ties together many classes for a micro major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a nice person, but her lectures are painful. This is essentially the biochemistry of microbes, not physiology and diversity. A lot of info in one lecture, and not much on the slides, so go to class. The entire content of her course could be taught in 2 weeks, but she loves to make things unnecessarily difficult. Good luck.

You can tell she's really passionate about what she does.  She's very willing to spend one-on-one time explaining stuff.  Grammatically her English is very good, and her accent isn't really that thick. She expects a lot out of you (which isn't bad) but sometimes it's hard to understand exactly what it is she's looking for, hence why clarity is a 3.

Dr. Alber is a very sweet person. You can tell she genuinely wants her students to do well and is willing to meet whenever. The class is definitely challenging but she makes herself very available to help. That being said , I did find the class difficult. But a very cool lady!

Dr. Alber is very nice and makes the class super easy. You get 5/10 on the quizzes just for writing your name and lab section and she only takes the top 5 quizzes into your final grade.  Tests are straight from lecture and not tricky.  She even boosted everyone's midterm score by 13% or so by taking off a question that  lot of people missed.
TERRIBLE TEACHER.
Terrible teacher- cannot even speak proper english grammatically, yet expects the students to spell complex organism. Hard to understand. Not helpful. Goes on tangents.
Very helpful teacher, takes pop quizes in lectures and asks you to come up with a question from previous lectures. Not bad professor

Class can be hard esp after 1st midterm, but if averages are low he offers midterm corrections and adds a curve at the end. I'd recomend going to class or knowing someone else who can send notes bc it's hard to learn the material without the class notes. To my knowledge he didn't post class notes often. Midterms/final was fair.
Horrible professor
I think that Husen was a good teacher and he was really hands on gave you a good look at what need to be done.

Dr. Husen is an amazing professor who loves what he teaches, and wants you to love it as well. The material is difficult but he explains it in a great way. He's extremely caring and more than willing to help answer any questions you might have. I hope to take another class with him in the future.

Bill is one of the best math professors I've had. This class can be difficult at times, but he explains things very well and the exams are fair. He also offered midterm corrections which was very generous.
Husen is a respected professor. He cares about students.
He is a kind person and a good professor.
bad professor

His lectures just confuse you more than anything. A lot of people (including me) only attend recitation and grades have improved since then. He rambles about unimportant details and is very dry. Hopefully you have a good TA to make up for it

The best math teacher I've ever had. Overall the class is fairly challenging but he presents the material in a way that really helps students to learn it. For exams he usually will put several proofs on the exam that were done in class and/or homework so if you practice those enough you will do fine.
Dr Husen is helpful and I liked the way he delivers the material. The problems in the exams mostly come from HW problems and examples in the book and class so I highly recommend going to lectures.
Husen is an excellent teacher in that he teaches the material in a very clear way. His exams are reasonably challenging, but very fair. He is a picky grader, though.

Very good at teaching/explaining the material especially when most of the class is confused. Lots of homework, which are good for practice. Exams were not too difficult. Material was pretty straightforward, too.
Very goos, understood everything he said. Put the work in and do the book problems and you will get an A.

If you're in business calc, chances are you're not great at math. It'll challenge you, but Husen is very clear. Textbook homework is not mandatory, but DO IT. At least some. This class is all about practice, so after lecture do maybe half the homework and it'll take you less than 30 minutes. Over-prepare for the second midterm as well.
I am not a math person at all.....but I enjoyed his class. As much as I hate Business Calculus, Husen was pretty cool and explained things decently. If you're a math whiz, you can get a B+ easily.
Bill is a nice guy and wants to help. His class is not easy, but if you do work then you'll get a good grade. He tells you exactly what he wants and is fair about it. great professor!
Very good teacher. Very clear and was always willing to elaborate where needed.

Husen is one of the best professors I have ever had, made all the topics clear and his tests were more than fair. If you can get him, do it, you will learn a lot and might even enjoy the class at the end.
He's very understandable and teaches well. He makes you feel very confident about doing well in his class.

My favorite math class I've taken at OSU. Dr. Husen taught the material very well and for engineers. He focused on applications, not theory, and gave many useful examples. Loved his mini-projects on the Fourier Transform and image compression. Very interesting and great class for engineers. He's very nice and tests are very fair. Recommended!
This is an amazing instructor. Very easy to understand. Explains everything really well. I wish I could've had him for all my math classes. I would definitely recommend him!

Best math professor/teacher I've ever had! VERY clear, explains things VERY well and lectures are organized. If you keep up on the work and go to lecture on occasion it is super easy because he actually teaches it!
This guy is my favorite! He explains everything very well and works through a lot of examples.
Good Math Prof. Works through problems and explains things very well. Devoted to helping students. He even reviews in lecture before every test. Wish I could have him for M132!

Good lecturer, he is American, and speaks very clear English - a huge bonus in Ohio State's math department.  His lectures are straightforward, and examples are easy to follow.  Go to lecture, do the homework, and this class is a breeze.  (The curve brought my grade down though, bummer).
The class was easier than I expected it to be.  He makes his points clearly and covers the material throughly. Do the homework and go to lecture if you want an A.
Best math prof @ OSU. Taught how he thought would be most clear even if it meant going a little astray from the book. Go to his lectures and pay attention. This class was a breeze.
good teacher, but only if you understand him the first time he makes a point.

He wasnt great but he wasnt terrible.  He just rushed through things, and wasn't exactly clear about everything.  If it wasn't for my T.A. this class would have been a tough one!  But probably would recommend over the other profs. who are mostly foreign and tough to understand.
Best math teacher I have ever had. Clear teaching and easy tests..Go to class
Good Guy.  Very helpful during office hours.  Based on professors my friends had, I had the best. Husen would go over stuff on exams the class before.

Amazing professor...this is the second time I've had Husen..once back in MA 150 and now for 571. Both times he made the subject crystal clear and the exams were fair and representative of the HW....be careful, the final was substantially harder than midterm

Calc at Ohio state is so lame. Don't balme husen, the class is meant to be a weed-out for pre-professional students. Stick with it, unless you're a physics/engineering/math major you will never use this stuff again. Husen is a pretty good lecturer. Go to class.

He's not an exciting lecturer, but he goes over all the material clearly and is a very approachable guy. Tests were fair and if you know the material well enough (Can learn it w/out attending lecture) you should do well.  Better than any other Math Lecturer I've had or even heard of...good guy
good teacher i switched into his class way better than Wong. goes over everything well test are kinda hard but final is easy. i suggest going to MSLC if you want to do good!

It was a hard class.  He sometimes went way too fast and it was hard to catch what he was talking about.  I wish he would do more examples in class.  His tests seem somewhat easier than the quizzes, and he's got a descent curve.

This class was impossible. Exams were impossible. Quizzes were alright. Used to think i was good at math before this class. Probably a really hard class regarless of which professor teaches it though.

Dr. Husen is an excellent professor.  Thanks to him, I understand not only how to do the math but why it works.  Reviews and exams are straightforward, no tricks.  Going to class (imagine that) and seeing examples helped me get an A.
Great lecturer. Learned a lot in his class. Made some hard topics easy.

Husen seems to enjoy teaching. I would say of all the possible lecturers, he truly is one of the best ones in Math. He is interested in what he does and comes prepared. He is willing to help you before or after class. However, do not miss his lectures, because he goes fast and his examples cannot be found in the book.

I really didn't like the subject matter of the class.  Husen spends a lot of time doing theorems and proofs, which went past me.  Fortunately he does examples later, and these are very important.  He's pretty helpful too if you talk to him.  WARNING: the first 3 weeks are like a joke, so get an A while you can.  The material gets abstract and hard.
His tests were qutie difficult but there was a ten percent curve (in my section, at least) I managed to get a B+!  Just don't expect what is on the notes and quizzes to be on the midterms and finals.

He's a good guy, pretty nice and is always trying to look out for the students. However, he goes a really fast pace, so you can't ever expect to have down time or miss a lecture cause he covers so much.

I SUCK @ math...but Dr. Husen was very clear and made me feel like I actually understood what he was talking about. He is very helpful and seems like a pretty cool guy. It seems like he enjoys what he does and that makes it so much easier to pay attention in lecture. Math sucks, but if you have to take it, I would definitely recommend Dr. Husen.

His lectures were very helpful and almost impossible to skip.  Tests wern't a good representation of the material learned in class, however, the test that can be found on his website (they're hidden, so look for them!) are EXACTLY like the ones he gives (same order and everything with a few numbers switched). Overall, wonderful teacher!
Such a good teacher! He made the class easy
AWESOME! I am sooo thankful I got him because some math lecturers make it impossible to pass!
Great professor for math
The class was pretty boring but he explains things very well. He is a really cool guy and a good professor.
He is a really laid back guy, and it's easy to learn off of him. I liked him a whole bunch!
Mr. Husen was a good professor, but by the end of the quarter I hate math now.
Cool guy who teaches well. He's not one that likes to listen to himself talk or make you feel stupid.
No Comments
No Comments
This guy is the****, probably the best teacher in the unniversity makes everything clear and helps peeps out

This professor is awesome! He explains things better then all the highschool math teachers I had.  If you are taking math 150, or any other course this guy teaches, do what you can to get into his class.  He really is a great professor.
This guy sucks! If you want an example don't expect one from him.

Excellent teacher.  Explains topics clear as day.  I had no calculus experience before college and this guy explained things so well that I hardly tried and got an A-, only because the class was not curved due to the average passing.
Excellent teacher, best Math 152 teacher Ohio State has!  Does example after example during lectures so when tests and quizes roll around you have already seen the questions most of the time!
Great Guy, really good at what he does. Doesn't always look it in his appearence. But good professor.

This was a very hard class and the exams were hard and u need to study alot to pass them. Although he uses alot of examples, he was unclear when he taught    and sometimes hard to follow, nice person though.

A very sincere guy who makes the class half decent.  Although math 152 is hard, he made it a lot better than he could have.  Makes some funny jokes and keeps class interested.  Lots Of Examples!!!! I loved that about him.
Best Math Teacher I have ever had.

A great professor.  The class is hard (as is to be expected) but he is always glad to help.  He's one of the few teachers that *wants* to teach rather than use teaching Calculus as a way to pay for research.
He is extremely hard.  He does go over examples but often goes very fast without taking the time to explain things.  I was good at math until I took this class with this professor.
Best math prof that I have had so far at OSU. Teaches you what you need to know.

He does not explain things in a language I could understand.  If you love math and it comes naturally to you, then you will be fine.  If you stuggle at it, though, and need extra help...choose another prof.!!
Class is standard, but exams kick your BUTT! He makes every concept and picks THE HARDEST problem to do for it...watch out
Easiest math class you'll ever take.  Forget the homework, try to stay awake in class, and DO THE PRACTICE MIDTERMS.  They are exact clones of the tests. oh, and no final!
Best math professor I have had at OSU. Makes the subject very easy. Do the practice exams and you will be fine, and go to class.
No Comments

I've learned a lot more from him than any other professor at OSU. He makes the course challenging, and the exams are horrible, but I learned a lot. I would rather have him than a professor who practically hands the students "A's"
No Comments

Math 571 is more challenging than Math 568.  Husen teaches both, but I would personally only take him for 571 because he actually proves the theorems that he puts on the board. If you pay attention, you should understand them and do well. Do the homework.

He is lazy. His lectures don't flow because it is obvious he doesn't prepare for them which makes them difficult to follow.  He doesn't work out example problems completely, pure laziness. Class always ended early and he made exams pretty difficult.

Often uses algebraic tricks without explaining how they work. Exams are very very difficult. Pick the hardest parts of the book and learn only that and you nmight get somewhere. Seems annoyed when asked for help.

This guy knows his stuff.  He thinks, speaks and communicates clearly.  I think he might be the best teacher for Math 571.  If you study hard, you can do well (and learn linear algebra) in his class.  He's the best non-honors math prof that I've had here.

He is a horrible teacher. Didn't respond to e-mail. No curve in the class, I got a D despite studying for hours. Very unfair, and gets angry if you ask questions. Expects you to just know everything on yr own. I learned from the book.

Review sheets not at all on par with his midterms.  Usually midterms are too long for the exam period.  It was easier to study from the book than it was from his notes.  Lectures did not prepare you for homework, homework didn't prepare you for midterms.
he got angry at the class when we forgot something we learned back in 10th grade math, gives decent notes, but be sure to study cuz his tests are much harder than his review sheets

He always seems available for help.  Lectures sometimes hard to pay attention to with lots of proofs and such, but gives review which is very difficult.  Tests/homework pretty difficult but pretty big curve to make up for it.
One of the best teachers for Calc. Exams are tough
Straight forward guy.

His lectures were pretty good but he didn't seem to want to challenge his students (for example he didn't give us a final because he didn't want to grade it).  This could be good or bad depending on if you like Math or if you are an Engineer :).

Knows his materials.  Speaks using complex mathematical terms, but somehow you understand exactly what he's trying to say.  Lectures clear and helpful, tests over basic/easy (class avg. around 85%).  Study the review sheets to get an A on every test!  :-)
He's very straight forward.  No trick midterm questions.  A very good teacher overall.  Also his midterm and final review sheets are just about all you need to ace the tests.
confusing
great to talk to if you needed help, very fair
No Comments
No Comments
Very straight to the point and, speaks softly.
decent
Good teacher!  Material starts out very easy until the first midterm.

The professor has very poor communication but you don't necessarily need to speak in this course. I tried to reach out to understand more on what was expected from an assignment and no response. Ended up trying my best and got 100% so no need to stress. Very light workload just annoying quizzes are 2 attempt open not & exams are 1 attempt proctor.

She is one of the most caring, thoughtful, and helpful professors! I was going through a rough time in my life while I was in her class (not because of her), and she always checked in to see if I need any help. You will be reading a lot, but she chooses great material, and is always willing to explain something if you need help! Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

Professor Pirim is a very caring person and if you put time into studying you will pass her class with no problem. You can drop 1 of the exam grades and the exams are very similar to the practice, so if you do the prep for the exams you will be fine.

One of the worst profs. Class is extremely difficult and she rushes through the material and is not good at explaining the concepts. She changes everything last minute including the date of both of our exams. Exams are worth 80% of your grade and the second exam is extremely difficult. Material isn't really useful at all, take advanced corporate.

reviews.comment: She is very kind and tries to explain everything the best she can but the class content is very difficult. The tests are heavily weighted but you can drop one. The second midterm was extremely hard.
Best Professor in Fisher. I would recommend everyone to take her class. She cares about her students a lot and you learn without realizing.
4229 seems overwhelming but Professor Pirim really cares about her students and makes the class interesting and wants everyone to learn, if you come to class and just pay attention you will be fine.

I have taken Options and Futures class last semester as one of my advanced courses. Wow what a great experience I had. She was by far the best professor I have ever had at OSU. She is very caring with amazing lectures. She loves teaching and show that she cares about her students success.. She is a rock star teacher.

This was one of the last classes that I took at Fisher and can say that Professor Pirim is the best professor I have ever had. This content of the class can be difficult at times but if you show up to class, stay engaged, and ask questions then you will have no problems. I wish I could have taken more classes similar to this.

Professor Pirim is one of the best professors at Fisher. Although she does set a hard standard with her course load, it is not extreme by any nature. The work is difficult, but that is to be expected considering that they are all senior level. She is very accessible outside of class, and will meet at literally almost any time during the week.

Terrible at lecturing, cannot explain concepts to save her life, and makes everything harder than it needs to be. Should have taken advanced corporate.
She is really good! Best prof in Fisher

Homework problems are very similar to exam questions are pretty similar. Easy stuffs the first midterm kind of challenging for me in the second half. She tried to scared us at beginning but lots of extra credits+over 20% A. Be sure to ask question for Cases and COME to class. Best professor in Fisher and the best choice for advanced finance.
She is really good! One of the best in Fisher...

reviews.comment: Incredibly tough class that covered derivatives from the perspective of someone who would need to hedge portfolios. Recently graduated and work at a bank, almost all of our portfolios need this so it was a handy class to understand that. Otherwise I wouldnt recommend, the material isnt as useful anywhere else. Very challenging topic, fair grades

reviews.comment: She is extremely nice, and makes things as clear as possible on lectures. If you go to class and do the practice problems then you will succeed in this class. She tried to scare us off the first day, but honestly it's not the hardest class you'll take at fisher nor the most work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult. I have great grades but just know you WILL need to work for this grade. If you are a graduating senior just stay away. She is a smart professor but she goes fast pace and assumes you should know everything. If you take notes and study you can get an A, it is just not what you want for one semester left. Take corporate.

reviews.comment: She is one of the most fair professors ive had. Yes the material is hard, but if you go to class and take notes... there will be zero surprises on the exams. Exam problems come directly from sample problems we do in class. She says the textbook is necessary but I never used it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does not take it easy on us. Mostly a seniors only course which means if you fail, you won't graduate on time. Just be aware ahead of time that you will need to at least put in a bit of effort for this course unlike some of the other classes offered in the business school. I'm very stressed out for the 2nd midterm and the final. I need to pass. plz

This class has been my hardest class at Fisher by far. It is an in depth class that focuses on options and futures from an academic perspective. If you want to be prepared for a career in investments this is NOT THE CLASS. Birsel does a poor job of explaining material and assumes everyone is as good as she is at math. TAKE CORPORATE OR RISK MGT.
