reviews.comment: She's not the best for explaining, but she did her best. The class is fast pace. but She's really helpful and patient if you go to office hour and pretty laid back. 3 fair exams, will just cover the topic she taught (need study from her exercise in class! she won't post the answer online). Will curve a little bit
Avoid Prof. Pirim like the plague. She breezes over tough topics that show up on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take corporate or risk instead
You need to work for your grade. She isn't the best at explaining things and thinks the class understands concepts just because it is easy to her.

Overall a pretty difficult class just because of the material. Not the teachers fault. Very lecture heavy class which can get boring and very confusing. Takes lots of understanding and practice to pass the exams. Very fair exams though, and homework is not bad. You don't need to work ridiculously hard, but you will need to work for your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher!Her exam are pretty easy and she gives you a review guide for each exam. Many times there will be exact problems with the same answers from the review on the exam. She is very, very forgiving and will help your grade out GREATLY if you mess up Awesome teacher! Put forth some effort and you'll pass. An A requires some work, though.

He is super nice and clearly loves linguistics. However, as someone only with a minor in Linguistics and not too much background with technical areas of the field, this class was quite difficult. He goes on a lot of random tangents that only sometimes matter, which is confusing. He explains things very wordily and unclear. Easy grader though!

Course was easy from start to end. The most required is readings before each class and some writing/presentation assignments; the readings will take up most outside of class preparation. Even though course was easy, class time was always entertaining; lots of class discussions with prof. and students. Will learn a lot about writing in Linguistics.

Took Phonology with Professor Koehnlein my first semester at OSU, it was a great class. The structure was lecture heavy and at times quite challenging but Professor K was always helpful in office hours and gave really good feedback. The final was super easy after having taken intensive notes all semester (open note/open book).

I loved Bjoern! He's super passionate about linguistics and it shows. There's a lot of reading assigned to prepare for lectures, both of which can be dry at times, but he's a really funny guy and I loved his german accent so that kept me interested. He's really helpful, super easy grader, and all around it was a great intro to linguistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Bjorn is really passionate about linguistics but lectures were boring and he goes on a lot of tangents that were funny but not really conducive to the class. Spent a lot of time reviewing concepts from previous classes which was weird for an honors class. Hes a really great guy though and likes to have fun and interesting discussions.

Koehnlein is a solid professor. Attendance doesnt matter as long as you turn in the (few) assignments in Carmen. He is not a particularly tough grader. He does have an accent and speaks rather quickly and I did have trouble understanding him at times.

The class was discussion based with various books assigned for homework. You were often expected to read 300+ pages in 2 days. Lots of response papers with vague instructions and grading criteria. No tests, just projects. Divided into groups for final project, but given next to no instruction. She is a tough grader, but is a nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was very fun and she was a good professor. I could tell that she really cared about the students and she made the online environment a comfortable one. You will have to read some longer papers (skimming them works), but you will also have to write essays for this course. Overall, if you try you'll be fine.

Readings were well-selected and engaging. This professor has a passion for the course material. Often had unclear grading criteria with no used rubric for essays. Lots of reading overall. At one point in the semester three essays were due over three weeks. Not a bad course or professor but there are better options. Final paper instead of exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor I have no words. She expected us to read like a whole book every single week and then write a 300 word essay on the whole book that needed detail and everything. I never got above a 90 on any of my essays and this was just not fair. There was never a steady rubric so I never knew why I missed points. Never take this class for a GE.

The professor has no soul. Despite suffering from many physical and mental ailments during this fully-online course, I was still expected to meet all deadlines with little to no flexibility. This class was so depressing, and it honestly made me want to drop out of college. She does not care about her students; do not take this class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The cutoff for an A is a 95 in this HONORS class. I do not recommend you take this class, unless you want to spend all your free time reading books and writing papers. Expect low grades and little to no feedback. Suparna i does not provide enough flexibility in extensions for medical conditions, which is absolutely ridiculous considering COVID-19.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Raised A cutoff to a 95, and never gave a paper grade over a 96 to anyone. Took off points without providing a reason, even when meeting privately. We read entire books in a week, expected to write 100 word max discussion posts and 300-500 word max essays with an unreasonable expectation of detail. Take a class with a normal grade scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was a very tough grader and never really told you what she wanted in a paper or how to improve your work. I was sick during the semester and had an excuse and she still failed me for two major although I did them, making my grade drop for the rest of the semester and I was unable to fix it in time. She never answered her email either.

Gave little to no feedback, not even a rubric. Our entire class recieved "good start" for our feedback on an assignment. Expected an unreasonable amount of detail in essays that had a maximum word count of 300. Increased cutoff for an A despite grading ridiculously hard. Take another class to fill your social diversity rq.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Bakshi is super disorganized in lecture and posting material online in a timely manner. The homework rarely has information we learned in class and do not relate well to the exams, which is frustrating and extra time consuming. The class is graded heavily on exams and there was one a week before the cumulative final exam.

Bakshi is super passionate about sustainable engineering and that helped a lot with motivation in completing assignments; however, he is pretty disorganized and his textbook isn't always the most helpful for homework. Sometimes he would say something would be posted by a certain time and it wouldn't until days later. Overall, it was fine.

I took this class an elective and found it to be one of the most interesting and engaging classes I took throughout my major. Professor Bakshi is an expert in sustainable engineering and his passion and understanding of the subject showed in the lectures. Dr. Bakshi fundamentally changed the way I view and analyze the world.

This class was my favorite class I've ever taken in CBE, even with it being remote. Dr.B was engaging and cared about the students. He cared the course was valuable. If you put in the effort, the class is not difficult compared to others. His lectures were interesting and all aspects of the class were well organized besides a few technical diff.

The lectures are very conceptual and then you go to do the self-graded homework and they are in depth calculations, most weeks requiring the assistance of office hours. There is also a vague group project in which you are randomly assigned. Also, he calls you out in front of the class if you glance at your phone or laptop during lecture so beware.

I want to love him more (he's really passionate about what he teaches) but he is so unorganized. He'll take points off for things he didnt specify he wanted (for example: he'll ask for a table, you'll make said table, he takes points off because you didnt include a graph too, which he didnt ask for). Group project is heavy, not much guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I actually think Bakshi is a pretty cool guy. A tad unorganized at times, but I feel like he actually genuinely cares about the students. Was always willing to work with the class in terms of rescheduling because of crazy weeks ( career fairs, other exams, etc.) The only thing I hated was the final worth 40 percent of your grade. Thats a lot...

The group project is terrible and requires you to work with unmotivated teammates on a project that should be assigned to a full-time engineer. The tests are almost nothing like the homework and there is no other study material provided. Don't take this class.
Good prof. VEry helpful.
Bakshi was the worst professor I have had in the field of engineering since I started at OSU in Fall of 04. He is unclear and makes easy concepts difficult.
Tends to make things overly mathematical which in this class disguises the potential real world value of the course. Didn't seem overly concerned about teaching, sometimes seemed unprepared.
No Comments
Gets the point across pretty well, but won't really help you very much.  He purposely gives you vague answers to make you think, which I personally found to be kind of irritating.
Great teacher. Easy to understand.

Mishra is that one college professor that is a close friend to you, makes you laugh in the class and makes sure that your doubts are cleared. He is hilarious and makes class very interactive and easy to understand. Explains everything in simple words and if you point out his mistake he will give a reaction that will surprise you.
Even though the class was a total goof, he still really wanted to help us learn and understand the material.

Instructor Mishra is new to teaching. I learned more from him than the actual professor. If you need to take Calculus he is the one. The class is tough, but he breaks it down in a way that one will understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Well prepared.
Had Prof. Bhushan for ME 765.  Was very helpful at all times with any part of the project.  Good personality and very intelligent.

Loves teaching. Is very knowledgable
Good Professor, when he comes to class :)
No Comments
No Comments

Make sure you attend class, especially before midterms and finals because he goes over example problems right before them. He explains things very thoroughly if you attend his office hours. He is also very nice and approachable. You will work, but he will reward you with good grades for your efforts!
He is a great guy, knows the material well, but the class was tough. He is very helpful and will go out of his way to help you. Exams are not easy, but the curve helps.

This TA alone is the best teacher i've ever had at OSU. You can truely tell that he loves teaching and will do anything for you to get a great grade in Econ 520. I wish all my professors and TA's had the attitude like him!!!!!!!!
No Comments

Very light grader and the coursework is very straightforward. There are 2 quizzes a week with an activity and a TopHat at the end of the week. Very manageable class. The quizzes are on carmen and the slides are provided as PDFs for the lectures, so you don't have to watch them.

Horrible professor, horrible class. Lecture videos are so long and the quizzes don't even cover the main points from the lecture. Two quizzes, always reading, watching videos, then small activities that just as a bunch of minuscule questions. Quizzes are bad, most random questions that you can't even find answers to in the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have immense rage for this class. Why on EARTH is there so much homework. There was sometimes TWO QUIZZES plus more homework and doing the quizzes would take forever. I would do ANYTHING but take this class again. Why is there more homework in this class than classes for my major. Don't take this class unless you want to go through torture

I took CSFRST 2374 for my history gened req and I dont regret it. Took me a while to get into the swing of things, but then I excelled in the course. Trina is very helpful, easily accessible and organizes her course very clearly. She seemed to love what the course had to offer and I did too!
Excellent.  Highly knowledgeable.
Good lectures.  Lots of reading.  Lots of paper writing.  Tough critic when grading papers, but well-meaning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The only assignments for this class are 3 essays. He is a tough grader which I was intimidated by at first. If you go to his office hours and talk to him about your papers, he will grade them himself (instead of his TA's) and he will give you a much better score since it shows that you cared and put in the extra effort. Extremely nice guy!
Knowledgeable.  Expert.  Writes textbooks.  Interesting insights.

Very boring. Business history is not a fun topic and if you can get away with it, try taking something else. I thought this class would be about the development of business throughout history. Not so much, several isolated examples with less focus on the big piture. emphasis on early Japan, again not fun. Tough grader!!!
Very knowledgeable and interesting.  Kind of tough, but he knows his stuff and genuinely cares about students.  Very good profession in my opinion.
Nice guy, but really hard grader. I've never recieved a C on a paper until this class. He is so knowledgeable that he expects perfection in papers.
really great
His only 2007 comments:  Nice person.  Pretends he is too sophisticated, but deep down he is human and friendly.  A hard grader, but has interesting insights.  9/10

has a great knowledge & passion for class subject matter - uses multiple forms of media such as audio tapes & picture slides - so in love with himself & arrogant it can be hard to watch - taking classes in business before taking this one might be extra helpful - fair grader - watch your grammar/structure in papers - he's a character

Very pleasant professor.  Walking library of information.  He has experienced so much and is a true historian.  Most brilliant professors I have met lack personality/humor/sympathy, but Dr. Blackford is an exception.  What more can I say, a brilliant man with a great personality.

Terrific professor. He clearly loves the material, and has a pretty interesting and relevant personal past associated with it. Not the easiest grader ever, but he's honest and consistent. He's also really personable, and funny as all get out. Take his classes, you won't regret it.

knowledgable but ignorant. very unprofessional and rude when i try to speak with the TA, he would try and have me stay away and not talk about the tests.he immidiately assumes i didnt read the f-in book.if there are records of identifiying students taking out books from the reserved,they should check it out bc i took out books 2-3 times week.

He was a great prof-very knowledgable-applies history to real life circumstances-uses a variety of teaching tools-video,radio, overheads. A hard grader on papers but will help you if you ask. Definately take him!
For being a Non-Native professor teaching a Native American history class, he was very knowledgeable. He was really nice, and for an upper-division class, it was very fun.
No Comments

Well, I thought Mansel was a pretty neat guy. I stopped by his office hours one time and talked about his Japan travels, which was totally awesome to me, as I am love travel. Very intelligent man, would recommend his classes to all, cute Indiana Jones hat ;)

Wasn't thrilled at having to take a history class, but it was fascinating. I took classes from him in the 80's, have found the knowledge useful many times since-it gives you a perpective from which to analyze business past and present.  The comparative class has been useful too.  Highly recommended!
No Comments
Fascinating guy.  Kinda sexy, for older man.  Don't tell him I said so.  Tries his best at humor.  Showed us pic of when he was 20 year old college student.  Hilarious!
Helpful.  Charming at times.  Witty & urbane.  Publishes many books.  Expert at business history.  Twinkle in eye.  A great listener to sob stories.  Very nice person, lol.
Very laid-back prof. Approachable, very knowledgable. Class was 4 short papers, no exams, which was a plus. Alot of reading, though. One of OSU's best...

I love this guy!   he's an older man who presents his material great....  he has expirienced alot of things right out of history,  and really keeps you interested. i actually liked this class, and he gives you alot of hints for his exams.

Prof. Blanas is a nice guy and is very engaging with passionate students. Obviously very knowledgeable about DBMS. Very poorly constructed slides and lectures though, and generally just not the best teacher. Anything I learned in this class had little to do with his instruction/assignments. Not the worst by any means, but still not great.

I actually really liked Professor Balanas.  The pace of his lectures were fairly slow, but I feel like I understood the material better because of that.  The exams are about what you see on the homeworks.  He's a nice guy, and it's a nice class to be in

Great person, okay lecturer. He's clearly passionate and cares about his students but his lectures don't really align with the content on Carmen, and sometimes it's hard to tell what's going on in class. Like others have mentioned, the slides are pretty random too. The HWs aren't bad, but can't be completed using only Carmen materials.

He would show up late, give a very sporradic lecture never really connected to a common progression. So, I'm not fully sure what I learned this semester despite the A. Notes were provided but they were just as hard to follow and sometimes weren't even his. If I had to teach a course with 5 minutes of prep time I'd do about as well as him, avoid.
Not sure where the bad ratings came from- his commitment to making the student experience positive is very commendable. One of my all time favorite CSE Profs! Not a hard grader as well!
Lots of extra credit, homework/ exams graded fairly. Always asks how we are doing/ if we are enjoying the course. THE GOAT!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Blanas does a great job of ensuring those who want to achieve a high grade can do so. Homework assignments are manageable, exams are fairly graded, and there is plenty of extra credit. He often asks for feedback to ensure students are having a positive experience. Spyros Blanas is one of my all time favorite CSE Profs!
Extremely knowledgeable and competent professor. Keeps classes up to date with current CSE tech. One of the best OSU CSE professors I've had.

Labs were graded fairly and he was nice. I had an A- the whole semester and the only reason I ended with a low grade is because I had to study for another final that was much harder the day before so I bombed this one. Really doable class and kind-hearted man. Lecture was boring tho. Make sure you know how to do the quizzes correctly!
Question and grading is confusing. You don't even know what he want to ask.

Worst professor I have ever met in OSU. If I am not a data analytics student who must take this course, even anyone give me money I will not take this course. Ok, he say sent him email to get adjustment on grading but no feedback. What is meaning for sending email? Waste my time?

I really liked Prof. Blanas as an instructor for this class as he is very knowledgeable about the world of databases and brings a lot of insight to the class. Be prepared to spend a lot of time reading academic papers on databases outside of class, and for a quiz during every class period. Overall I would take a class with Prof. Blanas again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took days/weeks to get back to students with information needed for homework or exam studying. Project requirements sometimes vague with expectation students would take time outside of class to meet with him. Course workload way too heavy for an undergrad. Homeworks did not prepare students for exams. Really knows subject material, good lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Can teach, but unprofessional and presumptuous when interacting with students both during class and office hours. If you like databases you can learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is extremely good at teaching. But not very helpful and expects a lot.

He is really awesome, knowledgable about various aspects of databases! I recommend taking this class if your major is databases or if you are really interested into doing further research on databases.

Hated the class structure, didn't like the way it was managed. Had a very bad experience. I do not recommend taking any class with him, I felt he is trying to promote himself and not to teach the students.
Was good at teaching concepts. However, tests were very hard and require lots of studying outside of class.

She did alright teaching course definitions/material, but her work on example problems was tough to follow, specifically with the complex vector notation that she uses. Teaching wise, she was alright, but her tests are insane. Lots of very long problems in a short amount of time. However, she is a lenient grader and will give partial credit.

Not a good professor. Doesn't explain problems well, skips steps, and doesn't show how she gets her answers. She also packs the curriculum with too many different types of examples, instead of focusing us on certain ones that we can practice over and over. Midterms too long, "study guides" are never helpful, nothing like the test. Very hard class.

She spends too much time explaining the content to the point where I had issues keeping focus, and it hurt my learning than if she went faster. Additionally, the textbook used for the class sucks to keep it honest. Buy or download the Hibbler Dynamics textbook for studying and learning, and use the one she asks for in class to check your homework.

The assignments aren't too hard, the bad thing is most of the grading is done by the TA who takes of a lot of points for simple errors. She also didn't explain why points were taken off so you can't correct your mistake.

Dr. Blevins is a really nice professor and did a good job considering this was her first semester at UT. She explains things very well and she's super sweet and clearly wants everyone to succeed. Her TA can be very difficult with grading and takes many points off each assignment making it hard to succeed.

Dr. Blevins was a great professor. She was brand new this semester at UT (Spring '25) and I feel like she did a great job at teaching a difficult statistics class. 4 quizzes (one of which is dropped), easy coding labs with partners every week, and an individual final project. Grading is done by TA's fully. Would definitely take her again!

Dr. Blevins is a very sweet professor and she is good at teaching. Lectures are important for the quizzes(hardest part in my opinion), but she posts good review slides. Labs are easy, homework is easy. Grading shouldn't be blamed on her since most of it is graded by her TA's. Don't listen to the haters who want an easy A, its not a free class.
nah dog dont do it

Crossing Guad to get to this class, I stopped checking the traffic light, because getting hit felt like luck. Blevins is soft-spoken, like a ghost who ruins your GPA. Grading is random. I've seen casino odds fairer than her rubrics. Came in confident. Left anxious and googling trade schools. Wouldn't recommend unless you're into academic masochism.
i cried over this class multiple times. she made stats unneccesarily complicated. not worth it

Takes off points unecessarily. She doesn't give nearly enough time for quizzes and she takes off a lot of points for small mistakes meaning the grades are always super low. You're better off taking another stats teacher who actually wants you to succeed.
my friend who is a math major (w/ a 4.0) has had to help me out and even with his help she's taken points off for literally no reason. just don't take this class if you want to save your sanity.

Prof Blevins is super nice, but an incredibly harsh grader. Majority of the grade is composed of 4 quizzes (one of which gets dropped), several labs, and a final project. The average on the 2nd quiz was failing and the last quiz was barely passing. Take someone else for stats and save your gpa.
Not worth it

I enjoyed Prof. Blevins class very much. The class isn't that challenging, but it is also not an easy A. You do have to make sure that you come to every class as she takes a grade on attendance, but usually she puts the lecture notes online as well. All quizzes and Exams were open note, but she was often a tricky grader.
he expects you to do the readings, attend class, and participate, but he's genuinely interested in having conversations with students; class does not feel dull.
I do not recommend taking this class just to fulfill a GE

Participation is a major part of the grade in this class. I did not miss a single lecture, but 5.5% of my final grade was deducted for not raising my hand enough in class (which admittedly I only did about 5 times during class). This made the difference between an A and an A- for me. This class was also a little boring and dry.

Beth is really kind and cares about her students! She's great at giving feedback on what you bring her, rather than trying to take over your project (which some studio professors tend to do). She has innovative ideas and tries to push your project further. I would definitely recommend her!

Mixed feelings about her. Ive heard negative things about her as a studio instructor, but she seems like a nice construction person. Often changed due dates to make it easier on students. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Always willing to help on labs. However, labs (charettes) were way too stressful and honestly detrimental to my mental state.

Beth is not the greatest lecturer. She doesn't make any of the material exciting or comprehendible, and its very dry, not to mention her PowerPoints have barely any notes and she breezes through them without repeating herself. The labs are extremely difficult and graded harshly, and since the class is graded by few things, no one I know has an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: GOAT! Highly recommend. She's a top 3 professor I've had at OSU.

Dr. B is a great professor! You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and gets to know them. The lectures are often discussion-based, which I normally don't love but I liked it in this course. I did well on exams even when I didn't feel prepared so you should be fine if you study. She always puts a few extra credit questions.

Dr. B is an awesome professor! 4370 was one of the first health science classes I've actually learned a lot in and I got a lot out of the class. Her exams are very fair, you do need to study a little and take notes in class but nothing unreasonable. Dr. B is very personable and kind and truly wants all of her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Listen take this class if you want to actually learn something. Its not hard if you put in the work or pay attention. I read these reviews before and was scared thinking she would be tough. This is the first professor who genuinely cares that we understand what she's teaching. Worst part about this class was coordinating the group work.

Extremely disorganized and showed up late to class most days including exam days which left us with less time to take the exams which were a lot of extended response. She was unprofessional and kept adding assignments at the very end of the semester. A lot of group work with a lack of time to actually discuss or even meet our group members.

I had high expectations for Dr B, but I was honestly disappointed by her lack of professionalism and felt as though she lacked mutual respect. She would constantly show up to class late and would sometimes even eat as she lectured which was gross. I really felt like this class was at the bottom of her priorities and it took forever to get grades

My favorite professor hands down in all my four years at OSU! Dr. B is a great professor that cares about her students, and allows her students to have their own opinion! You still have to try hard in her class but she gives you the recognition for your hard work! If you had to take one piece of advice from me, GO TO HER TEST REVIEW SESSIONS!

Dr. B is an amazing professor, the bad reviews on here are from her online course. Her in-person lectures are amazing and she makes the tests based on the things you talk about in class, she doesn't reuse old tests. If you go to class and pay attention you will pass if you study the study guide. No need to read the textbook. Group work sucks tho.

Dr. B is probably the best professor the Health Sciences major has to offer. Her class is very straightforward in terms of expectations for assignments/projects and test content. Her exams are very fair. You will succeed if you come to class and listen - the majority of things covered on her tests are very obviously highlighted in lectures.
She was very nice but her lectures were very dry. I could tell she cared about her students and I liked that she was very relatable but her teaching style was not my favorite.

Dr. B is an amazing teacher and such a kind person. If you show up to lecture and pay attention during class you will be just fine. Dr. B is the most understanding and supportive teacher I have had at Ohio State

Professor B is disorganized. Forgets to open modules, forgets to set due dates, gives feedback to a paper you submitted over 2 months later and BARELY ANY direction or instruction of what the assignment or papers are supposed to be. Group work was awful. I was in a group were only 2/5 people actually did work - she didn't care and we barely got anA
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was absolutely horrible. Professor B is very disorganized and not great at teaching. I didn't take anything away from that class material wise. We were forced to complete everything as a group project in groups of 5-6 and she didn't care if only 3 people did all the work. It was so much work for 3 credits. DEFINITELY NOT WORTH IT.
She is so wonderful! I have gotten on her virtual office hours before and we talked about life for almost an hour. She cares so much about her students and is so understanding.

Not accessible outside of class. Very scatterbrained. Showed up unprepared most days to lecture. Exams had info that we did not learn. Just be patient with her. She tries to relate to her students, its just frustrating her all over the place-ness!

One of the best lecturers in the Health Sciences department. Policy was not an easy class but she was always very knowledgable about all of the topics and created a great environment for asking questions. There were a lot of exams but the review sessions helped immensely. VERY slow grader though and policy briefs were a complete disaster.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr B was a caring teacher. However, her online courses were very unorganized and hard to follow. She also had us do a lot of group projects and outside homework that didnt relate to what we were learning in lecture.

If you are a Health Sciences student, you will eventually have Dr. B at some point. I cannot convey how good of a thing that this is. Dr. B has restored my faith in professors with her humor, positive attitude, and care about students. If you give effort and are actively listening during class you will succeed. She rocks!

Dr. B is one of the best professors I've had at OSU. She is young so she relates to you on a friendly level and is very flexible with adjusting due dates during assignment-heavy weeks. She makes lectures interesting and does a great job at highlighting information you will be tested on.

Dr. B is the best! Her lecture style is so relaxed and she condenses the material in a easy to understand way. She's little all over the place sometimes but not in a "you forgot to go over what we SHOULD know" way but more of a "giving a very specific example to help you understand the information better" way. Great prof!

Dr. Bs the best! I also took case studies with her (in class!) and that was great. She makes class really relaxed and discussion based. She really cares about her students and enjoys laughing/making class interesting. I took 3 classes with her and wish I couldve taken more. Shes a fairly new prof so shes kinda a friend and mentor to a lot of us

He only teaches off the textbook and gives no study guides or practice exams before a test so if you want to do well you have to read so much textbook without getting a general idea of what will be on the test. Quizzes were easy exams were very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is extremely boring and almost impossible to pay attention in. He showed up late for my class numerous times (which was only 55 minutes) and would ramble about random things that had nothing to do with law. I would suggest taking a different professor if you can unless you learn well by reading textbooks.

He has lots of interesting stories, but missing some ability to relay info in a way that students can fully grasp. Exams are difficult, even if you understand the concepts from his textbook. They take A LOT of application, some extremely nuanced where I would be stuck between the choice of two answers. Sad bec. I was looking forward to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He calls on people randomly, but no one was ever paying attention because of how boring lecture was. His exams are very tricky and designed to make you fail. He says your study materials are the quizzes but kept them locked after everyone completed them. He was rude sometimes but overall I think he meant well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He has the worst and most boring lectures ever. That being said, he is truly a nice guy if you get to know him. His exams are hard you really have to memorize the book basically. I had to study a lot to get an A in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I have mixed reviews about this class. The exams are tough and it is hard to prepare for it as the questions on the exam can be very niche, but John is a good professor and his stories a very interesting.

Oh god this class was/is awful. If you are anything like me and don't learn well from textbooks DO NOT TAKE BLACKBURN. His lectures are boring, drag on, and are monotone, there are no resources to help prepare for exams outside of weekly quizzes, he was rude to students on a few occasions in my class, and I don't know how I'm going to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
He really cares about his students and will do his at most best to try and be accommodating. Really amazing person, cares a lot about his students and actually wants to help you and understand things.
It is very reading heavy but we also go over it on Lectures.
Exams are the same format as the weekly quizzes and sometimes the same questions.

Blackburns cool and you can tell he's very knowledgeable on the topic hes teaching, but bro is a professional yapper. He will bring up one part from the reading and go on a tangent for 20 minutes unrelated to anything.
The course isn't anything absurd and you can succeed if you work hard. However the professor is an old as dirt, and very rude to students. His attitude is unacceptable to be teaching students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are useless, he gives minimal materials, and the entire class circles around one singular textbook that is unorganized and written entirely by him. Very nice and caring guy, but I cannot believe this course not only exists but is a business req. Tests are horribly made and make up well over 2/3rds of your grade. No one even shows up. Bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class can be boring, but he seems like a genuine professor. I recommend understanding his book. The book is easy to understand. Memorize the cases and their results. He goes over the material in class. Because class was in the evening many students didn't show up (including myself).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He may know what he is talking about, but he is not able to explain it concisely or thoroughly at all. The course structure is set up to make you struggle. I studied so much, went to every lecture, and still got a 60 on the final. The wording is meant to trick you. Basically, do everything you can not to take this class if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof. blackburn is SO kind and cares so much about his students. i spoke to him after probably every single class, and he had so much advice to offer. HOWEVER... this class sucks lol. he really doesn't actually teach you anything during lecture, so you'd be fine just reading the textbook and studying that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clueless class. If I weren't a law nerd, it'd have been tough. The professor rambles about his daughter and nonsense. I only attended the midterm and final—finished both in under 10 minutes (20 & 30 questions). His book is free online. Thought I was on Punk'd after the first lecture.

His lectures are incredibly useless, don't bother showing up to class, all he does is ramble on about randomness. He makes the exams way harder than needed. If you have him and it's still possible I would drop and get a different professor if you care about your GPA at all. Not a bad guy, seems to care about his students but he is a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blackburn's BUSFIN3500 class is a relatively easy one, with weekly writing assignments and open-note exams. While his lectures can be dry, the textbook is helpful. Unstuck study was a great study tool alongside the course materials.
Great professor and person who is very accomplished and qualified. Cares about his students.

He is a very nice guy, but he is very old and doesn't do a great job explaining the content. You basically have to read the entire book but it is probably the easiest textbook I've had to read. The class is based on only tests and a few quizzes so if you get a few questions wrong youre screwed. The test are hard too. Did curve the grade 5% though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is literally impossible. He expects you to read the textbook consistently & listen attentively in lectures, because many times his lectures will contradict the text. Studying does virtually nothing because the exam questions are so open-ended, & there is never a clear answer. He added 5% to everyones grade because we all did so poorly.
All exam based questions are impossible and he doesn't know how to teach at all. He talks very slow and doesnt care about his students at all.
Exams are impossible. Had an A going into the final and finished with a B-.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course was fine. Only graded by quizzes (which he gives answers for during class) and exams. You need to purchase one of his physical textbooks to succeed. I went to all the lectures but would have been perfectly fine if  I didn't. Course was fine, just boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fairest class participation grading system I ever encountered
Don't bother going to lecture because you won't learn anything. Grade is based off a few exams and you get no material to study so good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blackburn was a really nice guy, and his lectures were cool but he does go off-topic sometimes. His quizzes and tests are directly pulled from the textbook, and they were all so easy, as long as you read the textbook. However, the final was a mess :( and was not representative of what we learned at all IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was so stressful simply because his tests and quizzes were designed to trick you. Pay attention to every word in the question. Dont bother going to class, his lectures dont help because he always goes off track and rambles. Entire grade is made up of a few quizzes and two exams- no extra credit.
Lectures were monotonous and uncaptivating. Quiz questions were subjective. Hard to get good feedback or clarification. Entire grade determined quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty straightforward and easy class format. If you give an effort on the papers, you'll get 100%. Textbook is helpful for exams, but I didn't read it completely nor attend lecture/recordings. I've heard that he will restructure this class in the future because the grades are too high and this was used during COVID.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Short writing assignments every week that he gives 100% for if you give any effort. Strongly suggest reading the textbook and highlighting it because his in-person sessions are focused on discussion more than direct teaching. Open book exams were nice as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this during Fall of 2021. This class was an easy A. He gave 100% on each of the papers you write, and I learned about the current situation with law due to that you know. He sometimes wanders off track from the content, and will ramble a bit about his lawyer days, but since the material so easy I don't mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class. One weekly written assignment that everyone gets full credit for. Open note mid term and final exams. Lectures are recorded, and also has in person discussions which arent as useful imo. Great guy, a little dry. Do everything and youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Blackburn made our grades simple to complete and was very lenient with due dates. He is a great professor who really knows what he is talking about. Take his online section if you're able to!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: John is by far the best professor at Ohio State! He actually cares about the material and his students. Only gave 7 writing assignments so it was a nice break from all the other businesses courses. By far the best class I have taken! Please take him for BUSFIN3500 he is definitely the best option.

Professor Blackburn is a gem. He is such a kind person. His class was very easy he graded based on seven short written assignments worth 14 points each. He responds to email quickly if you ever have a question and he is super understanding. He is very down to earth! If you have a chance take legal environment with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures not required during COVID semesters, all you have to do is write 200-400 word responses each week. Most of the responses are opinion pieces so you don't really have to even watch the lecture videos. Seemed like a nice guy, super easy class, exactly the "break" we all needed during such a stressful semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy grader. Not many assignments, and no exams. I so enjoyed the difficulty of this class, especially during COVID when it seemed like all my classes got substantially harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had him online because of COVID. Only grades in class: 7 short ( each 200-400 words, worth 14 pts) essays, 1 due every week, and 1 Get-to-Know-You assignment for 2 pts. I got an A just by reading from the book. Good prof to take for 3500 if you're not looking to become a lawyer - teaches you the stuff you should be aware of without pressure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance to lectures and participation are the only things you get graded on, so make it a point to attend. Read and take good notes of his book, because even though it's participation, he often looks for specific answers. Don't let your points get docked for missing conceptual questions he throws out during class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: funny professor. 50% showing up to class 50% final. as long as you read the assigned readings and answer the questions that go with them, the test will be extremely easy.

Quite a bad professor, doesn't let you take notes by computer and look at you phone. Lecture is quite boring, makes class time quite a struggle to pass through. If you caught using your phone, he will unhesitatingly pick you out and put you to shame in the entire class while deducting a letter grade from your 50% worth participation grade

So far as you done the reading and go to class, you will be fine for most of the time. Quite a good teacher in terms of lecture. Just be careful he can be quite strict with using phones. You have been warned guys

He's such a sweet professor & means well. His class isn't that difficult it's pretty straight and to the point but you have to pay attention in class cause he pulls stuff directly from class for the exam. But study the stuff from the book and in class and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He is such a sweet professor - loves the subject matter and while it can be dry at times, he is randomly hilarious and the class is easy. Mostly common sense. Only one final exam and it was also super easy, just make sure you keep up on your readings and youll be fine. Come to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is an interesting guy and tries to make his lectures more fun. Tests can be difficult, but if you read the book and pay attention to his examples in lecture they're not that bad.

He refuses to use Canvas, so that makes things just so convenient (not). Occasionally spends over half the class telling a story that doesn't even clearly answer the question that was asked. One of the exams had 6 questions all based on one single line of the text that we did not focus on in class. Overall, avoid this prof.
ABSOLUTELY HORRIBLE PROFESSOR. WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN IN OSU
Dr. Blackburn is such a great guy! He cares about his students and tells funny stories in class. However, there is a lot of material shoved into 7 weeks. Overall, I would take him again.
He is so dry and rambly 4 tests in seven weeks so about the most minute of details and all cumulative No new info between third and fourth for some reason Ca real pain
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: John Blackburn was and is one of the great Professors at The Ohio State University. He kept you engaged and made Business Law intriguing, which I believe is very hard to do.

Professor Blackburn is the most easy going professor in the fisher college of business. If you look over the notes he emails to you, you will pass all the exams. Have fun and enjoy. Everyone usually gets A in his class. This one is a breeze.

Blackburn is probably your best option when it comes to taking law at OSU. This semester he did 4 exams, all worth 25%, including a cumulative final. Getting his book is a necessity, but he tells you what to read for each class so there isn't too much reading if you keep up with it. Lectures are boring but he randomly called on people occasionally.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Blackburn is an oldie, but a goodie. He follows an old-fashioned form of teaching (ex. No canvas), but his material is not difficult to learn and apply. Of course the class is over business law, but his character and stories make the lectures enjoyable. Not much reading to do, but make sure to actually study for exams because material can overlap.

The reason I did bad in this class is because I didn't want to buy the $50 book for a 1.5 credit half semester class. You will not do well with out the book. His lectures are examples from his experiences related to what the content in the book is. 95% of the exam is from the book, not lecture. Also, the only two grades are the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Read his textbook over and over again to prepare for his tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: John Blackburn is a pleasant person to talk to but is not good when it comes to teaching. When I took the class, the whole thing was graded on just two exams so if you fail both, well you're done for class. To me, lecture wasn't very helpful as he just went over what was written in the textbook. The two exams were challenging as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: People leave bad reviews on here, but if you put a little bit of effort into the class, you will be fine. Blackburn has done this his whole life and co-wrote the book, so he knows what he is talking about. Listen to him in class as he will go over scenarios that will be test questions. Read the book and outline it for the exams and you'll be fine.

I'm a junior and have never gotten less than an A in any class at Ohio State, but this is the one class that challenged me. I skipped class, but shouldn't have because listening to his rambles still helped. And you should try on the midterm even thought the final can be your only grade. basically memorize the textbook from front to back and notes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Horrible. Grades solely depend on the two exams. Riskyyyyy

This dude is a character & I loved him somewhat. Takes his time to get to class & talks about somewhat relevant stuff but it's hard to pay attention. 3 exams. If u do well on 1st 2  u wont have to take final. You'll probably take final. Entire class showed up to final. Cram 8 chapter book before final. My final  exam was C- & was bumped to a B-
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His class is simply POINTLESS! Lectures are 100% not needed, & about 10% of the class will show up. Exams are 100% of your grade and T/F & MC only. Almost everyone in our section got 50-75% on exams. Take another professor and save yourself the time and effort studying for his ridiculous exams. You'll teach yourself more about law than he ever will

Blackburn is a character. just sortof rambles on in lecture about what he feels (some of this stuff ends up on exams).  Grade was two midterms and an optional final, where the final can replace one or both midterms if it is higher.  Read the textbook well and pay close attention to T/F questions.  No office hours by appointment. Go to class

Professor Blackburn is a nice man and he shared personal experiences with the class that I enjoyed. That being said, he was not a very good teacher. From previous reviews of his class, it seems as if he has changed the formatting every semester. My debate and essay final was new this semester, and possibly unsuccessful. Late, ill-prepared, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Overall, I cannot complain. He mumbles and bumbles during lecture about random bs, but he was kind enough to put out a book, realized Pearson was making it too expensive, cancelled the contract and sold it for 200 dollars less. I respect him for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Didn't find the lecture helpful. He doesn't really talk about things that were exam related. Mainly talks about his opinions on law but test questions that were worded archaically and very standardized test like. I was one question away from a half a letter grade up. Going over test questions in class doesn't really help, I'd recommend office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Blackburn is by far the most entertaining and cooky professor I've had at Ohio State. We had two exams and an optional final. All were pretty tough but you can get by pretty well if you study his textbook. His lectures are a treat. Don't be afraid to ask about some of his questions/answers on exams, he gave our class back points for doing so.

He's okay. Tends to ramble in lecture. Make sure you read and understand the book. Grades consisted only of two midterms, which can be tricky, and an optional final. The final can only help in that it will replace any and all scores you did better on it  than both midterms. I got a B on both midterms, but got an A on the final and for the course.

The entire grade is based on a few exams (which are short multiple choice tests). If you don't like to read and are not good at memorizing text, then you will struggle. I did well by just reading the chapters over and over again before the exams. Reading  the book is all you need to do to get a good grade; you don't  have to pay attention in class.

This class was very unorganized. He sent out a one page syllabus via email because he did not open Carmen until after the first exam.  The only material you get to help study is the textbook.  The only grades are exams. Exams are very specific questions from the text.  His lectures are long, confusing, and not really over the content of the class.

Professor Blackburn changes up the way he runs the class every semester. This semester, there was 2 midterms and an optional final. To do well on them, you basically have to know business law like the back of your hand by reading the book very carefully (which he wrote). The lectures weren't mandatory and he basically rambles the whole time.

The tests are kind of tricky, but keep in mind that there is a curve and the dude understands that we're college students. In short, the grade you work for is the one you'll get. He's fair and knows what he is doing. Just show up on time and go to class and you'll do fine.

The lectures are lengthy and he tends to ramble so there's little point in attending. The class consisted of 5 quizzes worth 20 points each for a total of 100 points. Each point missed is 1% off your grade. A very difficult bonus quiz for 20 points is given at the end though which can help, but be ready to read quite a bit.
Super cool guy and definitely makes you think. The class isn't easy but it is very doable if you put the work into it and study for his quizzes. Go to class and read the book for sure.
The class is not helpful, but the exam is easy if you read the book.

Chapters are 40 pages long, each exam covers one chapter. You have to read through it very well or you won't do well. Each exam consists of 16 questions, there is only 3 exams, do mhe in more than one and you may be getting a B. He is a good guy, and gives extra credit opportunity. If you are smart or work hard you will get an A for sure
Only grades in the class were weekly quizzes, followed by a tricky bonus quiz.

Think of Walter White before he "broke bad" with a better sense of humor and you have John Blackburn. The dude is a legend. We received a bonus point for each class we attended (adds to 15 bonus points) and the class is only out of 60 points, so I ended up with over a 100% in the class. Without the bonus points the class would be kind of tough.

The set up of this class changes every session so don't be surprised when it's different than when your friend took it. He's very clear and has a dry sense of humor but kept you engaged .  Rambles a lot. Attending lecture will help your grade and all the questions come from the textbook which he explains in lecture. Overall very good.
He is very dry and boring; did not give my class much extra credit so I ended up with an A-. If you go to class and do the readings, theres no reason you shouldn't get at least a B+

Prof Blackburn was awesome. His lectures are slow, but his 'tests' that are just quizzes are easy. Most of the ViaResponse questions given in class are on the quiz. If you get under a 13 on any of the quizzes, just do the extra credit assignment. It can increase your grade by 10%. Also, he's got a sense of humor. A weird one, but he's good hearted.

I got a C on all three quizzes because they're out of fifteen points (though they come straight from lecture - hard to interpret answer during class sometimes).  Went to every class (credit for attendance) and wrote extra credit paper (five pages, choice topic, really easy) and got a 94.  You go John.

reading is really a big deal for business law, and you have to truly understand the reading in order to get a good grade. I did poorly on all three quiz and got a B- at last. But i am actually satisfied, because i thought i will fail this class. So B- is much better than D. Blacki gave full point of extra credit, but its a 10 pages long paper.
final grade is 3 exams each 15 questions that are rather confusing and meant to trick you up. very nice guy though just hard to understand
nice guy

"Blacki" is a very good teacher who clearly outlines what is important for the class.  Class consists of 3 quizzes all MC worth 15 pts each, 5 pts participation, and a 10 point extra credit paper. As long as you read, pay attention in lecture, and do the extra credit, it will be the easiest A you've ever had in Fisher.
His 3 exams are non cumulative and consist of 15 MC questions. There are usually a couple tricky ones but if you read the book (which he wrote) and pay attention in class they are super easy.

“Blacki" is a funny guy and nice enough to record attendance even for those who're late. grade is entirely based on 3 quizzes (15 mc question each,not cumulative).Not too hard to pass the average grade. Attendance is taken using viaresponse every class. You'll only need to read 3 chapters in total for 7 wks, which is not bad at all.

Quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had, not just in college but going all the way back to my pre-school days.  I would say bad words to describe her but it won't let me.  Don't take her, she is the worst.  She doesn't teach.

I had Bonnie for BUSOBA 2320 and 2321. The BUSOBA department is the absolute worst organized department in Fisher, if not the entire school. I swear Bonnie Schroeder and Terry Klinker saw what Marc Smith was doing, copied it but made everything worse. For the love of all things holy, my final exam building/room was locked and I could not get in.

She teaches everything completely different from the STAT 1430 class and makes everything exceptionally more difficult than it needs to be. I swear she chooses to teach the most difficult ways to reach an answer. I don't understand why she teaches things different from the 1st stat class, makes everything 10x harder to understand.
she makes me want to kms

Gambled away my health for an A. Not worth it. This class is unnecessarily stressful and at the end of the semester I got tinnitus from the stress of this course. Please do extra credit hw and don't believe anyone who says the group cases were easy. They were the bums of their group.

Hearing all the horror stories about this course, I entered with the mindset that time & effort would get me through it smoothly. I was wrong. This was by FAR the hardest & most time-consuming class I have taken in my 3 years at OSU. I cried as I studied for each exam. Bonnie makes everything horrifyingly confusing. Please do the HW extra credit.

this class was a living nightmare. there was about 10% of students who truly knew what they wad doing. whatever u do do not take it by her. She is a terrible teacher. my friends was able to explain the topics better than she ever did. Truly the worst course to take at fisher TRUST ME.  My grade was a b only becasue of the homeoworks
There is a lot of extra credit, and the exams are not as hard as everyone says. However, the lectures are incredibly boring, and one should expect to learn everything on their own.

While her lectures can be hard to pay attention to, the class itself is very well organized, has plenty of opportunities for extra credit, and the exams are extremely fair. She gives plenty of leeway when it comes to earning credit (HWs, extra test questions for bonus, etc.) and gives a few excused absences.

Bonnie's lectures are boring but they are not as bad as people say. If you choose to actively pay attention and try, you will succeed. The content is not difficult; it mimics AP Statistics. Bonnie's teaching is very confusing as she makes the content more complex. There is a ton of extra credit and leeway built into this class.

Quite possibly the worst course I have ever taken at any level of my education. The homework had typos and errors ever week. Bonnie did not submit grades on time and took several days after the hard deadline to post them, JUST TO GET THEM WRONG and email every student that they need an EXTRA WEEK to fix them. We pay 35 thousand a year for this bs?

Ok hear me out. This course is hard. However, Bonnie gives you lot of opportunities to succeed in this class (6% extra credit + curves). If you can build some strong study habits and come to class already having a pretty solid understanding of the material you will do very well. I hated statistics coming into this class, but now I actually like it.
Class kinda annoying basically teach the whole class to yourself. Honestly if you put in the work it's really not that bad.

Worst professor I've had at this school. Was very disinterested and rude during office hours, and she showed little willingness to actually teach students. Exams were challenging, lectures were uninspiring, and the three group projects lacked proper guidance. Tenured, out of touch, and a poor representation of this institution.

Had her for analytics and liked her much better. My TAs were english as a second language which made learning much more difficult. Your group mates are hit or miss on their quality and who grades your project has a big impact on the grade. Schroeder is a nice lady, but boring, just envision your grandma teaching you stats.
Just don't
Bonnie hates her students
Boring lecturer that makes everything much harder than it should be.

Incredibly boring and bad lecturer.The subject matter really shouldn't be that hard, but Schroeder essentially forces you to learn everything on your own as attending lecture was basically useless. I also remember her scolding some people for leaving lecture early even though attending is not required. I don't blame them for leaving early.

Bonnie has an old-school style of teaching that to me was very hard to learn from. You learn more from recitation than any lecture. You are required to watch lecture videos before lecture, then attend lecture where she talks about the same things, and goes on and on and in general, is not nice to students. I would not recommend.
Worst professor at Fisher. Her lectures are all over the place, and I don't think she ever got through all the slides. Exam averages are constantly 70 or below. Needs to retire.
Only take Bonnie if you hate yourself

Bonnie is REALLY BAD at teaching statistics, and I find the group cases to be pretty hurtful overall. I only did well in the class because most of the course content is in AP stats. The class is the poorest put-together I've ever been a part of. Exams start 30 mins after the scheduled exam time. Would not recommend unless you got a 4-5 on ap stats.
I have to say she is the most awful professor I have ever met. She does not explain our confusing group case grade even after class.

By far, one of the most difficult classes I've taken at OSU. Group cases aren't awful, but the exams are tough. Make sure you understand the conceptual aspects opposed to understanding the math (still try to understand the math. The conceptuals take up a large majority of the exam questions.

The worst teacher I've had in my time throughout college. Watching lecture videos and attending in person lectures only confuses you more. She could be teaching simple addition and still confuse her students. Group Projects aren't bad and plenty of points from homework/lecture quizzes. Take another professor if at all possible.
I don't know why Mrs. S has a low rating, she is 10x better than any other professor teaching these courses.
Can hardly understand the way she speaks as she thinks we are still in the 1980s and can't seem to make sense in any of her lecture videos.
Bonnie is the worst professor I've ever had. She expects you to learn very advanced material practically on your own and makes finding support almost impossible

It astonishes me on how you can be a teacher but know so little about actually teaching. The only business she needs to be taking care of is finding another job. Being inside an iron lung is easier than sitting through her class.

Bonnie's lectures can be pretty confusing, but you can get through this class with some effort. The TAs are a big help, and tools like unstuckstudy ai and the textbook make studying easier. Attend class, do the work, and you'll likely get a decent grade.
Just rude!

Extra credit is offered for doing the weekly homework, doing these without statcrunch will help prepare you for exams. I also highly suggest looking over the optional practice (at least the multiple choice portion) to study. Professor Schroeder did a great job and is extremely helpful in office hours and class, you just have to meet her halfway.

Her lectures are the most confusing things in the world, she thinks she is teaching to masters students not people who don't know the content. Worst professor in the entire school and Im not sure how she has a job since everyone hates her.
horrible professor. hasn't used a recently recorded lecture video in ages. bonnie makes everything a lot more confusing

I don't know how Bonnie still has a job after all these bad reviews. She doesn't care about students learning the material at all. If you want any help at all in this class you have to go to the TAs and even then they aren't sure on most stuff. Cstate use to teach this class for credit but Bonnie like always got the university to stop that.

I created an account simply to warn you of the dangers of attending a Bonnie Schroeder lecture.I have PTSD and have awoken several times throughout the middle of the night shaking and crying thinking about monotone,  low energy, empty content lectures.If you have the option to take the class with a non-english speaking professor choose that instead

I don't like to say mean things about professors who seem like nice people, but I have never experienced a worse teaching experience in my entire life. Everything she teaches is made much harder than it should be to understand, while her lecture videos and lectures are both confusing and incredibly monotonous.

Worked really hard in this class to get an A-. Group projects are so hard because nobody understands unless you go to office hours. TAs make this course easier, Bonnie makes it harder. Do your homework, it counts as like 5% extra credit.

Bonnie is a sweet lady, but in my opinion BUSOBA 2320 is a class that she makes quite difficult. She tends to over-explain every topic instead of the baseline knowledge for the exams. Everything you learn in this class tends to relate to real world examples and the 3 group cases you have to do during the course.

Bonnie is not as bad as people put her out to be. She is very knowledgeable about the content, but sometimes I feel like she is too smart to be teaching it at such a basic level. The material is very difficult, but Bonnie does her best to make it clear so that way we can actually learn something. The group cases are a huge hassle though
so hard for no reason

The only reason I have a good grade right now in the class is because of the extra credit you get from homework. Her lectures are soooo long and takes the first half to go over the notes she didnt get to the previous class so it seems like your always playing catchup. The 3 Group projects sucked because no one knew what they were doing.

Bonnie is a kind person, but she is the worst teacher I have ever taken in my life. The lecture videos are the most confusing things ever. Organic Chemistry Tutor and Khan Academy WILL be your best friend. Pray that you have a good TA because Bonnie makes learning this stuff absolutely infuriating. Good luck.

Bonnie was hands down the worst professor I have ever had at Ohio State. Her lecture videos are the most confusing monstrosities to ever exist. Watching them and studying for hours did not help me a single bit as I still struggled. It feels discouraging to ace every class, spend more time in statistics, and are unable to perform well in statistics.

This class took so much time and effort. It is much harder than 1430. If you dont know your terminology (which there is tons of) you will struggle. Its not so much Bonnie being a bad teacher, there is just tons of work not considering you have 4-5 other classes you are taking. Spent 6 hours a week outside of class and still was confused every week.

I spent the whole fall semester of my sophomore year watching her lecture videos. She is not good at teaching the content of the course. The only good thing about this course is that the homework is extra credit. I would never recommend her as a teacher.

I took this class twice, the 1st time i took it was spring of my sophomore year, I was taking a handful of other classes and stopped trying for this class and ended with a D+. The 2nd time I took it was summer going into my senior year, while working a 40+ hr internship I was able to become more committed to the class and ended w/ over a 100%.

F
Bonnie
Schroeder

Worst professor I've ever had and the is the sole reason this course is so hard. Her lectures make no sense and every class is forced to use them. You will have to teach yourself all the concepts yourself. I have no clue how this woman still has a job. Does not give answers in lecture either.

In my opinion, this class was easier than STAT-1430. The majority of this class is hypothesis testing, understanding when to reject and not to reject null hypothesis. So definitely understand hypothesis testing, it will be the case studies and the exams.

VERY generous professor, a ton of easy extra credit opportunities. The best way to ace the exams and case studies is go back and study the homework/quizzes from MyLab. If you do this and write down the equations/concepts on your formula sheet which she allows you to use on your exam, you will at least get a B in this class.

Extreme disconnect between online video lectures, in-person recitation, and the questions presented on the test. Expects you to be able to use statcrunch with minimal explanation and then doesn't allow it on tests. Requires two group projects which are fundamentally incompatible with the way a math class should work.

Overall bad experience.

Professor Schroeder does a fine job at explaining the material. There is mandatory attendance for lectures and recitations, but you are allowed to miss a few. Do the homework for extra credit! As long as you grind out the group projects and study this class is doable! I was able to finish with above a 100, so an A is definitely doable!

Bonnie is a nice person, I read the reviews before I took this course and got Draper for Lec. while having Bonnie for Rec. She's reasonable but I just never spoke during class. Overall, she does need to retire, she literally taught my father back in the early 90's. Aside from this, do good on the group cases, HW, and quizzes as that IS THE CURVE.

Bonnie is actually not that bad. When you talk to her after class, you will know she's actually a really nice person. The concepts are really boring and hard, but there are lots of extra credits opportunities. Be ready to finish the group case ASAP, there will be lots of people during the office hours if you start it late.
Bonnie taught this very easy class really well. She explained all concepts well and gave opportunities for extra credit. Great professor to take for this class.

Bonnie doesn't deserve all the hate she gets as a professor. She knows the material well and does her best to explain it when concepts are difficult. If you approach her after or outside of class, she is very sweet and answers all questions. Her lectures can be dry at times so be careful there. She builds a lot of grade forgiveness into the class.

Bonnie Schroeder needs to be removed from the Fisher staff. At least in the capacity she currently teaches in. I could see how she may not be as terrible for statisticians/math majors, but she cannot relate to low level statistics students comprehension. The material is already difficult enough as is. We as students need to take action against her.
Extremely difficult, mandatory attendance, yet completely useless. I guessed my way through this class. Thank god for the extra credit.

The class is standardized, so I don't know if another professor would've helped. 40 EC points from HW and extra 10 from info sheet and volunteering available (do if you want to pass). Group project are very confusing so ask TAs for help. Heavily relies on statcrunch but can't use for exams. Able to use note sheet for exams but only helps so much.

2 section tests that you were able to use your online resources. This helps you understand the material throughout the year but not when it comes to exam time, where you have to teach everything you learned a different way. Extra credit helps. Would have failed with out it. A great professor would have changed my outlook on this class. Never again

This class is unnecessarily hard. My biggest advice is to get an early start on the 3 case studies because if you wait- you'll be sitting in office hours surrounded by 50+ equally confused classmates. The case studies are graded super harshly but TAs help out a lot. The HW is also very hard but is extra credit. Go to lecture & recitation for pts!

This professor is awful. For the group case, one of her files shows that we should put the page with our signature as the FIRST page. However, another file requires us to use it as the LAST page. She can never go through all of her slides in class (she got 30 slides but she just talked about 20 of them). Don't choose her as your professor, RUN!

Avoid this professor at all costs. If you're teaching hard material, then you should try to help your students as much as possible, not leave them hanging before exams that make up a large portion of your grade. This class is so disorganized and chaotic. Terrible all-around.

Recitation class, she is one of the worst lecturers. If you did not like 1430 it will be a struggle. Just try to take Draper, there is not enough space in this review to complain well enough.

I will say if she still has "optional homework" DO IT, that is the curve, there is no curve.

All of the assignments are graded tough

Overall, this was an unnecessarily difficult course. You'll need to know how to utilize Stat Crunch and Excel for most assignments but the exams are entirely paper and pencil. I would recommend completing any extra credit and optional work as lecture videos and lecture itself provide very few examples, which is my main complaint with this class.

Horrible professor. Anyone who says the reviews here are overexaggerated, are simply lying to you. This class is only 3 credit hours, but trust me when I saw this: Treat it like a 4 or 5 credit hour class. The average student will need to dedicated at least 12-15 hours/week outside of class to at least get a C.

Easily the worst professor in Fisher. She adds so many extra steps to this class. This class is already difficult, but she makes it more so.

I was a 4.0 student up until I had her. If CSCC still offered this class, I would've taken it there. Sadly, she was the only available option to me at OSU.

Students were doing fine with recorded lectures by other teachers. The act of making class attendance mandatory went against what she declares in syllabus; you cant trust this class structure. Would definitely recommend terry klinker over her anyday.

This class expects you to teach yourself advanced statistics in itself. There is mandatory attendance, group cases, and weekly homework on statcrunch, whereas you can't use statcrunch on exams. Don't miss any extra credit opportunities. A very difficult class.

Never seen such a bad professor. Students did not understand her lectures in class and had to watch the videos when they got home. But she then canceled posting videos on the Carmen made by other teachers because of less attendance. Then, my grade gradually went down to C.
