I am taking this course as an audit.  The class is enjoyable and informative.  Dr.  Byram is knowledgeable and organized.  To get the most out of this class, it is best to be prepared and participate.

She is so boring.  Boring. Boring. Boring. WOW don't go to lecture. I literally signed the attendance and then left after the pop quiz (if there was one). All of her slides are online and so are the films. I read one of the five books she assigned and still got A's on the essays.

20% of your grade is based on attendance and pop quizzes, 40% on two essays, and the remaining 40% is the final. High-stakes, but the material is engaging and the essays are actually pretty short. Just be sure to read and show up for class.

She really loves the course she teaches and definitely wants her students to do well in the course.  Make sure you pay attention, take notes, and SHOW UP TO CLASS. She gives in-class pop quizzes so make sure to finish the required reading for the day before you show up and if you miss, make sure you are caught up in the films. PARTICIPATE!!!
She's a very reasonable and likable professor.  Shows a lot of films so it is easy to doze off.. but pay attention to the details!
Interesting person.  Truly cares about her students, but she does want them to learn a lot, so it can be difficult.  As long as you take good notes and participate, you shouldn't have a problem.

She is very passionate and cares about giving students a good education. Listens to feedback on the class and is a clear lecturer. A bit of a tough grader but if you pay attention and can write well you'll be fine. Really nice person overall.

The books and movies watched in class were interesting and overall I enjoyed the class. The essay grading was a bit tough and the feedback was unclear and unhelpful. The only reason I got an A in the class is because I aced the final. Attend lecture because of in class quizzes!
VERY hard grader. Do not recommend as a GEC.

She is a very hard grader, if you do not write exactly what she thinks you WILL get tons of points taken off. The class is only out of 100 points so it is difficult to do well. Do not recommend as a GEC.
Awful. If don't write exactly what she thinks, which is sometimes impossible to decipher, you get a million points off.
Easy class, but tough/annoying grader. If you don't say almost exactly what she believes or wants you will get points taken off. Does random things in class like run around and says random things.

She is by far the best professor I have ever had. She's always willing to go more than out of the way to help students if asked. She is a fantastic teacher, very intelligent, compassionate, and always looking to do better.

Very easy class as long as you do most of the readings and attend most of the classes. Movies and books were interesting but the subject matter can be upsetting at times. As long as you pay attention it is very easy to get an A.

She knew so much about the content and was really interested in what one liked and didn't like how the class was going and offered to change things if necessary. I recommend this class to everyone that is ready to face the Holocaust in detail.

I did 20% of reading,but I write well.No focus/prssure on each indiv. person,u could simply raise ur hand whn you'd like.She was very welcomng of different opinions-i noticd even the essays were "do u feel ___ occurred yes or no&explain why w/exmpls or quotes."NOT strictly "expln this".Cares about ur view! Answers emails.Kept "order" in the class.

This class seems like it should be really interesting, but the way that she conducts lectures is terrible. very very repetitive. the final exam is short answer and one long essay. your answers have to repeat back the statements/opinions she expressed in class. you're opinions or interpretations mean nothing.
Very good prof., I would recommend this class to anyone!

She may have had interest in the subject, but she clearly did not explain that to us.  It is frustrating that in a class that deals with such a sensitive subject she did not give any personal accounts of why she was teaching.  Her lectures were misguided, and her exams were detail specific.  The books/films were great, but she was useless.

It's obvious she has immense knowledge of literature but her incompetency of how to conduct a class, let alone a discussion is overwhelming. Answer questions as she would answer them as your opinion seems useless.

You have to go to class bc all her tests revolve around lecture material and the books you have to read. Test were 2 essay's and short answer. Very straight forward. Take the class if you can handle reading 50+ pages a night

Great professor, very serious and sometimes not very compassionate, but overall a great teacher. This class is a lot of reading, as well as a weekly essay, but because of the high number of grades, it isn't too hard to do well. Good, interesting class, definitely recommend this professor.
Katra rocks... if you are generally interested in learning, she is a great Prof.
No Comments

Prof Byrne is super cool. The reading might be a bit much sometimes and sometimes you can probably just skim but to get the most out of each class you should probs just do it. If you can, integrate Twilight into the discussion as often but as casually as possible. She'll love that.

I just took this class because it seemed like a manageable amount during Zoom University, but it ended up being my favorite class. Women's voices are important, and it was great getting to read women sharing their own stories. I couldn't believe that this was the first class I had learned about some of these topics

I really enjoyed the books we read and watching the lecture videos. Some of the assigned readings were challenging, but she did a great job of explaining both the arguments and the context in the short lecture videos. The class was asynchronous because of COVID, but I wish I could have been in the classroom with Professor Byrne
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Not my favorite. For a 3 credit course, she over works her students. Soo much reading its insane. Her grading is very vague and shes a ROUGH grader. I did pretty well in the class, but if youre looking for a GE, I would look elsewhere. She also didnt grade like anything until week 10 and is super slow to grade anything
A solid 1152 professor overall.

I thought he was really a helpful professor and he did a good job of pointing things out in his notes that the test makers will try to trip you up on. I like that he puts practice problems in his notes and he has been super nice and helpful whenever Ive asked him any questions. The class goes pretty fast but thats not his fault thats just 1172.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring voice and too fast

He was okay at explaining things, but personally I found recitations to be more useful in this class. He posts his full notes online after every lecture which was nice. I'd still recommend going to lectures so you can see him work the problems out. The textbook is free and online.
Dr. Heersink is a very kind and cool professor who cares about his students success. He explains things very fundamentally making it easier to understand topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Heersink is a very good professor, he is very helpful in his recitation and office hour. He posts notes for every lectures, which are very helpful. The pace of this class is very fast, and the material is hard overall. If you want to get a good grade, you really need to spend A LOT OF TIME after class. Overall a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A little bit awkward but that does not affect the teaching. Puts his filled out notes online after class and takes time to solve and explain questions students have. It can also be discerned he is very talented in mathematics. He is a good choice, no problems here.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He knows his stuff for sure, but he's a little awkward. He would call people out for not paying attention or talking too much, which was a little weird. But he was a nice guy and cared about the students.

Probably one of the worst econ profs at osu. Took both intermediate econ and financial aspects of international trade with him and did not get much out of the classes. His lectures are unclear and he basically tells us what will be on the test. Easy A cause of the latter, but intellectually, you miss out.

I've never seen a professor so incapable of teaching in my four years at OSU. His availability for office hours is one hour a week, which he usually cancels. Exams and quizzes are straight from the problem sets (he'll change numbers). If you plan on skipping class, just get the book because it's word for word what he puts on the chalk board.

Teaches above pre-requisites. Expected us all to know Calculus 3 , when the class was only supposed to be up to Calc 1. Copies the textbook on to the board, few explanations. Moves very fast. Worst professor I have ever had in my 3 years. You teach yourself with the book. Would avoid at all costs.

Overall, this was a waste of my money. He doesn't teach you anything. He copied and pasted the book onto the chalk board. He doesn't explain the concepts. He move so very fast and expects you to know exactly what he is talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Though he may not be a great teacher, he seems like he would like to give everyone in the class an A.  He uses a lower grading scale than the standard OSU scale and he literally tells the class what is going to be on the exams/quizzes while he's writing it on the board! Buying the textbook is a waste of money, all you need is your notes to study.

Just one thing u need to remember: never skip any class. Everything on the test was based on lecture. Just write everything he wrote on the board and u will be fine. Btw, don't trust his TAs,they are just graduate students and know nothing about this course.

He's South Korean so his accent is hard to get past at first, however after you get use to it there isn't much difficulty understanding (took me 2 classes). He will tell you what style of question will be on the tests and quizzes but change them up a bit. His class is very hard, you will have to study and do practice problems. He knows his stuff!

literally cannot understand a thing he says, spends entire class writing notes he took from textbook. just repeats what the textbook says and does not explain concepts or anything. worst econ professor i've ever had. had to read the textbook to try and teach myself, and by then it was too late. test are hard too.

i got an A- in his class, this guy does not know how to teach, its that simple, he tries but that's as far as he gets. just goes to the board with chalk and writes down stuff moving from left to right, back turned. I taught myself the whole course by doing his practice problems and reading the book, if you don't have that drive don't take him.
Worst econ professor I've ever had. Tough grader. Boring lectures. Basically you're just copying lecture notes from the blackboard. Choose other classes if you don't want to ruin your GPA.
His teaching style is merely by writing out notes on the board without explaining them. He also grades very harshly. He is not interested in helping students who email him or ask him for help.
He simply doesn't know how to make lectures interesting. Copying lecture notes directly from the textbook... Not flexible at all and there's no incentive to go to class.
Worst professor I have ever had.  I have never seen someone so incapable of engaging the class.
Simply doesn't know how to engage the class in lecture. Studying just from your notes didn't seem to be enough for the exams and quizzes. Must teach yourself from the textbook.

He's not an AMAZING professor, but not a 1.0 in my book. His presentations are pretty clear, the struggle is knowing what to focus on for quizzes/tests. You may have to use the ELC, but honestly I haven't really not had to for a class anyway. I wouldn't go out of my way to take his class of course, but don't freak out if you have to take him.
Simply reads off slides and talks to the ground. Completely incapable of engaging students as an instructor should. His lectures are like an audiobook of the textbook. You must teach yourself.

I have never been more disappointed in a professor in my time at OSU. Less than half of the class attended lecture because he was so hard to understand. I would consider myself a pretty good student( over 3.5 gpa) but my only hope in the class has been trying to teach the material to myself and scoring above the average.

This is the WORST professor I have ever taken at OSU (and I've had bad ones). Attending class is a joke as he teaches straight from the book and talks to the ground. Teaching yourself is the only way to go. Averages are 50% and he thinks that is acceptable. Truly an awful teacher. STAY AWAY!

Probably the worst professor I have ever had. And ive had some bad ones.  Exams and quizzes are extremely hard. Avg is usually between 50 and 60. Cannot understand what he is saying so you basically teach yourself. If there is another prof teaching, take them bc is cant get worse than this guy.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Genuinely cares about students and is passionate about the material. You can't go wrong with him.

Professor Hamann is very professional in what he does. He truly has a passion for art and teaching. The lectures themselves were extremely dry and boring, but it probably had more to do with the material/content, not necessarily the professor. He did, however, speak very quickly in lectures. He is very fair and wants you to succeed.

Class consists of midterm, one assignment, and final paper. Midterm is memorization heavy, which is typical with art history courses. He seems to be interested in what he is teaching, which to me is very important. Makes the lectures as interesting as possible. Easy & fast grader. Would take course again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fantastic Professor, makes what could be a boring subject (ancient Latin American art) pretty interesting and the workload is pretty low. The exam is tough but he is not a harsh grader. He also grades everything as fast as possible.

Great professor - exams depend on heavy memorization - as is typical in Art Hist classes. Projects are actually a lot of fun and professor is a lenient grader if you put forth the effort. Nice, likable, and engaging. A+ educator
So, lectures consisted of watching and listening to over 200 powerpoint slides per class. If you can handle that then the class was easy to study for and very reasonable.  I would take it again.

This class was an adventure. Professor Hamann thinks and teaches like no one else at OSU. He is incredibly smart and eloquent, his material is surprising, and the students clearly love him. Very creative assignments. He's also humble, and encouraging: had never seen a professor so happy after a class discussion.

Bucci is very passionate about computer science. However, the format of his course skews grades downwards. Multiple times I completed a project to receive feedback of "Great Work!" to still just get an 80%. Also, there isn't an attendance grade specifically, but rather a participation grade. Content is not difficult, the harsh grading is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bucci is hands down my favorite professor in the CSE classes that I have taken. Bucci is readily available to help during his office hours. I remember letting Bucci know that I'd be absent for a conference and he was very understanding and willing to work with my schedule. Love this guy!

Whoever says he is a bad professor did not put in the work. There are times where you question if he is speculating if you are dumb or not, but that is his personality. Fair grader, he is funny in lectures/labs, and is a great professor.
Horrible class environment
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have ever taken. No one got an A. Daily assignments and the class is very test based heavy. The exams are impossible and no curve. Prof gets mad when asking him questions.

Hands-down the BEST professor I've had at OSU. I had him for 2221 and then purposefully again for 2231. Many people will diss him because he is strict but if you show up, put in work, and genuinely care about the material he will battle for you and you will be amazing at coding reasoning. Also, he is hilarious. Go to his and grader office hours.

Paolo seems tough but he's just very passionate about the subject and expects students to put in the work. He's accessible and willing to give you feedback on anything you need. He's very knowledgeable and has a very specific way he wants things done, but everything in the class is absolutely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bucci is a kind and funny guy! His course expectations are pretty standard and if you show effort, he'll be more willing to give you tips on his tests. Basically, show up everyday and participate. His tests are fair and pretty reasonable, but I'd say you actually have to study for them, maybe take a day or two to study.

He's an excellent lecturer! His class is hard but fair if you put in the work, and he does such a good job explaining the concepts at a deeper level. He can be intimidating if you don't know him or if you're afraid of speaking up, but if you make an effort to approach him you'll find that he's a really funny and caring person. I loved class w/ him!

Midterm 1 & 2 averages were both failing grades, goes on to blame the students. Constantly complains that no one participates in his class, but then is mean to people who to participate, with no constructive criticism. He likes making examples out of people and embarrassing them. Just be kind Bucci, more people will talk, I can guarantee.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher at all. CSE 2231 exams are the hardest with him. Other SW2 class exams are open book ,open note. He makes the exams extremely hard. Doesn't do exam reviews. The median for Midterm 1 is 51 with no curve. OSU needs to make a set standard SW2 exams. Takes every question as  criticism and is defensive.
Everyone in my class received a 40% on midterm 1 and he blamed it on us...
Nice lecturer but not a good teacher, you can never get 10/10 in you project, any of the small problem will take your grades.

Easy exams with harsh points deductions for mistakes. 2221 is a horrendously designed course that is useless at teaching concepts. Be prepared for a tremendous amount of time wasted with lecture, lab, homework, and projects - none of which properly teach the core concepts of the class.
hard grader
Bad course to taken with him, heavy homework with limited percentage, strict exams which you might get deduction for not efficient of the code (the codes are written by hand based on paper)

He's notoriously hard, but if you have a strong coding background, it wasn't very hard. Midterms are a big percentage of grades, and if you have a bad day, it can drastically affect your grades. Doesn't give materials to help with exams. Project grades aren't explained with a clear rubric and I was left wondering. Pray for a good TA. Nice guy tho

the least accommodating professor i have ever had at osu. i was very ill (to the point of where i couldn't get out of bed) and it happened to be during finals week. i tried to ask him to rearrange my exam time so that i could heal before taking the exam but he was not allowing it. ended up having to retake this class b/c he is so not accommodating.

The class is challenging, but Bucci's teaching approach is effective if you put in the effort. The homework is manageable, and the tests are fair. Using resources like unstuck study alongside the lectures can really help with study prep.

His course is widely recognized as the most difficult. The exams are the hardest among all the professors, and the assignments are graded the most strictly. He designs the materials and teaches with great dedication. If you genuinely want to learn, choose him. If you're just looking for a good grade, avoid him.
C+ before curves, B after curves :)

So much homework, but it shouldn't be longer than 30 minutes and are preparation for lab the next day. Often comes off as exasperated with students when they don't raise their hands to answer questions or don't answer questions. This would be appropriate for older students, but his classes are mostly taken by freshman and sophomores. Informative.

Bucci is the head for sw 1 and 2 so the tests for all classes are very similar to his, the tests are also fair, they are hard but everything on his exams is stuff that he went over in class. tbh, most of the bad reviews come from people who don't try much. Additionally, he curves at the end by a decent amount. main advice is just put in effort.

I quickly figured out the people complaining about Bucci simply didn't put in the effort to learn OR needed their egos checked. Yes, he went off on a few people during class, but for good reasons...people being disrespectful and arguing with him or undermining his policies. He was really helpful to me outside of class, cares about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Bucci for SW1 and SW2. SW1 was a big learning curve, but I don't think that has too much to do with the way he taught. I was quite intimidated at first in SW1, but I soon realized that he is a caring teacher who is passionate about the subject. Tests are not hard to succeed on if you watch the video lectures and review labs.

He gets a bad reputation and it was intimidating at first but I would not be scared. I got a D on the first midterm and ended with an A still, very fair exams and the projects are easy points if you attend office hours. People who think his section is impossible to achieve in are simply not putting the time in.
terrible class environment, hard on grades with little grade opportunities (midterms are make or break), ego, awful experience and I recommend people to stay far away.
Among many things, doesn't communicate topics clearly

He's a very good professor in terms of teaching. If you want one 24 hour extension your probably not gonna get it. He is very passionate about the material but he does not curve and he tells the TAs to grade harder. This is good for us but I knew people who turned in significantly worse code get better grades than me in other sections.

He is a decent lecturer who conveys a clear understanding of the content, however he can be a little difficult to approach. After I started talking to him more and spent extra time practicing towards the end of the semester, I understood the content pretty well. He has a lot of insight and can genuinely make you a better programmer

Usually one of the only professors that makes attendance mandatory and teaches sections in the morning, so try not to take any software classes in the morning because you might have him. Very very tough grader. On exams, your entire code either has to be completely right or it's just wrong even if you think you deserve partial credit.
GREAT PERSOHN ONG

Whatever you do even if this is the only course available with this teacher do not take his class. He likes to see people fail and is the hardest grader. You won't understand his lectures and you will fail the class.

Anyone who complains about him likely didn't feel like putting in the effort to learn the content. Not a difficult class if you pay attention even the slightest bit. Very passionate professor, cares about what he does and wants to make you a better programmer, even if that means telling you that you are stupid because, maybe you are.

Bucci comes off as uncaring and almost rude professor. He wants everyone to participate but if you ask a question he might make you feel dumb for asking it. He understands the material, gives very informative lectures, and gives great feedback if you go his office hours prepared. The effort he demands makes all of his students better programmers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Bucci was one of the best professors that I have had in the CSE department in terms of teaching. He cares about his students and the knowledge that they take away from the class. If you wish to actually learn Software II content, I recommend taking Paolo Bucci.

Mr. Bucci is one of the most hard-headed professors I have ever met. If you want to take a class with a living fossil schedule his section of Software 2 or 1 and have a fun time asking him for help and having him talk to you like every question you asked was the stupidest question ever and that you don't know anything. Overall, bad professor.

Bucci is an incredible lecturer, and while he comes across as a little demeaning sometimes I think it comes from the fact that he simply knows so much. If you ask him a good question he gets noticeably excited, he really likes student participation. He is the course director for 2221 so he knows what is important to study for the midterms.
Work load is not too high, however expect graders to be tough. Things like missing a name on an assignment or submitting with the wrong file type will certainly lose you some points.

I can understand why people consider Professor Bucci a difficult teacher. His grading is harsh, his exams are harder than other professors teaching the same class, and he doesn't always appear very friendly. But I honestly feel like I took away a lot from his class. I like his teaching style and it's very easy to ask questions in or out of class.

Lectures are super bland and gets mad when asked questions. Doesn't go over any practice because all he asks for are questions in the class, and then briefly go over some points in the lectures not showing how to implement the code or use it. In Labs the work is there but you can barely ask questions and hope you don't get the professor to come.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is a very harsh grader, but does teach well
This professor is a really tough grader who captures every small mistake in the exam and then makes a big deduction. Never take any courses from him.
sooooo difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not sure why Bucci gets such a bad wrap. The class is definitely hard and some professors might have easier classes but this guy knows his stuff. Pretty sure he's the one that created the 2221/2231 sequence
There's no way that he can actually be a professor

A lot of people hate on this class because it is so different from any other coding course out there and it forces you to break with bad habits. In this class, you'll learn to code with rigorous discipline. If you want to become a better programmer that can write high quality code, this class if for you. If you put in the work, it will pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Need to read slides before class which difficult to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bucci admits to using outdated software, coursework, and material for this class. He has been using the same format and projects for over 6 years. Do not expect to learn any actual useful information. Scratch that, do not expect to learn anything from this guy. He offers no input for the labs. His lectures are catered to people with previous exp.

Bucci is a disgrace to Computer Science and Engineering in general. The first project in the class literally states on the rubric "teach yourself." Do not expect any real teaching from Bucci. Do not be surprised if you create functional code and still receive an F because it is not how he wants it. Bucc is the most unapproachable and rude professor

You will have to do a lot of studying outside of class and if you have questions that what you do in lectures. There are labs every other day and you have to finish them within the class period. Have projects every week and homework almost everyday. Need to watch lectures every other day before classes usually and very few days with no homework. GL

only good thing about him is he is knows stuff and accessible. But dare you ask a question you will be roasted like you never have been in your entire life. He is accessible and resources are there but if you want to ask questions make sure there are not a lot of people around you so the embarrassment you feel, which you will, stays to a minimum.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Extremely tough grader. Average on our first exam was 65%; our third was 60%. Ending with my first sub-A at OSU. If you make a tiny mistake, they will lacerate you. I've heard average is 20% higher in other profs' sections. Who gets an A vs who gets a B is determined not by how much you know, but by how good you are at tip-toeing on ice.

He definitely knows his stuff and is really passionate when it comes to CSE, specifically Software 1. He is not only a really tough grader and expects specific solutions, but you do have to study a lot if you want a decent grade on the quizzes. Be prepared to get ridiculed or criticized by him if you have any questions about the covered material

He always tells the class to ask questions, but once you ask a question, he makes you feel stupid for not understanding it. Says you shouldve watched and understood the lecture. Prerecorded lectures are made and lecture time is used as a Q&A rather than an actual lecture time. I dont recommend...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Makes his students feel like they do not know anything. It makes class feel like its a competition between him and his students. In reality, he should be working with students to help them learn and not putting them down. If you have another option, do not take him as your professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Puts down students if they do not know an answer to one of his questions. Leaves in class lectures completely open ended. The class is fun and engaging, but frankly, he is a poor lecturer and has no respect for his students.

Paulo made the curriculum for sw1 (cse2221) and 2 (cse2231). He is respected and knows what he is talking about but he can come off as arrogant and make students feel unworthy of his time. Didn't understand a topic at first glance? Get ready to be drilled with questions in a breakout room that make you feel like you know nothing. Best of luck.

Bucci writes the Software courses, so he has the best understanding of the content and what each assignment is trying to teach. Don't expect him to be your friend, but it is clear that he cares that his students learn things properly and practices the discipline. Highly recommend because if you can't learn from him, you won't from anybody else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Paolo is clearly very passionate about CSE, but he treats his students as if they are idiots and refuses to answer some questions that people are struggling with because if you use your head you can probably figure it out. Lectures are prerecorded and mandatory to watch, and he expects you to ALSO go to live lectures on zoom. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.
Taking online. Lectures are entirely per-recorded. Lecture time is "office hours" and refuses to go over content that is in the lectures even if you are still confused. Harsh grader.

In class attendance is recorded & has random 3 question quizzes on specific items. HE DOESNT CARE IF THE GRADERS DONT GRADE BY HIS CRITERIA. Grades on homework DO NOT SHOW YOUR PREPARATION FOR THE EXAMS. He grades Very harshly and questions may be very niche. He has a thick accent and talks quickly, you probably wont understand everything he says.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Paolo Bucci treats the students like they don't know anything and that us CS student are not thinking and are idiots. I guess he has the idea that he's doing it to make you better, but he does not treat any of his students with respect whatsoever. He has the idea that if scores are low, it is not because of him and his inability to teach, but on us
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He explains very good, HOWEVER he's a REALLY hard grader. If you need a good grade, RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Paolo is a hard grader and will pick out small details and seems angry, but in the end, he really cares about your learning and gives you very good feedback. He is willing to help outside of class if you are truly stuck. The lectures are very organized and although the slides are online, Paolo definitely clarifies and provides more details.

Paolo definitely understands the material well. However, if you ask questions he does make you feel like the stupidest person alive. If you want to succeed, you NEED to go to class. If you have the will to do well, you will. Just listen closely to what he says and remember them, because almost always he includes them on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Bucci for both SW1 and SW2. He is a great professor that expects nothing less than excellence from his students. Prof Bucci is a professor that will make sure that you never forget the core principles of what he is teaching you. Don't miss lectures or labs (for you own sake). Maybe wear an Inter Milan jersey to get on his good side.

Got consistent 9's and 10's on the projects, studied them before exams like everybody said to, looked at past exams, still was never really prepared and couldn't get higher than a C on the exams. He's definitely very smart and maybe it's because I took it at 8am, but this class is extremely difficult. DO NOT TAKE if you have a loaded schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't usually post here but a guy on reddit wished more people rated professors so here goes. Bucci is a good professor. His lectures are usually engaging and I, for one, find him pretty funny. He does grade exams pretty hard but usually the exam coding problems are similar to the projects. Some people practice for exams by writing code on paper.

Doesnt really explain much in class but if you so dare miss a single petty detail on an exam or a project ge will screw you over big time. The most earned grade for our MT2 was 30 and the second was an 80. Its an inverse bell curve, and no one likes that

Dr. Bucci is the embodiment of everything wrong with the CSE department at OSU. As course coordinator, he is the one responsible for the abhorrently bad material in Software I & II and his lectures show it. Exams are also significantly harder than other sections of 2231, it's seriously night and day how much harder they are.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Bucci for Software I and Software II. He is invested in the course material because he helped create the course content and he's a good teacher as well. However, he gets annoyed when his students don't ask questions, so be sure to do that. You must show up to lectures because there isn't a textbook for these courses.

He is a good and experienced professors. The reason why I rate him so low is because he grades strictly and may influence GPA greatly. The course is already difficult and he still grade strictly. This situation makes many common students who is not very good at CS struggle in his class. But the good students can learn more things from his class.
If you have other choice, never take his class. He has tough grading and you must have the code like his correct answer. And the exams are extremely difficult.

He is quite irritable. He gets annoyed when people don't answer questions. The reason for this is because no one ever asks questions, so he doesn't know what the students aren't understanding. He's really caring and wants the students to do well. He encourages questions, and doesn't give away answers. Sometimes may be hard to follow, but he's good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice guy overall, but his foundations 1 class makes me feel hopeless at many times. Doesn't do an adequate job preparing students for the work he assigns, and as a result the average grade of the class on even the homeworks is typically below an 80% which is unheard of even in difficult classes such as Math 1172 (which I received an A in).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Although he ends class late most of the time and is a tough grader, he is one of my favorite professors. It is so refreshing to have a professor that is so excited to teach everyday. He is clearly passionate about the subject and I learned a great deal from his class.
He really wants you to learn and is very passionate about the class!

I can honestly say that he has been one of the better teachers that I have had.  He challenged me to be better and I learned a lot from his class. His midterms and his finals are very difficult and he is a really tough grader. If you want to learn a lot then I would recommend him. If you need a good grade though I would choose someone else.

If you want a solid understanding of the course material that you're willing to work towards, there couldn't be a better choice.  He grades very fairly; you get exactly as many points as you deserve, and he's an enthusiastic and thorough  lecturer. His dry sense of humor can be misinterpreted as rudeness, but in the end he just wants you to succeed

CSE 2231 was not the most enjoyable class, but Paolo did a good job. The tests were very easy and the grading on those was perfectly fair, but the labs were graded pretty tough. Messing up one little thing meant 10% was dropped from your grade. One of the best teachers in the department, but if you're looking for an easy A I'd look elsewhere.

The lectures in his class weren't very helpful since he moves so quickly, but all of the slides are posted online. The group projects went well. The exams were fairly difficult. There was a lot of very specific questions that require knowing very minute details, yet he says "focus on overall concepts". He's nice though and does what he can to help.

He would sit in lab and say: "Why are you guys not asking any questions."  When you ask a question h would respond: "I don't know how you don't understand it's so simple." I would never take him for anything. There is no help or clarification.

Not going to lie, Bucci is tough but he really knows his stuff.  He really wants to make sure his students understand the course material which is why seems to get furstarted  when students don't understand - however he if you show that you're trying he really takes notice and is here to help you learn

Software 1 with Bucci was unnecessarily difficult. The class average was lower compared to the other sections. Grades too harshly on projects and tests, and tends to be condescending if you don;t understand a concept quickly. Many students hesitated to ask hi questions because of this. Take this course with someone else

I liked 23 of this class and when to him weekly for extra help the other 13. He will set up time to meet with students who ask for help but he will explain the material the same way, so if you don't get it the way he explains it, good luck. Very difficult teacher, can be degrading in lectures (not purpose), and re-iterates its our job to learn it

It is clear that Bucci is passionate about computer science, however, his class is unnecessarily difficult for a pre major class. He grades way too tough on projects and tests, and his averages are always lower than other classes. Take it with someone else if you dont want to risk not getting into the major
His coding techniques are ou of date, and teaches some knowledge no one would use in real world.
Great to listen to, great at speaking. Nice voice and accent. Very comforting.

Paolo is extremely knowledgeable of the field of CSE and is very passionate about the subject. The downside of this is it seems that he gets upset when you don't understand a topic. However, he really does care about students and will gladly work with you. Takes getting used and grades are lower, but you will learn more.
Averages always higher with other profs. Just take it with someone else.

He is very knowledgeable in his field and does an excellent job of explaining material. He is also very passionate about his job, a little too much at times as he can gets all worked up when students do not understand. His class is rather challenging, but if you put the time in you will excel.

He is extremely knowledgeable on the subject and can sometimes not understand why you're not understanding. However, he is more than willing to help you with any question and meet outside of office hours. His tests are comprehensive and not overly difficult, though the grades are final.

He is a very good teacher, but can be a little condescending (in a good way) when it comes to asking questions. He comes with a funny Italian accent, but it is very easy to understand. I recommend taking his classes.

He means well honestly, and the curve was quite generous even in a class of only 46 people during the summer. It was tough, and he is tough on grading. But you will learn too, a good guy but a little unfair on grading in an intro software sequence. Projects were rough too on grading. It is up to you if you think it's worth it with him. He does care

This class had a lot of material to cover. The problem is not only that, the teacher is not approachable at times. He grades too rough on things such as making sure you only have one return statement, and some performance things. The grader was who to watch for also. Your grade will suffer if you are not persistent and careful studying.
Take this course with a different instructor.

Just took this class and learned a lot.  The set up is confusing, but it was the first 2231 class in semesters.  Bucci came off as rude sometimes but it's just his personality.  Can be funny, can be nice if you get to know him
Overall he was a good teacher and it seemed like he truly cared about the students/class. All the material was extremely detailed. He can be good but strict. You learn a lot with his classes.
Difficult class, learned a lot. Paolo is very straight forward about his difficulty. He is a great professor and gave all the resources necessary to learn for ourselves outside of class.

HIGHLY intense class. Weekly labs are really weekly projects. He teaches the class as if you've mastered the Resolve sequence and/or had java in high school. Midterm and Final are all multiple choice. No HW grades except the labs. You don't get to keep your midterm test to study from. Beware of the time commitment!

I felt like I understood everything and even though my labs were all seemingly correct, points were taken off so strictly.  A good teacher and knows what he is talking about, but if you want a good grade, DONT take if from him.

One of the few professors that I know I will never forget. He makes his classes hard because he expects the best, but he is very helpful and it's easy to learn enough to impress him.  He doesn't tolerate laziness or ignorance.  Some interpret that as rudeness, I interpret it as realistic.  Amazing professor.
Everything stated in the previous comment is true. However, be aware that your grade likely will suffer from taking Bucci. Take him to learn from him, not to get an A.

Paolo is a master of his trade and the designer of the SCE sequence. He will challenge you to be your best, and expects exactly that. If you attend every lecture, I see no conceivable way to fall behind in this course. He is a funny guy, with a very appropriate temper.  Easily the best professor in my three years at this school thus far.

Good guy, funny too. Is very clear. Really summed up all the concepts of SCE series well. Don't believe what anyone says about him being super rude, I think he was a little surprised by it himself and made fun of himself about this page in class. Tests are tough and labs are expected to be done to exactly to specifications. Fair though, learn a lot

Paulo is one of the best profs I've had at Ohio State. His class is not easy, and he expects perfection, but he teaches very clearly and tells you exactly what he wants. He is extremely helpful in office hours and answers emails promptly. 421 is a great class, and I highly recommend Paulo for the class.

Paolo Bucci is the man.  He's very strict and albeit condescending, you will learn a lot from him.  The only experience I had in Java prior to his class was in high school, but now I definitely feel a lot more confident and well-versed in Java.  But this knowledge doesn't come without pain!

He likes to explain things about 4 different ways, but just repeats himself. Be careful with what time your class is because you're likely to fall asleep during his droning on the same topic. He grades hard and the tests are very difficult. He is NOT good with questions, so pick it up on your own time since you won't want to ask him...
He talks fast, but he's always willing to slow down. He's obviously very passionate about his job, and he's also very good at it. He's not the easiest professor, but he is very fair.
Very knowledgeable but not the easiest man to ask questions to. 421 labs can be tough but are doable. Midterm and final were very difficult.

I can tell he is passionate about the material he teaches but he wants everything done HIS way no matter what, (even if it is purely style or preference). He acts annoyed when you ask him questions in closed-labs or if he deems the question 'stupid'. You can get through the class if you have to but if you have another choice- take it.
Generally people who complain about him are the ones who get terrible grades.  It's definitely not Paolo's fault if you do poorly, because he explains everything you need to know and is very helpful.

Bucci is a man at war. He is very testy, but he seems to feel bad about it at the same time. Like, he'll make you out to be an idiot for some of the questions you ask, he's so testy even when in good spirits, but then he'd semi-apologize. Your code is terrible, no it's not TERRIBLE, but it's so very bad, I mean I've  seen worse, but MAN this code!

Excellent professor.  I'm taking him again for 421 where he's still an excellent teacher.  Very practical and gets his point across well.  Awesome sarcastic sense of humor.  Kind of a tough grader but he'll help you as much as you need.  Highly recommended.

Had him for 421 and 321.  Great professor - especially for 421.  His labs are very practical but his midterms/final require lots of studying.  He can be a little bit scary. I would take one of his classes again cause he is a awesome Italian dude. fahey...

I strongly recommend NOT taking Bucci if you need structured lectures and are slower at understanding CSE classes. His lectures never seemed to get to the point and he always came off as annoyed and insulting if you asked questions. I guess some people must like him, but PROCEED WITH CAUTION.

Paolo is one of the best teachers at Ohio State, and probably one of the most knowledgeable guys in the department.  He explains the material well, and is willing to help anyone.  Some people might mistake his passion for computer science as arrogance, but it is not.  He just wants you to know your stuff.  Everyone should take a class with him.

Paolo is extremely tough and a hard grader and a very fast speaker who can come off as intimidating.  That being said, he's one of the most helpful professors I've had and is EXTREMELY knowledgeable on the topic.  I learned an exceptional amount in this class.
A lot of people complained, but I liked his teaching style and went over things many times if you had questions.

If you don't put in time, he probably won't like you. If you put in time, you won't necessarily get an A since he is a tough grader but he is more than happy to help you. He expects a lot out of everyone, and doesn't give as many points as most for effort. Tough but fair, my favorite CSE professor out of the whole 221/222/321 series.

I actually think Paolo's one of the best guys in the department.  If you put forth the effort and do your labs ahead of time, he's more than willing to critique them, give you feedback, and let you change them.  He's very helpful and quick at responding to students outside of class, and he's a funny, good-natured guy.  And he DOES have cool hats!

Hard grader and has high expectations, but if you're making an effort he has no problem giving you the time of day with plenty of suggestions. Also has a good sense of humor about the whole bugs language thing.

He is the worst in CSE department. He  yells at you if you ask question. The exams are extremely hard. He is also a hard grader, he will go after the grader he you get perfect score. RUN A WAY FROM ELSE YOU DOOM.

This guy is terrible. I can't understand him with his rapid speech and Italian accent. He expects perfection on labs (which makes it really hard to get a 5) and yells at the students if the class does not participate or have questions. The average of our midterm was 60 while Long's section was 83. Oh and Bucci doesn't curve so don't expect an A.

Bucci's grading system is the worst I've ever seen. He changes grades that the teaching assistants mark. He expects perfection, but he isn't clear on how to achieve what he wants. When something is hard to understand, he continues to repeat himself as if explaining the matter badly multiple times will help.
Difficult to follow, showed his emotions too much.
Very very helpful, but He will get loud at times and he is definitely a harsh grader, he expects dedication and perfection.. I would take other classes with him.

This class is rediculous in the first place but Paolo makes it sickening. He does not help you.  His tests are crazy crazy difficult.  I hate him and I don't usually hate professors. And I can't understand a thing he says, damn accent.

I knew day one that he was going to make me cry. He doesn't spare any expense making his expectations clear, and he makes them high. He expects a whole lot of his students, and he's not very forgiving. He's a nice guy, but a crappy teacher. He does help, but he's not always convenient.

This guy gives his students extremelly hard tests. He doesn't prepare the students in any way for the test, but he expects perfection from the students like they are born geniuses. Not even Bill Gates or any famous programmers would be able to pass his impossible tests. Good luck with this guy.
No Comments

I think that he makes the class artificially harder by grading ridiculously hard.  He definitely knows what he is talking about, but his teaching style is condescending and demeaning at times.  He kind of discourages input from students who don't know what they're doing.

I agree with the previous guy that i didn't like Bucci very well at first....He has gotten better though..He is funny at times and explains things pretty well...The homework is tough because sometimes homework is assigned before he actually goes over the topic...Overall, decent prof, although i like

In the beginning I absolutely hated this guy, but towards the end he actually seemed to not be so bad. Sometimes his help would lead me in the wrong direction so I would ask the grader. The exams seemed to be much longer compared to CSE 221 since I didn't seem to have enough time both exams.
yells during the whole class.  very intimidating

OK when instructing but harsh on the grading.  Expects perfection in code.  Willing to help you out in office ours, but you think everything is fine until you get your grade back and you get a D because you made some minor mistake...
No Comments
No Comments
He gives very clear and thorough explanations, but sometimes he makes you feel guilty for making mistakes or not answer questions thrown out during lectures.
odd balance of grading hard (lots of points off for stupid mistakes), but going slowly and not expecting people to understand simple topics. Energetic and fun to listen to. Does explain things well.
Very energetic and knowledgeable. Bug's world game was a fun lab.

Dr. Bucci is an excellent instructor.  I'm not sure why anyone would have a problem with him.  He presented the material in a very clear manner.  He is an energetic, enthusiastic lecturer and was always willing to help.
He is very intimidating and has a short temper with coding mistakes, like there shouldn't be any...
I didn't like his style at all, almost 'mean'...
great teacher. very knowledgeable about the material. although he is helpful debugging your code, he makes you feel like an idiot while he's at it.

One of the most talented, amazing Officers the Air Force has to offer. He is sharp as a tack and knows the art of leading people. He takes the time to know his students and genuinely cares about everyone. He goes out of his way to help you.
He used to be a reservist, so he'll shoot you straight. Sporty.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor. He cares a lot about each of his students, and is a great model officer.

Lt Col Bone is an amazing teacher. Even though the class starts early in the morning, I never have any trouble staying awake. He always incorporates things into the class that make me motived to not only do better in school but to be a better person. I highly recommend taking this class if you are interested in learning more about leadership.

Do NOT take a class with her. Worst professor I have had at the college or even high school level. It was evident she did not grasp the material she was trying to teach or give notes on, often could not pronounce key words (tried to play that off as being cute), and could not answer questions in class. Material on test did not correlate to in class

I had her at OU and I'm not trying to be harsh, just honest, but she was awful. It is evident that she is teaching outside of her sub-discipline of Anthropology and has no idea what in the hell she is teaching. Tests were not at all what she said they would be. I would avoid her class at all costs.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER! Her notes don't make any sense and are all over the place. Exams are harder than what you would expect based on material and covers things you don't even learn.

Horrible. Initially comes off as pretty cool & then the crap sets in.  Attendance = mandatory. Sitting in circle = mandatory. This is the first 597 class that I have not enjoyed. Will pick apart essays incorrectly - I had my mom double-check that I was right and she has a Master's in English and taught in that field for many years. Grrr. Avoid!
Very bad teacher. She always took attendance and picked favorite students. Way to many essays! Lectured all the time, so student participation. She would never explain why she took of points.

She was awful. Classes were painstakingly boring, and tests were way too hard for an intro class. She also grades papers unfairly, and takes off points for no reason and then can't explain why when you ask her about it.

Greg was my professor for this class at the university of iowa. He was laid back and a good lecturer. I didn't find the class to be that demanding. I suppose if you want to get in law school it can be a challenge. But there is a glut of lawyers today as evidenced by the television commercials.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was mostly lectures, if you take notes you will be fine. Exams primarily draw from the slides. Caldiera is a wonderful professor with a great sense of humor and interest in the topic he teaches.
Takes TopHat attendance (ends up being 15% of grade); uploads lectures online, but in a very confusing manner; exams are impossible as he asks for minute details briefly mentioned in slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you aren't considering law school, or you don't have an interest in the Supreme Court, DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. That said, Caldeira is brilliant and highly regarded, look at his CV. He's extremely kind and helpful in office hours. Lectures are rough, he will lecture AT you for 80 minutes without stopping. Read every case and BRIEF THEM.

Material is interesting, but there's a lot of it. Professor Caldeira makes pretty confusing Powerpoint slides that don't help much, and will sometimes breeze through confusing concepts without clarifying or connecting them to broader ideas. Read the text before lecture to get the most out of his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Caldeira's lectures might be the cure to narcolepsy. He definitely knows his material but has no idea how to convey it. His notes are filled with acronyms that you will have no idea what they stand for when you go to prepare for his exams. He also uses terms that he does not go over and assumes you know what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst polisci class I have taken at OSU. Like every1 says on here, multiple choice exams in which 1 word makes the difference if you get the ? right. Lectures, textbook, and online notes, are not helpful. attendance is a part of your grade (you will be board). If it was not for the curve, many students would end up with D's and F's. AVOID HIM!!!!!!

The material was tough, the lectures were not helpful at all but attendance is mandatory. He takes attendance on this website that you have to pay $20 for. The 3 exams, which make up your course grade, are extremely tough. Sometimes one word can be the difference between a right and wrong answer. Textbook not necessary. Make study guides of cases.

Worst class I have ever taken. Clearly knows his stuff,but can't communicate that with the average student. He's also a law school prof and teaches the class like we're all about to pass the bar tomorrow. To pass an exam is to have an angel on your side. Do yourself a favor and pick a different class, or drop while you still have time.

As an aspiring law student, his tests are multiple choice and extremely unpractical. Exams are on Carmen, which tends to glitch and mess up your answers. It gives you no room to make your case like an actual law exam. He uses this STUPID attendance taking software called Tophat that you'll waste $20  on.  Don't waste time. Find a better class.

Terrible professor in a sense that he is VERY BORING. Exams are open booknotes, but WATCH OUT ! He'll put a lot of questions with: A,B,C,D, All of the above, none of the above, BC, AD? the answers will sometimes come down to a single word that makes the difference. Unless you plan on going to law school, there is no benefit in taking this course.

Extremely knowledgeable professor. Knows everything about every Supreme Court case ever. Textbook not essential, but does help. Only made it through about half of the scheduled court cases so not a terrible amount of work. Exams are specific but you get to use cheat sheets.

Has extensive knowledge on the material, but he doesn't appear to know how to communicate any of it. Caldeira looks starkly similar to the Doctor in the 1992 children's movie, Beethoven. He makes it pretty clear that he'd rather be doing something other than teaching.
Useful class but so boring you'll want to die. Tests are HARD despite being open book. Prof's notes are posted online but are extremely disorganized. Final exam looked nothing like the midterm.

Ridiculous multiple choice exams, but they are open notes so make a table or contents or something before hand because all it is is a looking-up fest for an hour and 48 minutes.  I didn't read the book and I highly doubt it helps, so don't bother, just use the notes.  The curve is large so if you can look stuff up you're fine. attendance required.

kinda boring, we just reviewed court briefs and that's it. there are three grades: exam one, final exam, and attendance. exams are open book and open note, but don't let that fool you; they are incredibly hard and often the difference between two potential answers for a question is a single word. there is a curve, but you may need all of it.
The class has mandatory attendance and is incredibly boring. Tests are open note, but they are somewhat difficult. Nice sized curve in the class.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS.  This guy is HORRIBLE.  No interest in teaching whatsoever, exams are horrible...AVOID.

We covered less than half the syllabus, a little dissapointing. Dr. Caldiera himself seems like a nice person but individual lectures themselves were dry and didn't explain overall legal reaching principles. He explained case after case but did not link or attempt to teach the court's overall case law approach. His class is survivable despite this.

Caldeira's a nice guy and everything but we barely covered any material. The class was a lot less challenging than expected, which can be good or bad depending on if you're in college to learn or not. He gets distracted easily and seemed to prefer one-on-one conversation to actual teaching. Maybe winter quarter is not a good time for him?

Extremely nice professor and very helpful...bring a pillow to class because his lectures are very boring. Seems very interested in the topics covered but he's the opposite when it comes to teaching...open book/note tests
Intelligent, well dressed, easily distracted from lecture topic-- clearly no interest whatsoever in teaching.
Hardly came to class and never responded to e-mails.  Seemed completely uninterested in teaching
he's a really nice man!! admittedly boring, and he was sick a LOT winter quarter. but he is very smart and is just really sweet. :)

He has actually been a pretty good teacher, especially later on in the quarter. Though he has made some "smart" comments, he does present the material relatively clearly and he does offer help when students need it.
No Comments
No Comments

His classes are mandatory and there are no grace sessions. I actually wanted to unplug my ears each of his lectures. He's a nice person but I genuinely feel anxious around him. His lectures are so boring and also calls on people and calls them "his victims." I also hate photoshop.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures align very well with exams; by paying attention to the lectures and lightly studying the readings, you will easily do well in the class. I asked him for advice on some of my assignments and that helped secure good grades on projects. He is very passionate and gives enthusiastic lectures that are genuinely enjoyable.

He's okay, for the rubrics of assignments you have to wait to see how he grades the first project to understand what he wants. They rubrics are the worst part, because he is quite harsh on techniques. But he gives thorough lectures and the assignments do help you learn the content. Just mid overall.

Overall very knowledgeable and funny guy. Lectures are interesting & participation is mandatory so do the readings - they aren't hard. Instructions for photoshop assignments aren't the clearest, examples would've helped, just ask questions. Minimal feedback on photoshop assignments so read the assignment requirements closely. Learned a lot!

Passionate about the class and material but the layout is a little annoying. The assignments are pretty easy as long as you put in effort and pay attention during class. The tests are what brought down my grade because he did not clearly layout what would be on exams. Overall this class is not terrible you just can't skip.

Lectures could be interesting so I did not mind going to class. However, the grading criteria for projects was not properly laid out and he did not provide sufficient examples to help you understand what he was looking for. Study guides did not help much for exams. This class was only my second B in college.

If you do not attend class, you will fail this course. I missed one day and it dropped my grade almost 2 letter grades. He is big on participation, if you do not participate, he will start assigning pop quizzes. He expects you to read the materials before the lecture. He has 3 exams for us, but the study guides did not really help with them. STUDY.

Leonardo grew on me throughout the semester; he has a passion for multimedia and what he does, and cares about his students. However, though there are eight assignments, you must work on them as each takes time and effort. It can cause burnout, and the turnaround time on projects is a lot; Leonardo grades strictly as if students are professionals.

Leo is definitly a tough grader, and he love to grade everything in his own view.  So, if you have to choose his class, remember to ask him about your work and you may improve a little on your grade. 
His lecture is interesting, but you have to write down every words on the powerpoint all by your own. 
Also, in-person final exam!! Close book also.

Never met a professor less willing to work with students. Carrizo painfully takes up the entire 2-hours he has to lecture. One day he spent over an hour explaining how a tripod works. Given the 8 multi-media assignments required it is fairly incomprehensible as to how out of 11 total things graded, 2 combine for 40% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT PROCRASTINATE! The worst thing I will say is the class is very busy, especially with a midterm project and exam along with a final project and exam. He does want his students to pass and if you go to him for help, he will try to help you. I could not have been more of a beginner in Adobe Premiere and I feel extremely comfortable with it now.

This class is straightforward. Everything is written out for you on Carmen. There are a lot of homework assignments, but he gives you everything you need to work ahead. He walks you through all the steps for photoshop projects as well. If you go to class and do the assignments, you'll get a good grade. He is incredibly knowledgeable and helpful.

Consistently has typos/grammatical errors on his quizzes/exams. Disorganized Carmen page. Have to turn into Dora the Explorer to find assignment/readings. This should be an easy class to pass but somehow he makes everything difficult and 10x harder than what it should be. His lectures are enjoyable, but that's your only saving grace.

Carrizo is undoubtedly one of the worst professors I've had, which is funny because he teaches what should be an incredibly easy and straightforward subject. Instead, he constantly lies, critiques, and stonewalls any and all assignments because he is so incredibly inflexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I respect his art, but he is NOT a good professor. Most of what we actually need to know for assignments is learned outside of it, on our own. The use of adobe and other applications is extremely tedious if you're a beginner. This class made me cry at least 8 times. He needs a TA, or maybe he shouldn't teach the class at all.
most boring four hours of my week, not an intelligently organized class, professor is not interesting or thoughtful

Disappointed. In such a print heavy program, I was looking forward to learning the foundations of multimedia. However, I'm leaving with only a frustration with the professor. Leo dishes out failing grades with minimal feedback. His lectures don't correspond with what he grades projects on and his exams do not test learning, but seem aimed to trick.

Among the worst profs Ive had in 4 yrs at OSU. His tests are filled w typos & grammar errorsbeyond what a language barrier couldve caused. He picks poor material to cover, doesnt explain it well, then gives 5 quizzes & a cumulative final on it. Design & written tests do not mix; the actual Design Dept. forgoes them altogether. This class had 7.

I was hesitant to take his class after reading looking at the reviews, but it was easily my favorite class I've taken in college. He is hilarious, and the projects are fun. I guess don't expect a super easy A, but his grading seemed very fair to me. Gives plenty of fair warning about the pop quizzes. Definitely disagree with most reviews on here.

I think that Leo is getting a bad rap on this site. The truth is, the man obviously cares about what he does, and he has a lot of experience to match. There are around 5 assignments that you will do for the majority of your grade. There are assigned readings, which aren't necessary if you attend class and pay attention. Don't procrastinate.

What's important to understand about Leonardo's class is foremost that it is Photojournalism based. Photojournalism, as opposed to photography is very subjective, there isn't much room for artistic expression in it. Leonardo's class is structured around this and he dose a great job of emphasizing the work required to make it the field.

He's Argentinian, and he's hilarious. Very confident guy. The toughest part about this class is that each grade is subjective, and that you can't skip. He takes attendance, but if you love this kind of subject the class really shouldn't be a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Arrogant and unhelpful. We were forced to listen to a condescending turd who is more interested in hearing himself talk than teaching anything beneficial. Gives vague and unhelpful critisms/ grades harshly on every project. He clearly grades based off of his personal preferences and wants next to no individual expression in the projects. Bad class!

Rubrics are vague, grading is subjective and unjustified, and attendance is required - 10 points per class with pop quizzes. Extremely arrogant and unwilling to show specific examples of what he's looking for in a design or project, so it's impossible to know if you'll get an A. Do yourself a favor and take this course with any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Instructions on assignments are unclear; he has no grading rubric. If he doesn't happen to like your designtough luck.  Has an arrogant air about him. Easily frustrated when questions are asked, as if his tutorials are the golden standard. He is absolutely emblematic of all that is contemptible about higher education.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: if you are signed up for this class, drop it and take it with a different professor.  It is impossible to satisfy this man no matter how good your completed work is.  The work you put in ends up being pointless because you will not be able to achieve the grades you deserve, especially based on the minimal things he actually teaches the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Leonardo says he grades his course tough because he understands that OSU's journalism program doesn't have the best reputation. Trouble is he's a big part of the problem. Lectures are jumbled and insufficient training for the quality he expects. Course only exists so the school of comm can feel better about the lack of multimedia training they give

He is not a knowledgeable lecturer. You will learn from this class by just working on the homework. Since he's a tough grader, it's not a good class to boost your GPA. He won't let you makeup for what you missed. Doesn't care much.

If you have the option to take the class with another instructor, do that. Gives pop quizzes, 2 homeworks every week, big projects, and mandatory attendance (only except if you're sick). He doesn't have standards for grading, you can meet all the requirements but if he doesn't like your design you'll get a bad grade. Doesn't explain the concept

Leonardo is very unrealistic with how much time he expects you to have outside of class to take photos.  There are many assignments and If you do not have a lot of free time outside of class, work, etc, I wouldn't recommend taking this class.  Don't expect to get an A for taking average photos, you'll have to work for it.

Leo loves what hew does, which unfortunately means that all students are expected to drop everything else they're doing and take pictures all over the city. The assignments can be hard and you shouldn't take this class unless photographing people is what your passion in life is. If that is not the case then get out while you can.
Exams weren't bad if you reviewed the lecture slides he provided. Attendance was mandatory & class was sometimes extremely boring to sit through.

Leonardo loves what he does.  He is so absorbed in his area that he thinks his students should make his class their one and only priority.  But, a little studying before exams got me easy A's.  His threats for extremely hard tests and grading turned out not to be anywhere near as hard as i was expecting from his self evaluation.

Celia is pretty amazing as teacher. She's energetic, understanding, informative and just plain awesome. She makes the material enjoyable by breaking up her lectures with small group discussions. Participation matters so be sure to either participate in lecture or in the small groups. She's a bit of a tough grader tho but ask her for feedback after!

Celia's Spanish class has been the best class I have taken at OSU. She is energetic and fun. She makes a boring subject really interesting. Attendance matters and there are participation points, however, if you talk to her she is very understanding. She answers back to emails quickly. I would absolutely recommend this class
Lecture for this class was so incredibly boring, and she was not very helpful.
Her lectures are incredibly dull and go on for ages. If you are taking this class, skip the lectures, and watch a YouTube video on the topic, you'll save yourself an hour and a headache.

Youtube will be your best friend because she overcomplicates everything but as long as you know the functions and how to use them you'll be more than fine for labs and tests. If you do struggle during labs, the TAs are very helpful. She reads directly off the slides but she welcomes questions so take advantage of that.

Genuinely one of the worst instructors I have ever encountered at this university. Her course is horribly boring, she drones on with little room for questions and hardly ever stops to insure that students understand where the functions and information is coming from, if you can take this course somewhere else or with a different professor do it.

Directions are terrible for the most part. Some pre/labs took ridiculous amount of time, but manageable. Some more confusing topics were not explained thoroughly-had to teach myself quite a few things. I'm not good with computers, but don't think this class had to be as stressful as Grimme made it. Easy enough class, but really disliked the prof.

Overall an outstanding professor. Explains everything very thoroughly, as everything from the lectures is what shows up in the prelab/inlab/ exams so they are not overly difficult. Is always willing to answer questions, and really wants students to do well in the class, as this class will be really helpful, especially the excel portion.
Never once posted a key for pre-labs or in class labs, so you never know why you are getting points taken off of assignments, and doesn't give clear grading criteria.

She has a horrible attitude. She is very snippy when you ask a simple question, yelled at students for small things such as grabbing papers, or signing in before she was ready for you to do so. Rarely was able help with questions, and grades hard.

The class is composed of lecture and labs. If you go to lecture, do the pre-lab on time and do the lab you will be okay for the midterm and final. This class can be time consuming so spend time studying and reviewing. Overall a doable class, A is possible if you follow the syllabus and show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cindy is great at explaining concepts and will always help if you need it. The class itself is pretty simple if you attend lectures and do your pre-labs!

Cindy was a good professor for this class. She runs her lectures and labs by following the slides and instructions closely, so it can be a little bit slow at times. But she is very helpful if you ask her questions one-on-one. The class is broken down into very managable lectures and labs.

Thought this class would be more difficult but Cindy is super helpful and breaks content down really well. Labs are more useful than the actual lectures and the midterm/finals are not bad if you study.

The class is ok I guess, if you don't know excel and access the class is beneficial but I feel like I learned more from the labs than the lecture itself. But the lecture isn't all useless. Easy class if you know your excel functions and basic access stuff it all pertains to the labs so if you know those you'll get an A. Super laid back overall.

I had Dr. Cioletti for 4411. She was one of if not the BEST instructors I have had at OSU. She is well prepared and engages with the students well. She is very approachable and transparent. She sets the students up for success but expects them to do the work themselves, which has taught me how to be self-sufficient. 10/10 would recommend!

Prof. Cioletti is great. She is knowledgeable about what she teaches, cares about your success, and is not very strict. The class (Contemporary Sport in the US) is fairly easy. Weekly/biweekly quizzes, many group projects, and couple of in-class discussion groups. Some of the group projects are relatively interesting. Attendance is important

Prof. Cioletti was great! Super sweet, doctoral student who genuinely wants your input. There's quite a bit of group discussion/project work but nothing difficult.
