She likes participation so speak up! She also brings in some great guest speakers. Friday in-person quizzes and one big podcast assignment over the span of the semester. Take her class!

Take my advice with a grain of salt, I am an electrical engineer with a physics minor. Class was well taught, homework was challenging but useful and Jay keeps the lectures funny, interesting and practical. Exams were hard, but he did curve. Jay was the only physics prof I had during my minor that was both a genius and knew how to teach well.

One of the best professors you can get from physics deprtment!! He knows a lot about physics and follows his own pedagogy inspired by Feynman. He enjoys talking with you if you are prepared and bring some questions. Go to talk with him! You will learn a lot and be amazed by his mind.
I can't praise his teaching enough. His lectures are really well done and the homework isn't too miserable. Take if you can: he's well worth your time

Dr. Jayaprakash is the perfect professor. He is brilliant, helpful, and has an unfathomably deep knowledge of physics. He teaches theory, intuition, applications, maths, and history with informative, helpful and very entertaining lectures. I wish he taught (nearly) every class during my college career because I would have learned so much more.

He was one of the best Physics professor in OSU...He tried to make you understand the concept of Quantum Mechanic perfectly. He always revised the materials covered in the class. His grading was fair too. However, because the Quantum Mechanic course was too hard to learn, I didn't get what I aimed for the grade...Quite rare to see him outside the c

In a word - awesome. His is one of the few classes that makes an hour long commute worth it. Definitely take any class he offers. Most of the prof's here have been good, but he is (so far) the one to beat as far as what a professor should be.

One of the best professors at this university. Great explanations, extremely helpful, and funny. He has great stories to add depth to what you are learning and the intangibles of a great teacher. Took quantum from him which is a difficult subject to teach and feel that I understand this batter than any other subject I have taken. Take his classes.

He puts all of the material for the class online, so you can teach yourself the material if you can't make it to class. When you can make it to lecture, he has many opportunities for extra credit, making the class quite easy to pass overall. I wouldn't say that the class itself is an easy A per se, but Dan makes it so easy to understand & get an A.

Dan is the best! He really helped me understand the material. When I was really struggling with a concept, he would stay with me passed his office hours to help me. I'm very lucky Dan was teaching this class. I recommended it to all my friends.
I loved having Dan as a professor! He is super nice, understanding, and is willing to help his students get an A. Good lectures, but slides online so attendance isn't mandatory. Great class!

What a great prof. He gives out extra credit as incentive to participate, which helps your grade and you understand the material better. He is great at explaining concepts and giving tangible examples. I would want no other microecon prof teaching this class, def take him if you can.
Daniel is really nice person. Easy A if you study.
This guy is hilarious. Helped me a lot to understand the material.

Daniel was awesome! He was only the TA for this course at the time but I learned all the material from him. He held exam reviews for us out of his own time, and was always available to go over the material.

Mardi seems like she cares about her work a lot and seems like the professional who "gets things done." However, she is very condescending and inconsiderate when talking to students, and puts you on the spot in class to critique your work. She is unclear in her expectations and doesn't present the material well. I wish I got more out of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Often nitpicks and twists words just to critique a student for no reason. She has a somewhat condescending way of approaching students, which turned me off. The class informed me of some of the ins/outs of nonprofits/fundraising, but nothing earth shattering. You have to attend class to get detailed instructions, 1 assignment/week, hard grader.
Sure there were a lot of handouts...suck it up/get organized.  I thought it was a great class; however, powerpoint is the way to go...away with the chalk board!
She was late to class a lot.  Gave real world examples.  Just wrote notes on board.
The class was painless and interesting.  She engages the class well and keeps the subject matter interesting.

DO NOT TAKE FROM HER!!!  She changed due dates of major projects at the last minute, handed out so many supplemental sheets of paper that it all became a blur.  Would say things in class and when asked about it later would say "I didn't say that!"  Changing the due dates without warning was the main problem.
She is very reasonable and an easy grader.  She has alot of experience and brings that into the classroom.  I highly recommend her for 745 or 746

Dr. Hirata is the best lecturer I have ever had. While his lectures are very dense, and if you zone out for like a minute, you're pretty much cooked, he provides a very complete understanding of the material, covering everything from derivation to application! Highly recommend his office hours; I genuinely feel enlightened every time!

This class is undeniably the hardest physics course you will take at Ohio State. Chris absolutely does the best he can to teach the material, and he does it well, but I cannot deny the fact that you might be completely lost in this class, so be prepared for that. Great guy, wants to make sure you understand everything, so ask questions!

Professor Hirata actually made Physics 1251 bearable, he is funny and extremely smart, and he always tries to give examples of concepts and show how each equation is derived. The class itself was awful, would not recommend, but if you have to take 1251, definitely try to get Hirata. He is amazing!

Dr Hirata is a brilliant guy, but sometimes that can create a barrier between him and his students. His lectures are very deep but you can get lost very easily if you aren't paying full attention. You might miss one detail during a lecture and the rest just doesn't make any sense. His exams are incredibly difficult, but a 75 ended up being an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Only received an A+ because of the 20% coronavirus curve. This class is so incredibly hard. Hirata is a very smart and nice guy. I can tell he wants to help his students. His knowledge however is just so above my basic understanding so it was hard to get on his level in lectures and actually understand what was going on. He tried though, he was new

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. Both the final and first midterm had failing averages. That said, the curve is great. 75% and above was an A. If you do all your work and study the curve will get you a decent grade. He cares about his students and uploads all his notes online. You mine as well take a class with OSU's resident genius.

He is a caring guy, and available outside of class but his exams are so hard and the quizzes too. He gives practices exams and quizzes they are hard but doable. When it comes to exams my friend hold you belt tight cause its harrrd. the average of the first exam was 44 and the highest was 80. the final was the same

This was by far the most difficult class I've taken during college, and I don't see anything topping it any time soon. Dr. Hirata made it very hard. Don't get me wrong he is a super caring and genuine guy, but his lectures were basically just complex derivations of difficult calculus equations. 1st exam avg was a 44% and it didn't get much better
Had him for three courses- 101, 102, and 104! Would not have wanted it another way.
CJ is frickin gawd allmighty!!  I loooove him, plus he's hawt with them piercings!!  His class is a blast!
A really great teacher. He is like another student. I truly enjoyed his class.

her lecture always makes students sleepy, and it's boring if you are not interested in human geography. But there are only 8 map quiz, 4 exams, and no finals. You'll get a good score if you try to memorize the worksheet. Maybe it's a little bit difficult for GE, but it's interesting for me to know some human geography all over the world.

The most boring class ever. She talks about 1 slide for 30 minutes. Half the class doesn't even show up. Then she expects you to know SO MUCH for the tests that are taken at the testing center. She doesn't realize this is just a GE for everyone.
Not good
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She forces you to go to the stupid testing center instead of taking exams in classes.
Terrible professor, boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Thank you.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Good professor,
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Porfessor Chabot is a great and kind person. When I encounter difficulties she was always willing to help me. She is also a great teacher, if you do the work you will have no problem.
The class was way too difficult. You are expected to remember everything she said during lecture. Tests and quizzes are taken in the testing center. I worked pretty hard and only earned a C+
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cindy Chabot has been my professor for 3 different geography courses, and she's definitely my favorite. She is very kind and is quick and generous with grades. Many comments on here appear to be students who may have blown off the class or not been interested in geography. If you are serious about college, she's a great professor.

She's an amazing lecturer. The course is very interesting and she adds some anecdotes that can help connect to the material. The grade is based on 4 exams and some map quizzes. I never bought the textbook, which you can get by on doing only if you attend every class and take notes on the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Most boring lectures I've ever had to sit through....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class had four exams consisting of mc's, short answer, extended response and extra credit. She gives questions to do as you read through the textbook and an extensive study guide that makes the exams easy. Don't take if you frequently skip class & don't read textbooks. She is a perfectly fair grader and is always willing to help.

A lot of people rate her badly, but I really enjoyed her class. There is a lot of info to know for exams, but she gives very clear study questions and all the essay and short answers are taken from those. She also tells you exactly what you need to read. She's really nice, too. If you take notes in class and do the study guides, you will do well.

Expects ENTIRELY too much. Exams consists of several mc, short answers, and 4 essays. She expects you to know every minute detail. And there are 4 exams throughout the semester. Way too much for a class many take as a GEC.

Most terrible professor I have ever had. She puts WAY too much information the the exams, be prepared to know information on hundreds of countries from the 1400's until present. IF YOU CAN GET DROP THE CLASS, DO IT!!!!!! I promise you will regret taking this!

she is the most boring teacher ive ever had. She literally will spend 30 minutes on a single slide just rambling about nonsense. The study guides are literally 300 questions for each test basically asking a question for every page of each chapter. IF YOU THINK THIS IS ACTUALLY GEOGRAPHY YOUR WRONG! Only extra credit if geography, rest is politics.

This was a great class.  I see a lot of people rated this class low, but professor Chabot makes it very easy to get a good grade if you do the work.  For every chapter she has a study guide with the specific pages you should read and the questions you must be able to answer.  While this is time consuming it is an easy way to get an A.

Class is boring. Harder then it needs to be. Alot of info required for exams. Basically a waste of time. Expected us to know too much when no one cared. extra credit quizzes,optional paper. dont take unless you actually like geography. i regretted wasting money, time and energy on the class.

the class was pretty hard definitely read the book and the study guide she gives, all the test questions come from there, lecture was a little boring but mandatory. Overall funny teacher but makes the class harder than it should be and easy extra credit points!

This class was supposed to be a GEC, and she made it much more difficult. Her lectures were pointless yet you were required to go to them because of the quizzes. She would spend most of the time telling stories rather than actually teaching the material

This is a pretty easy class. She offers easy extra credit map quizzes and the project you have to do is graded very easily. The tests are not bad either, but you have to put some effort in. The only bad thing is you have to read the book and attendance is required and she is pretty boring, but overall should be an easy A- or A

Class is super-easy so long as you follow prof's very excellent online reading guides. Map quizzes are extra credit and project isn't really that hard. Class is pretty dry but a good way to learn about a lot of different places.

This class was very easy but you MUST attend class or your grade gets docked.  Do all the readings on carmen and follow those questions  because those are verbatim on the exams.  Quizzes are all extra credit and can really pad your grade.  Paper is graded tough.

Oh my goodness. I was feeling homocidal in at least 90% of the lectures because they were so boring. The in-class videos were from the 1980's and were just painful to watch. You must read the textbook. Finished with over 100%, but I am not sure it was worth it at all. Take the class with a more interesting professor.
dry

Although the class is very easy as long as you read the book and take the hour or so to study for the 8 quizzes, she is an AWFUL teacher. Not only is attendance mandatory, but you have to listen to her monotone voice talk about things that are irrelevant to the tests. Bring other work or sleep. Class is pointless other than the videos shown.

I don't even know. She talked every class about pointless things that didn't show up on our exams at all, including staying on 1 map for an hour. She seems passionate about the class but it was nothing like I expected and going to mandatory lecture stupid, it would have been better to read the book each 2 hours we had class. Not recommended, sadly.

Very easy class, although somewhat boring.  Lectures were almost painful to sit through, and attendance was mandatory.  Quizzes were a easy, exams even easier, finished with like a 99% or something ridiculous.

Shes a very sweet lady. Sit in the front or else you probably will find it difficult to pay attention. She tends to drone on. As the class progressed it got more and more interesting. Read the textbook material and fill out the study/reading guides she gives you. They are extremely helpful. STUDY FOR THE EX. CREDIT QUIZES. They will save your grade

She takes attendance and you're only allowed 2 absences before it hurts your grade. Also, she gives extra credit in the form of quizzes which is hard to get because you have to memorize like 100 countries and cities combined, no joke. Three tests make up the class so if you don't test well.. not recommended..

She is really nice and always offers students her help. The the class is compromised of 3 tests. She also has about 8 quizzes where she will give you a list of 30-50 countries and cities you have to find on a blank map. On the quiz, she picks only 5 cities and countries which is rediculous! The quizzes can't hurt your grade though, just help it 4%

This lecturer really means well but she habitually underestimates our intelligence. She actually felt it was necessary to define lattitude and longitude for us. Her lectures are highly disorganized which makes it difficult to study for her exams. This has the potential to be a really great class but she skims over important points for trivialities.

To be quite honest it was one of the worst classes I have taken at OSU. She was the type of teacher that after the midterm you would look to the person sitting next to you and say 'What? when did we ever learn about X?'. Pure and complete nonsense.
As the others said, boring class, so bring a book, or laptop, etc. because she takes attendance (or just have a buddy sign the sheet for you).

This class is a joke.  She takes attendence, though lectures are pointless.  Lots of grade padding (10 "cushion" points on the exams) and extra credit opportunities.  She gives you a lot of material to know for the exams, but just fill out the end of chapter questions on Carmen and you will do fine.

I think there is just far too much material for these exams.  There is a ton of material that is fair game to use on the exam and it can be overwhelming.  The homework definately helps boost your grade, but I think the weekly quizzes are just marginally helpful for the exams.

This class is awful.  The tests are pretty rediculious considering you basically dont really know what's going to be on them.  She doesnt give a study guide and just stands up in the middle of class and rambels on for two hours.  Take another 597 class....

This class is so boring. Her tests are ridiculous...you pretty much have to study EVERYTHING...lectures..hand outs...readings...videos...maps, EVERYTHING. She gives u the test format but not a study guide...so you really don't know what will show up. I hate her class. Don't take this is you are trying to fulfill a GEC!

This class is extremely boring and if it can be substituted for another class I would really recommend it.  Attendance probably isnt required if ur not going for an A but the amount of material on the exams is just ridiculous.  Its almost impossible to study that much material on one of the most boring subjects out there, good luck

Easy easy class, tons of extra credit and grade padding, if you can't get at least a B in this class, you either aren't going to class or aren't staying awake. Prof. Chabot is a really nice lady, and simplifies the concepts very well, although maybe a little too well. Either way, do the work and it's and easy A.
The class in itself is reallllly boring but there is tons of extra credit.  If you do all the homework questions and at least half listen to the lectures, a good grade is really easy to get.

shady with the attendence.  does not change grade when its boarder line when a student attendents to all her classes. i and never walked out in the middle of her lectures like others.  find another geog 597 prof.  i heard the other one is a nice person.  her tests are base off the book or lecture.   her avg class grade was c+

She made the class fun and the material easy to understand.  She also had a great sense of humor and was very knowledgeable.  As a bonus, she got me interested in Michael Palin's travel documentaries.

This rating is for HTHRHSC 5900 btw but didn't appear as an option when selecting class code. She doesn't upload lecture slides or anything. Sometimes, she also tosses stuff on the test that wasn't taught. Her syllabus doesn't state that she'll take attendance or in-class participation points but she privately does which is just foul. Avoid!

Dr. Clutter is a pretty good professor.  I enjoyed going to lecture and she made the content enjoyable.  The class isn't to hard as particpation does matter in a way and a semester long projects take up a large chunk of your grade.  The tests aren't to bad but you probably need to study.  I would take another class with her again.

Jill was probably one of my favorite professors! While I took this course for a theme and didn't need to actually know any of the material, she made it worthwhile. She is fun and makes sure lectures aren't boring. She does have some tests throughout, but if you studying even a little bit, you'll be fine.
Jill Clutter was such a joy to experience as a professor! You can tell she genuinely loves what she does! Just pay attention to lecture and take good notes, and you will do great.

Super nice professor and has interesting content. The exams were not super difficult as a lot of the information was intuitive. There is a semester-long group project that is divided into three parts but they did not grade it super critically. Mini assignments during class count as a part of the grade and as long as you show up, you should be fine.

Dr. Clutter is such a joyful and spirited professor. She is also passionate about the course content and will often use anecdotes to help students learn. Overall, she made an 8am easier to wake up for and listen to.

Dr. Clutter is one of the best professors I've had during my time at Ohio State. She genuinely cares about each of her students. The slides she provides are vague so it is important to go to class. The textbook was required, but I didn't open it all year. Her exams take a little more studying than you might think, but overall this class is not bad!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Clutter's apparently vast knowledge of topics we covered, coupled with her skillful personable instruction style, facilitated our curiosity about- and better understanding of the healthcare systems with- and in which many of us now work.

Clutter was exactly like her name. She was disorganized and sporadic. I ended up with a B- in her class because there were few points in the class and she messed up a grade. After grades were posted, I reached out to her several times to get the mistake fixed with no reply. Nice lady, but all over the place and unreliable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Clutter is a great teacher and an even better person. It is clear that Dr. Clutter is at Ohio State because of her passion for her students and her ability to impact our lives. If you have the chance to take a class with Dr. Clutter, please do.

She's great. her tests are not really hard, but you should definitely study before hand. There are only 4 tests and two projects in the class that you get graded on. I told her I was worried about my grade and she waved me off and told me not to worry about it. Spends first half of class talking about "for the good of the cause" (current events).

She is so funny and sweet! Her tests aren't hard per se, but make sure you study and read parts of the book that pertain to lecture. Take good notes. Projects are easy and participation is graded and both with save your test grades. I still got an A. It's also better to not miss class, because she says a lot that aren't necessarily on slides!
incredible

Dr. Clay's class is very difficult, but there is a massive amount of resources available. The homework was extremely tedious, but made the exams feel super easy in comparison. Clay's lecture style is very fast and involved, and forces you to be actively learning in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Clay is incredibly caring and is very accessible to students. He has never made me feel inferior even when I am struggling- and when talking about his "boss" or professional life he makes sure to say "SHE" which means a lot as a woman in engineering. He genuinely changed my life and makes me want to wake up and go to class each morning.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Clay is the best of the best. MEB is a hard class, but Dr. Clay will teach you what you need to know to succeed. He provides tons of resources for students to do well if you put in the work. Plus he cares about his students and really makes an effort to get to know everyone.
Tons of homework and every hard exam. He wants students practice separation every single day and write without thinking during the exam.

MEB is hard but Dr. Clay is very supportive and will help you succeed. His lectures are fast paced but he's good at teaching and his office hours and meeting with him outside of class helped me. His genuine care for students is what sets him apart from other professors, for example he's the only professor I've had here who learns students' names.

Clay is the only reason I could have ever passed this class. Although his lectures are fast paced over hard and new material, he works with that in making time for students and creates ample amounts of office hours with his TA's. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He wants you to succeed in this course, so use him to help you succeed. Only mandatory for quizzes.

Cares deeply about his students and is a very active/encouraging lecturer. Looks forwards to office hours to help guide his students. Class difficulty will be lessened if you meet with him when need be and use his resources.

Dr Clay is always available to meet outside of class and wants his students to succeed. By no means is this class easy but he teaches the class so that if you pass you are very well set up for your future courses. The homework is extremely lengthy but his ta's are super helpful and meeting with them is detrimental to doing well. Office hours!!
good professor gives u all the knowledge but be ready to work.

Messes up while going through examples frequently (some of his solutions are also wrong) and goes through content way too quickly. Gives a ridiculous amount of homework and expects you to make his class your #1 priority. The only good part of this class were the TA's, they will actually teach you the content.
Honestly avoid at all costs. Expect a massive amount of work while taking this class. Don't expect a curve. Students will suck up to him because they want to work at Batelle

Dr. Clay is not only a great professor but also a great person. He cares about each individual's health, well-being, and success in pursuing a chemical engineering career. Sure, the class is tough and the workload is a decent amount, but, for the most part, there really is no busy work - all the work done prepares you well for exams and the future.

Dr. Clay cares a lot about getting to know you personally. Not only is he a great lecturer, he's a fun person to talk to. The workload is a lot, but you'll learn a lot more than you would with another professor. Also his office hours are golden and you need to take every chance you can to go to them. When in doubt, assume steady state.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Name the four ways to find vapor pressure? -Antoine Eqn. -Cox Charts -C.C -Steam Tables Name the five ways to get a Steam Economy greater than one? -High Feed Temp -Solvent other than water -Multi-stage -Super Heated Steam -Vapor Recompression #Assume steady state
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Clay is a real gem. He strives to know you by name and forms an interpersonal connection with you during his office hours. His love of memes is unmatched, and he's always available to help if needed. Yes, his class is very difficult, so expect lengthy homework assignments that are impossible to complete without help from the TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Clay is a great lecturer and has an emphasis on applying the material to problems. I swear by his office hours, and you can tell that he really cares about the well-being and success of his students. His class is definitely challenging, but if you put in the effort you can do well. He is a real gem.

I am not sure why he is rated so highly. He gave a ton of homework, made zero connection with me, and was incredibly fast paced. His hand-picked TAs told me they they could not help me on a question. My expectations were high, but were not met. I also wanted the good news first.

Clay is an excellent professor; however, he is very difficult and has a teaching style that some may not like; he puts people on the spot all the time in lectures. Overall, he is difficult, but you really learn the material and if you can get past this class with a good grade, you will be fine in your later chemE courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Clay does a great job teaching this course, but there is A LOT of homework. The best way to describe his teaching is tough but fair. He goes out of his way to be accessible to students outside of class to ensure they understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Clay is the best! If you have the choice, always pick Clay. He is preparing students for the real world, so you will have to work hard, but it is definitely worth it. Go to his office hours as much as possible. He is very helpful in a smaller setting and he never makes you feel stupid!!

I did better in Clay's Separations than in his MEB. Still, he gives lots of homework, moves faster than you thought possible, and loves to give hard exams. His lectures weren't as helpful in separations as in MEB, but he still explains things very clearly when you ask questions/go to office hours. If you put in the (lots of) work, you'll be okay.

Dr. Clay's class is probably one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. His exams are pretty hard and time constrained. His lectures and homeworks do a good job preparing you. Dr. Clay expects a lot from his students but he is a very nice person and a good professor. I learned a lot from him even though my grade wasn't the best. Prepare to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best (and toughest) profs/teachers I've ever had (Fall 2018). I learned a LOT in his class. However, to do well, his class really has to be your top priority. Homework requires a decent time investment, and you really need to also do the supplementary worksheets he provides to prep for the quizzes/exams. He is very helpful 1:1 as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Solid professor overall, but moves at a quick pace. He only uses slides to teach, which I don't find very effective, but it is quick and gets the job done. Flexible professor and knows his stuff well. Highly recommend talking to him since he gives good advice and is a nice guy overall. Curve is small, my 92 got curved to an A and about 16% get As.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is the only professor I've ever had who truly cares about his students. That being said his class is very very time consuming and tough. Clay gives you opportunities to excel but you have to be willing to put in the time week to week.

If you truly care about material and high volume work causes you not to learn well, don't take his class. He's a nice guy, but picks favorites. He will make you feel like he thinks your smart, or you will succeed in his class in the beginning but as soon as you start to struggle a little bit his attitude towards you changes completely.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: For a 3 credit class the work needed was more along the lines of a 6 credit class. The homework and tests are unnecessarily difficult, but you definitely learn the subject very well. Dr. Clay is the most caring and accessible teacher I've ever had. I hated the course, but I really didn't want to let him down and that pushed me to work harder.

He was a great professor, probably the best I have ever had! He went through the trouble of memorizing the name of every person in the class, so clearly he really does try to connect with the students and help them. He is very clear in what he expects you to learn and provides lots of actually helpful and relevant resources.

Dr. Clay may be tough, but because of that, you will 100% learn something in his class. He's always willing to help (even in matters outside of academia, like job preparedness), and in fact lent me some books to read because I was feeling a bit uneasy about my job search. He cares about his students, is a great lecturer, and very knowledgeable. A+

Dr. Clay is the best professor I have come across in the Chemical Engineering Department at OSU. He explains things well in his ppts, and he will go out of his way to help his students understand material as long as the student reaches halfway. Definitely homework heavy, but I've never learned so much and understood so much from a class before.

Don't take him if you struggle with anxiety. He will stress you out to no end and then not help you when you need it. He is good in class and can explain topics well but he is very harsh and causes more stress than necessary. I don't like him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He has too high expectations for the 3 hour class

Dr. Clay is by far the best professor I've had. His class is definitely harder compared to the other lecturers, but I'm sure it'll pay off in the future. He'll tell you that his 3 main focuses are on 1) teaching you what you need to know 2) your mental health and 3) your happiness. He's easy to talk to and explains material clearly. Exams are long.

He's not just a professor. He's a coach. He takes pride in the quality of students he trains. He's the sort who might randomly call on you and ask for fifty pushups. You'll spend >10 hrs on each weekly problem set. Exams are a time crunch and even fail straight A sophomores. If you hate working a lot, don't take his class. Also switch majors!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He is the best prof I've had so far! Super encouraging, friendly and makes the effort to know everybody in the class. He was genuinely interested in us and although I found the class very challenging he will always help and answer emails.
His class model is to teach you how to deal with a ridiculous amount of work, but is also set up to where you have to go to his office hours if you want to do well.
He will put you on the spot, but is most likely the most knowledgeable professor I have had to date. Unit ops papers suck, but that really isn't a product of the professor.

Clay is by far the best prof I have ever had. He challenges students by giving them tools to think on their own, but offers help in doing so. He goes above and beyond what is necessary. Don't understand a concept from lecture? He'll simplify it and you'll have it down within an hour. He offers an incredible amount of resources out of the classroom.
He will be the best professor you ever take. Lot to learn from him, worth all the effort he expects.

Daddy Clay is one of the best chemE profs at OSU. Very nice, loves to get to know you on a deep and personal level, and overall a chill guy. Lots of homework, but honestly this course is really cool and the information is very informative.

He's nails.  He will help you to the best of his ability at any time, even during the tests and quizzes.  He comes in on weekends to hold review sessions and takes all regrades seriously.  The only downside to him is he will make you work.  We probably did near 200 long problems for homework.  Best teacher I have ever had.

Great guy and professor. Really tries to get to know you. Is very helpful in one-on-one situations. Class moves too fast for him to get into too much detail during lecture, so if you have questions, ask him during office hours. HW is long, sometimes quite tedious. Quizzes and tests are straightforward and you get a cheat sheet. Overall good prof
Great professor all around, takes personal interest in students.

By far my favorite professor I have ever had.  He will learn everyone's names in the class by the second week and he really cares about his students.  The most approachable professor I've ever had and is always willing to help.  Expect to spend a lot of time out of class on homework because he makes you work. But hey, that's what college is for.

Clay gives pop quizzes. They're only pop quizzes if you don't go to class or you aren't paying attention, otherwise it's pretty obvious when he's hinting at having one. Clay is probably the best professor I've ever had. If you're struggling, go to office hours. The story about surprising everyone with pizza during a blizzard is true. That's Clay.

Very approachable, nice, and genuinely cares about teaching. He'll MAKE YOU WORK your grade but by the end of it you'll realize he is probably one of the best instructors  you'll ever have. Plus he understands that GPA matters and curves very generously. Took him during his first year teaching and he'll only get better.

Dr. Clay is someone the genuinely cares about his students and their progress in the class. He really wants to get to know you, so that you feel comfortable going to him for help. While his lectures weren't necessarily helpful when it came time to do the homework, he is more than willing to meet with you in or out of his office hours for help.

Dr. Clay makes the class tough, and you are going to have  to work for your grade. However, he will make sure that you understand everything no matter how long it takes him. This guy showed up the night before the exam in a blizzard to bring pizza and to hold a review session because he cares about his students! Ask questions and you will be fine.

Clay is a great guy and really cares about his students. Unit Ops just plain sucks. Grading varies from TA to TA and the reports are very long, but manageable in the given time. Clay's lectures are decent but his exams don't test knowledge they test memorization (AKA if it's not on your cheat sheet you're screwed.)

This applies only to Separation Processes.  I have heard that Dr. Clay is excellent when he teaches other classes.  However, in CBE 2523 he very lacking.  The majority of the information you are tested on is not what he goes over in class.  He spends a lot of time on information that is interesting, but not important.  TAKE DR BRUNELLI!!!!

John Clay is one of the most intellectually stimulating professors you can have.  He always has a question that will stump you, but he makes you stop and think because he knows that you can come up with an answer for him.  HOWEVER, unit ops lab reports are the absolutely worst thing you will do in college...

Great guy.  Really loves chemical engineering.  He is clear that he expects you to work hard but he makes sure you know he does it for your own benefit.  Lots of pop quizzes (go to lecture).  Homework took a while but helped solidify concepts.  Tests were difficult because of heavy time constraints.  Be smart and work quickly on exams!

Really cares about students. Tests start out easy but get really hard really fast. Homeworks are very long but help a lot. If you have the chance to take him, do it. You'll work really hard but it will be worth it

Very clear in his lectures. Tells you what he expects from you in order to do well. One of the few 8 am classes I have had were I didn't doze off into sleep. Always willing to help students. Some HWs are long but they help you understand the topic. Don't expect this to be an easy class, it may come off as such but it will get difficult in the end.

Best professor I have ever had the privilege to have at OSU. He was incredibly clear, cared about his students more than anybody I have ever met and is an all around good guy. The class wasn't easy (welcome to ChemE), but he graded fairly and there was a curve at the end. He was willing to do anything to make sure you got the grade you wanted.
Easy class, gets the job done, don't even need to go to lectures once you get the hang of it

Dull lectures that don't require attendance, but I'd go especially on review days before exams because she gives bonus info to that she doesn't post online to those who show up. Always willing to help with any questions and the TAs during lab time are pretty helpful too. Class isn't hard, just budget time and do all labs to the best of your ability

Super monotone professor, but is helpful outside class. Her lectures make you super sleepy. The 3 exams are multiple choice and out of 150 points (no final). There's 9 Pre Labs and In Labs you have to complete every week, Pre Labs can be super long. In Labs are easy and the TAs are nice.

I enjoyed this class by the end. I expected it to be easy, so I ended up getting a little overwhelmed. Once I put more time into this class, it was easier to understand. The labs were a lot of fun to complete, but make sure you stay on top of them. They can save you if you don't do well on exams, as the exams are 150 points and only 15 questions.

Claire does a good job explaining the lectures, although they can become very boring. She is very helpful during her office hours if you need help. lots of HW and busy work to boost your grade as well in case you don't do well on a test. Just stay on top of the pre labs and in labs and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: would not recommend her - rude, superior, no help when needed

Straight forward class with 2 exams and an online final test. Professor Claire is a nice person and willing to answer students' questions. However, she is somehow pushing fast in her lectures and you might need to do some self-study after class. The excel & database pre-lab and lab assignments are time-consuming but the attendance is not required.

A good teacher, very boring lectures however. Really monotone but good at going through excel, which can be hard to teach in lecture format. Overall good at explaining how to learn excel. Class itself is useful but very meticulous yet not hard, but each lab and prelab has very specific answers/requirements that can take a long time to complete.

Went to about 5 classes at the start of the semester. Excel really can't be taught in lecture form, so I just stopped going and figured out everything on my own. Really easy class. Accidentally missed a whole pre-lab and I still finished with an A. Quizzes are harder than the exams.

Very straightforward, rather boring lectures but easy to work with. Assignments are also straightforward and are related to the lectures. Two exams that are not hard at all as long as you've been paying attention and study. Just go to lecture, pay attention, do the labs, and study before the exams and it's an easy A. Feedback could be better.
so terrible

The way she designs her class is awful, it's impossible to do half of the things you need to because she doesn't explain anything and just uses the notes from the book. While she is nice and answers any questions you have, the only reason people go to class is to ask questions, not to pay attention. Basically, if you can avoid this class, do it.

Professor Collins is my favorite professor I have ever had at Ohio State. He knows everything about both Statics and how to TEACH to a room full of 20 somethings. He is extremely engaging, breaks every single concept down and relates to previous knowledge. I enjoyed statics from Physics 1250, but I absolutely love it now. Lectures are incredible!
Fantastic professor. Understands the gloomy overhead of his and does his best to make it a better environment. Engaging, funny, and understanding.

Collins took over my Statics 2040 class when the old professor left for health problems. He was nice but had a different mode of delivery that was harder to understand. The midterms also got noticeably more difficult when he took over. He would take a problem and add a component we never worked on to it. Over all difficult but nice.

Prof. Collins embraces that his class sucks and does a great job at keeping lectures engaging and helpful. One area that could improve is use of Carmen. Notes and practice exams were not posted, which made studying harder. Overall, he's a strong instructor who explains difficult material well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Like others have said, this was not an easy class. Despite this, Prof Collins did a great job of taking difficult concepts and making them seem almost elementary during lectures. He is also a fairly lenient grader, and set the course up so that you could not do great on one of the exams and still get a good grade.

The goat. Great lectures, definitely need to read the book to learn well in the class, but the lecture examples were very helpful for midterms and finals. Always made sure we got our bang for our tuition dollar. Class is hard, but he covered it simply. Thankfully, there is a 5-6% curve for the final grade

This guy embodies what I expected when I decided to major in engineering. Its easy to tell he cares about the subjects and loves teaching. His passion is unparallel and his office hours are very helpful. Only caveat is that the test and material is hard so do yourself a favor actually go to class, pay attention to the dude, study and you'll do fine

He taught very well and was clearly interested in teaching. He taught in a way that you understood what and why you were doing something as opposed to just knowing how to do it. He was very helpful in office hours, and his written homework was interesting and gave practice in solving problems numerically using MATLAB and Simulink.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The majority of professors in this department should take notes from this guy. He made an unbearably boring subject somewhat enjoyable. Clearly is interested in helping students learn and most enthusiastic professor I've had here.
goated prof, would take his class again if he teaches technical electives in the future.

He took something as boring and intimidating as system dynamics and made it interesting. He taught the course in a way that made sense and was one of the professors I got the most benefit out of when attending office hours. The only negative is he posted very little, if any, of the post lecture material online, but that didn't seem to matter.

Absolute legend, and I didn't even do very good in his class. Paul is one of the nicest teachers I've ever had and he actually cared about all his students. He also likes to start class off with random conversations about whatever the students want to discuss, whether it be sports, weekend activities, or pointers (his favorite).
absolute goat
The guy knows what he is doing and has great lectures that teach the content very well. He is also always available to help with assignments and is really chill.

Paul is the best; he is so easy to work with and talk to inside and outside of class. Definitely take this class with him because he makes it so much more manageable and enjoyable over the course of the semester. He is also so funny and will never fail to make you laugh. Class is a lot of work, but the grading criteria is clear.

Clingan was a great professor. I had him for both ENGR 1281.01H and ENGR 1282.01H. Both of the courses are structured by the FEH program, so the content of the class is not really up to him. Clingan did an amazing job though. He's funny, caring, and gives great lectures.
great guy. class is fun and he is fun. nothing bad to say. pretty easy A as long as your group stays on top of everything.
Paul cares about all of his student's learning and teaches in a fun and engaging way.

"A pointer
is a variable
that has as its value
the address
of another variable."
Great at teaching and super funny too. He made a difficult class the most fun one I've taken. Textbooks were offered, but I never bothered to read them since the same material was covered in class anyway.
Amazing guy. Genuinely funny and cares about the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best instructor for this course; you'll definitely get an A if you submit all the work and it's done competently, but you'll have to pour in tons of hours outside of class to finish the assignments in the first place.

GOAT. Amazing lectures, super caring, funny, and understanding professor. Make sure you go to class, if you Fundamentals of Engineering is a hard set of courses, honors or not, so be prepared to do a LOT of homework. His lectures helped me a lot with understanding how to do homework. Very nice guy
goat
Good teacher, tells jokes during lectures to keep it entertaining

My only gripe with Professor Clingan was how hard it could be to hear him at time in the class especially if you sat further in the back. Overall, he was a wonderful teacher, note that the readings and paying attention in class are extremely beneficial especially if you have no background in computer languages.

Very fun lectures and labs, however, this is a LOT of work for a 2 credit hour class. None of it is exceptionally difficult, but you're at the mercy of the teammates that you are assigned. Paul is an incredible professor and makes the class very fun to get involved in, and my lab team became some of my good friends. Highly recommend his class

Paul was one of the kindest and most resourceful professors that I have had thus far at OSU. He truly cares about his students and makes the at times boring content more lively with his humor. He offers great advice and is willing to sit and help students with various assignments!
Clingan is a fantastic, funny, and caring professor, and while the course is very difficult as is, Clingan does his best to make it as manageable as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had Paul for the FEH Nano project and definitely would recommend him. He is super laidback and has an extremely dry sense of humor. He's pretty approachable and cares about his students. Even though he's not an expert in nanotechnology/microbiology, he does his best to help you through the project along with the TA's.

Paul made a class that I was scared to take fun and mostly not overwhelming, even though it was a lot of work. He is funny, kind, genuine, and considerate. He always checked in on students for questions, comments, and concerns, and he actually listened and provided help or solutions if there were any. Even online, he was a fantastic professor!

Paul is just an awesome guy. FEH is a tough class both semesters, but he cares about his students and does his best to help you succeed. I thought he had a great sense of humor, and he was always available when I needed help.

FEH is a demanding course. With that being said, none of the problems I had in the class were with Clingan. He is an amazing person who deeply cares about how each and every one of his students is doing in class. He has a ridiculous amount of office hours too. One problem is that sometimes he moves a little fast, but his other qualities redeem him

Paul Clingan is an excellent instructor. I highly recommend him for the first year honors engineering courses. Most of the instructors chosen by FEH are of high caliber, and Clingan is no exception. There will be a lot of homework, but if you pay attention and go to class you will learn a lot.
Awesome dude

Mr. Clingan is a great professor. He knows the class is a lot of work regardless of how it's taught, so he makes it as bearable as he can. He lectures for about half an hour at the start of lectures and the rest of the time is yours. If you have any issues, he will do anything within his power to fix them and genuinely seems to like teaching.
You must stay on top of all of the work to pass this class.
Great guys, willing to help you if you need it. I like his sense of humor, his jokes help make the tough project a little more bearable. TAs do most of the grading.

ENGR 1282.01H is a very time consuming class for 3 credit hours, but it isn't very difficult in terms of grading. The robot project was very time consuming but not nearly as much as you may have heard. As long as you do the work you should get an A. The beginning SolidWorks section was fairly difficult though.

ENGR 1281.02H has a lot of homework, but as long as you do all of it you should get an A. The course is fairly standardized so your lecturer doesn't matter too much, but I found Clingan's lectures to be boring with too much forced "comedy". You can skip half the lectures and still get an A, however, as the content is fairly easy.
Would recommend. But NOT the .02 version. The advanced programming simply assigns more work. It will NOT help you learn more programming. Definitely just take 1281.01
Paul is a good guy, loved his class. Would recommend for FEH.
He's an good lecturer and overall great dude.  I don't remember the content in the class being to difficult.  He's very supportive during the extremely intensive robot project.

I had Paul for ENGR1281 and the robot project. He is absolutely hilarious and really easy to talk to. One of my favorite professors at OSU. His lectures are short, so be prepared to read the slides before class.
All around great guy. He wants you to succeed and truly cares about his students. He's super funny too. Really nice guy.
His videos about C and MATLAB  were the greatest pieces of art to ever grace my eyes. FEH is hard but Mr. Clingan is a great instructor.

Paul's a really good professor to have if you are being introduced to programming.  He spends most of the class walking around helping people after a short lecture.  TAs also were very helpful and personable.  Highly recommend his class, that being said, it is difficult and you better be ready to get Bs and Cs on things  you worked very hard on.

Paul was my favorite professor last year. He was so funny and helpful on everything and truly tried to get to know each of the students personally. He was clearly intelligent and loved helping students. I ended up changing my major out of engineering but I would take his robot class again for sure! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Paul has been by favorite professor in my first year at OSU. Extremely funny and really wants to get to know you. The 1282.02H class was challenging in terms of workload but Paul truly does his best to make it easier on the students. He's very supportive and always there for you. Overall great professor.
Paul is hilarious. He wants to help you learn.

Had Paul for first semester of FEH and Robot. Excellent teacher! His quirky sense of humor always makes class enjoyable. Probably one of my all time favorite teachers. If you are getting ready to take robot, have fun with it. It was the toughest, most rewarding, and most enjoyable classes I have taken.

Paul Clingan was my favorite professor I have had thus far in college! He was great at explaining the topics, making examples that were fun and interesting to the students. He has a dry sense of humor, but his jokes are hilarious and he will crack multiple jokes throughout the course of the class period. He and the TAs were also very helpful.

Class was the easiest I had first semester other than survey.  Paul makes it short and sweet during lecture and the class is easy to get a good grade in as long as you keep up with the assignments.  Worst part of the class was my TA experience, watch out, they don't want to help you.  Ask Paul directly when you have questions if you want help.

He "teaches" for all of 25 minutes of the 2 hour class and then left.  The TAs were the only ones there to help, but they always had to reference the key to help with questions.  You can go to his class, drop off your homework, and leave.  He does not care if you are there.
A terrific professor. Humorous, understanding, down to Earth. Truly a pleasure to have as a faculty member. Love this guy!

INCREDIBLE! Paul makes everything extremely clear from day one and is always willing to help. He is very knowledgeable in all matters regarding computers and he also makes class fun! You will likely hear between 5 and 7 great jokes per class period and taking this class at 8 AM was definitely a great way to start the day.

Great teacher. Makes everything extremely clear and is always willing to help. Each class starts with a brief lecture for about 10 minutes and he probably cracks about 6 or 7 great jokes in that time. The class was enjoyable, even though it was a lot of work. Lab reports were tough but you will make it through alive. Welcome to FEH.
Great professor for FEH. Really, really funny and helpful! Made class interesting and kept me awake for lectures even though it was an early class.
A good teacher, though his competence with the advanced stuff leaves a little to be desired.

Mr. Clingan is an excellent professor. He always keeps class moving and interesting. He was sick one day, and another prof. filled in. I could see a difference right away - I was weak on that day's content all the way through the final exam. The lab reports are strenuous, but spreading out the work eases the pain. Get Clingan if you can.
Awesome instructor! Very good sense of humor so I almost always enjoyed class. I'm definitely not a programmer, but he made it possible to succeed. I'm really glad someone recommended him to me.
ask about sexy halloween costume

Paul was a pretty nice guy before class, but once we got to London he started to give everyone a hard time and would offer almost no advice for what to do. I felt as though I was intruding on a personal trip and that he didn't have time for me. If you have the chance to go to London, GO. Just we warned.
He was an amazing teacher. Best I've had yet. His teaching style is really helpful and He makes the dry stuff interesting.
One of the coolest teachers I've ever had. He made the class much more interesting than what it might have been. Highly recommend taking a class from him!
Great guy, quite hilarious, and really enjoys teaching. Very helpful and approachable. Would highly recommend
Awesome teacher! Best I've had in engineering so far! You are very lucky if you get him. He is very approachable and helpful...a great teacher overall!

Clingan is a boss. If you can get him you should he is probably the best teacher i've had at ohio state because hes funny and is such a good teacher its almost hard not to get an A in his class. Nice guy, heck of a teacher. GET HIM

Fantastic teacher. Im not a great programmer but he made things easy by doing real examples on the board instead of muttering through slides already available to us. For all you engineers next year or in future years, make sure you get him. You won't regret it.
God of a teacher.  without question one of the best professors in the business.  Programming used to be hard, this guy fixes everything.  unbelievably amazing.
He is a great teacher that keeps the students interested.
He's a really great professor!  He is helpful and you can tell he cares a lot about his students.  Also kept the class lighthearted and fun even though it was stressful and a lot of work.

Really good professor with a real interest in students.  Will usually always be available to help students who may be struggling.  Some assignments can be difficult, but with the TA help and him around they are easier.  Highly recommended!
Really good professor.  No bull attitude.  He knows the material, and will get through the lectures quickly.  The course wasn't that interesting for me, but he definitely knows his stuff.
He keeps the class fun and light hearted, but the room temp tends to make me want to fall asleep sometimes.  He has an interesting sense of humor though!
He's far and awya my favorite professor. Let's face it, FEH material is exceedingly boring and a pain. At least you can have a teacher who is great to be around!

Awesome prof.  Took him for 192 and 193A.  Willing to help you out of class as much as needed.  In 193A, stayed every day towards the end of the quarter till 7:30 if we needed help in lab or on HW.  TAs like him, you will too.  Everything is reasonable, able to say something in different ways.  Best FEH prof, period.

Professor Clingan is bar none the best professor I've ever had.  He is extremely helpful and cares for his students.  And I'd be willing to bet you he's got a dirty joke to beat any one you've got to tell him.
he is wonderful
Great prof, comical, teaches material well in a "no-bull" fashion, very friendly and approachable, good TA's, knows his stuff
Very helpful, like chipotle, always a plus, gives an opportunity to ask any question in the world at the beginning of class
Baldilocks is my hero
Great teacher!
Nice Guy...Chipotle lover, very helpful, has good TA's!
Bald and Awesome
extremely helpful, funny as all get out, knows his stuff, the one class i could never fall asleep in
Really nice guy, chipotle fan as well, cant go wrong! really helpful, willing to work with students after class, on off days, made this uninteresting subject doable
Great class, very helpful guy. He'll bend over backwards to help you get through the quarter. Go with Clingan or Freuler for your FEH courses. Great profs.

Paul is a great teacher & a cool guy. He has a self depracating sense of humor that's pretty funny. Don't copy someone else's journal entry though! Even though they're worth like zero points That gets you in trouble.
Boring lectures make me sleepy, but other than that he's a good guy, knows his stuff, and down to earth.
Took for a 2 hour matlab course.  Really easygoing nice guy, very clear.  Class had no homework and was easy easy.  Get this dude!
proves that there are actually engineers with a sense of humor.  nice guy, and a good teacher.
Paul lets you call him by his first name because he wants you to be comfortable talking to him and asking for help.
great professor.helps students and understands them.
Good professor. Will work with students out of class if they need help. All-around nice guy.
hes just a great guy, and a great prof.
Easy class, get this professor.
Very good teacher, knows everything about the subject, extremely dedicated to his students. Great Guy, loves Chipotle!

Dr. Mejia is a very caring and flexible professor.  He is an awesome lecturer and took some extra time out of his day for me when I wanted to talk about some extra math concepts.  He was easily one of my best professors here!

Julian is rly nice and often asks if students get confused. Calc is a pretty tough subject, but Julian did lots of practice problems in class and posted his lecture notes. Even though I ended with a c+ that is completely my fault because I often skipped lectures and recitations and was also taking other heavy classes.  I recommend Julian!

Dr. Mejia is a good and fair professor. He is good at simplifying concepts and his lectures are a lot more lively than others. It did feel as if the progression of the semester did take a hit on lectures, but Calc 2 is a pretty concept-dense course, so it is understandable. Anything you could see on an exam, he made time for in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Mejia-Cordero is a great lecturer and knows his stuff. The material of Calculus 3 can be challenging at times, but its very manageable if you make sure that you close gaps in knowledge early, since a lot of things build off of the earlier concepts quickly. His notes are amazing and extremely organized. But SHOW UP TO CLASS. Its worth your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very organized, very prepared, lecture very cohesive, tests not that hard because the tests don't cover that much a ton of material.

Lectures were very clear and intuitive, and he provided guided notes which were clearly organized. Resources were easy to find outside of class, though the homework program used was a bit extreme in length, and difficult to use at times. Even so, the clarity of lectures and quizzes make the drudgery of the homework worth it.
He gives clear lectures and goes through plenty of examples.  His office hours are great and he responds to emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was my second time taking calculus so it was more like a review, but compared to my high school calc teacher this experience was much better. His teaching was efficient and straightforward, so lectures were always engaging and easy to digest. He did plenty of practice problems and was always willing to do more. Absolute Chad if you ask me.

This was my second time taking calculus so I did not have to pay too much attention in his lectures but he is by far the best math teacher i've ever had. He does a lot of practice problems in class and is very clear with his steps and helps you understand why he did what he did in his work.

This guy is very good at introducing new topics to the class and getting them to try simplified practice problems. If you attend lecture and actually pay attention and go along with his in-class participation practice, you should do just fine in this class. I found it to be very helpful. Definitely take Math 1151 with him if you get the chance!

While calculus sucks, this was my second time taking it and he made it much less painful. His lectures are easy to follow and super helpful. He's extremely nice and not at all intimidating. The only bad aspects about the class are things out of his control and decisions made by the department. If you have to take calculus take it w him!
This was the most interesting GE course I've taken, he is so nice

My favorite professor so far here at OSU. He is very understanding and shows clear interest within connecting students thoughts to his lectures. This was a amazing GE to take I would recommend it to anyone interested in learning something new!
This man is a king.

I love this course! Although there're some readings, as long as you're interested in this topic, it's enjoyable to read them as story books. He's passionate with what he does and it's wonderful to take the lectures. If you're sick, just tell him and no proof is needed. Such a great experience in my freshman year!
Very easy grader and accommodating professor. Fun and interesting lectures that I enjoyed listening to.

Prof. Collins is great and clearly is passionate about what he teaches, but the lectures can be quite dull. In my class, he pushed back almost every assignment due to us getting behind, and he is very willing to give extensions for the assignment.

He is one of the best professors at Ohio State! He cares about you as a student and is very understanding of mental health. Lectures can be a bit boring at times but they always got better with discussion. Participate in this class, you won't regret it! A bit heavy on reading at times but extremely doable, along with assignments. Take this class!

LOVED this dude. Very passionate about what he does, and clearly has fun teaching this class. Some lectures can be a bit uninteresting because you have to learn about Eastern Europe and the culture there, and other Slavic things, but still fun to listen to because he's very passionate about it. Heavyish reading here and there, but nothing too crazy
Amazing professor, very funny and caring about students. There's a lot of reading and you're expected to participate in group discussions, but it's a fun subject, so it doesn't seem annoying.

I must say that this course does involve a lot of reading, but the homework and essays are fair in terms of difficulty. I strongly suggest paying attention in class because a lot of the homework answers are on his slides. (:
Very easy overall but very paper heavy. He pushed off so many assignments this semester that we ended up having a huge paper due each week for 5 weeks in a row. It was doable but just frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Collins is an ANGEL! He's the most caring, understanding, respectable, and overall amazing professor I've ever had. He cares about our mental health and makes sure we are okay before anything else. His class is interesting and fun. He is laid back and wants us to succeed. If you show up to lectures and pay attention, you will easily pass!

Dr. Collins is amazing. He is empathetic and command the material like no other. Medieval Russia has been an amazing class. Dr. Collins is a great human being. His lectures are engaging and you don't pay attention to the clock. If he lectured for the rest of the day, I would sit happily. Assignments are cleverly engaging.

Professor Collins is very engaging in his lectures and low key funny. There is one geography quiz thats pretty easy as he guides you specifically whats on it. No homework he gives is particularly hard but a bit time consuming. The midterm and final are take home, and he always gives extensions. Very understanding about mental health. Great GE!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His quizzes are incredibly easy. There is very little homework, and the exam is take-home.

The best professor, hands down! He really cares about his students, as well as you can tell through his captivating lectures that he enjoys teaching the content. Very few assignments with flexible deadlines. Midterm and final are essays. A super easy and fun GE class (it counts for 2 GE requirements). Dr. Collins is funny and truly one of a kind

the coolest dude ever. amazing professor, absolutely taking another class with him. he is so understanding (especially if you need an extension for mental health reasons, i was too depressed to get to class a few days, and he was so sweet about it). he knows everything about russia and makes it so interesting.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! It was a class that you go... you listen and you learn. Short papers every few weeks and attendance are the majority of your grade. He was very understanding and extremely knowledgeable.

AWESOME GUY! Definitely take it if you are looking for a ridiculously easy GE. Takes attendance but class is fun and informative! He'll let you turn in (take home) exams and assignments late if you just ask. He is funny and nice. 2 essay exams, a few assignments, and a geography quiz are the grades. Super manageable and low stress. Take it!

So sweet and loved the topic he was discussing. He does take attendance, but I just had a friend sign me in and I would sign her in when either of us weren't there and we were fine. He doesn't care about deadlines and all of his assignments are essays based off of interpretation and questions from readings. He does take a while to give back grades

Great guy, makes lectures interesting, wish all professors were like him. Super lenient on due dates, but takes a while to return grades. The midterm, final and 5 assignments are all essays, but if you go to class (25% of your grade) you should have an easy time doing them by just paying attention during the discussions and won't have to read much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Be ready to read. Often allows you to have extra time to turn in assignments if you have to prioritize things over others. He understands that you are a human being and that you have a life outside of college.
Super easy. You don't even need to show up.

Dr. Collins is a great professor. He's extremely passionate about the material and keeps the class light-hearted and fun. The class was not difficult at all, and the material was interesting. Attendance is mandatory and 20% of your grade. My only negative is that he took months to return some grades.

There is no better professor suited to teach about vampires than Collins. EVERY class was captivating; the highlight of my day. Assigned reading could be heavy at times but always engrossing. We were able to really explore the origins of vampire myths and Slavic folklore in general. He is captivating to listen to and couldn't be more enthusiastic.

Dr. Collins was a great prof. Always willing to help students, gave really helpful study guides and answered questions quickly via email. He also gives extra credit on midterms, which are not hard if you study. Class was interesting and not only did I learn a lot, it was interesting stuff that I'll remember. I highly recommend his class.
I absolutely loved this class. If you keep up on the reading you will get a good grade. You will become extremely knowledgable about Eastern European vampire foklore.
Great class, great prof. Taught the material well and was interested in helping out. Easy to take notes, exams were well focused and fairly easy to take and do well on
Best teacher ever!!! Extremely helpful and there for you if you need anything. He is very passionate about teaching and that passion will eventually effect you too. Strongly recommended.

This man has single-handly restored my faith in the teaching community. Take Professor Collins, he is fair and extremely helpful with lots of extra credit. This professor has been my best experience at OSU. All he asks of you is to read articles and attend class and you learn a lot especially if your like me with no prior knowledge. TAKE HIM!

The class was not nearly as much about vampires as I was led to believe.  It was interesting, but A LOT of reading.  If you do not do the reading, you will not pass.  Tests are fairly difficult but if you keep on the reading and study hard you should pass.  He's very easy to understand in lectures, but not everyone on the test is from lecture.
No Comments
great prof
I love Doc Collins

Professor collings is amazing! This guy makes the lecture so interesting and loves to get the entire class involved. You won't find another professor who loves what he teaches as much as Professor Collins. Very helpful and friendly, and as long as you keep up with the readings and participate, you're basically guaranteed an A.
Awesome class, he's really into what he's doing, and passionate about having his students being into it as well, He's funny as well, it's a good time
This prof. is a living encyclopedia. Very helpful and interested in the subject matter. Very fair grading, and no surprises on the exams. Take him if you can.
Awesome guy! I had a C going into finals but with the 2 extra credit papers we could write and the easy final, I got an A for the class! Dr. Collins is the s***!
I loved this class. Very easy as long as you read the material (around 3 short readings every class) and go to class. He's eager to help and really funny if you get him talking about the 1980s.
Great class.  All you really have to do is go to class.  I would suggest taking this for a GEC.  Medival 213, medival moscow.  He knows the material very well.  Great guy to talk to.
I took the class years ago but have told many friends to take it and tehy loved it too.  The class is very interesting and it is easy to get a good grade, all you really have to do is go to class!!
Interesting class yet boring at times.  Collins really knows his stuff and is interested in teaching.
Great lectures, spends too much dead air time trying to get students involved in the discussion.  Otherwise very good at lecturing.
Easy class, interesting lecture, easy on the grading, lots of extra credit

very helpful and answered questions patiently. His explanations were clear, thorough, and well-reasoned, making the concepts easy for anyone to understand. He holds weekly quizzes that effectively prepare students for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was always willing to stay after class to answer questions, and his office hours were very accessible. He was always patient with questions and encouraged classroom participation. Moderate amount of homework, but made Calc 3 very understandable and digestible. Exams were very similar to sample exams.
Actually a good teacher and is usually available and happy to help. The midterms and final do look similar to the practice problem sets he puts out, so defintely study those.

He has really improved as a professor. His lectures can be a little tiresome but they are very helpful and he tries his best to make the content make sense. He is heavy on homework, giving out homework from the textbook and also free response questions, however they aren't the most difficult to complete. He also gave extra credit once.
Midterms are similar to practice problems/practice midterms. Pay attention in class and you will do great.

He is a really smart guy knows what he is doing if you ask him questions, overall course is very structured and clear grading criteria, the TAs do hlep as well

go to his office hours if you need help but he also responds to emails with a lot of detail

overall one of the better calc professors
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Quality professor. Runs the course reasonably, is kind and understanding to unforeseen circumstances. Very high quality. Class is super easy as long as you don't make dumb mistakes (like I did). Attendance isn't mandatory but he does take it some days and it's for a grade. Would take again.

Connor was a very good lecturer imo. He clearly explains a topic with a clear definition and describes it in practical terms. He then goes through an example or several examples. There are weekly online homeworks, 3 written homeworks, and a project, but this is all more than manageable. The midterms are easy so getting a good grade isn't bad.
Actually explains topics more in depth than the notes that are posted online and doesn't just read of a slide. Would recommend for Calc 3
Perhaps no professor is worse than him, he gives the impression that it is his task to fail or bring troubles to the students, if there is another professor, do not choose him.

Didn't teach himself, posted videos of other people explaining the topics. Extremely strict with the syllabus, didn't give me some points even though it was a technological error instead of a human error.

I had Connor for recitation as part of a flipped and flexible section of MATH1151, and he was great. His recitations were helpful in recapping and practicing some material in the lectures. You can tell he has a very good understanding of the subject and is genuinely wanting to be helpful. He is also understanding that the class is difficult.

Dr. Cassady made Calculus 1 feel like elementary Algebra. Truely one of the easiest math classes i've ever taken. And it's not because of the content, but rather how Dr.Cassady presented and taught the material.
