Took the class in person and had him as lecturer and TA. Not much HW if you space it out correctly. He responds to emails fast!

Took Math 1151 hybrid, so lectures online and he was my recitation TA. When I visited office hours he was pretty informative. He didn't make the curriculum but the class itself is set up to be extremely difficult and his recitations didn't help nearly as much as my own studying. Really depends on how comfortable you are with calculus.

She is just not a good professor at all. She was hard to understand, and is worse at math than most students. When I did the best on test I did attendance from my dorm room and studied on my own from lecturer notes.
If you take her class, don't even bother going to lecture she doesn't make any sense. Buy the premium version of the textbook and watch their video lessons if you want to understand what's happening.

Very nice professor, but she is a terrible lecturer. Slides are all over the place. Doesn't actually teach just does practice problems. No need to pay attention in lecture, just read the textbook. Overall class content is pretty easy, labs are my 13th reason though.

Her lectures were very boring, and she would focus too much time on individual problems to the point of creating more confusion than clarity. I'm sure part of it was because it was an 8 am, and she is still far from the worst professor at OSU, but it will definitely require some self-teaching to understand. I stopped attending lectures every day.

Was all over the place. 99% of the time I had no clue what she was saying and her notes were not clear at all. She wld jump from page to page on her slides and it made no sense. Very nice person tho. Good luck

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. If you have her, PLEASE switch into another class. The lectures were disorganized. Anne skips slides, which made it hard to take notes. Her handwriting on the board was also very difficult to read. The concepts were not explained fully, which meant that a lot of self-teaching was required. OSU please hire someone else.

she drives me insane her lectures suck, she doesn't set you up well for the course at all. the other chem professors gave such better lectures and practice problems/exam practice. avoid anne co at all costs.

Constantly messed up math in lecture, had to be corrected by students. I did not learn a thing in her lectures. She seems nice but her explanations do not make sense. Avoid her if you can. If you want a good grade in her class, you have to teach yourself the material-also Dr.N's lecture videos are online for 1220.

Her lectures and notes are unorganized, out of order, and ramble on. I got a free peer tutor through the STEM learning center, who was able to get me Dr. N's lecture videos which is the only reason I got a good grade. Even my tutor couldn't understand her notes. I'm sure she's a nice and smart woman, but do not take her as a professor if possible.

Genuinely she is such a sweet and caring person but her class is poorly organized and subsequently taught in an overly confusing manner. Her slides are consistently out of order and the only way any of the content stuck was through my TA. The best chance at passing this class is by actually reading the textbook and doing the homework assignments.

I think Dr. Co is super sweet and she really does care about the students. However, her slides are usually messed up and not in order and the way she explains some topics may not make sense all the time. The chemistry department in general allows very little flexibility so don't expect to have exams curved or extra credit assignments popping up.

Dr. Co is very nice and cares for her students, but the general chemistry here is just bad. The lectures are very boring, and hard to stay engaged. The lab is boring and repetitive and does not teach you much about what you are learning in lecture. 1210 and 1220 are difficult if you do not come from a strong foundation of chemistry.

The professor is very friendly. However, the lectures do not help me pass exams. Even after going to all office hours, I still failed the exams. This is very much because the information being taught is not in line with what is being tested on the exams. The whole chemistry department setup seems extremely backward; I suggest taking chem elsewhere.

Professor Co is very accomplished, don't get me wrong, but her class is extremely poorly taught. CHEM 1220 is already a hard clas,s and having a lecturer who doesn't have the slides in order, doesn't announce homework, and doesn't go as in depth as she should is extremely difficult—having taken AP Chem before, I felt lost every review and exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of times it seems like she doesn't know what she is doing and students have to correct her math. Her lectures aren't recorded, but she posts notes. If you miss a lecture, don't bother looking at the notes because she goes way out of order of the slides. I feel like I learn more from my TA. Please prioritize your professor when taking chem.

She has potential to be a great professor but her hand writing is chicken scratch and it's hard to hear her so my class is averaging a D on the exams. But she's probably one of the nicest professors I've met.

Dr. Co was an ok professor. Her lectures were confusing to follow as the slides she gave us didn't match up with her slides a lot of the time. She's also not the best at explaining some concepts and students would ask questions she didn't have an answer to. She used Piazza for students to ask questions outside of class and that was super helpful.

The curve wasnt fair at the end so make sure to read the textbook and watch Dr. Fuss lectures. And always take the practice exams because those are pretty similar to the types of exam questions. Lab becomes a grade saver

I did equally as much work (maybe slightly less) when I was in 1210 with Dr. Fus. You would have to put in a lot of work outside of lecture in order to understand the content, which includes reading the textbook and doing practice problems from the book. I also suggest reading the book before lecture (the syllabus outlines textbook sections).

Dr. Co is very knowledgable about chemistry but her lecture set up is needing some work. Often, her slides that are posted on carmen do not match the slides she teaches with and that made it difficult to follow. Also, she got behind near the end of the semester and I felt unprepared for the final exam. I did like her recitation set up though.

I taught myself all of chem 1220 because Co is absolutely awful at teaching. Sure she knows what she is talking about, but she is horrible at relaying that info. I attended a few lectures and then gave up because I could teach myself better. Attend Fus's lectures instead to get better grades on the exams.

Dr. Co knows what she's talking about, but isn't great at teaching the material. She doesn't make homework assignments clear, and doesn't set you up very well to do good on the exams. Be prepared to study a ton on your own.

she is kind and tries her best to help. you have to read and actively pay attention in class, but thats true for any chem class. these ratings are extreme, she is smart and knows what shes talking about. I have no skills in chem, so its taken extra reading and watching vids to have a good grade. dont go in with a bad attidude. get ready to work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very little learning that goes on. Practice problems are gone over, but it’s just completing the math and trying to keep up instead of explaining the material which many of the students try to ask during lecture but get too simple and generalized clarification. Lecture is structured to consider the textbook was understood when it was not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the only helpful thing for the midterms has been to study the practice midterms that are given by the chem department. don’t waste time trying to understand the mastering homework she assigns or her “notes”. she is all over the place, extremely disorganized. if you're a neat freak, forget this class.

horrible. lectures are disorganized and it seems like she doesn't even know what she's talking about sometimes. so unhelpful and doesnt teach stuff that is tested on in the exams. save ur time and just go to stolzfus' lectures or watch his videos since the exams are standardized across the chem department.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of these ratings are a bit extreme. Dr. Co is very kind. She answers tons of questions. Yes, the recitation quizzes are a drag, and you have to put in a lot of work and time doing reading and practice problems, but that's true for any lecturer. Dont go in with a negative attitude. These reviews acting as if shes stupid seem a bit misogynistic
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: While chemistry is a hard subject, I found Dr. Co to be very helpful and encouraging when trying to make students succeed. She even took time to host study sessions on Sundays before midterms. Yes, she is a good professor and cares about her students, but reading a book while going through/summarizing lecture notes also helped a lot.
She didn't really help me to understand the material. Easier learning from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She didn't explain the subject well and the exams were extremely difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Need to put in a lot of time outside of class to do well. Prof Co is very available for office hours and she does want students to succeed, but sometimes lectured too much about concepts that are not relevant for our grades instead of spending what little time we have to explain concepts more thoroughly. She didn't know what we did in lab.

Anne Co is possibly the worst lecturer Ive had. She goes through practice problems most of the class period without fully explaining concepts or why she takes in step in solving. I only got through the class by reading the textbook and spending countless hours doing practice problems and practice exams. Lab helps your grade and the bonus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: In class she focuses mostly on solving problems, rather that conceptual content which is what the midterms are mostly based on. She often doesn't even solve the problems fully; she will set them up, give the answer, and tell you to complete at home. However, Dr. Co truly cares about her students and is extremely helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: We are tested on math, how to solve problems in regards to chemistry a lot. Whenever an important problem showed up on Co's powerpoint she would say "Here is the answer, go home and solve it on your own". She wasted lecture time discussing concepts that were irrelevant and I taught myself the class (poorly because chem has always been a struggle).

She knows her stuff but cannot teach it in front of 300+ students. Go to office hours for help. Recommend watching Dr. Fus lecture videos and doing the dynamic study modules if they are available. Lectures are very confusing and not content based but focused on practice problems with no meaning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrendous. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She thinks 3 cubed is 9. She teaches herself during lectures and just gives answers to practice problems without knowing how to Get there. Average is always below 60% and no one gets 100. Worst class Ive ever taken. BY FAR.

Such a terrible teacher, contradicts herself constantly, gives non applicable information, gives quizzes in recitation that are irrelevant and not covered by her. Made me hate chemistry as a non pre med major trying to get a minor in chem. Take honors chemistry if you can.

The worst professor Ive had at OSU thus far. Her lectures were next to worthless: she went through example problems all class without any conceptual information - doing the problems on your own is the same as going. If you are unfortunate enough to get her, I recommend watching Dr. Fus online lectures to get a semblance of conceptual lecture.

The year I took Anne Co was the year that OSU did standardized midterms. She did not prepare the students for this. She never changed her notes or teaching style which great hurt the students. The mastering chem homework was a waste of time that did not benefit my learning of chemistry at all. I just bought a chegg account to do it.

Prof. CO knew the material, but would stand in front of the large class and fly through examples. Concepts were not focused on even though exams were very focused on concepts. Had trouble keeping up with the examples and struggled in the class. She also quickly flys through important concepts that are essential for success in the class.

The only reason i went to lecture is for the learning cat. extra credit and eventually i stopped going for that too considering how much of a massive waste of time it was. I would rather spend 3 hours with my textbook than an hour of listening to this lady ramble. Ive learned more from youtube videos than I have from her lecture. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Co was terrible. She doesn't even seem to understand the chemistry concepts herself, as she is constantly messing up every single example she does. She also doesn't cover the information that are on the standardized exams; she just covers what she wants to.

Every lecture basically consists of watching her fail to do example problems. I am convinced she has no idea what she is doing. She also has this annoying habit of suddenly increasing her speaking volume in the middle of a sentence to the point where she is basically shouting.

All she does in class is examples and she doesn't explain anything. Isn't the point of a lecture to learn concepts? It would be one thing if she explained why she was doing the examples a certain way, but it is basically just copying down her work without explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She was nice but hard to understand at times.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Anne Co is very passionate about teaching chemistry. However, this year the exams were standardized and Dr. Co did not at all prepare students for this level of testing. In review sessions and sometimes during lecture, students had to correct her on problems and even general equations. Lots of mastering chemistry, but it boosts your grade.

The entire chem department has now standardized their tests so don't even worry about trying to find an easy professor. Chemistry is hard either way although Dr. Co does have a better passion for the material then past professors, chem is just difficult in general.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Co is a nice lady, and you can tell that she is trying hard to teach us the material, but there are times that not even she knows how to do the material. Students would constantly have to correct her etc. Also, this year the exams were standardized, and our class was not prepared whatsoever for the incredibly difficult exams.

Most boring lecturer ever. She literally reads off her slides. Occasionally does a simple problem on her slide but takes the whole class to do it. She answers questions during lecture in a large class and wastes time and hence leaves a huge backlog of content. Her class gets curved down. Don't ever take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Co was such a great lecturer. Chemistry is not my favorite subject but she was really passionate about the material and made 8 am lecture exciting. I had to put in A LOT of time outside of the classroom reading, practicing problems, taking notes, etc. but it was manageable. She did co-teach with Dr. Vicki Wysocki which I did not love.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Anne Co is a good lecturer and she provided good examples during class. However, she paced the class way too slowly and the class got way behind. Overall, she's a solid teacher and the class did well, but Wysocki ruins the rest of the class if they ever co-teach 1220 again.

Anne Co is probably the best Chem professor I've had. She's very through in lecture and takes the time to explain stuff and go through calculations. The averages on the tests were high with more than 200 scoring higher than a 90. Chem is tough but she makes it bearable. She really cares about the students

Reading other reviews, I thought, she couldn't be that bad! However, it took only a few classes before she dropped personal information on me. I hope she has a therapist and doesn't continue to use other students as emotional dumping grounds. I have MUCH more to say but cannot within the character limit. In short, pretentious with zero boundaries

DO NOT I repeat DO NOT take a class with this professor at any cost. The worst teacher I have met Treats you like elementary schooler. Made everyone purchase a $90 set of art supplies on the first day of class. Two weeks later she kicks me out of the class because I have a 5 MINUTE scheduling conflict, then refuses to refund me the money.

Course work on the website needs to be rearranged and simplified. Questions regarding the course are not engaging at all. There is lots of information to study but not much time to actually develop the concepts and understanding more. Teamwork is not the best for online courses.

Alison Crocetta is one of the most unwelcoming professors I have ever had. Although I took this class just because I was passionate about the subject, I left the class completely deflated of my love for contemporary art due to her bland, pretentious teaching and bored, closed-off attitude. I got an A, but at what cost? Needs major improvement.

Not a hard class if you pay attention. Two big projects: interview a contemporary artist and a 6-minute presentation. The way the class is set up could be better (ex., being assigned a ? to answer in a group and not even being able to share the answer because time was allotted for only one question). But Alison is not a bad professor by any means
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Alison was extremely serious about the work and wanted everything done in a very specific way even the art projects. She also did not enter a single grade until the semester was over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a fun professor for 2100 and didn't expect anyone to be good at drawing. As long as you put effort into the work, you will do fine. Expect a lot of work during in person labs. The out of class work isn't bad at all. Very very much a stickler for attendance, more than I've ever seen. Other than that, very enjoyable class.
awful and boring but pretty easy to bs through

Never again it was a terrible experience. Every assignment is only a couple points. She didn't teach anything of value. If it wasn't a major course you dropped it. She offended a lot of her students and yelled for no reason. Difficulty is a 4 is because busy work made up your grade, but it was a constant stream. Tolerating her is a 5. No textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A if you're trying to fill a requirement for your art minor/major but the zoom classes are pretty unbearable. She's rude to students and has called out multiple people for "moving around" or being "too distracting" during zoom calls. Not a fun class. Don't recommend taking it if you don't absolutely need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She definitely puts in the work for the discussions, so she expects you to too. It's a lot of reading and videos, but the projects and discussions themselves are well explained and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Had her for Contemporary Art, class was discussion based but structured in a way that prevented disagreement. Tried to reach out multiple times to go to virtual office hours (during COVID) but never showed up. When discussing politics (which come up in the class more than they should) certain views are explicitly endorsed and others are vilified.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She gave mountains of work outside of class, at one point I stopped looking at it and it did not affect my grade. As long as you turn your work in and attend the weekly meeting you should pass this class. She seems like a nice person but I just don't care for contemporary art.

Alison does not seem to consider the challenges students face outside of her class. She laid some of the projects on thick and doubled us up on assignments (one group project), most students are only in it for the GE but she acts like we're all aspiring artists. She hasn't responded to any of my emails and she calls out students during lecture.

Alison is quirky. She is very talkative and often struggles to get to the point when we aren't drawing, as a result she often jumps from random topic to random topic while the students are forced to listen to her. It gets annoying but when we are drawing, she gets more focused and actually provides valuable feedback and advice. A mixed bag IMO.

Alison is usually very happy as long as you make an effort with your drawings. Lots of drawing required for homework, some materials annoying to lug around. She definitely allows for a lot of exploration regarding subject matter. Participation in critique is important, she's happy even if your comment is truly useless/stupid. Willing to help. Busy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Absolutely one of the craziest and weirdest professors I've had.  No very helpful when it comes to projects. Also allot of homework. Although I got an A it was a very tough course.

She demanded way more attention than the rest of my professors combined. She has no office hours and if you decide to email her with a question, don't be surprise if you don't get a reply back. Class average for exam is over an 80, but taking notes for her class and studying for her exam were difficult for me. One of the worst professors I had.

Easy and interesting class, Alison made me have a much higher respect for contemporary art. She was very helpful and I loved that she had guest artists come in and talk. Material was intriguing, and she fashioned the exams to be easy to pass. The only way you could fail is by not attending class, but Alison made me want to be in class everyday.

At first glance you might think Alison is going to be really cool.  If you have an ill-developed sense of personal art, then she may be just what you need--to push you to make bad, esoteric art, just like her.  She's fairly mean, unless you submit before her, and a bad listener.  Avoid taking her classes, unless you're into being told how to art.

Alison has a serious issue with boundaries with students. She conducts these relationships in a completely unprofessional way. She demands respect yet does not know how to demonstrate respect for another human being. The Ohio State University would be a better place without her. Heed the warning, run far away from this woman.
Class was super easy. No homework, just had to do the readings which were posted online (no textbook). Only have 2 exams and attendence that make up your grade

I've never had a professor so self-absorbed or self-important. Treats students like gum on the bottom of her shoe. Refuses to answer student questions, yet insists students answer hers to her exact specifications. If this class was not mandatory, I would have dropped it and waited to take it with someone else.
She was an excellent teacher! She had a real passion for what she was teaching.  I truly enjoyed her class.  As long as you show up and read the articles, the class is easy to pass.

Alison is amazing. She makes you think outside of the box. The class is somewhat challenging but in a good way. As long as you show up to class and complete your work on time, you'll be fine. I would highly suggest Alison to anyone, she is one of the best teachers I have ever had. I'm so glad I was able to have her!
easy and interesting class. she was very straightforward.

I think that Alicen is very smart, explains her ideas clearly and is very straight forwards with what she expects from her students.  I've seen some of her work and she definitely is not a hack however, the impression I get from her outside of class is that she is incredibly insecure and I think this is evident in what usually comes off as conceit.

Easy easy.  Come to class for attendance grade, pay attention, do or at least skim the readings (on carmen...no books req.), study her exam reviews and get an A.  Not a lot of out-of-class time spent.  Recommended.

If you take Art200 with her it will be way easier than it used to be. On the first day of class she said she used to assign writing and lots of reading but has cut it down to almost doing no work now, just show up for class and take an easy midterm and easy final. She's pretty cool.

it's unfortunate that most of the undergraduate student's don't appreciate what Alison has to offer. She really influences the work of the graduate students and she drives you to work harder. i am sorry that there are two different sides of her and very few people get to see how great she can really be.

Not only does she take all of the interest out of what should be interesting, and she talks so fast that you can hardly understand what she says! So bring your computer to type. It was torture to listen to her condescending, narcissistic, self-centered presentations with her haughty idea of what qualifies as art.

Clearly passionate about what she does, but this passion does not translate to her teaching methods very well.  As others have said, very condescending - if you are not an art star, you won't do well with her.  I once created a project she thought was offensive and anti-feminist and she yelled at me so long I finally cried.
This class was ridiculous. She lectures in an annoyingly condescending manner. It makes a class with interesting material tedious, you get sick of listening very quickly!

Alison Crocetta talks about contemporary art with such pompous self importance, it's enough to make anyone sick. She speaks to her class as though they were a group of 3rd graders. She is simultaneously condescending and banal. Sadly enough, some poor souls actually seem to buy into her version of what art must be. Stay far away from her, very far.

Alison is quite eccentric. She is bold and passionate. I found her amusing but I think many students think she is offensive. Attend class on time with an open mind and do the readings and you'll be fine. Oh, and whatever you do... don't plagiarize!
I completely agree with the last comments

She completely turned me off from becoming an art major.  I cannot stand to hear the sound of her voice.  She talks down to her class full of students and is completely self involved in a pedantic condescending and self-important way.

To be honest, Seth was the best professor I've had during my time at Osu. I am not even a Fisher student, but I will hands-down say he is the absolute best. This class does have a semester long group project, but if you put in the effort, you'll do just fine. He will also go out of his way to make sure that you are ready for presentations.
Seth was my boy when I took this class, he is a gem that OSU managed to get. He brought in many amazing area entrepreneurs that provided more than any book could.

Seth has mentioned being roasted on ratemyprofessor jokingly at least a thousand times so far, but he can rest assured that no one in their right mind would roast him. He's one of the top 5 professors I've had during my time at OSU. He's caring to a fault, makes time for his students, is fully feedback based, and makes everyone laugh daily.

Professor Cramer had not taught before my class, but he quickly became one of my favorite professors at Ohio State. He made himself as accessible as he could with his busy schedule, created worth-while projects, and facilitated FANTASTIC speakers. 100% recommend this course to anyone interested in entrepreneurship. I gained great advice from him.

Seth was one of the best professors/teachers I have ever had. Although he had not taught before this semester, his wisdom, value driven course load, and passion for helping students grow was invaluable. He brought real world/practical lessons into the classroom and never assigned busy work (the speaker lineup was stacked). TAKE THIS CLASS!

Seth is probably one of the most amazing professors I have ever had in college. He is always super easy to get a hold of, and we have the COOLEST speakers come in and speak to our class. Entrepreneurship has been a very good experience with Seth!

Easy class. The only reason I didn't get an A is cause I missed some assignments of my own volition. I liked the modules, and the quizzes were not hard. I also appreciated how he switched up the DB posts instead of doing the same format every week, like some other classes.
Easy class, granted it was online. He was VERY slow at posting weekly assignments but overall wasn't bad. Assignments are straight forward and not too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of my fav professors at OSU. Truly cares about all his students. Loved every class I've taken with him. Only downside is he's not easy to reach outside of class- terrible with checking email. Slow to grade assignments but will give everyone an A if he waits too long lol.

I took his class as part of COE (A summer program), and he did a great job lecturing and was more than willing to answer any questions and walk through concepts again. Overall, a great professor and I wish I attended Ohio State so I could take another class with him as my professional.

I actually took the COE class ANS 2370A with Dr. Cressman, and he was an amazing professor. His lectures were fun and super engaging, and he's very passionate about the subject. He made the class extremely hard to fail, and you could tell he genuinely cares about his students. Wish I went to OSU so that I could have taken more classes with him!

He is a fairly good lecturer and his classes are pretty good;unfortunately, his inability to answer emails is the big issue I had. I sent multiple emails on multiple occasions with questions pertaining to the class, and only once did I get a response 2 weeks after I sent the message. If you never need to email/reach out for anything, you'll be fine
The modules for the week were rarely posted on time
Professor Cressman is cool and very knowledgeable in cooking. I learned a good amount from him.

The class is made up of weekly discussion posts, quizzes, and exams. The content is not difficult, but the modules were never posted on time. Syllabus stated 5pm on Mondays but oftentimes the content was published on Tuesday evenings/Wednesday mornings. No discussion posts were graded until the end. Overall easy class, just not structured well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Though there are no textbooks, there is supplemental reading every week. There are weekly assignments and a weekly exam. The final took a very long time and you should prepare to use the whole time given. The information is outdated and some of it is even considered wrong today.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took MEATSCI 2010 (BBQ Science) with Dr. Cressman and it was an awesome class. He's an awesome educator and truly wants you to learn. Great guy and great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 2200.03 online was based on weekly quizzes, weekly module exams, and weekly packback discussions. Everything was pretty straightforward and easy to understand. Make sure to get everything done and you'll be fine. Overall, good class and good prof.

This was a great class to take as a GPA science booster class. I highly recommend. All of the assignments were on Carmen. There was an additional discussion post graded by AI, which was kind of cool as well. I highly recommend this class and professor.
This was an amazing class! Basically, the quizzes and exams were multiple choice on Carmen, and it was so nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class online and it was great! The material was very interesting and the embedded learning quizzes and module exams were extremely doable if you read the material. Dr. Cressman always commented on group discussions and was available if there were any questions or troubles. I was unsure if I'd like the online setting, but it was fun!

I liked Dr. Cressman, he's hilarious. But I think he went a little too in-depth for the class itself, it's supposed to be a basic intro. It does not have a biology prerequisite, but it should if he is going to incorporate so much biology concepts into the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was like being taught by an extremely intelligent puppy. Dr. Cressman genuinely cares about his students and his material, and although his lectures can get a little muddled, he explains things in detail if you ask. Very smart guy, I would take this class every semester if I had to.
Dr. Cressman was awesome!! He really goes into detail on exams just to make sure you understand what you're learning. He's a great professor and a great guy.

He is a smart man, and loves his job. he often brings in examples to class to assist in our learning, but his test can be challenging if you dont study or go to class. over all hes a nice guy and knows what he is talking about and if you are having trouble go to him during his office hours he will be more than willing to help

He's is great. He really keeps your attention. He doesn't "lecture", he makes it fun. I learned & retained a lot from his class. He is very intelligent and respected, but he is also a normal guy that you can talk to outside of class like you're buddies. Pop quizzes- if you attend class you know they're coming. Exams are slightly difficult but fair.
He is a good professor, tests are pretty hard because he expects yo to know everything in full.  He is a nice guy, but he does like to tease students, so don't take it personally.

Dr. Cressman is a genuinely nice guy and wants his students to learn. You can tell he is very intelligent and knows the subject matter well. Can be confusing, but if you ask questions he'll help. He always held question and answer sessions before tests and allowed you to come to office hours after to talk about things you did wrong after tests.
Dr. Cressman is a really nice guy!! He is a tough grader, but it's only because he wants you to understand the material. He's laid back and has a really adorable smile!
I loved Dr. Cressman! He's a little tough on his grading, but it's only because he wants you to understand the whole concept he's teaching. He's super laid back and has an adorable smile!

Dr. Cressman is new to Ohio State but I have him this semester for half of ANISCI 2100 along with Dr. Ana Hill. Cressman is a genuinely nice guy very laid back and very helpful when you ask him questions. He goes a lot into the chemistry and biological details of animal science though so don''t expect an easy A. Tough course but he will help you.

love this guy. one of the most bizarre class experiences ive ever had at 8am. i hated this class but i am a joco truther. he might seem unapproachable in lecture but he is very cool and helpful in office hours. it's probably the best biochem class to take if you know youre going to be completely lost on the math part. exams are so difficult tho LOL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of mini in-class quizzes worth very little points but they add up. Just copies and pastes his lectures from the textbook so if you can memorize the text book then you'll be fine. Almost not even worth going to class because he always fell behind in lecture, rush content towards exam time, and would provide new material the day before the exam
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: By far the worst Professor I have ever had. He was completely unorganized and not an effective teacher. There is no point in showing up to class. Try your best to take this class with any other professor.
Interesting guy, but I find him to be chill for the most part. Tests are pretty rough, but everything can be solved.
Lectures are very monotone and talks at 0.5x speed the class is super unorganised and the exam questions are HARD. 4 midterms and a cumulative final. This class ruined my life and potentially my GPA.

Prof is a great person, seems like a funny guy. Class has 4 MTs and a cumulative final which is lowk absurd. Had a MT every 3 weeks, and they were HARD. I would study a week in advance reviewing all the resources and barely get the avg. He is helpful prof tho and easy to access outside of class, and TAs were genuinely lifesavers. Office hours help

If you put in the work and have (at least some) interest in biochem, you can succeed. Dr. Cogan is easily accessible outside of class, and his TAs are the best I've ever had in a class. While midterms are very hard, there are a lot of points spread out throughout the class, and ALOT of extra office hours and review sessions. I loved this class.

I love JoCo as a person. However, his class is bizzare. He jumps around to different topics with no context and random tangents, and if you ask him a question regarding a practice problem HE assigned you, he is often confused on what it is asking as if he didn't write it last year. He will skip pages of material in class and then put it everywhere?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cogan is nice so I wish the class went better but it is incredibly difficult for no reason. The midterms are far beyond intro to bio chem level, TAs would often be stumped on the questions too. No amount of studying would ever get me to the point of understanding the type of questions he asks on the exam. Better taking with a different professor.

I found his teaching style to be difficult to follow, as his lectures were scattered and lacked organization. He often bounced around material rather than explaining anything. The class itself was unorganized, and tests were unnecessarily difficult compared to lecture. He also struggled to answer questions about practice problems he would make.

honestly this class has been my least favorite out of all my classes at osu, worse than ochem. Cogans exams are incredibly hard and he isn't the best at explaining material. His TA did most of the work with helping us before exams and explaining material. He also assigns a lot of Mastering HW. Try to get Wu or Shimko
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think he was a great professor. He is definitely painted out to be pretty rough but, he has changed the class structure completely I got a 65 % in the class which ended up being a B- and I never went to lecture (not recommending that) I did still watch his lectures. I think he is a great professor over all highly recommend.

He's overall ok when it comes to lecturing.  Can be boring and is prone to rambling but he usually is able to explain the content.  It also really helps he records his lectures.  There is a lot of homework and participation grades which helps alleviate the exam grades.  The exams are REALLY hard and you will have to study a ton to score ok on them.

Dr. Cogan is very nice and always helpful during office hours. Although, the lectures are boring and hard to follow because he rambles a lot. The exams are hard and you never know what will be on them. You have to study a lot on your own.
He has an interesting vibe but is always willing to help with experiments. I enjoyed this class a lot and thought it was a lot easier than the biochemistry major sequence. Wish he taught my lectures!

Dr. Cogan is the worst professor I've had at OSU. He lacks communication, his lectures are disorganized, and the material is confusing and unrelated to the MCAT. His tests feel like a guessing game, and I don't feel prepared for future classes. He often seems unprepared and unsure of his own material. I don't recommend taking him.

The open internet exams really threw me. At the time I was happy not to have to memorize the things that people in other classes did. However, now in subsequent classes that build off of BioChem I don't feel like I have as strong of a basis for the metabolic pathways that other students who took BioChem with other professors seem to have.

Dr. Cogan's lectures are quite boring but everything on the exams comes right from the slides. There are 4 midterms and a final which is a lot but the final was much easier than the midterms to take off some of the stress. There are a lot of free homework and participation points to help your grade. There was a decent curve too.
Listen to the people who say Cogan makes organic chemistry look like a complete joke. Avoid!!

This may have been the worst profess I have ever had. For reference I had Baldwin for OCHEM, and I found that her class was easier. He gives you no practice problems and we missed two whole chapters due to lectures that talked about nothing having to do with the class. If you are pre-med don't waste your time you will be underprepared for the MCAT.
Told us the first day that he wasn't expecting to teach

This section has four midterms and a final compared to other sections led by better professors that have two midterms and a noncumulative final. His exams are not indicative of your ability to understand the content. Lectures are beyond dry and he makes biochem an unpleasant experience.

Cogan focus a lot on diagrams in his lectures and on exams. The exams have difficult diagrams that are complicated and don't really test you on your biochemical knowledge. His lecture do focus on the most important topics, but he is a nice guy and the class is doable. If you work hard you can do fine.

Dr. Cogan is one of the best professors I've had at OSU. He cares deeply about seeing all of his students succeed. He is understanding, and will always work with you if you are struggling. Exams can be difficult, but they are doable and you're given all the resources to study. Highly recommend doing the practice exams and going to office hours.

Professor Cogan's class was a real challenge. The open-note exams are deceptively difficult, with content that often feels unrelated to lectures. Though disorganized at times, he genuinely cares about students. Unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for preparing - highly recommend.
Always willing to help. Has lots of chances to ask questions, lots of office hours. Has a large curve
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: extremely disorganized course and set up very strange. Exams are open internet but difficult, keeps the averages around 60-70%. Poor content time management skills and bad at communicating homework due dates changing to correlate. Overall an overwhelming course and the way his class is set up makes it significantly worse.

Honestly, the worst professor I have taken. I had a 4.0 GPA before this class; I'm sure I would have loved Biochemistry if he wasn't the professor. He is the worst lecturer, I don't think I learned a single thing in his class. He has a cumulative exam at the end that is closed-note and I had multiple panic attacks preparing for it. Take anyone else

This class was super hard for me, but I don't know how much of that was because of the prof since I suck at chemistry. The exams are open note but REALLY hard and deadlines always get moved around. Came across as kinda callous the first few classes but he actually really cares about his students even if doesn't seem like it at first impression.

Very good professor but has difficult tests. The tests are open notes, but that doesn't make them much easier. He is accessible via email and his Sunday office hours and review sessions are helpful. Lots of exams and quizzes.
Buddy is an absolute geed. Very unhelpful outside of class and disorganized. Thinks that some students ask questions for no reason.

His exams are so difficult it makes Ochem feel like a Communications course. Not studying for his exams is a completely viable strategy because most of the time it will not even help you. You will pass or fail based off luck alone. Luckily though, so will everyone else, and the class is curved. So if you just need a C, this is the class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was extremely unorganized and time management was not his strong suit. Tests are open note/internet however they're very difficult and seemed to have little to do with the material. He uses programs online to "help" with the tested material, however that means you need to troubleshoot and learn different programs in order to get correct answers.

Dr. Cogan's exams were open note and internet, but were difficult and unrelated to class material. Recitation content was completely separate from lecture, and you are expected to know material not taught to you. He didn't cover all the content before some exams, and gave us an ADDITIONAL EXAM TWO TIMES as a "part two" that was not on the syllabus.

Dr. Cogan is a great professor! His lectures really helped me to understand Biochem which is a very difficult topic, and he was always accessible outside of class. He really and truly cares for all of his students which is insane because he teaches 250+ in one class. The tests were difficult, but there is a curve. Good luck future students!

Dr. Cogan is very smart and nice but he talks in 2x speed. I'm not kidding when I say I have to rewatch all of his lectures which normally takes me over 2 hours to write everything he says. You really have to understand the concepts to do well in his class. Exams are open note but very tricky and every question makes you second guess yourself.

Dr. Cogan is bad with time management. We never had all the material in time for the exam and he always went on tangents during class. He doesnt go over his lecture notes before class and skips around to whatever pops in his head. We went over glycolysis/gluconeogenisis the citric acid cycle and the electron transport chain in the last 2 weeks. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although Prof Cogan isn't super organized and tends to ramble during lecture, he makes understanding the material quite easy. I would say his exams are very fair (he could make them way harder if he wanted to), and you definitely need to pay attention in lecture to do well. Loved the class!

Professor Cogan does his best to help students, but there are straight up just too many exams. We had 4 exams, 2 of which he didn't finish the material. So ON TOP of that we had 2 take home midterms and a comprehensive exam. Seemed like we were taking an exam every week, which is ridiculous. The good thing is they're open note/internet.
He cares about students but gives awful exams that really don't test your understandings of the topics covered in lecture. No real way to study for the tests either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cogan really does care about his students and their success. The class is a bit disorganized so you just have to go with it. I recommend going to lecture and his Sunday Office Hours for help. The class is difficult, but not extremely stressful because the exams are open note - but it is still very difficult with low averages.

Dr. Cogan is a great guy if you get to know him. He can tell when you put in the effort and rewards you for it. The class was difficult for me but he is reasonable. I went to nearly every office hour and was more often than not, the only person there. The class was curved HARD at the end. The practice exams + his note style are SUPER helpful imo.

It's hard to evaluate Dr. Cogan, as biochem is truly a difficult course. His teaching style is helpful, but lectures for the most part are a bit unnecessary although attendance is mandatory. Tests are open internet but the internet will not help you. It's the kind of class where everyone struggles but the curve helps everyone.
Lots of quizzes and homeworks but theyre open note so easy grade boosters. He also brought in guest speakers which was nice to get different views on what we were discussing
Great professor. Biochem is hard in general, I feel like he did a good job
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I reached out to ask for help regarding the material. I really was not doing well with the online content and the info was not sticking in my head. I asked if there were campus resources or ways to do better in studying. He replied, "These are not questions I can answer in an email. Did you even see I had online office hours last week?" Run.

Cogan is a nice guy, and always made time for students outside of class. His lectures and notes are difficult to follow. Exams were open note, application-based. He loved making us use various online tools during exams. He seemed experimental in his approach to this class. Wouldn't recommend taking the online course with Cogan.

People don't love his lectures, but he can be really helpful if you talk with him 1-on-1. Dr. Cogan ALWAYS finds time to meet, even though he teaches hundreds of students every semester. He has tons of experience helping people through biochemistry, so whatever problem you might have, he has probably taught someone with the same problem in the past

YOU NEED TO READ TEXT BEFORE CLASS or you will not be able to follow him especially middle end semester! Exam are difficult even when you study, lecture okay, he cares and takes personal time to help. talk to him he will help! Use the tools he gives and participate, he wants to see you genuinly involved. difficult quiz lots of homework Tophat ques

Dr. Cogan was an average professor and lecturer. I personally did better in the class when I started reading and taking DETAILED notes on the textbook sections before he covered them in class. All exams (minus the final) were open book/open note, but dont be fooled into thinking that makes them easy! Application exam questions, but fair grader.

Cogan has no business being a professor for this class. He gives you scientific papers that he pulls extremely minute questions from without ever actually teaching the subject material he is asking about. Our entire section was lost for his entire module and ended up dropping a letter grade in the class because of his lack of organization. Avoid.

Dr. Cogan was an average lecturer for me. The lectures can sometimes be hard to follow. Make sure to show up to class to answer tophat questions and do all the homework for easy points. The material itself is fairly easy to learn, but his exams were hard. A good amount of the questions were application. The exams did get easier in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cogan makes a large lecture very personalized by showing interest in the success of each of his students. Biochemistry is not the most interesting class so no matter who you have, it will be difficult to focus in class. Dr. Cogan will help whenever he can and truly cares about your success in his class, but you have to put work in to do well.

One of the first few weeks of class he quoted Trump, and I was immediately turned off. Hard to want to learn from him after that. Regardless he was always available when I needed and even though I struggled with the midterms because there was often a lot of material, he was willing to help when he could.

Dr. Cogan rally cares for his students and did a lot in terms of offering extra credit and points. He took his own time every Sunday evening to come in and assist students with questions and homework. Overall a good guy, just not a great professor when it came to actually teaching the material. Very hard exams so make sure to study well.

Dr Cogan truly cares about his students. He acknowledges that this class is difficult, and there is too much material for the time frame. His exams are difficult, but if you stay around average you can ride the curve. He gives generous points for in class participation and online homework, so do those if you think you'll struggle.

Dr. Cogan is a great professor who really cares about his students. He takes time out of his schedule to be accessible outside of class, and holds weekly review sessions. He also does in class questions/activities to help make the class more engaging. His exams can be difficult, but if you take time to study then you can do well in the class.

His lectures are boring, but you need to pay attention because the commentary he adds to the slides is often the material on the exams. The exams are specific and difficult, however they aren't too bad if you take the time to study for them and not cram too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although some days lectures don't seem to have anything to do with the course material, Dr. Cogan is always fun to listen to and learn from. His exams are extremely fair and you go in knowing exactly what will be on them. If there ever is a weird question on an exam feel free to argue why your answer was right and you'll probably get your points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Cogan is so nice and open to helping students; however, I probably wouldnt advise taking his class unless you have a solid understanding of Biochem. Exams are extremely difficult, even if you study weeks ahead of time it wont help much. I wouldnt advise this class if needed it for med school. We were behind and didn't cover as much material

Dr. Cogan is an exceptional professor who clearly cares about student success. He had office hours regularly and even held Sunday study sessions regularly for students. Dr. Cogan's tests were not exceedingly difficult if you pay attention in lecture (they're interesting), but his exams are largely lecture-based so you will not do well if you skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: People say he's caring but all I ever got from asking questions was condescension. He is available often but that wasn't much help to me. Pretty easy tests but part of the battle was understanding his notes and how he writes his questions. Just know the exam check lists he posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Cogan was a pretty great professor. His exams were tough and his lecture notes were sometimes really difficult to understand, but if you actually study and participate, you will do fine in his class.

Cogan is a fair and caring professor. The class is difficult but it's biochem. He gives a lot of opportunities to earn extra points and a lot of help outside of lectures. This class is hard but structured to help you be very successful if you put in the time and effort. He also does a great job of marking his notes with MCAT tested material.

He made Biochem4511 the most frustrating class. His lectures were filled with a bunch of nonsensical tangents and random facts that he found interesting. He assigned homework that did not translate from his lectures. Also, we got so far behind we had to learn two different chapters at once for the last several weeks. His tests are all application.

Dr. Cogan is very unorganized and goes so slow to the point the other biochem classes are a month or so ahead. Instead of cutting out material, in the last couple weeks he posted about 10 lecture videos to compensate for getting behind and gave a midterm less than a week before the final over 6 chapters, most of which he barely covered in lecture.

Overall, this class was extremely difficult. I do think he is fair though. He cares a lot about his students and opens his classroom every Sunday for 2 hours to help with the homework. If you go to these sessions you are guaranteed a 100% on these assignments, due to the help he gives and the group effort. His notes are confusing and exams are hard

Dr. Cogan is not a professor I would recommend to anyone. I have put fourth immense amount of effort to this class and have gotten nothing out of it. The lectures are not helpful by any means. He assigns copious amounts of homework that does not help to understand the material. If you can get any other professor for this course do it at all costs!!

Dr. Cogan is a fantastic professor! I wouldn't normally post a review on here but I was shocked at how many people found him to be difficult or confusing. His tests are fair, given that harder questions are straightforward because they are straight from concepts that he emphasized in class. Much easier than other biochem profs as far as I've heard.

Dr. Cogan is a great professor who really cares about his students. The course is challenging, but if you read the book and study you'll be fine. He's always looking for ways to improve his teaching methods, and he even does research on finding the best way to help kids learn. A really nice guy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved having Dr. Cogan. He made concepts a lot easier and was a big help in office hours. He is incredibly caring and genuinely a great guy.

I had him for Evidence and he was awesome! Okay, his lectures were not useful and I did not pay attention much. However, his midterm is so by the book if you are willing to take the time to read, decipher and learn the material you will do well. One of my higher grades in law school.

Lectures were worthless, only went for the participation points. Gave an extra ACS final exam at the very end, he was the only one in the department that gave this- very annoying. The tests weren't that bad, but questions were littered with gram. errors- hard to understand. Backwards classroom- its hard to do that successfully in a 200+ lecture.
He was very vague in lectures; test questions did not make sense. No matter how much you study you'll be confused during exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Cogan is my favorite professor at OSU. He is genuinely so caring of all of his students and wants everyone to do well. His tests are pretty difficult, but he is really helpful during office hours.

Cogan can be frustrating during lecture- his voice drones, and he tends to make Tophat questions ambiguous or with straight up mistakes. However, the TA's are great and recitations activities, clicker Q's act a grade buffer outside of exams. There are more than enough resources to succeed in this class despite him & his thing for Jeffrey Dahmer.

I don't get anything out of his lectures; they make no sense and are SO boring. His tests are very hard and confusing also. To prepare, go over in-class assignments and old exams, as he will often repeat questions, and watch his lecture videos, because they are over different material than in class lectures and he uses questions from them too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's awesome if you want to study abroad! Made the trip so enjoyable and class was really laid back and fun.

One of the worst I've ever had.  None of his material goes together; one day the syllabus said "chemistry of life," assigned reading was on scientific process, he lectured on evolution(which is supposed to be 1114), and the in-class activity had us prove squares were 2D. If I didn't already know I liked bio this class would have made me HATE it.

Dr. Cogan is one of the worst professors I've ever had. Much like the others who post on here, I think he is awful at explaining concepts, his lectures are scattered and unhelpful, and his tests are legitimately ridiculous. And because it's an honors class, he feels the need to make it more "interactive" like NO

This course with Cogan/Herman was my most difficult course by far. I would take notes during the incredibly boring lecture, take notes from the book, pay attention in lab and I still struggled on exams. I think the only people who felt confident in this class were those who have no life outside of school. Thought I knew the material too.

Offers extra credit, but then takes it away after you've done the work. Have had to basically beg for our proper extra credit and even then it wasn't given to us in full. For how long he's been teaching, he should be better at this by now.

Great professor, always willing to clarify any concepts or expectations in office hours or after class. Tests are well written and fair and the notes he gives are really helpful for studying. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Ohio State.
His lectures are really just not good, and the types of problems he uses are so out of everyone's league.  He didn't explain concepts well at all.

The worst professor I ve ever met. His course just give us nothing and the lecture is unbelievable boring. I mean it's not like a "only textbook knowledge " boring, it's like you pay atteintion to the whole course but you find you gain nothing. He even just tell us to reed whole chapter ourselves because he spend too much time in meaningless thing.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Lectures made no sense and constantly jumped around. Tests were even worse. Unfair grader and not organized at all, and his wording on tests and recitation assignments were out of this world. Take this class with someone else!

Tests were horrible and way advanced beyond the material covered in class. Lectures were incredibly boring. Didn't seem to care about the material or teaching it properly. I used the textbook to take all my own notes and it is the only reason I learned anything at all.

Easily the worst prof I have ever had. He is clueless when it comes to anything chemistry, especially anything organic. A large portion of this class is organic chemistry based, and he either skips over it, or gets confused. Also, he is often wrong about these concepts. Do not take his class unless you want to have a horrible experience.
He is very confusing, he's a great guy and definitely wants you to learn but I think his teaching style is just terrible.

To be fair, he's covering some tough material. Due to significant content overlap between this class and another, though, I know that he's teaching it badly. Things that were clear, detailed, and interesting in the other class became confusing and mind-numbingly dull. His tests are pretty easy though. Don't buy the book.

Do not take this class if you are preparing for the MCAT. Cogan is the stereotypical "scatterbrained professor" and his lectures are all over the place.  Test questions are frequently unclear and contradict what was told during class.  Relied on other professor's notes and the textbook to really teach me biochem.

Dr. Cogan was all over the place. He'd constantly cancel his office hours and his lectures were disjointed and confusing. The costly book bought for the class was worthless because his (very difficult) exams were solely over small details from in-class worksheets and lectures. You MUST attend class for any hope of a good grade.

It is required that you go to lecture to get a big portion of your grade in clicker points. However cogans lectures have 0 structure and bounce all over the place from day to day. DO NOT TAKE HIM unless you want to spend entire lectures each week on your phone and then go home to teach yourself all the material from what he calls notes and the book

Definitely have to go to class if you want a chance at a good grade. He gives lecture slides in advance but they are so general you need to be there to hear him explain and record the info. He is extremely laid back and definitely interested in the material but doesn't seem to caring about teaching it. His tests are beyond confusing. Study a lot.

Cogan is all over the place. He talks in circles and sometimes can't even understand his own diagrams on the notes.  Only way to do well was to record lectures and read the book.  The recitation activities were confusing and could show up on exams.  I felt like it was a disservice to my education to take him for such an important class.

Dr. Cogan has kind of an "all over the place" lecturing style but if you listen and pay attention, he repeats things a thousand times.  He clearly emphasizes what is important and his tests are definitely fair (not necessarily easy).  He tells funny stories that are completely random.  I really enjoyed his class though.
Boring lecturer... talks himself in circles and never gives a straight answer... tests make no sense and diagrams are confusing... nice guy at heart but not very professional and not a good professor

His notes are very confusing and his exams are very disorganized. I simply missed couple points not because I didn't know how to answer, it was because his questions were so unclear that they didn't seem like  questions. He didn't even number the questions on the exam.

Really an easy class provided that you have a little bit of biology background and are willing to go to lecture. Tests were more based on examples that he gave in class than on the material itself. He hands out a lot of free points just for showing up to lecture, and the class averages were a lot higher than some of the other 1113 classes.
Dr. Cogan is sort of boring in lecture, but is great outside of class and in office hours.  The class is pretty easy if you watch the videos and take the practice tests.
Tests are tough but fair. If you show up to lecture and put in the time studying you can do well in his class. He tests more on application and not facts which I liked but may not be for you.

Class felt like 4113 not 1113. Cares more about sounding intelligent than explaining things clearly. I have always thought I had a clear understanding of biology before I took this class. Although it is titled "energy transfer and development", I'm fairly certain he uses the same lecture content as his BIochem course. Hardest class I've taken.

Bio is my niche - but this professor made me think otherwise. His lectures are extremely unorganized, his notes don't make any sense and are extremely scattered. His exams are near to impossible and questions are phrased extremely ambiguously - I found myself getting 90s in Ochem and barely doing well in his class. He is a kind person and his biolo

Cogan is a pretty good professor. He sometimes mixes things up and can be hard to follow at times, but he's a nice guy and genuinely does care about his students succeeding and learning. Honestly, if you didn't get a good grade after how much he tries to make the subject matter easier for this class, you probably just didn't put in enough effort.

The worst professor I've ever taken a class with. Very confusing and can't answer his own questions. Tests look like they're in a foreign language. He is NOT flexible in meeting outside his scheduled office hours and treats students as inferiors. All I can say is "good luck" if you get stuck with him...
Not an easy professor. His class is really hard but recitation helps. If you have an issue he will help you out in his office hours. Really professional guy

Dr. Cogan is a great professor. He is extremely knowledgable, and will go out of his way to explain things if people don't understand them. People expect this class to be really easy, which its not. However, if you put in some time and effort, you'll be fine. He's also really helpful in office hours and a really cool guy overall.

Dr. Cogan is an excellent professor. His teaching philosophy is geared to differentiate the serious students from the undisciplined ones. That being said, I do not recommend that an uncommitted, uninterested student take his courses. Personally, I was very pleased with his lectures, class format, and test difficulty.

Cogan is the worst professor I have ever had. He is unorganized and assumes you have taken other biology classes before, which I hadn't. The only good thing I can think of about him is that he posts videos of the material online, which helps a lot. If you read the book you will be fine, but I recommend finding a new teacher besides Cogan.

Dr. Cogan, at best, can be described as mediocre. He is extremely unorganized; oftentimes waiting until a few hours before a lecture to post notes on Carmen. Furthermore, he constantly talks himself into circles which causes the class to lose focus and subsequently stop learning. AVOID IF YOU CAN.

He is SO disorganized. His notes don't make sense at ALL and his grammar is so poor that it's difficult to even know what he's asking on the exams. Take this class with Shimko if you can. If you have to take this class with Cogan, buy the old textbook; his notes are straight out of there. He doesn't use the new book.

This class was extremely difficult. Exam averages were in the D and F range, which is ridiculous. His notes are scattered, he didn't cover the last 5 chapters, and he doesn't clarify things very well. Fortunately, there are a lot of extra points that help bring grades up but if you have a choice, I would take a different professor.
While his information is slightly disorganized, his lectures are interesting and informative. His tests are hard but fair. He is also very open to meeting for office hours and mentoring students.
When his material did not make sense, he took the time to help when he did not have to.  Yes, some of his tests were tough, but I studied hard and ended up successful in the class.

By far the hardest professor I have had here at OSU, and I have taken the chem and physics series. His notes are terrible, his tests are impossible, and he goes over material twice without making anything more clear. We spent a month talking about every little detail about respiration and photosynthesis. He expects too much for a GE science course.

I disagree with several of the previous comments. His tests are average, he tries to make lecture interesting, he wants students to succeed. He gives bonus points for clicker questions and is willing to provide clarity when necessary. I really enjoyed his class. Biochem does get mixed in and there is critical thinking, but it's not horrible at all.
Cogan is all over the place with his notes and his midterms are super hard. Would not recommend him!

The test are challenging, yes. The class average will be low, but there are a ridiculous amount of opportunities to earn (full) points in other areas. Also, maybe those that claimed that he doesn't "care" about student's concerns never actually contacted him until the 11th hour-- he always clarified things I was confused on.

Cogan was okay. His notes weren't great and he had some trouble simplifying things. He tried to engage the class and most clicker questions were decent. He adjusted the exam difficulty, but beware the many application questions. Reasonable expectations. If you're interested in Biochem(it gets mixed in) and a critical thinker take him. TAs were good

Dr.Cogan is an excellent professor. He is responsible,serious and nice guy. Every one knows that biochem is hard course,he can use good examples to explain difficult questions that help students to easily understeand.Also he has a good team for REC. I have good experience with ths corse.

He talks in circle, jumps to random topics and has a hard time formatting his lectures/notes into an easy to understand format. At the beginning he was uncaring as to if anyone was struggling. Average on the first exam was a 58%. Very difficult although not impossible. Very Boring as well.

First time I've been in a class that unanimously answered "NO!" when a professor asked, "does that makes sense?" His exams are not legit, and infiltrated with charts/graphs/images. Often, more than one answer ends up being correct - not sure if on purpose, either. Basically, impossible lecturer to follow, and he doesn't use the book. Go figure!

Cogan is one of those professors who knows so much he can't simplify it down and explain it to an intro to bio class. Even the TA's say he is being unreasonable. His notes go in circles and make you even more confused. He doesn't offer much help outside of class, and is standoffish to his students. Avoid him if possible!
Not a good lecturer, doesn't make things clear, doesn't care if a student is struggling, will avoid questions and talk in circles.
Avoid Cogan !!!!!The course is extremely hard.  You have to study really hard to pass the course.

I bombed the first (and easiest) midterm which caused me to get a B+. The class was certainly difficult and there are A LOT of details. I was started doing heavy review for his exams at least a week before. The final's material was the most difficult. I had lecture 4 days a week at 8am so it was essential for me to record the lectures.
This guy was not that bad. If you put the work into the class, an A is not that hard to get. He presented information in lecture that would be on the exam, and that's all you need to succeed.

Avoid Cogan. Median grades were always very low. He moves at a very fast pace in lecture and many test questions are based off of diagrams he spends only cursory time explaining. Pay attention to very small details and stories, they pretty much always pop up on tests. Labs were easy, lecture is the beast here. Book is useless.

Very dry and monotone. Not always very clear. I highly recommend getting the book as well as seeking other resources. Exams weren't terrible, but be prepared to put in some time to do well in this class. Not my favorite professor, but not my worst.

Cogan was a terrible professor. AVOID HIM IF YOU CAN.  His exams were purely based on lecture, so having the textbook was pointless. His exams are ridiculously hard, so even if you go to lecture you are probably screwed. His claim is that even if everyone does bad on the exam, they will get points from lab. He NEVER answers emails from students.
I got an E on the midterm & final and still got a B+ in the class (bonus & labs). Love him!
gave exams with a median grade of a d and would not curve. very hard to understand and no kindness. do not recommend!
Study the study guides he gives you for the midterm and final because the book is useless. Labs are very easy, but he can be confusing during lecture.
Pretty good class.  Go for the clicker points.  The labs are easy, but pointless.

You'd have to try REALLY hard to fail this class. I went to all the labs which are easy, went to most of the lectures and got bonus points, and even though i got C's on the both midterm and final, i got a B+ overall.

Such an easy class. The textbook is not needed and all the lecture slides are posted online. Coming to class is smart because of the clicker points, which after 40 correct you can get extra credit. For a science GEC, this was the way to go.
He makes is lectures interesting and relates the material to everyday situations.

He was a little soft spoken, but was a great lecturer. I would recommend printing out all of his notes; they make the lectures easier to follow. His exams are tough, so study a lot and go talk to him if you ahve trouble. He is genuinely willing to help students.
Overall good teacher. Its a hard class in general but he's very helpful if you ask or go to office hours.

Much better than I was expecting.  Not too difficult, really tests on what he mentions in class. Sometimes ideas are not connected fully together, but when studying his slides and notes, it does make sense.  Definitely there to help you. Certainly a great human being and a good professor.

Dr. Cogan's class was great. He tells side stories and jokes here and there.  Makes class more enjoyable.  It's not as bad as everyone has said :)..He knows his stuff and teaches it well. There's A LOT to learn in this class. Make sure you go to lecture! Reading the textbook will help clarify details.

Dr. Cogan is one of the few professors in academia who truly concerns himself with the growth and learning of his students. This is likely due to him not being involved with research. To add, Dr. Cogan is an outstanding human being and teaches others to do so through his demonstration of being a genuinely good person. Thank you Dr. Cogan.

EASY. And that is saying a lot, because I hate biology. There were so many "easy-point" assignments and a lot of graded material that made it extremely easy to do well. There was one exam and it was extremely easy because you just study the quizzes and practice material...and the exam questions are literally the same but worded slightly different.

Dr. Cogan is just a great teacher. Biochem is a hard class but he made the material interesting and kept class upbeat. He told a lot of jokes and explained all the material so that it was easier to understand.
Dr. Cogan was nice. He helped me with anything I needed, and really taught the course well. I hate bio but i even thought it was interesting class

He was a cool guy and would crack the occasional joke. His tests were quite hard, failed the midterm and got a D on the final... I still ended up getting a B- in the class because the labs evened everything out. Kind of boring but hey it's bio.

I had Cogan for bio113 & biochem511. He's a really nice and down to earth guy. He's always willing help (if u cnt make it to his office hrs he'll gladly set up an apptmnt another time). He is very clear and def knows his stuff. He presents a lot of material during lecture. I feel tht ppl struggle in his class b/c they dont come prepared for lecture

Mr. Cogan offers lots of extra credit.  His material is very basic Biology that most people should have learned in high school.  The lectures did get boring, but that is because I don't care about Bio. He's a good guy.

Dr. Cogan wasn't as bad as I had heard.
